`crates/quen-core/src/build.rs`:

```rs
//! The game-build pin (docs/intent.md, "The game build"). quen finds a game update itself, never by a mod refusing to
//! load. The exe's sha256 is a build's identity, its PE header's TimeDateStamp the label people read, and Steam's
//! `buildid` ([`crate::detect::steam_buildid`]) a second, independent sign. Before a launch changes anything, the exe
//! is checked against the known builds ([`gate`]). The RE knowledge base's tables name the build they were made on
//! ([`Build::of_kb`]), so names, RVAs and seeds from one build are never applied to another.
//!
//! The Windows layer reads the config and passes the platform in; nothing here knows a game.

use std::fmt;
use std::fs;
use std::io;
use std::path::Path;
use std::str::FromStr;

use serde::{Serialize, Serializer};

use crate::journal::sha256_hex;

/// What a PE file header says of its build: the linker's TimeDateStamp, and the machine the image is for
/// (`IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_*`, 0x8664 for x64).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Pe {
    pub machine: u16,
    pub stamp: Stamp,
}

impl Pe {
    /// The file header of an image's bytes: a DOS header (`MZ`) whose `e_lfanew` points at the PE signature and the
    /// file header. Anything else is refused, saying what is missing.
    pub fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Pe, String> {
        if !bytes.starts_with(b"MZ") {
            return Err("no MZ header: not an exe".into());
        }
        let e_lfanew = bytes.get(0x3C..0x40).ok_or("the DOS header is cut off")?;
        let pe = u32::from_le_bytes(e_lfanew.try_into().expect("4 bytes")) as usize;
        if bytes.get(pe..pe.saturating_add(4)) != Some(b"PE\0\0") {
            return Err(format!(
                "no PE signature at {pe:#x}: a DOS program, or not an exe"
            ));
        }
        // After the signature: Machine, NumberOfSections, TimeDateStamp, and 12 more bytes of file header.
        let header = bytes
            .get(pe + 4..pe + 24)
            .ok_or("the PE file header is cut off")?;
        Ok(Pe {
            machine: u16::from_le_bytes([header[0], header[1]]),
            stamp: Stamp(u32::from_le_bytes(
                header[4..8].try_into().expect("4 bytes"),
            )),
        })
    }
}

/// A PE TimeDateStamp, a build's label: written `0x` and 8 uppercase hex digits, as the KB writes it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct Stamp(pub u32);

impl fmt::Display for Stamp {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "0x{:08X}", self.0)
    }
}

/// `0x` and exactly 8 hex digits, of either case: a digit short is another stamp, not this one.
impl FromStr for Stamp {
    type Err = String;

    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Stamp, String> {
        let hex = s.strip_prefix("0x").or_else(|| s.strip_prefix("0X"));
        hex.filter(|h| h.len() == 8 && h.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()))
            .and_then(|h| u32::from_str_radix(h, 16).ok())
            .map(Stamp)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("stamp {s:?} is not 0x and 8 hex digits"))
    }
}

impl Serialize for Stamp {
    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        serializer.collect_str(self)
    }
}

/// A game build: its exe's sha256 (lowercase hex), the identity, and its PE stamp, the label.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct Build {
    pub sha256: String,
    pub stamp: Stamp,
}

impl fmt::Display for Build {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "sha256 {} (PE stamp {})", self.sha256, self.stamp)
    }
}

impl Build {
    /// The build of an exe's bytes, refused unless they are a PE image ([`Pe::parse`]).
    pub fn of_exe(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Build, String> {
        let pe = Pe::parse(bytes)?;
        Ok(Build {
            sha256: sha256_hex(bytes),
            stamp: pe.stamp,
        })
    }

    /// The build of the exe at `path`. Errors name the path; one that isn't a PE image is `InvalidData`.
    pub fn read_exe(path: &Path) -> io::Result<Build> {
        let at = |kind, why: &dyn fmt::Display| {
            io::Error::new(kind, format!("{}: {why}", path.display()))
        };
        let bytes = fs::read(path).map_err(|e| at(e.kind(), &e))?;
        Build::of_exe(&bytes).map_err(|why| at(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, &why))
    }

    /// The build a KB table (`names.tsv`, `hooks.tsv`) was made on: its one `# build: sha256=<64 hex> stamp=0x<8 hex>`
    /// line, a comment to the table parsers, anywhere in the file. A table without one is refused, since nothing then
    /// says which build its RVAs are for. The error is the reason, with its line number when it has one.
    pub fn of_kb(text: &str) -> Result<Build, String> {
        let mut found: Option<(usize, Build)> = None;
        for (i, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {
            let comment = line.trim().strip_prefix('#').map(str::trim_start);
            let Some(fields) = comment.and_then(|c| c.strip_prefix("build:")) else {
                continue;
            };
            let at = |why: String| format!("line {}: {why}", i + 1);
            if let Some((first, _)) = &found {
                return Err(at(format!(
                    "a second build line (the first is line {first})"
                )));
            }
            let (mut sha, mut stamp) = (None, None);
            for field in fields.split_whitespace() {
                match field.split_once('=') {
                    Some(("sha256", v)) if sha.is_none() => sha = Some(sha256(v).map_err(at)?),
                    Some(("stamp", v)) if stamp.is_none() => stamp = Some(v.parse().map_err(at)?),
                    _ => return Err(at(format!("{field:?} is not one sha256= and one stamp="))),
                }
            }
            let (Some(sha256), Some(stamp)) = (sha, stamp) else {
                return Err(at("the build line needs both sha256= and stamp=".into()));
            };
            found = Some((i + 1, Build { sha256, stamp }));
        }
        found.map(|(_, build)| build).ok_or_else(|| {
            "no build line (# build: sha256=<64 hex> stamp=0x<8 hex>): which build are its RVAs for?".into()
        })
    }

    /// Refuses unless `exe` is this build, a KB table's: its names, RVAs and seeds are this build's only.
    pub fn check_exe(&self, exe: &Build) -> Result<(), String> {
        let why = match (self.sha256 == exe.sha256, self.stamp == exe.stamp) {
            (true, true) => return Ok(()),
            (true, false) => {
                "the same sha256 with another stamp: the KB's build line has its stamp wrong"
            }
            (false, true) => "the same PE stamp, other bytes: a patched or damaged exe",
            (false, false) => "another build: a game update, or another store's exe",
        };
        Err(format!("the KB is for {self}, but the exe is {exe}: {why}"))
    }
}

/// A sha256 cell: 64 hex digits of either case, as lowercase (the form [`sha256_hex`] and the ledger use).
fn sha256(cell: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    if cell.len() == 64 && cell.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
        Ok(cell.to_ascii_lowercase())
    } else {
        Err(format!("sha256 {cell:?} is not 64 hex digits"))
    }
}

/// One build quen knows: its exe's sha256, the platform it was verified on, and what people call it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Known {
    pub platform: &'static str,
    pub sha256: String,
    pub label: String,
}

/// The builds quen knows. The local config's value (key `known_builds`, read by the Windows layer) lists them:
///
/// ```text
/// known_builds = 'steam <sha256> 5.01 (Steam build <buildid>); gog <sha256> 5.01 (GOG)'
/// ```
///
/// Each entry is `<platform> <sha256> <label>`, with `;` between entries: the platform the build was verified on
/// (`steam` or `gog`, as [`crate::detect`] names them), the exe's sha256 (64 hex digits), and a label for people (the
/// rest of the entry). Blank entries are skipped, so `''` lists none. The adapter's own list and the config's are
/// parsed as one value, the adapter's first: the same build listed twice is kept once, and refused with two labels.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct KnownBuilds(pub Vec<Known>);

impl KnownBuilds {
    pub fn parse(value: &str) -> Result<KnownBuilds, String> {
        let mut known: Vec<Known> = Vec::new();
        for (i, entry) in value.split(';').map(str::trim).enumerate() {
            if entry.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let bad = |why: String| format!("known_builds entry {} ({entry:?}): {why}", i + 1);
            let (platform, rest) = entry.split_once(char::is_whitespace).unwrap_or((entry, ""));
            let rest = rest.trim_start();
            let (sha, label) = rest.split_once(char::is_whitespace).unwrap_or((rest, ""));
            let platform = match platform {
                "steam" => "steam",
                "gog" => "gog",
                other => return Err(bad(format!("platform {other:?} is not steam or gog"))),
            };
            let sha256 = sha256(sha).map_err(bad)?;
            let label = label.trim();
            if label.is_empty() {
                return Err(bad(
                    "no label: entries are <platform> <sha256> <label>".into()
                ));
            }
            match known
                .iter()
                .find(|k| k.platform == platform && k.sha256 == sha256)
            {
                Some(k) if k.label == label => {}
                Some(k) => {
                    return Err(bad(format!("listed before as {:?}: which is it?", k.label)));
                }
                None => known.push(Known {
                    platform,
                    sha256,
                    label: label.into(),
                }),
            }
        }
        Ok(KnownBuilds(known))
    }
}

/// The build gate's decision on an exe, made before a launch changes anything.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
#[serde(tag = "status", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Gate {
    /// A build known on the install's platform.
    Known { label: String },
    /// Not known: the launch is refused, nothing changed. `why` names the sha256 and the stamp.
    Unknown { why: String },
    /// Not known, but the launch passed `allow_unknown_build`: it goes ahead, and the boot row records that.
    AllowedUnknown { why: String },
}

impl Gate {
    /// The refusal, if the gate refuses: an unknown build without the override.
    pub fn refusal(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        match self {
            Gate::Unknown { why } => Some(why),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Whether `exe` may launch from an install on `platform` (as [`crate::detect`] names it, `None` for a folder no store
/// lists): known if `known` lists its sha256 for that platform. A GOG install is matched by `gog` entries only, so its
/// exe is an unknown build until someone verifies it there, never known by Steam's hashes, even for the same
/// bytes: GOG's other files may differ. A folder no store lists (a copied install) is matched by Steam's entries, the
/// platform quen is verified on. An unknown build is refused unless `allow_unknown`.
pub fn gate(exe: &Build, platform: Option<&str>, known: &KnownBuilds, allow_unknown: bool) -> Gate {
    let on = platform.unwrap_or("steam");
    let entry = |platform: &str| {
        known
            .0
            .iter()
            .find(|k| k.platform == platform && k.sha256 == exe.sha256)
    };
    if let Some(k) = entry(on) {
        return Gate::Known {
            label: k.label.clone(),
        };
    }
    let why = match (on, entry("steam")) {
        ("gog", Some(steam)) => format!(
            "the same bytes as Steam's {:?}, but GOG is untested: its other files may differ, so Steam's known \
             builds don't count for it",
            steam.label
        ),
        ("gog", None) => {
            "a GOG install's exe is an unknown build until it is verified there: GOG's exe and files may differ \
             from Steam's"
                .into()
        }
        _ => "not a build quen knows: a game update, or another store's exe".into(),
    };
    let place = match platform {
        Some(p) => format!("on {p}"),
        None => "in a folder no store lists".into(),
    };
    let why = format!(
        "the game's exe {place} is {exe}: {why}. Once it is verified, add `{on} {} <label>` to known_builds in \
         quen's config, or launch with allow_unknown_build (recorded on the boot row)",
        exe.sha256
    );
    if allow_unknown {
        Gate::AllowedUnknown { why }
    } else {
        Gate::Unknown { why }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::json;

    /// A synthetic PE image, not from any real binary: a DOS header pointing at the PE header at 0x80, `machine` and
    /// `stamp` in its file header, then `body`.
    fn exe(machine: u16, stamp: u32, body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut b = vec![0u8; 0x98];
        b[..2].copy_from_slice(b"MZ");
        b[0x3C..0x40].copy_from_slice(&0x80u32.to_le_bytes());
        b[0x80..0x84].copy_from_slice(b"PE\0\0");
        b[0x84..0x86].copy_from_slice(&machine.to_le_bytes());
        b[0x86..0x88].copy_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes()); // NumberOfSections
        b[0x88..0x8C].copy_from_slice(&stamp.to_le_bytes());
        b.extend_from_slice(body);
        b
    }

    fn build(stamp: u32, body: &[u8]) -> Build {
        Build::of_exe(&exe(0x8664, stamp, body)).unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_pe_header_gives_the_stamp_and_the_machine() {
        let pe = Pe::parse(&exe(0x8664, 0x1234_ABCD, b"code")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            pe,
            Pe {
                machine: 0x8664,
                stamp: Stamp(0x1234_ABCD)
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(pe.stamp.to_string(), "0x1234ABCD");
        let x86 = Pe::parse(&exe(0x014C, 0xFF, b"")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            (x86.machine, x86.stamp.to_string()),
            (0x014C, "0x000000FF".into())
        );

        let good = exe(0x8664, 1, b"");
        let mut ne = good.clone();
        ne[0x80..0x82].copy_from_slice(b"NE");
        let mut far = good.clone();
        far[0x3C..0x40].copy_from_slice(&u32::MAX.to_le_bytes());
        let cases: [(&[u8], &str); 8] = [
            (b"", "no MZ header"),
            (b"\x7fELF\x02\x01\x01\0", "no MZ header"),
            (b"ZM", "no MZ header"),
            (b"MZ", "the DOS header is cut off"),
            (&good[..0x3E], "the DOS header is cut off"),
            (&ne, "no PE signature at 0x80: a DOS program"),
            (&far, "no PE signature at 0xffffffff"),
            (&good[..0x97], "the PE file header is cut off"),
        ];
        for (bytes, why) in cases {
            let e = Pe::parse(bytes).unwrap_err();
            assert!(e.contains(why), "{why}: {e}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn stamps_are_written_as_the_kb_writes_them() {
        assert_eq!("0x0BADF00D".parse(), Ok(Stamp(0x0BAD_F00D)));
        assert_eq!("0X0badf00d".parse(), Ok(Stamp(0x0BAD_F00D)));
        assert_eq!(Stamp(10).to_string(), "0x0000000A");
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(Stamp(10)).unwrap(), "0x0000000A");
        for bad in [
            "0BADF00D",
            "0xBADF00D",
            "0x00BADF00D",
            "0x0BADF00G",
            "0x+BADF00D",
            "0x",
            "",
        ] {
            let e = bad.parse::<Stamp>().unwrap_err();
            assert!(e.contains("not 0x and 8 hex digits"), "{bad}: {e}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_exe_s_build_is_its_sha256_and_its_stamp() {
        let bytes = exe(0x8664, 0x1111_2222, b"synthetic build A");
        let a = Build::of_exe(&bytes).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            a,
            Build {
                sha256: sha256_hex(&bytes),
                stamp: Stamp(0x1111_2222)
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            serde_json::to_value(&a).unwrap(),
            json!({"sha256": sha256_hex(&bytes), "stamp": "0x11112222"})
        );
        assert_eq!(
            a.to_string(),
            format!("sha256 {} (PE stamp 0x11112222)", a.sha256)
        );
        // The same stamp over other bytes is another build.
        let b = build(0x1111_2222, b"synthetic build B");
        assert_ne!(a.sha256, b.sha256);
        assert_eq!(
            Build::of_exe(b"not an exe"),
            Err("no MZ header: not an exe".into())
        );

        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("quen-build-{}", std::process::id()));
        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let (good, bad, missing) = (
            dir.join("game.exe"),
            dir.join("notes.exe"),
            dir.join("none.exe"),
        );
        fs::write(&good, &bytes).unwrap();
        fs::write(&bad, "MZ").unwrap();
        let read = (
            Build::read_exe(&good),
            Build::read_exe(&bad),
            Build::read_exe(&missing),
        );
        fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).unwrap(); // this test's own temp folder
        assert_eq!(read.0.unwrap(), a);
        let bad_err = read.1.unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(bad_err.kind(), io::ErrorKind::InvalidData);
        let text = bad_err.to_string();
        assert!(
            text.contains("notes.exe") && text.contains("the DOS header is cut off"),
            "{text}"
        );
        let missing_err = read.2.unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(missing_err.kind(), io::ErrorKind::NotFound);
        assert!(
            missing_err.to_string().contains("none.exe"),
            "{missing_err}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_kb_names_its_build_on_a_comment_line() {
        let exe = build(0x0BAD_F00D, b"synthetic KB build");
        let line = format!("# build: sha256={} stamp=0x0BADF00D", exe.sha256);
        let table = format!(
            "# synthetic KB names, not from any real binary\n{line}\nrva\tname\tkind\tconfidence\tsource\tdate\n\
             0x1000\tf\tfunction\tO\ttest\t2026-01-01\n"
        );
        assert_eq!(Build::of_kb(&table), Ok(exe.clone()));
        assert_eq!(exe.check_exe(&exe), Ok(()));
        // Indented, no space after #, the fields swapped, an uppercase sha256: the same build.
        let loose = format!(
            "  #build:  stamp=0x0badf00d\tsha256={}\n",
            exe.sha256.to_uppercase()
        );
        assert_eq!(Build::of_kb(&loose), Ok(exe.clone()));

        let sha = &exe.sha256;
        for (text, why) in [
            ("rva\tname\n# a comment\n".to_owned(), "no build line"),
            ("# builds: notes\n".to_owned(), "no build line"),
            (
                format!("x\n{line}\n{line}\n"),
                "line 3: a second build line (the first is line 2)",
            ),

                "# build: stamp=0x0BADF00D\n".to_owned(),
                "line 1: the build line needs both",
            ),

                "is not 0x and 8 hex digits",
            ),

            assert!(e.contains(why), "{text:?}: {e}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn known_builds_parse_from_the_config_value() {
        let (a, b) = (sha256_hex(b"synthetic A"), sha256_hex(b"synthetic B"));

        );

            sha256: sha256.into(),
            label: label.into(),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            known.0,
            [
                entry("steam", &a, "1.0 (Steam build 7)"),
                entry("gog", &b, "GOG 1.0"),
                entry("steam", &b, "1.1"),
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(KnownBuilds::parse(""), Ok(KnownBuilds::default()));
        assert_eq!(KnownBuilds::parse(" ; "), Ok(KnownBuilds::default()));

        for (value, why) in [

            (format!("steam {a}"), "no label"),

                "platform \"epic\" is not steam or gog",
            ),

            (format!("steam {a} 1.0; steam {a} 1.1"), "entry 2 (\"steam "),
            (

                "listed before as \"1.0\": which is it?",
            ),
        ] {

            assert!(e.starts_with("known_builds entry "), "{e}");
            assert!(e.contains(why), "{value}: {e}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_gate_knows_a_listed_build_and_refuses_another_naming_both_values() {
        let (v1, v2) = (build(0x1111_1111, b"v1"), build(0x2222_2222, b"v2"));
        let known = KnownBuilds::parse(&format!("steam {} 1.0", v1.sha256)).unwrap();
        let one = Gate::Known {
            label: "1.0".into(),
        };
        assert_eq!(gate(&v1, Some("steam"), &known, false), one);
        assert_eq!(
            gate(&v1, Some("steam"), &known, true),
            one,
            "the override is unused"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            gate(&v1, None, &known, false),
            one,
            "a copied folder counts as Steam's"
        );
        assert_eq!(one.refusal(), None);
        assert_eq!(
            serde_json::to_value(&one).unwrap(),
            json!({"status": "known", "label": "1.0"})
        );

        let refused = gate(&v2, Some("steam"), &known, false);
        let why = refused.refusal().unwrap();
        assert!(
            why.contains(&v2.sha256) && why.contains("0x22222222"),
            "{why}"
        );
        assert!(why.contains("not a build quen knows"), "{why}");
        assert!(
            why.contains(&format!(
                "add `steam {} <label>` to known_builds",
                v2.sha256
            )),
            "{why}"
        );
        assert!(why.contains("allow_unknown_build"), "{why}");
        let allowed = gate(&v2, Some("steam"), &known, true);
        assert_eq!(
            allowed,
            Gate::AllowedUnknown {
                why: why.to_owned()
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(allowed.refusal(), None);
        assert_eq!(
            serde_json::to_value(&allowed).unwrap()["status"],
            "allowed_unknown"
        );
        let why = gate(&v2, None, &known, false).refusal().unwrap().to_owned();
        assert!(
            why.contains("in a folder no store lists") && why.contains("add `steam "),
            "{why}"
        );
        assert!(
            gate(&v1, Some("steam"), &KnownBuilds::default(), false)
                .refusal()
                .is_some()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn gog_is_an_unknown_build_until_verified_there() {
        let (v1, other) = (build(0x1111_1111, b"v1"), build(0x1111_1111, b"GOG's own"));
        let steam_only = KnownBuilds::parse(&format!("steam {} 1.0", v1.sha256)).unwrap();
        // The same bytes as Steam's known build: still unknown on GOG.
        let why = gate(&v1, Some("gog"), &steam_only, false)
            .refusal()
            .unwrap()
            .to_owned();
        assert!(
            why.contains("on gog") && why.contains(&v1.sha256) && why.contains("0x11111111"),
            "{why}"
        );
        assert!(
            why.contains("the same bytes as Steam's \"1.0\", but GOG is untested"),
            "{why}"
        );
        assert!(
            why.contains(&format!("add `gog {} <label>`", v1.sha256)),
            "{why}"
        );
        let why = gate(&other, Some("gog"), &steam_only, false)
            .refusal()
            .unwrap()
            .to_owned();
        assert!(why.contains("until it is verified there"), "{why}");
        assert!(matches!(
            gate(&v1, Some("gog"), &steam_only, true),
            Gate::AllowedUnknown { .. }
        ));
        // Once verified, a gog entry knows it, and a GOG-only entry doesn't count for Steam.
        let gog = KnownBuilds::parse(&format!("gog {} 1.0 (GOG)", other.sha256)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            gate(&other, Some("gog"), &gog, false),
            Gate::Known {
                label: "1.0 (GOG)".into()
            }
        );
        assert!(gate(&other, Some("steam"), &gog, false).refusal().is_some());
        assert!(gate(&other, None, &gog, false).refusal().is_some());
    }
}

```

`crates/quen-core/src/cvar.rs`:

```rs
//! A running game's config vars ("cvars"), found by name the way the harness's cvar_poke.py finds them (this is its
//! port), read, and their writes planned. Where a var object keeps its fields is the KB's, per build
//! (`cvar_layout.tsv`): nothing here knows a game.
//!
//! The method: the var's name, with a NUL before and after it, in a section that is neither writable nor executable;
//! a var object is a pointer to that name, 8-byte aligned in a writable section, less the name's offset. A hit counts
//! only if its type code is one the layout names, its value pointer points at its own live value, and its group is the
//! one asked for (`Group/Name`). Nothing here writes: a set or a restore is a [`Write`] the platform layer journals and
//! makes. It is a plain store, like cvar_poke's: the engine's setter (its clamp and on-changed callback) doesn't run.

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::fmt;
use std::io;
use std::ops::ControlFlow;

use serde::Serialize;

use crate::mem::{self, Image, Memory, SCN_EXECUTE, SCN_WRITE, Skipped, TsvError, Write};
use crate::seeds::{rva, tsv_rows};

const HEADER: [&str; 10] = [
    "build", "group", "name", "flags", "value", "default", "live", "bool", "int", "float",
];

/// One `cvar_layout.tsv` row: where one build's var objects keep their fields, as offsets from the object.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Layout {
    /// The build stamp, as [`mem::image`] gives it.
    pub build: String,
    /// Pointers to the group and name strings.
    pub group: u64,
    pub name: u64,
    /// A u32 whose low byte is the var's type code.
    pub flags: u64,
    /// A pointer to the live value.
    pub value: u64,
    pub default: u64,
    pub live: u64,
    /// The type codes of bool, int and float vars.
    pub codes: [u8; 3],
}

/// The layouts of a KB `cvar_layout.tsv`: a header row of `build group name flags value default live bool int float`,
/// then one row per build: the offsets as `0x` hex, the type codes as decimal bytes.
pub fn from_layout_tsv(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Layout>, TsvError> {
    let err = |line, msg| TsvError {
        file: "cvar_layout.tsv",
        line,
        msg,
    };
    let mut layouts: Vec<Layout> = Vec::new();
    for (line, [build, offsets @ .., b, i, f]) in
        tsv_rows(text, &HEADER).map_err(|(l, m)| err(l, m))?
    {
        let err = |msg| err(line, msg);
        if build.is_empty() || layouts.iter().any(|l| l.build == build) {
            return Err(err(format!("build {build:?} is blank or defined twice")));
        }
        let o = offsets
            .iter()
            .map(|cell| rva(cell).map(u64::from))
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
            .map_err(err)?;
        let code = |cell: &str| {
            cell.parse::<u8>()
                .map_err(|_| err(format!("type code {cell:?} is not 0-255")))
        };
        let codes = [code(b)?, code(i)?, code(f)?];
        if codes[0] == codes[1] || codes[1] == codes[2] || codes[0] == codes[2] {
            return Err(err(format!(
                "the type codes {codes:?} are not three different ones"
            )));
        }
        layouts.push(Layout {
            build: build.into(),
            group: o[0],
            name: o[1],
            flags: o[2],
            value: o[3],
            default: o[4],
            live: o[5],
            codes,
        });
    }
    Ok(layouts)
}

/// A var's type.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Kind {
    Bool,
    Int,
    Float,
}

const KINDS: [Kind; 3] = [Kind::Bool, Kind::Int, Kind::Float];

impl Layout {
    fn kind(&self, code: u8) -> Option<Kind> {
        Some(KINDS[self.codes.iter().position(|&c| c == code)?])
    }
}

/// A var's value: a bool's byte as it is (0 or 1, unless something else wrote it), an int or a float. Serialized as a
/// JSON number.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Serialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum Value {
    Bool(u8),
    Int(i32),
    Float(f32),
}

impl Value {
    fn decode(kind: Kind, b: &[u8]) -> Value {
        let word = || b[..4].try_into().expect("a 4-byte read");
        match kind {
            Kind::Bool => Value::Bool(b[0]),
            Kind::Int => Value::Int(i32::from_le_bytes(word())),
            Kind::Float => Value::Float(f32::from_le_bytes(word())),
        }
    }

    fn bytes(self) -> Vec<u8> {
        match self {
            Value::Bool(b) => vec![b],
            Value::Int(i) => i.to_le_bytes().to_vec(),
            Value::Float(f) => f.to_le_bytes().to_vec(),
        }
    }

    /// `text` as a value of `kind`: a bool is 0, 1, false or true; an int decimal, or `0x` / `0o` / `0b` with a sign
    /// before it, in i32's range; a float any finite number in f32's range. Nothing is truncated or wrapped.
    pub fn parse(kind: Kind, text: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
        let bad = |what| format!("{text:?} is not {what}");
        match kind {
            Kind::Bool => match text.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
                "0" | "false" => Ok(Value::Bool(0)),
                "1" | "true" => Ok(Value::Bool(1)),
                _ => Err(bad("a bool (0/1/true/false)")),
            },
            Kind::Int => int(text)
                .and_then(|i| i32::try_from(i).ok())
                .map(Value::Int)
                .ok_or_else(|| bad("an int in -2147483648..=2147483647")),
            // Through f64, as cvar_poke's float() and struct.pack('<f') round.
            Kind::Float => text
                .parse::<f64>()
                .ok()
                .map(|f| f as f32)
                .filter(|f| f.is_finite())
                .map(Value::Float)
                .ok_or_else(|| bad("a finite float")),
        }
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for Value {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Value::Bool(b) => write!(f, "{b}"),
            Value::Int(i) => write!(f, "{i}"),
            Value::Float(x) => write!(f, "{x:?}"),
        }
    }
}

/// Python's `int(text, 0)` without its underscores: a sign, then decimal (no leading zeros), or `0x` / `0o` / `0b`.
fn int(text: &str) -> Option<i64> {
    let (negative, digits) = match text.strip_prefix('-') {
        Some(rest) => (true, rest),
        None => (false, text.strip_prefix('+').unwrap_or(text)),
    };
    let lower = digits.to_ascii_lowercase();
    let (radix, digits) = match lower.get(..2) {
        Some("0x") => (16, &lower[2..]),
        Some("0o") => (8, &lower[2..]),
        Some("0b") => (2, &lower[2..]),
        _ => (10, &lower[..]),
    };
    let leading_zero = radix == 10 && digits.starts_with('0') && digits.bytes().any(|b| b != b'0');
    if digits.is_empty() || leading_zero || !digits.chars().all(|c| c.is_digit(radix)) {
        return None;
    }
    let n = i64::from_str_radix(digits, radix).ok()?;
    Some(if negative { -n } else { n })
}

/// A var as read: `Group/Name` as the object names itself (`Name` when it has no group), where it is, its type and
/// flags, its default and its live value.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct Var {
    pub name: String,
    pub address: u64,
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub kind: Kind,
    pub flags: u32,
    pub default: Value,
    pub live: Value,
}

/// What [`find`] saw.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct Found {
    /// The var objects that pass every check, ascending.
    pub vars: Vec<u64>,
    /// Pointer hits that failed one, and which.
    pub rejected: Vec<Rejected>,
    /// What couldn't be read, so may hold a name or a var nobody saw.
    pub skipped: Vec<Skipped>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct Rejected {
    pub address: u64,
    pub why: String,
}

/// Every var object for `full` (`Name` or `Group/Name`; the group may hold `/` itself) in `image`.
pub fn find(mem: &dyn Memory, image: &Image, layout: &Layout, full: &str) -> Found {
    let (group, name) = match full.rsplit_once('/') {
        Some((group, name)) => (Some(group), name),
        None => (None, full),
    };
    let mut found = Found::default();
    let needle = [&[0], name.as_bytes(), &[0]].concat();
    let mut names = HashSet::new();
    let mut buf = Vec::new();
    for s in image
        .sections
        .iter()
        .filter(|s| s.flags & (SCN_EXECUTE | SCN_WRITE) == 0)
    {
        let tail = needle.len() as u64 - 1;
        let _ = mem::chunks(
            mem,
            s.base,
            s.size,
            tail,
            &mut buf,
            &mut found.skipped,
            |at, b| {
                let hits = b
                    .windows(needle.len())
                    .enumerate()
                    .filter(|(_, w)| *w == needle);
                names.extend(hits.map(|(i, _)| at + i as u64 + 1));
                ControlFlow::Continue(())
            },
        );
    }
    let mut objects = Vec::new();
    for s in image.sections.iter().filter(|s| s.flags & SCN_WRITE != 0) {
        if names.is_empty() {
            break;
        }
        let _ = mem::chunks(
            mem,
            s.base,
            s.size,
            0,
            &mut buf,
            &mut found.skipped,
            |at, b| {
                for (i, q) in b.chunks_exact(8).enumerate() {
                    let site = at + 8 * i as u64;
                    let pointer = u64::from_le_bytes(q.try_into().expect("8 bytes"));
                    if names.contains(&pointer) && site - s.base >= layout.name {
                        objects.push(site - layout.name);
                    }
                }
                ControlFlow::Continue(())
            },
        );
    }
    objects.sort_unstable();
    for address in objects {
        match check(mem, layout, address, group) {
            Ok(()) => found.vars.push(address),
            Err(why) => found.rejected.push(Rejected { address, why }),
        }
    }
    found
}

/// Why the object at `obj` is not a var (of `group`, if given): its type code, its value pointer, its group.
fn check(mem: &dyn Memory, layout: &Layout, obj: u64, group: Option<&str>) -> Result<(), String> {
    let [code] = at(mem, obj + layout.flags)?;
    if layout.kind(code).is_none() {
        return Err(format!("type code {code}"));
    }
    let value = u64::from_le_bytes(at(mem, obj + layout.value)?);
    let live = obj + layout.live;
    if value != live {
        return Err(format!(
            "value pointer {value:#x}, not its live value at {live:#x}"
        ));
    }
    if let Some(group) = group {
        let found = string(mem, u64::from_le_bytes(at(mem, obj + layout.group)?));
        if found.as_deref() != Some(group) {
            return Err(format!("group {found:?}"));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn at<const N: usize>(mem: &dyn Memory, address: u64) -> Result<[u8; N], String> {
    let mut b = [0; N];
    mem.read(address, &mut b)
        .map(|()| b)
        .map_err(|e| format!("can't read {N} bytes at {address:#x}: {e}"))
}

/// The NUL-terminated string at `address`, at most 128 bytes of it; `None` for a null or unreadable pointer.
fn string(mem: &dyn Memory, address: u64) -> Option<String> {
    if address == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    // A short string may end near the end of its region: then read only to the end of its page.
    let mut b = vec![0; 128];
    if mem.read(address, &mut b).is_err() {
        b.truncate((0x1000 - address % 0x1000).min(128) as usize);
        mem.read(address, &mut b).ok()?;
    }
    let end = b.iter().position(|&c| c == 0).unwrap_or(b.len());
    Some(String::from_utf8_lossy(&b[..end]).into_owned())
}

/// The one var `found` holds for `full`, or why not.
pub fn one(found: &Found, full: &str) -> Result<u64, String> {
    if let [obj] = found.vars[..] {
        return Ok(obj);
    }
    let list: Vec<String> = found.vars.iter().map(|v| format!("{v:#x}")).collect();
    let hint = match found.vars.len() {
        0 if !found.skipped.is_empty() => {
            format!(" ({} ranges couldn't be read)", found.skipped.len())
        }
        0 => String::new(),
        _ if !full.contains('/') => " (give Group/Name)".into(),
        _ => " (the same group and name twice)".into(),
    };
    Err(format!(
        "{full}: {} matching config objects [{}]; need exactly 1{hint}",
        found.vars.len(),
        list.join(", ")
    ))
}

/// Reads the var object at `obj`.
pub fn read(mem: &dyn Memory, layout: &Layout, obj: u64) -> io::Result<Var> {
    let field = |offset: u64, len: usize| {
        let mut b = vec![0; len];
        mem.read(obj + offset, &mut b).map(|()| b)
    };
    let pointer =
        |offset| field(offset, 8).map(|b| u64::from_le_bytes(b.try_into().expect("8 bytes")));
    let flags = u32::from_le_bytes(field(layout.flags, 4)?.try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
    let code = flags as u8;
    let kind = layout.kind(code).ok_or_else(|| {
        io::Error::new(
            io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,
            format!("{obj:#x}: type code {code}, not a var's"),
        )
    })?;
    let size = if kind == Kind::Bool { 1 } else { 4 };
    let name = string(mem, pointer(layout.name)?).unwrap_or_default();
    let name = match string(mem, pointer(layout.group)?) {
        Some(group) => format!("{group}/{name}"),
        None => name,
    };
    Ok(Var {
        name,
        address: obj,
        kind,
        flags,
        default: Value::decode(kind, &field(layout.default, size)?),
        live: Value::decode(kind, &field(layout.live, size)?),
    })
}

/// What a write puts in a var.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Set<'a> {
    /// A value as text, parsed as the var's type ([`Value::parse`]).
    Value(&'a str),
    /// The var's default (not the settings file's value, if that differs).
    Default,
}

/// The write that puts `set` in `var`'s live value, as just read; or why not.
pub fn plan(var: &Var, layout: &Layout, set: Set) -> Result<Write, String> {
    let new = match set {
        Set::Default => var.default,
        Set::Value(text) => Value::parse(var.kind, text)
            .map_err(|e| format!("{e} for {:?} var {}", var.kind, var.name))?,
    };
    Ok(Write {
        address: var.address + layout.live,
        old: var.live.bytes(),
        new: new.bytes(),
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::mem::{Kind as RegionKind, Region};

    /// A synthetic layout, not any game's.
    fn layout(build: &str) -> Layout {
        Layout {
            build: build.into(),
            group: 0x10,
            name: 0x08,
            flags: 0x20,
            value: 0x28,
            default: 0x18,
            live: 0x1c,
            codes: [7, 8, 9],
        }
    }

    /// A PE-shaped image built in a byte vector: headers, `.text`, `.rdata` (the strings) and `.data` (the objects),
    /// and every read at `base` + offset into it. Like cvar_poke's selftest image, laid out by [`layout`].
    struct Img {
        base: u64,
        bytes: std::cell::RefCell<Vec<u8>>,
        /// Ranges every read fails on.
        bad: Vec<std::ops::Range<u64>>,
        strings: Vec<(String, u64)>,
        next_string: usize,
        next_object: usize,
    }

    const TEXT: usize = 0x1000;
    const RDATA: usize = 0x2000;
    const DATA: usize = 0x4000;
    const STAMP: u32 = 0x1234_abcd;

    impl Img {
        fn new(base: u64) -> Img {
            let mut b = vec![0u8; 0x6000];
            b[0x3c..0x40].copy_from_slice(&0x80u32.to_le_bytes());
            b[0x80..0x84].copy_from_slice(b"PE\0\0");
            b[0x86..0x88].copy_from_slice(&3u16.to_le_bytes());
            b[0x88..0x8c].copy_from_slice(&STAMP.to_le_bytes());
            b[0x94..0x96].copy_from_slice(&0xf0u16.to_le_bytes());
            let sections = [
                (&b".text"[..], TEXT, 0x1000, 0x6000_0020u32),
                (b".rdata", RDATA, 0x2000, 0x4000_0040),
                (b".data", DATA, 0x2000, 0xc000_0040),
            ];
            for (i, (name, va, size, flags)) in sections.into_iter().enumerate() {
                let s = 0x80 + 24 + 0xf0 + 40 * i;
                b[s..s + name.len()].copy_from_slice(name);
                b[s + 8..s + 12].copy_from_slice(&(size as u32).to_le_bytes());
                b[s + 12..s + 16].copy_from_slice(&(va as u32).to_le_bytes());
                b[s + 36..s + 40].copy_from_slice(&flags.to_le_bytes());
            }
            Img {
                base,
                bytes: b.into(),
                bad: Vec::new(),
                strings: Vec::new(),
                next_string: RDATA,
                next_object: DATA,
            }
        }

        /// `text`, NUL before and after, in `.rdata` (once per text): its address.
        fn string(&mut self, text: &str) -> u64 {
            if let Some((_, at)) = self.strings.iter().find(|(s, _)| s == text) {
                return *at;
            }
            let at = self.next_string;
            let mut b = self.bytes.borrow_mut();
            b[at + 1..at + 1 + text.len()].copy_from_slice(text.as_bytes());
            self.next_string += text.len() + 2;
            let address = self.base + at as u64 + 1;
            self.strings.push((text.into(), address));
            address
        }

        fn put(&self, address: u64, bytes: &[u8]) {
            let at = (address - self.base) as usize;
            self.bytes.borrow_mut()[at..at + bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(bytes);
        }

        /// A var object in `.data` by [`layout`]: its address. `value` overrides the value pointer.
        fn var(
            &mut self,
            group: &str,
            name: &str,
            code: u8,
            default: Value,
            value: Option<u64>,
        ) -> u64 {
            let l = layout("");
            let obj = self.base + self.next_object as u64;
            self.next_object += 0x30;
            let (group, name) = (self.string(group), self.string(name));
            self.put(obj + l.group, &group.to_le_bytes());
            self.put(obj + l.name, &name.to_le_bytes());
            self.put(obj + l.flags, &(0x200 | u32::from(code)).to_le_bytes());
            self.put(obj + l.value, &value.unwrap_or(obj + l.live).to_le_bytes());
            self.put(obj + l.default, &default.bytes());
            self.put(obj + l.live, &default.bytes());
            obj
        }

        fn apply(&self, w: &Write) {
            assert_eq!(
                self.get(w.address, w.old.len()),
                w.old,
                "the plan read what is there"
            );
            self.put(w.address, &w.new);
        }

        fn get(&self, address: u64, len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
            let mut b = vec![0; len];
            self.read(address, &mut b).unwrap();
            b
        }

        fn image(&self) -> Image {
            mem::image(self, self.base).unwrap()
        }
    }

    impl Memory for Img {
        fn read(&self, address: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<()> {
            let b = self.bytes.borrow();
            let end = address.saturating_add(buf.len() as u64);
            let gone = self.bad.iter().any(|r| r.start < end && address < r.end);
            match address.checked_sub(self.base).map(|at| at as usize) {
                Some(at) if !gone && at + buf.len() <= b.len() => {
                    buf.copy_from_slice(&b[at..at + buf.len()]);
                    Ok(())
                }
                _ => Err(io::Error::other(format!(
                    "nothing readable at {address:#x}"
                ))),
            }
        }

        fn regions(&self) -> io::Result<Vec<Region>> {
            let size = self.bytes.borrow().len() as u64;
            Ok(vec![Region {
                base: self.base,
                size,
                kind: RegionKind::Image,
                protect: 0x02,
                section: None,
            }])
        }
    }

    const BASE: u64 = 0x7ff6_0000_0000;

    /// cvar_poke's selftest cases, on the synthetic layout.
    fn sample() -> (Img, Vec<u64>) {
        let mut img = Img::new(BASE);
        // A pointer to a name in .text is not an object: only writable sections hold them.
        let use_x = img.string("UseX");
        for at in (0x1100..0x1200).step_by(8) {
            img.put(BASE + at, &use_x.to_le_bytes());
        }
        let objs = vec![
            img.var("Rendering/RT", "Tlas", 9, Value::Float(800.0), None),
            img.var("Rendering/RT", "Budget", 8, Value::Int(0), None),
            img.var("Rendering", "UseX", 7, Value::Bool(1), None),
            img.var("Rendering", "Enabled", 7, Value::Bool(1), None),
            img.var("Other", "Enabled", 7, Value::Bool(0), None),
            img.var("Other", "Broken", 5, Value::Int(0), None),
            img.var("Other", "Twice", 8, Value::Int(3), None),
            img.var("Other", "Twice", 8, Value::Int(4), None),
        ];
        (img, objs)
    }

    #[test]
    fn images_give_their_stamp_and_sections() {
        let img = Img::new(BASE);
        let image = img.image();
        assert_eq!(image.stamp, "0x1234ABCD");
        let names: Vec<(&str, u64, u64)> = image
            .sections
            .iter()
            .map(|s| (s.name.as_str(), s.base - BASE, s.size))
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(
            names,
            [
                (".text", 0x1000, 0x1000),
                (".rdata", 0x2000, 0x2000),
                (".data", 0x4000, 0x2000)
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(image.sections[2].flags & SCN_WRITE, SCN_WRITE);
        img.put(BASE + 0x80, b"NE\0\0");
        assert!(
            mem::image(&img, BASE)
                .unwrap_err()
                .to_string()
                .contains("no PE header")
        );
        assert!(mem::image(&img, 0x10).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn finds_one_var_by_name_or_group_and_name() {
        let (img, objs) = sample();
        let image = img.image();
        let l = layout("b");
        let one = |full: &str| super::one(&find(&img, &image, &l, full), full);
        assert_eq!(one("Tlas"), Ok(objs[0]));
        assert_eq!(one("Rendering/RT/Tlas"), Ok(objs[0]));
        assert_eq!(one("Other/Enabled"), Ok(objs[4]));
        let two = one("Enabled").unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            two.contains("2 matching config objects") && two.contains("give Group/Name"),
            "{two}"
        );
        assert!(one("Other/Twice").unwrap_err().contains("2 matching"));
        assert!(one("NoSuchVar").unwrap_err().contains("0 matching"));
        assert!(one("Rendering/RT/UseX").unwrap_err().contains("0 matching"));
        let broken = find(&img, &image, &l, "Broken");
        assert!(broken.vars.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(
            broken.rejected,
            [Rejected {
                address: objs[5],
                why: "type code 5".into()
            }]
        );
        let wrong_group = find(&img, &image, &l, "Rendering/RT/UseX");
        assert_eq!(
            wrong_group.rejected.len(),
            1,
            "the .text pointers are not even hits"
        );
        assert_eq!(wrong_group.rejected[0].why, "group Some(\"Rendering\")");
        // A value pointer that isn't the object's own live value.
        img.put(objs[1] + l.value, &0u64.to_le_bytes());
        let found = find(&img, &image, &l, "Budget");
        assert!(
            found.rejected[0]
                .why
                .starts_with("value pointer 0x0, not its live value"),
            "{found:?}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_lists_what_it_could_not_read() {
        let (mut img, objs) = sample();
        img.bad.push(BASE + 0x4000..BASE + 0x4001);
        let image = img.image();
        let found = find(&img, &image, &layout("b"), "Tlas");
        assert!(found.vars.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(
            (found.skipped.len(), found.skipped[0].base),
            (1, BASE + 0x4000)
        );
        let why = one(&found, "Tlas").unwrap_err();
        assert!(why.ends_with("(1 ranges couldn't be read)"), "{why}");
        img.bad.clear();
        assert_eq!(find(&img, &image, &layout("b"), "Tlas").vars, [objs[0]]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn reads_and_plans_sets_and_restores() {
        let (img, objs) = sample();
        let l = layout("b");
        let var = read(&img, &l, objs[0]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            var,
            Var {
                name: "Rendering/RT/Tlas".into(),
                address: objs[0],
                kind: Kind::Float,
                flags: 0x209,
                default: Value::Float(800.0),
                live: Value::Float(800.0),
            }
        );
        let json = serde_json::to_value(&var).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            (json["type"].clone(), json["live"].clone()),
            ("float".into(), 800.0.into())
        );
        let set = plan(&var, &l, Set::Value("400")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            (set.address, &set.old[..], &set.new[..]),
            (
                objs[0] + l.live,
                &800f32.to_le_bytes()[..],
                &400f32.to_le_bytes()[..]
            )
        );
        img.apply(&set);
        let var = read(&img, &l, objs[0]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(var.live, Value::Float(400.0));
        img.apply(&plan(&var, &l, Set::Default).unwrap());
        assert_eq!(read(&img, &l, objs[0]).unwrap().live, Value::Float(800.0));
        // An int, a bool by word, and the bool's neighbour bytes left alone.
        let budget = read(&img, &l, objs[1]).unwrap();
        img.apply(&plan(&budget, &l, Set::Value("256")).unwrap());
        assert_eq!(read(&img, &l, objs[1]).unwrap().live, Value::Int(256));
        let use_x = read(&img, &l, objs[2]).unwrap();
        let off = plan(&use_x, &l, Set::Value("FALSE")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!((off.old.clone(), off.new.clone()), (vec![1], vec![0]));
        img.apply(&off);
        assert_eq!(read(&img, &l, objs[2]).unwrap().live, Value::Bool(0));
        for (var, text, why) in [
            (&use_x, "2", "is not a bool"),
            (&budget, "1.5", "is not an int"),
            (&budget, "2147483648", "is not an int"),
            (&var, "1e39", "finite float"),
            (&var, "nan", "finite float"),
        ] {
            let e = plan(var, &l, Set::Value(text)).unwrap_err();
            assert!(e.contains(why) && e.contains(&var.name), "{text}: {e}");
        }
        assert!(
            read(&img, &l, objs[5])
                .unwrap_err()
                .to_string()
                .contains("type code 5")
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn values_parse_as_cvar_poke_s_do() {
        let int = |t| Value::parse(Kind::Int, t);
        for (text, n) in [
            ("0", 0),
            ("-7", -7),
            ("+7", 7),
            ("0x10", 16),
            ("-0X10", -16),
            ("0o17", 15),
            ("0b101", 5),
            ("000", 0),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(int(text), Ok(Value::Int(n)), "{text}");
        }
        for text in [

            "-",
            "010",
            "0x",
            "0x+5",
            "1_000",
            " 1",
            "1.0",

        ] {
            assert!(int(text).is_err(), "{text:?}");
        }
        assert_eq!(Value::parse(Kind::Float, "0.1"), Ok(Value::Float(0.1)));
        assert_eq!(Value::parse(Kind::Float, "-2"), Ok(Value::Float(-2.0)));
        assert_eq!(Value::parse(Kind::Bool, "True"), Ok(Value::Bool(1)));
        assert_eq!(Value::Float(800.0).to_string(), "800.0");
    }

    #[test]
    fn layout_rows_parse() {
        let header = HEADER.join("\t");

            (

                "not 0-255",
            ),
            (
                "b-2\t0x10\t0x8\t0x20\t0x28\t0x18\t0x1c\t7\t7\t9",

            ),
            ("b-2\t0x10", "2 columns"),
        ] {
            let e = from_layout_tsv(&format!("{text}{row}\n")).unwrap_err();
            assert!(e.msg.contains(why) && e.line == 4, "{row:?}: {e}");
            assert!(e.to_string().starts_with("cvar_layout.tsv line 4: "));
        }
    }
}
