`crates/quen-core/src/detect.rs`:

```rs
//! Where a game is installed, found rather than asked: Steam's library folders and app manifests, and GOG's
//! registry entries (the Windows layer reads those and passes them in). Every find is a candidate: with two (a 5.01
//! and a 4.04 copy, say), the agent asks the user which one. quen never picks.
//!
//! The tools quen uses beside the game are found the same way, where their installers put them ([`installed`]).
//!
//! GOG installs are untested: GOG's exe may differ from Steam's, and mods built against Steam's are reported
//! not to work there. Every GOG candidate says so, so the user hears it before picking one.

use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// An install found on this machine.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Install {
    pub dir: PathBuf,
    /// `steam` or `gog`.
    pub platform: &'static str,
    /// The store's own build or version: Steam's `buildid`, GOG's `ver`.
    pub build: Option<String>,
}

impl Install {
    pub fn status(&self) -> &'static str {
        status(self.platform)
    }
}

/// `tested` for Steam, the platform quen is verified on; `untested` for any other.
pub fn status(platform: &str) -> &'static str {
    if platform == "steam" {
        "tested"
    } else {
        "untested"
    }
}

/// A Valve KeyValues text node (`libraryfolders.vdf`, `appmanifest_*.acf`): a string, or a block of keyed nodes.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Vdf {
    Str(String),
    Block(Vec<(String, Vdf)>),
}

impl Vdf {
    /// The whole file as one block of its top-level pairs; `None` if it isn't KeyValues text.
    pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Option<Vdf> {
        let mut tokens = tokens(text)?.into_iter();
        let block = block(&mut tokens, false)?;
        Some(Vdf::Block(block))
    }

    /// The first value under `key` (case-insensitive, as Steam reads them).
    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&Vdf> {
        match self {
            Vdf::Block(pairs) => pairs
                .iter()
                .find(|(k, _)| k.eq_ignore_ascii_case(key))
                .map(|(_, v)| v),
            Vdf::Str(_) => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn str(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        match self {
            Vdf::Str(s) => Some(s),
            Vdf::Block(_) => None,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
enum Token {
    Open,
    Close,
    Str(String),
}

/// Quoted strings (with `\\`, `\"`, `\n`, `\t`), bare words, braces and `//` comments.
fn tokens(text: &str) -> Option<Vec<Token>> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut chars = text.chars().peekable();
    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
        match c {
            '{' => out.push(Token::Open),
            '}' => out.push(Token::Close),
            '"' => {
                let mut s = String::new();
                loop {
                    match chars.next()? {
                        '"' => break,
                        '\\' => s.push(match chars.next()? {
                            'n' => '\n',
                            't' => '\t',
                            other => other,
                        }),
                        other => s.push(other),
                    }
                }
                out.push(Token::Str(s));
            }
            '/' if chars.peek() == Some(&'/') => while chars.next_if(|&c| c != '\n').is_some() {},
            c if c.is_whitespace() => {}
            c => {
                let mut s = String::from(c);
                while let Some(c) = chars.next_if(|c| !c.is_whitespace() && !"{}\"".contains(*c)) {
                    s.push(c);
                }
                out.push(Token::Str(s));
            }
        }
    }
    Some(out)
}

/// Key-value pairs up to the closing brace (`inner`) or the end of the file.
fn block(tokens: &mut impl Iterator<Item = Token>, inner: bool) -> Option<Vec<(String, Vdf)>> {
    let mut pairs = Vec::new();
    loop {
        let key = match tokens.next() {
            Some(Token::Str(key)) => key,
            Some(Token::Close) if inner => return Some(pairs),
            None if !inner => return Some(pairs),
            _ => return None,
        };
        let value = match tokens.next()? {
            Token::Str(s) => Vdf::Str(s),
            Token::Open => Vdf::Block(block(tokens, true)?),
            Token::Close => return None,
        };
        pairs.push((key, value));
    }
}

/// Steam's libraries: each one `steamapps\libraryfolders.vdf` lists, in either format (a block with a `path` per
/// library, or before 2021 a path per number), then Steam's own folder, once each. The file's spelling comes first:
/// the registry's is lowercase with forward slashes.
pub fn steam_libraries(steam: &Path) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let mut libraries = Vec::new();
    let vdf = fs::read_to_string(steam.join("steamapps").join("libraryfolders.vdf"));
    let vdf = vdf.ok().and_then(|text| Vdf::parse(&text));
    let root = vdf.as_ref().and_then(|v| v.get("libraryfolders"));
    if let Some(Vdf::Block(entries)) = root {
        for (_, entry) in entries {
            let path = entry.str().or_else(|| entry.get("path")?.str());
            // Old files also hold keys like "TimeNextStatsReport": numbers, not paths.
            if let Some(path) = path.filter(|p| p.contains(['\\', '/'])) {
                libraries.push(PathBuf::from(path));
            }
        }
    }
    libraries.push(steam.to_owned());
    dedup(libraries, |p| p)
}

/// Where Steam installed `appid`: each library holding `steamapps\appmanifest_<appid>.acf`, as
/// `steamapps\common\<installdir>`, with the manifest's `buildid`.
pub fn steam(steam: &Path, appid: &str) -> Vec<Install> {
    let found = steam_libraries(steam).into_iter().filter_map(|library| {
        let apps = library.join("steamapps");
        let (dir, build) = manifest(&apps, appid)?;
        Some(Install {
            dir: apps.join("common").join(dir),
            platform: "steam",
            build,
        })
    });
    found.collect()
}

/// Steam's `buildid` for the install in `game_dir` (`<library>\steamapps\common\<installdir>`), from the app manifest
/// beside it, whose `installdir` must name that folder: a second sign of the game's build, independent of the exe's
/// sha256. It is the build of Steam's whole download, so it also changes with an update that leaves the exe
/// alone. `None` when no manifest there names the folder (a GOG install, a copied folder) or it has no `buildid`.
pub fn steam_buildid(game_dir: &Path, appid: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let common = game_dir.parent()?;
    if !common.file_name()?.eq_ignore_ascii_case("common") {
        return None;
    }
    let (dir, build) = manifest(common.parent()?, appid)?;
    game_dir
        .file_name()?
        .eq_ignore_ascii_case(dir)
        .then_some(build)?
}

/// The `installdir` and `buildid` of `appid`'s manifest in the `steamapps` folder `apps`; `None` if there is none, it
/// isn't KeyValues text, or it names no install folder.
fn manifest(apps: &Path, appid: &str) -> Option<(String, Option<String>)> {
    let text = fs::read_to_string(apps.join(format!("appmanifest_{appid}.acf"))).ok()?;
    let vdf = Vdf::parse(&text)?;
    let state = vdf.get("AppState")?;
    let field = |key| Some(state.get(key)?.str()?.to_owned());
    let dir = field("installdir").filter(|d| !d.is_empty())?;
    Some((dir, field("buildid")))
}

/// Every install: Steam's for `appid` (if Steam was found) and the GOG entries, kept when `is_game` says the folder
/// holds the game, once each (by path, case-insensitively).
pub fn installs(
    steam_dir: Option<&Path>,
    appid: &str,
    gog: Vec<Install>,
    is_game: impl Fn(&Path) -> bool,
) -> Vec<Install> {
    let mut all = steam_dir.map(|s| steam(s, appid)).unwrap_or_default();
    all.extend(gog);
    all.retain(|i| is_game(&i.dir));
    dedup(all, |i| &i.dir)
}

/// Every file at `pattern` under `root`, sorted: names joined by `\`, where a name holding `*` matches each name with
/// that prefix and suffix (case aside, as Windows compares them). Where an installer puts a tool, one folder per
/// version: each version is listed, so the user picks one (quen never does). Read-only.
pub fn installed(root: &Path, pattern: &str) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let mut found = vec![root.to_owned()];
    for part in pattern.split('\\').filter(|p| !p.is_empty()) {
        found = match part.to_lowercase().split_once('*') {
            None => found.into_iter().map(|dir| dir.join(part)).collect(),
            Some((prefix, suffix)) => {
                let fits = |name: &str| {
                    let name = name.to_lowercase();
                    name.len() >= prefix.len() + suffix.len()
                        && name.starts_with(prefix)
                        && name.ends_with(suffix)
                };
                let entries = found
                    .iter()
                    .flat_map(|dir| fs::read_dir(dir).into_iter().flatten());
                entries
                    .flatten()
                    .filter(|e| fits(&e.file_name().to_string_lossy()))
                    .map(|e| e.path())
                    .collect()
            }
        };
    }
    found.retain(|p| p.is_file());
    found.sort();
    found
}

/// The first of each path, compared case-insensitively and with either slash.
fn dedup<T>(items: Vec<T>, path: impl Fn(&T) -> &Path) -> Vec<T> {
    let key = |p: &Path| {
        let s = p.to_string_lossy().replace('/', "\\").to_lowercase();
        s.trim_end_matches('\\').to_owned()
    };
    let mut seen = Vec::new();
    items
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|item| {
            let k = key(path(item));
            let new = !seen.contains(&k);
            seen.push(k);
            new
        })
        .collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A temp folder for one test, gone afterwards (only what the test made in it).
    struct Temp(PathBuf);

    impl Temp {
        fn new(name: &str) -> Temp {
            let dir =
                std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("quen-detect-{name}-{}", std::process::id()));
            fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
            Temp(dir)
        }

        fn put(&self, rel: &str, text: &str) -> PathBuf {
            let path = self.0.join(rel);
            fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
            fs::write(&path, text).unwrap();
            path
        }
    }

    impl Drop for Temp {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0); // this test's own temp folder
        }
    }

    /// `path` as a vdf string: backslashes doubled.
    fn esc(path: &Path) -> String {
        path.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "\\\\")
    }

    fn manifest(appid: u32, dir: &str, build: &str) -> String {
        format!(
            "\"AppState\"\n{{\n\t\"appid\"\t\t\"{appid}\"\n\t\"name\"\t\t\"Synthetic\"\n\t\"installdir\"\t\t\"{dir}\"\n\
             \t\"buildid\"\t\t\"{build}\"\n\t\"InstalledDepots\"\n\t{{\n\t\t\"1\"\n\t\t{{\n\t\t\t\"manifest\"\t\t\"7\"\n\
             \t\t}}\n\t}}\n}}\n"
        )
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_keyvalues_with_escapes_comments_and_bare_words() {
        let v = Vdf::parse("// c\n\"a\" { \"b\\\\c\" \"d\\\"e\" bare word \"n\" { } }").unwrap();
        let a = v.get("A").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a.get("b\\c").and_then(Vdf::str), Some("d\"e"));
        assert_eq!(a.get("bare").and_then(Vdf::str), Some("word"));
        assert_eq!(a.get("n"), Some(&Vdf::Block(vec![])));
        for bad in ["\"a\" {", "\"a\" }", "\"a\"", "\"a\" \"b"] {
            assert_eq!(Vdf::parse(bad), None, "{bad}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn finds_the_game_in_every_steam_library_and_on_gog() {
        let t = Temp::new("steam");
        let steam = t.0.join("Steam");
        let lib2 = t.0.join("Library Two");
        let lib3 = t.0.join("lib3");
        // The current format, which lists the Steam folder itself too.
        let vdf = format!(
            "\"libraryfolders\"\n{{\n\t\"0\"\n\t{{\n\t\t\"path\"\t\t\"{}\"\n\t\t\"apps\"\n\t\t{{\n\t\t\t\"10\"\t\t\"1\"\n\
             \t\t}}\n\t}}\n\t\"1\"\n\t{{\n\t\t\"path\"\t\t\"{}\"\n\t}}\n\t\"2\"\n\t{{\n\t\t\"path\"\t\t\"{}\"\n\t}}\n}}\n",
            esc(&steam),
            esc(&lib2),
            esc(&lib3),
        );
        t.put("Steam/steamapps/libraryfolders.vdf", &vdf);
        assert_eq!(
            steam_libraries(&steam),
            vec![steam.clone(), lib2.clone(), lib3.clone()]
        );
        if cfg!(windows) {
            // As the registry spells it: the file's spelling wins.
            let registry = steam.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase().replace('\\', "/");
            let registry = PathBuf::from(registry);
            assert_eq!(steam_libraries(&registry)[0], steam);
        }
        t.put(
            "Steam/steamapps/appmanifest_10.acf",
            &manifest(10, "Game A", "111"),
        );
        t.put(
            "Library Two/steamapps/appmanifest_10.acf",
            &manifest(10, "Game B", "222"),
        );
        t.put(
            "Library Two/steamapps/appmanifest_20.acf",
            &manifest(20, "Other", "9"),
        );
        t.put("lib3/steamapps/appmanifest_10.acf", "not keyvalues {");
        let a = steam.join("steamapps").join("common").join("Game A");
        let b = lib2.join("steamapps").join("common").join("Game B");
        let gog = t.0.join("GOG Games").join("Game");
        t.put("Steam/steamapps/common/Game A/game.exe", "");
        t.put("Library Two/steamapps/common/Game B/game.exe", "");
        t.put("GOG Games/Game/game.exe", "");
        let gogs = vec![
            Install {
                dir: gog.clone(),
                platform: "gog",
                build: Some("4.04".into()),
            },
            // The same folder twice in the registry, and one that holds no game.
            Install {
                dir: PathBuf::from(gog.to_string_lossy().to_uppercase()),
                platform: "gog",
                build: None,
            },
            Install {
                dir: t.0.join("empty"),
                platform: "gog",
                build: None,
            },
        ];
        let found = installs(Some(&steam), "10", gogs, |d| d.join("game.exe").is_file());
        let want = [
            (a, "steam", Some("111")),
            (b, "steam", Some("222")),
            (gog, "gog", Some("4.04")),
        ];
        let got: Vec<_> = found
            .iter()
            .map(|i| (i.dir.clone(), i.platform, i.build.as_deref()))
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(got, want);
        let status: Vec<&str> = found.iter().map(Install::status).collect();
        assert_eq!(status, ["tested", "tested", "untested"], "GOG is untested");
        // Each install's buildid from the manifest beside it, also without Steam's library list.
        assert_eq!(steam_buildid(&found[0].dir, "10").as_deref(), Some("111"));
        assert_eq!(steam_buildid(&found[1].dir, "10").as_deref(), Some("222"));
        assert_eq!(
            steam_buildid(&found[2].dir, "10"),
            None,
            "GOG has no Steam buildid"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            steam_buildid(&found[1].dir, "20"),
            None,
            "app 20's manifest names Other"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            steam_buildid(&lib3.join("steamapps").join("common").join("Game"), "10"),
            None
        );
        assert!(installs(Some(&steam), "30", vec![], |_| true).is_empty());
        assert!(installs(None, "10", vec![], |_| true).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_buildid_is_only_the_manifest_s_that_names_the_folder() {
        let t = Temp::new("buildid");
        let apps = t.0.join("lib").join("steamapps");
        t.put(
            "lib/steamapps/appmanifest_10.acf",
            &manifest(10, "Game A", "333"),
        );
        let common = apps.join("common");
        assert_eq!(
            steam_buildid(&common.join("Game A"), "10").as_deref(),
            Some("333")
        );
        // The folder's name, compared as Steam does: case aside.
        assert_eq!(
            steam_buildid(&common.join("GAME a"), "10").as_deref(),
            Some("333")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            steam_buildid(&common.join("Game B"), "10"),
            None,
            "another folder"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            steam_buildid(&apps.join("other").join("Game A"), "10"),
            None,
            "not in common"
        );
        assert_eq!(steam_buildid(Path::new("Game A"), "10"), None);
        t.put(
            "lib/steamapps/appmanifest_20.acf",
            "\"AppState\"\n{\n\t\"installdir\"\t\t\"Game C\"\n}\n",
        );
        assert_eq!(
            steam_buildid(&common.join("Game C"), "20"),
            None,
            "no buildid"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_installed_version_is_listed_and_nothing_else() {
        let t = Temp::new("installed");
        let nsys = r"NVIDIA Corporation\Nsight Systems*\target-windows-x64\nsys.exe";
        let old = t.put(
            "NVIDIA Corporation/Nsight Systems 2025.1.1/target-windows-x64/nsys.exe",
            "",
        );
        // A `*` name matches case aside, on any file system.
        let new = t.put(
            "NVIDIA Corporation/nsight systems 2025.3.2/target-windows-x64/nsys.exe",
            "",
        );
        // Another tool's folder, a version without the exe, and a folder where the exe should be.
        t.put(
            "NVIDIA Corporation/Nsight Graphics 2025.2/host/ngfx.exe",
            "",
        );
        t.put("NVIDIA Corporation/Nsight Systems 2024.1/readme.txt", "");
        let dir = "NVIDIA Corporation/Nsight Systems 9/target-windows-x64/nsys.exe";
        fs::create_dir_all(t.0.join(dir)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(installed(&t.0, nsys), vec![old, new]);
        let pm = t.put("Intel/PresentMon/App/PresentMon-2.4.1-x64.exe", "");
        t.put("Intel/PresentMon/App/PresentMonService.exe", "");
        let pattern = r"Intel\PresentMon\App\PresentMon-*.exe";
        assert_eq!(installed(&t.0, pattern), vec![pm]);
        assert!(installed(&t.0.join("missing"), nsys).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn reads_the_old_libraryfolders_format_and_no_file_at_all() {
        let t = Temp::new("old");
        let steam = t.0.join("Steam");
        assert_eq!(steam_libraries(&steam), vec![steam.clone()]);
        let old = format!(
            "\"LibraryFolders\"\n{{\n\t\"TimeNextStatsReport\"\t\t\"1234\"\n\t\"ContentStatsID\"\t\t\"-5\"\n\
             \t\"1\"\t\t\"{}\"\n}}\n",
            esc(&t.0.join("D")),
        );
        t.put("Steam/steamapps/libraryfolders.vdf", &old);
        assert_eq!(steam_libraries(&steam), vec![t.0.join("D"), steam.clone()]);
    }
}

```

`crates/quen-core/src/disk.rs`:

```rs
//! The capture root on disk, and quen's other leftovers under the data root ([`leftovers`]): every file there, which
//! boot it belongs to, what its ledger row says, the usage by boot, kind and age, and what a cleanup takes and where
//! to. It only reads and plans: quen's capture_clean (crates/quen disk.rs) removes the files, to the Recycle Bin, or
//! through Windows' own question before a permanent delete.

use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::SystemTime;

use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::{Value, json};

use crate::ledger::CaptureRow;

/// A file over this is listed on its own (profiler outputs: a RenderDoc capture is 3-5 GB).
pub const LARGE: u64 = 1_000_000_000;
const GB: f64 = 1e9;

/// A file under the capture root, or one of quen's leftovers under the data root.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct File {
    /// Relative to the capture root (a leftover's: to the data root), `/` separators.
    pub rel: String,
    pub bytes: u64,
    pub age_days: f64,
    /// From its folder: a boot's id, or its session (see `Ledger::boot_folders`), else its ledger row's.
    pub boot: Option<i64>,
    /// The lowercase extension, as `captures.kind` has it (`file` without one); a leftover's kind ([`LEFTOVERS`]).
    pub kind: String,
    /// Its ledger row, if it has one.
    pub capture: Option<i64>,
    /// Kept by a cleanup unless named by its capture id (`CaptureRow::cited`).
    pub cited: bool,
    /// One of quen's leftovers under the data root ([`leftovers`]), not a capture-root file.
    pub leftover: bool,
}

/// The kinds of quen's leftovers under the data root ([`leftovers`]).
pub const LEFTOVERS: [&str; 6] = [
    "session_logs",
    "settings_backups",
    "query_spills",
    "ledger_backups",
    "packages",
    "to_delete",
];

/// GB with two decimals.
pub fn gb(bytes: u64) -> f64 {
    (bytes as f64 / GB * 100.0).round() / 100.0
}

/// Every file under `dir`, recursively: its path and size. A folder that can't be read is skipped.
fn walk(dir: &Path, out: &mut Vec<(PathBuf, fs::Metadata)>) {
    for entry in fs::read_dir(dir).into_iter().flatten().flatten() {
        match entry.metadata() {
            Ok(m) if m.is_dir() => walk(&entry.path(), out),
            Ok(m) => out.push((entry.path(), m)),
            Err(_) => {}
        }
    }
}

/// `path` under `root`, its names joined with `/`. Split by the platform's own separators: on Linux a `\` is part of
/// a name.
fn relative(root: &Path, path: &Path) -> Option<String> {
    let names: Vec<_> = path
        .strip_prefix(root)
        .ok()?
        .iter()
        .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy())
        .collect();
    Some(names.join("/"))
}

/// Every folder under `root`, relative with `/` separators; a link isn't followed.
pub fn folders(root: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut todo = vec![root.to_path_buf()];
    while let Some(dir) = todo.pop() {
        for entry in fs::read_dir(&dir).into_iter().flatten().flatten() {
            if entry.file_type().is_ok_and(|t| t.is_dir()) {
                let path = entry.path();
                out.extend(relative(root, &path));
                todo.push(path);
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

/// The bytes under `dir`, recursively (0 when it doesn't exist).
pub fn total(dir: &Path) -> u64 {
    let mut files = Vec::new();
    walk(dir, &mut files);
    files.iter().map(|(_, m)| m.len()).sum()
}

/// `path` lowercase with `/` separators, for comparing ledger paths with files.
fn norm(path: &str) -> String {
    path.replace('\\', "/").to_lowercase()
}

/// Every file under `root` at `now`, joined to the ledger: `rows` (its captures on disk) and `folders` (the folder
/// names that belong to a boot, lowercase).
pub fn scan(
    root: &Path,
    now: SystemTime,
    rows: &[CaptureRow],
    folders: &[(String, i64)],
) -> Vec<File> {
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    walk(root, &mut found);
    let mut files: Vec<File> = found
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(|(path, meta)| {
            let rel = relative(root, &path)?;
            let row = rows.iter().find(|r| norm(&r.path) == rel.to_lowercase());
            let first = rel.split('/').next().unwrap_or_default().to_lowercase();
            let folder = folders.iter().find(|(f, _)| *f == first).map(|(_, b)| *b);
            let kind = Path::new(&rel)
                .extension()
                .map_or("file".into(), |x| x.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase());
            Some(File {
                boot: folder.or(row.and_then(|r| r.boot_id)),
                kind,
                capture: row.map(|r| r.id),
                cited: row.is_some_and(|r| r.cited),
                ..file(rel, &meta, now)
            })
        })
        .collect();
    files.sort_by(|a, b| a.rel.cmp(&b.rel));
    files
}

/// `rel`, with its size and its age at `now`: no boot, kind or row yet.
fn file(rel: String, meta: &fs::Metadata, now: SystemTime) -> File {
    let age = meta
        .modified()
        .ok()
        .and_then(|t| now.duration_since(t).ok());
    File {
        rel,
        bytes: meta.len(),
        age_days: age.map_or(0.0, |a| a.as_secs_f64() / 86_400.0),
        boot: None,
        kind: String::new(),
        capture: None,
        cited: false,
        leftover: false,
    }
}

/// quen's leftovers under the data root `data` at `now`, beside the capture root, by kind ([`LEFTOVERS`]): each
/// session's log folder (`logs\<secs>-<session>`: `session_logs`, and the settings backups in its `backup` folder:
/// `settings_backups`), ledger_query's spill files (`logs\queries`: `query_spills`), the ledger's backups from before
/// each migration (`state\backups`: `ledger_backups`), the files in `packages` but those `keep` names, lowercase (the
/// installed package's zip: `packages`), and what earlier cleanups moved to `_to_delete` (`to_delete`). Nothing else
/// under the data root is one: not its config, ledger or journal, `logs\serve.log`, nor the save backups. A session's
/// files carry its boot, from `folders` (as [`scan`] takes them).
pub fn leftovers(
    data: &Path,
    now: SystemTime,
    folders: &[(String, i64)],
    keep: &[String],
) -> Vec<File> {
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    for area in [
        data.join("logs"),
        data.join("state").join("backups"),
        data.join("packages"),
        data.join("_to_delete"),
    ] {
        walk(&area, &mut found);
    }
    let boot = |session: &str| {
        let id = session.rsplit_once('-').map(|(_, id)| id.to_lowercase())?;
        folders.iter().find(|(f, _)| *f == id).map(|(_, b)| *b)
    };
    let mut files: Vec<File> = found
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(|(path, meta)| {
            let rel = relative(data, &path)?;
            let parts: Vec<&str> = rel.split('/').collect();
            let (kind, boot) = match parts[..] {
                ["logs", "queries", ..] => ("query_spills", None),
                ["logs", session, "backup", _, ..] => ("settings_backups", boot(session)),
                ["logs", session, _, ..] => ("session_logs", boot(session)),
                ["state", "backups", ..] => ("ledger_backups", None),
                ["packages", name] if !keep.contains(&name.to_lowercase()) => ("packages", None),
                ["_to_delete", _, ..] => ("to_delete", None),
                _ => return None,
            };
            Some(File {
                boot,
                kind: kind.into(),
                leftover: true,
                ..file(rel, &meta, now)
            })
        })
        .collect();
    files.sort_by(|a, b| a.rel.cmp(&b.rel));
    files
}

/// What [`missing`] found.
#[derive(Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Missing {
    /// The rows whose file is gone: those of quen's boots first, then of imported boots, then of no boot, each sorted.
    pub ids: Vec<i64>,
    /// How many of `ids` are of quen's boots, of imported boots and of no boot.
    pub by: [usize; 3],
    /// Rows whose file is under the harness's `cap` folder instead: not missing.
    pub in_harness: usize,
    /// Rows of imported boots and of no boot left out of `ids`: no harness folder to look in.
    pub unresolved: usize,
}

/// The rows (captures the ledger says are on disk) that no file of `files` matches: removed by hand, or kept under
/// another capture root (feature tests 2b). The harness import records its files by their path in its `cap` folder,
/// and without a boot but for its boot logs (finding 36), so each is looked for under `harness` (that folder) first.
/// Without it, or when none of them is there (not the folder they were imported from), the rows of imported boots and
/// of no boot are left out as `unresolved`.
pub fn missing(rows: &[CaptureRow], files: &[File], harness: Option<&Path>) -> Missing {
    let found: std::collections::HashSet<i64> = files.iter().filter_map(|f| f.capture).collect();
    let there =
        |r: &CaptureRow| harness.is_some_and(|h| h.join(r.path.replace('\\', "/")).is_file());
    let gone: Vec<(&CaptureRow, bool)> = rows
        .iter()
        .filter(|r| !found.contains(&r.id))
        .map(|r| (r, there(r)))
        .collect();
    let in_harness = gone.iter().filter(|(_, there)| *there).count();
    let mut out = Missing {
        in_harness,
        ..Missing::default()
    };
    let mut ids: Vec<(usize, i64)> = Vec::new();
    for (r, there) in gone {
        let origin = if r.boot_id.is_none() {
            2
        } else {
            usize::from(r.imported)
        };
        if in_harness == 0 && origin > 0 {
            out.unresolved += 1;
        } else if !there {
            ids.push((origin, r.id));
            out.by[origin] += 1;
        }
    }
    ids.sort_unstable();
    out.ids = ids.into_iter().map(|(_, id)| id).collect();
    out
}

/// The usage: totals by boot (largest first), by kind and by age, and every file over [`LARGE`].
pub fn usage(files: &[File]) -> Value {
    let sum = |f: &dyn Fn(&File) -> bool| {
        let picked: Vec<&File> = files.iter().filter(|x| f(x)).collect();
        let bytes: u64 = picked.iter().map(|x| x.bytes).sum();
        (picked.len(), bytes)
    };
    let mut boots: Vec<Option<i64>> = files.iter().map(|f| f.boot).collect();
    boots.sort();
    boots.dedup();
    let mut by_boot: Vec<(u64, Value)> = boots
        .into_iter()
        .map(|boot| {
            let (n, bytes) = sum(&|f| f.boot == boot);
            let newest = files
                .iter()
                .filter(|f| f.boot == boot)
                .map(|f| f.age_days)
                .fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min);
            let days = (newest * 10.0).round() / 10.0;
            (
                bytes,
                json!({"boot": boot, "files": n, "gb": gb(bytes), "newest_age_days": days}),
            )
        })
        .collect();
    by_boot.sort_by(|a, b| b.0.cmp(&a.0));
    let mut kinds: Vec<&str> = files.iter().map(|f| f.kind.as_str()).collect();
    kinds.sort();
    kinds.dedup();
    let by_kind: Vec<Value> = kinds
        .into_iter()
        .map(|kind| {
            let (n, bytes) = sum(&|f| f.kind == kind);
            json!({"kind": kind, "files": n, "gb": gb(bytes)})
        })
        .collect();
    let ages = [
        ("under 1 day", 0.0, 1.0),
        ("1 to 7 days", 1.0, 7.0),
        ("7 to 30 days", 7.0, 30.0),
        ("over 30 days", 30.0, f64::INFINITY),
    ];
    let by_age: Vec<Value> = ages
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(age, from, to)| {
            let (n, bytes) = sum(&|f| f.age_days >= from && f.age_days < to);
            json!({"age": age, "files": n, "gb": gb(bytes)})
        })
        .collect();
    let (n, bytes) = sum(&|_| true);
    json!({
        "files": n,
        "gb": gb(bytes),
        "by_boot": by_boot.into_iter().map(|(_, v)| v).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        "by_kind": by_kind,
        "by_age": by_age,
        "large": large(files.iter()),
    })
}

/// The files over [`LARGE`].
pub fn large<'a>(files: impl Iterator<Item = &'a File>) -> Vec<Value> {
    files
        .filter(|f| f.bytes > LARGE)
        .map(|f| json!({"path": f.rel, "gb": gb(f.bytes), "boot": f.boot, "kind": f.kind}))
        .collect()
}

/// Which files a cleanup takes: those every given filter matches (boot ids, older than so many days, kinds), and
/// those named by capture id. A cited file is kept unless named. `missing`: the rows whose file is gone ([`missing`])
/// are marked removed too, to `missing`; no file moves for them.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct Select {
    pub boots: Option<Vec<i64>>,
    pub older_than_days: Option<f64>,
    pub kinds: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub capture_ids: Vec<i64>,
    pub missing: bool,
}

impl Select {
    /// From a tool's arguments `boots`, `older_than_days`, `kinds`, `capture_ids` and `missing`; the caller checks for
    /// others.
    pub fn parse(args: &Value) -> Result<Select, String> {
        let ints = |key: &str| -> Result<Option<Vec<i64>>, String> {
            let Some(v) = args.get(key) else {
                return Ok(None);
            };
            let ids = v
                .as_array()
                .and_then(|a| a.iter().map(Value::as_i64).collect());
            ids.map(Some)
                .ok_or(format!("{key} must be an array of whole numbers"))
        };
        let kinds =
            match args.get("kinds") {
                None => None,
                Some(v) => {
                    let kinds: Option<Vec<String>> = v.as_array().and_then(|a| {
                        a.iter()
                            .map(|k| Some(k.as_str()?.trim_start_matches('.').to_lowercase()))
                            .collect()
                    });
                    Some(kinds.ok_or(
                        "kinds must be an array of file extensions, e.g. [\"rdc\", \"png\"]",
                    )?)
                }
            };
        let older_than_days = match args.get("older_than_days") {
            None => None,
            Some(v) => Some(
                v.as_f64()
                    .filter(|d| *d >= 0.0)
                    .ok_or("older_than_days must be a number from 0")?,
            ),
        };
        let missing = match args.get("missing") {
            None => false,
            Some(v) => v.as_bool().ok_or("missing must be true or false")?,
        };
        Ok(Select {
            boots: ints("boots")?,
            older_than_days,
            kinds,
            capture_ids: ints("capture_ids")?.unwrap_or_default(),
            missing,
        })
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        *self == Select::default()
    }

    /// Whether every given filter matches `f` (never without one).
    fn matches(&self, f: &File) -> bool {
        let any = self.boots.is_some() || self.older_than_days.is_some() || self.kinds.is_some();
        any && self
            .boots
            .as_ref()
            .is_none_or(|b| f.boot.is_some_and(|x| b.contains(&x)))
            && self.older_than_days.is_none_or(|d| f.age_days > d)
            && self.kinds.as_ref().is_none_or(|k| k.contains(&f.kind))
    }
}

/// Where a cleanup sends a file.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum To {
    RecycleBin,
    /// What the Recycle Bin can't take whole: Windows' own dialog asks the user whether to delete it permanently, and
    /// no keeps it in place.
    AskDelete,
}

/// What a cleanup takes, and the cited files it keeps.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct Plan {
    pub take: Vec<(File, To)>,
    pub kept: Vec<File>,
}

/// The cleanup `select` asks for. `recycle_max`: the largest file the Recycle Bin takes whole, None when it takes
/// nothing (it would delete instead); for bigger files Windows asks the user ([`To::AskDelete`]).
pub fn plan(files: &[File], select: &Select, recycle_max: Option<u64>) -> Plan {
    let mut out = Plan::default();
    for f in files {
        let named = f.capture.is_some_and(|id| select.capture_ids.contains(&id));
        if !named && !select.matches(f) {
            continue;
        }
        if f.cited && !named {
            out.kept.push(f.clone());
            continue;
        }
        let to = match recycle_max {
            Some(max) if f.bytes <= max => To::RecycleBin,
            _ => To::AskDelete,
        };
        out.take.push((f.clone(), to));
    }
    out
}

/// The folders of `dirs` (folders under the root of `files`, [`folders`]) that a cleanup taking `taken` (their `rel`)
/// empties, deepest first: each that holds no file but taken ones, at any depth, and held a taken file or lies in a
/// selected boot's folder (`boots`: their names, lowercase), with its subfolders (feature tests 2b, 2c).
pub fn emptied(dirs: &[String], files: &[File], taken: &[&str], boots: &[&str]) -> Vec<String> {
    let beneath = |dir: &str, rel: &str| {
        rel.strip_prefix(dir)
            .is_some_and(|rest| rest.starts_with('/'))
    };
    let goes = |dir: &str| {
        let first = dir.split('/').next().unwrap_or_default().to_lowercase();
        let held = taken.iter().any(|t| beneath(dir, t)) || boots.contains(&first.as_str());
        let left = files
            .iter()
            .any(|f| beneath(dir, &f.rel) && !taken.contains(&f.rel.as_str()));
        held && !left
    };
    let mut out: Vec<String> = dirs
        .iter()
        .filter(|d| {
            std::iter::successors(Some(d.as_str()), |a| a.rsplit_once('/').map(|(up, _)| up))
                .any(goes)
        })
        .cloned()
        .collect();
    out.sort_by(|a, b| b.len().cmp(&a.len()).then(a.cmp(b)));
    out
}

impl Plan {
    /// Its summary: files and GB by destination, and the cited files kept.
    pub fn summary(&self) -> Value {
        let to = |dest: To| {
            let picked: Vec<&File> = self
                .take
                .iter()
                .filter(|(_, t)| *t == dest)
                .map(|(f, _)| f)
                .collect();
            json!({"files": picked.len(), "gb": gb(picked.iter().map(|f| f.bytes).sum())})
        };
        let kept: Vec<Value> = self
            .kept
            .iter()
            .map(|f| json!({"path": f.rel, "capture_id": f.capture}))
            .collect();
        json!({
            "files": self.take.len(),
            "gb": gb(self.take.iter().map(|(f, _)| f.bytes).sum()),
            "recycle_bin": to(To::RecycleBin),
            "ask_delete": to(To::AskDelete),
            "kept_cited": kept,
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use std::time::Duration;

    use super::*;

    /// A capture root of this test's own: a profiler boot's folder, a session folder, a file of no boot.
    struct Temp(PathBuf);

    impl Temp {
        fn new(name: &str) -> Temp {
            let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("quen-disk-{name}-{}", std::process::id()));
            let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir); // this test's own temp folder, from an earlier run
            Temp(dir)
        }

        fn put(&self, rel: &str, bytes: usize) {
            let path = self.0.join(rel);
            fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
            fs::write(path, vec![7u8; bytes]).unwrap();
        }
    }

    impl Drop for Temp {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0); // this test's own temp folder
        }
    }

    fn row(id: i64, path: &str, boot: Option<i64>, cited: bool) -> CaptureRow {
        CaptureRow {
            id,
            path: path.into(),
            boot_id: boot,
            imported: false,
            cited,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn files_join_their_boot_and_row_and_sum_by_boot_kind_and_age() {
        let t = Temp::new("scan");
        t.put("132/l1.rdc", 500);
        t.put("ab12cd/shot.png", 30);
        t.put("ab12cd/run.csv", 20);
        t.put("loose.txt", 5);
        let rows = [
            row(1, r"132\L1.rdc", Some(132), false),
            row(2, "ab12cd/shot.png", Some(130), true),
        ];
        let folders = [("132".to_owned(), 132), ("ab12cd".to_owned(), 130)];
        let now = SystemTime::now() + Duration::from_secs(10 * 86_400);
        let files = scan(&t.0, now, &rows, &folders);
        let got: Vec<String> = files
            .iter()
            .map(|f| {
                format!(
                    "{} {:?} {} {:?} {}",
                    f.rel, f.boot, f.kind, f.capture, f.cited
                )
            })
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(
            got,
            [
                "132/l1.rdc Some(132) rdc Some(1) false",
                "ab12cd/run.csv Some(130) csv None false",
                "ab12cd/shot.png Some(130) png Some(2) true",
                "loose.txt None txt None false",
            ]
        );
        assert!(
            files.iter().all(|f| (f.age_days - 10.0).abs() < 0.1),
            "{files:?}"
        );
        // Feature tests 2b: rows whose file is gone are counted.
        let gone = [
            rows[0].clone(),
            row(9, "old/x.png", Some(9), false),
            row(5, "y.png", None, true),
        ];
        let want = |ids: Vec<i64>, by, in_harness, unresolved| Missing {
            ids,
            by,
            in_harness,
            unresolved,
        };
        // Without a harness folder, only quen's boots' rows count as missing.
        assert_eq!(missing(&gone, &files, None), want(vec![9], [1, 0, 0], 0, 1));
        // The harness's cap folder holds two of the imported rows' files: those are not missing, the rest are.
        let h = Temp::new("harness");
        h.put("cap/boot_a/shot.png", 1);
        h.put(r"cap/z.png", 1);
        let imported = |id, path: &str| CaptureRow {
            imported: true,
            ..row(id, path, Some(3), false)
        };
        let harness = [
            imported(7, "z.png"),
            imported(8, r"boot_a\shot.png"),
            imported(6, "gone.png"),
            row(5, "y.png", None, true),
            row(9, "old/x.png", Some(9), false),
        ];
        let cap = h.0.join("cap");
        assert_eq!(
            missing(&harness, &files, Some(&cap)),
            want(vec![9, 6, 5], [1, 1, 1], 2, 0)
        );
        // A folder that holds none of them is not theirs: as without one.
        assert_eq!(
            missing(&harness, &files, Some(&h.0)),
            want(vec![9], [1, 0, 0], 0, 4)
        );
        assert_eq!(total(&t.0), 555);
        let mut dirs = super::folders(&t.0);
        dirs.sort();
        assert_eq!(dirs, ["132", "ab12cd"]);
        let u = usage(&files);
        assert_eq!(u["files"], 4);
        assert_eq!(u["by_boot"][0]["boot"], 132, "largest first: {u}");
        assert_eq!(u["by_boot"][1]["files"], 2);
        assert_eq!(u["by_age"][2]["files"], 4, "7 to 30 days: {u}");
        assert_eq!(u["large"], json!([]));
        // On Linux a `\` is part of a name, not a separator (CI, 2026-10-18).
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            t.put(r"x\y.png", 1);
            let files = scan(&t.0, now, &[], &[]);
            assert!(files.iter().any(|f| f.rel == r"x\y.png"), "{files:?}");
            assert!(!super::folders(&t.0).iter().any(|d| d == "x"));
        }
    }

    /// The owner's rule (2026-10-19): one cleanup covers every leftover of quen's under the data root, and only those.

    }

    #[test]
    fn a_cleanup_takes_what_every_filter_matches_keeps_the_cited_and_routes_by_size() {
        let file = |rel: &str, bytes, age_days, boot, kind: &str, capture, cited| File {
            rel: rel.into(),
            bytes,
            age_days,
            boot,
            kind: kind.into(),
            capture,
            cited,
            leftover: false,
        };
        let files = [
            file(
                "132/l1.rdc",
                5_000_000_000,
                2.0,
                Some(132),
                "rdc",
                Some(1),
                false,
            ),
            file("s1/kf0.png", 9, 40.0, Some(130), "png", Some(2), true),
            file("s1/f1.png", 9, 40.0, Some(130), "png", Some(3), false),
            file("s1/ab.csv", 9, 40.0, Some(130), "csv", None, false),
            file("old/x.png", 9, 40.0, None, "png", None, false),
        ];
        let take = |s: &Select, max| -> Vec<(String, To)> {
            plan(&files, s, max)
                .take
                .into_iter()
                .map(|(f, to)| (f.rel, to))
                .collect()
        };
        let pngs = Select::parse(&json!({"kinds": [".PNG"], "older_than_days": 30})).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            take(&pngs, Some(4_000_000_000)),
            [
                ("s1/f1.png".into(), To::RecycleBin),
                ("old/x.png".into(), To::RecycleBin)
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            plan(&files, &pngs, None).kept[0].rel,
            "s1/kf0.png",
            "cited: kept"
        );
        // Named by id, a cited file goes too; boot 130's files only; an rdc too big for the bin, or no bin.
        let named = Select::parse(&json!({"boots": [130], "capture_ids": [2]})).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(take(&named, Some(1)).len(), 3);
        assert!(plan(&files, &named, Some(1)).kept.is_empty());
        let rdc = Select::parse(&json!({"boots": [132]})).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            take(&rdc, Some(4_000_000_000)),
            [("132/l1.rdc".into(), To::AskDelete)]
        );
        let all = Select::parse(&json!({"older_than_days": 0})).unwrap();
        assert!(take(&all, None).iter().all(|(_, to)| *to == To::AskDelete));
        let summary = plan(&files, &all, None).summary();
        assert_eq!(
            (
                summary["files"].as_u64(),
                summary["ask_delete"]["files"].as_u64()
            ),
            (Some(4), Some(4))
        );
        // Nothing without a filter or a name; missing alone takes no file; bad shapes refused.
        assert!(Select::parse(&json!({})).unwrap().is_empty());
        assert!(take(&Select::default(), Some(1)).is_empty());
        let missing = Select::parse(&json!({"missing": true})).unwrap();
        assert!(missing.missing && !missing.is_empty() && take(&missing, Some(1)).is_empty());
        for bad in [
            json!({"boots": ["x"]}),
            json!({"older_than_days": -1}),
            json!({"kinds": "png"}),
            json!({"missing": 1}),
        ] {
            assert!(Select::parse(&bad).is_err(), "{bad}");
        }
    }

    /// Feature tests 2c: the folders a cleanup empties, which capture_usage shows before and capture_clean removes.
    #[test]
    fn a_cleanup_empties_the_folders_it_leaves_with_no_file() {
        let file = |rel: &str| File {
            rel: rel.into(),
            bytes: 1,
            age_days: 0.0,
            boot: None,
            kind: "png".into(),
            capture: None,
            cited: false,
            leftover: false,
        };
        let files = [
            file("1/a/x.png"),
            file("1/b.png"),
            file("s1/kf0.png"),
            file("other/y.png"),
        ];
        let dirs = [
            "1", "1/a", "1/a/deep", "1/c", "s1", "s1/l3c", "other", "empty",
        ]
        .map(String::from);
        let taking =
            |n: usize| -> Vec<&str> { files[..n].iter().map(|f| f.rel.as_str()).collect() };
        // 1/a held the taken file: it goes with its empty subfolder; 1 still holds b.png; no unrelated folder goes.
        assert_eq!(emptied(&dirs, &files, &taking(1), &[]), ["1/a/deep", "1/a"]);
        // A selected boot's folder keeps kf0.png; its empty l3c goes.
        assert_eq!(
            emptied(&dirs, &files, &taking(1), &["s1"]),
            ["1/a/deep", "s1/l3c", "1/a"]
        );
        // Both of 1's files taken: 1 goes, with every folder in it.
        assert_eq!(
            emptied(&dirs, &files, &taking(2), &[]),
            ["1/a/deep", "1/a", "1/c", "1"]
        );
    }
}
```

`crates/quen-core/src/drift.rs`:

```rs
//! measure_ab's drift guard (finding 73): in boot 181 the world changed by itself about 1.5 min after photo mode opened
//! (48 to 60 fps), 4 s after a toggle, and an A/B straddling it gave a meaningless verdict. Two checks: window 1's
//! frame time against its state's later windows, and a fingerprint of the world, read before and after each window
//! (never inside one), between the reads of one state.

use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::Value;

use crate::trace::{Body, vec3};

/// The radius of the fingerprint's actor count, metres (world_actors' default).
pub const RADIUS_M: f32 = 30.0;
/// How far window 1 may sit from its state's later windows, in times the later windows' drift, before
/// [`first_window`] says so.
// ponytail: a guess (boot 181's step was far beyond it); tune once live A/Bs show how far a settled window 1 strays.
pub const FIRST_FACTOR: f64 = 3.0;
/// What counts as a change between two fingerprints of one state: the player or the camera moved this far (metres) or
/// turned this far (degrees); the actors within [`RADIUS_M`] changed by 3 or more and by over half the larger count.
// ponytail: guesses, wide on purpose (boot 176's crowd within 8 m went 12, 14, 7 in one state); tune on live runs.
const MOVED_M: f64 = 1.0;
const TURNED_DEG: f64 = 10.0;

/// The world as cheap reads show it: world.get's player and weather, cam.get's pose and world.actors' count.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct Fingerprint {
    pub player_pos: [f64; 3],
    /// Degrees.
    pub player_heading: f64,
    pub camera_pos: [f64; 3],
    /// [pitch, yaw, roll], degrees.
    pub camera_rot: [f64; 3],
    /// The alive actors within [`RADIUS_M`] of the player.
    pub actors: u64,
    pub weather: String,
}

impl Fingerprint {
    /// From the replies' data of world.get, cam.get and world.actors.
    pub fn new(world: &Value, camera: &Value, actors: &Value) -> Result<Fingerprint, String> {
        let player = Body::player(world)?;
        Ok(Fingerprint {
            player_pos: player.pos,
            player_heading: player.heading,
            camera_pos: vec3(&camera["pos"]).ok_or("cam.get without pos")?,
            camera_rot: vec3(&camera["rot"]).ok_or("cam.get without rot")?,
            actors: actors["found"]
                .as_u64()
                .ok_or("world.actors without found")?,
            weather: world["weather"]
                .as_str()
                .ok_or("world.get without weather")?
                .into(),
        })
    }

    /// How this differs from `from`, beyond the tolerances; empty when it doesn't.
    pub fn changes(&self, from: &Fingerprint) -> Vec<String> {
        let moved =
            |a: [f64; 3], b: [f64; 3]| (0..3).map(|i| (a[i] - b[i]).powi(2)).sum::<f64>().sqrt();
        let turned = |a: f64, b: f64| {
            let d = (a - b).rem_euclid(360.0);
            d.min(360.0 - d)
        };
        let camera_turned = (0..3)
            .map(|i| turned(self.camera_rot[i], from.camera_rot[i]))
            .fold(0.0, f64::max);
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for (what, by, unit, max) in [
            (
                "the player moved",
                moved(self.player_pos, from.player_pos),
                "m",
                MOVED_M,
            ),
            (
                "the player turned",
                turned(self.player_heading, from.player_heading),
                "deg",
                TURNED_DEG,
            ),
            (
                "the camera moved",
                moved(self.camera_pos, from.camera_pos),
                "m",
                MOVED_M,
            ),
            ("the camera turned", camera_turned, "deg", TURNED_DEG),
        ] {
            if by > max {
                out.push(format!("{what} {by:.2} {unit}"));
            }
        }
        let (a, b) = (from.actors, self.actors);
        let d = a.abs_diff(b);
        if d >= 3 && 2 * d > a.max(b) {
            out.push(format!(
                "the actors within {RADIUS_M} m went from {a} to {b}"
            ));
        }
        if self.weather != from.weather {
            out.push(format!(
                "the weather went from {} to {}",
                from.weather, self.weather
            ));
        }
        out
    }
}

/// Per state, the first read whose fingerprint differs from that state's first read, and how. `reads` in order, each
/// with its state's label and its name ("window 3 (A) before").
pub fn world_changes(reads: &[(&str, String, &Fingerprint)]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut labels: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
    for (label, ..) in reads {
        if !labels.contains(label) {
            labels.push(label);
        }
    }
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for label in labels {
        let mut of = reads.iter().filter(|(l, ..)| *l == label);
        let Some((_, first, from)) = of.next() else {
            continue;
        };
        if let Some((name, changes)) = of
            .map(|(_, name, fp)| (name, fp.changes(from)))
            .find(|(_, c)| !c.is_empty())
        {
            out.push(format!(
                "{name} differs from {first}: {}",
                changes.join(", ")
            ));
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Window 1's mean frame time against its state's later windows: `means`, the windows' labels and mean frame times in
/// order. Some when it differs from their mean by more than [`FIRST_FACTOR`] times the largest drift among the windows
/// after it (the spread of each state's later windows).
pub fn first_window(means: &[(&str, f64)]) -> Option<String> {
    let ((label, first), rest) = means.split_first()?;
    let of = |l: &str| -> Vec<f64> {
        rest.iter()
            .filter(|(o, _)| *o == l)
            .map(|(_, m)| *m)
            .collect()
    };
    let same = of(label);
    if same.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let step = (first - same.iter().sum::<f64>() / same.len() as f64).abs();
    let spread = |v: Vec<f64>| {
        v.iter().copied().fold(f64::MIN, f64::max) - v.iter().copied().fold(f64::MAX, f64::min)
    };
    let later = rest.iter().map(|(l, _)| spread(of(l))).fold(0.0, f64::max);
    (step > FIRST_FACTOR * later).then(|| {
        format!(
            "window 1 ({label}) is {step:.2} ms from {label}'s later windows, over {FIRST_FACTOR} times the later \
             windows' drift ({later:.2} ms): the world may have changed after it"
        )
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::json;

    fn fp(x: f64, yaw: f64, actors: u64, weather: &str) -> Fingerprint {
        let world = json!({"player": {"pos": [x, 0, 0], "heading": 90}, "weather": weather});
        let camera = json!({"camera": "photo", "pos": [x, -2, 1.8], "rot": [0, yaw, 0], "fov": 60});
        Fingerprint::new(&world, &camera, &json!({"found": actors, "actors": []})).unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_fingerprint_needs_every_read() {
        let world = json!({"player": {"pos": [1, 2, 3], "heading": 4}, "weather": "WT_Clear"});
        let camera = json!({"pos": [0, 0, 0], "rot": [0, 0, 0]});
        let found = json!({"found": 7});
        assert_eq!(Fingerprint::new(&world, &camera, &found).unwrap().actors, 7);
        for (w, c, a) in [
            (
                json!({"player": {"pos": [1, 2, 3], "heading": 4}}),
                camera.clone(),
                found.clone(),
            ),
            (world.clone(), json!({"pos": [0, 0, 0]}), found.clone()),
            (world.clone(), camera.clone(), json!({"actors": []})),
            (
                json!({"weather": "WT_Clear"}),
                camera.clone(),
                found.clone(),
            ),
        ] {
            assert!(Fingerprint::new(&w, &c, &a).is_err(), "{w} {c} {a}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn changes_beyond_the_tolerances_are_named() {
        let base = fp(0.0, 10.0, 12, "WT_Clear");
        assert!(
            fp(0.5, 15.0, 7, "WT_Clear").changes(&base).is_empty(),
            "within: crowds vary"
        );
        // Turns wrap at 360.
        assert!(fp(0.0, -350.0, 12, "WT_Clear").changes(&base).is_empty());
        let all = fp(2.0, 40.0, 4, "WT_Rain").changes(&base);
        assert_eq!(
            all,
            [
                "the player moved 2.00 m",
                "the camera moved 2.00 m",
                "the camera turned 30.00 deg",
                "the actors within 30 m went from 12 to 4",
                "the weather went from WT_Clear to WT_Rain"
            ]
        );
        assert!(
            fp(0.0, 10.0, 2, "WT_Clear")
                .changes(&fp(0.0, 10.0, 0, "WT_Clear"))
                .is_empty()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_first_differing_read_of_each_state_is_named() {
        let (a, moved, b) = (
            fp(0.0, 0.0, 10, "WT_Clear"),
            fp(5.0, 0.0, 10, "WT_Clear"),
            fp(0.0, 0.0, 30, "WT_Clear"),
        );
        let reads = [
            ("A", "window 1 (A) before".to_string(), &a),
            ("A", "window 1 (A) after".to_string(), &a),
            ("B", "window 2 (B) before".to_string(), &b),
            ("B", "window 2 (B) after".to_string(), &b),
            ("A", "window 3 (A) before".to_string(), &moved),
            ("A", "window 3 (A) after".to_string(), &a),
            ("B", "window 4 (B) before".to_string(), &b),
        ];
        // Another crowd in B than in A is the toggle's doing: only a change within one state counts.
        assert_eq!(
            world_changes(&reads),
            [
                "window 3 (A) before differs from window 1 (A) before: the player moved 5.00 m, the camera moved 5.00 m"
            ]
        );
        assert!(world_changes(&reads[..4]).is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn window_1_far_from_the_rest_is_named() {
        // Boot 181's shape: the world changed after window 1, the later windows agree.
        let note = first_window(&[("A", 20.8), ("B", 16.7), ("A", 16.6), ("B", 16.75)]).unwrap();
        assert!(
            note.starts_with("window 1 (A) is 4.20 ms from A's later windows"),
            "{note}"
        );
        assert!(note.contains("(0.05 ms)"), "{note}");
        // Within three times the later drift, or no later window of its state: nothing.
        assert_eq!(
            first_window(&[("A", 16.7), ("B", 16.7), ("A", 16.6), ("B", 16.75)]),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            first_window(&[("A", 20.0), ("B", 23.0), ("A", 20.0), ("B", 23.0)]),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(first_window(&[("A", 20.0), ("B", 23.0), ("B", 23.0)]), None);
        assert_eq!(first_window(&[]), None);
    }
}
```

`crates/quen-core/src/gamedata/bundle.rs`:

```rs
//! The game's bundles (`POTATO70`): a 32-byte header, the table of contents, then the entries' bytes. Two table
//! layouts: 304-byte entries with a u64 offset (the remaster's bundles and REDkit's packer: the header's word at 20 ends
//! in 5), and 320-byte entries with a u32 offset (an older packer a community mod ships: it ends in 3). An entry is raw
//! (compression 0), a zlib stream (1) or an LZ4 block (4, 5); its crc32 is of the decompressed bytes. Read-only.

use std::io::{self, Read, Seek, SeekFrom};

use flate2::read::ZlibDecoder;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

use crate::journal::hex;

const MAGIC: &[u8; 8] = b"POTATO70";
const HEADER: usize = 32;
/// A table of contents larger than this isn't a bundle's (the game's largest is 10 MB).
const TOC_MAX: usize = 256 << 20;

/// One entry of the table of contents.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Entry {
    /// As the table spells it, `\` between folders.
    pub name: String,
    pub offset: u64,
    pub size: u32,
    pub zsize: u32,
    /// Of the decompressed bytes.
    pub crc32: u32,
    pub compression: u32,
}

/// A bundle's table of contents.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Toc {
    /// The entry stride: 304 or 320.
    pub layout: usize,
    pub entries: Vec<Entry>,
    /// sha256 of the header and the table: the bundle's identity without reading its gigabytes.
    pub sha256: String,
}

fn u32_at(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_le_bytes(b[at..at + 4].try_into().expect("4 bytes"))
}

/// The table of contents of the bundle `r`. Err: not a bundle, or a table layout quen doesn't know (the header's
/// words in the reason).
pub fn toc(r: &mut (impl Read + Seek)) -> Result<Toc, String> {
    let mut header = [0u8; HEADER];
    r.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0))
        .and_then(|_| r.read_exact(&mut header))
        .map_err(|e| format!("its header: {e}"))?;
    if &header[..8] != MAGIC {
        return Err(format!("not a bundle: it begins {}", hex(&header[..8])));
    }
    let size = u32_at(&header, 16) as usize;
    let word = u32_at(&header, 20);
    let layout = match word & 0xFFFF {
        5 => 304,
        3 => 320,
        _ => 0,
    };
    if layout == 0 || !size.is_multiple_of(layout) || size > TOC_MAX {
        return Err(format!(
            "a table layout quen doesn't know: header words {word:#010x} {:#010x} {:#010x}, table size {size}",
            u32_at(&header, 24),
            u32_at(&header, 28)
        ));
    }
    let mut table = vec![0; size];
    r.read_exact(&mut table)
        .map_err(|e| format!("its table of contents: {e}"))?;
    let mut sha = Sha256::new();
    sha.update(header);
    sha.update(&table);
    let entries = table
        .chunks_exact(layout)
        .map(|e| {
            let name = e[..256].split(|&b| b == 0).next().unwrap_or_default();
            let name = name.iter().map(|&b| char::from(b)).collect();
            let at = |i| u32_at(e, i);
            match layout {
                304 => Entry {
                    name,
                    offset: u64::from(at(272)) | u64::from(at(276)) << 32,
                    size: at(280),
                    zsize: at(284),
                    crc32: at(288),
                    compression: at(292),
                },
                _ => Entry {
                    name,
                    offset: u64::from(at(284)),
                    size: at(276),
                    zsize: at(280),
                    crc32: at(312),
                    compression: at(316),
                },
            }
        })
        .collect();
    Ok(Toc {
        layout,
        entries,
        sha256: hex(&sha.finalize()),
    })
}

/// Entry `e`'s bytes from the bundle `r` of `len` bytes: whole (`limit` None: exactly `size` bytes, else an error), or
/// at least its first `limit` bytes (fewer when the entry is shorter). The crc is the caller's to check
/// ([`crc_ok`]). Err: the entry runs past the bundle's end, a compression quen doesn't read, or bytes that don't
/// decompress.
pub fn read(
    r: &mut (impl Read + Seek),
    len: u64,
    e: &Entry,
    limit: Option<usize>,
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    if e.offset.saturating_add(e.zsize.into()) > len {
        return Err(format!(
            "runs past the bundle's end: offset {} + {} bytes > {len}",
            e.offset, e.zsize
        ));
    }
    let size = e.size as usize;
    let want = limit.map_or(size, |l| l.min(size));
    let io = |e: io::Error| e.to_string();
    r.seek(SeekFrom::Start(e.offset)).map_err(io)?;
    let mut raw = r.take(e.zsize.into());
    // Grown as read: `size` is the table's word, not yet the bytes'.
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    match e.compression {
        0 => {
            raw.take(want as u64).read_to_end(&mut out).map_err(io)?;
        }
        1 => {
            let unzip = ZlibDecoder::new(raw)
                .take(want as u64)
                .read_to_end(&mut out);
            unzip.map_err(|e| format!("zlib: {e}"))?;
        }
        4 | 5 => {
            // Grown as read too: a damaged zsize (up to 4 GB) must not reserve that much up front.
            let mut src = Vec::new();
            raw.read_to_end(&mut src).map_err(io)?;
            out = lz4_block(&src, want)?;
        }
        c => return Err(format!("compression {c}, which quen doesn't read")),
    }
    if limit.is_none() && out.len() != size {
        return Err(format!(
            "decompressed to {} bytes, the table says {size}",
            out.len()
        ));
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Whether `bytes` (the whole entry) have the crc32 the table gives.
pub fn crc_ok(e: &Entry, bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {
    crc32fast::hash(bytes) == e.crc32
}

/// Decodes an LZ4 block (no frame), stopping once `limit` bytes are out. Malformed input is an error, never a panic.
pub fn lz4_block(src: &[u8], limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let bad = || "a malformed LZ4 block".to_string();
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(limit.min(src.len().saturating_mul(4)));
    let mut i = 0;
    // A length: the token's nibble, then while it is 15 each next byte added until one under 255.
    let length = |i: &mut usize, mut n: usize| -> Result<usize, String> {
        if n == 15 {
            loop {
                let b = *src.get(*i).ok_or_else(bad)?;
                *i += 1;
                n += usize::from(b);
                if b != 255 {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(n)
    };
    while i < src.len() && out.len() < limit {
        let token = src[i];
        i += 1;
        let n = length(&mut i, usize::from(token >> 4))?;
        out.extend_from_slice(src.get(i..i + n).ok_or_else(bad)?);
        i += n;
        // The last sequence has literals only.
        if i >= src.len() || out.len() >= limit {
            break;
        }
        let back = usize::from(u16::from_le_bytes([
            src[i],
            *src.get(i + 1).ok_or_else(bad)?,
        ]));
        i += 2;
        if back == 0 || back > out.len() {
            return Err(bad());
        }
        let m = (length(&mut i, usize::from(token & 15))? + 4).min(limit - out.len());
        // Byte by byte: a match may overlap what it copies.
        let from = out.len() - back;
        for k in 0..m {
            out.push(out[from + k]);
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use flate2::Compression;
    use flate2::write::ZlibEncoder;
    use std::io::{Cursor, Write};

    /// "abc", then a match 3 back for 9, then "!": 13 bytes.
    pub(crate) const LZ4: [u8; 8] = [0x35, b'a', b'b', b'c', 3, 0, 0x10, b'!'];
    pub(crate) const LZ4_OUT: &[u8] = b"abcabcabcabc!";

    pub(crate) fn zlib(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut z = ZlibEncoder::new(Vec::new(), Compression::default());
        z.write_all(data).unwrap();
        z.finish().unwrap()
    }

    /// A bundle of `layout` holding `files`: (name, the bytes as stored, the size and crc32 of the decompressed bytes,
    /// compression).
    pub(crate) fn bundle(layout: usize, files: &[(&str, Vec<u8>, &[u8], u32)]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let toc = layout * files.len();
        let mut out = MAGIC.to_vec();
        let word: u32 = if layout == 304 {
            0x8df0_0005
        } else {
            0x0001_0003
        };
        for w in [0u32, 0, toc as u32, word, 0, 0] {
            out.extend(w.to_le_bytes());
        }
        let mut data: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
        let mut table = Vec::new();
        for (name, stored, plain, compression) in files {
            let offset = (HEADER + toc + data.len()) as u32;
            let mut e = vec![0u8; layout];
            e[..name.len()].copy_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
            let put = |e: &mut Vec<u8>, at: usize, v: u32| {
                e[at..at + 4].copy_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes())
            };
            let (size, zsize, crc) = (
                plain.len() as u32,
                stored.len() as u32,
                crc32fast::hash(plain),
            );
            if layout == 304 {
                for (at, v) in [
                    (272, offset),
                    (280, size),
                    (284, zsize),
                    (288, crc),
                    (292, *compression),
                ] {
                    put(&mut e, at, v);
                }
            } else {
                for (at, v) in [
                    (276, size),
                    (280, zsize),
                    (284, offset),
                    (312, crc),
                    (316, *compression),
                ] {
                    put(&mut e, at, v);
                }
            }
            table.extend(e);
            data.extend(stored);
        }
        out.extend(table);
        out.extend(data);
        out
    }

    /// Both layouts read back byte for byte, raw, zlib and LZ4, whole and as a prefix; the crc checks.
    #[test]
    fn both_layouts_read_back() {
        let text = b"hello, bundle".repeat(20);
        let b304 = bundle(
            304,
            &[
                ("a\\raw.txt", b"raw bytes".to_vec(), b"raw bytes", 0),
                ("b\\z.txt", zlib(&text), &text, 1),
                ("c\\lz.txt", LZ4.to_vec(), LZ4_OUT, 5),
            ],
        );
        let b320 = bundle(320, &[("d\\lz.txt", LZ4.to_vec(), LZ4_OUT, 4)]);
        for (bytes, layout, want) in [
            (&b304, 304, vec![&b"raw bytes"[..], &text, LZ4_OUT]),
            (&b320, 320, vec![LZ4_OUT]),
        ] {
            let mut r = Cursor::new(bytes);
            let toc = toc(&mut r).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(toc.layout, layout);
            assert_eq!(toc.sha256.len(), 64);
            for (e, want) in toc.entries.iter().zip(want) {
                let got = read(&mut r, bytes.len() as u64, e, None).unwrap();
                assert_eq!(got, want, "{}", e.name);
                assert!(crc_ok(e, &got));
                let head = read(&mut r, bytes.len() as u64, e, Some(3)).unwrap();
                assert!(head.len() >= 3 && want.starts_with(&head), "{}", e.name);
            }
        }
        let mut r = Cursor::new(&b304);
        let toc = toc(&mut r).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(toc.entries[1].name, "b\\z.txt");
        assert!(!crc_ok(&toc.entries[1], b"other"));
    }

    /// An unknown header word or an entry past the end is an error naming why, never a panic; so is a broken LZ4
    /// block.
    #[test]
    fn bad_bundles_and_blocks_are_errors() {
        let mut b = bundle(304, &[("x", b"abc".to_vec(), b"abc", 0)]);
        let mut odd = b.clone();
        odd[20] = 7;
        let why = toc(&mut Cursor::new(&odd)).unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            why.contains("layout") && why.contains("0x8df00007"),
            "{why}"
        );
        assert!(toc(&mut Cursor::new(b"POTATO71")).is_err());
        let e = toc(&mut Cursor::new(&b)).unwrap().entries.remove(0);
        let short = b.len() as u64 - 1;
        let why = read(&mut Cursor::new(&b), short, &e, None).unwrap_err();
        assert!(why.contains("past the bundle's end"), "{why}");
        b.truncate(b.len() - 1);
        assert!(read(&mut Cursor::new(&b), b.len() as u64 + 1, &e, None).is_err());
        let unknown = Entry {
            compression: 2,
            ..e.clone()
        };
        assert!(read(&mut Cursor::new(&b), 1 << 20, &unknown, None).is_err());
        for broken in [&[0x35, b'a'][..], &[0x05, 9, 0], &[0xf0]] {
            assert!(lz4_block(broken, 100).is_err(), "{broken:?}");
        }
        assert_eq!(lz4_block(&LZ4, 5).unwrap().len(), 5);
    }
}
```
