```rs
use std::io::Cursor;

use half::f16;
use serde::Serialize;

use crate::hdr::{self, BT709_LUMA, BT2020_TO_BT709, Encoding, Region, mat3};
use crate::stats::summarise;

/// One number for a measurement row.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct Row {
    pub metric: String,
    pub value: f64,
    pub unit: &'static str,
}

/// A decoded screenshot: R, G, B per pixel, row-major from the top, as its encoding stores them (srgb8 codes 0 to 255,
/// PQ code values 0 to 1, scRGB values); alpha dropped.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Image {
    width: u32,
    height: u32,
    encoding: Encoding,
    rgb: Vec<f32>,
}

const NO_PIXEL: &str = "the crop has no pixel with finite values";

impl Image {
    /// The file's bytes as `encoding` says they are: an 8-bit RGB PNG, a 16-bit RGB PNG with cICP BT.2020 PQ, a
    /// little-endian float16 `.npy` of shape (height, width, 4). Refuses any other file, and `pq_codes_f16` (a devkit
    /// EXR: no file quen takes).
    pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8], encoding: Encoding) -> Result<Image, String> {
        let (width, height, rgb) = match encoding {
            Encoding::Srgb8 => png(bytes, false)?,
            Encoding::PqBt2020U16 => png(bytes, true)?,
            Encoding::ScrgbF16 => npy(bytes)?,
            Encoding::PqCodesF16 => {
                return Err(
                    "pq_codes_f16 (a devkit EXR) isn't an encoding quen's screenshots use".into(),
                );
            }
        };
        if width == 0 || height == 0 {
            return Err(format!("a {width}x{height} image"));
        }
        Ok(Image {
            width,
            height,
            encoding,
            rgb,
        })
    }

    pub fn width(&self) -> u32 {
        self.width
    }

    pub fn height(&self) -> u32 {
        self.height
    }

    pub fn encoding(&self) -> Encoding {
        self.encoding
    }

    /// The crop `[x, y, width, height]` in whole pixels from the top-left, or with `fraction` in fractions of the
    /// frame's width and height (each edge rounded to the nearest pixel); None: the whole frame.
    pub fn region(&self, crop: Option<[f64; 4]>, fraction: bool) -> Result<Region, String> {
        let (w, h) = (self.width, self.height);
        let Some([x, y, cw, ch]) = crop else {
            return Ok(Region {
                x: 0,
                y: 0,
                width: w,
                height: h,
            });
        };
        let [x0, y0, x1, y1] = if fraction {
            if [x, y, cw, ch].iter().any(|v| !(0.0..=1.0).contains(v)) {
                return Err("a fraction crop is 4 numbers from 0 to 1".into());
            }
            let edge = |f: f64, n: u32| (f * f64::from(n)).round();
            [edge(x, w), edge(y, h), edge(x + cw, w), edge(y + ch, h)]
        } else {
            if [x, y, cw, ch].iter().any(|v| *v < 0.0 || v.fract() != 0.0) {
                return Err("a pixel crop is 4 whole numbers from 0".into());
            }
            [x, y, x + cw, y + ch]
        };
        if x1 <= x0 || y1 <= y0 || x1 > f64::from(w) || y1 > f64::from(h) {
            return Err(format!(
                "crop [{x}, {y}, {cw}, {ch}] is empty or leaves the {w}x{h} frame"
            ));
        }
        Ok(Region {
            x: x0 as u32,
            y: y0 as u32,
            width: (x1 - x0) as u32,
            height: (y1 - y0) as u32,
        })
    }

    /// Refuses a region that is empty or leaves the frame (one not from [`Image::region`]).
    fn inside(&self, r: Region) -> Result<(), String> {
        let fits =
            |at: u32, len: u32, max: u32| len > 0 && at.checked_add(len).is_some_and(|e| e <= max);
        match fits(r.x, r.width, self.width) && fits(r.y, r.height, self.height) {
            true => Ok(()),
            false => Err(format!(
                "region {}x{} at ({}, {}) is empty or leaves the {}x{} frame",
                r.width, r.height, r.x, r.y, self.width, self.height
            )),
        }
    }

    /// Every pixel of `r`, as stored.
    fn all(&self, r: Region) -> impl Iterator<Item = [f32; 3]> + '_ {
        (r.y..r.y + r.height).flat_map(move |y| {
            let start = (y as usize * self.width as usize + r.x as usize) * 3;
            self.rgb[start..start + r.width as usize * 3]
                .chunks_exact(3)
                .map(|p| [p[0], p[1], p[2]])
        })
    }

    /// The pixels of `r` whose three values are finite: every metric leaves the others out.
    fn pixels(&self, r: Region) -> impl Iterator<Item = [f32; 3]> + '_ {
        self.all(r).filter(|p| finite(*p))
    }

    /// How many pixels of `r` the metrics leave out: a NaN or infinity in the `.npy` (the PNGs hold none).
    pub fn non_finite(&self, r: Region) -> Result<usize, String> {
        self.inside(r)?;
        Ok(self.all(r).filter(|p| !finite(*p)).count())
    }

    /// The unit token of the stored values: `srgb8`, `pq` or `scrgb`.
    fn code_unit(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self.encoding {
            Encoding::Srgb8 => "srgb8",
            Encoding::PqBt2020U16 | Encoding::PqCodesF16 => "pq",
            Encoding::ScrgbF16 => "scrgb",
        }
    }

    /// The unit of linear light: `relative` for srgb8 (sRGB white = 1), else `nits`.
    fn light_unit(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self.encoding {
            Encoding::Srgb8 => "relative",
            _ => "nits",
        }
    }

    /// Linear light in BT.709 primaries: relative for srgb8, nits for the HDR files.
    fn light(&self, p: [f32; 3]) -> [f32; 3] {
        match self.encoding {
            Encoding::Srgb8 => p.map(|c| srgb_to_linear(c / 255.0)),
            Encoding::PqBt2020U16 | Encoding::PqCodesF16 => {
                mat3(&BT2020_TO_BT709, p.map(hdr::pq_to_nits))
            }
            Encoding::ScrgbF16 => p.map(hdr::scrgb_to_nits),
        }
    }

    /// What hue and differences read: srgb8 codes as stored, PQ BT.2020 code values for the HDR files (scRGB encoded
    /// as the PNG is: negatives and above 10,000 nits clamp).
    fn coded(&self, p: [f32; 3]) -> [f32; 3] {
        match self.encoding {
            Encoding::ScrgbF16 => {
                hdr::bt709_to_bt2020(p.map(hdr::scrgb_to_nits)).map(hdr::nits_to_pq)
            }
            _ => p,
        }
    }

    /// Per channel R, G, B: the mean and median of the stored values (`<c>_<srgb8|pq|scrgb>_mean`, `_median`), and the
    /// mean of linear light (`<c>_lin_mean`, relative or nits).
    pub fn channels(&self, r: Region) -> Result<Vec<Row>, String> {
        self.inside(r)?;
        let mut lin = [0.0; 3];
        for p in self.pixels(r) {
            for (sum, v) in lin.iter_mut().zip(self.light(p)) {
                *sum += f64::from(v);
            }
        }
        let mut rows = Vec::new();
        for (c, name) in ["r", "g", "b"].into_iter().enumerate() {
            let s = summarise(self.pixels(r).map(|p| f64::from(p[c])).collect()).ok_or(NO_PIXEL)?;
            let u = self.code_unit();
            rows.extend([
                row(format!("{name}_{u}_mean"), s.mean, u),
                row(format!("{name}_{u}_median"), s.median, u),
                row(
                    format!("{name}_lin_mean"),
                    lin[c] / s.count as f64,
                    self.light_unit(),
                ),
            ]);
        }
        Ok(rows)
    }

    /// BT.709 luminance of linear light: mean, median, p95 and max (`luminance_<nits|relative>_<stat>`).
    pub fn luminance(&self, r: Region) -> Result<Vec<Row>, String> {
        self.inside(r)?;
        let y: Vec<f64> = self.pixels(r).map(|p| luma(self.light(p))).collect();
        let max = y.iter().copied().fold(f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::max);
        let s = summarise(y).ok_or(NO_PIXEL)?;
        let u = self.light_unit();
        Ok([
            ("mean", s.mean),
            ("median", s.median),
            ("p95", s.p95),
            ("max", max),
        ]
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(stat, v)| row(format!("luminance_{u}_{stat}"), v, u))
        .collect())
    }

    /// The share of pixels whose HSV hue lies from `hue[0]` to `hue[1]` degrees (both included; from above to wraps
    /// through 0) with saturation at least `s_min` and value at least `v_min`, over srgb8 codes / 255 or PQ BT.2020 code
    /// values. A gray pixel has no hue. `hue_<from>_<to>_share`.
    pub fn hue_share(
        &self,
        r: Region,
        hue: [u32; 2],
        s_min: f64,
        v_min: f64,
    ) -> Result<Row, String> {
        self.inside(r)?;
        let scale = if self.encoding == Encoding::Srgb8 {
            255.0
        } else {
            1.0
        };
        let [from, to] = hue.map(f64::from);
        let (mut n, mut hits) = (0u64, 0u64);
        for p in self.pixels(r) {
            n += 1;
            // Equal stored channels are gray, whatever the conversion to PQ codes rounds them to.
            if p[0] == p[1] && p[1] == p[2] {
                continue;
            }
            let [red, green, blue] = self.coded(p).map(|v| f64::from(v) / scale);
            let max = red.max(green).max(blue);
            let d = max - red.min(green).min(blue);
            if d <= 0.0 || max < v_min || d / max < s_min {
                continue;
            }
            let h = if max == red {
                60.0 * ((green - blue) / d).rem_euclid(6.0)
            } else if max == green {
                60.0 * ((blue - red) / d + 2.0)
            } else {
                60.0 * ((red - green) / d + 4.0)
            };
            hits += u64::from(if from <= to {
                (from..=to).contains(&h)
            } else {
                h >= from || h <= to
            });
        }
        if n == 0 {
            return Err(NO_PIXEL.into());
        }
        Ok(row(
            format!("hue_{}_{}_share", hue[0], hue[1]),
            hits as f64 / n as f64,
            "share",
        ))
    }

    /// The difference from `reference` over `r`: the mean of each pixel's largest |a − b| over R, G and B, in srgb8
    /// levels or PQ code units (`diff_<srgb8|pq>_mean`). With `noise`, a second capture of this one's state: the same
    /// against it (`floor_<u>_mean`) and the ratio (`diff_over_floor`, left out when the floor is 0).
    pub fn diff_rows(
        &self,
        reference: &Image,
        noise: Option<&Image>,
        r: Region,
    ) -> Result<Vec<Row>, String> {
        let u = if self.encoding == Encoding::Srgb8 {
            "srgb8"
        } else {
            "pq"
        };
        let diff = self.diff(reference, r)?;
        let mut rows = vec![row(format!("diff_{u}_mean"), diff, u)];
        if let Some(noise) = noise {
            let floor = self.diff(noise, r)?;
            rows.push(row(format!("floor_{u}_mean"), floor, u));
            if floor > 0.0 {
                rows.push(row("diff_over_floor".into(), diff / floor, "ratio"));
            }
        }
        Ok(rows)
    }

    /// Refuses images of another size or encoding: within a comparison the capture path stays the same.
    fn diff(&self, other: &Image, r: Region) -> Result<f64, String> {
        self.inside(r)?;
        let (a, b) = (
            (self.width, self.height, self.encoding),
            (other.width, other.height, other.encoding),
        );
        if a != b {
            return Err(format!(
                "comparison refused: {}x{} {} vs {}x{} {}",
                a.0, a.1, a.2, b.0, b.1, b.2
            ));
        }
        let (mut sum, mut n) = (0.0, 0u64);
        for (pa, pb) in self
            .all(r)
            .zip(other.all(r))
            .filter(|(a, b)| finite(*a) && finite(*b))
        {
            let (pa, pb) = (self.coded(pa), other.coded(pb));
            sum += f64::from((0..3).map(|c| (pa[c] - pb[c]).abs()).fold(0.0, f32::max));
            n += 1;
        }
        match n {
            0 => Err(NO_PIXEL.into()),
            n => Ok(sum / n as f64),
        }
    }
}

fn row(metric: String, value: f64, unit: &'static str) -> Row {
    Row {
        metric,
        value,
        unit,
    }
}

fn finite(p: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
    p.iter().all(|v| v.is_finite())
}

fn luma(rgb: [f32; 3]) -> f64 {
    rgb.iter()
        .zip(BT709_LUMA)
        .map(|(&v, w)| f64::from(v) * w)
        .sum()
}

/// The sRGB EOTF (IEC 61966-2-1), a code in 0..=1 to linear light.
fn srgb_to_linear(c: f32) -> f32 {
    if c <= 0.04045 {
        c / 12.92
    } else {
        ((c + 0.055) / 1.055).powf(2.4)
    }
}

/// An RGB or RGBA PNG: 8-bit (`pq` false), or 16-bit with cICP BT.2020 PQ (`pq`), as capture.rs and
/// [`hdr::Frame::write_png_pq`] write them. Width, height, and R, G, B per pixel (16-bit codes / 65535).
fn png(bytes: &[u8], pq: bool) -> Result<(u32, u32, Vec<f32>), String> {
    // A 4K 16-bit frame is about 50 MB of pixels: above the decoder's default 64 MiB for anything larger.
    let limits = png::Limits { bytes: 1 << 30 };
    let mut reader = png::Decoder::new_with_limits(Cursor::new(bytes), limits)
        .read_info()
        .map_err(|e| format!("PNG: {e}"))?;
    let cicp = reader
        .info()
        .coding_independent_code_points
        .map(|c| (c.color_primaries, c.transfer_function));
    if pq && cicp != Some((9, 16)) {
        return Err(format!(
            "a pq_bt2020_u16 PNG carries cICP BT.2020 PQ (9, 16); this one {cicp:?}"
        ));
    }
    let size = reader
        .output_buffer_size()
        .ok_or("PNG: too large to decode")?;
    let mut buf = vec![0; size];
    let info = reader
        .next_frame(&mut buf)
        .map_err(|e| format!("PNG: {e}"))?;
    let channels = match info.color_type {
        png::ColorType::Rgb => 3,
        png::ColorType::Rgba => 4,
        other => return Err(format!("a {other:?} PNG, not RGB")),
    };
    let (depth, bytes_per) = if pq {
        (png::BitDepth::Sixteen, 2)
    } else {
        (png::BitDepth::Eight, 1)
    };
    if info.bit_depth != depth {
        return Err(format!(
            "a {}-bit PNG where its encoding needs {} bits",
            info.bit_depth as u8, depth as u8
        ));
    }
    let (w, h) = (info.width as usize, info.height as usize);
    let mut rgb = Vec::with_capacity(w * h * 3);
    for line in buf.chunks_exact(info.line_size).take(h) {
        for px in line[..w * channels * bytes_per].chunks_exact(channels * bytes_per) {
            for c in 0..3 {
                rgb.push(match pq {
                    true => f32::from(u16::from_be_bytes([px[c * 2], px[c * 2 + 1]])) / 65535.0,
                    false => f32::from(px[c]),
                });
            }
        }
    }
    Ok((info.width, info.height, rgb))
}

/// A `.npy` as [`hdr::Frame::write_npy`] writes it: version 1.0, `<f2`, C order, shape (height, width, 4).
fn npy(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(u32, u32, Vec<f32>), String> {
    let bad = |why: &str| format!("not a float16 RGBA .npy as quen writes it: {why}");
    let rest = bytes
        .strip_prefix(b"\x93NUMPY\x01\x00")
        .ok_or_else(|| bad("no version 1.0 NUMPY magic"))?;
    let len = rest.get(..2).ok_or_else(|| bad("truncated"))?;
    let len = usize::from(u16::from_le_bytes([len[0], len[1]]));
    let header = rest
        .get(2..2 + len)
        .and_then(|h| std::str::from_utf8(h).ok())
        .ok_or_else(|| bad("truncated header"))?;
    if !header.contains("'descr': '<f2'") || !header.contains("'fortran_order': False") {
        return Err(bad(header.trim()));
    }
    let shape = header
        .split("'shape': (")
        .nth(1)
        .and_then(|s| s.split(')').next())
        .ok_or_else(|| bad("no shape"))?;
    let dims: Vec<usize> = shape
        .split(',')
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
        .map(str::parse)
        .collect::<Result<_, _>>()
        .map_err(|_| bad(shape))?;
    let [h, w, 4] = dims[..] else {
        return Err(bad(&format!("shape ({shape})")));
    };
    let data = &rest[2 + len..];
    if Some(data.len()) != h.checked_mul(w).and_then(|n| n.checked_mul(8)) {
        return Err(bad(&format!(
            "{} data bytes for shape ({shape})",
            data.len()
        )));
    }
    let size = |n: usize| u32::try_from(n).map_err(|_| bad("too large"));
    let rgb = data
        .chunks_exact(8)
        .flat_map(|px| (0..3).map(move |c| f16::from_le_bytes([px[c * 2], px[c * 2 + 1]]).to_f32()))
        .collect();
    Ok((size(w)?, size(h)?, rgb))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::hdr::{Frame, Pixels, SCRGB_WHITE_NITS};

    fn close(a: f64, b: f64, tol: f64) -> bool {
        (a - b).abs() <= tol
    }

    /// `rows` as (metric, value) pairs, for lookups.
    fn value(rows: &[Row], metric: &str) -> f64 {
        rows.iter()
            .find(|r| r.metric == metric)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no {metric} in {rows:?}"))
            .value
    }

    /// An 8-bit RGB PNG of `px`, as capture.rs encodes the SDR grab.
    fn srgb8(width: u32, height: u32, px: &[[u8; 3]]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let mut encoder = png::Encoder::new(&mut out, width, height);
        encoder.set_color(png::ColorType::Rgb);
        encoder.set_depth(png::BitDepth::Eight);
        let mut writer = encoder.write_header().unwrap();
        writer.write_image_data(&px.concat()).unwrap();
        writer.finish().unwrap();
        out
    }

    /// An scRGB frame of `px` (RGB in scRGB units, alpha 1), and quen's two HDR files of it: the .npy and the PQ PNG.
    fn hdr_files(width: u32, height: u32, px: &[[f32; 3]]) -> (Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>) {
        let s = px
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|p| [p[0], p[1], p[2], 1.0])
            .map(f16::from_f32)
            .collect();
        let frame = Frame::new(width, height, Pixels::ScrgbF16(s)).unwrap();
        let (mut npy, mut png) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        frame.write_npy(&mut npy).unwrap();
        frame.write_png_pq(&mut png).unwrap();
        (npy, png)
    }

    fn nits(n: f32) -> [f32; 3] {
        [n / SCRGB_WHITE_NITS; 3]
    }

    /// srgb8, hand-computed: red, green, blue and gray 128 in a 2x2 frame.
    #[test]
    fn srgb8_metrics_match_hand_values() {
        let file = srgb8(
            2,
            2,
            &[[255, 0, 0], [0, 255, 0], [0, 0, 255], [128, 128, 128]],
        );
        let img = Image::decode(&file, Encoding::Srgb8).unwrap();
        let all = img.region(None, false).unwrap();
        let ch = img.channels(all).unwrap();
        // R: 255, 0, 0, 128: mean 95.75, median between 0 and 128.
        assert_eq!(value(&ch, "r_srgb8_mean"), 95.75);
        assert_eq!(value(&ch, "r_srgb8_median"), 64.0);
        let gray = ((128.0 / 255.0 + 0.055) / 1.055f64).powf(2.4);
        assert!(
            close(value(&ch, "r_lin_mean"), (1.0 + gray) / 4.0, 1e-6),
            "{ch:?}"
        );
        assert!(ch.iter().all(|r| r.unit
            == if r.metric.contains("lin") {
                "relative"
            } else {
                "srgb8"
            }));

        let y = img.luminance(all).unwrap();
        // Y: 0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722 and the gray's linear value; sorted 0.0722, 0.2126, gray, 0.7152.
        assert!(close(
            value(&y, "luminance_relative_mean"),
            (0.2126 + 0.7152 + 0.0722 + gray) / 4.0,
            1e-6
        ));
        assert!(close(
            value(&y, "luminance_relative_median"),
            (0.2126 + gray) / 2.0,
            1e-6
        ));
        assert!(close(value(&y, "luminance_relative_max"), 0.7152, 1e-6));
        // p95: rank 2.85, between gray and 0.7152.
        assert!(close(
            value(&y, "luminance_relative_p95"),
            gray + 0.85 * (0.7152 - gray),
            1e-6
        ));

        // Hues 0, 120 and 240; gray has none.
        let share = |hue, s, v| img.hue_share(all, hue, s, v).unwrap().value;
        assert_eq!(share([200, 280], 0.0, 0.0), 0.25);
        assert_eq!(share([350, 10], 0.0, 0.0), 0.25, "wraps through 0");
        assert_eq!(share([0, 360], 0.0, 0.0), 0.75);
        assert_eq!(share([0, 360], 0.0, 1.0), 0.75, "v 1 is the full code");
        assert_eq!(
            img.hue_share(all, [200, 280], 0.0, 0.0).unwrap().metric,
            "hue_200_280_share"
        );

        // A crop: the right column, in pixels and as fractions.
        let right = img.region(Some([1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0]), false).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(img.region(Some([0.5, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0]), true).unwrap(), right);
        assert_eq!(value(&img.channels(right).unwrap(), "g_srgb8_mean"), 191.5);
    }

    /// The PQ PNG and the .npy of one HDR shot, hand-computed in nits: black and 10,000 nits are exact in PQ; 80 and
    /// 400 nits, and red at 80 nits a channel, within a 16-bit PQ step.
    #[test]
    fn hdr_files_give_nits_and_agree() {
        let px = [
            nits(0.0),
            nits(10_000.0),
            nits(80.0),
            nits(400.0),
            [1.0, 0.0, 0.0],
            nits(400.0),
        ];
        let (npy, png) = hdr_files(3, 2, &px);
        let scrgb = Image::decode(&npy, Encoding::ScrgbF16).unwrap();
        let pq = Image::decode(&png, Encoding::PqBt2020U16).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            (scrgb.width(), scrgb.height(), pq.width(), pq.height()),
            (3, 2, 3, 2)
        );

        let all = scrgb.region(None, false).unwrap();
        let red = 0.2126 * 80.0;
        // Y: 0, 10000, 80, 400, 17.008, 400: sorted 0, 17.008, 80, 400, 400, 10000.
        let mean = (10_000.0 + 80.0 + 400.0 + red + 400.0) / 6.0;
        for (img, tol) in [(&scrgb, 0.05), (&pq, 0.5)] {
            let y = img.luminance(all).unwrap();
            assert!(
                close(value(&y, "luminance_nits_mean"), mean, tol * 6.0),
                "{:?}: {y:?}",
                img.encoding()
            );
            assert!(
                close(value(&y, "luminance_nits_median"), 240.0, tol * 2.0),
                "{y:?}"
            );
            assert!(
                close(value(&y, "luminance_nits_max"), 10_000.0, 1.0),
                "{y:?}"
            );
            // p95: rank 4.75, between 400 and 10,000.
            assert!(
                close(value(&y, "luminance_nits_p95"), 400.0 + 0.75 * 9600.0, 2.0),
                "{y:?}"
            );
            assert!(y.iter().all(|r| r.unit == "nits"));
            let ch = img.channels(all).unwrap();
            // Linear R in BT.709: 0, 10000, 80, 400, 80, 400.
            assert!(
                close(value(&ch, "r_lin_mean"), 10_960.0 / 6.0, tol * 6.0),
                "{ch:?}"
            );
            assert!(
                close(value(&ch, "g_lin_mean"), 10_880.0 / 6.0, tol * 6.0),
                "{ch:?}"
            );
        }
        // Stored values: scRGB as is (R: 0, 125, 1, 5, 1, 5), PQ as codes 0 to 1 (black 0, 10,000 nits 1).
        let ch = scrgb.channels(all).unwrap();
        assert!(close(value(&ch, "r_scrgb_mean"), 137.0 / 6.0, 1e-3));
        assert_eq!(value(&ch, "r_scrgb_median"), 3.0);
        let corner = pq.region(Some([0.0, 0.0, 2.0, 1.0]), false).unwrap();
        let ch = pq.channels(corner).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(value(&ch, "g_pq_mean"), 0.5);
        assert!(ch.iter().any(|r| r.unit == "pq"));

        // Hue over PQ BT.2020 codes: only the red pixel has one, and both files agree.
        for img in [&scrgb, &pq] {
            assert!(close(
                img.hue_share(all, [350, 30], 0.1, 0.0).unwrap().value,
                1.0 / 6.0,
                1e-9
            ));
            assert_eq!(img.hue_share(all, [60, 300], 0.0, 0.0).unwrap().value, 0.0);
        }
    }

    /// diff: srgb8 levels and PQ code units, the floor and the ratio; a size or encoding mismatch refuses.
    #[test]
    fn diff_against_a_reference_and_a_floor() {
        let base = [[100u8, 100, 100]; 4];
        let mut moved = base;
        moved[3] = [100, 120, 90];
        let mut noisy = base;
        noisy[0] = [102, 100, 100];
        let img = |px: &[[u8; 3]]| Image::decode(&srgb8(2, 2, px), Encoding::Srgb8).unwrap();
        let (a, b, n) = (img(&base), img(&moved), img(&noisy));
        let all = a.region(None, false).unwrap();
        let rows = a.diff_rows(&b, Some(&n), all).unwrap();
        // The largest |a - b| is 20 levels in one pixel of four, the floor 2 in one.
        assert_eq!(value(&rows, "diff_srgb8_mean"), 5.0);
        assert_eq!(value(&rows, "floor_srgb8_mean"), 0.5);
        assert_eq!(value(&rows, "diff_over_floor"), 10.0);
        let same = a.diff_rows(&a, Some(&a), all).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(same.len(), 2, "no ratio over a zero floor: {same:?}");

        // HDR: one pixel from 100 to 1000 nits in green: PQ(1000) - PQ(100) in BT.2020 green, a quarter on average.
        let mut px = [nits(100.0); 4];
        let (npy_a, png_a) = hdr_files(2, 2, &px);
        px[3][1] = 1000.0 / SCRGB_WHITE_NITS;
        let (npy_b, _) = hdr_files(2, 2, &px);
        let (sa, sb) = (
            Image::decode(&npy_a, Encoding::ScrgbF16).unwrap(),
            Image::decode(&npy_b, Encoding::ScrgbF16).unwrap(),
        );
        let step = |n: f32| hdr::nits_to_pq(hdr::bt709_to_bt2020([100.0, n, 100.0])[1]);
        let want = f64::from(step(1000.0) - step(100.0)) / 4.0;
        let rows = sa.diff_rows(&sb, None, all).unwrap();
        assert!(
            close(value(&rows, "diff_pq_mean"), want, 1e-6),
            "{rows:?} vs {want}"
        );
        let pq = Image::decode(&png_a, Encoding::PqBt2020U16).unwrap();
        let tall = Image::decode(&srgb8(1, 4, &base), Encoding::Srgb8).unwrap();
        for (x, y) in [(&sa, &pq), (&a, &sa), (&a, &tall)] {
            assert!(
                x.diff_rows(y, None, all)
                    .unwrap_err()
                    .contains("comparison refused")
            );
        }
    }

    /// Refusals: a file that isn't what its encoding says, a crop outside the frame, a region not from `region`.
    #[test]
    fn refuses_what_it_cannot_read() {
        let sdr = srgb8(2, 1, &[[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]);
        let (npy, png) = hdr_files(2, 1, &[nits(1.0), nits(2.0)]);
        let short = npy[..npy.len() - 2].to_vec();
        for (bytes, enc, why) in [
            (&sdr, Encoding::PqBt2020U16, "cICP"),
            (&png, Encoding::Srgb8, "16-bit PNG"),
            (&npy, Encoding::Srgb8, "PNG"),
            (&sdr, Encoding::ScrgbF16, "NUMPY"),
            (&short, Encoding::ScrgbF16, "data bytes"),
            (&npy, Encoding::PqCodesF16, "devkit EXR"),
        ] {
            let err = Image::decode(bytes, enc).unwrap_err();
            assert!(err.contains(why), "{enc}: {err}");
        }
        let mut f4 = npy.clone();
        let at = f4.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"<f2'").unwrap();
        f4[at + 2] = b'4';
        assert!(Image::decode(&f4, Encoding::ScrgbF16).is_err());

        let img = Image::decode(&sdr, Encoding::Srgb8).unwrap();
        for (crop, fraction) in [
            ([0.0, 0.0, 3.0, 1.0], false),
            ([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0], false),
            ([0.5, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0], false),
            ([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.5], true),
            ([0.0, 0.0, 0.1, 1.0], true),
        ] {
            assert!(
                img.region(Some(crop), fraction).is_err(),
                "{crop:?} {fraction}"
            );
        }
        let outside = Region {
            x: 1,
            y: 0,
            width: 2,
            height: 1,
        };
        assert!(img.channels(outside).is_err() && img.luminance(outside).is_err());
    }

    /// A NaN pixel in the .npy is left out of every metric and counted.
    #[test]
    fn non_finite_pixels_are_left_out() {
        let (mut npy, _) = hdr_files(2, 1, &[nits(80.0), nits(160.0)]);
        let n = npy.len();
        npy[n - 8..n - 6].copy_from_slice(&f16::NAN.to_le_bytes());
        let img = Image::decode(&npy, Encoding::ScrgbF16).unwrap();
        let all = img.region(None, false).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(img.non_finite(all).unwrap(), 1);
        assert!(close(
            value(&img.luminance(all).unwrap(), "luminance_nits_mean"),
            80.0,
            0.05
        ));
        let only = img.region(Some([1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]), false).unwrap();
        assert!(img.channels(only).unwrap_err().contains("finite"));
    }
}

```

`crates/quen-core/src/input.rs`:

```rs
//! w3ctl.py and console_type.py as data: key tokens, the timed plan of key events game_keys sends (what
//! `w3ctl.py keys --dry-run` prints), a console line's plan (each character by its US virtual key, sent as the scancode
//! the game's layout gives that key), and the checks of the console's prompt row (the typed text before Enter, the
//! prompt gone after the close). The Windows layer sends a plan with SendInput and checks the game's focus before every
//! event.

/// w3ctl's key hold (REDengine drops very short synthetic taps) and its pause between key tokens.
pub const HOLD_MS: u64 = 200;
pub const GAP_MS: u64 = 400;
/// The longest hold or wait a token may ask for: a plan blocks the session thread while it runs.
pub const MAX_MS: u64 = 60_000;
/// Console typing. Every key event of a line's text is `CHAR_MS` after the one before (down, 30, up, 30, next, shift
/// included): live boot 2's holds arrived at 30 ms 4 of 4, 16 ms 2 of 2, 8 ms 1 of 2 and 0 ms 0 of 4, so the game drops
/// a tap shorter than its frame. About 60 ms a character, faster than a person types. The console and Enter keys keep
/// w3ctl's hold, then `CONSOLE_OPEN_MS` for the console to take the text, `SETTLE_MS` before each read of the prompt
/// row (the text before Enter, the prompt gone after the close), and `ENTER_MS` for the line to run before the close.
/// ponytail: 30 ms is about 1.5 frames at boot 1's ~50 fps; below about 33 fps a 30 ms tap may drop again (the check
/// before Enter then refuses the line), and CHAR_MS goes up.
pub const CHAR_MS: u64 = 30;
pub const CONSOLE_OPEN_MS: u64 = 300;
pub const ENTER_MS: u64 = 300;
pub const SETTLE_MS: u64 = 300;
/// The Set-1 scancode of the key left of 1 (US `~`). The console's own key is VK_OEM_3 on the game's keyboard layout,
/// which the Windows layer looks up (verified live on a non-US layout); this is the fallback, and `grave` / `tilde`.
pub const GRAVE: u16 = 0x29;

/// One step of a plan.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Event {
    /// A key by Set-1 scancode (>= 0x100: E0-extended), down or up.
    Key { name: String, sc: u16, up: bool },
    /// A pause; `why` is w3ctl's label (hold, gap, wait) or console_type's (tap, shift, settle).
    Sleep { ms: u64, why: &'static str },
}

const NAMED: [(&str, u16); 33] = [
    ("escape", 0x01),
    ("esc", 0x01),
    ("tab", 0x0F),
    ("backspace", 0x0E),
    ("enter", 0x1C),
    ("space", 0x39),
    ("lshift", 0x2A),
    ("rshift", 0x36),
    ("lctrl", 0x1D),
    ("lalt", 0x38),
    ("rctrl", 0x11D),
    ("ralt", 0x138),
    ("up", 0x148),
    ("down", 0x150),
    ("left", 0x14B),
    ("right", 0x14D),
    ("insert", 0x152),
    ("delete", 0x153),
    ("home", 0x147),
    ("end", 0x14F),
    ("pgup", 0x149),
    ("pageup", 0x149),
    ("pgdn", 0x151),
    ("pagedown", 0x151),
    ("ctrl", 0x1D),
    ("shift", 0x2A),
    ("alt", 0x38),
    ("period", 0x34),
    ("minus", 0x0C),
    ("comma", 0x33),
    ("grave", GRAVE),
    ("tilde", GRAVE),
    ("console", GRAVE),
];

/// w3ctl's scancode table: a-z, 0-9, f1-f12 and the names above (lower case).
pub fn scancode(name: &str) -> Option<u16> {
    if let [c] = name.as_bytes() {
        let rows = [("qwertyuiop", 0x10), ("asdfghjkl", 0x1E), ("zxcvbnm", 0x2C)];
        for (row, first) in rows {
            if let Some(i) = row.find(char::from(*c)) {
                return Some(first + i as u16);
            }
        }
        if c.is_ascii_digit() {
            return Some(0x02 + (u16::from(c - b'0') + 9) % 10); // 1 = 0x02 ... 9 = 0x0A, 0 = 0x0B
        }
    }
    let f = name
        .strip_prefix('f')
        .filter(|n| !n.starts_with('0') && n.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()));
    match f.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok()) {
        Some(n @ 1..=10) => return Some(0x3A + n),
        Some(n @ 11..=12) => return Some(0x4C + n),
        _ => {}
    }
    NAMED.iter().find(|(n, _)| *n == name).map(|&(_, sc)| sc)
}

/// A chord that acts on Windows rather than the game, which game_keys never sends (security review): Alt+Tab,
/// Alt+Esc, Alt+F4, Ctrl+Esc (and Ctrl+Shift+Esc), Ctrl+Alt+anything. The Windows keys aren't in the table at all.
fn acts_on_windows(keys: &[&str]) -> bool {
    let has = |names: &[&str]| keys.iter().any(|k| names.contains(k));
    let ctrl = has(&["ctrl", "lctrl", "rctrl"]);
    let alt = has(&["alt", "lalt", "ralt"]);
    let esc = has(&["escape", "esc"]);
    (alt && (esc || has(&["tab", "f4"]))) || (ctrl && (alt || esc))
}

/// w3ctl's `parse_tokens`: each token is a key or a chord (`ctrl+shift+e`: pressed in order, released in
/// reverse), `name:ms` holds it that long instead of `hold`, `wait:ms` sleeps; `gap` goes between key tokens. The key
/// `console` is `console` (the layout's console key). Refused: an unknown key (the Windows keys among them), a chord
/// that acts on Windows (`acts_on_windows`), a bad or missing duration, one over `MAX_MS`.
pub fn plan<S: AsRef<str>>(
    tokens: &[S],
    hold: u64,
    gap: u64,
    console: u16,
) -> Result<Vec<Event>, String> {
    let mut plan = Vec::new();
    let mut keyed = false;
    for token in tokens {
        let token = token.as_ref();
        let lower = token.to_lowercase();
        let (name, ms) = lower.split_once(':').unwrap_or((&lower, ""));
        let ms = match ms {
            "" => None,
            ms if ms.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) => Some(
                ms.parse()
                    .ok()
                    .filter(|ms| *ms <= MAX_MS)
                    .ok_or(format!("token {token:?}: over {MAX_MS} ms"))?,
            ),
            _ => return Err(format!("bad duration in token {token:?}")),
        };
        if name == "wait" {
            let ms = ms.ok_or("wait needs a duration, e.g. wait:500")?;
            plan.push(Event::Sleep { ms, why: "wait" });
            continue;
        }
        let keys = name
            .split('+')
            .map(|k| match k {
                "console" => Ok((k, console)),
                "win" | "lwin" | "rwin" => Err(format!(
                    "{k:?}: the Windows key acts on Windows, not the game; refused"
                )),
                _ => scancode(k).map(|sc| (k, sc)).ok_or(format!(
                    "unknown key {k:?}; known: a-z 0-9 f1-f12 and {}",
                    NAMED.map(|(n, _)| n).join(" ")
                )),
            })
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, String>>()?;
        let names: Vec<&str> = keys.iter().map(|&(k, _)| k).collect();
        if acts_on_windows(&names) {
            return Err(format!(
                "token {token:?}: that chord acts on Windows, not the game (Alt+Tab, Alt+Esc, Alt+F4, Ctrl+Esc, \
                 Ctrl+Shift+Esc, Ctrl+Alt+any); refused"
            ));
        }
        if keyed {
            plan.push(Event::Sleep {
                ms: gap,
                why: "gap",
            });
        }
        let key = |&(name, sc): &(&str, u16), up| Event::Key {
            name: name.into(),
            sc,
            up,
        };
        plan.extend(keys.iter().map(|k| key(k, false)));
        plan.push(Event::Sleep {
            ms: ms.unwrap_or(hold),
            why: "hold",
        });
        plan.extend(keys.iter().rev().map(|k| key(k, true)));
        keyed = true;
    }
    Ok(plan)
}

/// w3ctl's `describe`: one line of a dry run.
pub fn describe(event: &Event) -> String {
    match event {
        Event::Sleep { ms, why } => format!("sleep {ms:>5} ms  ({why})"),
        Event::Key { name, sc, up } => format!(
            "key   {:<4}  {name:<9} sc=0x{:02X}{}",
            if *up { "up" } else { "down" },
            sc & 0xFF,
            if *sc > 0xFF { " ext" } else { "" }
        ),
    }
}

/// The characters the console types besides letters (virtual keys A-Z) and digits (0-9): (character, US virtual key,
/// shift). The console reads a key's virtual key on the active layout through a US table (first experiment boot,
/// measured on a non-US layout: the US `-` position arrived as `=` there), so a character is its US virtual key and
/// shift, and the Windows layer sends whatever scancode the game's layout gives that virtual key.
///
/// Not typed yet, because no one has seen the console take them: `@` (VK 2 + shift), `"` (VK_OEM_7 + shift), `#` (VK 3 +
/// shift), `\` (VK_OEM_5), `|` (VK_OEM_5 + shift). `~` is VK_OEM_3 + shift, the console key itself, so it can't be
/// typed. Once a live check shows the console takes one, it is one row here.
const TYPED: [(char, u16, bool); 7] = [
    (' ', 0x20, false), // VK_SPACE
    (',', 0xBC, false), // VK_OEM_COMMA
    ('.', 0xBE, false), // VK_OEM_PERIOD
    ('-', 0xBD, false), // VK_OEM_MINUS
    ('(', 0x39, true),  // VK 9
    (')', 0x30, true),  // VK 0
    ('_', 0xBD, true),  // VK_OEM_MINUS
];

/// A character's US virtual key and whether shift goes with it: letters (capitals with shift), digits, `TYPED`.
pub fn console_vk(c: char) -> Option<(u16, bool)> {
    match c {
        'a'..='z' => Some((c.to_ascii_uppercase() as u16, false)),
        'A'..='Z' | '0'..='9' => Some((c as u16, c.is_ascii_uppercase())),
        _ => TYPED
            .iter()
            .find(|&&(t, ..)| t == c)
            .map(|&(_, vk, shift)| (vk, shift)),
    }
}

/// The scancode of a `console_vk` virtual key on the US layout: what console_type.py typed, and the layout quen plans
/// with where there is no game window to ask (dry runs, parity).
pub fn us_scancode(vk: u16) -> Option<u16> {
    match vk {
        0x30..=0x39 | 0x41..=0x5A => {
            scancode(&char::from(vk as u8).to_ascii_lowercase().to_string())
        }
        0x20 => Some(0x39),
        0xBC => Some(0x33),
        0xBE => Some(0x34),
        0xBD => Some(0x0C),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// One console line's plan, console_type.py's keys at quen's own pace (`CHAR_MS`): open the console (its key held
/// `HOLD_MS`, then `CONSOLE_OPEN_MS`); each character down and up (shift down and up around a shifted one) by the
/// scancode `scancode_of` gives its US virtual key on the game's layout, `CHAR_MS` apart; a pause labelled `typed`
/// (`SETTLE_MS`), after which the Windows layer reads the prompt row ([`console_text`]) and presses Enter only if the
/// line shows; then Enter and `ENTER_MS`. With `close`, [`console_close`]. A load leaves `close` off: its close key
/// would land on the loading screen (first experiment boot), so game_load closes the console once gameplay is back.
/// Refused, nothing planned: a character with no US virtual key, or one whose key the layout lacks.
pub fn console_line(
    line: &str,
    console: u16,
    scancode_of: &dyn Fn(u16) -> Option<u16>,
    close: bool,
) -> Result<Vec<Event>, String> {
    let (mut bad, mut missing, mut taps) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    for c in line.chars() {
        match console_vk(c) {
            None => bad.push(c),
            Some((vk, shift)) => match scancode_of(vk) {
                None => missing.push(c),
                Some(sc) => taps.push((c, sc, shift)),
            },
        }
    }
    if !bad.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!(
            "characters the console can't type: {bad:?}; nothing typed (letters, digits, space and , . - ( ) _ only)"
        ));
    }
    if !missing.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!(
            "characters with no key on the game's keyboard layout: {missing:?}; nothing typed"
        ));
    }
    let open = format!("wait:{CONSOLE_OPEN_MS}");
    let mut plan = plan(&["console", &open], HOLD_MS, GAP_MS, console)?;
    let mut typed = Vec::new();
    for (c, sc, shift) in taps {
        let name = c.to_string();
        let shift = |up| shift.then(|| key("lshift", 0x2A, up));
        typed.extend(shift(false));
        typed.extend([key(&name, sc, false), key(&name, sc, true)]);
        typed.extend(shift(true));
    }
    for event in typed {
        if matches!(plan.last(), Some(Event::Key { .. })) {
            plan.push(Event::Sleep {
                ms: CHAR_MS,
                why: "char",
            });
        }
        plan.push(event);
    }
    plan.push(Event::Sleep {
        ms: SETTLE_MS,
        why: "typed",
    });
    let enter = format!("wait:{ENTER_MS}");
    plan.extend(self::plan(&["enter", &enter], HOLD_MS, GAP_MS, console)?);
    if close {
        plan.extend(console_close(console));
    }
    Ok(plan)
}

/// Closes the console: its key held `HOLD_MS`, then `SETTLE_MS` before the check that its prompt is gone.
pub fn console_close(console: u16) -> Vec<Event> {
    vec![
        key("console", console, false),
        Event::Sleep {
            ms: HOLD_MS,
            why: "hold",
        },
        key("console", console, true),
        Event::Sleep {
            ms: SETTLE_MS,
            why: "settle",
        },
    ]
}

/// After a line that didn't show on the prompt (the check before Enter): a backspace per character, `CHAR_MS` apart, to
/// take back whatever of it arrived, then [`console_close`]. Enter never went, so nothing ran, and the next line starts
/// on an empty prompt.
pub fn console_clear(chars: usize, console: u16) -> Vec<Event> {
    let char_ms = || Event::Sleep {
        ms: CHAR_MS,
        why: "char",
    };
    let back = |up| key("backspace", 0x0E, up);
    let mut plan: Vec<Event> = (0..chars)
        .flat_map(|_| [back(false), char_ms(), back(true), char_ms()])
        .collect();
    plan.extend(console_close(console));
    plan
}

fn key(name: &str, sc: u16, up: bool) -> Event {
    Event::Key {
        name: name.into(),
        sc,
        up,
    }
}

/// The console's '>' prompt, as (row, column) of a 1280x720 frame: the glyph's lit points (console_type.py's).
const PROMPT_ON: [(usize, usize); 7] = [
    (106, 4),
    (106, 5),
    (106, 6),
    (107, 6),
    (107, 7),
    (108, 4),
    (108, 5),
];
/// The glyph's black outline, as 2x2 squares of a 3840x2160 frame (top row, left column): above the top arm, the notch
/// between the arms, below the bottom arm. The game draws the glyph opaque, outline and all, so these read dark over
/// any background, where console_type.py's dark points beside the glyph show what the translucent console lets through
/// (live boot 3 outdoors at dusk: up to 137 there, 0-4 here, 184 on the glyph; indoors 33 there).
/// ponytail: measured at 4K only; other sizes read the same spots by area.
const PROMPT_OUTLINE: [(usize, usize); 7] = [
    (314, 10),
    (314, 12),
    (320, 10),
    (322, 10),
    (322, 12),
    (328, 14),
    (328, 16),
];
/// How much brighter the glyph must read than its outline, and a typed column's brightest point than its darkest.
const CONTRAST: i32 = 100;
/// Where typed text sits on the prompt's row, in 1280x720 terms: from column 9 rightwards, rows 102-112 (live boot 2 at
/// 4K: the text from column 10, x-height rows 105-110, the cursor 103-110, descenders to 111).
const TEXT_COL: usize = 9;
const TEXT_ROWS: std::ops::RangeInclusive<usize> = 102..=112;
/// The widest a typed character draws, in those columns, plus room: live boot 2's `quenxyz` spanned 33 (4.7 each).
const TEXT_PER_CHAR: usize = 8;

/// A pixel of a 1280x720 frame as a square of a 3840x2160 one.
fn cell((row, col): (usize, usize)) -> (usize, usize, usize) {
    (3 * row, 3 * col, 3)
}

/// A frame (`bgra`: `w` x `h` pixels, rows top-down) read at a square of a 3840x2160 frame (top row, left column, side)
/// scaled to it by area (cv2's INTER_AREA), on its darkest channel; and the prompt's levels there: its glyph's dimmest
/// lit point and its outline's brightest point.
fn prompt_levels(
    bgra: &[u8],
    w: usize,
    h: usize,
) -> (impl Fn((usize, usize, usize)) -> i32, i32, i32) {
    let (sx, sy) = (w as f64 / 3840.0, h as f64 / 2160.0);
    let at = move |(row, col, side): (usize, usize, usize)| {
        let (x0, x1) = (col as f64 * sx, (col + side) as f64 * sx);
        let (y0, y1) = (row as f64 * sy, (row + side) as f64 * sy);
        let mut sum = [0.0f64; 3];
        for y in y0 as usize..(y1.ceil() as usize).min(h) {
            let wy = (y1.min(y as f64 + 1.0) - y0.max(y as f64)).max(0.0);
            for x in x0 as usize..(x1.ceil() as usize).min(w) {
                let wx = (x1.min(x as f64 + 1.0) - x0.max(x as f64)).max(0.0);
                for (ch, s) in sum.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                    let v = bgra.get((y * w + x) * 4 + ch).copied().unwrap_or(0);
                    *s += f64::from(v) * wx * wy;
                }
            }
        }
        let area = (x1 - x0) * (y1 - y0);
        sum.map(|s| (s / area).round().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as i32)
            .into_iter()
            .min()
            .unwrap_or(0)
    };
    let on = PROMPT_ON
        .map(|p| at(cell(p)))
        .into_iter()
        .min()
        .unwrap_or(0);
    let off = PROMPT_OUTLINE.map(|(row, col)| at((row, col, 2)));
    (at, on, off.into_iter().max().unwrap_or(255))
}

/// console_type.py's `console_open`: whether the console's prompt shows in a frame, read at a fixed spot
/// ([`prompt_levels`]): the glyph `CONTRAST` brighter than its own outline, on any background (console_type.py's dark
/// points missed it over a bright sky: live boot 3). ponytail: one glyph at 5.01's spot, unseen in 4.04. At a scale
/// like 1080p's 1.5 the area average thins a one-pixel glyph (the parity case: 151 of 220), so a thinner one there may
/// read as closed. A frame smaller than 720p is read by area too, where cv2 interpolates.
pub fn console_open(bgra: &[u8], w: usize, h: usize) -> bool {
    let (_, on, off) = prompt_levels(bgra, w, h);
    on - off > CONTRAST
}

/// Before Enter: what the prompt's row shows of `line`. None: no prompt shows ([`console_open`]). Else the columns
/// right of the prompt, within `TEXT_PER_CHAR` a character, whose brightest point is `CONTRAST` over their darkest (a
/// typed character is white strokes in a black outline, opaque like the prompt; the background the console lets
/// through is smooth, or dark), and the fewest that `line` lights: one a character, spaces aside (`.` `i` `l` `(`
/// light about one), and 2 at least, over the cursor's one (live boot 2 at 4K: `quenxyz` lit 32, an empty prompt 0,
/// its cursor 85 over the dark; live boot 3 over the sky: a 44-character line lit 183, the same sky with no text 0).
/// ponytail: it catches a line mostly dropped, not a character or two; the bright minimap near column 1120 counts for a
/// line over about 140 characters, and a sharp edge in the scene behind (a roof on the sky) may count too.
pub fn console_text(bgra: &[u8], w: usize, h: usize, line: &str) -> Option<(usize, usize)> {
    let (at, on, off) = prompt_levels(bgra, w, h);
    if on - off <= CONTRAST {
        return None;
    }
    let chars = line.chars().count();
    let end = (TEXT_COL + TEXT_PER_CHAR * chars).min(1280);
    let lit = (TEXT_COL..end)
        .filter(|&col| {
            let levels = TEXT_ROWS.clone().map(|row| at(cell((row, col))));
            let (lo, hi) = levels.fold((255, 0), |(lo, hi), v| (v.min(lo), v.max(hi)));
            hi - lo > CONTRAST
        })
        .count();
    Some((lit, line.chars().filter(|&c| c != ' ').count().max(2)))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn lines(tokens: &[&str]) -> Vec<String> {
        plan(tokens, HOLD_MS, GAP_MS, 0x27)
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .map(describe)
            .collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn tokens_plan_as_w3ctl_does() {
        assert_eq!(
            lines(&["wait:100", "Ctrl+P:150", "up", "console"]),
            [
                "sleep   100 ms  (wait)",
                "key   down  ctrl      sc=0x1D",
                "key   down  p         sc=0x19",
                "sleep   150 ms  (hold)",
                "key   up    p         sc=0x19",
                "key   up    ctrl      sc=0x1D",
                "sleep   400 ms  (gap)",
                "key   down  up        sc=0x48 ext",
                "sleep   200 ms  (hold)",
                "key   up    up        sc=0x48 ext",
                "sleep   400 ms  (gap)",
                "key   down  console   sc=0x27",
                "sleep   200 ms  (hold)",
                "key   up    console   sc=0x27",
            ]
        );
        let sc = |k| scancode(k).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            [
                sc("1"),
                sc("9"),
                sc("0"),
                sc("f1"),
                sc("f10"),
                sc("f11"),
                sc("f12"),
                sc("grave")
            ],
            [0x02, 0x0A, 0x0B, 0x3B, 0x44, 0x57, 0x58, 0x29]
        );
        assert_eq!(lines(&["e:"]), lines(&["e"]));
        for bad in [
            "wait", "wait:", "e:x", "e:+5", "e:1:2", "a++b", "", "f13", "f01", "f0", "nokey",
            "e:60001",
        ] {
            assert!(plan(&[bad], HOLD_MS, GAP_MS, GRAVE).is_err(), "{bad:?}");
        }
    }

    /// The security review: nothing game_keys sends may act on Windows itself.
    #[test]
    fn keys_that_act_on_windows_are_refused() {
        for bad in [
            "win",
            "lwin",
            "rwin:100",
            "lwin+l",
            "win+r",
            "alt+tab",
            "lalt+tab",
            "ralt+f4",
            "alt+f4:50",
            "alt+esc",
            "ctrl+escape",
            "lctrl+lshift+escape",
            "ctrl+shift+esc",
            "ctrl+alt+e",
            "lctrl+ralt+delete",
            "alt+ctrl+t",
        ] {
            let why = plan(&[bad], HOLD_MS, GAP_MS, GRAVE).unwrap_err();
            assert!(why.contains("acts on Windows"), "{bad:?}: {why}");
        }
        // The same keys, apart or with the game's own chords, are the game's.
        for fine in [
            &["alt", "tab"][..],
            &["lalt+e"],
            &["escape"],
            &["ctrl+shift+e"],
            &["lshift+f4"],
            &["ctrl+p"],
            &["ralt"],
        ] {
            assert!(plan(fine, HOLD_MS, GAP_MS, GRAVE).is_ok(), "{fine:?}");
        }
    }

    fn keys(plan: &[Event]) -> Vec<(u16, bool)> {
        plan.iter()
            .filter_map(|e| match e {
                Event::Key { sc, up, .. } => Some((*sc, *up)),
                Event::Sleep { .. } => None,
            })
            .collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn console_lines_open_type_and_close() {
        let plan = console_line("a(B", 0x27, &us_scancode, true).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            keys(&plan),
            [
                (0x27, false),
                (0x27, true),
                (0x1E, false),
                (0x1E, true),
                (0x2A, false),
                (0x0A, false),
                (0x0A, true),
                (0x2A, true),
                (0x2A, false),
                (0x30, false),
                (0x30, true),
                (0x2A, true),
                (0x1C, false),
                (0x1C, true),
                (0x27, false),
                (0x27, true),
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            plan.last(),
            Some(&Event::Sleep {
                ms: SETTLE_MS,
                why: "settle"
            })
        );
        // Live boot 2: every key event of the text is CHAR_MS after the one before (down, 30, up, 30, next, shift
        // too), then the `typed` pause where the prompt row is read, and only then Enter.
        let open = plan
            .iter()
            .position(|e| matches!(e, Event::Sleep { why: "wait", .. }))
            .unwrap();
        let text: Vec<&Event> = plan[open + 1..].iter().take(10 * 2 - 1).collect();
        for (i, event) in text.iter().enumerate() {
            let char_ms = Event::Sleep {
                ms: CHAR_MS,
                why: "char",
            };
            assert_eq!(i % 2 == 1, **event == char_ms, "event {i}: {plan:?}");
        }
        assert_eq!(
            plan[open + 1 + 10 * 2 - 1..open + 1 + 10 * 2 + 1],
            [
                Event::Sleep {
                    ms: SETTLE_MS,
                    why: "typed"
                },
                key("enter", 0x1C, false)
            ]
        );
        // A load's line stops after Enter: its close key would land on the loading screen.
        let load = console_line("a", 0x27, &us_scancode, false).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(keys(&load)[4..], [(0x1C, false), (0x1C, true)]);
        // A line that didn't show: a backspace for each character, then the close; never Enter.
        let clear = console_clear(2, 0x27);
        assert_eq!(
            keys(&clear),
            [
                (0x0E, false),
                (0x0E, true),
                (0x0E, false),
                (0x0E, true),
                (0x27, false),
                (0x27, true),
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(clear[1], clear[3]);
        assert_eq!(
            clear[1],
            Event::Sleep {
                ms: CHAR_MS,
                why: "char"
            }
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            load.last(),
            Some(Event::Sleep {
                ms: ENTER_MS,
                why: "wait"
            })
        ));
        for (bad, named) in [
            ("say('hi')", '\''),
            ("é", 'é'),
            ("a;b", ';'),
            ("x\ty", '\t'),
            ("a@b", '@'),
            ("æøå", 'å'),
        ] {
            let why = console_line(bad, GRAVE, &us_scancode, true).unwrap_err();
            assert!(why.contains(&format!("{named:?}")), "{bad:?}: {why}");
        }
    }

    /// A character is its US virtual key: on a layout that puts VK_OEM_MINUS elsewhere, `-` and `_` go to that key, and
    /// on one without it they are refused before anything is typed.
    #[test]
    fn characters_follow_the_layout_s_virtual_keys() {
        let moved = |vk| {
            if vk == 0xBD {
                Some(0x35)
            } else {
                us_scancode(vk)
            }
        };
        let plan = console_line("a-_", GRAVE, &moved, true).unwrap();
        let typed = &keys(&plan)[2..10];
        assert_eq!(
            typed,
            [
                (0x1E, false),
                (0x1E, true),
                (0x35, false),
                (0x35, true),
                (0x2A, false),
                (0x35, false),
                (0x35, true),
                (0x2A, true),
            ]
        );
        let none = |vk| (vk != 0xBD).then(|| us_scancode(vk)).flatten();
        let why = console_line("a-b", GRAVE, &none, true).unwrap_err();
        assert!(why.contains("'-'") && why.contains("no key"), "{why}");
        assert_eq!(console_vk('q'), Some((0x51, false)));
        assert_eq!(console_vk('Q'), Some((0x51, true)));
        assert_eq!(console_vk('7'), Some((0x37, false)));
        assert_eq!(console_vk('~'), None);
    }

    /// Fills a square of a 3840x2160 frame (top row, left column, side).
    fn fill(px: &mut [u8], (row, col, side): (usize, usize, usize), level: u8) {
        for y in row..row + side {
            px[(y * 3840 + col) * 4..(y * 3840 + col + side) * 4].fill(level);
        }
    }

    /// Fills the 3x3 block of a 3840x2160 frame that is (row, col) at 1280x720.
    fn paint(px: &mut [u8], at: (usize, usize), level: u8) {
        fill(px, cell(at), level);
    }

    /// A 3840x2160 frame of `bg`, with the prompt when `prompt`: its glyph's points at `level`, its outline black, as the
    /// game draws it.
    fn frame(prompt: bool, level: u8, bg: u8) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut px = vec![bg; 3840 * 2160 * 4];
        if prompt {
            for at in PROMPT_ON {
                paint(&mut px, at, level);
            }
            for (row, col) in PROMPT_OUTLINE {
                fill(&mut px, (row, col, 2), 0);
            }
        }
        px
    }

    /// console_type.py's dark points beside the glyph, which quen read until live boot 3.
    const BESIDE: [(usize, usize); 8] = [
        (105, 5),
        (105, 6),
        (105, 7),
        (107, 3),
        (107, 4),
        (109, 5),
        (109, 6),
        (109, 7),
    ];

    /// The sky behind the console's prompt row in live boot 3's outdoor frame, rows 102-112 (its darker band dips at the
    /// prompt): what the translucent console let through, re-created, not copied.
    const SKY: [u8; 11] = [137, 137, 136, 138, 139, 143, 151, 158, 166, 168, 176];

    /// A frame at the levels live boot 3 measured where quen reads, re-created: the glyph's points (224 255 184 255 230
    /// 224 238), its outline (4 4 0 0 0 0 0), over `bg` with the prompt row's band `band` (rows 102-112) when given.
    fn boot3(prompt: bool, bg: u8, band: Option<[u8; 11]>) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut px = vec![bg; 3840 * 2160 * 4];
        for (row, level) in TEXT_ROWS.zip(band.unwrap_or([bg; 11])) {
            px[(3 * row * 3840) * 4..(3 * row + 3) * 3840 * 4].fill(level);
        }
        if prompt {
            for (at, level) in PROMPT_ON
                .into_iter()
                .zip([224, 255, 184, 255, 230, 224, 238])
            {
                paint(&mut px, at, level);
            }
            for ((row, col), level) in PROMPT_OUTLINE.into_iter().zip([4, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]) {
                fill(&mut px, (row, col, 2), level);
            }
        }
        px
    }

    /// The levels console_type.py's points read: the glyph's dimmest, the brightest beside it.
    fn beside(px: &[u8]) -> (i32, i32) {
        let (at, on, _) = prompt_levels(px, 3840, 2160);
        (on, BESIDE.map(|p| at(cell(p))).into_iter().max().unwrap())
    }

    /// Live boot 3: outdoors at dusk the dark points beside the glyph read the sky (up to 137 against the glyph's 184),
    /// so game_load refused a line typed right ("no prompt"), and the check that the console closed read an open one as
    /// closed. The glyph's own outline stays dark there. Its frames' levels, re-created.
    #[test]
    fn the_prompt_shows_over_a_bright_sky() {
        let sky = boot3(true, 137, Some(SKY));
        let (on, by) = beside(&sky);
        assert!(
            on - by <= 100,
            "console_type.py's points read it closed: {on} {by}"
        );
        assert!(console_open(&sky, 3840, 2160), "the outline reads it open");
        // Open indoors (the beside points 33), closed indoors (every point 1-2), closed over the sky.
        assert!(console_open(&boot3(true, 1, None), 3840, 2160));
        assert!(!console_open(&boot3(false, 2, None), 3840, 2160));
        assert!(!console_open(&boot3(false, 137, Some(SKY)), 3840, 2160));
        // The typed line over the sky: each character's strokes white, the sky between. Over the same sky with
        // nothing typed, no column (halfway from the beside points to the glyph, the sky's lower rows counted all 352).
        let line = "quenload(Synthetic_Save_Name_For_The_Sky_Ab)";
        assert_eq!(console_text(&sky, 3840, 2160, line), Some((0, 44)));
        let mut typed = sky.clone();
        for col in (10..10 + 47 * line.len() / 10).filter(|c| c % 5 != 4) {
            paint(&mut typed, (107, col), 255);
        }
        let (lit, least) = console_text(&typed, 3840, 2160, line).unwrap();
        assert!(lit >= least && lit == 165, "{lit} {least}");
    }

    /// The prompt as live boot 2's 4K frames drew it, in shape: the glyph at 184-255, and the bold glyph's inner
    /// corner and right tips lit part way (133, 70, 59), which console_type.py's dark points included.
    fn bold() -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut px = frame(true, 184, 1);
        for (at, level) in [((107, 5), 133), ((106, 7), 70), ((108, 7), 59)] {
            paint(&mut px, at, level);
        }
        px
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_prompt_shows_only_lit_against_dark() {
        assert!(console_open(&frame(true, 200, 10), 3840, 2160));
        assert!(!console_open(&frame(false, 200, 10), 3840, 2160));
        assert!(!console_open(&frame(true, 100, 10), 3840, 2160));
        assert!(console_open(&frame(true, 101, 10), 3840, 2160));
        // Over a white sky the outline stays black: seen. Without the glyph, the sky alone: closed.
        assert!(console_open(&frame(true, 255, 250), 3840, 2160));
        assert!(!console_open(&frame(false, 255, 250), 3840, 2160));
        assert!(!console_open(&[], 3840, 2160));
        // The bold 4K glyph reads as open (console_type.py's points read it as closed: 184 - 133 < 100).
        assert!(console_open(&bold(), 3840, 2160));
    }

    /// Before Enter: the text right of the prompt, counted in lit columns against the fewest the line lights.
    #[test]
    fn the_typed_text_shows_on_the_prompt_row() {
        let text = |px: &[u8], line| console_text(px, 3840, 2160, line);
        let mut px = bold();
        // An empty prompt, its cursor dimmer than halfway (live boot 2: 86): nothing typed shows.
        for row in 103..=110 {
            paint(&mut px, (row, 10), 86);
        }
        assert_eq!(text(&px, "quenload(x)"), Some((0, 11)));
        assert_eq!(text(&px, ""), Some((0, 2)));
        // `quenxyz` as live boot 2 saw it: 33 columns from column 10, all but one lit.
        for col in (10..43).filter(|&c| c != 29) {
            paint(&mut px, (107, col), 250);
        }
        // The minimap's bright pixels far right are beyond the line's columns.
        paint(&mut px, (105, 1124), 255);
        assert_eq!(text(&px, "quenxyz"), Some((32, 7)));
        // A long line of which only those 7 characters arrived: fewer lit columns than characters.
        let long = "quenload(Quen_Typing_Check_0123456789_ABCDEFGHIJ_klmnop-qrstuv)";
        assert_eq!(text(&px, long), Some((32, 63)));
        assert_eq!(
            text(&px, "a b"),
            Some((22, 2)),
            "the window is 8 columns a character"
        );
        // No prompt: nothing to read.
        assert_eq!(text(&frame(false, 200, 10), "quenxyz"), None);
    }
}

```

`crates/quen-core/src/journal.rs`:

```rs
//! The append-only session journal and its replay, against a file-system trait so both run on any OS.
//!
//! A `Step` line is on disk before each action starts and a `Done` line follows it. [`replay`] walks the journal
//! backwards and undoes every started step, but only what still verifies: anything changed since is reported and left
//! as found. A normal `end` is a replay of the live journal, so there is one undo path.

use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::ffi::OsString;
use std::io;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

/// The file operations the journal and its replay need. A path may name a file or (a parked mod) a folder.
pub trait Fs {
    fn read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>>;
    /// Writes a temp file beside `path`, fsyncs it and renames it over `path`: readers see the old bytes or the new.
    fn write_atomic(&self, path: &Path, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()>;
    /// Renames on one volume, keeping the file id. Fails if `to` exists.
    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;
    fn exists(&self, path: &Path) -> bool;
    /// Lowercase hex sha256 of a file's bytes. A real implementation defines it over a folder's whole tree.
    fn sha256(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<String> {
        Ok(sha256_hex(&self.read(path)?))
    }
    /// An opaque identity that a rename on one volume keeps (volume serial and file id on Windows).
    fn file_id(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<String>;
    fn fsync(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;
    /// Sends `path` to the Recycle Bin: nothing is ever deleted for good.
    fn recycle(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;
    /// Copies the folder `from` (on this PC) to `to`, where nothing is, with its whole tree. A flat file system (no
    /// folders, as [`MemFs`]) copies the one entry.
    fn copy_tree(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
        self.write_atomic(to, &self.read(from)?)
    }
    /// A file's last write time, in nanoseconds since 1970.
    fn mtime(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<u64>;
    fn set_mtime(&self, path: &Path, nanos: u64) -> io::Result<()>;
}

pub fn sha256_hex(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    hex(&Sha256::digest(data))
}

/// [`sha256_hex`] of a file, read in 1 MiB pieces: a capture may be gigabytes.
pub fn sha256_file(path: &Path) -> io::Result<String> {
    let mut file = std::fs::File::open(path)?;
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    let mut buf = vec![0; 1 << 20];
    loop {
        let n = io::Read::read(&mut file, &mut buf)?;
        if n == 0 {
            return Ok(hex(&hasher.finalize()));
        }
        hasher.update(&buf[..n]);
    }
}

pub(crate) fn hex(digest: &[u8]) -> String {
    digest.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}

/// One journal line.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "rec", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Record {
    /// On disk before its action starts.
    Step { id: u64, action: Action },
    /// Written after the action with this id finished.
    Done { id: u64 },
}

/// An action, with what replay needs to undo it safely.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "op", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Action {
    /// Copies `src` to `backup`; `sha` is of the bytes copied. Nothing to undo: patches restore from it, and a fully
    /// undone session recycles it.
    Backup {
        src: PathBuf,
        backup: PathBuf,
        sha: String,
    },
    /// Rewrites `path`, backed up earlier in the journal; `mtime` is its write time then (journals before 2026-10-18
    /// have none). Undo: restore the backup, and that write time (feature tests 2: NVIDIA's signed interposer came back
    /// with a new one).
    Patch {
        path: PathBuf,
        sha_before: String,
        sha_after: String,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        mtime: Option<u64>,
        /// Keys whose `Key=Value` lines don't count when the live file is compared with the one put back, and
        /// `[Section]` headers that don't either: a live file that differs only in them isn't kept beside, and a note
        /// says so (dx12user.settings: what the launch wrote and LastGameVersion, findings 35 and 82). Journals before
        /// quen 0.1.8 have none.
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
        ignore: Vec<String>,
    },
    /// Renames `from` (a mod being parked) to `to`. Undo: rename it back.
    Move {
        from: PathBuf,
        to: PathBuf,
        sha: String,
        file_id: String,
    },
    /// A new file about to be written at `path` (a Place's stage, `<dest>.quen-stage`), before it is (a crash
    /// between the write and the Place step left it unjournaled). Undo: recycle it if it is still there with these
    /// bytes; once placed, it is gone.
    Stage { path: PathBuf, sha: String },
    /// Renames a staged new file (this sha and file id) to `dest`, where nothing was. Undo: recycle it.
    Place {
        dest: PathBuf,
        sha: String,
        file_id: String,
    },
    /// A file that may appear at `path`, where none was when the journal began: the log a staged mod may write (the end
    /// copies the boot's logs into the session's game-logs first), or a file wcc_lite writes in the game's documents
    /// folder (script_compile). Undo: recycle it if it is there.
    NewLog { path: PathBuf },
    /// A mod folder about to be copied to `path` (`Mods\<name>`) from this PC, where nothing was at the launch
    /// (finding 38). Undo: recycle it if it is there, a copy cut off by a crash included: its source stays on the PC.
    NewDir { path: PathBuf },
    /// A file the game rewrites by itself during the session, backed up earlier in the journal, with its sha and write
    /// time then: Witcher 3 recompiles its scripts into `content\content0\x64.final.redscripts` when a script mod is
    /// parked (first experiment boot), and reorders the lines of input.settings at every launch (live boot 1). Undo:
    /// the backup back, bytes and write time. With `keep` (input.settings, where the user rebinds keys in the game's
    /// menu), a live file whose lines differ from the backup's in more than their order is first kept beside, as a
    /// patch's is (journals before 2026-10-18 have no `keep`).
    Rebuilt {
        path: PathBuf,
        sha: String,
        mtime: u64,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")]
        keep: bool,
    },
    /// A write into the running game's memory (a cvar's live value, a `mem_patch`). Nothing to undo: the value
    /// lives only in the game process, which every replay path has ended first (it dies with the session's job). The
    /// step is the session's record of it: saves written after `t` (seconds since 1970) are tainted.
    GameMemory { what: String, t: u64 },
}

/// Writes the journal. Each record rewrites the whole file through [`Fs::write_atomic`], so a crash leaves the journal
/// with or without the record, never a torn line.
pub struct Journal<'a> {
    fs: &'a dyn Fs,
    path: PathBuf,
    text: Vec<u8>,
    next: u64,
}

impl<'a> Journal<'a> {
    /// Starts a journal at `path`. Refuses if one is there: replay it first.
    pub fn create(fs: &'a dyn Fs, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Self> {
        if fs.exists(path) {
            let why = format!("{} exists: replay it first", path.display());
            return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists, why));
        }
        Ok(Self {
            fs,
            path: path.to_owned(),
            text: Vec::new(),
            next: 1,
        })
    }

    /// Continues the journal at `path`, which this process writes (a live session's): new steps are numbered after the
    /// ids already there. Refuses a journal whose last line is cut off.
    pub fn open(fs: &'a dyn Fs, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Self> {
        let text = fs.read(path)?;
        if text.last().is_some_and(|&b| b != b'\n') {
            let why = format!("{}: the last line is cut off", path.display());
            return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, why));
        }
        let last = text
            .split(|&b| b == b'\n')
            .filter_map(|line| serde_json::from_slice::<Record>(line).ok())
            .map(|r| match r {
                Record::Step { id, .. } | Record::Done { id } => id,
            })
            .max();
        Ok(Self {
            fs,
            path: path.to_owned(),
            text,
            next: last.unwrap_or(0) + 1,
        })
    }

    /// Puts `action`'s step on disk and returns its id for [`Journal::done`]. Start the action only after this returns.
    pub fn step(&mut self, action: Action) -> io::Result<u64> {
        let id = self.next;
        self.append(&Record::Step { id, action })?;
        self.next += 1;
        Ok(id)
    }

    pub fn done(&mut self, id: u64) -> io::Result<()> {
        self.append(&Record::Done { id })
    }

    /// Takes step `id` back off, before its done line, when its action never happened (the game refused a verb:
    /// feature tests 2c). Refused unless it is the journal's last line, so nothing after it can depend on it.
    pub fn retract(&mut self, id: u64) -> io::Result<()> {
        let body = self.text.strip_suffix(b"\n").unwrap_or_default();
        let start = body.iter().rposition(|&b| b == b'\n').map_or(0, |i| i + 1);
        match serde_json::from_slice(&body[start..]) {
            Ok(Record::Step { id: last, .. }) if last == id => {}
            _ => {
                return Err(io::Error::other(format!(
                    "step {id} isn't the journal's last line"
                )));
            }
        }
        self.fs.write_atomic(&self.path, &self.text[..start])?;
        self.text.truncate(start);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn append(&mut self, record: &Record) -> io::Result<()> {
        let len = self.text.len();
        serde_json::to_writer(&mut self.text, record)?;
        self.text.push(b'\n');
        let written = self.fs.write_atomic(&self.path, &self.text);
        if written.is_err() {
            self.text.truncate(len);
        }
        written
    }
}

/// What a replay did and what it left, newest step first.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct ReplayReport {
    /// One line per action undone.
    pub undone: Vec<String>,
    /// Live files that differed from what quen wrote, kept beside as `<name>.quen-current` (`-2`, `-3`, ... when that
    /// name holds other bytes) before the restore.
    pub kept: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// Steps not undone because their files no longer verify; those files are left exactly as found.
    pub left: Vec<Left>,
    /// Placed files and spent backups, sent to the Recycle Bin.
    pub recycled: Vec<PathBuf>,
    /// Complete journal lines (1-based) that don't parse: any step on them was not undone.
    pub unreadable: Vec<usize>,
    /// A torn last line, interrupted steps, backups kept.
    pub notes: Vec<String>,
}

impl ReplayReport {
    /// Every started step was undone (live files may still have been kept beside: see `kept`).
    pub fn clean(&self) -> bool {
        self.left.is_empty() && self.unreadable.is_empty()
    }
}

/// A step replay left alone, and why.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct Left {
    pub step: u64,
    pub action: Action,
    pub why: String,
}

/// Undoes every started step of `journal`, newest first. A torn last line is ignored with a note: a step's line is on
/// disk before its action starts, so that action never ran. Backups are recycled only when every step was undone.
pub fn replay(journal: &[u8], fs: &dyn Fs) -> ReplayReport {
    replay_with(journal, fs, &|_, _| None)
}

/// [`replay`], where `elsewhere` is asked about a parked file gone from both its names (`from`, the moved file's id):
/// Some(note) says where its data is kept (a mod manager's purge unlinked it, its own copy stays), and the step counts as
/// done with that note.
pub fn replay_with(
    journal: &[u8],
    fs: &dyn Fs,
    elsewhere: &dyn Fn(&Path, &str) -> Option<String>,
) -> ReplayReport {
    let mut report = ReplayReport::default();
    let mut steps = Vec::new();
    let mut done = Vec::new();
    let lines: Vec<&[u8]> = journal.split(|&b| b == b'\n').collect();
    for (i, line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
        if line.trim_ascii().is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        match serde_json::from_slice(line) {
            Ok(Record::Step { id, action }) => steps.push((id, action)),
            Ok(Record::Done { id }) => done.push(id),
            Err(_) if i + 1 == lines.len() => {
                report.notes.push(format!(
                    "line {} is torn (cut off mid-write): ignored",
                    i + 1
                ));
            }
            Err(_) => report.unreadable.push(i + 1),
        }
    }
    for (id, _) in steps.iter().filter(|(id, _)| !done.contains(id)) {
        report
            .notes
            .push(format!("step {id} has no done line: it was interrupted"));
    }
    for (i, (id, action)) in steps.iter().enumerate().rev() {
        if let Err(Why(why)) = undo(fs, &steps[..i], action, elsewhere, &mut report) {
            report.left.push(Left {
                step: *id,
                action: action.clone(),
                why,
            });
        }
    }
    // An atomic write a crash cut off leaves `<path>.quen-tmp` beside a file the journal names.
    for (_, action) in &steps {
        let (Action::Patch { path, .. }
        | Action::Rebuilt { path, .. }
        | Action::Stage { path, .. }) = action
        else {
            continue;
        };
        let mut tmp = OsString::from(path);
        tmp.push(".quen-tmp");
        let tmp = PathBuf::from(tmp);
        if fs.exists(&tmp) {
            match fs.recycle(&tmp) {
                Ok(()) => report.recycled.push(tmp),
                Err(e) => report.notes.push(format!("kept {}: {e}", tmp.display())),
            }
        }
    }
    for (_, action) in &steps {
        let Action::Backup { backup, sha, .. } = action else {
            continue;
        };
        if !fs.exists(backup) {
            continue;
        }
        let spent = report.clean() && fs.sha256(backup).is_ok_and(|s| s == *sha);
        match spent.then(|| fs.recycle(backup)) {
            Some(Ok(())) => report.recycled.push(backup.clone()),
            Some(Err(e)) => report
                .notes
                .push(format!("kept backup {}: {e}", backup.display())),
            None if report.clean() => report
                .notes
                .push(format!("kept backup {}: fails its sha", backup.display())),
            None => report.notes.push(format!(
                "kept backup {}: not every step was undone",
                backup.display()
            )),
        }
    }
    report
}

/// Why a step was left as found.
struct Why(String);

impl From<String> for Why {
    fn from(why: String) -> Self {
        Self(why)
    }
}

impl From<io::Error> for Why {
    fn from(e: io::Error) -> Self {
        Self(format!("I/O error: {e}"))
    }
}

/// Undoes one action if its files still verify. `earlier` are the steps before it, where a patch finds its backup;
/// `elsewhere` is [`replay_with`]'s.
fn undo(
    fs: &dyn Fs,
    earlier: &[(u64, Action)],
    action: &Action,
    elsewhere: &dyn Fn(&Path, &str) -> Option<String>,
    report: &mut ReplayReport,
) -> Result<(), Why> {
    match action {
        Action::Backup { .. } => {}
        Action::Patch {
            path,
            sha_before,
            sha_after,
            mtime,
            ignore,
        } => {
            let (backup, original) = backup_of(earlier, path)?;
            let live = if fs.exists(path) {
                Some(fs.sha256(path)?)
            } else {
                None
            };
            if live.as_ref() == Some(original) {
                return Ok(());
            }
            let bytes = backed_up(fs, backup, original)?;
            // A state this journal didn't write (the game rewrote the file): keep it beside, so neither is lost.
            if let Some(live) = live
                && live != *sha_after
                && live != *sha_before
            {
                let current = fs.read(path)?;
                let counted = |data: &[u8]| {
                    let mut lines = sorted_lines(data);
                    lines.retain(|l| {
                        !ignore.iter().any(|i| i.starts_with('[') && i == l.trim())
                            && !l
                                .split_once('=')
                                .is_some_and(|(k, _)| ignore.iter().any(|i| i == k.trim()))
                    });
                    lines
                };
                if !ignore.is_empty() && counted(&current) == counted(&bytes) {
                    report.notes.push(format!(
                        "{}: the game's copy differed from the one put back only in {}: not kept",
                        path.display(),
                        ignore.join(", ")
                    ));
                } else {
                    keep_beside(fs, path, &current, &live, report)?;
                }
            }
            fs.write_atomic(path, &bytes)?;
            if let Some(mtime) = mtime {
                fs.set_mtime(path, *mtime)?;
            }
            report.undone.push(format!(
                "restored {} from {}",
                path.display(),
```
