```rs
                backup.display()
            ));
        }
        Action::Move {
            from,
            to,
            sha,
            file_id,
        } => {
            if verifies(fs, to, sha, file_id)? {
                // The same file back at its place (a mod manager relinked it): the parked name goes, the data stays
                // linked. ponytail: a folder's id is its own, so a relinked folder still counts as taken; compare its
                // files' ids if a manager's deploy during a session comes up.
                if verifies(fs, from, sha, file_id)? {
                    fs.recycle(to)?;
                    report.recycled.push(to.clone());
                    report.undone.push(format!(
                        "{} was back at {} (the same file, relinked): its parked name recycled",
                        to.display(),
                        from.display()
                    ));
                    return Ok(());
                }
                if fs.exists(from) {
                    return Err(format!(
                        "{} is taken again, the parked copy stays",
                        from.display()
                    )
                    .into());
                }
                fs.rename(to, from)?;
                if let Err(e) = fs.fsync(from) {
                    report.notes.push(format!("fsync {}: {e}", from.display()));
                }
                report
                    .undone
                    .push(format!("moved {} back to {}", to.display(), from.display()));
            } else if fs.exists(to) {
                return Err(format!(
                    "{} changed since it was moved (sha or file id)",
                    to.display()
                )
                .into());
            } else if !fs.exists(from)
                && let Some(note) = elsewhere(from, file_id)
            {
                report.notes.push(note);
            } else if !verifies(fs, from, sha, file_id)? {
                let why = format!(
                    "neither {} nor {} is what was moved",
                    from.display(),
                    to.display()
                );
                return Err(why.into());
            }
        }
        Action::Rebuilt {
            path,
            sha,
            mtime,
            keep,
        } => {
            let same = fs.exists(path) && fs.sha256(path)? == *sha;
            if same && fs.mtime(path)? == *mtime {
                return Ok(());
            }
            if !same {
                let (backup, original) = backup_of(earlier, path)?;
                if original != sha {
                    return Err(
                        format!("the backup of {} is of other bytes", path.display()).into(),
                    );
                }
                let bytes = backed_up(fs, backup, original)?;
                if *keep && fs.exists(path) {
                    let live = fs.read(path)?;
                    if sorted_lines(&live) != sorted_lines(&bytes) {
                        keep_beside(fs, path, &live, &sha256_hex(&live), report)?;
                    }
                }
                fs.write_atomic(path, &bytes)?;
            }
            fs.set_mtime(path, *mtime)?;
            report.undone.push(format!(
                "put {} back as it was before the game rebuilt it",
                path.display()
            ));
        }
        Action::Stage { path, sha } => {
            if fs.exists(path) {
                if fs.sha256(path)? != *sha {
                    let why = format!("{} holds other bytes than quen staged", path.display());
                    return Err(why.into());
                }
                fs.recycle(path)?;
                report.recycled.push(path.clone());
                report.undone.push(format!(
                    "removed the staged {} (Recycle Bin)",
                    path.display()
                ));
            }
        }
        Action::GameMemory { what, .. } => report
            .notes
            .push(format!("{what}: nothing to undo, it ended with the game")),
        Action::NewLog { path } => {
            if fs.exists(path) {
                fs.recycle(path)?;
                report.recycled.push(path.clone());
                report.undone.push(format!(
                    "removed {}, new since the journal began (Recycle Bin)",
                    path.display()
                ));
            }
        }
        Action::NewDir { path } => {
            if fs.exists(path) {
                fs.recycle(path)?;
                report.recycled.push(path.clone());
                report.undone.push(format!(
                    "removed the staged mod {} (Recycle Bin)",
                    path.display()
                ));
            }
        }
        Action::Place { dest, sha, file_id } => {
            if verifies(fs, dest, sha, file_id)? {
                fs.recycle(dest)?;
                report.recycled.push(dest.clone());
                report
                    .undone
                    .push(format!("removed {} (Recycle Bin)", dest.display()));
            } else if fs.exists(dest) {
                return Err(format!(
                    "{} changed since it was placed (sha or file id)",
                    dest.display()
                )
                .into());
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Keeps `live` (the bytes at `path` now, `sha` theirs) beside it as `<name>.quen-current`, or `-2`, `-3`, ... where
/// that name holds other bytes: a kept copy, an earlier session's included, is never replaced. A copy that
/// holds these bytes already is reused.
fn keep_beside(
    fs: &dyn Fs,
    path: &Path,
    live: &[u8],
    sha: &str,
    report: &mut ReplayReport,
) -> Result<(), Why> {
    for n in 1..1000 {
        let mut current = OsString::from(path);
        current.push(".quen-current");
        if n > 1 {
            current.push(format!("-{n}"));
        }
        let current = PathBuf::from(current);
        if !fs.exists(&current) {
            fs.write_atomic(&current, live)?;
        } else if fs.sha256(&current)? != sha {
            continue;
        }
        report.kept.push(current);
        return Ok(());
    }
    Err(format!("{}: 999 kept copies beside it already", path.display()).into())
}

/// A text file's non-empty lines, trimmed and sorted: two files with the same lines in another order compare equal.
fn sorted_lines(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<String> {
    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(data);
    let mut lines: Vec<String> = text
        .lines()
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|l| !l.is_empty())
        .map(str::to_owned)
        .collect();
    lines.sort();
    lines
}

/// The backup of `path` earlier in the journal, and the sha of what it holds.
fn backup_of<'a>(earlier: &'a [(u64, Action)], path: &Path) -> Result<(&'a Path, &'a String), Why> {
    let backup = earlier.iter().rev().find_map(|(_, a)| match a {
        Action::Backup { src, backup, sha } if src == path => Some((backup.as_path(), sha)),
        _ => None,
    });
    backup.ok_or_else(|| format!("no backup of {} earlier in the journal", path.display()).into())
}

/// A backup's bytes, if they still have the sha the journal recorded.
fn backed_up(fs: &dyn Fs, backup: &Path, sha: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Why> {
    match fs.read(backup) {
        Ok(bytes) if sha256_hex(&bytes) == sha => Ok(bytes),
        _ => Err(format!("backup {} is missing or fails its sha", backup.display()).into()),
    }
}

/// Whether `path` exists with this sha and file id.
fn verifies(fs: &dyn Fs, path: &Path, sha: &str, file_id: &str) -> io::Result<bool> {
    Ok(fs.exists(path) && fs.sha256(path)? == sha && fs.file_id(path)? == file_id)
}

/// An in-memory [`Fs`] for tests. Every path is a leaf holding bytes, so a parked mod folder is one entry.
/// `write_atomic` and [`MemFs::put`] make a new file (a new id, and its write time a newer one); `rename` keeps both.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct MemFs {
    state: RefCell<MemState>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
struct MemState {
    files: BTreeMap<PathBuf, (u64, Vec<u8>, u64)>,
    recycled: Vec<PathBuf>,
    next_id: u64,
}

impl MemFs {
    /// Creates or replaces `path` as a new file, as another program would.
    pub fn put(&self, path: impl AsRef<Path>, data: impl AsRef<[u8]>) {
        let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut();
        let id = state.next_id;
        state.next_id += 1;
        state
            .files
            .insert(path.as_ref().to_owned(), (id, data.as_ref().to_vec(), id));
    }

    /// Gives the file at `from` the second name `to`, as a hardlink does: the same id and bytes.
    pub fn link(&self, from: impl AsRef<Path>, to: impl AsRef<Path>) {
        let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut();
        if let Some(file) = state.files.get(from.as_ref()).cloned() {
            state.files.insert(to.as_ref().to_owned(), file);
        }
    }

    /// Every file and its bytes.
    pub fn files(&self) -> BTreeMap<PathBuf, Vec<u8>> {
        self.state
            .borrow()
            .files
            .iter()
            .map(|(path, (_, data, _))| (path.clone(), data.clone()))
            .collect()
    }

    /// What went to the Recycle Bin, in order.
    pub fn recycled(&self) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
        self.state.borrow().recycled.clone()
    }

    fn file<T>(&self, path: &Path, get: impl FnOnce(&(u64, Vec<u8>, u64)) -> T) -> io::Result<T> {
        self.state
            .borrow()
            .files
            .get(path)
            .map(get)
            .ok_or_else(|| missing(path))
    }
}

fn missing(path: &Path) -> io::Error {
    io::Error::new(
        io::ErrorKind::NotFound,
        format!("{} not found", path.display()),
    )
}

impl Fs for MemFs {
    fn read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
        self.file(path, |(_, data, _)| data.clone())
    }

    fn write_atomic(&self, path: &Path, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {
        self.put(path, data);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
        let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut();
        if state.files.contains_key(to) {
            return Err(io::Error::new(
                io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists,
                format!("{} exists", to.display()),
            ));
        }
        let file = state.files.remove(from).ok_or_else(|| missing(from))?;
        state.files.insert(to.to_owned(), file);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn exists(&self, path: &Path) -> bool {
        self.state.borrow().files.contains_key(path)
    }

    fn file_id(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<String> {
        self.file(path, |(id, ..)| id.to_string())
    }

    fn fsync(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
        self.file(path, |_| ())
    }

    fn recycle(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
        let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut();
        state.files.remove(path).ok_or_else(|| missing(path))?;
        state.recycled.push(path.to_owned());
        Ok(())
    }

    fn mtime(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<u64> {
        self.file(path, |&(.., mtime)| mtime)
    }

    fn set_mtime(&self, path: &Path, nanos: u64) -> io::Result<()> {
        let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut();
        let file = state.files.get_mut(path).ok_or_else(|| missing(path))?;
        file.2 = nanos;
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn records_are_one_json_object_per_line() {
        let fs = MemFs::default();
        let path = Path::new("J/journal.jsonl");
        let mut journal = Journal::create(&fs, path).unwrap();
        let action = Action::Move {
            from: "M/a".into(),
            to: "P/a".into(),
            sha: "00".into(),
            file_id: "7".into(),
        };
        let id = journal.step(action.clone()).unwrap();
        journal.done(id).unwrap();
        let text = String::from_utf8(fs.read(path).unwrap()).unwrap();
        let want = concat!(
            r#"{"rec":"step","id":1,"action":{"op":"move","from":"M/a","to":"P/a","sha":"00","file_id":"7"}}"#,
            "\n",
            r#"{"rec":"done","id":1}"#,
            "\n",
        );
        assert_eq!(text, want);
        let first: Record = serde_json::from_str(text.lines().next().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(first, Record::Step { id: 1, action });
    }

    #[test]
    fn journal_refuses_to_start_over_an_old_one() {
        let fs = MemFs::default();
        fs.put("J/journal.jsonl", "");
        let err = Journal::create(&fs, Path::new("J/journal.jsonl"))
            .err()
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(err.kind(), io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists);
    }

    #[test]
    fn mem_fs_keeps_ids_across_renames_only() {
        let fs = MemFs::default();
        fs.put("a", "x");
        let id = fs.file_id(Path::new("a")).unwrap();
        fs.rename(Path::new("a"), Path::new("b")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs.file_id(Path::new("b")).unwrap(), id);
        fs.write_atomic(Path::new("b"), b"x").unwrap();
        assert_ne!(fs.file_id(Path::new("b")).unwrap(), id);
        fs.put("c", "y");
        let err = fs.rename(Path::new("b"), Path::new("c")).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err.kind(), io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists);
        assert_eq!(fs.sha256(Path::new("c")).unwrap(), sha256_hex(b"y"));
        fs.recycle(Path::new("c")).unwrap();
        assert!(!fs.exists(Path::new("c")));
        assert_eq!(fs.recycled(), [PathBuf::from("c")]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sha256_is_lowercase_hex() {
        let want = "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855";
        assert_eq!(sha256_hex(b""), want);
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_open_journal_continues_its_ids_and_game_writes_undo_nothing() {
        let fs = MemFs::default();
        fs.put("M/a", "mod");
        let path = Path::new("J/journal.jsonl");
        let (from, to) = (PathBuf::from("M/a"), PathBuf::from("P/a"));
        let mut journal = Journal::create(&fs, path).unwrap();
        let moved = journal
            .step(Action::Move {
                from: from.clone(),
                to: to.clone(),
                sha: fs.sha256(&from).unwrap(),
                file_id: fs.file_id(&from).unwrap(),
            })
            .unwrap();
        fs.rename(&from, &to).unwrap();
        journal.done(moved).unwrap();
        drop(journal);
        let mut journal = Journal::open(&fs, path).unwrap();
        let what = "cvar Rendering/X set 1".to_string();
        let write = journal
            .step(Action::GameMemory {
                what: what.clone(),
                t: 7,
            })
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(write, 2);
        journal.done(write).unwrap();
        // A step the game refused goes back off; only the last line can.
        let before = fs.read(path).unwrap();
        let refused = journal
            .step(Action::GameMemory {
                what: "channel weather".into(),
                t: 8,
            })
            .unwrap();
        assert!(journal.retract(write).is_err(), "not the last line");
        journal.retract(refused).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fs.read(path).unwrap(), before);
        assert!(journal.retract(refused).is_err(), "gone already");
        let report = replay(&fs.read(path).unwrap(), &fs);
        assert!(report.clean(), "{report:#?}");
        assert_eq!(report.undone, ["moved P/a back to M/a"]);
        assert_eq!(
            report.notes,
            [format!("{what}: nothing to undo, it ended with the game")]
        );

        fs.put(path, "{\"rec\":\"done\",\"id\":1}\n{\"rec\":\"st");
        let err = Journal::open(&fs, path).err().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(err.kind(), io::ErrorKind::InvalidData);
    }

    /// A parked hardlink a mod manager put back at its place (the same file): the parked name goes, the step is done.
    /// One its purge unlinked from both names: done when `elsewhere` knows where its data is, else left.
    #[test]
    fn a_relinked_or_purged_parked_file_is_no_failed_undo() {
        let park = |fs: &MemFs| {
            let (from, to) = (
                PathBuf::from("G/bin/a.dll"),
                PathBuf::from("G/parked/a.dll"),
            );
            let mut journal = Journal::create(fs, Path::new("J")).unwrap();
            let id = journal
                .step(Action::Move {
                    from: from.clone(),
                    to: to.clone(),
                    sha: fs.sha256(&from).unwrap(),
                    file_id: fs.file_id(&from).unwrap(),
                })
                .unwrap();
            fs.rename(&from, &to).unwrap();
            journal.done(id).unwrap();
            (from, to, fs.read(Path::new("J")).unwrap())
        };
        let fs = MemFs::default();
        fs.put("S/a.dll", "dll");
        fs.link("S/a.dll", "G/bin/a.dll");
        let (from, to, journal) = park(&fs);
        fs.link("S/a.dll", &from);
        let report = replay(&journal, &fs);
        assert!(report.clean(), "{report:#?}");
        assert_eq!(fs.recycled(), std::slice::from_ref(&to));
        assert!(fs.exists(&from) && !fs.exists(&to));
        assert!(
            report.undone[0].contains("the same file, relinked"),
            "{report:#?}"
        );
        // Another file at the place: taken, as before.
        let fs = MemFs::default();
        fs.put("G/bin/a.dll", "dll");
        let (from, _, journal) = park(&fs);
        fs.put(&from, "dll");
        assert!(replay(&journal, &fs).left[0].why.contains("is taken again"));
        // Purged: both names gone.
        let fs = MemFs::default();
        fs.put("S/a.dll", "dll");
        fs.link("S/a.dll", "G/bin/a.dll");
        let (from, to, journal) = park(&fs);
        let id = fs.file_id(&to).unwrap();
        fs.recycle(&to).unwrap();
        let left = replay(&journal, &fs);
        assert!(left.left[0].why.starts_with("neither"), "{left:#?}");
        let purged = |path: &Path, file: &str| {
            (path == from && file == id)
                .then(|| "Vortex purged it; deploy in Vortex to put it back".to_owned())
        };
        let report = replay_with(&journal, &fs, &purged);
        assert!(report.clean(), "{report:#?}");
        assert_eq!(
            report.notes,
            ["Vortex purged it; deploy in Vortex to put it back"]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_and_blank_journals_undo_nothing() {
        let fs = MemFs::default();
        fs.put("a", "x");
        for journal in [&b""[..], b"\n", b"\n\r\n  \n"] {
            assert_eq!(replay(journal, &fs), ReplayReport::default());
        }
        assert_eq!(fs.files().len(), 1);
    }
}
```

`crates/quen-core/src/ledger.rs`:

```rs
//! The SQLite ledger (docs/intent.md, "The ledger"): schema and migrations, typed ingest, a read-only query with a
//! time limit, the doc-reference scanner, the cleanup-candidate list, the import of the Python harness's history, and
//! game knowledge: REA's answers as a cache, the RE knowledge base's index, and `about`. It records files by path and
//! sha256 and never deletes one.
//!
//! The schema is `schema/NNNN_*.sql` at the repo root, embedded at build time and applied in order by
//! `PRAGMA user_version`; before the first migration of an existing ledger, a copy at its old version goes to
//! `backups/` beside it. `schema/README.md` describes every table and view for the agents that query them
//! ([`schema_description`]). Every connection sets a busy timeout and `foreign_keys=ON`, and read-write ones use WAL,
//! so several quen processes can share one database.

mod ingest;
mod kb;
mod knowledge;
mod migrate;
pub(crate) mod refs;

pub use ingest::{
    BootEnd, BootModStatus, BootStart, Capture, Claim, Game, LoadStatus, METHOD_FAMILIES,
    Measurement, ModVersion, Outcome, PlayerPose, Pose, Provenance, ReTarget, Row, Save, Sweep,
    SweepFrame, SweepRun, Tag,
};
pub use kb::{KbClaims, KbScan, Section, git_head, sections};
pub use knowledge::{
    About, BundleImport, CaptureRef, Extraction, canonical, extraction_key, profile_digest,
};
pub use migrate::{Harness, Plan, Summary};
pub(crate) use refs::glob;
pub use refs::{Candidate, CaptureRow, Ref, ScanSummary, Scanner};

use std::fmt;
use std::fs::{self, File};
use std::path::Path;
use std::sync::mpsc::{self, RecvTimeoutError};
use std::thread;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use rusqlite::types::{Value as SqlValue, ValueRef};
use rusqlite::{Connection, ErrorCode, OpenFlags, TransactionBehavior};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::Value;

/// The migrations in order: applying entry `i` brings `user_version` to `i + 1`. A shipped one is never edited, only
/// followed by a new one (AGENTS.md; tests/ledger_upgrade.rs pins each file's sha256).
const MIGRATIONS: &[&str] = &[
    include_str!("../../../schema/0001_init.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0002_mods.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0003_harness_info.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0004_claims_strict.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0005_views.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0006_sweeps.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0007_captures_removed.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0008_captures_missing.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0009_knowledge.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0010_saves_made_by_boot.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0011_play_sessions.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0012_pose_yaw_optional.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0013_captures_deleted.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0014_boot_samplers.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0015_mod_kinds.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0016_provenance_other.sql"),
];

/// The schema version this build migrates to.
pub const SCHEMA_VERSION: i64 = MIGRATIONS.len() as i64;

/// `PRAGMA application_id` of a ledger ('quen'), set by the first migration.
const APPLICATION_ID: i64 = 0x7175_656E;

const BUSY_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);

/// Every table and view of the ledger for an agent that queries it: what each holds, its columns, how the rows relate,
/// and example queries for common questions (each runs as is through [`Ledger::query`]).
pub fn schema_description() -> &'static str {
    include_str!("../../../schema/README.md")
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum Error {
    /// Refused after checking, before anything was written.
    Refused(String),
    /// A query ran past its time limit and was interrupted.
    TimeLimit,
    Sqlite(rusqlite::Error),
}

pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Error>;

impl fmt::Display for Error {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Error::Refused(why) => write!(f, "refused, nothing changed: {why}"),
            Error::TimeLimit => f.write_str("query interrupted at its time limit"),
            // Several agents at once: what SQLite's "database is locked" means here.
            Error::Sqlite(rusqlite::Error::SqliteFailure(e, _))
                if e.code == ErrorCode::DatabaseBusy =>
            {
                write!(
                    f,
                    "busy: another connection had the ledger locked (another quen writing, or a program with a \
                     transaction open on it, e.g. a database viewer with unsaved changes), and quen waits up to {} s \
                     for a lock; try again",
                    BUSY_TIMEOUT.as_secs()
                )
            }
            // The callers name the ledger.
            Error::Sqlite(e) => write!(f, "{e}"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for Error {
    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {
        match self {
            Error::Sqlite(e) => Some(e),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

impl From<rusqlite::Error> for Error {
    fn from(e: rusqlite::Error) -> Self {
        Error::Sqlite(e)
    }
}

/// The rows of [`Ledger::query`], as JSON values (a blob becomes lowercase hex).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct Rows {
    pub columns: Vec<String>,
    pub rows: Vec<Vec<Value>>,
}

/// About how many characters of a hit's text [`Ledger::search`] shows, the match in the middle.
const EXCERPT: usize = 120;

/// One value [`Ledger::search`] found: its table, its row's rowid (None in a table `WITHOUT ROWID`), its column, and
/// about [`EXCERPT`] characters of it around the first match, `…` where it was cut.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct Hit {
    pub table: String,
    pub id: Option<i64>,
    pub column: String,
    pub excerpt: String,
}

/// One connection to the ledger. Connections from [`Ledger::open_readonly`] can only read: their writes fail in SQLite.
pub struct Ledger {
    conn: Connection,
}

impl Ledger {
    /// Opens the ledger at `path`, creating it if missing, and migrates it to [`SCHEMA_VERSION`]. Before the first
    /// migration of an existing ledger, it copies it to `backups/quen-v<version>-<UTC time>.db` beside it, and never
    /// deletes a backup. Refuses, before changing anything, a path inside a git work tree (the source tree is one:
    /// AGENTS.md), a database that isn't a ledger, a ledger from a newer quen, and a migration whose backup failed. The
    /// parent folder must exist.
    pub fn open(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Ledger> {
        let path = path.as_ref();
        let abs = std::path::absolute(path)
            .map_err(|e| Error::Refused(format!("can't resolve {}: {e}", path.display())))?;
        if let Some(tree) = abs
            .ancestors()
            .skip(1)
            .find(|dir| dir.join(".git").exists())
        {
            return Err(Error::Refused(format!(
                "{} is inside the git work tree {}; the ledger belongs under the data root",
                abs.display(),
                tree.display()
            )));
        }
        Ledger::init(Connection::open(path)?, Some(&abs))
    }

    /// A private in-memory ledger with the full schema.
    pub fn open_in_memory() -> Result<Ledger> {
        Ledger::init(Connection::open_in_memory()?, None)
    }

    /// A read-only connection to an existing ledger, for `ledger.query` and for quen processes without the lock.
    /// Refuses a database that isn't a ledger, and a ledger from a newer quen.
    pub fn open_readonly(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Ledger> {
        let conn = Connection::open_with_flags(
            path,
            OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY | OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_NO_MUTEX,
        )?;
        configure(&conn)?;
        conn.pragma_update(None, "query_only", true)?;
        let app: i64 = conn.pragma_query_value(None, "application_id", |r| r.get(0))?;
        if app != APPLICATION_ID {
            return Err(Error::Refused("not a quen ledger".into()));
        }
        refuse_newer(conn.pragma_query_value(None, "user_version", |r| r.get(0))?)?;
        Ok(Ledger { conn })
    }

    /// Checks and migrates the database `conn` opened, then fills in extraction rvas (`fill_rvas`); `path` is its file,
    /// where one is to be backed up.
    fn init(mut conn: Connection, path: Option<&Path>) -> Result<Ledger> {
        configure(&conn)?;
        // The checks run under the write lock, so a second quen opening a new ledger at the same time waits, then
        // finds it migrated.
        let tx = conn.transaction_with_behavior(TransactionBehavior::Immediate)?;
        let app: i64 = tx.pragma_query_value(None, "application_id", |r| r.get(0))?;
        let version: i64 = tx.pragma_query_value(None, "user_version", |r| r.get(0))?;
        let empty: bool =
            tx.query_row("SELECT count(*) = 0 FROM sqlite_schema", [], |r| r.get(0))?;
        if app != APPLICATION_ID && !(app == 0 && empty) {
            return Err(Error::Refused("the database isn't a quen ledger".into()));
        }
        refuse_newer(version)?;
        // Testers keep their ledger across quen updates, so an existing one is copied before it migrates. Under this
        // lock: a second quen opening it meanwhile waits, then finds it migrated and backed up once.
        if let Some(path) = path.filter(|_| (1..SCHEMA_VERSION).contains(&version)) {
            back_up(&tx, path, version)?;
        }
        for (done, sql) in MIGRATIONS.iter().enumerate().skip(version as usize) {
            tx.execute_batch(sql)?;
            tx.pragma_update(None, "user_version", done as i64 + 1)?;
        }
        tx.commit()?;
        // Turning WAL on needs the database to itself. Among concurrent first opens of a new ledger (several agents at
        // once), SQLite has answered it BUSY at once, not after the busy timeout (seen twice in thousands of opens).
        // The ledger then stays in rollback mode, as safe but with readers holding writers off, until a later open
        // turns WAL on.
        match conn.pragma_update_and_check(None, "journal_mode", "wal", |r| r.get::<_, String>(0)) {
            Err(rusqlite::Error::SqliteFailure(e, _)) if e.code == ErrorCode::DatabaseBusy => {}
            other => {
                other?;
            }
        }
        let mut ledger = Ledger { conn };
        ledger.fill_rvas()?;
        Ok(ledger)
    }

    /// Runs `f` in one write transaction: everything it wrote stays, or after an error nothing does. The transaction
    /// takes the write lock at once (BEGIN IMMEDIATE): a deferred one that reads first fails with BUSY at its first
    /// write while another connection writes, instead of waiting out the busy timeout. Inside another `atomic` it is a
    /// savepoint. Every read-then-write in the ledger goes through here.
    pub fn atomic<T>(&mut self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Ledger) -> Result<T>) -> Result<T> {
        let outer = self.conn.is_autocommit();
        self.conn.execute_batch(if outer {
            "BEGIN IMMEDIATE"
        } else {
            "SAVEPOINT atomic"
        })?;
        let out = f(self);
        self.conn.execute_batch(match (outer, out.is_ok()) {
            (true, true) => "COMMIT",
            (true, false) => "ROLLBACK",
            (false, true) => "RELEASE atomic",
            (false, false) => "ROLLBACK TO atomic; RELEASE atomic",
        })?;
        out
    }

    /// Runs one read-only `SELECT` or `WITH` statement with positional parameters (`?1`, `?2`, …; null, bool, number or
    /// string) and returns all its rows, or [`Error::TimeLimit`] if it runs longer than `time_limit`. Anything else,
    /// including a `WITH` that writes, is refused unrun.
    pub fn query(&self, sql: &str, params: &[Value], time_limit: Duration) -> Result<Rows> {
        let refused = || {
            Error::Refused("ledger.query runs a single read-only SELECT or WITH statement".into())
        };
        let mut rest = sql.trim_start();
        loop {
            if let Some(r) = rest.strip_prefix("--") {
                rest = r.split_once('\n').map_or("", |(_, r)| r).trim_start();
            } else if let Some(r) = rest.strip_prefix("/*") {
                rest = r.split_once("*/").map_or("", |(_, r)| r).trim_start();
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
        let keyword: String = rest.chars().take_while(char::is_ascii_alphabetic).collect();
        if !keyword.eq_ignore_ascii_case("select") && !keyword.eq_ignore_ascii_case("with") {
            return Err(refused());
        }
        let mut stmt = match self.conn.prepare(sql) {
            Err(rusqlite::Error::MultipleStatement) => return Err(refused()),
            stmt => stmt?,
        };
        if !stmt.readonly() {
            return Err(refused());
        }
        let params = params
            .iter()
            .map(|p| match p {
                Value::Null => Ok(SqlValue::Null),
                Value::Bool(b) => Ok(SqlValue::Integer(i64::from(*b))),
                Value::Number(n) => Ok(n.as_i64().map_or_else(
                    || SqlValue::Real(n.as_f64().unwrap_or(f64::NAN)),
                    SqlValue::Integer,
                )),
                Value::String(s) => Ok(SqlValue::Text(s.clone())),
                _ => Err(Error::Refused(
                    "query parameters are null, bool, number or string".into(),
                )),
            })
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
        let columns = stmt.column_names().into_iter().map(String::from).collect();
        let width = stmt.column_count();
        let to_json = |v: ValueRef<'_>| match v {
            ValueRef::Null => Value::Null,
            ValueRef::Integer(n) => n.into(),
            ValueRef::Real(x) => serde_json::Number::from_f64(x).map_or(Value::Null, Value::Number),
            ValueRef::Text(t) => String::from_utf8_lossy(t).into(),
            ValueRef::Blob(b) => b
                .iter()
                .map(|x| format!("{x:02x}"))
                .collect::<String>()
                .into(),
        };

        // rusqlite's progress handler needs its `hooks` feature, so a watchdog thread interrupts the statement at the
        // deadline instead, unless `done` is dropped first. Both end the statement with SQLITE_INTERRUPT.
        let interrupt = self.conn.get_interrupt_handle();
        let (done, wait) = mpsc::channel::<()>();
        let rows: rusqlite::Result<Vec<Vec<Value>>> = thread::scope(|scope| {
            scope.spawn(move || {
                if wait.recv_timeout(time_limit) == Err(RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) {
                    interrupt.interrupt();
                }
            });
            let rows = stmt
                .query_map(rusqlite::params_from_iter(&params), |row| {
                    (0..width).map(|i| row.get_ref(i).map(to_json)).collect()
                })
                .and_then(|rows| rows.collect());
            drop(done);
            rows
        });
        match rows {
            Err(rusqlite::Error::SqliteFailure(e, _))
                if e.code == ErrorCode::OperationInterrupted =>
            {
                Err(Error::TimeLimit)
            }
            rows => Ok(Rows {
                columns,
                rows: rows?,
            }),
        }
    }

    /// Every text value in every table (not the views, which repeat their rows; not SQLite's own tables) that contains
    /// `text`, case-insensitively for ASCII letters only (SQLite's LIKE), by table, then id. The tables and columns come
    /// from the database itself, so a table a later migration adds is searched too. Each table is one [`Ledger::query`],
    /// within what is left of `time_limit`; [`Error::TimeLimit`] once it is spent. An empty `text` is refused.
    pub fn search(&self, text: &str, time_limit: Duration) -> Result<Vec<Hit>> {
        if text.is_empty() {
            return Err(Error::Refused("the search text is empty".into()));
        }
        let deadline = Instant::now() + time_limit;
        let left = || {
            Some(deadline.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now()))
                .filter(|d| !d.is_zero())
                .ok_or(Error::TimeLimit)
        };
        let columns = self.query(
            "SELECT t.name, t.wr, c.name FROM pragma_table_list AS t, pragma_table_info(t.name) AS c \
             WHERE t.schema = 'main' AND t.type = 'table' AND t.name NOT LIKE 'sqlite\\_%' ESCAPE '\\' \
             ORDER BY t.name, c.cid",
            &[],
            left()?,
        )?;
        let pattern = format!(
            "%{}%",
            text.replace('\\', "\\\\")
                .replace('%', "\\%")
                .replace('_', "\\_")
        );
        let pattern = [Value::String(pattern)];
        let needle = text.to_ascii_lowercase();
        // ASCII lowercasing keeps every byte offset, so the match found in the copy is on char boundaries in `value`.
        let excerpt = |value: &str| {
            let (at, end) = value
                .to_ascii_lowercase()
                .find(&needle)
                .map_or((0, 0), |at| (at, at + needle.len()));
            let side = EXCERPT.saturating_sub(value[at..end].chars().count()) / 2;
            let from = value[..at]
                .char_indices()
                .rev()
                .take(side)
                .last()
                .map_or(at, |(i, _)| i);
            let to = value[end..]
                .char_indices()
                .nth(side)
                .map_or(value.len(), |(i, _)| end + i);
            let cut = |yes: bool| if yes { "…" } else { "" };
            format!(
                "{}{}{}",
                cut(from > 0),
                &value[from..to],
                cut(to < value.len())
            )
        };
        let quote = |name: &str| format!("\"{}\"", name.replace('"', "\"\""));
        let mut hits = Vec::new();
        for table in columns.rows.chunk_by(|a, b| a[0] == b[0]) {
            let name = table[0][0].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
            let id = if table[0][1] == 1 { "NULL" } else { "rowid" };
            let cols: Vec<&str> = table.iter().filter_map(|c| c[2].as_str()).collect();
            let tests: Vec<String> = cols
                .iter()
                .map(|c| {
                    let c = quote(c);
                    format!("typeof({c}) = 'text' AND {c} LIKE ?1 ESCAPE '\\'")
                })
                .collect();
            let values: Vec<String> = tests
                .iter()
                .zip(&cols)
                .map(|(test, c)| format!("iif({test}, {}, NULL)", quote(c)))
                .collect();
            let sql = format!(
                "SELECT {id}, {} FROM {} WHERE {} ORDER BY 1",
                values.join(", "),
                quote(name),
                tests.join(" OR ")
            );
            for row in self.query(&sql, &pattern, left()?)?.rows {
                for (column, value) in cols.iter().zip(&row[1..]) {
                    if let Some(value) = value.as_str() {
                        hits.push(Hit {
                            table: name.into(),
                            id: row[0].as_i64(),
                            column: (*column).into(),
                            excerpt: excerpt(value),
                        });
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(hits)
    }
}

fn configure(conn: &Connection) -> Result<()> {
    conn.busy_timeout(BUSY_TIMEOUT)?;
    conn.pragma_update(None, "foreign_keys", true)?;
    Ok(())
}

fn refuse_newer(version: i64) -> Result<()> {
    if version > SCHEMA_VERSION {
        return Err(Error::Refused(format!(
            "the ledger has schema version {version}, newer than this quen's {SCHEMA_VERSION}"
        )));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Copies the ledger at `path`, at schema version `version`, to `backups/quen-v<version>-<UTC time>.db` beside it, and
/// flushes the copy to disk. `conn` holds the write lock, so the copy is the ledger exactly as the migrations find it;
/// `VACUUM INTO` can't run inside that transaction, so a second connection makes it. The file is created new, so no
/// backup is ever replaced; when the copy fails, the empty or partial file this call created is removed, since it would
/// pass for a backup, and the open is refused.
fn back_up(conn: &Connection, path: &Path, version: i64) -> Result<()> {
    let refused = |e: &dyn fmt::Display| {
        Error::Refused(format!(
            "the ledger at schema version {version} must be backed up before it migrates, and the backup failed: {e}"
        ))
    };
    let dir = path.with_file_name("backups");
    fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(|e| refused(&format!("{}: {e}", dir.display())))?;
    let t: String = conn.query_row("SELECT strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ', 'now')", [], |r| r.get(0))?;
    let to = dir.join(format!("quen-v{version}-{t}.db"));
    let name = to
        .to_str()
        .ok_or_else(|| refused(&format!("{} isn't valid Unicode", to.display())))?;
    let file = File::options()
        .write(true)
        .create_new(true)
        .open(&to)
        .map_err(|e| refused(&format!("{}: {e}", to.display())))?;
    let copy = || -> std::result::Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
        let source = Connection::open_with_flags(
            path,
            OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY | OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_NO_MUTEX,
        )?;
        source.busy_timeout(BUSY_TIMEOUT)?;
        source.execute("VACUUM INTO ?1", [name])?;
        Ok(file.sync_all()?)
    };
    let copied = copy();
    drop(file);
    copied.map_err(|e| {
        let _ = fs::remove_file(&to);
        refused(&format!("{}: {e}", to.display()))
    })
}
```

```rs
//! fields. Times are UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`; the schema refuses any other spelling.

use rusqlite::types::{ToSql, ToSqlOutput};

/// A string enum stored as its name; the schema's CHECK lists the same names (tested in tests/ledger_db.rs).
macro_rules! sql_enum {
    ($(#[$m:meta])* $name:ident { $($(#[$vm:meta])* $var:ident = $s:literal,)+ }) => {
        $(#[$m])*
        #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
        pub enum $name {
            $($(#[$vm])* #[serde(rename = $s)] $var,)+
        }

        impl $name {
            pub const ALL: &[$name] = &[$($name::$var),+];

            pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
                match self {
                    $($name::$var => $s,)+
                }
            }
        }

        impl ToSql for $name {
            fn to_sql(&self) -> rusqlite::Result<ToSqlOutput<'_>> {
                Ok(self.as_str().into())
            }
        }
    };
}

}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct BootEnd {
    pub t_end: String,
    pub outcome: Outcome,
    pub failure: Option<String>,
    /// Every memory patch and data write of the boot, as the journal recorded them.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub patches: Vec<Value>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Capture {
    pub boot_id: Option<i64>,
    /// Relative to the capture root, either separator.
    pub path: String,
    pub sha256: String,
    pub bytes: i64,
    pub kind: String,
    pub method: Option<String>,
    pub encoding: Option<Encoding>,
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "flag")]
    pub includes_overlay: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "flag")]
    pub includes_desktop: Option<bool>,
    pub display_state: Option<Map<String, Value>>,
    pub frame_state: Option<Map<String, Value>>,
    pub pose_id: Option<i64>,
    pub t: String,
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "flag_or_false")]
    pub pinned: bool,
}

/// A flag column: true or false, or 1 or 0 as `ledger_query` shows it (feature tests 2c: a copied row was refused).
fn flag<'de, D: Deserializer<'de>>(d: D) -> std::result::Result<Option<bool>, D::Error> {
    match Option::<Value>::deserialize(d)? {
        None | Some(Value::Null) => Ok(None),
        Some(Value::Bool(b)) => Ok(Some(b)),
        Some(v) if v == 0 => Ok(Some(false)),
        Some(v) if v == 1 => Ok(Some(true)),
        Some(v) => Err(D::Error::custom(format!(
            "{v}: expected true, false, 1 or 0"
        ))),
    }
}

fn flag_or_false<'de, D: Deserializer<'de>>(d: D) -> std::result::Result<bool, D::Error> {
    Ok(flag(d)?.unwrap_or(false))
}

/// The method families a measurement may name: the playbook's list (docs/agents.md §2), one per independent method.
pub const METHOD_FAMILIES: &[&str] = &[
    "presentmon",
    "tracy",
    "nsight",
    "renodx_devkit",
    "screenshot",
    "renderdoc",
    "static_re",
    "mem",
    "files",
    "game_state",
];

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Measurement {

    pub capture_id: Option<i64>,
    pub metric: String,
    pub value: Option<f64>,
    pub unit: Option<String>,
    pub state_label: Option<String>,
    /// A lowercase identifier (`presentmon`, `tracy`, …); claims count distinct families as independent methods.
    pub method_family: String,
    pub tag: Tag,
    pub run_id: Option<String>,
    pub note: Option<String>,
    /// The extraction a static_re (or decompiler) row was read from (schema 0009).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub extraction_id: Option<i64>,
    /// What the world did during the row's window (schema 0011): user, live, paused or photo.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub world: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Claim {

    pub scope: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Deserialize)]

pub struct Pose {

    pub camera: [f64; 3],
    /// Pitch, yaw, roll in degrees.

    pub save_id: Option<i64>,

}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct PlayerPose {

}

/// A camera sweep, stored canonical.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Sweep {

    pub sweep: sweep::Sweep,
    /// The save row its world loads.
    pub save_id: Option<i64>,
    /// The pose row each keyframe was recorded as, in keyframe order and null where none; or empty.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub poses: Vec<Option<i64>>,
    pub note: Option<String>,
}

/// One playback of a sweep.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct SweepRun {
```
