`crates/quen-core/src/protocol.rs`:

```rs
//! The command channel between quen and an in-game end, as JSON lines (docs/intent.md, "The in-game package").
//!
//! Game-neutral: the Witcher 3 end is `W3Quen.asi` + `modQuen` (quen's package, `w3/`), and CET, BG3SE or UE4SS ends
//! can reuse this side.
//! One message per line, newline-terminated. A request is one flat object, the verb's fields beside `id` and `ttl_ms`:
//! `{"id":7,"ttl_ms":2000,"verb":"load","save":"..."}`. Verbs are typed: `exec` names an exec function and its
//! arguments, never a raw console line. Unknown verbs and fields, oversize lines and non-finite floats are refused
//! both ways.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize, de::DeserializeOwned};
use std::fmt;

use crate::sweep::{self, Ease, Keyframe, Mode, Path, Speed, is_default};

/// The longest request line, without its newline. The in-game end reads requests into a buffer of this size.
pub const MAX_REQUEST_BYTES: usize = 4096;
/// The longest reply line, without its newline. Larger than a request: `listsaves` returns every save name.
pub const MAX_REPLY_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Request {
    pub id: u64,
    /// The in-game end drops a request older than this instead of running it late.
    pub ttl_ms: u32,
    #[serde(flatten)]
    pub verb: Verb,
}

/// `pos` and `rot` pass through unchanged, in whatever units the in-game end's scripts take. Verbs without fields are
/// empty structs, not unit variants: serde lets a unit variant of a tagged enum ignore stray fields.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "verb", deny_unknown_fields)]
pub enum Verb {
    /// Load the save whose name matches, case-insensitively, with or without `.sav`.
    #[serde(rename = "load")]
    Load { save: String },
    #[serde(rename = "loadlast")]
    LoadLast {},
    #[serde(rename = "listsaves")]
    ListSaves {},
    #[serde(rename = "cam.get")]
    CamGet {},
    #[serde(rename = "cam.set")]
    CamSet {
        pos: [f32; 3],
        rot: [f32; 3],
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        fov: Option<f32>,
    },
    /// Place the player (it taints later saves).
    #[serde(rename = "teleport")]
    Teleport { pos: [f32; 3], rot: [f32; 3] },
    #[serde(rename = "settime")]
    SetTime { day: u32, hour: u32 },
    #[serde(rename = "weather")]
    Weather { name: String },
    #[serde(rename = "pause")]
    Pause { on: bool },
    /// Load a camera path on the photo-mode camera, replacing a loaded one: `realtime` plays it from the
    /// next tick by local time, `step` (with `fps`) sets frame 0 and holds. The game interpolates the keyframes as
    /// `sweep::Path` does, so they must be canonical (`Path::keys`). At most `sweep::MAX_KEYFRAMES`.
    #[serde(rename = "cam.path")]
    CamPath {
        mode: Mode,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        fps: Option<u32>,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "is_default")]
        speed: Speed,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "is_default")]
        ease: Ease,
        keys: Vec<Keyframe>,
    },
    /// Set frame `n` of a loaded step path, its time `n / fps`; the reply's data is the read-back.
    #[serde(rename = "cam.frame")]
    CamFrame { n: u32 },
    /// Unload the path; the camera stays where it is.
    #[serde(rename = "cam.stop")]
    CamStop {},
    /// Write a new manual save, as the menu's "Empty save slot" does. No fields: a request can't name a slot, a
    /// save type or an existing save, so it can't ask for an overwrite or a quicksave.
    #[serde(rename = "save")]
    Save {},
    /// Read the player's position and heading, the game time (day and hour) and the weather's name; changes nothing.
    #[serde(rename = "world.get")]
    WorldGet {},
    /// Show `text` on screen (the game's notification) for `duration_ms`, 1 to [`MAX_NOTICE_MS`] (from quen-w3 0.1.15;
    /// none: 8 s); changes nothing in the game. 1 to [`MAX_NOTICE_BYTES`] bytes, no control character.
    #[serde(rename = "notice")]
    Notice {
        text: String,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        duration_ms: Option<u32>,
    },
    /// Take the notification down (from quen-w3 0.1.15): its 0.3 s fade starts on the tick that replies.
    #[serde(rename = "notice.hide")]
    NoticeHide {},
    /// Play the game's sound event `event` (from quen-w3 0.1.15), a name as [`crate::trace::plain_name`] checks it.
    #[serde(rename = "sound")]
    Sound { event: String },
    /// Open (`on`) or close photo mode by the game's own functions, never by keys; closing skips its exit dialog.
    #[serde(rename = "photo.mode")]
    PhotoMode { on: bool },
    /// Read photo mode's own state (the reply's data, as after every photo set below); changes nothing.
    #[serde(rename = "photo.get")]
    PhotoGet {},
    /// Photo mode's own weather: a name of the area's list.
    #[serde(rename = "photo.weather")]
    PhotoWeather { name: String },
    /// Photo mode's environment definition, by a path the game lists (`photo.list` envs).
    #[serde(rename = "photo.env")]
    PhotoEnv { path: String },
    /// Photo mode's time of day, `minute` as its menu's slider passes it: minutes of the day, 0 to below 1440.
    #[serde(rename = "photo.time")]
    PhotoTime { minute: f32 },
    /// Photo mode's grading sliders: the ones given, at least one.
    #[serde(rename = "photo.grade")]
    PhotoGrade {
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        exposure: Option<f32>,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        contrast: Option<f32>,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        highlights: Option<f32>,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        saturation: Option<f32>,
        /// Kelvin.
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        temperature: Option<f32>,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        vignette: Option<f32>,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        grain: Option<f32>,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        chromatic_aberration: Option<f32>,
    },
    /// Photo mode's weather (the world's back), env (none) or grading (the sliders as photo mode opened).
    #[serde(rename = "photo.reset")]
    PhotoReset { part: PhotoPart },
    /// Photo mode's one-off world tick and cloth simulation, in seconds, 0 to [`MAX_TICK_S`]: at least one.
    #[serde(rename = "photo.tick")]
    PhotoTick {
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        tick_s: Option<f32>,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        cloth_s: Option<f32>,
    },
    /// The area's weather names or every environment definition's path, those holding `filter` (any case) if given.
    #[serde(rename = "photo.list")]
    PhotoList {
        what: PhotoListed,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        filter: Option<String>,
    },
    /// Add `count` of the item `name` (its own name, spaces allowed) to the player's inventory, as the console's
    /// `additem` does, and with `equip` equip the first; the reply's data reads the item's count back (it taints later
    /// saves). 1 to [`MAX_ITEM_BYTES`] bytes, no control character; `count` 1 to [`MAX_ITEM_COUNT`].
    #[serde(rename = "items.add")]
    ItemsAdd {
        name: String,
        count: u32,
        equip: bool,
    },
    /// Read the alive actors within `radius` of the player, nearest first, at most `max`: each one's position, heading,
    /// velocity, names and flags (the reply's data); changes nothing. `radius` above 0 to [`MAX_ACTORS_RADIUS`], `max`
    /// 1 to [`MAX_ACTORS`]. From quen-w3 0.1.12: only those with `tag`, and with `class` the gameplay entities of that
    /// class instead, actors or not; each with its id. Both names as [`crate::trace::plain_name`] checks them.
    #[serde(rename = "world.actors")]
    WorldActors {
        radius: f32,
        max: u32,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        tag: Option<String>,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        class: Option<String>,
    },
    /// Read what the rendered camera sees (quen-w3 0.1.13): the alive actors within `radius` of the camera, or of `at`,
    /// the player among them, nearest first, at most `max`; with `entity_id` only the entity of that id (`world.actors`'
    /// `id`; the request's own `id` is taken).
    /// Each one projected for the rendered camera, its box's share of the frame, and its first `points` of head, torso
    /// and origin each tested by a ray from the camera. `radius` above 0 to [`MAX_ACTORS_RADIUS`], `max` 1 to
    /// [`MAX_FRAME`], `points` 0 to 3. Changes nothing.
    #[serde(rename = "scene.frame")]
    SceneFrame {
        radius: f32,
        max: u32,
        points: u32,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        at: Option<[f32; 3]>,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
        entity_id: Option<i32>,
    },
    /// Read the ground at points, `xyz` flat (x, y, z per point, 1 to [`MAX_QUERIES`] points): the navmesh z within
    /// `range` of each z, a ray down through that range, the water; with `radius` above 0 whether a navmesh circle of
    /// that radius is free there, with `search` above 0 the nearest safe spot within it. Changes nothing.
    #[serde(rename = "scene.ground")]
    SceneGround {
        xyz: Vec<f32>,
        range: f32,
        radius: f32,
        search: f32,
    },
    /// Cast a ray from a to b per segment (`segments` flat: ax, ay, az, bx, by, bz; 1 to [`MAX_QUERIES`]), or with
    /// `radius` above 0 sweep a sphere of that radius: the first hit. Changes nothing.
    #[serde(rename = "scene.ray")]
    SceneRay { segments: Vec<f32>, radius: f32 },
    /// Test a navmesh lane `width` wide from a to b per segment (as scene.ray's): clear or not, the furthest point
    /// reached towards b, the distance to the nearest obstacle. Changes nothing.
    #[serde(rename = "nav.line")]
    NavLine { segments: Vec<f32>, width: f32 },
    /// Turn the photo-mode camera's no-clip on, or back to what photo mode's menu has.
    #[serde(rename = "cam.noclip")]
    CamNoclip { on: bool },
    /// Run the global `exec function` named `function` with `args`, as the console runs `function(args)` (quen-w3
    /// 0.1.13): W3Quen.asi calls the game's console executor, no console is typed. [`Verb::exec_line`] is the line.
    #[serde(rename = "exec")]
    Exec {
        function: String,
        #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
        args: Vec<String>,
    },
    /// Turn the game's free camera on or off (quen-w3 0.1.17: `EnableFreeCamera`); the reply's data is the free-camera
    /// state, as `freecam.get`'s with a radius of 30.
    #[serde(rename = "freecam")]
    FreeCam { on: bool },
    /// Move the free camera, which must be on, to `pos` facing `rot` (`MoveFreeCamera`); data as `freecam`'s.
    #[serde(rename = "freecam.set")]
    FreeCamSet { pos: [f32; 3], rot: [f32; 3] },
    /// Read the free camera's state: on, its position, the rendered camera's pose, the player's, the pause, and the
    /// alive actors within `radius` (above 0 to [`MAX_ACTORS_RADIUS`]) of the rendered camera and of the player.
    #[serde(rename = "freecam.get")]
    FreeCamGet { radius: f32 },
}

/// What `photo.reset` puts back.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum PhotoPart {
    Weather,
    Env,
    Grading,
}

/// What `photo.list` lists.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum PhotoListed {
    Weathers,
    Envs,
}

/// The longest notice text, in bytes.
pub const MAX_NOTICE_BYTES: usize = 160;
/// The longest notice, in milliseconds: an hour.
pub const MAX_NOTICE_MS: u32 = 3_600_000;
/// The longest `photo.list` filter, in bytes.
pub const MAX_FILTER_BYTES: usize = 200;
/// The longest `photo.tick` time, in seconds (photo mode's menu itself passes 0.00001 s and 1 s).
pub const MAX_TICK_S: f32 = 10.0;
/// The longest `items.add` item name, in bytes.
pub const MAX_ITEM_BYTES: usize = 200;
/// The most of one item `items.add` adds.
pub const MAX_ITEM_COUNT: u32 = 1000;
/// The widest `world.actors` radius, in the scripts' units (metres).
pub const MAX_ACTORS_RADIUS: f32 = 100.0;
/// The most actors one `world.actors` reply holds: 50 of them, the display name cut at 80 characters and the entity at
/// 255 (quen-w3 0.1.11), take about 53 KB at worst (every entity character a `\`, escaped; every name character 3
/// UTF-8 bytes), under [`MAX_REPLY_BYTES`]. Names full of control characters (6 bytes each, escaped) would exceed it:
/// the ASI then answers that the reply is too long.
pub const MAX_ACTORS: u32 = 50;
/// The most entities one `scene.frame` reads: with 3 points, 48 rays in the tick, under the runner design's cap of 64
/// rays a tick (until measured).
pub const MAX_FRAME: u32 = 16;
/// The most points, segments or lanes one `scene.ground`, `scene.ray` or `nav.line` takes: the design's 16 queries a
/// tick.
pub const MAX_QUERIES: usize = 16;
/// `scene.ground`'s widest `range` and `search`, `radius` (metres), and `scene.ray`'s and `nav.line`'s widest.
pub const MAX_GROUND_RANGE: f32 = 100.0;
pub const MAX_GROUND_SEARCH: f32 = 50.0;
pub const MAX_GROUND_RADIUS: f32 = 10.0;
pub const MAX_SWEEP_RADIUS: f32 = 2.0;
pub const MAX_NAV_WIDTH: f32 = 5.0;
/// `exec`: at most this many arguments, each at most `MAX_EXEC_ARG_BYTES`, the whole line at most `MAX_EXEC_LINE_BYTES`.
pub const MAX_EXEC_ARGS: usize = 8;
pub const MAX_EXEC_ARG_BYTES: usize = 100;
pub const MAX_EXEC_LINE_BYTES: usize = 512;

/// An `exec` argument the console's tokenizer reads: printable ASCII without `"` or `'` (it ends a quoted token at
/// either, with no escapes: witcher3-mods re notes/console_exec.md).
fn exec_arg(a: &str) -> bool {
    a.len() <= MAX_EXEC_ARG_BYTES
        && a.bytes()
            .all(|b| (0x20..0x7f).contains(&b) && b != b'"' && b != b'\'')
}

/// An argument passed bare: one the tokenizer reads whole (no space, comma or parenthesis); the rest go in `"`.
fn bare(a: &str) -> bool {
    !a.is_empty()
        && a.bytes()
            .all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"_.+-".contains(&b))
}

/// The coordinates a scene verb passes: finite, inside sweep's world.
fn coords(v: &[f32]) -> bool {
    v.iter()
        .all(|x| x.is_finite() && f64::from(x.abs()) < sweep::MAX_COORD)
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Reply {
    /// The id of the request this answers.
    pub id: u64,
    pub ok: bool,
    /// What happened, or why not.
    pub text: String,
    /// Read-back, such as a camera pose or the save list.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub data: Option<serde_json::Value>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Error {
    /// The line is longer than the cap for its direction.
    TooLong { len: usize, max: usize },
    /// Not one JSON object of the expected shape: bad JSON, a line break inside, an unknown verb or field, a wrong type.
    Malformed(String),
    /// Well-formed, but a value the game must not get: a non-finite float, an hour past 23, an empty name.
    Invalid(String),
}

impl fmt::Display for Error {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Error::TooLong { len, max } => write!(f, "message of {len} bytes, the limit is {max}"),
            Error::Malformed(msg) => write!(f, "malformed message: {msg}"),
            Error::Invalid(msg) => write!(f, "invalid message: {msg}"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for Error {}

/// photo.grade's sliders, in the order the game reads them back (the photo read-back's `grading`).
pub const GRADING: [&str; 8] = [
    "exposure",
    "contrast",
    "highlights",
    "saturation",
    "temperature",
    "vignette",
    "grain",
    "chromatic_aberration",
];

impl Verb {
    /// photo.grade's values in [`GRADING`]'s order, or photo.tick's tick_s and cloth_s; none for another verb.
    pub fn photo_values(&self) -> Vec<Option<f32>> {
        match *self {
            Verb::PhotoGrade {
                exposure,
                contrast,
                highlights,
                saturation,
                temperature,
                vignette,
                grain,
                chromatic_aberration,
            } => vec![
                exposure,
                contrast,
                highlights,
                saturation,
                temperature,
                vignette,
                grain,
                chromatic_aberration,
            ],
            Verb::PhotoTick { tick_s, cloth_s } => vec![tick_s, cloth_s],
            _ => Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    fn check(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let finite = |v: &[f32]| v.iter().all(|x| x.is_finite());
        let name = |s: &str| !s.is_empty() && !s.bytes().any(|b| b < 0x20);
        match self {
            Verb::PhotoWeather { name: s } | Verb::PhotoEnv { path: s } if !name(s) => Err(
                Error::Invalid("an empty name, or one with a control character".into()),
            ),
            Verb::PhotoList {
                filter: Some(filter),
                ..
            } if !name(filter) || filter.len() > MAX_FILTER_BYTES => Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                "a filter is 1 to {MAX_FILTER_BYTES} bytes, no control character"
            ))),
            Verb::ItemsAdd { name: s, count, .. }
                if !name(s)
                    || s.len() > MAX_ITEM_BYTES
                    || !(1..=MAX_ITEM_COUNT).contains(count) =>
            {
                Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                    "items.add: a name of 1 to {MAX_ITEM_BYTES} bytes, no control character, and a count of 1 \
                     to {MAX_ITEM_COUNT}"
                )))
            }
            Verb::WorldActors {
                radius,
                max,
                tag,
                class,
            } if !(*radius > 0.0
                && *radius <= MAX_ACTORS_RADIUS
                && (1..=MAX_ACTORS).contains(max)
                && [tag, class]
                    .iter()
                    .all(|n| n.as_deref().is_none_or(crate::trace::plain_name))) =>
            {
                Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                    "world.actors: a radius above 0 to {MAX_ACTORS_RADIUS}, a max of 1 to {MAX_ACTORS}, and a tag or \
                     class of 1 to 64 letters, digits and _"
                )))
            }
            Verb::PhotoTime { minute } if !(0.0..1440.0).contains(minute) => Err(Error::Invalid(
                format!("photo.time minute {minute}: 0 to below 1440"),
            )),
            Verb::PhotoGrade { .. } | Verb::PhotoTick { .. } => {
                let given: Vec<f32> = self.photo_values().into_iter().flatten().collect();
                let tick = matches!(self, Verb::PhotoTick { .. });
                if given.is_empty() || !finite(&given) {
                    Err(Error::Invalid("no value given, or one not finite".into()))
                } else if tick && !given.iter().all(|s| (0.0..=MAX_TICK_S).contains(s)) {
                    Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                        "photo.tick seconds 0 to {MAX_TICK_S}"
                    )))
                } else {
                    Ok(())
                }
            }
            Verb::CamSet { pos, rot, fov }
                if !finite(pos) || !finite(rot) || fov.is_some_and(|f| !f.is_finite()) =>
            {
                Err(Error::Invalid("cam.set with a non-finite number".into()))
            }
            Verb::Teleport { pos, rot } | Verb::FreeCamSet { pos, rot }
                if !finite(pos) || !finite(rot) =>
            {
                Err(Error::Invalid("a pose with a non-finite number".into()))
            }
            Verb::FreeCamGet { radius } if !(*radius > 0.0 && *radius <= MAX_ACTORS_RADIUS) => {
                Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                    "freecam.get: a radius above 0 to {MAX_ACTORS_RADIUS}"
                )))
            }
            Verb::SetTime { hour, .. } if *hour > 23 => {
                Err(Error::Invalid(format!("settime hour {hour}, past 23")))
            }
            Verb::Load { save: name } | Verb::Weather { name } if name.is_empty() => {
                Err(Error::Invalid("an empty name".into()))
            }
            Verb::Notice { text, duration_ms }
                if text.is_empty()
                    || text.len() > MAX_NOTICE_BYTES
                    || text.bytes().any(|b| b < 0x20)
                    || duration_ms.is_some_and(|ms| !(1..=MAX_NOTICE_MS).contains(&ms)) =>
            {
                Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                    "a notice is 1 to {MAX_NOTICE_BYTES} bytes, no control character, for 1 to {MAX_NOTICE_MS} ms"
                )))
            }
            Verb::Sound { event } if !crate::trace::plain_name(event) => Err(Error::Invalid(
                "a sound event is 1 to 64 letters, digits and _".into(),
            )),
            Verb::CamPath {
                mode,
                fps,
                speed,
                ease,
                keys,
            } => sweep::check_playback(*mode, *fps)
                .and_then(|()| Path::new(keys, *speed, *ease))
                .and_then(|path| {
                    if path.keys() == keys.as_slice() {
                        Ok(())
                    } else {
                        Err(sweep::SweepError(
                            "keyframes not canonical: send Path::keys".into(),
                        ))
                    }
                })
                .map_err(|e| Error::Invalid(format!("cam.path: {e}"))),
            Verb::SceneFrame {
                radius,
                max,
                points,
                at,
                ..
            } if !(*radius > 0.0
                && *radius <= MAX_ACTORS_RADIUS
                && (1..=MAX_FRAME).contains(max)
                && *points <= 3
                && at.is_none_or(|a| coords(&a))) =>
            {
                Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                    "scene.frame: a radius above 0 to {MAX_ACTORS_RADIUS}, a max of 1 to {MAX_FRAME}, points 0 to 3, \
                     an at of finite coordinates"
                )))
            }
            Verb::SceneGround {
                xyz,
                range,
                radius,
                search,
            } if !(per(xyz, 3)
                && *range > 0.0
                && *range <= MAX_GROUND_RANGE
                && (0.0..=MAX_GROUND_RADIUS).contains(radius)
                && (0.0..=MAX_GROUND_SEARCH).contains(search)) =>
            {
                Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                    "scene.ground: 1 to {MAX_QUERIES} points of finite x, y, z, a range above 0 to \
                     {MAX_GROUND_RANGE}, a radius 0 to {MAX_GROUND_RADIUS}, a search 0 to {MAX_GROUND_SEARCH}"
                )))
            }
            Verb::SceneRay { segments, radius }
                if !(per(segments, 6) && (0.0..=MAX_SWEEP_RADIUS).contains(radius)) =>
            {
                Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                    "scene.ray: 1 to {MAX_QUERIES} segments of finite a and b, a radius 0 to {MAX_SWEEP_RADIUS}"
                )))
            }
            Verb::NavLine { segments, width }
                if !(per(segments, 6) && (0.0..=MAX_NAV_WIDTH).contains(width)) =>
            {
                Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                    "nav.line: 1 to {MAX_QUERIES} segments of finite a and b, a width 0 to {MAX_NAV_WIDTH}"
                )))
            }
            Verb::Exec { function, args } => {
                let line = self.exec_line().unwrap_or_default();
                if !crate::trace::plain_name(function)
                    || args.len() > MAX_EXEC_ARGS
                    || !args.iter().all(|a| exec_arg(a))
                    || line.len() > MAX_EXEC_LINE_BYTES
                {
                    return Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                        "exec: a function name of 1 to 64 letters, digits and _, at most {MAX_EXEC_ARGS} arguments \
                         of at most {MAX_EXEC_ARG_BYTES} bytes of printable ASCII without quotes, a line of at most \
                         {MAX_EXEC_LINE_BYTES} bytes"
                    )));
                }
                Ok(())
            }
            _ => Ok(()),
        }
    }

    /// An `exec` verb's console line, as W3Quen.asi builds it from the verb: `function(a, b)`, an argument bare when the
    /// console's tokenizer reads it whole (letters, digits and `_ . + -`), else in `"`. None for another verb.
    pub fn exec_line(&self) -> Option<String> {
        let Verb::Exec { function, args } = self else {
            return None;
        };
        let args: Vec<String> = args
            .iter()
            .map(|a| match bare(a) {
                true => a.clone(),
                false => format!("\"{a}\""),
            })
            .collect();
        Some(format!("{function}({})", args.join(", ")))
    }

    /// The `exec` verb for a console line `function` or `function(a, b, ...)`: each argument bare or in `"` or `'`,
    /// spaces around it dropped. The verb's own checks follow.
    pub fn exec(line: &str) -> Result<Verb, Error> {
        let bad = |why: &str| Error::Invalid(format!("exec line {line:?}: {why}"));
        let line_t = line.trim();
        let name_end = line_t
            .find(|c: char| !(c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_'))
            .unwrap_or(line_t.len());
        let (function, rest) = line_t.split_at(name_end);
        let rest = rest.trim();
        let mut args = Vec::new();
        if !rest.is_empty() {
            let inner = rest
                .strip_prefix('(')
                .and_then(|r| r.strip_suffix(')'))
                .ok_or_else(|| bad("after the name, only (arguments)"))?;
            if !inner.trim().is_empty() {
                for piece in split_args(inner).ok_or_else(|| bad("a quote that doesn't close"))? {
                    let p = piece.trim();
                    let quoted = p.len() >= 2
                        && matches!(p.as_bytes()[0], b'"' | b'\'')
                        && matches!(p.as_bytes()[p.len() - 1], b'"' | b'\'');
                    let arg = if quoted { &p[1..p.len() - 1] } else { p };
                    if !quoted && (arg.is_empty() || arg.contains(['(', ')', '"', '\''])) {
                        return Err(bad(
                            "an empty argument, or one with a parenthesis or quote outside quotes",
                        ));
                    }
                    args.push(arg.to_string());
                }
            }
        }
        let verb = Verb::Exec {
            function: function.into(),
            args,
        };
        verb.check()?;
        Ok(verb)
    }
}

/// `v` holds whole groups of `n` coordinates, 1 to [`MAX_QUERIES`] of them.
fn per(v: &[f32], n: usize) -> bool {
    !v.is_empty() && v.len().is_multiple_of(n) && v.len() / n <= MAX_QUERIES && coords(v)
}

/// The pieces of an argument list between commas outside quotes (a quote runs to the next `"` or `'`, as the
/// console's tokenizer reads it); None if a quote doesn't close.
fn split_args(s: &str) -> Option<Vec<&str>> {
    let (mut out, mut start, mut quote) = (Vec::new(), 0, false);
    for (i, b) in s.bytes().enumerate() {
        match b {
            b'"' | b'\'' => quote = !quote,
            b',' if !quote => {
                out.push(&s[start..i]);
                start = i + 1;
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    (!quote).then(|| {
        out.push(&s[start..]);
        out
    })
}

/// One request line, newline included.
pub fn encode_request(request: &Request) -> Result<String, Error> {
    request.verb.check()?;
    encode(request, MAX_REQUEST_BYTES)
}

/// A request from one line, with or without its newline.
pub fn decode_request(line: &str) -> Result<Request, Error> {
    let request: Request = decode(line, MAX_REQUEST_BYTES)?;
    request.verb.check()?;
    Ok(request)
}

/// One reply line, newline included.
pub fn encode_reply(reply: &Reply) -> Result<String, Error> {
    encode(reply, MAX_REPLY_BYTES)
}

/// A reply from one line, with or without its newline.
pub fn decode_reply(line: &str) -> Result<Reply, Error> {
    decode(line, MAX_REPLY_BYTES)
}

fn encode<T: Serialize>(message: &T, max: usize) -> Result<String, Error> {
    let mut line = serde_json::to_string(message).map_err(|e| Error::Malformed(e.to_string()))?;
    if line.len() > max {
        return Err(Error::TooLong {
            len: line.len(),
            max,
        });
    }
    line.push('\n');
    Ok(line)
}

fn decode<T: DeserializeOwned>(line: &str, max: usize) -> Result<T, Error> {
    let line = line.strip_suffix('\n').unwrap_or(line);
    let line = line.strip_suffix('\r').unwrap_or(line);
    if line.len() > max {
        return Err(Error::TooLong {
            len: line.len(),
            max,
        });
    }
    if line.contains('\n') {
        return Err(Error::Malformed("a line break inside the message".into()));
    }
    serde_json::from_str(line).map_err(|e| Error::Malformed(e.to_string()))
}

    /// The exec verb's line, as W3Quen.asi builds it (test.cpp checks the same lines), and the verb read from a console
    /// line: arguments bare or quoted, spaces dropped.
    #[test]
    fn exec_lines_round_trip_between_console_text_and_the_verb() {
        let exec = |f: &str, args: &[&str]| Verb::Exec {
            function: f.into(),
            args: args.iter().map(|a| a.to_string()).collect(),
        };
        assert_eq!(exec("npcavoid", &[]).exec_line().unwrap(), "npcavoid()");
        assert_eq!(
            exec("addset", &["EIST_Wolf", "true", "a b", "", "1.5e-3", "x,y"])
                .exec_line()
                .unwrap(),
            r#"addset(EIST_Wolf, true, "a b", "", 1.5e-3, "x,y")"#
        );
        assert_eq!(Verb::CamGet {}.exec_line(), None);
        for (line, want) in [
            ("npcavoid()", exec("npcavoid", &[])),
            ("  npcavoid  ", exec("npcavoid", &[])),
            ("settime(1,22)", exec("settime", &["1", "22"])),
            (
                "addset( EIST_Wolf , true )",
                exec("addset", &["EIST_Wolf", "true"]),
            ),
            (
                r#"say("hello, world", 'x y', "")"#,
                exec("say", &["hello, world", "x y", ""]),
            ),
            ("f(  )", exec("f", &[])),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(Verb::exec(line).unwrap(), want, "{line}");
        }
        for line in [
            "",
            "(1)",
            "f(1",
            "f 1",
            "f(1) x",
            "f(,1)",
            "f(1,)",
            r#"f("a)"#,
            r#"f("a'b")"#,
            r#"f("a"b)"#,
            "f(a(b))",
            "f(\u{e9})",
            "f(a\tb)",
            "two words",
            &"n".repeat(65),
            &format!("f({})", ["1"; MAX_EXEC_ARGS + 1].join(",")),
            &format!("f({})", "x".repeat(MAX_EXEC_ARG_BYTES + 1)),
        ] {
            assert!(
                matches!(Verb::exec(line), Err(Error::Invalid(_))),
                "{line:?}: {:?}",
                Verb::exec(line)
            );
        }
        // Every argument within its cap, the line over its own: 8 quoted arguments of 99 bytes make 825.
        let arg = "a b".repeat(33);
        let long = exec("f", &[arg.as_str(); MAX_EXEC_ARGS]);
        assert!(matches!(
            encode_request(&request(long)),
            Err(Error::Invalid(_))
        ));
    }

    /// The scene verbs' caps: the runner design's 16 queries and 64 rays a tick.
    #[test]
    fn scene_verbs_refuse_past_their_caps() {
        let invalid = |verb: Verb| {
            let req = request(verb);
            assert!(
                matches!(encode_request(&req), Err(Error::Invalid(_))),
                "{req:?}"
            );
        };
        let frame = |radius: f32, max: u32, points: u32, at: Option<[f32; 3]>| Verb::SceneFrame {
            radius,
            max,
            points,
            at,
            entity_id: None,
        };
        for verb in [
            frame(0.0, 1, 0, None),
            frame(100.5, 1, 0, None),
            frame(f32::NAN, 1, 0, None),
            frame(10.0, 0, 0, None),
            frame(10.0, MAX_FRAME + 1, 0, None),
            frame(10.0, 1, 4, None),
            frame(10.0, 1, 0, Some([f32::INFINITY, 0.0, 0.0])),
            frame(10.0, 1, 0, Some([1e6, 0.0, 0.0])),
        ] {
            invalid(verb);
        }
        const { assert!(MAX_FRAME * 3 <= 64, "rays a tick") };
        let ground = |xyz: Vec<f32>, range: f32, radius: f32, search: f32| Verb::SceneGround {
            xyz,
            range,
            radius,
            search,
        };
        for verb in [
            ground(vec![], 10.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            ground(vec![1.0, 2.0], 10.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            ground(vec![0.0; 3 * (MAX_QUERIES + 1)], 10.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            ground(vec![0.0, 0.0, f32::NAN], 10.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            ground(vec![0.0; 3], 0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            ground(vec![0.0; 3], 100.5, 0.0, 0.0),
            ground(vec![0.0; 3], 10.0, -0.1, 0.0),
            ground(vec![0.0; 3], 10.0, 10.5, 0.0),
            ground(vec![0.0; 3], 10.0, 0.5, 50.5),
        ] {
            invalid(verb);
        }
        for segments in [vec![], vec![0.0; 5], vec![0.0; 6 * (MAX_QUERIES + 1)]] {
            invalid(Verb::SceneRay {
                segments: segments.clone(),
                radius: 0.0,
            });
            invalid(Verb::NavLine {
                segments,
                width: 0.5,
            });
        }
        invalid(Verb::SceneRay {
            segments: vec![0.0; 6],
            radius: 2.5,
        });
        invalid(Verb::NavLine {
            segments: vec![0.0; 6],
            width: -1.0,
        });
        let full = Verb::SceneGround {
            xyz: vec![-99_999.99; 3 * MAX_QUERIES],
            range: 10.0,
            radius: 0.5,
            search: 50.0,
        };
        assert!(encode_request(&request(full)).is_ok());
    }

    /// A photo.grade of exposure and temperature only.

        Verb::PhotoGrade {
            exposure,
            contrast: None,
            highlights: None,
            saturation: None,
            temperature,
            vignette: None,
            grain: None,
            chromatic_aberration: None,
        }
    }

    /// The photo verbs' wire shapes, as W3Quen.asi's test sends them; the values photo.grade and photo.tick give.
    #[test]
    fn photo_verbs_are_flat_and_leave_out_what_is_not_given() {
        let line = |verb| encode_request(&request(verb)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            line(photo_grade(Some(0.5), Some(6550.0))),
            "{\"id\":7,\"ttl_ms\":2000,\"verb\":\"photo.grade\",\"exposure\":0.5,\"temperature\":6550.0}\n"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            line(Verb::PhotoReset {
                part: PhotoPart::Weather
            }),
            "{\"id\":7,\"ttl_ms\":2000,\"verb\":\"photo.reset\",\"part\":\"weather\"}\n"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            line(Verb::PhotoList {
                what: PhotoListed::Weathers,
                filter: None
            }),
            "{\"id\":7,\"ttl_ms\":2000,\"verb\":\"photo.list\",\"what\":\"weathers\"}\n"
        );
        let mut want = vec![None; 8];
        want[0] = Some(0.5);
        want[4] = Some(6550.0);
        assert_eq!(photo_grade(Some(0.5), Some(6550.0)).photo_values(), want);
        assert_eq!(GRADING[4], "temperature");
        assert!(Verb::PhotoGet {}.photo_values().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn photo_verbs_refuse_what_the_game_must_not_get() {
        let invalid = |verb: Verb| {
            let req = request(verb);
            assert!(
                matches!(encode_request(&req), Err(Error::Invalid(_))),
                "{req:?}"
            );
            // serde_json writes a non-finite number as null, which doesn't decode at all.
            let line = serde_json::to_string(&req).unwrap();
            assert!(decode_request(&line).is_err(), "{line}");
        };
        invalid(Verb::PhotoWeather {
            name: String::new(),
        });
        invalid(Verb::PhotoEnv {
            path: "a\tb".into(),
        });
        for minute in [-0.5, 1440.0, f32::NAN, f32::INFINITY] {
            invalid(Verb::PhotoTime { minute });
        }
        invalid(photo_grade(None, None));
        invalid(photo_grade(Some(f32::NAN), None));

```

`crates/quen-core/src/reshade.rs`:

```rs
//! Checked edits of a ReShade-style ini (ReShade.ini, its RenoDX add-on sections), byte-identical to the harness's
//! `ini_writer.set_values`: only the named keys' lines of one `[section]` change, each keeping its own line ending, and a
//! missing key (or section) is refused, skipped or appended, as asked. Values are written as RenoDX and ReShade write
//! them.

/// A value to write: a number (formatted like `std::to_chars(float)`) or a one-line string.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub enum Value<'a> {
    Number(f64),
    Text(&'a str),
}

/// ReShade's line trim: around a line, before it decides what the line is.
const WS: &[char] = &[' ', '\t', '\r', '\n'];

/// The shortest text that reads back as the same `f32`, integers without `.0`: `100`, `0.8`, `1e-05`.
pub fn number(v: f64) -> Result<String, String> {
    if !v.is_finite() {
        return Err(format!("non-finite value {v}"));
    }
    if v.fract() == 0.0 && v.abs() < (1 << 24) as f64 {
        return Ok(format!("{}", v as i64));
    }
    let f32 = v as f32;
    for p in 1..10 {
        let s = general(v, p);
        if s.parse::<f64>().is_ok_and(|back| back as f32 == f32) {
            return Ok(s);
        }
    }
    Ok(format!("{f32:?}"))
}

/// Python's `f"{v:.{p}g}"` for a finite `v` and `p >= 1`: `p` significant digits, fixed while the exponent is in
/// `-4..p`, else `d.ddde-XX`; trailing zeros and a bare point dropped.
fn general(v: f64, p: usize) -> String {
    let sci = format!("{:.*e}", p - 1, v);
    let (mantissa, exp) = sci.split_once('e').expect("{:e} has an exponent");
    let exp: i32 = exp.parse().expect("{:e}'s exponent is a number");
    let trim = |s: &str| {
        if s.contains('.') {
            s.trim_end_matches('0').trim_end_matches('.').to_owned()
        } else {
            s.to_owned()
        }
    };
    if (-4..p as i32).contains(&exp) {
        trim(&format!("{:.*}", (p as i32 - 1 - exp) as usize, v))
    } else {
        let sign = if exp < 0 { '-' } else { '+' };
        format!("{}e{sign}{:02}", trim(mantissa), exp.abs())
    }
}

fn written(value: Value) -> Result<String, String> {
    match value {
        Value::Number(v) => number(v),
        Value::Text(s) if s.contains(['\r', '\n', '\0']) || s != s.trim_matches([' ', '\t']) => {
            Err(format!("string value {s:?}: one line, no edge spaces"))
        }
        Value::Text(s) => Ok(s.into()),
    }
}

/// What a line is to ReShade: `None` for a blank or comment line (`;`, `/`, `#`), a section header's name, or a key.
#[derive(PartialEq)]
enum Kind<'a> {
    Section(&'a str),
    Key(&'a str),
}

fn kind(line: &str) -> Option<Kind<'_>> {
    let s = line.trim_matches(WS);
    match s.chars().next()? {
        ';' | '/' | '#' => None,
        '[' => {
            let name = s.find(']').map_or(s, |at| &s[..at]);
            Some(Kind::Section(name.trim_matches([' ', '\t', '[', ']'])))
        }
        _ => Some(Kind::Key(
            s.split_once('=')
                .map_or(s, |(k, _)| k)
                .trim_matches([' ', '\t']),
        )),
    }
}

/// Python's `str.splitlines(keepends=True)`: each line with its own break.
fn split_lines(text: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    let breaks = [
        '\n', '\r', '\u{b}', '\u{c}', '\u{1c}', '\u{1d}', '\u{1e}', '\u{85}', '\u{2028}',
        '\u{2029}',
    ];
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut start = 0;
    let mut chars = text.char_indices().peekable();
    while let Some((i, c)) = chars.next() {
        if !breaks.contains(&c) {
            continue;
        }
        let mut end = i + c.len_utf8();
        if c == '\r' && chars.peek().is_some_and(|&(_, n)| n == '\n') {
            chars.next();
            end += 1;
        }
        out.push(&text[start..end]);
        start = end;
    }
    if start < text.len() {
        out.push(&text[start..]);
    }
    out
}

/// What [`set_values`] does with a key its `[section]` doesn't have.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub enum Missing {
    /// Refuses, as it does a missing section.
    Refuse,
    /// Appends the key after the section's last non-blank line.
    Add,
    /// The same, a missing section first appended at the end of the file.
    AddSection,
    /// Leaves the key out; a missing section leaves the file as it is.
    Skip,
}

/// Sets `values` (in order) in the one `[section]` of `data`. A section appearing twice, or a key starting two lines
/// there, is refused; a missing one is handled as `missing` says. A UTF-8 BOM and every other byte stay.
pub fn set_values(
    data: &[u8],
    section: &str,
    values: &[(&str, Value)],
    missing: Missing,
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    if values.is_empty() {
        return Err("no values".into());
    }
    let bom: &[u8] = if data.starts_with(b"\xef\xbb\xbf") {
        b"\xef\xbb\xbf"
    } else {
        b""
    };
    let text = std::str::from_utf8(&data[bom.len()..]).map_err(|e| format!("not UTF-8: {e}"))?;
    let lines = split_lines(text);
    let nl = if text.contains("\r\n") { "\r\n" } else { "\n" };
    let heads: Vec<usize> = (0..lines.len())
        .filter(|&i| kind(lines[i]) == Some(Kind::Section(section)))
        .collect();
    let head = match heads[..] {
        [head] => head,
        [] if missing == Missing::Skip => return Ok(data.to_vec()),
        [] if missing == Missing::AddSection => {
            let mut out = data.to_vec();
            if !text.is_empty() && !text.ends_with(['\n', '\r']) {
                out.extend(nl.as_bytes());
            }
            out.extend(format!("[{section}]{nl}").bytes());
            // A name that doesn't read back as `[section]` is refused here: found 0 times.
            return set_values(&out, section, values, Missing::Add);
        }
        _ => return Err(format!("[{section}] found {} times", heads.len())),
    };
    let start = head + 1;
    let end = (start..lines.len())
        .find(|&i| matches!(kind(lines[i]), Some(Kind::Section(_))))
        .unwrap_or(lines.len());
    let mut new: Vec<String> = lines.iter().map(|l| (*l).to_owned()).collect();
    let mut inserts = Vec::new();
    for &(key, value) in values {
        if key.is_empty()
            || key != key.trim_matches(WS)
            || key.contains(['=', '[', ']', '\r', '\n', ';', '#', '/'])
        {
            return Err(format!("bad key {key:?}"));
        }
        let value = written(value)?;
        let hits: Vec<usize> = (start..end)
            .filter(|&i| kind(lines[i]) == Some(Kind::Key(key)))
            .collect();
        match hits[..] {
            [i] => {
                let body = lines[i].trim_end_matches(['\r', '\n']);
                new[i] = format!("{key}={value}{}", &lines[i][body.len()..]);
            }
            [] => match missing {
                Missing::Refuse => return Err(format!("{key} not in [{section}]")),
                Missing::Add | Missing::AddSection => inserts.push(format!("{key}={value}")),
                Missing::Skip => {}
            },
            _ => return Err(format!("{key} appears {} times in [{section}]", hits.len())),
        }
    }
    if !inserts.is_empty() {
        let last = (start..end)
            .rev()
            .find(|&i| !lines[i].trim_matches(WS).is_empty());
        let at = last.unwrap_or(head) + 1;
        if !new[at - 1].ends_with(['\n', '\r']) {
            new[at - 1].push_str(nl);
        }
        new.splice(at..at, inserts.into_iter().map(|line| line + nl));
    }
    let mut out = bom.to_vec();
    out.extend(new.concat().into_bytes());
    Ok(out)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn numbers_are_the_shortest_f32_text() {
        let cases = [
            (100.0, "100"),
            (0.8, "0.8"),
            (0.75, "0.75"),
            (1e-5, "1e-05"),
            (-2.0, "-2"),
            (0.30000001192092896, "0.3"),
            (-0.0, "0"),
            (16777216.0, "16777216"),
            (1.5e10, "1.5e+10"),
            (123456.7, "123456.7"),
            (0.0001, "0.0001"),
            (0.00012, "0.00012"),
            (1.23456789, "1.2345679"),
            (1e-7, "1e-07"),
            (1234567.89, "1234567.9"),
            (99999.99, "99999.99"),
            (1e20, "1e+20"),
            (-0.000123456, "-0.000123456"),
        ];
        // The expected texts are what ini_writer.fmt printed for these values.
        for (v, want) in cases {
            assert_eq!(number(v).unwrap(), want, "{v}");
        }
        assert!(number(f64::NAN).is_err() && number(f64::INFINITY).is_err());
        assert!(written(Value::Text("a\nb")).is_err() && written(Value::Text(" x")).is_err());
        assert_eq!(written(Value::Text("")).unwrap(), "");
    }

    const INI: &str = "\u{feff}[ADDON]\r\nLoadFromDllMain=\r\n\r\n[renodx]\r\n ; note\r\nSettingsMode=1\r\n\r\n\
                       [renodx-preset1]\r\nToneMapGameNits=203\r\n  Black = 0 \r\n\r\n[OTHER]\r\nToneMapGameNits=1\r\n";

    fn set(section: &str, values: &[(&str, Value)], missing: Missing) -> Result<String, String> {
        set_values(INI.as_bytes(), section, values, missing).map(|b| String::from_utf8(b).unwrap())
    }

    #[test]
    fn edits_only_the_named_lines_of_one_section() {
        let out = set(
            "renodx-preset1",
            &[("ToneMapGameNits", Value::Number(250.0))],
            Missing::Refuse,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            out,
            INI.replace("ToneMapGameNits=203", "ToneMapGameNits=250")
        );
        // A key line with spaces around `=` is rewritten as Key=value, its line ending kept.
        let out = set(
            "renodx-preset1",
            &[("Black", Value::Number(0.5))],
            Missing::Refuse,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, INI.replace("  Black = 0 \r\n", "Black=0.5\r\n"));
        let path = r"devkit\renodx-devkit.addon64";
        let out = set(
            "ADDON",
            &[("LoadFromDllMain", Value::Text(path))],
            Missing::Refuse,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            out,
            INI.replace(
                "LoadFromDllMain=\r\n",
                &format!("LoadFromDllMain={path}\r\n")
            )
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_missing_key_is_appended_after_the_last_non_blank_line() {
        let out = set(
            "renodx",
            &[("DevAutoReload", Value::Number(1.0))],
            Missing::Add,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            out,
            INI.replace(
                "SettingsMode=1\r\n",
                "SettingsMode=1\r\nDevAutoReload=1\r\n"
            )
        );
        // At the end of a file without a final line break, the break is added first.
        let data = "[A]\nX=1";
        let out = set_values(
            data.as_bytes(),
            "A",
            &[("Y", Value::Number(2.0))],
            Missing::Add,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, b"[A]\nX=1\nY=2\n");
        let out = set_values(b"[A]\n", "A", &[("Y", Value::Number(2.0))], Missing::Add).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, b"[A]\nY=2\n");
    }

    #[test]
    fn refuses_on_any_doubt() {
        assert!(
            set(
                "renodx",
                &[("DevAutoReload", Value::Number(1.0))],
                Missing::Refuse
            )
            .is_err()
        );
        assert!(set("nope", &[("X", Value::Number(1.0))], Missing::Add).is_err());
        assert!(set("renodx", &[("A=B", Value::Number(1.0))], Missing::Add).is_err());
        assert!(set("renodx", &[], Missing::Add).is_err());
        let twice = "[A]\nX=1\nX=2\n";
        assert!(
            set_values(
                twice.as_bytes(),
                "A",
                &[("X", Value::Number(3.0))],
                Missing::Refuse
            )
            .is_err()
        );
        let heads = "[A]\nX=1\n[A]\n";
        for missing in [
            Missing::Refuse,
            Missing::Add,
            Missing::AddSection,
            Missing::Skip,
        ] {
            let err = set_values(heads.as_bytes(), "A", &[("X", Value::Number(3.0))], missing);
            assert_eq!(err.unwrap_err(), "[A] found 2 times", "{missing:?}");
        }
    }

    /// Live 2026-10-22: a ReShade.ini as ReShade writes it fresh has no [ADDON].
    #[test]
    fn a_missing_section_or_key_is_skipped_or_added() {
        const FRESH: &str = "\u{feff}[GENERAL]\r\nPresetPath=.\\ReShadePreset.ini\r\n";
        let key = [("LoadFromDllMain", Value::Text(r"devkit\x.addon64"))];
        let empty = [("LoadFromDllMain", Value::Text(""))];
        let set = |data: &str, values: &[(&str, Value)], missing| {
            set_values(data.as_bytes(), "ADDON", values, missing)
                .map(|b| String::from_utf8(b).unwrap())
        };
        let no_key = "\u{feff}[ADDON]\r\nOther=1\r\n\r\n[GENERAL]\r\n";
        for data in [FRESH, no_key] {
            assert_eq!(set(data, &empty, Missing::Skip).unwrap(), data);
        }
        // The BOM and CRLF kept; the section at the end, the key after the section's last non-blank line.
        assert_eq!(
            set(FRESH, &key, Missing::AddSection).unwrap(),
            format!("{FRESH}[ADDON]\r\nLoadFromDllMain=devkit\\x.addon64\r\n")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            set(no_key, &key, Missing::AddSection).unwrap(),
            no_key.replace(
                "Other=1\r\n",
                "Other=1\r\nLoadFromDllMain=devkit\\x.addon64\r\n"
            )
        );
        assert_eq!(
            set("X=1", &key, Missing::AddSection).unwrap(),
            "X=1\n[ADDON]\nLoadFromDllMain=devkit\\x.addon64\n"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            set("", &key, Missing::AddSection).unwrap(),
            "[ADDON]\nLoadFromDllMain=devkit\\x.addon64\n"
        );
        assert!(set(FRESH, &key, Missing::Add).is_err());
        // A section name that doesn't read back as itself is refused.
        let odd = set_values(FRESH.as_bytes(), "A]B", &key, Missing::AddSection);
        assert_eq!(odd.unwrap_err(), "[A]B] found 0 times");
    }

    #[test]
    fn lines_split_as_python_splits_them() {
        assert_eq!(split_lines("a\r\nb\rc\nd"), ["a\r\n", "b\r", "c\n", "d"]);
        assert_eq!(split_lines("a\u{2028}b\u{c}"), ["a\u{2028}", "b\u{c}"]);
        assert!(split_lines("").is_empty());
    }
}
```

`crates/quen-core/src/saves.rs`:

```rs
//! The user's saves. A snapshot of the gamesaves folder (names, sizes, write times) and what changed between two,
//! the guard ported from ini_session.py's `guard_saves`, the wait for the folder to go quiet before a kill, and its
//! copy into the data root before a launch. Only files at the folder's top level count.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::fs;
use std::io;
use std::path::Path;
use std::thread::sleep;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

/// The Witcher 3 saves the game writes by itself (and Steam's cloud file): the guard lets them change. The menu's Save
/// Game always writes a `ManualSave_*`, so letting `CheckPoint_*` pass loses no guard (ini_session.py).
pub const W3_AUTO_SAVES: &[&str] = &["AutoSave", "CheckPoint", "steam_autocloud"];

/// A folder's files by name: size and write time.
pub type Snapshot = BTreeMap<String, (u64, Option<SystemTime>)>;

/// The files in `dir` now. A missing or unreadable folder is empty.
pub fn snapshot(dir: &Path) -> Snapshot {
    let entries = fs::read_dir(dir).into_iter().flatten().flatten();
    entries
        .filter_map(|e| {
            let meta = e.metadata().ok().filter(|m| m.is_file())?;
            let name = e.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
            Some((name, (meta.len(), meta.modified().ok())))
        })
        .collect()
}

/// The names that are new, changed or gone between two snapshots, sorted.
pub fn changed(before: &Snapshot, after: &Snapshot) -> Vec<String> {
    let names: BTreeSet<&String> = before
        .keys()
        .chain(after.keys())
        .filter(|name| before.get(*name) != after.get(*name))
        .collect();
    names.into_iter().cloned().collect()
}

/// The guard: the changed names that aren't the game's own saves (names starting with one of `auto`, case as given).
/// Any of them means a key confirmed something it shouldn't have (a manual save written, the quicksave replaced), and
/// the session must end at once.
pub fn unexpected<'a>(changed: &'a [String], auto: &[&str]) -> Vec<&'a str> {
    changed
        .iter()
        .map(String::as_str)
        .filter(|name| !auto.iter().any(|prefix| name.starts_with(prefix)))
        .collect()
}

/// The Witcher 3 manual saves (the menu's Save Game, and game_save): `ManualSave_<hex>_<hex>_<hex>`, its `.sav` with a
/// `.png` and, for some, a `.json` (feature tests 3).
pub const W3_MANUAL: &str = "ManualSave_";
const W3_MANUAL_FILES: &[&str] = &[".sav", ".png", ".json"];

/// game_save's check: what changed from `before` to `after`, beside the game's own saves (`auto`), must be one new
/// manual save and nothing else: a new `<base>.sav` whose base starts with [`W3_MANUAL`], and new files of that base
/// only. Ok: those files, sorted (none: nothing changed). Err: every changed name, when anything else changed (an
/// existing file, a second save, a quicksave).
pub fn new_save(
    before: &Snapshot,
    after: &Snapshot,
    auto: &[&str],
) -> Result<Vec<String>, Vec<String>> {
    let all = changed(before, after);
    let names = unexpected(&all, auto);
    let new = |name: &str| !before.contains_key(name) && after.contains_key(name);
    let savs: Vec<&str> = names
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .filter(|n| new(n) && n.starts_with(W3_MANUAL) && n.ends_with(".sav"))
        .collect();
    let ours = |base: &str, name: &str| {
        new(name)
            && W3_MANUAL_FILES
                .iter()
                .any(|ext| name.strip_prefix(base) == Some(ext))
    };
    let owned = || names.iter().map(|n| n.to_string()).collect();
    match savs[..] {
        [] if names.is_empty() => Ok(Vec::new()),
        [sav] if names.iter().all(|n| ours(&sav[..sav.len() - 4], n)) => Ok(owned()),
        _ => Err(owned()),
    }
}

/// Waits until `dir` has stayed unchanged for `quiet`, at most `max`. The seconds waited, and whether it went quiet.
pub fn wait_quiet(dir: &Path, quiet: Duration, max: Duration) -> (f64, bool) {
    let start = Instant::now();
    let (mut last, mut since) = (snapshot(dir), Instant::now());
    loop {
        let waited = (start.elapsed().as_secs_f64() * 100.0).round() / 100.0;
        if since.elapsed() >= quiet {
            return (waited, true);
        }
        if start.elapsed() >= max {
            return (waited, false);
        }
        sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
        let now = snapshot(dir);
        if now != last {
            (last, since) = (now, Instant::now());
        }
    }
}

/// What [`backup`] did.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Backup {
    /// Files copied, and their bytes.
    pub copied: usize,
    pub bytes: u64,
    /// Older copies moved aside into `older/` before a newer one replaced them.
    pub kept: usize,
}

/// Copies every file of `src` that `dst` lacks, or holds with another size or write time, into `dst`, keeping its
/// write time, so `dst` mirrors `src` as it is now. A copy it replaces is first moved to
/// `dst/older/<name>.<its write time in Unix seconds>`, and files gone from `src` stay: nothing is ever lost. Unchanged
/// files aren't read, so only the first backup copies everything.
pub fn backup(src: &Path, dst: &Path) -> io::Result<Backup> {
    let mut done = Backup::default();
    let have = snapshot(dst);
    for (name, state) in snapshot(src) {
        if have.get(&name) == Some(&state) {
            continue;
        }
        let to = dst.join(&name);
        if let Some((_, old)) = have.get(&name) {
            let secs = old
                .and_then(|t| t.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).ok())
                .map_or(0, |d| d.as_secs());
            let older = dst.join("older");
            fs::create_dir_all(&older)?;
            let mut aside = older.join(format!("{name}.{secs}"));
            for n in 1.. {
                if !aside.exists() {
                    break;
                }
                aside = older.join(format!("{name}.{secs}-{n}"));
            }
            fs::rename(&to, aside)?;
            done.kept += 1;
        }
        fs::create_dir_all(dst)?;
        done.bytes += fs::copy(src.join(&name), &to)?;
        if let Some(t) = state.1 {
            fs::File::options().write(true).open(&to)?.set_modified(t)?;
        }
        done.copied += 1;
    }
    Ok(done)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A temp folder for one test, gone afterwards (only what the test made in it).
    struct Temp(std::path::PathBuf);

    impl Temp {
        fn new(name: &str) -> Temp {
            let dir =
                std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("quen-saves-{name}-{}", std::process::id()));
            fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
            Temp(dir)
        }
    }

    impl Drop for Temp {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0); // this test's own temp folder
        }
    }

    fn touch(path: &Path, data: &str, secs: u64) {
        fs::write(path, data).unwrap();
        let t = UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::from_secs(secs);
        fs::File::options()
            .write(true)
            .open(path)
            .unwrap()
            .set_modified(t)
            .unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn changes_and_the_guard() {
        let tmp = Temp::new("guard");
        let dir = &tmp.0;
        touch(&dir.join("QuickSave.sav"), "q", 100);
        touch(&dir.join("AutoSave_1.sav"), "a", 100);
        touch(&dir.join("ManualSave_1.sav"), "m", 100);
        fs::create_dir(dir.join("sub")).unwrap();
        let before = snapshot(dir);
        assert_eq!(before.len(), 3, "folders don't count");
        touch(&dir.join("AutoSave_1.sav"), "a2", 200);
        touch(&dir.join("CheckPoint_2.sav"), "c", 200);
        assert!(unexpected(&changed(&before, &snapshot(dir)), W3_AUTO_SAVES).is_empty());
        touch(&dir.join("QuickSave.sav"), "q", 300);
        fs::remove_file(dir.join("ManualSave_1.sav")).unwrap();
        let all = changed(&before, &snapshot(dir));
        assert_eq!(
            all,
            [
                "AutoSave_1.sav",
                "CheckPoint_2.sav",
                "ManualSave_1.sav",
                "QuickSave.sav"
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            unexpected(&all, W3_AUTO_SAVES),
            ["ManualSave_1.sav", "QuickSave.sav"]
        );
        assert!(snapshot(&dir.join("missing")).is_empty());
    }

    /// game_save accepts one new manual save (its .sav with a .png and maybe a .json) beside the game's own saves, and
    /// nothing else: an overwrite, a quicksave, two saves or a stray file next to the new one are refused whole.
    #[test]
    fn one_new_manual_save_and_nothing_else() {
        let tmp = Temp::new("new-save");
        let dir = &tmp.0;
        touch(&dir.join("ManualSave_user.sav"), "old", 100);
        touch(&dir.join("ManualSave_user.png"), "old", 100);
        let before = snapshot(dir);
        let check = || new_save(&before, &snapshot(dir), W3_AUTO_SAVES);
        assert_eq!(check(), Ok(vec![]), "nothing yet");
        touch(&dir.join("AutoSave_9.sav"), "a", 200);
        assert_eq!(check(), Ok(vec![]), "the game's own saves pass");
        touch(&dir.join("ManualSave_new.sav"), "new", 200);
        touch(&dir.join("ManualSave_new.png"), "new", 200);
        touch(&dir.join("ManualSave_new.json"), "new", 200);
        let three = [
            "ManualSave_new.json",
            "ManualSave_new.png",
            "ManualSave_new.sav",
        ];
        assert_eq!(check(), Ok(three.map(String::from).to_vec()));
        for (bad, data) in [
            ("ManualSave_user.sav", "overwritten"),
            ("QuickSave.sav", "q"),
            ("ManualSave_menu.sav", "a second save"),
            ("ManualSave_new.sav.bak", "a stray file"),
            ("notes.txt", "a stray file"),
        ] {
            let path = dir.join(bad);
            let existed = path.exists();
            touch(&path, data, 300);
            let names = check().expect_err(bad);
            assert!(names.iter().any(|n| n == bad), "{bad}: {names:?}");
            match existed {
                true => touch(&path, "old", 100),
                false => fs::remove_file(&path).unwrap(),
            }
            assert!(check().is_ok(), "{bad} put back");
        }
        fs::remove_file(dir.join("ManualSave_new.sav")).unwrap();
        assert!(check().is_err(), "a .png without its new .sav");
        fs::remove_file(dir.join("ManualSave_user.png")).unwrap();
        touch(&dir.join("ManualSave_new.sav"), "new", 200);
        assert!(check().is_err(), "an old file gone");
    }

    #[test]
    fn backup_mirrors_and_keeps_what_it_replaces() {
        let tmp = Temp::new("backup");
        let (src, dst) = (
            tmp.0.join("gamesaves"),
            tmp.0.join("data").join("gamesaves"),
        );
        fs::create_dir_all(&src).unwrap();
        touch(&src.join("QuickSave.sav"), "q1", 100);
        touch(&src.join("ManualSave_1.sav"), "m1", 100);
        let first = backup(&src, &dst).unwrap();
        assert_eq!((first.copied, first.bytes, first.kept), (2, 4, 0));
        assert_eq!(snapshot(&dst), snapshot(&src), "sizes and write times kept");
        assert_eq!(
            backup(&src, &dst).unwrap(),
            Backup::default(),
            "nothing changed"
        );

        touch(&src.join("QuickSave.sav"), "q2!", 200);
        fs::remove_file(src.join("ManualSave_1.sav")).unwrap();
        let second = backup(&src, &dst).unwrap();
        assert_eq!((second.copied, second.kept), (1, 1));
        assert_eq!(
            fs::read_to_string(dst.join("QuickSave.sav")).unwrap(),
            "q2!"
        );
        let older = dst.join("older").join("QuickSave.sav.100");
        assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(older).unwrap(), "q1");
        assert_eq!(
            fs::read_to_string(dst.join("ManualSave_1.sav")).unwrap(),
            "m1",
            "a save gone from gamesaves stays in the copy"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn waits_until_the_folder_stops_changing() {
        let tmp = Temp::new("quiet");
        let dir = tmp.0.clone();
        let writer = std::thread::spawn({
            let dir = dir.clone();
            move || {
                for i in 0..8 {
                    fs::write(dir.join("save.sav"), vec![0u8; i + 1]).unwrap();
                    sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
                }
            }
        });
        let (secs, quiet) = wait_quiet(&dir, Duration::from_millis(400), Duration::from_secs(10));
        writer.join().unwrap();
        assert!(quiet && secs >= 0.8, "{secs} s, quiet {quiet}");
        let (_, quiet) = wait_quiet(&dir, Duration::from_secs(5), Duration::from_millis(300));
        assert!(!quiet, "returned quiet before `quiet` passed");
    }
}
```

`crates/quen-core/src/scene.rs`:

```rs
//! Placement for quen's scene tools (`game_frame`, `game_place`): the photo-mode camera pose that frames a subject from
//! one side, and the yaw that faces a point. The game's conventions, as quen's camera and trace tools use them: a
//! camera's or a body's forward is (-sin yaw, cos yaw) in world xy, so +yaw turns left; pitch is the angle above the
//! horizon (sweep.rs's poses).

use crate::sweep::Pose;

/// A side of the subject: degrees from its forward, +90 its left (+yaw turns left).
pub const SIDES: [(&str, f64); 4] = [
    ("front", 0.0),
    ("left", 90.0),
    ("back", 180.0),
    ("right", -90.0),
];

/// A side's degrees by name.
pub fn side(name: &str) -> Option<f64> {
    SIDES.iter().find(|(n, _)| *n == name).map(|(_, d)| *d)
}

/// An angle in degrees, in (-180, 180].
pub fn wrap(deg: f64) -> f64 {
    let a = deg - 360.0 * (deg / 360.0).round();
    if a <= -180.0 { a + 360.0 } else { a }
}

/// The unit forward of `yaw` degrees, in world xy.
pub fn forward(yaw: f64) -> [f64; 2] {
    let r = yaw.to_radians();
    [-r.sin(), r.cos()]
}

/// The yaw whose forward points from `from` to `to` in xy; none when they are within a millimetre.
pub fn facing(from: [f64; 2], to: [f64; 2]) -> Option<f64> {
    let (dx, dy) = (to[0] - from[0], to[1] - from[1]);
    (dx.hypot(dy) >= 1e-3).then(|| wrap((-dx).atan2(dy).to_degrees()))
}

/// The rotation `[pitch, yaw, 0]` that looks from `from` at `to` (pitch negative looking down); none when they are within
/// a millimetre in xy.
pub fn aim(from: [f64; 3], to: [f64; 3]) -> Option<[f64; 3]> {
    let yaw = facing([from[0], from[1]], [to[0], to[1]])?;
    let flat = (to[0] - from[0]).hypot(to[1] - from[1]);
    Some([(to[2] - from[2]).atan2(flat).to_degrees(), yaw, 0.0])
}

/// How a subject is framed: from `side` degrees off its forward, `distance` metres away from the aim point in xy,
/// `height` metres above it, with `fov` degrees.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub struct Framing {
    pub side: f64,
    pub distance: f64,
    pub height: f64,
    pub fov: f64,
}

/// The camera pose that frames `aim` (a point on a subject whose heading is `heading`) as `f` says: the camera
/// `f.distance` out along the subject's forward turned by `f.side`, `f.height` above the aim point, looking at it, no
/// roll.
pub fn frame_pose(aim: [f64; 3], heading: f64, f: &Framing) -> Pose {
    let out = forward(heading + f.side);
    let pos = [
        aim[0] + f.distance * out[0],
        aim[1] + f.distance * out[1],
        aim[2] + f.height,
    ];
    let pitch = (-f.height).atan2(f.distance).to_degrees();
    Pose {
        pos,
        rot: [pitch, wrap(heading + f.side + 180.0), 0.0],
        fov: f.fov,
    }
}

/// The unit vector a pose looks along, in world xyz.
pub fn look(p: &Pose) -> [f64; 3] {
    let (pitch, [x, y]) = (p.rot[0].to_radians(), forward(p.rot[1]));
    [x * pitch.cos(), y * pitch.cos(), pitch.sin()]
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn close(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool {
        (a - b).abs() < 1e-9
    }

    /// The direction from `p`'s position to `aim`, unit.
    fn towards(p: &Pose, aim: [f64; 3]) -> [f64; 3] {
        let d = [aim[0] - p.pos[0], aim[1] - p.pos[1], aim[2] - p.pos[2]];
        let n = (d[0] * d[0] + d[1] * d[1] + d[2] * d[2]).sqrt();
        d.map(|c| c / n)
    }

    #[test]
    fn sides_frame_the_subject_from_where_they_say() {
        let aim = [604.87, 2089.32, 32.6];
        // A subject facing +y (heading 0): its front is +y, its left -x, its back -y, its right +x.
        let want = [
            ("front", [0.0, 3.0], 180.0),
            ("left", [-3.0, 0.0], -90.0),
            ("back", [0.0, -3.0], 0.0),
            ("right", [3.0, 0.0], 90.0),
        ];
        for (name, offset, yaw) in want {
            let f = Framing {
                side: side(name).unwrap(),
                distance: 3.0,
                height: 0.0,
                fov: 40.0,
            };
            let p = frame_pose(aim, 0.0, &f);
            assert!(
                close(p.pos[0] - aim[0], offset[0]) && close(p.pos[1] - aim[1], offset[1]),
                "{name}: {p:?}"
            );
            assert!(close(p.rot[1], yaw), "{name}: {p:?}");
            assert_eq!((p.rot[0], p.rot[2], p.fov), (0.0, 0.0, 40.0));
            let (look, to) = (look(&p), towards(&p, aim));
            assert!(
                (0..3).all(|c| close(look[c], to[c])),
                "{name}: looks {look:?}, aim {to:?}"
            );
        }
    }

    /// Any heading, side and height: the camera stands the asked distance off in xy and the height above, and looks
    /// straight at the aim point.
    #[test]
    fn a_framing_looks_at_its_aim_from_any_heading() {
        let aim = [-12.5, 40.25, 3.0];
        for heading in [-179.0, -127.3, -45.0, 0.0, 33.3, 90.0, 180.0] {
            for side in [0.0, 90.0, 180.0, -90.0, 30.0, -150.0] {
                for (distance, height) in [(3.0, 0.0), (1.5, 0.8), (8.0, -1.0)] {
                    let f = Framing {
                        side,
                        distance,
                        height,
                        fov: 50.0,
                    };
                    let p = frame_pose(aim, heading, &f);
                    let d = [p.pos[0] - aim[0], p.pos[1] - aim[1]];
                    assert!(close(d[0].hypot(d[1]), distance), "{heading} {side}: {p:?}");
                    assert!(close(p.pos[2] - aim[2], height));
                    let (look, to) = (look(&p), towards(&p, aim));
                    assert!(
                        (0..3).all(|c| close(look[c], to[c])),
                        "{heading} {side} {height}: {look:?} {to:?}"
                    );
                    // The camera stands on the asked side: along the subject's forward turned by `side`.
                    let out = forward(heading + side);
                    assert!(close(d[0] * out[0] + d[1] * out[1], distance));
                    assert!(p.rot[1] > -180.0 && p.rot[1] <= 180.0);
                }
            }
        }
        // Above the aim it looks down, below it up.
        let above = frame_pose(
            aim,
            0.0,
            &Framing {
                side: 0.0,
                distance: 2.0,
                height: 2.0,
                fov: 40.0,
            },
        );
        assert!(close(above.rot[0], -45.0), "{above:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn facing_points_the_forward_at_the_target() {
        assert_eq!(facing([0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 5.0]), Some(0.0));
        assert!(close(facing([0.0, 0.0], [-5.0, 0.0]).unwrap(), 90.0));
        assert!(close(facing([0.0, 0.0], [5.0, 0.0]).unwrap(), -90.0));
        assert!(close(facing([1.0, 1.0], [1.0, -4.0]).unwrap(), 180.0));
        assert_eq!(facing([1.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0005]), None);
        for yaw in [-170.0, -60.0, 0.0, 45.0, 135.0] {
            let [x, y] = forward(yaw);
            assert!(close(
                facing([10.0, 10.0], [10.0 + 3.0 * x, 10.0 + 3.0 * y]).unwrap(),
                yaw
            ));
        }
        assert_eq!(wrap(-180.0), 180.0);
        assert_eq!(wrap(540.0), 180.0);
        assert!(close(wrap(-190.0), 170.0));
        assert_eq!(side("up"), None);
    }

    /// Boot 237's qfcrel(10, 0, 2): from (661.08, 1881.99, 11.73) at 1.7 m above Geralt (668.99, 1875.87, 9.94), sent
    /// rot (-0.53, -127.70, 0), which put him at the frame's centre. A pose aimed so looks at its target.
    #[test]
    fn aim_looks_from_a_point_at_a_target() {
        let rot = aim([661.08, 1881.99, 11.73], [668.99, 1875.87, 11.64]).unwrap();
        assert!(
            (rot[0] - -0.52).abs() < 0.01 && (rot[1] - -127.73).abs() < 0.01,
            "{rot:?}"
        );
        assert_eq!(rot[2], 0.0);
        let (from, to) = ([1.0, 2.0, 10.0], [4.0, 6.0, 5.0]);
        let p = Pose {
            pos: from,
            rot: aim(from, to).unwrap(),
            fov: 40.0,
        };
        let (look, want) = (look(&p), towards(&p, to));
        assert!((0..3).all(|c| close(look[c], want[c])), "{look:?} {want:?}");
        assert_eq!(aim(from, [1.0, 2.0005, 0.0]), None);
    }
}
```
