`crates/quen-core/src/seeds.rs`:

```rs
//! The REA (Ghidra) seed file, generated from the RE knowledge base (docs/intent.md, "Game knowledge").
//!
//! REA reads `REA_GHIDRA_SEED_FILE`: `address<TAB>kind[<TAB>name]` lines with absolute VAs, kind `function`, `label` or
//! `code`, names of 1 to 2000 characters without whitespace, at most 1 M entries. The KB keeps RVAs, so VA = RVA +
//! [`IMAGE_BASE`]. RVAs are `0x`-prefixed hex of at most 32 bits, which also catches a VA pasted where an RVA belongs.
//!
//! REA applies a seed file to whichever exe it opens, so a seed file is made for one build: `names.tsv` names
//! its build on a `# build:` line ([`Build::of_kb`]), [`seed_file`] refuses an exe of another build, and the file goes
//! to a path named by the build ([`path`]), which `REA_GHIDRA_SEED_FILE` then names.

use serde::de::{Deserialize, Deserializer, MapAccess, Visitor};
use std::fmt;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use crate::build::Build;

/// witcher3.exe's preferred image base, where REA's Ghidra import places it.
pub const IMAGE_BASE: u64 = 0x1_4000_0000;
/// The longest name, in UTF-16 units as REA's JavaScript and Ghidra's Java count them.
pub const MAX_NAME: usize = 2000;
/// The most seeds REA reads.
pub const MAX_SEEDS: usize = 1_000_000;

const TSV_HEADER: [&str; 6] = ["rva", "name", "kind", "confidence", "source", "date"];

/// Sorted by declaration order after the address, so the file's line order is fixed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum Kind {
    Function,
    Label,
    Code,
}

impl Kind {
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Kind::Function => "function",
            Kind::Label => "label",
            Kind::Code => "code",
        }
    }
}

/// One seed line. A function may have a name, a label must, a code seed has none.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Seed {
    pub va: u64,
    pub kind: Kind,
    pub name: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Error {
    /// A bad `names.tsv` line: header, column count, address, kind or name.
    Tsv {
        line: usize,
        msg: String,
    },
    /// A bad `func_names.json`: not an object of strings, or a bad key or name.
    Json(String),
    Duplicate {
        va: u64,
        kind: Kind,
    },
    /// REA applies labels after functions and makes them primary, so the label would rename the function.
    LabelAtFunction(u64),
    TooMany(usize),
    /// `names.tsv`'s build line is missing or bad, or the exe is another build.
    Build(String),
}

impl fmt::Display for Error {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Error::Tsv { line, msg } => write!(f, "names.tsv line {line}: {msg}"),
            Error::Json(msg) => write!(f, "func_names.json: {msg}"),
            Error::Duplicate { va, kind } => write!(f, "{va:#x} has two {} seeds", kind.as_str()),
            Error::LabelAtFunction(va) => {
                write!(
                    f,
                    "{va:#x} has a function and a label seed: the label would rename the function"
                )
            }
            Error::TooMany(n) => write!(f, "{n} seeds, REA reads at most {MAX_SEEDS}"),
            Error::Build(msg) => write!(f, "names.tsv: {msg}"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for Error {}

/// REA's seed file for `exe` from a KB `names.tsv` ([`render`] of [`from_names_tsv`]), refused unless `exe` is the
/// build the table's build line names. It goes to [`path`]`(exe)` in the KB.
pub fn seed_file(names_tsv: &str, exe: &Build) -> Result<String, Error> {
    let (build, seeds) = from_names_tsv(names_tsv)?;
    build.check_exe(exe).map_err(Error::Build)?;
    render(seeds)
}

/// Where a build's seed file goes, relative to the KB folder: `seeds/<stamp>-<first 16 hex digits of its sha256>.tsv`.
/// `REA_GHIDRA_SEED_FILE` names it, so the setting says which build its names are for, and each build's seeds are a
/// file of their own.
pub fn path(build: &Build) -> PathBuf {
    let sha: String = build.sha256.chars().take(16).collect();
    Path::new("seeds").join(format!("{}-{sha}.tsv", build.stamp))
}

/// The build a KB `names.tsv` names ([`Build::of_kb`]) and its seeds: a header row of `rva name kind confidence source
/// date`, then one row per name (see [`tsv_rows`]). An empty name cell means no name.
pub fn from_names_tsv(text: &str) -> Result<(Build, Vec<Seed>), Error> {
    let build = Build::of_kb(text).map_err(Error::Build)?;
    let err = |line, msg| Error::Tsv { line, msg };
    let rows = tsv_rows(text, &TSV_HEADER).map_err(|(line, msg)| err(line, msg))?;
    let seeds = rows
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(line, [rva, name, kind, _confidence, _source, _date])| {
            let kind = match kind {
                "function" => Kind::Function,
                "label" => Kind::Label,
                "code" => Kind::Code,
                _ => {
                    let msg = format!("kind {kind:?} is not function, label or code");
                    return Err(err(line, msg));
                }
            };
            seed(rva, kind, name).map_err(|msg| err(line, msg))
        })
        .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
    Ok((build, seeds))
}

/// The rows of a KB TSV file (`names.tsv`, `patches.tsv`): `header` first, then rows of as many tab-separated cells,
/// each trimmed, with their 1-based line numbers. Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are skipped. The error is a
/// line number and the reason.
pub(crate) fn tsv_rows<'a, const N: usize>(
    text: &'a str,
    header: &[&str; N],
) -> Result<Vec<Row<'a, N>>, (usize, String)> {
    let mut rows = Vec::new();
    let mut seen = false;
    for (i, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {
        if line.trim().is_empty() || line.trim_start().starts_with('#') {
            continue;
        }
        let cells: Vec<&str> = line.split('\t').map(str::trim).collect();
        if !seen {
            if cells[..] != header[..] {
                return Err((
                    i + 1,
                    format!("the header must be {}", header.join(" <TAB> ")),
                ));
            }
            seen = true;
            continue;
        }
        let row = cells
            .try_into()
            .map_err(|cells: Vec<_>| (i + 1, format!("{} columns, expected {N}", cells.len())))?;
        rows.push((i + 1, row));
    }
    if !seen {
        return Err((text.lines().count() + 1, "no header row".into()));
    }
    Ok(rows)
}

/// A KB TSV row: its line number and its cells.
pub(crate) type Row<'a, const N: usize> = (usize, [&'a str; N]);

/// A KB RVA cell: `0x`-prefixed hex of at most 32 bits. The error is the reason, without the location.
pub(crate) fn rva(cell: &str) -> Result<u32, String> {
    let hex = cell
        .strip_prefix("0x")
        .or_else(|| cell.strip_prefix("0X"))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    if hex.is_empty() || !hex.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
        return Err(format!("address {cell:?} is not 0x-prefixed hex"));
    }
    u32::from_str_radix(hex, 16).map_err(|_| format!("RVA {cell} is over 32 bits: a VA?"))
}

/// The function seeds of a `func_names.json` object: RVA keys, name values. Keys starting with `_` (such as `_about`)
/// are notes and skipped. A key that appears twice is a duplicate, not silently the last one.
pub fn from_func_names_json(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Seed>, Error> {
    let Entries(entries) = serde_json::from_str(text).map_err(|e| Error::Json(e.to_string()))?;
    let names = entries.into_iter().filter(|(key, _)| !key.starts_with('_'));
    names
        .map(|(key, value)| {
            let name = value
                .as_str()
                .ok_or_else(|| Error::Json(format!("{key}: the name is not a string")))?;
            seed(&key, Kind::Function, name).map_err(|msg| Error::Json(format!("{key}: {msg}")))
        })
        .collect()
}

/// The seed file's text, sorted by address then kind so that reordering the inputs doesn't change it (REA treats any
/// seed change as a new analysis).
pub fn render(mut seeds: Vec<Seed>) -> Result<String, Error> {
    if seeds.len() > MAX_SEEDS {
        return Err(Error::TooMany(seeds.len()));
    }
    seeds.sort_by_key(|s| (s.va, s.kind));
    if let Some(pair) = seeds
        .windows(2)
        .find(|w| (w[0].va, w[0].kind) == (w[1].va, w[1].kind))
    {
        return Err(Error::Duplicate {
            va: pair[0].va,
            kind: pair[0].kind,
        });
    }
    // Function sorts right before Label, so a pair at one address is adjacent.
    if let Some(pair) = seeds
        .windows(2)
        .find(|w| w[0].va == w[1].va && (w[0].kind, w[1].kind) == (Kind::Function, Kind::Label))
    {
        return Err(Error::LabelAtFunction(pair[0].va));
    }
    Ok(seeds
        .iter()
        .map(|s| match &s.name {
            Some(name) => format!("{:#x}\t{}\t{name}\n", s.va, s.kind.as_str()),
            None => format!("{:#x}\t{}\n", s.va, s.kind.as_str()),
        })
        .collect())
}

/// One seed from an RVA cell, a kind and a name cell (blank for none). Each whitespace run in the name, the ends
/// trimmed first, becomes `_`. The error is the reason, without the location.
fn seed(rva: &str, kind: Kind, name: &str) -> Result<Seed, String> {
    let rva = self::rva(rva)?;
    let name = name.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join("_");
    let name = (!name.is_empty()).then_some(name);
    match (kind, &name) {
        (Kind::Code, Some(_)) => return Err("a code seed takes no name".into()),
        (Kind::Label, None) => return Err("a label seed needs a name".into()),
        (_, Some(name)) if name.encode_utf16().count() > MAX_NAME => {
            return Err(format!("name longer than {MAX_NAME} characters"));
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    Ok(Seed {
        va: IMAGE_BASE + u64::from(rva),
        kind,
        name,
    })
}

/// A JSON object's entries in file order, duplicate keys kept.
struct Entries(Vec<(String, serde_json::Value)>);

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Entries {
    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
        struct EntriesVisitor;
        impl<'de> Visitor<'de> for EntriesVisitor {
            type Value = Entries;
            fn expecting(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
                f.write_str("an object of RVA keys and name values")
            }
            fn visit_map<A: MapAccess<'de>>(self, mut map: A) -> Result<Entries, A::Error> {
                let mut entries = Vec::new();
                while let Some(entry) = map.next_entry()? {
                    entries.push(entry);
                }
                Ok(Entries(entries))
            }
        }
        deserializer.deserialize_map(EntriesVisitor)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::build::Stamp;
    use crate::journal::sha256_hex;

    const HEADER: &str = "rva\tname\tkind\tconfidence\tsource\tdate\n";

    /// A synthetic build, not from any real binary.
    fn build(stamp: u32, exe: &[u8]) -> Build {
        Build {
            sha256: sha256_hex(exe),
            stamp: Stamp(stamp),
        }
    }

    fn kb() -> Build {
        build(0x0BAD_F00D, b"synthetic exe")
    }

    fn build_line(build: &Build) -> String {
        format!("# build: sha256={} stamp={}\n", build.sha256, build.stamp)
    }

    /// The build line goes anywhere: here, after the rows, so the rows keep their line numbers.
    fn names(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Seed>, Error> {
        let (build, seeds) = from_names_tsv(&format!("{text}{}", build_line(&kb())))?;
        assert_eq!(build, kb());
        Ok(seeds)
    }

    fn tsv(rows: &str) -> Result<Vec<Seed>, Error> {
        names(&format!("{HEADER}{rows}"))
    }

    fn function(va: u64, name: &str) -> Seed {
        Seed {
            va,
            kind: Kind::Function,
            name: Some(name.into()),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn names_tsv_to_seed_file() {
        let text = "\
# synthetic KB names, not from any real binary
\r
rva\tname\tkind\tconfidence\tsource\tdate\r
0x1000\toperator new\tfunction\tO\ttest\t2026-01-01\r
  # an indented comment
0x2a0\t\tcode\tI\ttest\t2026-01-01
0X1F0\tTable::Lookup\u{a0} slot \tlabel\tO\ttest\t2026-01-01
0x00000010\t\tfunction\tO\ttest\t
0x1000\t\tcode\tO\ttest\t2026-01-01
";
        let seeds = names(text).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(seeds[0], function(0x1_4000_1000, "operator_new"));
        assert_eq!(
            seeds[1],
            Seed {
                va: 0x1_4000_02a0,
                kind: Kind::Code,
                name: None
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            seeds[3],
            Seed {
                va: 0x1_4000_0010,
                kind: Kind::Function,
                name: None
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            render(seeds).unwrap(),
            "0x140000010\tfunction\n\
             0x1400001f0\tlabel\tTable::Lookup_slot\n\
             0x1400002a0\tcode\n\
             0x140001000\tfunction\toperator_new\n\
             0x140001000\tcode\n"
        );
        let label = Seed {
            va: 0x1_4000_1000,
            kind: Kind::Label,
            name: Some("slot".into()),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            render(vec![label, function(0x1_4000_1000, "f")]),
            Err(Error::LabelAtFunction(0x1_4000_1000))
        );
        assert!(names(HEADER).unwrap().is_empty());
        assert_eq!(render(vec![]).unwrap(), "");
    }

    #[test]
    fn func_names_json_to_function_seeds() {
        let json = r#"{
            "_about": {"note": "synthetic names", "count": 2},
            "0x12AB34C": "CRT thread_start",
            "0x10": "  padded   name ",
            "_todo": "skipped"
        }"#;
        let seeds = from_func_names_json(json).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            seeds,
            vec![
                function(0x1_412A_B34C, "CRT_thread_start"),
                function(0x1_4000_0010, "padded_name")
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            render(seeds).unwrap(),
            "0x140000010\tfunction\tpadded_name\n0x1412ab34c\tfunction\tCRT_thread_start\n"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            from_func_names_json(r#"{"0x10": ""}"#).unwrap(),
            vec![Seed {
                va: 0x1_4000_0010,
                kind: Kind::Function,
                name: None
            }]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn duplicates_are_refused_across_spellings_and_inputs() {
        let mut seeds = tsv("0x12AB34C\tfrom tsv\tfunction\tO\ttest\t2026-01-01\n").unwrap();
        seeds.extend(from_func_names_json(r#"{"0x12ab34c": "from json"}"#).unwrap());
        assert_eq!(
            render(seeds),
            Err(Error::Duplicate {
                va: 0x1_412A_B34C,
                kind: Kind::Function
            })
        );
        let seeds = tsv("0x10\ta\tlabel\tO\tt\td\n0x0010\tb\tlabel\tO\tt\td\n").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            render(seeds),
            Err(Error::Duplicate {
                va: 0x1_4000_0010,
                kind: Kind::Label
            })
        );
        let seeds = from_func_names_json(r#"{"0x10": "a", "0x10": "b"}"#).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            render(seeds),
            Err(Error::Duplicate {
                va: 0x1_4000_0010,
                kind: Kind::Function
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn bad_rows_are_refused_with_their_line() {
        for (row, why) in [
            ("1AB4\tn\tfunction\tO\tt\td", "not 0x-prefixed hex"),
            ("0x\tn\tfunction\tO\tt\td", "not 0x-prefixed hex"),
            ("0xZZ\tn\tfunction\tO\tt\td", "not 0x-prefixed hex"),
            ("0x+1A\tn\tfunction\tO\tt\td", "not 0x-prefixed hex"),
            ("4096\tn\tfunction\tO\tt\td", "not 0x-prefixed hex"),
            ("0x140001000\tn\tfunction\tO\tt\td", "over 32 bits"),
            ("0x10\t\tlabel\tO\tt\td", "needs a name"),
            ("0x10\t \tlabel\tO\tt\td", "needs a name"),
            ("0x10\tn\tcode\tO\tt\td", "takes no name"),
            ("0x10\tn\tdata\tO\tt\td", "is not function, label or code"),
            (
                "0x10\tn\tFunction\tO\tt\td",
                "is not function, label or code",
            ),
            ("0x10\tn\tfunction\tO\tt", "5 columns"),
            ("0x10 n function O t d", "1 columns"),
        ] {
            match tsv(&format!("0x20\tok\tfunction\tO\tt\td\n# note\n{row}\n")) {
                Err(Error::Tsv { line: 4, msg }) => assert!(msg.contains(why), "{row:?}: {msg}"),
                other => panic!("{row:?}: {other:?}"),
            }
        }
        assert!(matches!(
            names("# only a comment\n\n"),
            Err(Error::Tsv { line: 4, .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            names("rva\tname\tkind\n"),
            Err(Error::Tsv { line: 1, .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            names("0x10\tn\tfunction\tO\tt\td\n"),
            Err(Error::Tsv { line: 1, .. })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn names_are_capped_at_2000_characters() {
        let row = |name: &str| tsv(&format!("0x10\t{name}\tfunction\tO\tt\td\n"));
        assert_eq!(
            row(&"n".repeat(MAX_NAME)).unwrap()[0]
                .name
                .as_ref()
                .unwrap()
                .len(),
            MAX_NAME
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            row(&"n".repeat(MAX_NAME + 1)),
            Err(Error::Tsv { .. })
        ));
        // Whitespace runs shrink before the cap is checked; an astral character counts as two.
        assert!(row(&format!("{} {}", "n".repeat(1000), "n".repeat(999))).is_ok());
        assert!(matches!(
            row(&format!("{}\u{1F600}", "n".repeat(MAX_NAME - 1))),
            Err(Error::Tsv { .. })
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn bad_json_is_refused() {
        for (json, why) in [
            (r#"["0x10"]"#, "an object"),
            (r#"{"0x10": 7}"#, "not a string"),
            (r#"{"0x10": null}"#, "not a string"),
            (r#"{"16": "n"}"#, "not 0x-prefixed hex"),
            (r#"{"0x1_0": "n"}"#, "not 0x-prefixed hex"),
            (r#"{"0x100000000": "n"}"#, "over 32 bits"),
            (r#"{"0x10": "n""#, "EOF"),
        ] {
            match from_func_names_json(json) {
                Err(Error::Json(msg)) => assert!(msg.contains(why), "{json}: {msg}"),
                other => panic!("{json}: {other:?}"),
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn at_most_a_million_seeds() {
        let seeds = vec![
            Seed {
                va: IMAGE_BASE,
                kind: Kind::Code,
                name: None
            };
            MAX_SEEDS + 1
        ];
        assert_eq!(render(seeds), Err(Error::TooMany(MAX_SEEDS + 1)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_seed_file_is_made_for_the_kb_s_build_only() {
        let rows = format!("{HEADER}0x1000\tf\tfunction\tO\ttest\t2026-01-01\n");
        let table = format!("{}{rows}", build_line(&kb()));
        let want = "0x140001000\tfunction\tf\n";
        assert_eq!(seed_file(&table, &kb()).as_deref(), Ok(want));

        let update = build(0x1234_5678, b"synthetic update");
        let patched = build(0x0BAD_F00D, b"synthetic exe, patched");
        for (exe, why) in [(&update, "another build"), (&patched, "the same PE stamp")] {
            let e = seed_file(&table, exe).unwrap_err();
            assert!(matches!(&e, Error::Build(msg) if msg.contains(why)), "{e}");
            assert!(
                e.to_string().starts_with("names.tsv: the KB is for "),
                "{e}"
            );
        }
        let e = seed_file(&rows, &kb()).unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            matches!(&e, Error::Build(msg) if msg.starts_with("no build line")),
            "{e}"
        );

        // Named by the build, so each build's seeds are a file of their own.
        let sha = &kb().sha256[..16];
        assert_eq!(
            path(&kb()),
            Path::new("seeds").join(format!("0x0BADF00D-{sha}.tsv"))
        );
        assert_ne!(path(&patched), path(&kb()));
        assert_ne!(path(&update), path(&kb()));
    }
}
```

`crates/quen-core/src/settings.rs`:

```rs
//! Byte-exact overrides of a Witcher 3 `dx12user.settings` (an INI-like file, CRLF or LF), with the semantics of
//! the harness's `W3_SETTINGS` (flat) and `W3_SECTION_SETTINGS` (per section) switches, except that a missing section
//! is appended (the harness refuses it). Every byte an override doesn't name stays identical. [`validate`] runs both
//! on an in-memory copy: it is what runs before any backup.

use std::fmt;
use std::ops::Range;

/// Why a set of overrides can't be applied. Nothing is written when one comes back.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SettingsError {
    /// An item that isn't `Key=Value` (flat) or `Section:Key=Value` (per section) with a non-empty key and section,
    /// a key not starting with `[`, and no line break.
    BadItem(String),
    /// A flat key must start exactly one line, as `Key=`.
    KeyCount { key: String, found: usize },
    /// A section's header line `[Section]` must occur at most once; with none, no line may be the header but for case,
    /// spaces, a BOM or its line break (`found` 0), since the game may read that one as the section.
    SectionCount { section: String, found: usize },
    /// A key may start at most one line of its section.
    KeyInSection {
        section: String,
        key: String,
        found: usize,
    },
}

impl fmt::Display for SettingsError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::BadItem(item) => write!(
                f,
                "override {item:?} is not Key=Value (flat) or Section:Key=Value (per section) on one line"
            ),
            Self::KeyCount { key, found } => {
                write!(
                    f,
                    "key {key:?} starts {found} lines, an override needs exactly 1"
                )
            }
            Self::SectionCount { section, found: 0 } => write!(
                f,
                "no exact section header [{section}], only a near one (case, spaces, a BOM, no line break): \
                 not added beside it"
            ),
            Self::SectionCount { section, found } => {
                write!(
                    f,
                    "section header [{section}] is on {found} lines, needs exactly 1"
                )
            }
            Self::KeyInSection {
                section,
                key,
                found,
            } => {
                write!(
                    f,
                    "key {key:?} starts {found} lines of [{section}], at most 1 allowed"
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for SettingsError {}

/// Applies a flat spec `Key=Value[,Key=Value...]` in order, so a later value wins. Each key must start exactly one line
/// of the file as `Key=` (matched literally); that line's value is replaced literally, up to its line break.
pub fn apply_flat(data: &[u8], spec: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, SettingsError> {
    let mut out = data.to_vec();
    for item in items(spec, ',') {
        let (key, value) = key_value(item, item)?;
        let hits: Vec<Range<usize>> = lines(&out)
            .filter_map(|l| value_of(&out, &l, key))
            .collect();
        let [hit] = hits.as_slice() else {
            return Err(SettingsError::KeyCount {
                key: key.into(),
                found: hits.len(),
            });
        };
        out.splice(hit.clone(), value.bytes());
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Applies a per-section spec `Section:Key=Value[;...]` in order. The header line `[Section]`, followed by its line
/// break, may occur once; the section's body runs to the next line starting with `[`, or the end. A key already in the
/// body (at most once) gets the new value; otherwise `Key=Value` goes on a new line right after the header. A section
/// the file lacks (a mod's menu group before its first run) is appended, header and key, unless a line is its header
/// but for case, spaces, a BOM or its line break. New lines end in CRLF if the file holds any CRLF, else LF.
pub fn apply_sections(data: &[u8], spec: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, SettingsError> {
    let mut out = data.to_vec();
    for item in items(spec, ';') {
        let bad = || SettingsError::BadItem(item.into());
        let (section, kv) = item.split_once(':').ok_or_else(bad)?;
        if section.is_empty() || section.contains(['\r', '\n']) {
            return Err(bad());
        }
        let (key, value) = key_value(item, kv)?;
        let header = format!("[{section}]");
        let eol = if out.windows(2).any(|w| w == b"\r\n") {
            "\r\n"
        } else {
            "\n"
        };
        let all: Vec<Line> = lines(&out).collect();
        let heads: Vec<usize> = (0..all.len())
            .filter(|&i| all[i].eol && out[all[i].start..all[i].end] == *header.as_bytes())
            .collect();
        let head = match heads[..] {
            [head] => head,
            [] if !all.iter().any(|l| {
                let text = &out[l.start..l.end];
                text.strip_prefix(b"\xef\xbb\xbf")
                    .unwrap_or(text)
                    .trim_ascii()
                    .eq_ignore_ascii_case(header.as_bytes())
            }) =>
            {
                if !out.is_empty() && out.last() != Some(&b'\n') {
                    out.extend_from_slice(eol.as_bytes());
                }
                out.extend_from_slice(format!("{header}{eol}{key}={value}{eol}").as_bytes());
                continue;
            }
            _ => {
                return Err(SettingsError::SectionCount {
                    section: section.into(),
                    found: heads.len(),
                });
            }
        };
        let hits: Vec<Range<usize>> = all[head + 1..]
            .iter()
            .take_while(|l| out.get(l.start) != Some(&b'['))
            .filter_map(|l| value_of(&out, l, key))
            .collect();
        match hits.as_slice() {
            [] => {
                let at = all[head].next;
                out.splice(at..at, format!("{key}={value}{eol}").into_bytes());
            }
            [hit] => {
                out.splice(hit.clone(), value.bytes());
            }
            _ => {
                return Err(SettingsError::KeyInSection {
                    section: section.into(),
                    key: key.into(),
                    found: hits.len(),
                });
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Applies `flat`, then `sections`, to an in-memory copy of `data`. Run it before any backup: an error names the key
/// or section at fault and means nothing was touched; the result is the patched file, identical outside the overrides.
pub fn validate(data: &[u8], flat: &str, sections: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, SettingsError> {
    apply_sections(&apply_flat(data, flat)?, sections)
}

/// The non-empty items of a spec, so an empty spec or a trailing separator is no override.
fn items(spec: &str, sep: char) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
    spec.split(sep).filter(|item| !item.is_empty())
}

/// Splits `Key=Value` at the first `=`, so the value may hold more. `item` is the whole spec item, for the error.
fn key_value<'a>(item: &str, kv: &'a str) -> Result<(&'a str, &'a str), SettingsError> {
    match kv.split_once('=') {
        Some((key, value))
            if !key.is_empty() && !key.starts_with('[') && !kv.contains(['\r', '\n']) =>
        {
            Ok((key, value))
        }
        _ => Err(SettingsError::BadItem(item.into())),
    }
}

/// A line of the file: `start..end` is its text without the line break (a `\r` before the `\n` belongs to the break),
/// `next` is where the following line starts, and `eol` says whether it ends in `\n` (the last line may not).
struct Line {
    start: usize,
    end: usize,
    next: usize,
    eol: bool,
}

fn lines(data: &[u8]) -> impl Iterator<Item = Line> + '_ {
    let mut start = 0;
    std::iter::from_fn(move || {
        if start == data.len() {
            return None;
        }
        let nl = data[start..]
            .iter()
            .position(|&b| b == b'\n')
            .map(|i| start + i);
        let next = nl.map_or(data.len(), |i| i + 1);
        let mut end = nl.unwrap_or(data.len());
        if end > start && data[end - 1] == b'\r' {
            end -= 1;
        }
        let line = Line {
            start,
            end,
            next,
            eol: nl.is_some(),
        };
        start = next;
        Some(line)
    })
}

/// Where the value of `line` is, if the line starts with `key=`.
fn value_of(data: &[u8], line: &Line, key: &str) -> Option<Range<usize>> {
    let text = &data[line.start..line.end];
    (text.starts_with(key.as_bytes()) && text.get(key.len()) == Some(&b'='))
        .then_some(line.start + key.len() + 1..line.end)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A synthetic settings file: `MotionBlur` is in two sections, `[Empty]` has no keys.
    const LF: &str = "[Rendering]\nAllowFG=true\nMotionBlur=true\n[Rendering/MtRender]\nThreads=4\n\
                      [Empty]\n[Gameplay]\nAutoRotate=true\nMotionBlur=false\n";

    fn crlf(text: &str) -> String {
        text.replace('\n', "\r\n")
    }

    fn flat(data: &str, spec: &str) -> Result<String, SettingsError> {
        apply_flat(data.as_bytes(), spec).map(|out| String::from_utf8(out).unwrap())
    }

    fn sections(data: &str, spec: &str) -> Result<String, SettingsError> {
        apply_sections(data.as_bytes(), spec).map(|out| String::from_utf8(out).unwrap())
    }

    #[test]
    fn flat_replaces_one_value_and_nothing_else() {
        let want = LF.replace("AllowFG=true", "AllowFG=false");
        assert_eq!(flat(LF, "AllowFG=false").unwrap(), want);
        assert_eq!(flat(&crlf(LF), "AllowFG=false").unwrap(), crlf(&want));
    }

    #[test]
    fn flat_needs_exactly_one_line_per_key() {
        let missing = flat(LF, "AllowFG=false,Missing=1").unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            missing,
            SettingsError::KeyCount {
                key: "Missing".into(),
                found: 0
            }
        );
        assert!(missing.to_string().contains("\"Missing\""));
        // A key repeated in another section is ambiguous for a flat override.
        let twice = flat(&crlf(LF), "MotionBlur=false").unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            twice,
            SettingsError::KeyCount {
                key: "MotionBlur".into(),
                found: 2
            }
        );
        assert!(twice.to_string().contains("\"MotionBlur\""));
    }

    #[test]
    fn flat_keys_match_literally_at_line_start() {
        let data = "Key=1\nKeyX=2\n Indented=3\nkey=4\nA.B=5\nSpaced = 6\nA*=7\n";
        assert_eq!(flat(data, "Key=9").unwrap(), data.replace("Key=1", "Key=9"));
        assert_eq!(flat(data, "A.B=0").unwrap(), data.replace("A.B=5", "A.B=0"));
        assert_eq!(flat(data, "A*=0").unwrap(), data.replace("A*=7", "A*=0"));
        for key in ["Indented", "Spaced", "KEY", "A"] {
            let err = flat(data, &format!("{key}=0")).unwrap_err();
            assert_eq!(
                err,
                SettingsError::KeyCount {
                    key: key.into(),
                    found: 0
                }
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn flat_applies_in_order_so_the_later_value_wins() {
        let out = flat(LF, "AllowFG=1,Threads=8,AllowFG=2").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            out,
            LF.replace("AllowFG=true", "AllowFG=2")
                .replace("Threads=4", "Threads=8")
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn values_are_literal() {
        let value = r"a\1\\b$0${x}=c\n";
        let out = flat(LF, &format!("Threads={value}")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out, LF.replace("Threads=4", &format!("Threads={value}")));
        let out = sections(
            LF,
            &format!("Gameplay:MotionBlur={value};Empty:New={value}"),
        )
        .unwrap();
        let want = LF
            .replace("MotionBlur=false", &format!("MotionBlur={value}"))
            .replace("[Empty]\n", &format!("[Empty]\nNew={value}\n"));
        assert_eq!(out, want);
    }

    #[test]
    fn last_line_without_line_break() {
        assert_eq!(flat("A=1\nB=2", "B=3").unwrap(), "A=1\nB=3");
        assert_eq!(flat("A=1\r\nB=2\r", "B=3").unwrap(), "A=1\r\nB=3\r");
        assert_eq!(sections("[S]\nA=1", "S:A=2").unwrap(), "[S]\nA=2");
    }

    #[test]
    fn sections_replace_only_inside_their_section() {
        let want = LF.replace("MotionBlur=false", "MotionBlur=true");
        assert_eq!(sections(LF, "Gameplay:MotionBlur=true").unwrap(), want);
        let want = LF.replace("Threads=4", "Threads=2");
        assert_eq!(
            sections(&crlf(LF), "Rendering/MtRender:Threads=2").unwrap(),
            crlf(&want)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn sections_insert_right_after_the_header() {
        let want = LF.replace("[Gameplay]\n", "[Gameplay]\nHdr=1\n");
        assert_eq!(sections(LF, "Gameplay:Hdr=1").unwrap(), want);
        assert_eq!(sections(&crlf(LF), "Gameplay:Hdr=1").unwrap(), crlf(&want));
        // Any CRLF in the file makes the inserted line CRLF.
        assert_eq!(
            sections("[A]\nX=1\r\n", "A:Y=2").unwrap(),
            "[A]\nY=2\r\nX=1\r\n"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn sections_insert_into_an_empty_section() {
        let want = LF.replace("[Empty]\n", "[Empty]\nNew=1\n");
        assert_eq!(sections(LF, "Empty:New=1").unwrap(), want);
        assert_eq!(
            sections("[A]\nX=1\n[B]\n", "B:Y=2").unwrap(),
            "[A]\nX=1\n[B]\nY=2\n"
        );
        assert_eq!(sections("[B]\r\n", "B:Y=2").unwrap(), "[B]\r\nY=2\r\n");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_missing_section_is_appended() {
        // Finding 63: a mod's menu group before its first run.
        assert_eq!(
            sections(LF, "NpcAvoid:Radius=8").unwrap(),
            format!("{LF}[NpcAvoid]\nRadius=8\n")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            sections(&crlf(LF), "NpcAvoid:Radius=8;NpcAvoid:On=1").unwrap(),
            crlf(&format!("{LF}[NpcAvoid]\nOn=1\nRadius=8\n"))
        );
        // A last line without a break gets the file's break first; an empty file gets just the section.
        assert_eq!(
            sections("[A]\r\nX=1", "B:Y=2").unwrap(),
            "[A]\r\nX=1\r\n[B]\r\nY=2\r\n"
        );
        assert_eq!(sections("", "A:B=1").unwrap(), "[A]\nB=1\n");
    }

    #[test]
    fn section_header_must_occur_once() {
        let none = |section: &str| SettingsError::SectionCount {
            section: section.into(),
            found: 0,
        };
        // A header but for case, spaces, a BOM or its line break: the game may read it as the section.
        assert_eq!(
            sections(LF, "rendering:A=1").unwrap_err(),
            none("rendering")
        );
        assert_eq!(sections("[A] \nX=1\n", "A:X=2").unwrap_err(), none("A"));
        assert_eq!(sections("X=1\n[A]", "A:X=2").unwrap_err(), none("A"));
        assert_eq!(
            sections("\u{feff}[A]\r\nX=1\r\n", "A:X=2").unwrap_err(),
            none("A")
        );
        let twice = sections("[A]\nX=1\n[A]\nY=1\n", "A:X=2").unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            twice,
            SettingsError::SectionCount {
                section: "A".into(),
                found: 2
            }
        );
        assert!(none("A").to_string().contains("[A]"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn section_key_may_occur_at_most_once() {
        let err = sections("[A]\nX=1\nX=2\n[B]\nX=3\n", "A:X=9").unwrap_err();
        let want = SettingsError::KeyInSection {
            section: "A".into(),
            key: "X".into(),
            found: 2,
        };
        assert_eq!(err, want);
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("\"X\"") && err.to_string().contains("[A]"));
        // A key repeated in other sections is fine.
        assert_eq!(
            sections("[A]\nX=1\n[B]\nX=3\n", "B:X=9").unwrap(),
            "[A]\nX=1\n[B]\nX=9\n"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn sections_apply_in_order_so_the_later_value_wins() {
        let out = sections(LF, "Gameplay:Hdr=1;Gameplay:Hdr=2;Rendering:AllowFG=0").unwrap();
        let want = LF
            .replace("[Gameplay]\n", "[Gameplay]\nHdr=2\n")
            .replace("AllowFG=true", "AllowFG=0");
        assert_eq!(out, want);
    }

    #[test]
    fn bad_items_are_refused() {
        for spec in [
            "NoEquals",
            "=1",
            "[Rendering]=1",
            "A=1\nB=2",
            "AllowFG=1,Threads",
        ] {
            let err = flat(LF, spec).unwrap_err();
            assert!(
                matches!(err, SettingsError::BadItem(_)),
                "{spec:?}: {err:?}"
            );
        }
        for spec in [
            "NoColon=1",
            ":A=1",
            "Gameplay:NoEquals",
            "Gameplay:=1",
            "Gameplay:A=1\r",
            "A\n:B=1",
        ] {
            let err = sections(LF, spec).unwrap_err();
            assert!(
                matches!(err, SettingsError::BadItem(_)),
                "{spec:?}: {err:?}"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_specs_change_nothing() {
        assert_eq!(flat(LF, "").unwrap(), LF);
        assert_eq!(
            flat(LF, ",AllowFG=0,").unwrap(),
            LF.replace("AllowFG=true", "AllowFG=0")
        );
        assert_eq!(sections(LF, ";;").unwrap(), LF);
        assert_eq!(validate(LF.as_bytes(), "", "").unwrap(), LF.as_bytes());
    }

    #[test]
    fn validate_runs_flat_then_sections() {
        let data = crlf(LF);
        let out = validate(
            data.as_bytes(),
            "Threads=8,AllowFG=false",
            "Rendering/MtRender:Threads=9;Gameplay:Hdr=1",
        );
        let want = LF
            .replace("Threads=4", "Threads=9")
            .replace("AllowFG=true", "AllowFG=false")
            .replace("[Gameplay]\n", "[Gameplay]\nHdr=1\n");
        assert_eq!(out.unwrap(), crlf(&want).into_bytes());
        // Either half refuses the whole override.
        let err = validate(data.as_bytes(), "AllowFG=false", "gameplay:A=1").unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            err,
            SettingsError::SectionCount {
                section: "gameplay".into(),
                found: 0
            }
        );
        let err = validate(data.as_bytes(), "Nope=1", "Gameplay:Hdr=1").unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            err,
            SettingsError::KeyCount {
                key: "Nope".into(),
                found: 0
            }
        );
    }
}

```

`crates/quen-core/src/stats.rs`:

```rs
//! PresentMon 2.x: one window's command line, its CSV stats, and the within-boot A/B verdict.
//!
//! The header row names the columns, matched without regard to case. Cells may be empty or `NA`; both are skipped. The
//! first [`SKIP_ROWS`] data rows are dropped because they can straddle the window's start (parity with the Python).
//! Percentiles interpolate linearly between ranks, as numpy's default does.

use serde::Serialize;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::fmt;

/// Data rows dropped from the start of every capture.
pub const SKIP_ROWS: usize = 5;

const FRAME: &str = "MsBetweenPresents";
const GPU_BUSY: &str = "MsGPUBusy";
const GPU_TIME: &str = "MsGPUTime";
const CPU_BUSY: &str = "MsCPUBusy";
const PRESENT_MODE: &str = "PresentMode";

/// One column's numeric cells after the drop.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct Summary {
    pub count: usize,
    pub mean: f64,
    pub median: f64,
    pub p95: f64,
}

/// One PresentMon window. An optional column is `None` when the header lacks it or no number is left in it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct Stats {
    /// MsBetweenPresents.
    pub frame_ms: Summary,
    /// MsGPUBusy.
    pub gpu_busy_ms: Option<Summary>,
    /// MsGPUTime.
    pub gpu_time_ms: Option<Summary>,
    /// MsCPUBusy.
    pub cpu_busy_ms: Option<Summary>,
    /// The most common PresentMode, the first seen on a tie; `None` when the column is missing or empty.
    pub present_mode: Option<String>,
    /// More than one PresentMode among the kept rows.
    pub present_mode_mixed: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub enum Verdict {
    #[serde(rename = "inside drift")]
    InsideDrift,
    #[serde(rename = "outside drift")]
    OutsideDrift,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct AbVerdict {
    /// Per label, the spread of its windows' mean frame times: |first − second| for the usual two windows.
    pub drift_ms: BTreeMap<String, f64>,
    /// The mean of the second label's window means minus the first label's.
    pub diff_ms: f64,
    pub verdict: Verdict,
    /// The PresentMode every window ran in.
    pub present_mode: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Error {
    /// Not a CSV table: no header, an unterminated quote, or a row whose width differs from the header's.
    Csv {
        line: usize,
        msg: String,
    },
    MissingColumn(&'static str),
    /// A cell of a used column is neither a finite number nor empty or `NA`.
    BadNumber {
        line: usize,
        column: &'static str,
        cell: String,
    },
    /// No frame time is left after the first [`SKIP_ROWS`] data rows.
    NoFrames {
        rows: usize,
    },
    /// The windows don't form an A/B run: not exactly two labels, or a label with one window.
    Order(String),
    /// A window's PresentMode is unknown, mixed, or differs from the others.
    PresentMode(String),
}

impl fmt::Display for Error {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Error::Csv { line, msg } => write!(f, "CSV line {line}: {msg}"),
            Error::MissingColumn(name) => write!(f, "the CSV has no {name} column"),
            Error::BadNumber { line, column, cell } => {
                write!(f, "CSV line {line}: {column} {cell:?} is not a number")
            }
            Error::NoFrames { rows } => write!(
                f,
                "no frame time after dropping {SKIP_ROWS} of {rows} data rows"
            ),
            Error::Order(msg) => write!(f, "not an A/B run: {msg}"),
            Error::PresentMode(msg) => write!(f, "present mode: {msg}"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for Error {}

/// PresentMon's command line for one window of `secs` on the process `pid`, its CSV to `csv`. The flags are
/// `ini_session.py perf`'s, with two differences: the target is the pid, never an image name (that would also record
/// another copy of the game), and the trace session is quen's own (`--session_name quen --stop_existing_session`), so a
/// session a killed run left can't block the next window and the user's own PresentMon session is never touched. `extra`
/// (perf's `W3_PM_FLAGS`) may hold only `--track_*` / `--no_track_*` switches, e.g. `--track_pc_latency` (the column
/// that tells real frames from generated ones) or `--track_frame_type`: the rest would change what or where it records.
pub fn presentmon_args(
    exe: &str,
    pid: u32,
    secs: u32,
    csv: &str,
    extra: &[String],
) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    let switch = |f: &str| {
        let name = f.strip_prefix("--no_track_").or(f.strip_prefix("--track_"));
        name.is_some_and(|n| !n.is_empty() && n.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c == '_'))
    };
    if let Some(bad) = extra.iter().find(|f| !switch(f)) {
        return Err(format!(
            "PresentMon flag {bad:?}: only --track_* and --no_track_* switches (quen sets the rest)"
        ));
    }
    let (pid, secs) = (pid.to_string(), secs.to_string());
    let mut argv: Vec<String> = [
        exe,
        "--process_id",
        &pid,
        "--timed",
        &secs,
        "--terminate_after_timed",
        "--output_file",
        csv,
        "--no_console_stats",
        "--session_name",
        "quen",
        "--stop_existing_session",
    ]
    .map(String::from)
    .into();
    argv.extend_from_slice(extra);
    Ok(argv)
}

/// The stats of one PresentMon CSV.
pub fn parse(csv: &str) -> Result<Stats, Error> {
    let mut records = records(csv)?.into_iter();
    let (_, header) = records.next().ok_or_else(|| Error::Csv {
        line: 1,
        msg: "no header row".into(),
    })?;
    let rows: Vec<_> = records.collect();
    if let Some((line, row)) = rows.iter().find(|(_, row)| row.len() != header.len()) {
        let msg = format!("{} fields, the header has {}", row.len(), header.len());
        return Err(Error::Csv { line: *line, msg });
    }
    let kept = rows.get(SKIP_ROWS..).unwrap_or_default();
    let column = |name: &str| {
        header
            .iter()
            .position(|h| h.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
    };
    let cells = |i: usize| {
        kept.iter()
            .map(move |(line, row)| (*line, row[i].trim()))
            .filter(|(_, cell)| !cell.is_empty() && *cell != "NA")
    };
    let summary = |name: &'static str| -> Result<Option<Summary>, Error> {
        let Some(i) = column(name) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let mut values = Vec::new();
        for (line, cell) in cells(i) {
            match cell.parse::<f64>() {
                Ok(v) if v.is_finite() => values.push(v),
                _ => {
                    return Err(Error::BadNumber {
                        line,
                        column: name,
                        cell: cell.into(),
                    });
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(summarise(values))
    };

    if column(FRAME).is_none() {
        return Err(Error::MissingColumn(FRAME));
    }
    let frame_ms = summary(FRAME)?.ok_or(Error::NoFrames { rows: rows.len() })?;
    let mut modes: Vec<(&str, usize)> = Vec::new();
    for (_, mode) in column(PRESENT_MODE).into_iter().flat_map(cells) {
        match modes.iter_mut().find(|(m, _)| *m == mode) {
            Some((_, n)) => *n += 1,
            None => modes.push((mode, 1)),
        }
    }
    // max_by_key returns the last of equal maxima; reversed, that is the first seen.
    let most = modes.iter().rev().max_by_key(|(_, n)| *n);
    Ok(Stats {
        frame_ms,
        gpu_busy_ms: summary(GPU_BUSY)?,
        gpu_time_ms: summary(GPU_TIME)?,
        cpu_busy_ms: summary(CPU_BUSY)?,
        present_mode: most.map(|(m, _)| m.to_string()),
        present_mode_mixed: modes.len() > 1,
    })
}

/// The verdict of an ordered run such as A,B,A,B or A,B,B,A. The first window's label is the baseline A; there must be
/// one other label, and each label needs two or more windows. "Outside drift" only if |diff| exceeds every label's drift.
pub fn ab_verdict<L: AsRef<str>>(windows: &[(L, Stats)]) -> Result<AbVerdict, Error> {
    let mut labels: Vec<(&str, Vec<f64>)> = Vec::new();
    let mut present_mode: Option<&str> = None;
    for (label, stats) in windows {
        let label = label.as_ref();
        let mode = match (&stats.present_mode, stats.present_mode_mixed) {
            (Some(mode), false) => mode.as_str(),
            (Some(_), true) => {
                return Err(Error::PresentMode(format!("window {label} mixed several")));
            }
            (None, _) => return Err(Error::PresentMode(format!("window {label} has none"))),
        };
        if let Some(first) = present_mode
            && first != mode
        {
            return Err(Error::PresentMode(format!(
                "window {label} ran in {mode:?}, an earlier one in {first:?}"
            )));
        }
        present_mode = Some(mode);
        match labels.iter_mut().find(|(l, _)| *l == label) {
            Some((_, means)) => means.push(stats.frame_ms.mean),
            None => labels.push((label, vec![stats.frame_ms.mean])),
        }
    }
    let [(_, a), (_, b)] = labels.as_slice() else {
        return Err(Error::Order(format!(
            "{} labels, expected two",
            labels.len()
        )));
    };
    if let Some((label, _)) = labels.iter().find(|(_, means)| means.len() < 2) {
        return Err(Error::Order(format!(
            "label {label} has one window, drift needs two"
        )));
    }
    let mean = |v: &[f64]| v.iter().sum::<f64>() / v.len() as f64;
    let spread = |v: &[f64]| {
        v.iter().copied().fold(f64::MIN, f64::max) - v.iter().copied().fold(f64::MAX, f64::min)
    };
    let diff_ms = mean(b) - mean(a);
    let drift_ms: BTreeMap<String, f64> = labels
        .iter()
        .map(|(l, means)| (l.to_string(), spread(means)))
        .collect();
    let outside = drift_ms.values().all(|drift| diff_ms.abs() > *drift);
    Ok(AbVerdict {
        drift_ms,
        diff_ms,
        verdict: if outside {
            Verdict::OutsideDrift
        } else {
            Verdict::InsideDrift
        },
        present_mode: present_mode.unwrap_or_default().to_string(),
    })
}

/// Count, mean, median and p95 (linear between ranks, numpy's default) of `values`; None when empty.
pub fn summarise(mut values: Vec<f64>) -> Option<Summary> {
    if values.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    values.sort_by(f64::total_cmp);
    let percentile = |q: f64| {
        let rank = q * (values.len() - 1) as f64;
        let (lo, hi) = (values[rank.floor() as usize], values[rank.ceil() as usize]);
        lo + (hi - lo) * rank.fract()
    };
    Some(Summary {
        count: values.len(),
        mean: values.iter().sum::<f64>() / values.len() as f64,
        median: percentile(0.5),
        p95: percentile(0.95),
    })
}

/// The non-blank records of a CSV text, each with the line it starts on. Handles quoted fields (`""` is a quote, and
/// commas and line breaks inside quotes are kept), CRLF and a UTF-8 BOM.
fn records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<(usize, Vec<String>)>, Error> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let (mut record, mut field) = (Vec::new(), String::new());
    let (mut line, mut start, mut quoted) = (1, 1, false);
    let mut chars = text
        .strip_prefix('\u{feff}')
        .unwrap_or(text)
        .chars()
        .peekable();
    let mut end_record = |record: &mut Vec<String>, field: &mut String, start: usize| {
        record.push(std::mem::take(field));
        let record = std::mem::take(record);
        if record != [""] {
            out.push((start, record));
        }
    };
    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
        if c == '\n' {
            line += 1;
        }
        match (quoted, c) {
            (true, '"') if chars.peek() == Some(&'"') => {
                chars.next();
                field.push('"');
            }
            (true, '"') => quoted = false,
            (true, _) => field.push(c),
            (false, '"') if field.is_empty() => quoted = true,
            (false, ',') => record.push(std::mem::take(&mut field)),
            (false, '\r') => {}
            (false, '\n') => {
                end_record(&mut record, &mut field, start);
                start = line;
            }
            (false, _) => field.push(c),
        }
    }
    if quoted {
        return Err(Error::Csv {
            line: start,
            msg: "unterminated quote".into(),
        });
    }
    end_record(&mut record, &mut field, start);
    Ok(out)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const HEADER: &str = "Application,ProcessID,SwapChainAddress,PresentRuntime,SyncInterval,PresentFlags,\
                          AllowsTearing,PresentMode,FrameType,CPUStartTime,MsBetweenSimulationStart,MsBetweenPresents,\
                          MsBetweenDisplayChange,MsInPresentAPI,MsUntilDisplayed,MsCPUBusy,MsCPUWait,MsGPULatency,\
                          MsGPUTime,MsGPUBusy,MsGPUWait";
    const FLIP: &str = "Hardware: Independent Flip";

    /// A synthetic PresentMon CSV: five warm-up rows of 999 ms, then one row per frame time. GPU busy is frame − 2,
    /// GPU time frame − 1, CPU busy frame / 2.
    fn csv(frames: &[f64], mode: &str) -> String {
        let row = |ms: f64| {
            format!(
                "game.exe,4242,0x0000000000ABCDEF,DXGI,0,0,1,{mode},Application,1234.5,NA,{ms},{ms},0.1,{ms},{},0.2,NA,{},{},0.3\n",
                ms / 2.0,
                ms - 1.0,
                ms - 2.0
            )
        };
        let mut out = format!("{HEADER}\n");
        for _ in 0..SKIP_ROWS {
            out += &row(999.0);
        }
        for &ms in frames {
            out += &row(ms);
        }
        out
    }

    fn close(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool {
        (a - b).abs() < 1e-9
    }

    #[test]
    fn presentmon_args_take_the_pid_and_only_track_switches() {

            [
                "pm.exe",
                "--process_id",
                "4242",
                "--timed",
                "15",
                "--terminate_after_timed",
                "--output_file",
                "a b.csv",
                "--no_console_stats",
                "--session_name",
                "quen",
                "--stop_existing_session",
                "--track_pc_latency",
                "--no_track_input",
            ]
        );
        for bad in [
            "--process_name",
            "--output_stdout",
            "--track_",
            "--track_PC",
            "-track_x",
            "",
        ] {
            let err = presentmon_args("pm.exe", 1, 1, "x.csv", &[bad.into()]).unwrap_err();
            assert!(err.contains("only --track_*"), "{bad}: {err}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn summarises_after_the_warm_up_rows() {
        let frames: Vec<f64> = (1..=10).map(f64::from).collect();
        let stats = parse(&csv(&frames, FLIP)).unwrap();
        let f = &stats.frame_ms;
        assert_eq!(f.count, 10);
        assert!(
            close(f.mean, 5.5) && close(f.median, 5.5) && close(f.p95, 9.55),
            "{f:?}"
        );
        let gpu = stats.gpu_busy_ms.unwrap();
        assert!(
            close(gpu.mean, 3.5) && close(gpu.median, 3.5) && close(gpu.p95, 7.55),
            "{gpu:?}"
        );
        assert!(close(stats.gpu_time_ms.unwrap().mean, 4.5));
        assert!(close(stats.cpu_busy_ms.unwrap().mean, 2.75));
        assert_eq!(stats.present_mode.as_deref(), Some(FLIP));
        assert!(!stats.present_mode_mixed);

        let one = parse(&csv(&[16.0], FLIP)).unwrap().frame_ms;
        assert_eq!(
            one,
            Summary {
                count: 1,
                mean: 16.0,
                median: 16.0,
                p95: 16.0
            }
        );
        let odd = parse(&csv(&[3.0, 1.0, 2.0], FLIP)).unwrap().frame_ms;
        assert!(close(odd.median, 2.0) && close(odd.p95, 2.9), "{odd:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn skips_na_and_empty_cells_and_absent_columns() {

MsBetweenPresents,MsGPUBusy,PresentMode,MsCPUBusy
1,1,Composed: Flip,NA
1,1,Composed: Flip,NA
1,1,Composed: Flip,NA
1,1,Composed: Flip,NA

10,NA,Composed: Flip,NA
20,,NA,
```
