//! The doc-reference scanner and the cleanup candidates (docs/intent.md, "Captures"), on synthetic docs and paths.

mod ledger_common;

use ledger_common::{boot, capture, game, rows};
use quen_core::ledger::{Error, Ledger, Ref, ScanSummary, Scanner};
use serde_json::json;

const ROOT: &str = r"D:\fixture\renodx\tmp\witcher3\cap";

const KNOWN: &[&str] = &[
    "ini/perf_A.csv",          // 0
    "ini/perf_B.csv",          // 1
    "ngfx/TAG/frame1.png",     // 2
    "ngfx/TAG/frame2.png",     // 3
    "ngfx/TAG/sub/trace.json", // 4
    "ngfx/OTHER/y.png",        // 5
    "glow_front.png",          // 6
    "glow_side.png",           // 7
];

/// What each reference in `text` matches, as (raw, known indices).
fn found(text: &str) -> Vec<(String, Vec<usize>)> {
    Scanner::new(ROOT, KNOWN)
        .unwrap()
        .refs(text)
        .into_iter()
        .map(|r| (r.raw, r.matches))
        .collect()
}

fn one(text: &str) -> Vec<usize> {
    let f = found(text);
    assert_eq!(f.len(), 1, "{text:?} gave {f:?}");
    f.into_iter().next().unwrap().1
}

#[test]

        "/d/fixture/renodx/tmp/witcher3/cap/glow_front.png",
        r"tmp\witcher3\cap\glow_front.png",
        r"%USERPROFILE%\renodx\tmp\witcher3\cap\glow_front.png",
        r"$env:USERPROFILE\renodx\tmp\witcher3\cap\glow_front.png",
        r#"Copy-Item "$ENV:UserProfile\renodx\tmp\witcher3\cap\glow_front.png" ."#,
        "~/renodx/tmp/witcher3/cap/glow_front.png",
        r"..\witcher3\cap\\glow_front.png",
        "./cap/GLOW_FRONT.PNG",
        "CAP/Glow_Front.png",

#[test]
fn references_are_cut_out_of_prose_markdown_code_and_json() {
    let text = "Shots: `cap/glow_front.png`, [side](cap/glow_side.png) and **cap/ini/perf_A.csv**.\n\

                OUT=cap/ngfx/TAG/frame1.png; echo 'cap/ngfx/TAG/frame2.png'";

            (2, r"cap\\ngfx\\OTHER\\y.png", &[5]),
            (2, "cap/glow_front.png", &[6]),
            (2, "cap/glow_side.png", &[7]),
            (3, "cap/ngfx/TAG/frame1.png", &[2]),
            (3, "cap/ngfx/TAG/frame2.png", &[3]),

#[test]
fn globs_and_braces_expand_against_the_known_paths() {
    assert_eq!(one("cap/*.png"), [6, 7], "* doesn't cross a separator");
    assert_eq!(one("cap/glow_*.png"), [6, 7]);
    assert_eq!(one("cap/ngfx/*/frame*.png"), [2, 3]);
    assert_eq!(one("cap/ngfx/*/"), [2, 3, 4, 5]);
    assert_eq!(one("cap/ngfx/T*"), [2, 3, 4], "a glob may name folders");
    assert_eq!(one("cap/ini/perf_{A,B}.csv"), [0, 1]);
    assert_eq!(
        one("cap/{glow_{front,side}.png,ini/perf_A.csv}"),
        [0, 6, 7],
        "nested"
    );
    assert_eq!(one("cap/{ngfx/OTHER,ini}/*"), [0, 1, 5]);
    assert_eq!(
        one("cap/glow_{front,missing}.png"),
        [6],
        "one alternative is enough"
    );
    assert!(
        one("cap/glow_{front}.png").is_empty(),
        "a group without a comma is literal"
    );
    assert!(
        one("cap/ini/perf_{A,B.csv").is_empty(),
        "an unclosed group is literal"
    );
    let start = std::time::Instant::now();
    assert!(one(&format!("cap/{}z", "*g".repeat(40))).is_empty());
    assert_eq!(one(&format!("cap/{}*.png", "*".repeat(40))), [6, 7]);
    assert!(
        start.elapsed() < std::time::Duration::from_secs(2),
        "many stars stay cheap"
    );
}

const NOW: &str = "2026-10-17T12:00:00Z";
const OLD: &str = "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z";

struct Fixture {
    l: Ledger,
    ids: Vec<(&'static str, i64)>,
}

impl Fixture {
    fn id(&self, path: &str) -> i64 {
        self.ids.iter().find(|(p, _)| *p == path).unwrap().1
    }

    fn candidates(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        self.l
            .cleanup_candidates(NOW, 30, &[r"INI\ORIG\", "tpl_menu_"])
            .unwrap()
            .into_iter()
            .map(|c| c.path)
            .collect()
    }
}

/// One capture per cleanup rule, plus two plain old ones from a reviewed boot.
fn fixture() -> Fixture {
    let mut l = Ledger::open_in_memory().unwrap();
    let g = game(&mut l);
    let reviewed = boot(&mut l, g, "2026-08-30T10:00:00Z");
    l.review(reviewed, "2026-09-02T09:00:00Z").unwrap();
    let unreviewed = boot(&mut l, g, "2026-08-31T10:00:00Z");
    let mut ids = Vec::new();
    for (path, boot, t) in [
        ("a.png", Some(reviewed), OLD),
        ("b.png", Some(reviewed), OLD),
        ("ini/orig/general.ini", Some(reviewed), OLD),
        ("tpl_menu_load.png", Some(reviewed), OLD),
        ("recent.png", Some(reviewed), "2026-10-10T00:00:00Z"),
        ("thirty_days.png", Some(reviewed), "2026-09-17T12:00:00Z"),
        ("unreviewed.png", Some(unreviewed), OLD),
        ("no_boot.png", None, OLD),
    ] {
        ids.push((path, capture(&mut l, boot, path, t)));
    }
    let pinned = l
        .add_capture(&quen_core::ledger::Capture {
            boot_id: Some(reviewed),
            path: "pinned.png".into(),
            sha256: ledger_common::sha(4),
            kind: "png".into(),
            t: OLD.into(),
            pinned: true,
            ..Default::default()
        })
        .unwrap();
    ids.push(("pinned.png", pinned));
    Fixture { l, ids }
}

#[test]
fn cleanup_lists_only_unreferenced_unpinned_old_reviewed_captures() {
    let f = fixture();
    assert_eq!(f.candidates(), ["a.png", "b.png"]);
    assert!(matches!(
        f.l.cleanup_candidates("yesterday", 30, &[]),
        Err(Error::Refused(_))
    ));
    let all = f.l.cleanup_candidates(NOW, 30, &[]).unwrap();
    let paths: Vec<&str> = all.iter().map(|c| c.path.as_str()).collect();
    assert_eq!(
        paths,
        [
            "a.png",
            "b.png",
            "ini/orig/general.ini",
            "tpl_menu_load.png"
        ],
        "without hard pins"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        (all[0].capture_id, all[0].bytes, all[0].t.as_str()),
        (f.id("a.png"), 1024, OLD)
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_capture_added_after_the_review_was_not_reviewed() {
    let mut f = fixture();
    let b = rows(
        &f.l,
        "SELECT boot_id FROM captures WHERE path = 'a.png'",
        &[],
    )[0][0]
        .as_i64();
    // The fixture's boot was reviewed at 2026-09-02T09:00:00Z.
    capture(&mut f.l, b, "at_review.png", "2026-09-02T09:00:00Z");
    capture(&mut f.l, b, "after_review.png", "2026-09-02T09:00:01Z");
    assert_eq!(f.candidates(), ["a.png", "b.png", "at_review.png"]);
}

#[test]
fn scanning_records_references_and_a_rescan_replaces_them() {
    let mut f = fixture();
    let docs = [
        (
            "PROGRESS.md",
            "Kept: cap/a.png and cap/gone.png\n\nAll old ones: cap/{b,zzz}.png\n",
        ),
        ("cap/run.sh", "cp out.png $ROOT/cap/x.png\nls cap/*.png"),
    ];
    let summary = f.l.scan_docs(&docs, ROOT, NOW).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        summary,
        ScanSummary {
            docs: 2,
            refs: 5,
            dangling: 2
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(
        f.candidates(),
        [] as [&str; 0],
        "a.png and b.png are referenced"
    );

    let progress = rows(
        &f.l,
        "SELECT line, raw, capture_id, dangling, t_scanned FROM doc_refs WHERE doc_path = 'PROGRESS.md' ORDER BY id",
        &[],
    );
    assert_eq!(
        progress,
        [
            vec![
                json!(1),
                json!("cap/a.png"),
                json!(f.id("a.png")),
                json!(0),
                json!(NOW)
            ],
            vec![
                json!(1),
                json!("cap/gone.png"),
                json!(null),
                json!(1),
                json!(NOW)
            ],
            vec![
                json!(3),
                json!("cap/{b,zzz}.png"),
                json!(f.id("b.png")),
                json!(0),
                json!(NOW)
            ],
        ]
    );
    let glob_rows = rows(
        &f.l,
        "SELECT count(*) FROM doc_refs WHERE doc_path = 'cap/run.sh'",
        &[],
    );
    assert_eq!(
        glob_rows,
        [vec![json!(9)]],
        "cap/*.png matches the 8 top-level pngs; $ROOT/cap/x.png is a dangling reference"
    );

    // The edited PROGRESS.md no longer mentions a.png; run.sh still references both through its glob.
    f.l.scan_docs(
        &[("PROGRESS.md", "Only cap/b.png now")],
        ROOT,
        "2026-10-17T13:00:00Z",
    )
    .unwrap();
    let progress = rows(
        &f.l,
        "SELECT raw, dangling FROM doc_refs WHERE doc_path = 'PROGRESS.md'",
        &[],
    );
    assert_eq!(progress, [vec![json!("cap/b.png"), json!(0)]]);
    assert_eq!(f.candidates(), [] as [&str; 0]);
    f.l.scan_docs(&[("cap/run.sh", "")], ROOT, "2026-10-17T13:00:00Z")
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(f.candidates(), ["a.png"], "b.png is still in PROGRESS.md");
}

#[test]
fn a_refused_scan_leaves_the_rows_alone() {
    let mut f = fixture();
    f.l.scan_docs(&[("PROGRESS.md", "cap/a.png")], ROOT, NOW)
        .unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        f.l.scan_docs(&[("PROGRESS.md", "")], r"D:\", NOW),
        Err(Error::Refused(_))
    ));
    assert!(
        f.l.scan_docs(&[("PROGRESS.md", "")], ROOT, "not a time")
            .is_err()
    );
    let left = rows(&f.l, "SELECT raw FROM doc_refs", &[]);
    assert_eq!(left, [vec![json!("cap/a.png")]]);
}

`crates/quen-core/tests/ledger_sweeps.rs`:

```rs
//! Camera sweeps in the ledger (schema 0006): stored canonical once by name, their keyframes'
//! poses, and their runs frame by frame.

mod ledger_common;

use ledger_common::{TempDb, boot, capture, game, rows, sha};
use quen_core::journal::sha256_hex;
use quen_core::ledger::{
    Error, Ledger, Pose, Row, SCHEMA_VERSION, Save, Sweep, SweepFrame, SweepRun,
};
use quen_core::sweep::{self, Mode};
use rusqlite::Connection;
use serde_json::{Value, json};

#[track_caller]
fn refused<T: std::fmt::Debug>(r: Result<T, Error>, needle: &str) {
    match r {
        Err(Error::Refused(why)) => assert!(why.contains(needle), "{why:?} lacks {needle:?}"),
        other => panic!("expected a refusal about {needle:?}, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

/// A 7 s sweep through a synthetic room, written as an agent might: yaw 350 and roll -180 are canonical -10 and 180.
fn room() -> sweep::Sweep {
    serde_json::from_value(json!({
        "keyframes": [
            {"t": 0, "pos": [100, 200, 10], "rot": [-5, 350, -180], "fov": 60},
            {"t": 2, "pos": [103, 201, 10.5], "rot": [0, 10, -180], "fov": 60, "ease": "ease_in_out"},
            {"t": 7, "pos": [98, 205, 11], "rot": [0, 60, -180], "fov": 50}
        ],
        "world": {"save": "synthetic save", "time": {"day": 2, "hour": 22}, "paused": true}
    }))
    .unwrap()
}

fn pose(l: &mut Ledger, name: &str) -> i64 {
    l.add_pose(&Pose {
        name: name.into(),
        camera: [100.0, 200.0, 10.0],
        rotation: [-5.0, -10.0, 180.0],
        fov: 60.0,
        ..Default::default()
    })
    .unwrap()
}

fn count(l: &Ledger, table: &str) -> Value {
    rows(l, &format!("SELECT count(*) FROM {table}"), &[])[0][0].clone()
}

#[test]
fn a_sweep_is_stored_canonical_once_by_name() {
    let mut l = Ledger::open_in_memory().unwrap();
    let g = game(&mut l);
    let save = l
        .add_save(&Save {
            game_id: g,
            file: "synthetic save.sav".into(),
            sha256: sha(5),
            ..Default::default()
        })
        .unwrap();
    let (p0, p2) = (pose(&mut l, "room 0"), pose(&mut l, "room 2"));
    let row = Sweep {
        name: "room pan".into(),
        sweep: room(),
        save_id: Some(save),
        poses: vec![Some(p0), None, Some(p2)],
        note: Some("synthetic".into()),
    };
    let id = l.add_sweep(&row).unwrap();

    let canonical = room().canonical().unwrap().to_json();
    assert!(
        canonical.contains(r#""rot":[-5.0,-10.0,180.0]"#),
        "{canonical}"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        rows(
            &l,
            "SELECT name, sha256, sweep, save_id, note FROM sweeps",
            &[]
        ),
        vec![vec![
            json!("room pan"),
            json!(sha256_hex(canonical.as_bytes())),
            json!(canonical),
            json!(save),
            json!("synthetic")
        ]]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        rows(
            &l,
            "SELECT sweep_id, keyframe, pose_id FROM sweep_keyframes ORDER BY keyframe",
            &[]
        ),
        vec![
            vec![json!(id), json!(0), json!(p0)],
            vec![json!(id), json!(2), json!(p2)]
        ]
    );

    // The same sweep under its name again, even spelled differently: the same row, nothing added.
    let again = Sweep {
        sweep: room().canonical().unwrap(),
        poses: vec![],
        ..row.clone()
    };
    assert_eq!(l.add_sweep(&again).unwrap(), id);
    assert_eq!(
        (count(&l, "sweeps"), count(&l, "sweep_keyframes")),
        (json!(1), json!(2))
    );

    // Another sweep under that name, a broken sweep, or a pose list that doesn't match: refused, nothing written.
    let mut other = row.clone();
    other.sweep.keyframes[2].fov = 55.0;
    refused(l.add_sweep(&other), "name this one anew");
    let mut broken = row.clone();
    broken.name = "broken".into();
    broken.sweep.keyframes.truncate(1);
    refused(l.add_sweep(&broken), "1 keyframes");
    let mut short = row.clone();
    short.name = "short".into();
    short.poses.pop();
    refused(l.add_sweep(&short), "2 poses for 3 keyframes");
    assert_eq!(
        (count(&l, "sweeps"), count(&l, "sweep_keyframes")),
        (json!(1), json!(2))
    );

    // The same path under a second name shares the hash.
    let twin = l
        .add_sweep(&Sweep {
            name: "room pan, again".into(),
            poses: vec![],
            ..row
        })
        .unwrap();
    assert_ne!(twin, id);
    let shas = rows(&l, "SELECT count(DISTINCT sha256) FROM sweeps", &[]);
    assert_eq!(shas, vec![vec![json!(1)]]);
}

#[test]
fn runs_hold_their_frames_and_nothing_past_the_end() {
    let mut l = Ledger::open_in_memory().unwrap();
    let g = game(&mut l);
    let b = boot(&mut l, g, "2026-10-17T20:00:00Z");
    let s = l
        .add_sweep(&Sweep {
            name: "room pan".into(),
            sweep: room(),
            save_id: None,
            poses: vec![],
            note: None,
        })
        .unwrap();
    let run = |l: &mut Ledger, mode: Mode, fps: Option<u32>| {
        l.add_sweep_run(&SweepRun {
            sweep_id: s,
            boot_id: Some(b),
            mode,
            fps,
            t: "2026-10-17T20:05:00Z".into(),
        })
    };
    let live = run(&mut l, Mode::Realtime, None).unwrap();
    let step = run(&mut l, Mode::Step, Some(30)).unwrap();
    refused(run(&mut l, Mode::Step, None), "step with fps None");
    refused(run(&mut l, Mode::Realtime, Some(30)), "realtime with fps");
    refused(
        run(&mut l, Mode::Step, Some(sweep::MAX_FPS + 1)),
        "1 to 240",
    );
    assert!(
        l.add_sweep_run(&SweepRun {
            sweep_id: s + 1,
            boot_id: None,
            mode: Mode::Realtime,
            fps: None,
            t: "2026-10-17T20:05:00Z".into()
        })
        .is_err(),
        "no such sweep"
    );
    assert_eq!(count(&l, "sweep_runs"), json!(2));

    // 7 s at 30 fps: frames 0 to 210.
    let c: Vec<i64> = (0..4)
        .map(|i| {
            capture(
                &mut l,
                Some(b),
                &format!("1/frame{i}.png"),
                "2026-10-17T20:06:00Z",
            )
        })
        .collect();
    let frame = |l: &mut Ledger, run_id: i64, frame: u32, capture_id: i64| {
        l.add_sweep_frame(&SweepFrame {
            run_id,
            frame,
            capture_id,
        })
    };
    frame(&mut l, step, 0, c[0]).unwrap();
    frame(&mut l, step, 210, c[1]).unwrap();
    refused(frame(&mut l, step, 211, c[2]), "its frames are 0 to 210");
    refused(frame(&mut l, live, 0, c[2]), "real time");
    refused(frame(&mut l, step + 5, 0, c[2]), "no sweep run");
    assert!(
        frame(&mut l, step, 1, c[0]).is_err(),
        "a capture is one frame"
    );
    assert!(
        frame(&mut l, step, 0, c[3]).is_err(),
        "a frame has one capture"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        rows(
            &l,
            "SELECT run_id, frame, capture_id FROM sweep_frames ORDER BY frame",
            &[]
        ),
        vec![
            vec![json!(step), json!(0), json!(c[0])],
            vec![json!(step), json!(210), json!(c[1])]
        ]
    );
}

#[test]
fn sweep_rows_ingest_from_json_and_runs_need_the_lock() {
    let mut l = Ledger::open_in_memory().unwrap();
    let parse = |v: Value| serde_json::from_value::<Row>(v).unwrap();
    let sweep = parse(json!({"table": "sweeps", "name": "room pan", "sweep": room()}));
    let run = parse(
        json!({"table": "sweep_runs", "sweep_id": 1, "boot_id": null, "mode": "step", "fps": 24,
        "t": "2026-10-17T20:05:00Z"}),
    );
    assert!(!sweep.needs_lock() && run.needs_lock());
    let ids = l.ingest(&[sweep, run]).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(ids, [Some(1), Some(1)]);
    let c = capture(&mut l, None, "frame0.png", "2026-10-17T20:06:00Z");
    let frame = parse(json!({"table": "sweep_frames", "run_id": 1, "frame": 168, "capture_id": c}));
    assert!(frame.needs_lock());
    assert_eq!(l.ingest(&[frame]).unwrap(), [None]);
    let late = parse(json!({"table": "sweep_frames", "run_id": 1, "frame": 169, "capture_id": c}));
    refused(l.ingest(&[late]), "row 0: frame 169 of sweep run 1");

    for bad in [
        json!({"table": "sweeps", "name": "x", "sweep": room(), "pose": []}),
        json!({"table": "sweep_runs", "sweep_id": 1, "boot_id": null, "mode": "slow", "fps": null, "t": "2026-10-17T20:05:00Z"}),
        json!({"table": "sweep_frames", "run_id": 1, "frame": -1, "capture_id": c}),
    ] {
        assert!(serde_json::from_value::<Row>(bad.clone()).is_err(), "{bad}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_schema_holds_without_the_rust_checks() {
    let db = TempDb::new();
    drop(Ledger::open(&db.0).unwrap());
    let c = Connection::open(&db.0).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        c.query_row("PRAGMA user_version", [], |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0))
            .unwrap(),
        SCHEMA_VERSION
    );
    let two = room().canonical().unwrap().to_json();
    c.execute(
        "INSERT INTO sweeps (id, name, sha256, sweep) VALUES (1, 'room', ?1, ?2)",
        [sha(1), two],
    )
    .unwrap();
    for sql in [
        // One keyframe, not JSON, a blank name.
        format!(
            "INSERT INTO sweeps (name, sha256, sweep) VALUES ('one', '{}', '{{\"keyframes\":[{{}}]}}')",
            sha(2)
        ),
        format!("INSERT INTO sweeps (name, sha256, sweep) VALUES ('bad', '{}', 'nope')", sha(2)),
        format!("INSERT INTO sweeps (name, sha256, sweep) VALUES (' ', '{}', '{{\"keyframes\":[1,2]}}')", sha(2)),
        // Step without fps, real time with one, an unknown mode, an fps out of range.
        "INSERT INTO sweep_runs (sweep_id, mode, t) VALUES (1, 'step', '2026-10-17T20:05:00Z')".into(),
        "INSERT INTO sweep_runs (sweep_id, mode, fps, t) VALUES (1, 'realtime', 30, '2026-10-17T20:05:00Z')".into(),
        "INSERT INTO sweep_runs (sweep_id, mode, t) VALUES (1, 'slow', '2026-10-17T20:05:00Z')".into(),
        "INSERT INTO sweep_runs (sweep_id, mode, fps, t) VALUES (1, 'step', 241, '2026-10-17T20:05:00Z')".into(),
        "INSERT INTO sweep_runs (sweep_id, mode, t) VALUES (1, 'realtime', '2026-10-17 20:05')".into(),
    ] {
        assert!(c.execute(&sql, []).is_err(), "{sql}");
    }
    c.execute(
        "INSERT INTO sweep_runs (sweep_id, mode, fps, t) VALUES (1, 'step', 240, '2026-10-17T20:05:00Z')",
        [],
    )
    .unwrap();
}

`crates/quen-core/tests/ledger_tools.rs`:

```rs
//! The core of the ledger tools: row batches for `ledger_ingest` / `quen ledger add`, and the import of the Python
//! harness's history, over a synthetic harness folder this test writes.

mod ledger_common;

use std::fs;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

use ledger_common::{TempDb, boot, game, rows, sha};
use quen_core::ledger::{Error, Harness, Ledger, Row, Summary};
use serde_json::{Value, json};

fn parse(rows: Value) -> Vec<Row> {
    serde_json::from_value(rows).unwrap()
}

#[test]
fn a_batch_is_written_whole_or_not_at_all() {
    let mut l = Ledger::open_in_memory().unwrap();
    let g = game(&mut l);
    let b = boot(&mut l, g, "2026-10-10T10:00:00Z");
    let m = json!({"table": "measurements", "boot_id": b, "capture_id": null, "metric": "frame_ms", "value": 23.1,
                   "unit": "ms", "state_label": "A", "method_family": "tracy", "tag": "M", "run_id": null, "note": null});
    let save = json!({"table": "saves", "game_id": g, "file": "Synthetic_1.sav", "sha256": sha(5)});
    let bad = json!({"table": "measurements", "boot_id": b, "capture_id": null, "metric": "frame_ms", "value": 1.0,
                     "unit": null, "state_label": null, "method_family": "Not A Family", "tag": "M", "run_id": null,
                     "note": null});

    let batch = parse(json!([m, save, bad]));
    assert!(batch[0].needs_lock() && !batch[1].needs_lock());
    match l.ingest(&batch) {
        Err(Error::Refused(why)) => assert!(why.starts_with("row 2: "), "{why}"),
        other => panic!("expected a refusal, got {other:?}"),
    }
    let count = "SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM measurements) + (SELECT count(*) FROM saves)";
    assert_eq!(rows(&l, count, &[]), [[json!(0)]]);

    let label = json!({"table": "mod_versions", "content_hash": sha(7), "kind": "asi", "name": "Synthetic",
                       "version": "1.0", "provenance": "nexus_file", "source": "Synthetic-1-0.zip"});
    let re =
        json!({"table": "re_refs", "target": {"measurement": 1}, "kb_path": "notes/synthetic.md"});
    let ids = l.ingest(&parse(json!([m, save, label, re]))).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(ids, [Some(1), Some(1), None, Some(1)]);

    let unknown =
        json!([{"table": "saves", "game_id": g, "file": "x.sav", "sha256": sha(6), "extra": 1}]);
    assert!(serde_json::from_value::<Vec<Row>>(unknown).is_err());
    assert!(serde_json::from_value::<Vec<Row>>(json!([{"table": "boots", "game_id": g}])).is_err());
}

/// A synthetic harness folder in the temp folder; the test's own files go with it.
struct Fixture(PathBuf);

impl Fixture {
    fn new(name: &str) -> Fixture {
        let dir =
            std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("quen-migrate-test-{}-{name}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir); // a leftover of this same test
        Fixture(dir)
    }

    fn put(&self, rel: &str, text: &str) {
        let path = self.0.join(rel);
        fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
        fs::write(path, text).unwrap();
    }

    fn harness(&self) -> Harness {
        Harness {
            dir: self.0.join("harness"),
            game_exe: self.0.join("game").join("game.exe"),
            gamesaves: Some(self.0.join("gamesaves")),
            doc_roots: vec![self.0.join("harness")],
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for Fixture {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0); // this test's own temp folder
    }
}

/// A local `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` for `secs`, as the harness writes its `t` fields.
fn local(l: &Ledger, secs: i64) -> String {
    let t = rows(
        l,
        "SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', ?1, 'unixepoch', 'localtime')",
        &[json!(secs)],
    );
    t[0][0].as_str().unwrap().into()
}

fn utc(secs: i64) -> String {
    let l = Ledger::open_in_memory().unwrap();
    let t = rows(
        &l,
        "SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', ?1, 'unixepoch')",
        &[json!(secs)],
    );
    t[0][0].as_str().unwrap().into()
}

fn mtime(fx: &Fixture, log: &str) -> i64 {
    let meta = fs::metadata(fx.0.join("harness").join("cap").join(log)).unwrap();
    meta.modified()
        .unwrap()
        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
        .unwrap()
        .as_secs() as i64
}

fn traceback(error: &str) -> String {
    format!(
        "boot failed, restored: {{}}\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n  File \"harness.py\", line 9, in boot\n    \
         raise\n{error}\n"
    )
}

#[test]
fn the_harness_history_is_imported_once() {
    let fx = Fixture::new("once");
    let now = SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
        .unwrap()
        .as_secs() as i64;
    let (t_ok, t_jsonl, t_failed) = (now - 1200, now - 600, now - 60);
    let scratch = Ledger::open_in_memory().unwrap();
    let ended = local(&scratch, t_jsonl + 120);

    let info = json!({"t_boot": t_ok as f64 + 0.25, "save": null, "quicksave": {"save": "Synthetic_1.sav"},
                      "no_devkit": true, "parked": ["modSynthetic"]});

                unread,

                null,
                null,
                "perf_boot_failed.log"
            ],
            [
                utc(failed2),
                utc(failed2),

    assert_eq!(saves[0][..2], [json!("Synthetic_1.sav"), json!("1 | hut")]);

        ]

    // A second run adds nothing; a new boot record is the only addition after that.
    let again = l.plan_migration(&h).unwrap().summary;
    assert_eq!(
        (
            again.files_new,
            again.boots_new,
            again.saves_new,
            again.files_changed
        ),
        (0, 0, 0, 0)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        l.apply_migration(&h, l.plan_migration(&h).unwrap())
            .unwrap()
            .refs,
        2
    );
    assert_eq!(rows(&l, "SELECT count(*) FROM boots", &[]), [[json!(5)]]);
    let more = json!({"event": "boot", "t_boot": now as f64 + 5.0});
    fx.put(
        "harness/cap/boots.jsonl",
        &(jsonl.join("\n") + "\n" + &more.to_string() + "\n"),
    );
    let later = l.plan_migration(&h).unwrap().summary;
    assert_eq!(
        (
            later.files_new,
            later.files_changed,
            later.boots_new,
            later.jsonl_boots
        ),
        (0, 1, 1, 3)
    );

    fx.put("harness/cap/ini/session.lock", "{}");
    match l.apply_migration(&h, l.plan_migration(&h).unwrap()) {
        Err(Error::Refused(why)) => assert!(why.contains("session.lock"), "{why}"),
        other => panic!("expected a refusal, got {other:?}"),
    }
    assert_eq!(rows(&l, "SELECT count(*) FROM boots", &[]), [[json!(5)]]);
}

//! ledger is backed up before its first migration, and a ledger from every older version comes through with its rows.

/// The migrations in `schema/`, in order: (file name, text).
fn migrations() -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let dir = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../schema");
    let mut files: Vec<(String, String)> = fs::read_dir(&dir)
        .unwrap()
        .map(|e| e.unwrap().file_name().into_string().unwrap())
        .filter(|name| name.ends_with(".sql"))
        .map(|name| {
            let text = fs::read_to_string(dir.join(&name)).unwrap();
            (name, text)
        })
        .collect();
    files.sort();
    files
}

#[test]
fn shipped_migrations_are_never_edited() {
    let files = migrations();
    for (i, (name, text)) in files.iter().enumerate() {
        assert!(
            name.starts_with(&format!("{:04}_", i + 1)),
            "schema/{name}: migrations are numbered 0001, 0002, ... without gaps"
        );
        let sha = sha256_hex(text.as_bytes());
        match SHIPPED.iter().find(|(pinned, _)| pinned == name) {
            Some((_, pin)) => assert_eq!(
                &sha, pin,
                "schema/{name} changed after it shipped: restore it and put the change in a new migration"
            ),
            None => panic!(
                "schema/{name} has no pin: add (\"{name}\", \"{sha}\") to SHIPPED; from then on it never changes"
            ),
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(files.len(), SHIPPED.len(), "a pinned migration is gone");
    assert_eq!(
        files.len() as i64,
        SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "ledger.rs's MIGRATIONS embeds every file in schema/"
    );
}

/// A ledger at schema version `k` as a quen of that version left it: the first `k` migrations, WAL, and synthetic rows
/// in every table it has. The connection stays open, so the rows may still be in the WAL.
fn old_ledger(path: &Path, k: usize) -> Connection {
    let c = Connection::open(path).unwrap();
    for (_, sql) in &migrations()[..k] {
        c.execute_batch(sql).unwrap();
    }
    c.pragma_update(None, "user_version", k as i64).unwrap();

        .unwrap();
    let entries = if k == 1 {
        // 0001's shape: name, a free-text kind and sha256.

               VALUES (1, 'W3Perf', 'asi', '{}', 0), (1, 'modAlpha', 'mod', '{}', 1);",
            sha(5),
            sha(6)

    } else {
        format!(
            "INSERT INTO mod_set_entries (mod_set_id, kind, name, parked, home, content_hash, file_count, bytes,

           VALUES (1, 1, 'shots/P1_a.png', '{c}', 10, 'screenshot', 'printwindow', 'srgb8', 1, '2026-10-10T10:30:00Z'),

/// Every row of some tables: (table, its rows ordered by the columns asked for).
type Snapshot = Vec<(String, Vec<Vec<Sql>>)>;

/// The tables of `c` and their column names.
fn columns(c: &Connection) -> Vec<(String, Vec<String>)> {
    let mut stmt = c
        .prepare(
            "SELECT m.name, group_concat(p.name, ',' ORDER BY p.cid) FROM sqlite_schema m, pragma_table_info(m.name) p
             WHERE m.type = 'table' GROUP BY m.name ORDER BY m.name",
        )
        .unwrap();
    stmt.query_map([], |r| {
        let cols: String = r.get(1)?;
        Ok((r.get(0)?, cols.split(',').map(String::from).collect()))
    })
    .unwrap()
    .map(Result::unwrap)
    .collect()
}

fn snapshot(c: &Connection, tables: &[(String, Vec<String>)]) -> Snapshot {
    tables
        .iter()
        .map(|(table, cols)| {
            let list = cols.join(", ");
            let mut stmt = c
                .prepare(&format!("SELECT {list} FROM {table} ORDER BY {list}"))
                .unwrap();
            let rows = stmt
                .query_map([], |r| {
                    (0..cols.len()).map(|i| r.get::<_, Sql>(i)).collect()
                })
                .unwrap()
                .map(Result::unwrap)
                .collect();
            (table.clone(), rows)
        })
        .collect()
}

/// The files in the ledger's backups folder.
fn backups(db: &TempDb) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let mut files: Vec<PathBuf> = match fs::read_dir(db.dir().join("backups")) {
        Ok(dir) => dir.map(|e| e.unwrap().path()).collect(),
        Err(_) => vec![],
    };
    files.sort();
    files
}

#[test]
fn a_ledger_from_every_older_version_upgrades_after_a_backup() {
    const { assert!(SCHEMA_VERSION >= 2) };
    for k in 1..SCHEMA_VERSION as usize {
        let db = TempDb::new();
        let old = old_ledger(&db.0, k);
        let tables = columns(&old);
        let before = snapshot(&old, &tables);
        assert!(
            before.iter().all(|(_, rows)| !rows.is_empty()),
            "v{k}: every table has rows"
        );

        let l = Ledger::open(&db.0).unwrap();
        drop(old);
        let version = rows(&l, "SELECT user_version FROM pragma_user_version", &[]);
        assert_eq!(version, vec![vec![json!(SCHEMA_VERSION)]], "v{k}");

        // The backup: one file, named for the old version and the time, holding the ledger as it was.
        let files = backups(&db);
        assert_eq!(files.len(), 1, "v{k}: {files:?}");
        let name = files[0].file_name().unwrap().to_str().unwrap().to_string();
        let stamp = name
            .strip_prefix(&format!("quen-v{k}-"))
            .and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix(".db"))
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("v{k}: backup named {name}"));
        assert!(
            stamp.len() == 16
                && stamp.as_bytes()[8] == b'T'
                && stamp.ends_with('Z')
                && stamp.chars().filter(char::is_ascii_digit).count() == 14,
            "v{k}: {stamp} is a UTC time"
        );
        let backup = Ledger::open_readonly(&files[0]).unwrap();
        let backed_up = rows(&backup, "SELECT user_version FROM pragma_user_version", &[]);
        assert_eq!(
            backed_up,
            vec![vec![json!(k)]],
            "v{k}: the backup opens at its version"
        );
        drop(backup);
        let raw = Connection::open_with_flags(&files[0], OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            snapshot(&raw, &tables),
            before,
            "v{k}: the backup holds every row"
        );
        drop(raw);

        // Every row survives the migrations; 0002 renamed mod_set_entries.sha256 to content_hash.
        let now = Connection::open(&db.0).unwrap();
        let renamed: Vec<(String, Vec<String>)> = tables
            .iter()
            .map(|(table, cols)| {
                let cols = cols
                    .iter()

                        ("mod_set_entries", "sha256") => "content_hash".to_string(),
                        _ => c.clone(),

        let fk: i64 = now
            .query_row("SELECT count(*) FROM pragma_foreign_key_check", [], |r| {

            })
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(fk, 0, "v{k}");
        // 0008: removed_to takes 'missing' too (feature tests 2c), and still no value outside its list.
        now.execute(

        )
        .unwrap();
        let other = "UPDATE captures SET removed_to = 'elsewhere' WHERE id = 1";
        assert!(now.execute(other, []).is_err(), "v{k}");
        drop(now);

        // The views work over the old rows.
        let conditions = rows(
            &l,

             ORDER BY boot_id",
            &[],
        );
        assert_eq!(
            conditions[0],
            [
                json!(1),
                json!(sha(1)),
                json!(sha(3)),
                json!(0),
                Value::Null,
                Value::Null,
                Value::Null
            ],
            "v{k}: a boot from before 0005 has busy unknown"
        );
        let comparison = rows(
            &l,
            "SELECT comparable, differs, unknown, busy, varies FROM boot_comparison WHERE a_id = 1 AND b_id = 2",
            &[],
        );
        let varies = if k >= 2 {
            "mod_status,settings"
        } else {
            "settings"
        };
        assert_eq!(
            comparison,
            vec![vec![
                json!(0),
                json!(""),
                json!("busy"),
                json!(""),
                json!(varies)
            ]],
            "v{k}"
        );

            &[],
        );
        assert_eq!(measured, vec![vec![json!(5), json!(4), json!(1)]], "v{k}");
        let captured = rows(
            &l,

        assert_eq!(
            captured,
            vec![vec![json!("P1"), json!("2026-10-10T10:00:00Z")]],
            "v{k}"
        );
        let claim = rows(

            &[],

        assert_eq!(
            claim,

                json!(1),
                json!("presentmon,static_re"),
                json!("re/notes/pools.md"),
                json!(2),
                json!(1)

            "v{k}"

        // 0009: an older claim has no key and no grades, and the knowledge tables start empty (a v9 ledger's hold its

             FROM claims",

        let knowledge = if k >= 9 { 3 } else { 0 };
        assert_eq!(
            graded,

                Value::Null,
                Value::Null,
                json!(knowledge)
            ]],
            "v{k}"
        );
        // 0010: an older save was made by nobody quen knows of; a new one can name its boot.
        let made = rows(&l, "SELECT made_by_boot FROM saves", &[]);

        let now = Connection::open(&db.0).unwrap();

            .unwrap();
        let unknown = "UPDATE saves SET made_by_boot = 99 WHERE id = 1";
        assert!(now.execute(unknown, []).is_err(), "v{k}: a boot that isn't");
        now.execute("UPDATE saves SET made_by_boot = NULL WHERE id = 1", [])
            .unwrap();
        // 0011: an older boot was a test launch and an older row's world unknown; a play boot never compares with one.
        let old = rows(

            .unwrap();

        // 0002's pairing of home, file count and bytes.
        now.pragma_update(None, "foreign_keys", true).unwrap();
        now.execute_batch(&format!(

               VALUES (1, 'bin', 'dsound.dll', 1, 'quen-parked/bin/dsound.dll', '{0}', 1, 5),

        now.execute_batch(&format!(

        drop(now);

                json!("B"),
                json!("outside drift")

            "v{k}"
        );
        drop(l);

        drop(Ledger::open(&db.0).unwrap());
        assert_eq!(

            files,
            "v{k}: a current ledger isn't backed up again"
        );
    }

#[test]
fn a_new_or_current_ledger_is_not_backed_up() {
    let db = TempDb::new();
    drop(Ledger::open(&db.0).unwrap());
    drop(Ledger::open(&db.0).unwrap());
    assert!(!db.dir().join("backups").exists());
}

fn refused(r: Result<Ledger, Error>, needle: &str) {
    match r {
        Err(Error::Refused(why)) => assert!(why.contains(needle), "{why:?} lacks {needle:?}"),
        Err(e) => panic!("expected a refusal about {needle:?}, got {e}"),
        Ok(_) => panic!("expected a refusal about {needle:?}, got a ledger"),
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_failed_backup_refuses_and_changes_nothing() {
    let k = SCHEMA_VERSION as usize - 1;
    let db = TempDb::new();
    let old = old_ledger(&db.0, k);
    let tables = columns(&old);
    let before = snapshot(&old, &tables);
    drop(old);

    // The backups folder can't be made: a file has its name.
    let blocker = db.dir().join("backups");
    fs::write(&blocker, "not a folder").unwrap();
    refused(Ledger::open(&db.0), "backed up");
    assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(&blocker).unwrap(), "not a folder");
    let raw = Connection::open(&db.0).unwrap();
    let version: i64 = raw
        .query_row("PRAGMA user_version", [], |r| r.get(0))
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(version, k as i64, "not migrated");
    assert_eq!(snapshot(&raw, &tables), before);
    drop(raw);
    fs::remove_file(&blocker).unwrap();

    // A backup is never replaced: a file already named for this second is kept, and the open refused. The names are
    // taken for the next minute, so the open below falls inside them.
    fs::create_dir(&blocker).unwrap();
    let clock = Connection::open_in_memory().unwrap();
    let names: Vec<PathBuf> = (0..60)
        .map(|s| {
            let t: String = clock
                .query_row(
                    "SELECT strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ', 'now', ?1 || ' seconds')",
                    [s],
                    |r| r.get(0),
                )
                .unwrap();
            blocker.join(format!("quen-v{k}-{t}.db"))
        })
        .collect();
    for name in &names {
        fs::write(name, "an earlier backup").unwrap();
    }
    refused(Ledger::open(&db.0), "backed up");
    for name in &names {
        assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(name).unwrap(), "an earlier backup");
    }
    assert_eq!(backups(&db).len(), names.len(), "no other file");
    let raw = Connection::open(&db.0).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(snapshot(&raw, &tables), before);
    drop(raw);

    // Once the backup can be made, the upgrade goes ahead.
    for name in &names {
        fs::remove_file(name).unwrap();
    }
    let l = Ledger::open(&db.0).unwrap();
    let version = rows(&l, "SELECT user_version FROM pragma_user_version", &[]);
    assert_eq!(version, vec![vec![json!(SCHEMA_VERSION)]]);
    assert_eq!(backups(&db).len(), 1);
}

#[test]
fn readonly_connections_refuse_a_newer_ledger_and_read_an_older_one() {
    let db = TempDb::new();
    drop(old_ledger(&db.0, 1));
    let r = Ledger::open_readonly(&db.0).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        rows(&r, "SELECT user_version FROM pragma_user_version", &[]),
        vec![vec![json!(1)]],
        "read as it is, not migrated"
    );
    drop(r);
    assert!(backups(&db).is_empty());
    Connection::open(&db.0)
        .unwrap()
        .pragma_update(None, "user_version", SCHEMA_VERSION + 1)
        .unwrap();
    refused(Ledger::open_readonly(&db.0), "newer");
}

`crates/quen-core/tests/ledger_views.rs`:

```rs
//! The investigation views (schema 0005) and `ledger::schema_description`: the description names
//! every table, view and column, and each of its example queries answers its question on a synthetic ledger.

mod ledger_common;

use std::collections::BTreeSet;

use ledger_common::{rows, sha};
use quen_core::ledger::{
    BootEnd, BootStart, Capture, Claim, Game, Ledger, Measurement, ModVersion, Outcome, Pose,
    Provenance, ReTarget, Tag, schema_description,
};
use quen_core::mods::{Kind, ModEntry};
use quen_core::stats::{self, Stats, Summary};
use serde_json::{Value, json};

/// The description's sections for tables and views: (name, "table" or "view", the section's text).
fn sections() -> Vec<(String, String, String)> {
    let mut out: Vec<(String, String, String)> = Vec::new();
    for line in schema_description().lines() {
        if line.starts_with('#') {
            let heading = line.strip_prefix("### ").and_then(|h| h.strip_suffix(')'));
            if let Some((name, kind)) = heading.and_then(|h| h.split_once(" (")) {
                out.push((name.into(), kind.into(), String::new()));
                continue;
            }
            out.push((String::new(), String::new(), String::new()));
        } else if let Some(last) = out.last_mut() {
            last.2 += line;
            last.2 += "\n";
        }
    }
    out.retain(|(name, _, _)| !name.is_empty());
    out
}

/// The description's example queries, in order.
fn examples() -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut open: Option<String> = None;
    for line in schema_description().lines() {
        match (&mut open, line) {
            (None, "```sql") => open = Some(String::new()),
            (Some(sql), "```") => {
                out.push(std::mem::take(sql));
                open = None;
            }
            (Some(sql), line) => {
                sql.push_str(line);
                sql.push('\n');
            }
            (None, _) => {}
        }
    }
    out
}

#[test]
fn the_description_names_every_table_view_and_column() {
    let l = Ledger::open_in_memory().unwrap();
    let schema: BTreeSet<(String, String)> = rows(
        &l,
        "SELECT name, type FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type IN ('table', 'view')",
        &[],
    )
    .into_iter()
    .map(|r| (r[0].as_str().unwrap().into(), r[1].as_str().unwrap().into()))
    .collect();
    let described: BTreeSet<(String, String)> = sections()
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(name, kind, _)| (name, kind))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(
        described, schema,
        "one '### name (table)' or '### name (view)' section each"
    );
    for (name, _, text) in sections() {
        for column in rows(&l, "SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info(?1)", &[json!(name)]) {
            let column = column[0].as_str().unwrap();
            assert!(
                text.contains(&format!("`{column}`")),
                "the section on {name} doesn't name its column `{column}`"
            );
        }
    }
}

fn entry(kind: Kind, name: &str, build: u32, config: Option<u32>) -> ModEntry {
    ModEntry {
        kind,
        name: name.into(),
        home: format!("%GAME_DIR%/{name}").into(),
        parked: false,
        content_hash: sha(build),
        file_count: 1,
        bytes: 1,
        config_hash: config.map(sha),
        config_values: Default::default(),
    }
}

/// A boot on the morning of day `day` of October 2026, finished ok unless `outcome` says otherwise.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Launch {
    day: u32,
    game: i64,
    set: i64,
    devkit: bool,
    busy_with: &'static [&'static str],
    some_cvar: Option<&'static str>,
    patches: Vec<Value>,
    outcome: Option<Outcome>,
}

fn launch(l: &mut Ledger, b: Launch) -> i64 {
    let id = l
        .start_boot(&BootStart {
            game_id: b.game,
            t_start: format!("2026-10-{:02}T10:00:00Z", b.day),
            settings_diff: b.some_cvar.map(|v| {
                json!({"Rendering": {"SomeCvar": v}})
                    .as_object()
                    .cloned()
                    .unwrap()
            }),
            devkit: Some(b.devkit),
            busy_with: Some(b.busy_with.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect()),
            ..Default::default()
        })
        .unwrap();
    l.set_boot_mod_set(id, b.set).unwrap();
    l.finish_boot(
        id,
        &BootEnd {
            t_end: format!("2026-10-{:02}T11:00:00Z", b.day),
            outcome: b.outcome.unwrap_or(Outcome::Ok),
            failure: None,
            patches: b.patches,
        },
    )
    .unwrap();
    id
}

/// One measurement row.
fn row(
    l: &mut Ledger,
    boot: Option<i64>,
    (metric, value): (&str, f64),
    (run, label): (Option<&str>, Option<&str>),
    (family, tag): (&str, Tag),
) -> i64 {
    l.add_measurement(&Measurement {
        boot_id: boot,
        capture_id: None,
        metric: metric.into(),
        value: Some(value),
        unit: Some("ms".into()),
        state_label: label.map(String::from),
        method_family: family.into(),
        tag,
        run_id: run.map(String::from),
        note: None,
        extraction_id: None,
        world: None,
    })
    .unwrap()
}

/// Frame-time windows, `label` value pairs in order, as measure_ab records them.
fn windows(l: &mut Ledger, boot: i64, run: &str, windows: &[(&str, f64)]) -> Vec<i64> {
    windows
        .iter()
        .map(|&(label, ms)| {
            row(
                l,
                Some(boot),
                ("frame_ms_mean", ms),
                (Some(run), Some(label)),
                ("presentmon", Tag::M),
            )
        })
        .collect()
}

fn claim(l: &mut Ledger, text: &str, support: &[(i64, bool)]) -> i64 {
    let id = l
        .add_claim(&Claim {
            text: text.into(),
            scope: Some("5.01".into()),
        })
        .unwrap();
    for &(m, supports) in support {
        l.support(id, m, supports).unwrap();
    }
    id
}

/// An example query's cases: (its params, the rows it must return).
type Cases = Vec<(Vec<Value>, Vec<Vec<Value>>)>;

#[test]
fn the_example_queries_answer_their_questions() {
    let mut l = Ledger::open_in_memory().unwrap();
    let game = |l: &mut Ledger, n| {
        l.add_game(&Game {
            name: "synthetic".into(),
            exe_path: "%GAME_DIR%/bin/x64/game.exe".into(),
            exe_sha256: sha(n),
            build_stamp: None,
        })
        .unwrap()
    };
    let (g1, g2) = (game(&mut l, 1), game(&mut l, 2));
    l.add_mod_version(&ModVersion {
        content_hash: sha(10),
        kind: Kind::Asi,
        name: "W3ElementMap".into(),
        version: "v1".into(),
        provenance: Provenance::GitCommit,
        source: "abc1234".into(),
    })
    .unwrap();
    let set_a = l
        .add_mod_set(&[
            entry(Kind::Asi, "W3ElementMap", 10, Some(20)),
            entry(Kind::ModsFolder, "modX", 30, None),
            entry(Kind::ModsFolder, "modGone", 32, None),
        ])
        .unwrap();
    let set_b = l
        .add_mod_set(&[
            entry(Kind::Asi, "W3ElementMap", 11, Some(20)),
            entry(Kind::ModsFolder, "modX", 30, None),
            entry(Kind::ModsFolder, "modNew", 31, None),
        ])
        .unwrap();
    let base = |day, some_cvar| Launch {
        day,
        game: g1,
        set: set_a,
        some_cvar,
        ..Default::default()
    };
    let b1 = launch(
        &mut l,
        Launch {
            patches: vec![json!({"cvar": "SomeCvar"})],
            ..base(10, Some("0"))
        },
    );
    let b2 = launch(&mut l, base(11, Some("0")));
    let b3 = launch(&mut l, base(12, Some("1")));
    let b4 = launch(
        &mut l,
        Launch {
            devkit: true,
            ..base(13, Some("1"))
        },
    );
    let b5 = launch(
        &mut l,
        Launch {
            game: g2,
            set: set_b,
            ..base(14, None)
        },
    );
    let b6 = launch(
        &mut l,
        Launch {
            set: set_b,
            busy_with: &["cargo.exe"],
            ..base(15, Some("0"))
        },
    );
    let b7 = launch(&mut l, base(16, Some("0")));
    let b8 = launch(
        &mut l,
        Launch {
            outcome: Some(Outcome::Recovered),
            ..base(17, Some("0"))
        },
    );

    // The cvar's A/B run on b1, b4 and b7, and another run on b1; two plain windows on each other boot.
    let ab = [("off", 20.0), ("on", 21.0), ("off", 20.25), ("on", 21.125)];
    windows(&mut l, b1, "sess1-somecvar", &ab);
    let noise = [("a", 20.0), ("b", 20.5), ("a", 20.75), ("b", 20.25)];
    windows(&mut l, b1, "sess1-noise", &noise);

#[test]
fn ab_runs_gives_measure_abs_verdict() {
    let mut l = Ledger::open_in_memory().unwrap();
    let g = ledger_common::game(&mut l);
    let b = ledger_common::boot(&mut l, g, "2026-10-10T10:00:00Z");
    let runs: &[&[(&str, f64)]] = &[
        &[("A", 20.0), ("B", 21.0), ("A", 20.3), ("B", 21.2)],
        &[("A", 20.0), ("B", 20.1), ("A", 20.4), ("B", 20.2)],
        &[("A", 20.0), ("B", 21.0), ("B", 21.5), ("A", 20.9)],
        &[
            ("A", 10.0),
            ("A", 10.1),
            ("B", 10.5),
            ("B", 10.6),
            ("B", 10.55),
        ],
        // |diff| equal to a drift is inside it.
        &[("A", 0.0), ("B", 1.5), ("A", 1.0), ("B", 1.5)],
        &[("B", 5.0), ("A", 4.0), ("B", 5.25), ("A", 4.5)],
    ];
    for (i, run) in runs.iter().enumerate() {
        windows(&mut l, b, &format!("run-{i}"), run);
        let labelled: Vec<(&str, Stats)> = run
            .iter()
            .map(|&(label, mean)| {
                let summary = Summary {
                    count: 1,
                    mean,
                    median: mean,
                    p95: mean,
                };
                let stats = Stats {
                    frame_ms: summary,
                    gpu_busy_ms: None,
                    gpu_time_ms: None,
                    cpu_busy_ms: None,
                    present_mode: Some("Hardware: Independent Flip".into()),
                    present_mode_mixed: false,
                };
                (label, stats)
            })
            .collect();
        let want = stats::ab_verdict(&labelled).unwrap();
        let got = &rows(
            &l,
            "SELECT verdict, diff, first_label, first_drift, second_label, second_drift FROM ab_runs WHERE run_id = ?1",
            &[json!(format!("run-{i}"))],
        )[0];
        assert_eq!(got[0], json!(want.verdict), "run {i}");
        assert!(
            (got[1].as_f64().unwrap() - want.diff_ms).abs() < 1e-9,
            "run {i}"
        );
        for (label, drift) in [(&got[2], &got[3]), (&got[4], &got[5])] {
            let want = want.drift_ms[label.as_str().unwrap()];
            assert!((drift.as_f64().unwrap() - want).abs() < 1e-9, "run {i}");
        }
    }

    // One state, or one window in a state: no verdict.
    windows(&mut l, b, "single", &[("A", 20.0), ("A", 20.1)]);
    windows(&mut l, b, "short", &[("A", 20.0), ("B", 21.0), ("A", 20.1)]);
    let none = rows(
        &l,
        "SELECT run_id, states, second_label, verdict FROM ab_runs WHERE run_id IN ('single', 'short') ORDER BY run_id",
        &[],
    );
    assert_eq!(
        none,
        [
            vec![json!("short"), json!(2), json!("B"), Value::Null],
            vec![json!("single"), json!(1), Value::Null, Value::Null],
        ]
    );
}

```

`crates/quen-core/tests/parity.rs`:

```rs
//! Offline parity with the Python harness: the same synthetic inputs go through the harness's own
//! functions and through quen-core, and the answers must match. `parity/driver.py` runs the harness side from the folder
//! named by `QUEN_HARNESS_DIR`; without it, or without Python, each test prints a skip line and passes.
//!
//! A case marked `known` is a reviewed difference: the test fails when it stops differing, so the mark goes once a side
//! changes. `cargo test --test parity -- --nocapture` prints one line per case.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::io::{self, Write};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

use quen_core::boot::{self, Inputs, RenoDx};
use quen_core::cvar::{self, Layout, Set};
use quen_core::journal::{Fs, Journal, replay, sha256_hex};
use quen_core::mem::{self, Memory, Region};
use quen_core::park::{self, Entry, Listing};
use quen_core::stats::{self, Summary};
use quen_core::{bridge_log, input, settings};
use serde_json::{Value, json};

struct Case {
    name: &'static str,
    input: Value,
    /// Why the two sides are known to answer differently; `None`: they must agree.
    // ponytail: a known difference only asserts "still differs", not both answers; pin them if one ever matters.
    known: Option<&'static str>,
}

/// Runs `cases` through the driver as `kind` and through `rust`, and compares each pair of answers with `eq`. Both
/// refusing counts as equal: the messages differ by design.
fn parity(
    kind: &str,
    cases: Vec<Case>,
    rust: impl Fn(&Value) -> Value,
    eq: impl Fn(&Value, &Value) -> bool,
) {
    let Some(harness) = std::env::var_os("QUEN_HARNESS_DIR") else {
        println!("parity {kind}: skipped, QUEN_HARNESS_DIR is not set");
        return;
    };
    let scratch = Scratch::new(kind);
    let inputs: Vec<Value> = cases
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(i, case)| {
            let mut input = case.input.clone();
            input["kind"] = kind.into();
            input["dir"] = scratch.0.join(i.to_string()).to_string_lossy().into();
            input
        })
        .collect();
    let Some(python) = driver(&harness, &inputs) else {
        return;
    };
    assert_eq!(python.len(), cases.len(), "one answer per case");
    let mut wrong = Vec::new();
    for ((case, input), py) in cases.iter().zip(&inputs).zip(&python) {
        let rs = rust(input);
        let equal = match (py.get("ok"), rs.get("ok")) {
            (Some(p), Some(r)) => eq(p, r),
            (None, None) => true,
            _ => false,
        };
        let known = case
            .known
            .map(|why| format!(" ({why})"))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let shown = if equal { "equal" } else { "differs" };
        println!("parity {kind:<10} {:<30} {shown}{known}", case.name);
        if equal == case.known.is_some() {
            let what = if equal {
                "now equal: drop its known mark"
            } else {
                "differs"
            };
            wrong.push(format!(
                "{}: {what}\n  input  {input}\n  python {py}\n  rust   {rs}",
                case.name
            ));
        }
    }
    assert!(wrong.is_empty(), "parity {kind}:\n{}", wrong.join("\n"));
}

/// The harness's answers, one per input; `None` (skipped) when Python can't be started.
fn driver(harness: &OsStr, inputs: &[Value]) -> Option<Vec<Value>> {
    let script = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("tests/parity/driver.py");
    let spawned = Command::new("python")
        .arg("-B")
        .arg(&script)
        .env("QUEN_HARNESS_DIR", harness)
        .env("PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE", "1")
        .stdin(Stdio::piped())
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::piped())
        .spawn();
    let mut child = match spawned {
        Ok(child) => child,
        Err(e) => {
            println!("parity: skipped, python can't be started: {e}");
            return None;
        }
    };
    let request = serde_json::to_vec(inputs).unwrap();
    child.stdin.take().unwrap().write_all(&request).unwrap();
    let out = child.wait_with_output().unwrap();
    assert!(
        out.status.success(),
        "driver failed:\n{}",
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr)
    );
    Some(serde_json::from_slice(&out.stdout).expect("driver answers JSON"))
}

/// One test's scratch folder in the OS temp folder; everything the driver made in it goes with it.
struct Scratch(PathBuf);

impl Scratch {
    fn new(kind: &str) -> Scratch {
        let nanos = SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
            .unwrap()
            .as_nanos();
        let dir =
            std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("quen-parity-{kind}-{}-{nanos}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir(&dir).unwrap();
        Scratch(dir)
    }
}

impl Drop for Scratch {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
    }
}

fn text(input: &Value, key: &str) -> String {
    input[key].as_str().unwrap().to_string()
}

fn refused(e: impl std::fmt::Display) -> Value {
    json!({"err": e.to_string()})
}

// ---- dx12user.settings overrides -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A synthetic settings file: `MotionBlur` is in two sections, `[Empty]` has no keys.
const LF: &str = "[Rendering]\nAllowFG=true\nMotionBlur=true\n[Rendering/MtRender]\nThreads=4\n\
                  [Empty]\n[Gameplay]\nAutoRotate=true\nMotionBlur=false\n";

/// Bytes as a string of chars U+0000..U+00FF, one per byte: the driver reads it as Latin-1.
fn latin1(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    bytes.iter().map(|&b| char::from(b)).collect()
}

#[test]
fn settings_overrides() {
    let crlf = LF.replace('\n', "\r\n");
    let lit = "Key=1\nKeyX=2\n Indented=3\nkey=4\nA.B=5\nSpaced = 6\nA*=7\n";
    let bom = b"\xef\xbb\xbfAllowFG=true\r\nX=1\r\n";
    let template = "Python's section replace reads the value as a regex template";
    let appended = "the harness refuses a missing section, quen appends it (finding 63)";
    let c = |name, data: &[u8], flat: &str, sections: &str, known| Case {
        name,
        input: json!({"data": latin1(data), "flat": flat, "sections": sections}),
        known,
    };
    let (lf, crlf) = (LF.as_bytes(), crlf.as_bytes());
    let cases = vec![
        c("flat_lf", lf, "AllowFG=false", "", None),
        c("flat_crlf", crlf, "AllowFG=false", "", None),
        c(
            "flat_later_wins",
            lf,
            "AllowFG=1,Threads=8,AllowFG=2",
            "",
            None,
        ),
        c("flat_missing_key", lf, "AllowFG=false,Missing=1", "", None),
        c(
            "flat_key_in_two_sections",
            crlf,
            "MotionBlur=false",
            "",
            None,
        ),
        c("flat_literal_key", lit.as_bytes(), "Key=9", "", None),
        c(
            "flat_regex_chars_in_key",
            lit.as_bytes(),
            "A.B=0,A*=0",
            "",
            None,
        ),
        c("flat_indented_line", lit.as_bytes(), "Indented=0", "", None),
        c("flat_other_case", lit.as_bytes(), "KEY=0", "", None),
        c("flat_spaced_key", lit.as_bytes(), "Spaced=0", "", None),
        c(
            "flat_value_literal",
            lf,
            r"Threads=a\1\\b$0${x}=c\n",
            "",
            None,
        ),
        c("flat_last_line_no_eol", b"A=1\nB=2", "B=3", "", None),
        c("flat_last_line_cr_only", b"A=1\r\nB=2\r", "B=3", "", None),
        c("flat_bom_first_line", bom, "AllowFG=false", "", None),
        c("flat_bom_other_line", bom, "X=2", "", None),
        c(
            "flat_non_utf8_bytes",
            b"Name=\xe9t\xe9\nX=1\n",
            "X=2",
            "",
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "flat_unicode_key",
            "Cl\u{e9}=1\nX=1\n".as_bytes(),
            "Cl\u{e9}=2",
            "",
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "flat_bare_cr_in_value",
            b"A=1\r2\nB=3\n",
            "A=9",
            "",
            Some("Python's value stops at a bare CR, Rust's runs to the LF"),
        ),
        c(
            "flat_line_break_in_value",
            b"A=0\nC=0\n",
            "A=1\nC=2",
            "",
            Some("Python writes the line break (two C= lines), Rust refuses"),
        ),
        c("flat_no_equals", lf, "NoEquals", "", None),
        c("flat_empty_key", lf, "=1", "", None),
        c("flat_header_as_key", lf, "[Rendering]=1", "", None),
        c("flat_bad_second_item", lf, "AllowFG=1,Threads", "", None),
        c("sec_replace", lf, "", "Gameplay:MotionBlur=true", None),
        c(
            "sec_replace_crlf",
            crlf,
            "",
            "Rendering/MtRender:Threads=2",
            None,
        ),
        c("sec_insert", lf, "", "Gameplay:Hdr=1", None),
        c("sec_insert_crlf", crlf, "", "Gameplay:Hdr=1", None),
        c("sec_insert_mixed_eol", b"[A]\nX=1\r\n", "", "A:Y=2", None),
        c("sec_insert_empty_section", lf, "", "Empty:New=1", None),
        c(
            "sec_insert_last_section",
            b"[A]\nX=1\n[B]\n",
            "",
            "B:Y=2",
            None,
        ),
        c("sec_insert_header_only", b"[B]\r\n", "", "B:Y=2", None),
        c("sec_last_line_no_eol", b"[S]\nA=1", "", "S:A=2", None),
        c("sec_missing", lf, "", "Missing:A=1", Some(appended)),
        c("sec_other_case", lf, "", "rendering:A=1", None),
        c(
            "sec_header_trailing_space",
            b"[A] \nX=1\n",
            "",
            "A:X=2",
            None,
        ),
        c("sec_header_no_eol", b"X=1\n[A]", "", "A:X=2", None),
        c(
            "sec_regex_chars",
            b"[AxB]\nX=0\n[A.B]\nX=0\n",
            "",
            "A.B:X=1",
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "sec_bom_header",
            b"\xef\xbb\xbf[A]\r\nX=1\r\n",
            "",
            "A:X=2",
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "sec_duplicate_header",
            b"[A]\nX=1\n[A]\nY=1\n",
            "",
            "A:X=2",
            Some("Python edits the first [A], Rust refuses a repeated header"),
        ),
        c(
            "sec_key_twice",
            b"[A]\nX=1\nX=2\n[B]\nX=3\n",
            "",
            "A:X=9",
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "sec_key_in_other_section",
            b"[A]\nX=1\n[B]\nX=3\n",
            "",
            "B:X=9",
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "sec_later_wins",
            lf,
            "",
            "Gameplay:Hdr=1;Gameplay:Hdr=2;Rendering:AllowFG=0",
            None,
        ),
        c("sec_insert_backslash", lf, "", r"Empty:New=a\1", None),
        c(
            "sec_replace_group_ref",
            lf,
            "",
            r"Gameplay:MotionBlur=a\1b",
            Some(template),
        ),
        c(
            "sec_replace_double_backslash",
            lf,
            "",
            r"Gameplay:MotionBlur=a\\b",
            Some(template),
        ),
        c("sec_no_colon", lf, "", "NoColon=1", None),
        c("sec_empty_section", lf, "", ":A=1", None),
        c("sec_no_equals", lf, "", "Gameplay:NoEquals", None),
        c(
            "sec_empty_key",
            lf,
            "",
            "Gameplay:=1",
            Some("Python inserts a line =1, Rust refuses an empty key"),
        ),
        c("empty_specs", lf, "", "", None),
        c("separators_only", lf, ",AllowFG=0,", ";;", None),
        c(
            "flat_then_sections",
            crlf,
            "Threads=8,AllowFG=false",
            "Rendering/MtRender:Threads=9;Gameplay:Hdr=1",
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "flat_ok_sections_bad",
            crlf,
            "AllowFG=false",
            "Nope:A=1",
            Some(appended),
        ),
        c(
            "flat_bad_sections_ok",
            crlf,
            "Nope=1",
            "Gameplay:Hdr=1",
            None,
        ),
        c("empty_file_flat", b"", "A=1", "", None),
        c("empty_file_section", b"", "", "A:B=1", Some(appended)),
    ];
    parity(
        "settings",
        cases,
        |input| {
            let data: Vec<u8> = text(input, "data")
                .chars()
                .map(|c| u8::try_from(c).unwrap())
                .collect();
            match settings::validate(&data, &text(input, "flat"), &text(input, "sections")) {
                Ok(out) => json!({"ok": latin1(&out)}),
                Err(e) => refused(e),
            }
        },
        |p, r| p == r,
    );
}

// ---- park plans ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A synthetic game: the bridges, the harness's own mods, a junction, a stray file, two plain mods and an add-on.
const MODS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    ("modZeta", "dir"),
    ("modAlpha", "dir"),
    ("modLinked", "junction"),
    ("readme.txt", "file"),
    ("modW3GameStateBridge", "dir"),
    ("modNativeBridge", "dir"),
    ("modRenoDXTest", "dir"),
];
const BIN: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    ("witcher3.exe", "file"),
    ("Tweaks.asi", "file"),
    ("W3GameStateBridge.asi", "file"),
    ("WitcherNativeBridge.asi", "file"),
    ("Other.ADDON64", "file"),
    ("dxgi.dll", "file"),
    ("d3d12.dll", "file"),
    ("renodx-thewitcher3remastered.addon64", "file"),
    ("renodx-devkit.addon64", "file"),
];
/// The W3 Game State Bridge's pair, as quen learns it from the files (park::learn): the harness never parks it.
const GSB: &[[&str; 2]] = &[["W3GameStateBridge.asi", "modW3GameStateBridge"]];

/// The harness's own names it never parks (W3_PARK_RENODX unset): what the adapter adds to `W3_NEVER_PARK` (park.rs).
const HARNESS_OWN: &[&str] = &[
    "modRenoDXTest",
    "renodx-devkit.addon64",
    "renodx-thewitcher3remastered.addon64",
];

fn listing(dir: &Path) -> Vec<Entry> {
    std::fs::read_dir(dir)
        .unwrap()
        .map(|entry| {
            let entry = entry.unwrap();
            let kind = entry.file_type().unwrap();
            Entry {
                name: entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
                is_dir: kind.is_dir(),
                is_link: kind.is_symlink(),
            }
        })
        .collect()
}

#[test]
fn park_plans() {
    let with = |extra: &[(&'static str, &'static str)], base: &[(&'static str, &'static str)]| {
        [base, extra].concat()
    };
    let quen_mods = with(&[("modQuen", "dir")], MODS);
    let quen_bin = with(&[("W3Quen.asi", "file")], BIN);
    let unicode = with(&[("modB\u{e9}ta", "dir")], MODS);
    let asi_dir = with(&[("plugins.asi", "dir")], BIN);
    let spaced_mods = with(&[("mod Spaced", "dir")], MODS);
    let spaced_bin = with(&[("My Tweaks.asi", "file")], BIN);
    let link_mods = with(&[("modSym", "dirlink")], MODS);
    let link_bin = with(&[("Sym.asi", "filelink"), ("Linked.asi", "junction")], BIN);
    let c =
        |name, mods: &[(&str, &str)], bin: &[(&str, &str)], park: &str, keep: &str, known| Case {
            name,
            input: json!({"mods": mods, "bin": bin, "park": park, "keep": keep}),
            known,
        };
    let kept = "Python parks a name both requested and kept, Rust refuses";
    let quen = "Python predates quen's own mods";
    let link = "Python skips a junction in Mods but refuses the plan for any other link, Rust skips every link";
    let bridge = "quen's ALL parks the W3GSB pair whole (learned from the files); the harness never parks it";
    let cases = vec![
        c("one_name", MODS, BIN, "modAlpha", "", None),
        c(
            "any_case_and_home",
            MODS,
            BIN,
            " modalpha , TWEAKS.ASI,other.addon64,DXGI.DLL",
            "",
            None,
        ),
        c("all", MODS, BIN, "ALL", "", Some(bridge)),
        c(
            "all_keep",
            MODS,
            BIN,
            "ALL",
            "MODZETA, dxgi.dll",
            Some(bridge),
        ),
        c(
            "names_beside_all",
            MODS,
            BIN,
            "tweaks.asi,ALL,modZeta",
            "modAlpha",
            Some(bridge),
        ),
        c(
            "bridge_named",
            MODS,
            BIN,
            "modAlpha,w3gamestatebridge.asi",
            "",
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "bridge_pair_named",
            MODS,
            BIN,
            "W3GameStateBridge.asi,modW3GameStateBridge",
            "",
            Some(
                "quen parks W3GSB both halves together (its pair, learned from the files); the harness never parks it",
            ),
        ),
        c(
            "bridge_beside_all",
            MODS,
            BIN,
            "ALL,modNativeBridge",
            "",
            None,
        ),
        c("harness_mod_named", MODS, BIN, "modRenoDXTest", "", None),
        c(
            "renodx_addon_named",
            MODS,
            BIN,
            "renodx-thewitcher3remastered.addon64",
            "",
            None,
        ),
        c("unknown_mod", MODS, BIN, "modAlpha,modMissing", "", None),
        c("unknown_asi", MODS, BIN, "Missing.asi", "", None),
        c("junction", MODS, BIN, "modLinked", "", None),
        c("file_in_mods", MODS, BIN, "readme.txt", "", None),
        c("exe_not_parkable", MODS, BIN, "witcher3.exe", "", None),
        c("repeated", MODS, BIN, "modAlpha,MODALPHA", "", None),
        c("dot_dot", MODS, BIN, "..", "", None),
        c("path", MODS, BIN, "../modAlpha", "", None),
        c("space", MODS, BIN, "mod Alpha", "", None),
        c("leading_dot", MODS, BIN, ".hidden", "", None),
        c("leading_dash", MODS, BIN, "-x", "", None),
        c("lowercase_all", MODS, BIN, "all", "", None),
        c("empty", MODS, BIN, "", "", None),
        c("blank_items", MODS, BIN, " , ", "", None),
        c(
            "all_twice",
            MODS,
            BIN,
            "ALL,ALL",
            "",
            Some("Python drops every ALL, Rust refuses the repeat"),
        ),
        c(
            "keep_typo_with_all",
            MODS,
            BIN,
            "ALL",
            "modZetta",
            Some("Python ignores an unknown keep name and parks modZeta, Rust refuses"),
        ),
        c(
            "keep_typo_without_all",
            MODS,
            BIN,
            "modZeta",
            "modTypo",
            Some("Python reads keep only under ALL, Rust checks it always"),
        ),
        c(
            "named_and_kept",
            MODS,
