```rs
            "modAlpha",
            Some(kept),
        ),
        c(
            "named_and_kept_no_all",
            MODS,
            BIN,
            "modAlpha",
            "modalpha",
            Some(kept),
        ),
        c(
            "quen_mods_under_all",
            &quen_mods,
            &quen_bin,
            "ALL",
            "",
            Some(quen),
        ),
        c(
            "quen_mod_named",
            &quen_mods,
            &quen_bin,
            "modQuen",
            "",
            Some(quen),
        ),
        c("unicode_under_all", &unicode, BIN, "ALL", "", None),
        c("unicode_named", &unicode, BIN, "modb\u{c9}ta", "", None),
        c(
            "space_folder_named",
            &spaced_mods,
            BIN,
            "mod Spaced",
            "",
            None,
        ),
        c("space_folder_under_all", &spaced_mods, BIN, "ALL", "", None),
        c("space_asi_under_all", MODS, &spaced_bin, "ALL", "", None),
        c(
            "unicode_kept_under_all",
            &unicode,
            BIN,
            "ALL",
            "modb\u{c9}ta",
            Some(bridge),
        ),
        c(
            "space_kept_under_all",
            &spaced_mods,
            &spaced_bin,
            "ALL",
            "mod Spaced,My Tweaks.asi",
            Some(bridge),
        ),
        c("symlink_folder_named", &link_mods, BIN, "modSym", "", None),
        c(
            "symlink_folder_under_all",
            &link_mods,
            BIN,
            "ALL",
            "",
            Some(link),
        ),
        c("symlink_asi_named", MODS, &link_bin, "Sym.asi", "", None),
        c(
            "junction_asi_named",
            MODS,
            &link_bin,
            "Linked.asi",
            "",
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "links_in_bin_under_all",
            MODS,
            &link_bin,
            "ALL",
            "",
            Some(link),
        ),
        c(
            "devkit_addon_named",
            MODS,
            BIN,
            "renodx-devkit.addon64",
            "",
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "asi_folder_under_all",
            MODS,
            &asi_dir,
            "ALL",
            "",
            Some("Python lists a folder named *.asi under ALL and refuses, Rust skips it"),
        ),
        c("asi_folder_named", MODS, &asi_dir, "plugins.asi", "", None),
    ];
    let never: Vec<&str> = park::W3_NEVER_PARK
        .iter()
        .chain(HARNESS_OWN)
        .copied()
        .collect();
    parity(
        "park",
        cases,
        |input| {
            let dir = PathBuf::from(text(input, "dir"));
            let (mods_dir, bin_dir) = (dir.join("Mods"), dir.join("bin"));
            let (mods, bin) = (listing(&mods_dir), listing(&bin_dir));
            let plan = park::plan(
                &text(input, "park"),
                &text(input, "keep"),
                &never,
                GSB,
                Listing {
                    dir: &mods_dir,
                    entries: &mods,
                },
                Listing {
                    dir: &bin_dir,
                    entries: &bin,
                },
                &dir.join("parked"),
                &park::More::default(),
            );
            match plan {
                Ok(plan) => {
                    // ponytail: compared as sets; the order of independent renames carries no meaning.
                    let mut names: Vec<String> = plan
                        .moves
                        .iter()
                        .map(|m| m.from.file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy().into_owned())
                        .collect();
                    names.sort();
                    json!({"ok": names})
                }
                Err(e) => refused(e),
            }
        },
        |p, r| p == r,
    );
}

// ---- bridge log ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Bridge log lines, one per flags value.
fn log(flags: &[i64]) -> String {
    flags
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(seq, f)| format!("push seq={seq} flags={f} weather=1 region=2 hour=12\n"))
        .collect()
}

#[test]
fn bridge_flags_and_loaded() {
    use bridge_log::{CUTSCENE, DLGFLAG, FADE, SCENE, VALID};
    let c = |name, before: String, after: String, known| Case {
        name,
        input: json!({"before": before, "after": after}),
        known,
    };
    let crlf = |flags: &[i64]| log(flags).replace('\n', "\r\n");
    let mut cases = vec![
        c("load_then_gameplay", log(&[3, 3]), log(&[0, 3]), None),
        c("fade_counts_as_load", log(&[3]), log(&[257, 73]), None),
        c("load_before_the_call", log(&[0]), log(&[3, 3]), None),
        c("no_load", String::new(), log(&[3, 3]), None),
        c("ends_loading", String::new(), log(&[3, 0]), None),
        c("photo_and_env_bits", String::new(), log(&[0, 1157]), None),
        c("nothing_after", log(&[0, 3]), String::new(), None),
        c("empty_log", String::new(), String::new(), None),
        c("crlf", crlf(&[3]), crlf(&[0, 3]), None),
        c("bom", format!("\u{feff}{}", log(&[3])), log(&[0, 3]), None),
        c(
            "word_boundary_and_junk",
            String::new(),
            "prevflags=7 my_flags=8 2flags=9 (flags=17) x.flags=33\n\
             flags=-1 flags= flags=- flags=--2 flags=x flags=flags=65\nflags=129abc flags=007\n"
                .into(),
            None,
        ),
        c("negative_last", String::new(), log(&[0, -1]), None),
        c(
            "beyond_i64",
            String::new(),
            "flags=0\nflags=99999999999999999999\nflags=3\n".into(),
            Some("Python keeps a value beyond i64, Rust skips it (flags are 11 bits)"),
        ),
    ];
    for (name, busy) in [
        ("ends_in_scene", SCENE),
        ("ends_in_cutscene", CUTSCENE),
        ("ends_in_fade", FADE),
        ("ends_in_dialogue", DLGFLAG),
    ] {
        cases.push(c(name, String::new(), log(&[0, VALID | busy]), None));
    }
    parity(
        "bridge",
        cases,
        |input| {
            let before = text(input, "before");
            let all = bridge_log::flags(&(before.clone() + &text(input, "after")));
            let loaded = bridge_log::loaded_after(&all, bridge_log::flags(&before).len());
            json!({"ok": {"flags": all, "loaded": loaded}})
        },
        |p, r| p == r,
    );
}

#[test]
fn bridge_bit_names() {
    let case = Case {
        name: "sig_bits",
        input: json!({}),
        known: Some("quen's state adds bit 2048, menu (quen-w3 0.1.6); the harness has none"),
    };
    parity(
        "bits",
        vec![case],
        |_| {
            let names: Vec<&str> = (0..bridge_log::BITS.len())
                .map(|i| bridge_log::names(1 << i)[0])
                .collect();
            json!({"ok": names})
        },
        |p, r| p == r,
    );
}

// ---- PresentMon CSV stats --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const HEADER: &str = "Application,ProcessID,SwapChainAddress,PresentRuntime,SyncInterval,PresentFlags,\
                      AllowsTearing,PresentMode,FrameType,CPUStartTime,MsBetweenSimulationStart,MsBetweenPresents,\
                      MsBetweenDisplayChange,MsInPresentAPI,MsUntilDisplayed,MsCPUBusy,MsCPUWait,MsGPULatency,\
                      MsGPUTime,MsGPUBusy,MsGPUWait";

/// A synthetic PresentMon CSV: five warm-up rows of 999 ms, then one row per frame time. GPU busy is frame − 2, GPU
/// time frame − 1, CPU busy frame / 2.
fn pm(frames: &[f64]) -> String {
    let row = |ms: f64| {
        format!(
            "game.exe,4242,0x0000000000ABCDEF,DXGI,0,0,1,Hardware: Independent Flip,Application,1234.5,NA,{ms},{ms},\
             0.1,{ms},{},0.2,NA,{},{},0.3\n",
            ms / 2.0,
            ms - 1.0,
            ms - 2.0
        )
    };
    let mut out = format!("{HEADER}\n");
    for _ in 0..stats::SKIP_ROWS {
        out += &row(999.0);
    }
    for &ms in frames {
        out += &row(ms);
    }
    out
}

/// A table of the four stats columns, five warm-up rows of 1, then `rows`.
fn table(rows: &str) -> String {
    "MsBetweenPresents,MsGPUBusy,MsCPUBusy,PresentMode\n".to_string()
        + &"1,1,1,m\n".repeat(stats::SKIP_ROWS)
        + rows
}

/// Numbers equal within `tol`, everything else exactly.
fn close(p: &Value, r: &Value, tol: f64) -> bool {
    match (p, r) {
        (Value::Number(p), Value::Number(r)) => {
            (p.as_f64().unwrap() - r.as_f64().unwrap()).abs() <= tol
        }
        (Value::Array(p), Value::Array(r)) => {
            p.len() == r.len() && p.iter().zip(r).all(|(p, r)| close(p, r, tol))
        }
        (Value::Object(p), Value::Object(r)) => {
            p.len() == r.len()
                && p.iter()
                    .all(|(k, p)| r.get(k).is_some_and(|r| close(p, r, tol)))
        }
        _ => p == r,
    }
}

#[test]
fn presentmon_stats() {
    let c = |name, csv: String, known| Case {
        name,
        input: json!({"csv": csv}),
        known,
    };
    let mut seed = 0x5eed_u64;
    let long: Vec<f64> = (0..600)
        .map(|_| {
            seed = seed
                .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
                .wrapping_add(1_442_695_040_888_963_407);
            8.0 + (seed >> 40) as f64 / f64::from(1 << 24) * 32.0
        })
        .collect();
    let ten: Vec<f64> = (1..=10).map(f64::from).collect();
    let quoted = pm(&[10.0, 12.0, 14.0])
        .replacen("PresentMode", "\"PresentMode\"", 1)
        .replacen("MsBetweenPresents", "\"MsBetweenPresents\"", 1);
    let nan = "Python averages it to NaN, Rust refuses the capture";
    let nothing = "Python reports NaN, Rust refuses";
    let ragged = "Python reads a ragged row, Rust refuses the table";
    let cases = vec![
        c("ten_frames", pm(&ten), None),
        c("one_frame", pm(&[16.0]), None),
        c("odd_count", pm(&[3.0, 1.0, 2.0]), None),
        c("long_window", pm(&long), None),
        c("crlf", pm(&ten).replace('\n', "\r\n"), None),
        // Neither side tells generated frames from real ones: every present counts (PITFALLS: frame gen).
        c(
            "frame_gen_rows",
            pm(&ten).replacen(",Application,", ",AMD_AFMF,", 9),
            None,
        ),
        c("bom_and_quoted_header", format!("\u{feff}{quoted}"), None),
        c("blank_lines", pm(&ten).replacen("\n", "\n\n", 3), None),
        c(
            "na_and_blank_cells",
            table("10,NA,,m\n20,,NA,m\n30,6,4,NA\n40,8,,\n"),
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "na_frame_cell",
            table("10,1,1,m\nNA,4,1,m\n30,6,1,m\n"),
            Some("Python's frames counts rows, Rust's count frame-time cells"),
        ),
        c(
            "spaces_around_numbers",
            table(" 10 , 8 , 5 ,m\n 20,9 ,6,m\n"),
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "space_only_cell",
            table("10,8, ,m\n20,9,6,m\n"),
            Some("Python fails on float(' '), Rust reads it as blank"),
        ),
        c(
            "lowercase_header",
            pm(&ten).replacen("MsBetweenPresents", "msbetweenpresents", 1),
            Some(
                "Python matches column names exactly as PresentMon writes them, Rust ignores case",
            ),
        ),
        c("nan_cell", table("10,1,1,m\nNaN,1,1,m\n"), Some(nan)),
        c("inf_cell", table("10,1,1,m\ninf,1,1,m\n"), Some(nan)),
        c("text_cell", table("10,1,1,m\n20,fast,1,m\n"), None),
        c(
            "bad_cell_in_warm_up",
            "MsBetweenPresents\nbad\n".to_string() + &"1\n".repeat(stats::SKIP_ROWS),
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "no_frame_column",
            "MsGPUBusy,PresentMode\n".to_string() + &"1,a\n".repeat(8),
            Some(nothing),
        ),
        c("warm_up_only", pm(&[]), Some(nothing)),
        c("short_row", pm(&ten) + "game.exe,1\n", Some(ragged)),
        c(
            "long_row",
            pm(&ten).replacen("0.3\n", "0.3,extra\n", 7),
            Some(ragged),
        ),
        c(
            "quoted_cells",
            "PresentMode,\"MsBetweenPresents\"\n".to_string()
                + &"x,1\n".repeat(stats::SKIP_ROWS)
                + "\"Mode, \"\"odd\"\"\nline\",2\n\n\"Mode, \"\"odd\"\"\nline\",4",
            None,
        ),
    ];
    parity(
        "presentmon",
        cases,
        |input| {
            let s = match stats::parse(&text(input, "csv")) {
                Ok(s) => s,
                Err(e) => return refused(e),
            };
            // The harness's NaN for a column without numbers is quen's None.
            let of = |col: &Option<Summary>, f: fn(&Summary) -> f64| {
                col.as_ref().map_or(json!("nan"), |s| json!(f(s)))
            };
            let (frame, gpu, cpu) = (&Some(s.frame_ms.clone()), &s.gpu_busy_ms, &s.cpu_busy_ms);
            json!({"ok": {
                "perf": {
                    "frames": s.frame_ms.count,
                    "frame_ms": s.frame_ms.mean,
                    "gpu_busy_ms": of(gpu, |s| s.mean),
                    "gpu_time_ms": of(&s.gpu_time_ms, |s| s.mean),
                    "cpu_busy_ms": of(cpu, |s| s.mean),
                },
                "medians": [s.frame_ms.count, s.frame_ms.median, of(gpu, |s| s.median), of(cpu, |s| s.median)],
                "p95": [of(frame, |s| s.p95), of(gpu, |s| s.p95)],
            }})
        },
        // perf rounds means to 3 places and medians to 2; numpy's p95 is the same interpolation.
        |p, r| {
            close(&p["perf"], &r["perf"], 5e-4 + 1e-9)
                && close(&p["medians"], &r["medians"], 5e-3 + 1e-9)
                && close(&p["p95"], &r["p95"], 1e-9)
        },
    );
}

// ---- cvars (cvar_poke) -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Where the synthetic images load.
const CVAR_BASE: u64 = 0x7ff6_0000_0000;

/// A memory image: reads at `CVAR_BASE` + offset.
struct Flat(Vec<u8>);

impl Memory for Flat {
    fn read(&self, address: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        let at = address.wrapping_sub(CVAR_BASE) as usize;
        let src = self.0.get(at..at.saturating_add(buf.len()));
        buf.copy_from_slice(src.ok_or_else(|| std::io::Error::other("outside the image"))?);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn regions(&self) -> std::io::Result<Vec<Region>> {
        Ok(vec![])
    }
}

fn hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    bytes.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}

/// A PE-shaped image like cvar_poke's selftest one: headers, `.text` (pointers to a name, which are not objects),
/// `.rdata` (the strings) and `.data` (the var objects, laid out by `l`). A var's type is an index into `l.codes`, or
/// `None` for a code the layout doesn't know; a var named `BadPtr` gets a null value pointer.
fn cvar_image(l: &Layout, vars: &[(&str, &str, Option<usize>, f64, f64)]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let (text, rdata, data) = (0x1000, 0x2000, 0x3000);
    let mut b = vec![0u8; 0x4000];
    let put = |b: &mut Vec<u8>, at: usize, v: &[u8]| b[at..at + v.len()].copy_from_slice(v);
    put(&mut b, 0x3c, &0x80u32.to_le_bytes());
    put(&mut b, 0x80, b"PE\0\0");
    put(&mut b, 0x86, &3u16.to_le_bytes());
    put(&mut b, 0x94, &0xf0u16.to_le_bytes());
    let sections = [
        (".text", text, 0x6000_0020u32),
        (".rdata", rdata, 0x4000_0040),
        (".data", data, 0xc000_0040),
    ];
    for (i, (name, va, flags)) in sections.into_iter().enumerate() {
        let s = 0x80 + 24 + 0xf0 + 40 * i;
        put(&mut b, s, name.as_bytes());
        put(&mut b, s + 8, &0x1000u32.to_le_bytes());
        put(&mut b, s + 12, &(va as u32).to_le_bytes());
        put(&mut b, s + 36, &flags.to_le_bytes());
    }
    let mut strings: Vec<(String, u64)> = Vec::new();
    let mut next = rdata;
    let mut string = |b: &mut Vec<u8>, s: &str| {
        if let Some((_, at)) = strings.iter().find(|(t, _)| t == s) {
            return *at;
        }
        put(b, next + 1, s.as_bytes());
        let at = CVAR_BASE + next as u64 + 1;
        next += s.len() + 2;
        strings.push((s.into(), at));
        at
    };
    let ends = [
        l.group + 8,
        l.name + 8,
        l.value + 8,
        l.flags + 4,
        l.default + 4,
        l.live + 4,
    ];
    let stride = ends.into_iter().max().unwrap().next_multiple_of(8) as usize;
    let unknown = (0..=255).find(|c| !l.codes.contains(c)).unwrap();
    for (i, &(group, name, kind, default, live)) in vars.iter().enumerate() {
        let obj = data + i * stride;
        let field = |offset: u64| obj + offset as usize;
        let (group, name_at) = (string(&mut b, group), string(&mut b, name));
        put(&mut b, field(l.group), &group.to_le_bytes());
        put(&mut b, field(l.name), &name_at.to_le_bytes());
        let code = kind.map_or(unknown, |k| l.codes[k]);
        put(
            &mut b,
            field(l.flags),
            &(0x200 | u32::from(code)).to_le_bytes(),
        );
        let value = if name == "BadPtr" {
            0
        } else {
            CVAR_BASE + field(l.live) as u64
        };
        put(&mut b, field(l.value), &value.to_le_bytes());
        for (offset, v) in [(l.default, default), (l.live, live)] {
            let bytes = match kind {
                Some(0) => vec![v as u8],
                Some(2) => (v as f32).to_le_bytes().to_vec(),
                _ => (v as i32).to_le_bytes().to_vec(),
            };
            put(&mut b, field(offset), &bytes);
        }
    }
    let use_x = string(&mut b, "UseX");
    for at in (text + 0x100..text + 0x200).step_by(8) {
        put(&mut b, at, &use_x.to_le_bytes());
    }
    b
}

/// cvar_poke's `run` (find, show, encode, the write) on a synthetic image, against quen-core's find, read and plan.
/// The layout is the KB's row (`cvar_layout.tsv` in `QUEN_KB_DIR`) for the build cvar_poke checks, so no game's
/// layout is in this repo. Both sides answer the object's offset and the whole image after the action.
#[test]
fn cvar_find_read_and_write() {
    let (Some(harness), Some(kb)) = (
        std::env::var_os("QUEN_HARNESS_DIR"),
        std::env::var_os("QUEN_KB_DIR"),
    ) else {
        println!("parity cvar: skipped, QUEN_HARNESS_DIR or QUEN_KB_DIR is not set");
        return;
    };
    let scratch = Scratch::new("cvar-build");
    let dir = scratch.0.join("0").to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    let Some(build) = driver(&harness, &[json!({"kind": "cvar_build", "dir": dir})]) else {
        return;
    };
    let build = build[0]["ok"]
        .as_str()
        .expect("the build cvar_poke checks")
        .to_string();
    let tsv = std::fs::read_to_string(Path::new(&kb).join("cvar_layout.tsv"))
        .expect("the KB's cvar_layout.tsv");
    let l = cvar::from_layout_tsv(&tsv)
        .unwrap()
        .into_iter()
        .find(|l| l.build == build)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("cvar_layout.tsv has no row for build {build}"));
    let (b, i, f) = (Some(0), Some(1), Some(2));
    let vars = [
        ("Rendering/RT", "Tlas", f, 800.0, 800.0),
        ("Rendering/RT", "Budget", i, 0.0, 0.0),
        ("Rendering", "UseX", b, 1.0, 1.0),
        ("Rendering", "Enabled", b, 1.0, 1.0),
        ("Other", "Enabled", b, 0.0, 0.0),
        ("Other", "Broken", None, 0.0, 0.0),
        ("Other", "Twice", i, 3.0, 3.0),
        ("Other", "Twice", i, 4.0, 4.0),
        ("Other", "Moved", f, 1.5, 2.5),
        ("Other", "BadPtr", i, 0.0, 0.0),
    ];
    let image = hex(&cvar_image(&l, &vars));
    let c = |name, var: &str, action: Option<&str>, value: Option<&str>, known| Case {
        name,
        input: json!({"base": CVAR_BASE, "image": image, "name": var, "action": action, "value": value}),
        known,
    };
    let (set, restore) = (Some("set"), Some("restore"));
    let cases = vec![
        c("read", "Tlas", None, None, None),
        c("read_group_name", "Rendering/RT/Tlas", None, None, None),
        c("set_float", "Tlas", set, Some("400"), None),
        c("set_float_fraction", "Tlas", set, Some("0.1"), None),
        c("set_float_exponent", "Tlas", set, Some("1e3"), None),
        c("set_float_negative", "Tlas", set, Some("-2.5"), None),
        c("set_float_too_big", "Tlas", set, Some("1e39"), None),
        c(
            "set_float_inf",
            "Tlas",
            set,
            Some("inf"),
            Some("Python writes inf, quen takes finite floats only"),
        ),
        c(
            "set_float_underscore",
            "Tlas",
            set,
            Some("1_0"),
            Some("Python's float() takes 1_0, quen doesn't"),
        ),
        c("restore", "Other/Moved", restore, None, None),
        c("restore_at_default", "Tlas", restore, None, None),
        c("set_int", "Rendering/RT/Budget", set, Some("256"), None),
        c("set_int_hex", "Budget", set, Some("0x10"), None),
        c("set_int_negative", "Budget", set, Some("-7"), None),
        c("set_int_leading_zero", "Budget", set, Some("010"), None),
        c("set_int_fraction", "Budget", set, Some("1.5"), None),
        c("set_int_too_big", "Budget", set, Some("2147483648"), None),
        c(
            "set_int_underscore",
            "Budget",
            set,
            Some("1_000"),
            Some("Python's int() takes 1_000, quen doesn't"),
        ),
        c("set_bool_false", "UseX", set, Some("false"), None),
        c("set_bool_true_upper", "UseX", set, Some("TRUE"), None),
        c("set_bool_two", "UseX", set, Some("2"), None),
        c("group_picks_one", "Other/Enabled", set, Some("1"), None),
        c("two_by_name", "Enabled", None, None, None),
        c("same_group_and_name_twice", "Other/Twice", None, None, None),
        c("unknown_type_code", "Broken", None, None, None),
        c("no_such_var", "NoSuchVar", None, None, None),
        c("wrong_group", "Rendering/RT/UseX", None, None, None),
        c("value_pointer_not_self", "BadPtr", None, None, None),
    ];
    parity(
        "cvar",
        cases,
        |input| {
            let hex_in = text(input, "image");
            let bytes = (0..hex_in.len())
                .step_by(2)
                .map(|i| u8::from_str_radix(&hex_in[i..i + 2], 16).unwrap());
            let mem = Flat(bytes.collect());
            let name = text(input, "name");
            let image = mem::image(&mem, CVAR_BASE).unwrap();
            let obj = match cvar::one(&cvar::find(&mem, &image, &l, &name), &name) {
                Ok(obj) => obj,
                Err(e) => return refused(e),
            };
            let var = cvar::read(&mem, &l, obj).unwrap();
            let set = match input["action"].as_str() {
                Some("set") => Some(Set::Value(input["value"].as_str().unwrap())),
                Some(_) => Some(Set::Default),
                None => None,
            };
            let mut after = mem.0.clone();
            if let Some(set) = set {
                let w = match cvar::plan(&var, &l, set) {
                    Ok(w) => w,
                    Err(e) => return refused(e),
                };
                let at = (w.address - CVAR_BASE) as usize;
                after[at..at + w.new.len()].copy_from_slice(&w.new);
            }
            json!({"ok": {"obj": obj - CVAR_BASE, "image": hex(&after)}})
        },
        |p, r| p == r,
    );
}

/// quen's PresentMon command line in perf's form: its two deliberate differences mapped back (the pid for perf's image
/// name, and quen's own trace session), so everything else must be perf's, in perf's order.
fn perf_form(argv: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut args = argv.iter();
    while let Some(arg) = args.next() {
        match arg.as_str() {
            "--process_id" => {
                args.next();
                out.extend(["--process_name".into(), "witcher3.exe".into()]);
            }
            "--session_name" => drop(args.next()),
            "--stop_existing_session" => {}
            _ => out.push(arg.clone()),
        }
    }
    out
}

#[test]
fn presentmon_command_line() {
    let c = |name, flags: &str, secs: u32, known| Case {
        name,
        input: json!({"flags": flags, "tag": "parity", "secs": secs}),
        known,
    };
    let any = "perf passes any W3_PM_FLAGS on, quen only --track_* / --no_track_* switches";
    let cases = vec![
        c("no_flags", "", 10, None),
        c("one_second", "", 1, None),
        c("pc_latency", "--track_pc_latency", 15, None),
        c(
            "two_switches_spaced",
            "  --track_pc_latency   --track_frame_type ",
            600,
            None,
        ),
        c("no_track_switch", "--no_track_input", 15, None),
        c("another_target", "--process_name other.exe", 10, Some(any)),
        c("no_csv", "--output_stdout", 10, Some(any)),
    ];
    parity(
        "presentmon_argv",
        cases,
        |input| {
            let csv =
                Path::new(&text(input, "dir")).join(format!("perf_{}.csv", text(input, "tag")));
            let flags: Vec<String> = text(input, "flags")
                .split_whitespace()
                .map(String::from)
                .collect();
            let secs = input["secs"].as_u64().unwrap() as u32;
            match stats::presentmon_args("pm.exe", 4242, secs, &csv.to_string_lossy(), &flags) {
                Ok(argv) => json!({"ok": perf_form(&argv[1..])}),
                Err(e) => refused(e),
            }
        },
        |p, r| p == r,
    );
}

// ---- w3ctl key plans, console_type lines and its prompt check --------------------------------------------------------

/// The Rust plan's lines, as the driver's `keys` prints them.
fn plan_lines(input: &Value) -> Value {
    let tokens: Vec<String> = serde_json::from_value(input["tokens"].clone()).unwrap();
    let (hold, gap) = (
        input["hold"].as_u64().unwrap(),
        input["gap"].as_u64().unwrap(),
    );
    match input::plan(&tokens, hold, gap, input::GRAVE) {
        Ok(plan) => json!({"ok": plan.iter().map(input::describe).collect::<Vec<_>>()}),
        Err(e) => refused(e),
    }
}

#[test]
fn key_plans() {
    let (hold, gap) = (input::HOLD_MS, input::GAP_MS);
    let c = |name, tokens: &[&str], known| Case {

        input: json!({"tokens": tokens, "hold": hold, "gap": gap}),
        known,
    };
    let letters: Vec<String> = ('a'..='z').map(String::from).collect();
    let letters: Vec<&str> = letters.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
    let named = "escape esc tab backspace enter space lshift rshift lctrl lalt rctrl ralt up down left right insert \
                 delete home end pgup pageup pgdn pagedown ctrl shift alt period minus comma";
    let named: Vec<&str> = named.split(' ').collect();
    let cap = "Rust caps a hold or wait at 60 s: a plan blocks the session thread";
    let os = "quen refuses the Windows keys and chords that act on Windows, not the game (security review)";
    let mut cases = vec![

        ),

        ),

        c(
            "digits",
            &["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "8", "9", "0"],
            None,
        ),
        c("letters", &letters, None),
        c("named", &named, None),
        c("repeat_in_chord", &["a+a"], None),
        c("at_the_cap", &["wait:60000", "e:60000"], None),

        c("wait_empty", &["wait:"], None),
        c("wait_word", &["wait:x"], None),

        c("decimal", &["e:1.5"], None),
        c("space_in_ms", &["e: 5"], None),
        c("empty_chord_part", &["a++b"], None),
        c("plus_only", &["+"], None),
        c("empty_token", &[""], None),
        c("unknown", &["nokey"], None),
        c("wait_in_chord", &["wait+a"], None),
        c("f13", &["f13"], None),
        c("f01", &["f01"], None),
        c("bad_after_good", &["e", "nokey"], None),
        c("superscript_digit", &["e:\u{b2}"], None),
        c(
            "arabic_indic_digit",
            &["e:\u{663}"],
            Some(
                "Python's isdigit and int take any Unicode digit, Rust only ASCII (game_keys passes ASCII only)",
            ),
        ),
        c("over_the_cap", &["wait:60001"], Some(cap)),
        c("beyond_u64", &["wait:99999999999999999999"], Some(cap)),
        c("windows_key", &["lwin"], Some(os)),
        c("windows_chord", &["win+r"], Some(os)),
        c("alt_tab", &["alt+tab"], Some(os)),
        c("alt_f4", &["lalt+f4"], Some(os)),
        c("ctrl_shift_esc", &["ctrl+shift+escape"], Some(os)),
        c("ctrl_alt_any", &["ctrl+alt+e"], Some(os)),
    ];
    cases.push(Case {
        name: "own_hold_and_gap",
        input: json!({"tokens": ["a", "b:100", "c"], "hold": 250, "gap": 500}),
        known: None,
    });
    parity("keys", cases, plan_lines, |p, r| p == r);
}

/// A plan's keys and sleeps without names (console_type's taps are all named "k").
fn bare(plan: &[input::Event]) -> Vec<String> {
    plan.iter()
        .map(|e| match e {
            input::Event::Key { sc, up, .. } => {
                format!("key {} 0x{sc:03X}", if *up { "up" } else { "down" })
            }
            input::Event::Sleep { ms, .. } => format!("sleep {ms}"),
        })
        .collect()
}

#[test]
fn console_lines() {
    let c = |name, line: &str, known| Case {
        name,
        input: json!({ "line": line }),
        known,
    };
    let cases = vec![
        c("settime", "settime(1,22)", None),
        c("quenload", "quenload(QuickSave_01)", None),
        c("weather_name", "changeweather(WT_Clear)", None),
        c("punctuation", "a b,c.d-e_f", None),
        c("digits", "0123456789", None),
        c("capitals", "ABC xyz", None),
        c("empty", "", None),
        c("quote", "say('hi')", None),
        c("accent", "\u{e9}", None),
        c("accented_capital", "\u{c9}", None),
        c("semicolon", "a;b", None),
        c("tab", "x\ty", None),
        c(
            "kelvin_sign",
            "\u{212a}",
            Some(
                "Python lowercases the Kelvin sign to k and types shift+k; Rust refuses non-ASCII (so does game_console)",
            ),
        ),
    ];
    // The same keys in the same order; the pace is quen's own since live boot 1 (a line's text back to back, not
    // console_type's 60 ms taps), so sleeps aren't compared.
    let keys = |plan: &Value| {
        let lines = plan.as_array().into_iter().flatten();
        let keys = lines.filter(|l| !l.as_str().is_some_and(|l| l.starts_with("sleep")));
        keys.cloned().collect::<Vec<Value>>()
    };
    parity(
        "console",
        cases,
        |i| match input::console_line(&text(i, "line"), input::GRAVE, &input::us_scancode, true) {
            Ok(plan) => json!({ "ok": bare(&plan) }),
            Err(e) => refused(e),
        },
        |p, r| keys(p) == keys(r),
    );
}

#[test]
fn console_prompt() {
    let c = |name, w: u32, h: u32, prompt: bool, fg: Value, bg: u8| Case {
        name,
        input: json!({"w": w, "h": h, "prompt": prompt, "fg": fg, "bg": bg}),

    let lit = || json!(220);

        Case {

                 glyph's 151); quen reads the glyph's outline (12) since live boot 3, so it sees the prompt",
            ),
            ..c("fhd_glyph_too_thin", 1920, 1080, true, lit(), 12)
        },
        c("fhd_closed", 1920, 1080, false, lit(), 12),

        c("at_the_threshold", 3840, 2160, true, json!(100), 0),

    cases.push(Case {

// ---- the boot's file changes and the end's restore ---------------------------------------------------------------

/// The real file system for the Rust side of the boot cases. A file's id is its creation time (a rename keeps it), a
/// folder's sha covers its files' names and bytes, and recycling moves a file into the case's own trash folder.
struct Disk {
    trash: PathBuf,
}

impl Fs for Disk {
    fn read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
        std::fs::read(path)
    }
    fn write_atomic(&self, path: &Path, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {
        let mut tmp = path.as_os_str().to_owned();
        tmp.push(".quen-tmp");
        std::fs::write(&tmp, data)?;
        std::fs::rename(&tmp, path)
    }
    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
        if self.exists(to) {
            return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists, "exists"));
        }
        std::fs::rename(from, to)
    }
    fn exists(&self, path: &Path) -> bool {
        std::fs::symlink_metadata(path).is_ok()
    }
    fn sha256(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<String> {
        if !path.is_dir() {
            return Ok(sha256_hex(&std::fs::read(path)?));
        }
        let files = tree(path, None);
        Ok(sha256_hex(serde_json::to_string(&files)?.as_bytes()))
    }
    fn file_id(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<String> {
        Ok(format!("{:?}", std::fs::metadata(path)?.created()?))
    }
    fn fsync(&self, _path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
    fn recycle(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&self.trash)?;
        let n = std::fs::read_dir(&self.trash)?.count();
        std::fs::rename(path, self.trash.join(n.to_string()))
    }
    fn mtime(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<u64> {
        let since = std::fs::metadata(path)?
            .modified()?
            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH);
        Ok(since.map_or(0, |d| d.as_nanos() as u64))
    }
    fn set_mtime(&self, path: &Path, nanos: u64) -> io::Result<()> {
        let t = UNIX_EPOCH + std::time::Duration::from_nanos(nanos);
        std::fs::File::options()
            .write(true)
            .open(path)?
            .set_modified(t)
    }
}

/// Every folder (a name ending in `/`) and file (its bytes as Latin-1) under `root` but `skip`, as the driver's `tree`.
fn tree(root: &Path, skip: Option<&Path>) -> BTreeMap<String, Value> {
    let mut out = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut todo = vec![root.to_owned()];
    while let Some(dir) = todo.pop() {
        for entry in std::fs::read_dir(&dir).unwrap() {
            let path = entry.unwrap().path();
            if Some(path.as_path()) == skip {
                continue;
            }
            let rel = path
                .strip_prefix(root)
                .unwrap()
                .to_string_lossy()
                .replace('\\', "/");
            if path.is_dir() {
                out.insert(format!("{rel}/"), Value::Null);
                todo.push(path);
            } else {
                out.insert(rel, json!(latin1(&std::fs::read(&path).unwrap())));
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

/// A synthetic game and documents folder like the user's: ReShade with RenoDX, the state bridge, three mods (one of
/// them the bridge's), two loose ASIs, steam_appid.txt, CRLF settings and a ReShade.ini with a BOM.
fn boot_files() -> BTreeMap<&'static str, String> {
    let settings = "[Rendering]\r\nDLSSGMode=2\r\nVSync=true\r\nMotionBlur=true\r\n[Rendering/DRS]\r\nAllowed=1\r\n\
                    [Gameplay]\r\nCameraAutoRotX=true\r\nCameraAutoRotY=true\r\n[Version]\r\nConfigVersion=7\r\n";
    let reshade = "\u{feff}[ADDON]\r\nLoadFromDllMain=\r\n\r\n[GENERAL]\r\nPresetPath=.\\ReShadePreset.ini\r\n\r\n\
                   [renodx-thewitcher3remastered]\r\nSettingsMode=1\r\n\r\n[renodx-thewitcher3remastered-preset1]\r\n\
                   ToneMapGameNits=203\r\nToneMapPeakNits=1000\r\n";
    BTreeMap::from([
        ("docs/dx12user.settings", settings.to_owned()),
        ("docs/gamesaves/QuickSave.sav", "quick".to_owned()),
        (
            "game/bin/config/base/general.ini",
            "[General]\r\nGameLanguage=en\r\n".to_owned(),
        ),
        ("game/bin/x64_dx12/witcher3.exe", "MZ stand-in".to_owned()),
        ("game/bin/x64_dx12/steam_appid.txt", "292030".to_owned()),
        ("game/bin/x64_dx12/ReShade.ini", latin1(reshade.as_bytes())),
        (
            "game/bin/x64_dx12/ReShadePreset.ini",
            "Techniques=SyntheticHdr\r\nX=1\r\n".to_owned(),
        ),
        ("game/bin/x64_dx12/dxgi.dll", "reshade".to_owned()),
        (
            "game/bin/x64_dx12/renodx-thewitcher3remastered.addon64",
            "renodx".to_owned(),
        ),
        (
            "game/bin/x64_dx12/W3GameStateBridge.asi",
            "bridge".to_owned(),
        ),
        ("game/bin/x64_dx12/Tweaks.asi", "tweaks".to_owned()),
        (
            "game/Mods/modAlpha/content/blob0.bundle",
            "alpha".to_owned(),
        ),
        (
            "game/Mods/modBeta/content/scripts/local/beta.ws",
            "beta".to_owned(),
        ),
        (
            "game/Mods/modW3GameStateBridge/content/scripts/local/w3gsb.ws",
            "w3gsb".to_owned(),
        ),
        (
            "game/content/content0/x64.final.redscripts",
            "compiled".to_owned(),
        ),
    ])
}

/// quen-core's boot on its own copy of the case's files: plan, apply through a journal, the files at the launch, then
/// a replay of the journal and the parking folders, empty again, removed (as quen does after a replay).
fn boot_rust(input: &Value) -> Value {
    let root = PathBuf::from(format!("{}-rust", text(input, "dir")));
    for (rel, data) in input["files"].as_object().unwrap() {
        let path = root.join(rel);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
        let bytes: Vec<u8> = data.as_str().unwrap().chars().map(|c| c as u8).collect();
        std::fs::write(path, bytes).unwrap();
    }
    let (game, quen) = (root.join("game"), root.join("quen"));
    let env = |key: &str| input["env"][key].as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_owned();
    let bin = boot::bin_dir(&game);
    let (mods, bin_entries) = (listing(&game.join("Mods")), listing(&bin));
    let preset: Vec<(String, f64)> = input["preset"]
        .as_array()
        .unwrap()
        .iter()
        .map(|kv| {
            let (k, v) = kv.as_str().unwrap().split_once('=').unwrap();
            (k.to_owned(), v.parse().unwrap())
        })
        .collect();
    let preset: Vec<(&str, f64)> = preset.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.as_str(), *v)).collect();
    let never: Vec<&str> = [park::W3_NEVER_PARK, HARNESS_OWN].concat();
    let (flat, sections, park_names, keep) = (
        env("W3_SETTINGS"),
        env("W3_SECTION_SETTINGS"),
        env("W3_PARK_MODS"),
        env("W3_PARK_KEEP"),
    );
    let devkit = if env("W3_NO_DEVKIT") == "1" {
        ""
    } else {
        r"devkit\renodx-devkit.addon64"
    };
    let backups = quen.join("backup");
    let documents = root.join("docs");
    let inputs = Inputs {
        game_dir: &game,
        documents: &documents,
        backups: &backups,
        fg: env("W3_KEEP_FG") == "1",
        vsync: env("W3_VSYNC_OFF") != "1",
        flat: &flat,
        sections: &sections,
        park: &park_names,
        keep: &keep,
        never_park: &never,
        pairs: GSB,
        mods: &mods,
        bin: &bin_entries,
        more: park::More::default(),
        renodx: Some(RenoDx {
            addon: "renodx-thewitcher3remastered.addon64",
            preset: &preset,
        }),
        load_from_dll_main: Some(devkit),
        play: false,
    };
    let fs = Disk {
        trash: quen.join("trash"),
    };
    let changes = match boot::plan(&fs, &inputs) {
        Ok(changes) => changes,
        Err(e) => return refused(e),
    };
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&backups).unwrap();
    for change in &changes {
        if let boot::Change::Move { to, .. } = change {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(to.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
        }
    }
    let path = quen.join("journal.jsonl");
    let mut journal = Journal::create(&fs, &path).unwrap();
    boot::apply(&fs, &mut journal, &changes, &|| false).unwrap();
    let at_launch = tree(&root, Some(&quen));
    let report = replay(&std::fs::read(&path).unwrap(), &fs);
    assert!(report.clean() && report.kept.is_empty(), "{report:#?}");
    let parked = game.join(boot::PARKED);
    for dir in [parked.join("Mods"), parked.join("bin"), parked.clone()] {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir(dir); // fails unless empty
    }
    let prefix = format!("game/{}/", boot::PARKED);
    let mut names: Vec<&str> = at_launch
        .keys()
        .filter_map(|k| k.strip_prefix(&prefix))
        .filter_map(|rest| rest.strip_prefix("Mods/").or(rest.strip_prefix("bin/")))
        .filter_map(|rest| rest.split('/').next())
        .filter(|name| !name.is_empty())
        .collect();
    names.sort();
    names.dedup();
    let files: BTreeMap<&String, &Value> = at_launch
        .iter()
        .filter(|(k, _)| !k.starts_with(&prefix))
        .collect();
    json!({"ok": {
        "launch": {"files": files, "parked": names},
        "argv": ["game/bin/x64_dx12/witcher3.exe"],
        "after": tree(&root, Some(&quen)),
    }})
}

#[test]
fn boot_files_and_restore() {
    let base = boot_files();
    let with = |changes: &[(&'static str, &str)]| {
        let mut files = base.clone();
        for (rel, data) in changes {
            files.insert(rel, (*data).to_owned());
        }
        files
    };
    let settings = &base["docs/dx12user.settings"];
    let no_fg = settings.replace("DLSSGMode=2\r\n", "");
    let lf = settings.replace("\r\n", "\n");
    let c = |name, files: &BTreeMap<&str, String>, env: Value, preset: &[&str], known| Case {
        name,
        input: json!({"files": files, "env": env, "preset": preset, "save": null}),
        known,
    };
    let console =
        Some("quen turns the console on for every boot (its save load types a console line)");
    let all = json!({
        "W3_PARK_MODS": "ALL", "W3_PARK_KEEP": "modBeta", "W3_VSYNC_OFF": "1", "W3_NO_DEVKIT": "1",
        "W3_SETTINGS": "MotionBlur=false", "W3_SECTION_SETTINGS": "Rendering/DRS:Allowed=0;Gameplay:Hdr=1",
    });
    let general_has_it = with(&[
        ("docs/dx12user.settings", &lf),
        (
            "game/bin/config/base/general.ini",
            "[General]\nDBGConsoleOn=false\nX=1\n",
        ),
    ]);
    let cases = vec![
        c("plain", &base, json!({}), &[], console),
        c(
            "park_two",
            &base,
            json!({"W3_PARK_MODS": "modAlpha,Tweaks.asi"}),
            &[],
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "park_all_overrides_preset",
            &base,
            all,
            &[
                "ToneMapGameNits=250",
                "ToneMapPeakNits=800.5",
                "+DevNew=0.1",
            ],
            Some(
                "quen's ALL parks the W3GSB pair whole (learned from the files); the harness never parks it",
            ),
        ),
        c(
            "keep_fg",
            &base,
            json!({"W3_KEEP_FG": "1", "W3_PARK_MODS": "modBeta"}),
            &[],
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "lf_settings_console_key",
            &general_has_it,
            json!({"W3_PARK_MODS": "modAlpha"}),
            &[],
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "bad_override",
            &base,
            json!({"W3_SETTINGS": "Missing=1"}),
            &[],
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "no_dlssg_line",
            &with(&[("docs/dx12user.settings", &no_fg)]),
            json!({}),
            &[],
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "settings_of_4_04",
            &with(&[("docs/w3ver.active", "404")]),
            json!({}),
            &[],
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "preset_typo",
            &base,
            json!({"W3_PARK_MODS": "modAlpha"}),
            &["ToneMapGameNitz=1"],
            None,
        ),
        c(
            "section_value_backslash",
            &base,
            json!({"W3_SECTION_SETTINGS": r"Rendering/DRS:Allowed=a\1"}),
            &[],
            Some(
                "the harness's section replace reads its value as a regex template: it refuses, quen writes it",
            ),
        ),
        c(
            "never_park_bridge",
            &base,
            json!({"W3_PARK_MODS": "W3GameStateBridge.asi"}),
            &[],
            None,
        ),
    ];
    parity("boot", cases, boot_rust, |p, r| p == r);
}

```

`crates/quen-core/tests/parity/driver.py`:

```py
"""Parity driver for tests/parity.rs: runs synthetic cases through the Python harness's own functions
and prints one JSON result per case.

The functions come from the harness folder named by QUEN_HARNESS_DIR, as source only: the top-level statements that
define them run in a namespace of the driver's own. None of the harness's import-time work happens (its chdir, its
folders, its numpy / cv2 / Win32 imports), nothing is written there, and the game's real paths are never set: a global
the driver doesn't supply is a NameError, not a fallback to the real game.

stdin: a JSON list of cases {"kind", "dir" (an empty scratch folder of the test's), ...};
stdout: a JSON list of {"ok": result} or {"err": "Type: message"}, one per case.
"""
import ast, contextlib, csv, glob, hashlib, importlib.util, io, json, math, os, re, shutil, struct, sys, time, types, warnings
import numpy as np

HARNESS = os.environ["QUEN_HARNESS_DIR"]
if os.name == "nt": import _winapi


def load(file, names, **env):
    """The top-level defs and assignments of HARNESS/file that bind any of `names`, run in a fresh namespace."""
    path = os.path.join(HARNESS, file)
    tree = ast.parse(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read(), path)

    def binds(node):
        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)): return {node.name}
        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign): return {n.id for t in node.targets for n in ast.walk(t) if isinstance(n, ast.Name)}
        if isinstance(node, ast.AugAssign) and isinstance(node.target, ast.Name): return {node.target.id}  # SC |= {...}
        return set()
    body = [n for n in tree.body if binds(n) & names]
    missing = names - set().union(*map(binds, body))
    if missing: raise SystemExit(f"{file}: no top-level {sorted(missing)}")
    ns = {"os": os, "re": re, "csv": csv, "json": json, "sys": sys, "time": time, "np": np, **env}
    exec(compile(ast.Module(body, []), path, "exec"), ns)
    return ns


# ROOT only names the parking folder, which park_names never touches.
IS = load("ini_session.py", {"apply_settings", "park_home", "park_names", "PLAIN", "BRIDGE", "bridge_flags", "bridge_loaded",
                             "perf", "PRESENTMON", "SIG_BITS"}, ROOT="%GAME_DIR%")
B404 = load("boot404.py", {"medians"})
W3 = load("w3ctl.py", {"SC", "parse_tokens", "describe", "die"})
CT = load("console_type.py", {"US", "SHIFTED", "PROMPT_ON", "PROMPT_OFF", "console_open", "tap", "main"})
CP = load("cvar_poke.py", {"TYPES", "CHUNK", "sections", "read_section", "cstr", "find", "show", "encode", "run"},
          struct=struct)
PP = load("pool_probe.py", {"STAMP"})


def write(path, text):
    with open(path, "wb") as f: f.write(text.encode())


def settings(case):
    """apply_settings on a copy; the file's bytes travel as Latin-1 text, one char per byte."""
    p = os.path.join(case["dir"], "dx12user.settings")
    with open(p, "wb") as f: f.write(case["data"].encode("latin-1"))
    IS["apply_settings"](p, case["flat"], case["sections"])
    return open(p, "rb").read().decode("latin-1")


def layout(case):
    """The synthetic Mods and bin folders of a park case (the Rust side lists the same folders). Outside the case's
    try: a link that can't be made fails the run instead of passing for a refusal."""
    for folder, entries in (("Mods", case["mods"]), ("bin", case["bin"])):
        os.mkdir(os.path.join(case["dir"], folder))
        for name, kind in entries:
            p = os.path.join(case["dir"], folder, name)
            if kind == "dir": os.mkdir(p)
            elif kind == "file": open(p, "wb").close()
            else:  # a junction, dirlink or filelink to a target outside the listing
                target = os.path.join(case["dir"], "target-" + name)
                open(target, "wb").close() if kind == "filelink" else os.mkdir(target)
                if kind == "junction" and os.name == "nt": _winapi.CreateJunction(target, p)
                else: os.symlink(target, p, target_is_directory=kind != "filelink")


def park(case):
    """park_names over the case's layout."""
    IS["MODS"], IS["GAME"] = (os.path.join(case["dir"], d) for d in ("Mods", "bin"))
    os.environ.update(W3_PARK_MODS=case["park"], W3_PARK_KEEP=case["keep"])
    os.environ.pop("W3_PARK_RENODX", None)
    return sorted(IS["park_names"]())


def bridge(case):
    """bridge_loaded is called with the `before` log on disk, its check after `after` was appended."""
    IS["GAME"] = case["dir"]
    p = os.path.join(case["dir"], "W3GameStateBridge.log")
    write(p, case["before"])
    in_game = IS["bridge_loaded"](0)
    write(p, case["before"] + case["after"])
    return {"flags": IS["bridge_flags"](0), "loaded": bool(in_game(0))}


def presentmon(case):
    """perf with PresentMon stubbed to copy the synthetic CSV, boot404's medians, and numpy's p95 (no harness function
    has one) over the rows and cells perf keeps."""
    src = os.path.join(case["dir"], "in.csv")
    write(src, case["csv"])
    IS["OUT"] = case["dir"]
    IS["subprocess"] = types.SimpleNamespace(run=lambda argv, **_: shutil.copyfile(src, argv[argv.index("--output_file") + 1]))
    IS["W"] = types.SimpleNamespace(procs=dict)
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()): perf = IS["perf"]("parity")
    del perf["tag"]
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(src, encoding="utf-8-sig")))[5:]
    cells = lambda k: [float(r[k]) for r in rows if r.get(k) not in (None, "", "NA")]
    p95 = [float(np.percentile(v, 95)) if v else math.nan for v in (cells("MsBetweenPresents"), cells("MsGPUBusy"))]
    return {"perf": perf, "medians": B404["medians"]([src]), "p95": p95}


def cvar(case):
    """cvar_poke's run (find, show, then --set / --restore) on the case's image, its prints swallowed: the object's
    offset and the image after."""
    base, img = case["base"], bytearray.fromhex(case["image"])

    def rd(addr, fmt):
        o = addr - base
        return struct.unpack_from(fmt, img, o)[0] if 0 <= o <= len(img) - struct.calcsize(fmt) else None

    def wr(addr, data): img[addr - base:addr - base + len(data)] = data
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
        obj = CP["run"](rd, base, case["name"], case["action"], case["value"], lambda: wr)
    return {"obj": obj - base, "image": img.hex()}


def cvar_build(case):
    """The build cvar_poke's layout is checked for (pool_probe's STAMP), as the KB writes it."""
    return "0x%08X" % PP["STAMP"]


def presentmon_argv(case):
    """perf's PresentMon command line, the exe left out, with W3_PM_FLAGS = case["flags"]; PresentMon stubbed to record it
    and write a small CSV."""
    IS["OUT"], seen = case["dir"], []
    def run(argv, **_):
        seen.append(argv[1:])
        write(argv[argv.index("--output_file") + 1], "MsBetweenPresents\n" + "1\n" * 8)
    IS["subprocess"], IS["W"] = types.SimpleNamespace(run=run), types.SimpleNamespace(procs=dict)
    os.environ["W3_PM_FLAGS"] = case["flags"]
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()): IS["perf"](case["tag"], case["secs"])
    return seen[0]


def tree(root, skip=()):
    """Every folder (a name ending in "/", no content) and file (its bytes as Latin-1) under root, by relative path."""
    out = {}
    for r, dirs, files in os.walk(root):
        dirs[:] = sorted(d for d in dirs if os.path.join(r, d) not in skip)
        for d in dirs: out[os.path.relpath(os.path.join(r, d), root).replace(os.sep, "/") + "/"] = None
        for f in files: out[os.path.relpath(os.path.join(r, f), root).replace(os.sep, "/")] = open(os.path.join(r, f), "rb").read().decode("latin-1")
    return out


def launched(files):
    """A tree at launch without the parking folder, and the names parked there (its marker aside)."""
    park = "game/mods_parked_by_harness/"
    names = sorted({k[len(park):].split("/")[0] for k in files if k.startswith(park) and k != park} - {"parked.json"})
    return {"files": {k: v for k, v in files.items() if not k.startswith(park)}, "parked": names}


class Launched(BaseException):
    """Raised by the stubbed Popen: the boot stops where it would start the game."""


def boot(case):
    """ini_session.py's own `boot` on a synthetic game and documents folder (case["files"]), stopped where it would
    launch the game: the files as the game would find them, then as boot's own failure cleanup (kill_all, restore,
    unpark, unlock: what `end` runs) leaves them. Every global it reads is set here; its processes, window and keys are
    stubs, and its harness folder is the case's own."""
    root = case["dir"]
    for rel, data in case["files"].items():
        p = os.path.join(root, *rel.split("/"))
        if rel.endswith("/"): os.makedirs(p, exist_ok=True); continue
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
        with open(p, "wb") as f: f.write(data.encode("latin-1"))
    game, docs, harness = (os.path.join(root, d) for d in ("game", "docs", "harness"))
    bin_, ini = os.path.join(game, "bin", "x64_dx12"), os.path.join(harness, "cap", "ini")
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(ini, "orig"))
    seen = {}

    def popen(cmd, cwd=None):
        seen["at_launch"], seen["argv"] = tree(root, {harness}), [os.path.relpath(a, root).replace(os.sep, "/") for a in cmd]
        raise Launched()
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("ini_writer", os.path.join(HARNESS, "ini_writer.py"))
    iw = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(iw)
    files = {"ini": os.path.join(bin_, "ReShade.ini"), "preset": os.path.join(bin_, "ReShadePreset.ini"),
             "settings": os.path.join(docs, "dx12user.settings"), "general": os.path.join(game, "bin", "config", "base", "general.ini")}
    ns = load("ini_session.py", {"boot", "Laps", "need_501", "versions", "apply_settings", "unpark", "park_names", "park_home",
                                 "park", "PLAIN", "BRIDGE", "signals_plan", "save_path", "saves_newest_first", "write_p1", "parse_kv",
                                 "patch_bytes", "console_on", "launch_cmd", "kill_all", "ident", "restore", "remove_rdx",
                                 "remove_signals", "unlock", "sha", "tree_sha"},
              ROOT=game, GAME=bin_, MODS=os.path.join(game, "Mods"), INI=files["ini"], PRESET=files["preset"],
              SETTINGS=files["settings"], GENERAL=files["general"], SAVES=os.path.join(docs, "gamesaves"), FILES=files,
              OUT=ini, ORIG=os.path.join(ini, "orig"), STATE=os.path.join(ini, "state.json"), STARTED=os.path.join(ini, "started.json"),
              BOOTS=os.path.join(harness, "cap", "boots.jsonl"), ADDON=os.path.join(bin_, "renodx-thewitcher3remastered.addon64"),
              BUILD=os.path.join(harness, "no-build.addon64"), VAXIS=os.path.join(game, "Mods", "modGraphicsControl"),
              RDX_DST=os.path.join(game, "Mods", "modRenoDXTest"), RDX_MARK="rdx_mod", SIG_MARK="signals.json",
              MOD="renodx-thewitcher3remastered", P1="renodx-thewitcher3remastered-preset1", set_values=iw.set_values,
              W=types.SimpleNamespace(LOCK=os.path.join(ini, "session.lock"), procs=dict, chain=lambda _: [(1, "python.exe"), (2, "parent.exe")]),
              pids=list, own=lambda *a, **k: None, quen_live=lambda: None, sh=lambda *a: types.SimpleNamespace(stdout="", returncode=0),
              subprocess=types.SimpleNamespace(Popen=popen),
              ctypes=types.SimpleNamespace(windll=types.SimpleNamespace(user32=types.SimpleNamespace(GetForegroundWindow=lambda: 0))),
              shutil=shutil, glob=glob, hashlib=hashlib)
    for k in [k for k in os.environ if k.startswith("W3_")]: del os.environ[k]
    os.environ.update(W3_ADDON_ANY="1", **case["env"])
    cwd = os.getcwd(); os.chdir(harness)  # boot writes .w3ctl_prev into its working folder
    try:
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()): ns["boot"](*ns["parse_kv"](case["preset"]), case["save"])
        raise RuntimeError("boot returned without launching")
    except Launched:
        pass
    finally:
        os.chdir(cwd)
    return {"launch": launched(seen["at_launch"]), "argv": seen["argv"], "after": tree(root, {harness})}


def keys(case):
    """parse_tokens + describe: the lines `w3ctl.py keys TOKENS --dry-run` prints after its header."""
    return [W3["describe"](ev) for ev in W3["parse_tokens"](case["tokens"], case["hold"], case["gap"])]


def console(case):
    """console_type's main with the game stubbed in front, every key and sleep recorded (its two w3ctl calls through
    parse_tokens with w3ctl's defaults, the layout's console key left at 0x29); the closing check sees a black frame."""
    seen = []
    def event(ev):
        seen.append(f"sleep {round(ev[1])}" if ev[0] == "sleep" else f"key {'up' if ev[3] else 'down'} 0x{ev[2]:03X}")
    def w3ctl(argv, check):
        for ev in W3["parse_tokens"](argv[argv.index("keys") + 1:], 200, 400): event(ev)
    CT.update(W=types.SimpleNamespace(session_guard=lambda: None, find_game=lambda: 1, is_fg=lambda hwnd: True, send=event),
              subprocess=types.SimpleNamespace(run=w3ctl), time=types.SimpleNamespace(sleep=lambda s: event(("sleep", s * 1000))),
              grab=lambda gdi: np.zeros((720, 1280, 3), np.uint8), cv2=__import__("cv2"))
    CT["main"](case["line"])
    return seen


def prompt(case):
    """console_open on a synthetic w x h frame: `bg` (or `noise`: random pixels from that seed), the prompt's lit pixels
    scaled from 720p (edges rounded) at `fg` when `prompt`. The frame goes to frame.bgra for the Rust side."""
    w, h = case["w"], case["h"]
    img = (np.random.default_rng(case["noise"]).integers(0, 256, (h, w, 3), np.uint8) if "noise" in case
           else np.full((h, w, 3), case["bg"], np.uint8))
    if case["prompt"]:
        for r, c in zip(*CT["PROMPT_ON"]):
            img[round(r * h / 720):round((r + 1) * h / 720), round(c * w / 1280):round((c + 1) * w / 1280)] = case["fg"]
    np.dstack([img, np.full((h, w), 255, np.uint8)]).tofile(os.path.join(case["dir"], "frame.bgra"))
    CT["cv2"] = __import__("cv2")
    return bool(CT["console_open"](img))


def bits(case):
    return list(IS["SIG_BITS"])


def clean(x):
    """JSON has no NaN: a non-finite float goes out as its name."""
    if isinstance(x, float) and not math.isfinite(x): return str(x)
    if isinstance(x, (list, tuple)): return [clean(v) for v in x]
    if isinstance(x, dict): return {k: clean(v) for k, v in x.items()}
    return x


warnings.simplefilter("ignore")  # numpy's mean-of-nothing warning: the NaN it returns is the result
KINDS = {f.__name__: f for f in (settings, park, bridge, presentmon, presentmon_argv, bits, cvar, cvar_build, boot,
                                  keys, console, prompt)}
out = []
for case in json.loads(sys.stdin.buffer.read()):
    os.makedirs(case["dir"])
    if case["kind"] == "park": layout(case)
    try: out.append({"ok": clean(KINDS[case["kind"]](case))})
    except (Exception, SystemExit) as e: out.append({"err": f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"})
json.dump(out, sys.stdout)

```

`crates/quen-core/tests/restore_journal.rs`:

```rs
//! Crash injection for the session journal (docs/intent.md, "The session journal"). A scripted session (back up 4
//! files, patch 2, park 3 mods and a Vortex mod's DLL, menu XML and DLC folder, place 2 files) is cut at every byte of every step's lines; each replay must give the
//! user's files back exactly, or report every difference it leaves. All files are synthetic.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::ops::Range;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use quen_core::journal::{Action, Fs, Journal, MemFs, ReplayReport, replay, sha256_hex};
use quen_core::park::{self, Entry, Home, Listing, Managed};
use quen_core::settings;

/// quen's own data root: the journal, backups and staged files, none of them the user's.
const DATA: &str = "QUEN";
const JOURNAL: &str = "QUEN/state/journal.jsonl";
const SETTINGS: &str = "DOCS/dx12user.settings";
const PRESET: &str = "GAME/bin/x64/ReShadePreset.ini";
const PARKED_GAMMA: &str = "GAME/quen-parked/Mods/modGamma";
const PLACED_A: &str = "GAME/bin/x64/quen_pack_a.asi";

enum Op {
    Backup(PathBuf, PathBuf),
    Patch(PathBuf, Vec<u8>),
    Move(PathBuf, PathBuf),
    /// Stage the bytes, then rename the staged file to the destination.
    Place(PathBuf, PathBuf, &'static str),
}

fn backup_of(path: &str) -> PathBuf {
    Path::new(DATA)
        .join("backup")
        .join(Path::new(path).file_name().unwrap())
}

/// The user's files before the session: 4 config files, 3 mods (one with a non-ASCII name, so cuts split a UTF-8
/// character), a Vortex mod's DLL (a hardlink of its staging copy), menu XML and DLC folder, and a bin file nobody
/// touches.
fn user_state() -> MemFs {
    let fs = MemFs::default();
    fs.put(
        "GAME/bin/x64/ReShade.ini",
        "[GENERAL]\nPresetPath=.\\ReShadePreset.ini\n",
    );
    fs.put(PRESET, "Techniques=SyntheticA,SyntheticB\n");
    fs.put(
        SETTINGS,
        "[Rendering]\r\nMotionBlur=true\r\n[Gameplay]\r\nAutoRotate=true\r\n",
    );
    fs.put("DOCS/general.ini", "[General]\nDBGConsoleOn=false\n");
    fs.put("GAME/Mods/modAlpha", "alpha tree");
    fs.put("GAME/Mods/modBeta", "beta tree");
    fs.put("GAME/Mods/modGamma", "gamma tree");
    fs.put("GAME/bin/x64/untouched.dll", "not ours");
    fs.put("STAGING/W3LoadFix/bin/x64_dx12/dsound.dll", "proxy");
    fs.link(
        "STAGING/W3LoadFix/bin/x64_dx12/dsound.dll",
        "GAME/bin/x64/dsound.dll",
    );
    fs.put("GAME/menu/w3loadfix.xml", "<menu/>");
    fs.put("GAME/DLC/dlcExtra", "dlc tree");
    fs
}

/// The scripted session over [`user_state`]: back up 4 files, patch 2, park 3 mods and the Vortex mod's 3 units by
/// `ALL`, place 2 files.
fn session() -> (MemFs, Vec<Op>) {
    let fs = user_state();
    let configs = [
        "GAME/bin/x64/ReShade.ini",
        PRESET,
        SETTINGS,
        "DOCS/general.ini",
    ];
    let mut ops: Vec<Op> = configs
        .iter()
        .map(|c| Op::Backup(c.into(), backup_of(c)))
        .collect();
    let settings = fs.read(Path::new(SETTINGS)).unwrap();
    let settings = settings::validate(
        &settings,
        "MotionBlur=false",
        "Gameplay:AutoRotate=false;Rendering:Hdr=1",
    );
    ops.push(Op::Patch(SETTINGS.into(), settings.unwrap()));
    let preset = settings::apply_flat(&fs.read(Path::new(PRESET)).unwrap(), "Techniques=").unwrap();
    ops.push(Op::Patch(PRESET.into(), preset));
    let mods: Vec<Entry> = ["modAlpha", "modBeta", "modGamma", "modQuen"]
        .map(|name| Entry {
            name: name.into(),
            is_dir: true,
            is_link: false,
        })
        .into();
    let mods = Listing {
        dir: Path::new("GAME/Mods"),
        entries: &mods,
    };
    let file = |name: &str, is_dir| Entry {
        name: name.into(),
        is_dir,
        is_link: false,
    };
    let (bin, menu, dlc) = (
        [file("dsound.dll", false), file("untouched.dll", false)],
        [file("w3loadfix.xml", false)],
        [file("dlcExtra", true)],
    );
    let managed = [Managed {
        label: "W3LoadFix 1.0.8 (nexus 13881)".into(),
        names: vec!["nexus:13881".into()],
        units: vec![
            (Home::Bin, "dsound.dll".into()),
            (Home::Menu, "w3loadfix.xml".into()),
            (Home::Dlc, "dlcExtra".into()),
        ],
        ties: Vec::new(),
    }];
    let more = park::More {
        menu: Some(Listing {
            dir: Path::new("GAME/menu"),
            entries: &menu,
        }),
        dlc: Some(Listing {
            dir: Path::new("GAME/DLC"),
            entries: &dlc,
        }),
        managed: &managed,
        ..park::More::default()
    };
    let bin = Listing {
        dir: Path::new("GAME/bin/x64"),
        entries: &bin,
    };
    let plan = park::plan(
        "ALL",
        "",
        park::W3_NEVER_PARK,
        &[],
        mods,
        bin,
        Path::new("GAME/quen-parked"),
        &more,
    )
    .unwrap();
    ops.extend(plan.moves.into_iter().map(|m| Op::Move(m.from, m.to)));
    ops.push(Op::Place(
        Path::new(DATA).join("stage/a.asi"),
        PLACED_A.into(),
        "pack a",
    ));
    ops.push(Op::Place(
        Path::new(DATA).join("stage/b.ini"),
        "GAME/bin/x64/quen_pack_b.ini".into(),
        "pack b",
    ));
    (fs, ops)
}

/// The journal step for `op`, as the session writes it before acting (a place stages its file first).
fn action(fs: &MemFs, op: &Op) -> Action {
    match op {
        Op::Backup(src, backup) => Action::Backup {
            src: src.clone(),
            backup: backup.clone(),
            sha: fs.sha256(src).unwrap(),
        },
        Op::Patch(path, bytes) => Action::Patch {
            path: path.clone(),
            sha_before: fs.sha256(path).unwrap(),
            sha_after: sha256_hex(bytes),
            mtime: Some(fs.mtime(path).unwrap()),
            // As a launch journals dx12user.settings: its forced keys and the game's version stamp (finding 35).
            ignore: match path == Path::new(SETTINGS) {
                true => vec!["AutoRotate".into(), "LastGameVersion".into()],
                false => Vec::new(),
            },
        },
        Op::Move(from, to) => Action::Move {
            from: from.clone(),
            to: to.clone(),
            sha: fs.sha256(from).unwrap(),
            file_id: fs.file_id(from).unwrap(),
        },
        Op::Place(staged, dest, bytes) => {
            fs.write_atomic(staged, bytes.as_bytes()).unwrap();
            Action::Place {
                dest: dest.clone(),
                sha: sha256_hex(bytes.as_bytes()),
                file_id: fs.file_id(staged).unwrap(),
            }
        }
    }
}

fn perform(fs: &MemFs, op: &Op) {
    match op {
        Op::Backup(src, backup) => fs.write_atomic(backup, &fs.read(src).unwrap()),
        Op::Patch(path, bytes) => fs.write_atomic(path, bytes),
        Op::Move(from, to) => fs.rename(from, to),
        Op::Place(staged, dest, _) => fs.rename(staged, dest),
    }
    .unwrap()
}

/// A session stopped at step `k` (0-based): steps before it ran in full; step `k` has its Step and Done lines in the
/// journal, and its action ran only if `perform`.
struct Run {
    fs: MemFs,
    journal: Vec<u8>,
    step: Range<usize>,
    done: Range<usize>,
}

fn run(make: fn() -> (MemFs, Vec<Op>), k: usize, perform_k: bool) -> Run {
    let (fs, ops) = make();
    let path = Path::new(JOURNAL);
    let mut journal = Journal::create(&fs, path).unwrap();
    let len = || fs.read(path).map_or(0, |j| j.len());
    for op in &ops[..k] {
        let id = journal.step(action(&fs, op)).unwrap();
        perform(&fs, op);
        journal.done(id).unwrap();
    }
    let start = len();
    let id = journal.step(action(&fs, &ops[k])).unwrap();
    let mid = len();
    if perform_k {
        perform(&fs, &ops[k]);
    }
    journal.done(id).unwrap();
    let journal = fs.read(path).unwrap();
    Run {
        step: start..mid,
        done: mid..journal.len(),
        journal,
        fs,
    }
}

/// The user's files: everything outside quen's data root.
fn user_files(fs: &MemFs) -> BTreeMap<PathBuf, Vec<u8>> {
    fs.files()
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|(path, _)| !path.starts_with(DATA))
        .collect()
}

fn backups(fs: &MemFs) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    fs.files()
        .into_keys()
        .filter(|path| path.starts_with(Path::new(DATA).join("backup")))
        .collect()
}

/// Cuts the journal of `make`'s session at every byte of every step's lines, crashing before or after the action as
/// the cut allows, and checks that each replay restores the user's files exactly. Returns the number of replays.
fn crash_everywhere(make: fn() -> (MemFs, Vec<Op>)) -> usize {
    let (fs, ops) = make();
    let original = user_files(&fs);
    let mut replays = 0;
    for k in 0..ops.len() {
        for perform_k in [false, true] {
            let run = run(make, k, perform_k);
            // Not performed: the crash came while the Step line was written, or just after.
            // Performed: just after the action, or while its Done line was written.
            let cuts = if perform_k {
                run.step.end..=run.done.end
            } else {
                run.step.start..=run.step.end
            };
            for cut in cuts {
                let fs = run.fs.clone();
                let report = replay(&run.journal[..cut], &fs);
                let at = format!(
                    "step {} of {}, performed {perform_k}, cut at byte {cut}",
                    k + 1,
                    ops.len()
                );
                assert_eq!(user_files(&fs), original, "{at}: {report:#?}");
                assert!(
                    report.clean() && report.kept.is_empty(),
                    "{at}: {report:#?}"
                );
                assert_eq!(
                    backups(&fs),
                    Vec::<PathBuf>::new(),
                    "{at}: backups not recycled"
                );
                // A cut inside a line (not just before its line break) tears it.
                let torn = cut > 0
                    && run.journal[cut - 1] != b'\n'
                    && run.journal.get(cut) != Some(&b'\n');
                assert_eq!(
                    report.notes.iter().any(|n| n.contains("torn")),
                    torn,
                    "{at}: {report:#?}"
                );
                replays += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    replays
}

#[test]
fn every_crash_point_of_the_session_restores_the_user_files() {
    assert_eq!(session().1.len(), 14);
    let replays = crash_everywhere(session);
    assert!(replays > 14 * 100, "{replays} replays");
}

#[test]
fn every_crash_point_of_a_file_patched_twice_restores_it() {
    fn twice() -> (MemFs, Vec<Op>) {
        let fs = user_state();
        let once = settings::apply_flat(&fs.read(Path::new(SETTINGS)).unwrap(), "MotionBlur=false")
            .unwrap();
        let twice = settings::apply_sections(&once, "Gameplay:AutoRotate=false").unwrap();
        let ops = vec![
            Op::Backup(SETTINGS.into(), backup_of(SETTINGS)),
            Op::Patch(SETTINGS.into(), once),
            Op::Patch(SETTINGS.into(), twice),
        ];
        (fs, ops)
    }
    assert!(crash_everywhere(twice) > 3 * 100);
}

/// The whole session run, its journal complete.
fn ended() -> (MemFs, Vec<u8>) {
    let (_, ops) = session();
    let run = run(session, ops.len() - 1, true);
    (run.fs, run.journal)
}

/// Every user file that differs from `original` is named by the report: kept beside, or in a step it left.
fn assert_reported(original: &BTreeMap<PathBuf, Vec<u8>>, fs: &MemFs, report: &ReplayReport) {
    let now = user_files(fs);
    let named: BTreeSet<&Path> = report
        .kept
        .iter()
        .map(PathBuf::as_path)
        .chain(report.left.iter().flat_map(|left| match &left.action {
            Action::Backup { src, backup, .. } => vec![src.as_path(), backup.as_path()],
            Action::Patch { path, .. } => vec![path.as_path()],
            Action::Move { from, to, .. } => vec![from.as_path(), to.as_path()],
            Action::Place { dest, .. } => vec![dest.as_path()],
            Action::Rebuilt { path, .. }
            | Action::Stage { path, .. }
            | Action::NewLog { path }
            | Action::NewDir { path } => {
                vec![path.as_path()]
            }
            Action::GameMemory { .. } => vec![],
        }))
        .collect();
    for path in original.keys().chain(now.keys()) {
        if original.get(path) != now.get(path) {
            assert!(
                named.contains(path.as_path()),
                "{} differs, unreported: {report:#?}",
                path.display()
            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_full_replay_ends_the_session() {
    let (fs, journal) = ended();
    assert_ne!(user_files(&fs), user_files(&user_state()));
    let report = replay(&journal, &fs);
    assert_eq!(user_files(&fs), user_files(&user_state()));
    assert!(
        report.clean() && report.kept.is_empty() && report.notes.is_empty(),
        "{report:#?}"
    );
    assert_eq!(report.undone.len(), 2 + 6 + 2, "{report:#?}");
    // The placed files and the four spent backups went to the Recycle Bin, nothing was deleted.
    assert_eq!(fs.recycled(), report.recycled);
    assert_eq!(report.recycled.len(), 2 + 4);
    assert!(backups(&fs).is_empty());
    // A second replay of the same journal finds nothing left to do.
    let again = replay(&journal, &fs);
    assert!(
        again.clean() && again.undone.is_empty() && again.recycled.is_empty(),
        "{again:#?}"
    );
    assert_eq!(user_files(&fs), user_files(&user_state()));
}

#[test]
fn a_config_the_game_rewrote_is_kept_beside_then_restored() {
    let (fs, journal) = ended();
    fs.put(
        SETTINGS,
        "[Rendering]\r\nMotionBlur=false\r\nWrittenByTheGame=1\r\n",
    );
    let report = replay(&journal, &fs);
    let current = PathBuf::from(format!("{SETTINGS}.quen-current"));
    assert_eq!(report.kept, std::slice::from_ref(&current));
    assert!(report.clean(), "{report:#?}");
    let files = fs.files();
    assert_eq!(
        files[&current],
        b"[Rendering]\r\nMotionBlur=false\r\nWrittenByTheGame=1\r\n"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        files[Path::new(SETTINGS)],
        user_state().read(Path::new(SETTINGS)).unwrap()
    );
    assert_reported(&user_files(&user_state()), &fs, &report);
}

/// Finding 35: a copy that differs from the user's only in the step's ignored keys isn't kept beside; a note says so.
#[test]
fn a_rewrite_only_in_ignored_keys_is_not_kept() {
    let (fs, journal) = ended();
    fs.put(
        SETTINGS,
        "[Rendering]\r\nMotionBlur=true\r\n[Gameplay]\r\nAutoRotate=false\r\nLastGameVersion=5.01\r\n",
    );
    let report = replay(&journal, &fs);
    assert!(report.kept.is_empty() && report.clean(), "{report:#?}");
    assert!(
        report
            .notes
            .iter()
            .any(|n| n.contains("only in AutoRotate, LastGameVersion: not kept")),
        "{report:#?}"
    );
    assert_eq!(user_files(&fs), user_files(&user_state()));
}

/// Finding 82: at the end the game's copy differs from the user's only in what the launch wrote (forced keys, a
/// `settings` override, VSync, an appended section the game moved) and LastGameVersion: not kept. A value the game
/// changed besides (a mod menu's) is kept.
#[test]
fn a_copy_holding_only_the_launchs_own_settings_is_not_kept() {
    use quen_core::boot::{self, Inputs};
    let user = "[Rendering]\r\nDLSSGMode=2\r\nVSync=true\r\nMotionBlur=true\r\n[Gameplay]\r\nCameraAutoRotX=true\r\n\
                CameraAutoRotY=true\r\n[Version]\r\nConfigVersion=7\r\nLastGameVersion=5.00\r\n";
    let inputs = Inputs {
        game_dir: Path::new("GAME"),
        documents: Path::new("DOCS"),
        backups: &Path::new(DATA).join("backup"),
        fg: false,
        vsync: false,
        flat: "MotionBlur=false",
        sections: "QuenLiveCheck:Probe=1",
        park: "",
        keep: "",
        never_park: park::W3_NEVER_PARK,
        pairs: &[],
        mods: &[],
        bin: &[],
        more: park::More::default(),
        renodx: None,
        load_from_dll_main: None,
        play: false,
    };
    for (game_changed, kept) in [(false, 0), (true, 1)] {
        let fs = MemFs::default();
        fs.put(SETTINGS, user);
        fs.put("GAME/bin/config/base/general.ini", "[General]\r\nX=1\r\n");
        let changes = boot::plan(&fs, &inputs).unwrap();
        let mut journal = Journal::create(&fs, Path::new(JOURNAL)).unwrap();
        boot::apply(&fs, &mut journal, &changes, &|| false).unwrap();
        // The game rewrites it: the appended section moved to the top, its version stamp, and maybe a menu value.
        let written = String::from_utf8(fs.read(Path::new(SETTINGS)).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert!(written.contains("[QuenLiveCheck]\r\nProbe=1"), "{written}");
        let rest = written.replace("[QuenLiveCheck]\r\nProbe=1\r\n", "");
        let mut by_game = format!("[QuenLiveCheck]\r\nProbe=1\r\n{rest}").replace("5.00", "5.01");
        if game_changed {
            by_game = by_game.replace(
                "CameraAutoRotX=false",
                "CameraAutoRotX=false\r\nMenuOption=2",
            );
        }
        fs.put(SETTINGS, by_game);
        let report = replay(&fs.read(Path::new(JOURNAL)).unwrap(), &fs);
        assert!(report.clean(), "{report:#?}");
        assert_eq!(
            report.kept.len(),
            kept,
            "game changed {game_changed}: {report:#?}"
        );
        assert_eq!(fs.read(Path::new(SETTINGS)).unwrap(), user.as_bytes());
    }
}

/// An atomic write a crash cut off leaves `<file>.quen-tmp` beside a file the journal names; the replay sends it to
/// the Recycle Bin.
#[test]
fn a_cut_off_atomic_write_leaves_no_temp_file() {
    let (fs, journal) = ended();
    let tmp = PathBuf::from(format!("{SETTINGS}.quen-tmp"));
    fs.put(&tmp, "cut off mid-write");
    let report = replay(&journal, &fs);
    assert!(report.clean(), "{report:#?}");
    assert!(
        !fs.exists(&tmp) && report.recycled.contains(&tmp),
        "{report:#?}"
    );
    assert_eq!(user_files(&fs), user_files(&user_state()));
}

/// An earlier session's `.quen-current` with other bytes once left the step, the journal and every launch
/// blocked. The live file now goes beside under the next free name, the earlier copy untouched, and the replay is
/// clean; a second replay reuses the copy that holds the same bytes.
#[test]
fn an_older_quen_current_is_never_overwritten() {
    let (fs, journal) = ended();
    fs.put(SETTINGS, "written by the game");
    fs.put(
        format!("{SETTINGS}.quen-current"),
        "kept by an earlier session",
    );
    let report = replay(&journal, &fs);
    assert!(report.clean(), "{report:#?}");
    let second = PathBuf::from(format!("{SETTINGS}.quen-current-2"));
    assert_eq!(report.kept, std::slice::from_ref(&second));
    let files = fs.files();
    assert_eq!(files[&second], b"written by the game");
    assert_eq!(
        files[&PathBuf::from(format!("{SETTINGS}.quen-current"))],
        b"kept by an earlier session"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        files[Path::new(SETTINGS)],
        user_state().read(Path::new(SETTINGS)).unwrap()
    );
    assert!(backups(&fs).is_empty());
}

#[test]

        "{report:#?}"

}

#[test]

#[test]
```
