/// One of [`tools`]: the verb from its arguments, checked as the protocol checks it; the package and (but for
/// listsaves) a loaded game; the journal for the verbs that taint saves; then the verb and its reply.
pub(crate) fn call(
    session: &Session,
    call: &mut Call,
    name: &str,
    args: &Value,
) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let known: &[&str] = match name {
        "game_pause" => &["on"],
        "game_settime" => &["day", "hour"],
        "game_weather" => &["name", "settle_s"],
        "game_teleport" => &["pos", "rot"],
        "game_items" => &["name", "count", "equip"],
        "world_actors" => &["radius", "max", "tag", "class"],
        _ => &[],
    };
    let cx = ctx(session, args, known)?;
    let settle = match args.get("settle_s").filter(|v| !v.is_null()) {
        None => None,
        Some(v) => Some(
            v.as_f64()
                .filter(|s| (0.0..=SETTLE_MAX_S).contains(s))
                .map(Duration::from_secs_f64)
                .ok_or(format!("settle_s must be seconds, 0 to {SETTLE_MAX_S}"))?,
        ),
    };
    let verb = match name {
        "game_listsaves" => Verb::ListSaves {},
        "world_get" => Verb::WorldGet {},
        "world_actors" => Verb::WorldActors {
            radius: match args.get("radius") {
                None => ACTORS_RADIUS,
                Some(v) => v
                    .as_f64()
                    .ok_or("radius must be a number of metres".to_string())?
                    as f32,
            },
            max: match args.get("max") {
                None => ACTORS_MAX,
                Some(_) => whole(args, "max", MAX_ACTORS)?,
            },
            tag: args
                .get("tag")
                .map(|_| text(args, "tag"))
                .transpose()?
                .map(Into::into),
            class: args
                .get("class")
                .map(|_| text(args, "class"))
                .transpose()?
                .map(Into::into),
        },
        "game_pause" => Verb::Pause {
            on: args["on"]
                .as_bool()
                .ok_or("on must be true or false".to_string())?,
        },
        "game_settime" => Verb::SetTime {
            day: whole(args, "day", i32::MAX as u32)?,
            hour: whole(args, "hour", 23)?,
        },
        "game_weather" => Verb::Weather {
            name: text(args, "name")?.into(),
        },
        "game_teleport" => Verb::Teleport {
            pos: vec3(args, "pos")?.ok_or("pos must be [x, y, z]".to_string())?,
            rot: vec3(args, "rot")?.unwrap_or_default(),
        },
        "game_items" => Verb::ItemsAdd {
            name: text(args, "name")?.into(),
            count: match args.get("count") {
                None => 1,
                Some(_) => whole(args, "count", MAX_ITEM_COUNT)?,
            },
            equip: game::flag(args, "equip")?,
        },
        _ => return Err(Done::Refused(format!("unknown tool {name:?}"))),
    };
    let request = Request {
        id: 1,
        ttl_ms: 0,
        verb: verb.clone(),
    };
    protocol::encode_request(&request).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    doctor::installed(&[&doctor::PACKAGE], cx.config, name)?;
    if name == "world_get" {
        doctor::package_at_least(cx.config, doctor::BEFORE_WORLD, "world_get", "0.1.5")?;
    }
    if name == "game_items" || name == "world_actors" {
        doctor::package_at_least(cx.config, doctor::BEFORE_ITEMS, name, "0.1.10")?;
    }
    if let Verb::WorldActors { tag, class, .. } = &verb
        && (tag.is_some() || class.is_some())
    {
        let tool = "world_actors with tag or class";
        doctor::package_at_least(cx.config, doctor::BEFORE_ENTITIES, tool, "0.1.12")?;
    }
    let last = cx.last_flags();
    if name != "game_listsaves" && last.is_none_or(|f| f & VALID == 0) {
        let why = format!(
            "quen's state shows {}: {name} needs a loaded game. Nothing sent",
            game::shown(last)
        );
        return Err(why.into());
    }
    let channel = cx.channel()?;
    call.lap("check");
    let mut fields = Map::new();
    let taints = matches!(
        verb,
        Verb::SetTime { .. } | Verb::Weather { .. } | Verb::Teleport { .. } | Verb::ItemsAdd { .. }
    );
    let journal = match taints {
        true => {
            let what = format!(
                "channel {}",
                serde_json::to_string(&verb).unwrap_or_default()
            );
            Some(cx.journal(&what, None, true)?)
        }
        false => None,
    };
    let reply = channel.call(verb, REPLY_MAX);
    call.lap("reply");
    // A verb the game refused never ran (feature tests 2c).
    if let Some((mut journal, id)) = journal {
        let ran = !matches!(reply, Err(Error::Refused(..)));
        let note = cx.settle(&mut journal, id, ran);
        fields.extend(note.map(|n| ("journal_note".to_string(), json!(n))));
    }
    match reply {
        Ok(reply) => {
            if name == "game_pause" {
                note_pause(cx.live, &reply);
            }
            fields.insert("reply".into(), json!(reply.text));
            if matches!(request.verb, Verb::SetTime { .. } | Verb::Weather { .. }) {
                let mut confirmed = confirm(&cx, &request.verb, &mut fields);
                call.lap("confirm");
                // Finding 41: in gameplay the name is all the read-back shows; what blends on is observed only.
                let gameplay = last.is_some_and(|f| f & PHOTO == 0);
                if confirmed.is_ok() && gameplay && matches!(request.verb, Verb::Weather { .. }) {
                    fields.insert("blend".into(), json!(BLEND));
                    if let Some(d) = settle {
                        if crate::measure::settle(call, d, "game_weather") {
                            fields.insert("settled_s".into(), json!(d.as_secs_f64()));
                            call.lap("settle");
                        } else {
                            let why =
                                format!("{} during settle_s, after the change", call.stop_cause());
                            confirmed = Err(why);
                        }
                    }
                }
                return match confirmed {
                    Ok(()) => Ok(fields),
                    Err(why) => Err(Done::Failed(why, fields)),
                };
            }
            // Finding 42: the item's count read back; an equip it doesn't show fails, the item added.
            if let Verb::ItemsAdd { equip, .. } = request.verb {
                let inventory = reply.data.unwrap_or_default();
                let equipped = inventory["equipped"] == true;
                fields.insert("inventory".into(), inventory);
                if equip && !equipped {
                    let why = "the item was added, but the game reads it back as not equipped";
                    return Err(Done::Failed(why.into(), fields));
                }
                return Ok(fields);
            }
            // Finding 51: found and actors, as the game read them.
            if name == "world_actors" {
                if let Some(Value::Object(data)) = reply.data {
                    fields.extend(data);
                }
                return Ok(fields);
            }
            // Only listsaves and world.get read back.
            let key = if name == "world_get" {
                "world"
            } else {
                "saves"
            };
            if name == "game_listsaves" {
                let no_file = no_file(cx.config, reply.data.as_ref());
                fields.extend(no_file.map(|n| ("no_file".to_string(), n)));
            }
            fields.extend(reply.data.map(|data| (key.to_string(), data)));
            Ok(fields)
        }
        Err(e) => Err(e.done(fields)),
    }
}

/// The names of `saves` (listsaves' list) with no file in gamesaves, matched as game_load matches: a cloud-only save
/// keeps its case and ".sav" (finding 34). None when gamesaves can't be read.
fn no_file(config: &crate::config::Config, saves: Option<&Value>) -> Option<Value> {
    let files: Vec<String> = std::fs::read_dir(config.saves_dir()?)
        .ok()?
        .flatten()
        .map(|e| e.file_name().to_string_lossy().to_lowercase())
        .collect();
    let on_disk = |n: &str| {
        let n = n.to_lowercase();
        files.contains(&n) || files.contains(&format!("{n}.sav"))
    };
    let names: Vec<&str> = saves?
        .as_array()?
        .iter()
        .filter_map(Value::as_str)
        .filter(|n| !on_disk(n))
        .collect();
    Some(json!(names))
}

/// Reads the world back (world.get) until it shows `verb`'s settime or weather, at most [`CONFIRM_READS`] times; the
/// last read-back goes into `fields` as `world`. Err, the change sent either way: not shown, or no read-back (finding
/// 26: in photo mode the weather verb was answered while the weather stayed).
fn confirm(cx: &Ctx, verb: &Verb, fields: &mut Fields) -> Result<(), String> {
    let unverified = "the change was sent, but is unverified";
    if let Some(old) =
        doctor::package_version(cx.config).filter(|v| doctor::BEFORE_WORLD.contains(v))
    {
        return Err(format!(
            "{unverified}: quen's package in the game is {old}, and reading it back (world.get) needs quen-w3 0.1.5 or later"
        ));
    }
    let (key, want, what) = match verb {
        Verb::SetTime { day, hour } => (
            "time",
            json!({"day": day, "hour": hour}),
            format!("the clock as day {day} hour {hour}"),
        ),
        Verb::Weather { name } => ("weather", json!(name), format!("the weather as {name}")),
        _ => unreachable!("only settime and weather are read back"),
    };
    let start = Instant::now();
    for read in 0..CONFIRM_READS {
        if read > 0 {
            std::thread::sleep(CONFIRM_EVERY);
        }
        let world = cx
            .channel()
            .map_err(|why| Error::Refused(why, None))
            .and_then(|c| c.call(Verb::WorldGet {}, REPLY_MAX));
        let world = match world {
            Ok(reply) => reply.data.unwrap_or_default(),
            Err(e) => {
                fields.extend(e.game_text().map(|t| ("game_text".to_string(), json!(t))));
                return Err(format!(
                    "{unverified}: reading it back (world.get): {}",
                    e.why()
                ));
            }
        };
        let shown = world[key] == want;
        fields.insert("world".into(), world);
        if shown {
            return Ok(());
        }
    }
    let mut why = format!(
        "the game didn't read back {what} in {:.1} s: world.{key} is what it read last",
        start.elapsed().as_secs_f32()
    );
    // A weather change not shown in photo mode or under quen's pause was applied once they ended (finding 31).
    let (photo, paused) = (
        cx.last_flags().is_some_and(|f| f & PHOTO != 0),
        cx.live.paused.get(),
    );
    let ends = match (photo, paused) {
        (true, true) => Some("photo mode closes and quen's pause lifts"),
        (true, false) => Some("photo mode closes"),
        (false, true) => Some("quen's pause lifts"),
        (false, false) => None,
    };
    if photo {
        why += "; quen's state shows photo mode, where game_photo (quen-w3 0.1.9) sets photo mode's own weather and \
            time";
    }
    if paused {
        why += "; quen's pause is on";
    }
    if let Some(ends) = ends {
        why += &format!(
            "; the change may still apply once {ends} (seen 2026-10-19): read world_get before you measure"
        );
    }
    Err(why)
}

/// The load verb for the save named `save`, on `channel`. modQuen's refusal names no save, so quen then lists the
/// game's saves and says which match as modQuen matches them: case-insensitive, ".sav" optional (finding 28).
pub(crate) fn load(cx: &Ctx, channel: Channel, save: &str) -> Result<Reply, Error> {
    match channel.call(Verb::Load { save: save.into() }, REPLY_MAX) {
        Err(Error::Refused(why, Some(text))) if text.starts_with(NOT_ONE) => Err(Error::Refused(
            format!("{why}; {}", matching(cx, save)),
            Some(text),
        )),
        out => out,
    }
}

/// The game's save list right after a refused load: how many it holds, and the names matching `save` (listsaves'
/// names: bare and lowercase, a cloud-only save with its case and ".sav"). A match differs from `save` only in case and
/// ".sav", so the names are quen's own words.
fn matching(cx: &Ctx, save: &str) -> String {
    let key = |s: &str| {
        let s = s.to_lowercase();
        s.strip_suffix(".sav").map(str::to_owned).unwrap_or(s)
    };
    let listed = cx.channel().and_then(|c| {
        c.call(Verb::ListSaves {}, REPLY_MAX)
            .map_err(|e| e.why().to_string())
    });
    let names = match listed {
        Ok(reply) => reply.data.unwrap_or_default(),
        Err(why) => return format!("listing the game's saves after it: {why}"),
    };
    let names: Vec<&str> = names
        .as_array()
        .map(|a| a.iter().filter_map(Value::as_str).collect())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let hits: Vec<&str> = names
        .iter()
        .copied()
        .filter(|n| key(n) == key(save))
        .collect();
    match hits.is_empty() {
        true => format!(
            "the game's save list right after held {} saves, none matching",
            names.len()
        ),
        false => format!(
            "the game's save list right after held {} saves, matching: {}",
            names.len(),
            hits.join(", ")
        ),
    }
}

/// Keeps quen's pause as a `pause` verb's reply says it (modQuen's "quen's pause is on" / "off").
pub(crate) fn note_pause(live: &crate::session::Live, reply: &Reply) {
    live.paused
        .set(reply.text.starts_with("quen's pause is on"));
}

/// A whole-number argument, 0 to `max`.
fn whole(args: &Value, key: &str, max: u32) -> Result<u32, String> {
    let v = args
        .get(key)
        .ok_or(format!("{key} is required: a whole number from 0 to {max}"))?;
    v.as_u64()
        .filter(|n| *n <= u64::from(max))
        .map(|n| n as u32)
        .ok_or(format!("{key} must be a whole number from 0 to {max}"))
}

/// An optional `[a, b, c]` argument of numbers.
fn vec3(args: &Value, key: &str) -> Result<Option<[f32; 3]>, String> {
    let Some(v) = args.get(key) else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    let n: Option<Vec<f32>> = v
        .as_array()
        .filter(|a| a.len() == 3)
        .and_then(|a| a.iter().map(|x| x.as_f64().map(|x| x as f32)).collect());
    let n = n.ok_or(format!("{key} must be three numbers"))?;
    Ok(Some([n[0], n[1], n[2]]))
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::game::tests::{Fake, PARTS};
    use std::cell::Cell;
    use std::fs;
    use std::io::Read;
    use std::sync::Arc;
    use std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool;
    use std::thread::{self, JoinHandle};

    thread_local! {
        /// The pid the channel's server must have in unit tests: the test's own, where its stand-in serves. Unset, it
        /// is the game's.
        pub(crate) static SERVER: Cell<Option<u32>> = const { Cell::new(None) };
    }

    pub(crate) type Answer = Box<dyn Fn(&Request) -> Vec<String> + Send>;

    /// A stand-in for W3Quen.asi's pipe on `token`, in a thread, for `conns` connections: it checks each client is this
    /// process (as the ASI checks quen's pid), then sends `answer`'s lines for each request line (none: silence) until
    /// the client leaves. Joined, it gives the requests it read. Its first instance is up when this returns.
    pub(crate) fn fake_game(token: &str, conns: usize, answer: Answer) -> JoinHandle<Vec<Request>> {
        serve(token, Some(conns), answer, Arc::default())
    }

    /// [`fake_game`] for any number of connections, until `stop` is set: for a sampler, whose reads depend on time.
    pub(crate) fn fake_game_until(
        token: &str,
        answer: Answer,
        stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    ) -> JoinHandle<Vec<Request>> {
        serve(token, None, answer, stop)
    }

    fn serve(
        token: &str,
        conns: Option<usize>,
        answer: Answer,
        stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    ) -> JoinHandle<Vec<Request>> {
        let name = format!(r"\\.\pipe\quen-w3-{token}");
        let first = Pipe::create(&name, true).unwrap();
        thread::spawn(move || {
            let (mut next, mut seen) = (first, Vec::new());
            for _ in 0..conns.unwrap_or(usize::MAX) {
                let pipe = next;
                let start = Instant::now();
                let gone = || stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
                let came = pipe
                    .accept(|| gone() || start.elapsed().as_secs() > 10)
                    .unwrap();
                if !came && gone() {
                    break;
                }
                assert!(came, "no client within 10 s");
                // The next instance is up before this client leaves, so the next open never finds none.
                next = Pipe::create(&name, false).unwrap();
                assert_eq!(pipe.peer_pid(true).unwrap(), std::process::id());
                let (mut got, mut buf) = (Vec::new(), [0; 4096]);
                loop {
                    let n = (&pipe).read(&mut buf).unwrap();
                    if n == 0 {
                        break;
                    }
                    got.extend_from_slice(&buf[..n]);
                    while let Some(nl) = got.iter().position(|&b| b == b'\n') {
                        let line: Vec<u8> = got.drain(..=nl).collect();
                        let line = std::str::from_utf8(&line).unwrap();
                        let request = protocol::decode_request(line).unwrap();
                        for reply in answer(&request) {
                            (&pipe).write_all(reply.as_bytes()).unwrap();
                        }
                        seen.push(request);
                    }
                }
            }
            seen
        })
    }

    /// A reply line as W3Quen.cpp writes one.
    pub(crate) fn reply(id: u64, ok: bool, text: &str, data: Option<Value>) -> String {
        let reply = Reply {
            id,
            ok,
            text: text.into(),
            data,
        };
        protocol::encode_reply(&reply).unwrap()
    }

    fn open(token: &str) -> Channel {
        Channel::open(token, std::process::id()).unwrap()
    }

    /// A reply may be 64 KiB of any script mod's text; a result carries at most 2 KiB of it, cut on a character
    /// boundary and marked.
    #[test]
    fn game_text_is_capped_on_a_character_boundary() {
        assert_eq!(game_text("short"), "short");
        let long = "é".repeat(5000);
        let cut = game_text(&long);
        assert!(cut.ends_with("... (cut at 2048 bytes)"), "{cut}");
        assert_eq!(cut.len(), 2048 + "... (cut at 2048 bytes)".len());
    }

    /// Every reply form the game sends: the script's ok, read-back and refusal, and the ASI's own: expired, queue full,
    /// no reply, and a refusal with id 0. Another request's line is skipped.
    #[test]
    fn every_reply_form_the_game_sends() {
        // The stand-in answers each load by its save name.
        let server = fake_game(
            "replies",
            7,
            Box::new(|r| {
                let Verb::Load { save } = &r.verb else {
                    unreachable!()
                };
                let (id, ok, text, data) = match save.as_str() {
                    "ok" => (r.id, true, "loading the save matching ok", None),
                    "data" => (r.id, true, "2 saves", Some(json!(["a", "b"]))),
                    "none" => (r.id, false, "not exactly one save matches none", None),
                    "expired" => (r.id, false, "expired: waited 6000 ms, ttl 5000 ms", None),
                    "full" => (r.id, false, "refused: 16 commands already wait", None),
                    "lost" => (r.id, false, "modQuen gave no reply (a script error?)", None),
                    _ => (0, false, "refused: malformed message: no id", None),
                };
                vec![
                    reply(r.id + 1000, true, "another request's", None),
                    reply(id, ok, text, data),
                ]
            }),
        );
        let send = |save: &str| {
            let verb = Verb::Load { save: save.into() };
            open("replies").call(verb, REPLY_MAX)
        };
        assert_eq!(send("ok").unwrap().text, "loading the save matching ok");
        assert_eq!(send("data").unwrap().data, Some(json!(["a", "b"])));
        for (save, ran) in [
            ("none", "no"),
            ("expired", "no"),
            ("full", "no"),
            ("zero", "no"),
            ("lost", "unknown"),
        ] {
            match (send(save), ran) {
                (Err(Error::Refused(..)), "no") | (Err(Error::Failed(..)), "unknown") => {}
                (out, _) => panic!("{save}: {out:?}"),
            }
        }
        assert_eq!(server.join().unwrap().len(), 7);
    }

    /// The client gives up after its timeout, quickly, and says so; a game that closes the channel is a failure too.
    #[test]
    fn a_silent_or_closing_game_fails_in_time() {
        let server = fake_game("silent", 1, Box::new(|_| Vec::new()));
        let start = Instant::now();
        let out = open("silent").call(Verb::Pause { on: true }, Duration::from_millis(300));
        assert!(
            start.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(2),
            "{:?}",
            start.elapsed()
        );
        assert!(
            matches!(&out, Err(Error::Failed(why, None)) if why.contains("no reply within 0.3 s")),
            "{out:?}"
        );
        let seen = server.join().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(seen.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(seen[0].ttl_ms, 300, "the ttl is the timeout");

        let pipe = Pipe::create(r"\\.\pipe\quen-w3-closing", true).unwrap();
        let server = thread::spawn(move || {
            pipe.accept(|| false).unwrap();
            let mut buf = [0; 64];
            let _ = (&pipe).read(&mut buf);
        });
        let out = open("closing").call(Verb::ListSaves {}, REPLY_MAX);
        assert!(
            matches!(&out, Err(Error::Failed(why, None)) if why.contains("closed the channel")),
            "{out:?}"
        );
        server.join().unwrap();
    }

    /// The channel is the game's only: another token finds no pipe, and a pipe another process serves is refused.
    #[test]
    fn opens_only_the_session_s_pipe_from_the_game() {
        let down = Channel::open("no-such-channel", std::process::id())
            .err()
            .unwrap();
        assert!(down.contains("isn't up"), "{down}");
        let server = fake_game("squatter", 1, Box::new(|_| Vec::new()));
        let other = Channel::open("squatter", std::process::id() + 4)
            .err()
            .unwrap();
        assert!(other.contains("not the game"), "{other}");
        assert!(server.join().unwrap().is_empty(), "nothing was sent");
    }

    /// A session whose channel this test serves, its state showing gameplay.
    pub(crate) fn served(test: &str) -> Fake {
        SERVER.set(Some(std::process::id()));
        let fx = Fake::new(test);
        let log = fx.dir.join("game/bin/x64_dx12/W3QuenState.log");
        fs::write(log, "push flags=1\n").unwrap();
        fx
    }

    pub(crate) fn token(fx: &Fake) -> String {
        fx.session().live.unwrap().channel
    }

    /// One session for several calls, so its patch list carries over.
    fn run(session: &mut Session, tool: &str, args: Value) -> Value {
        let mut call = session.call(crate::mcp::Conn::nobody(), Value::Null, None);
        let done = game::call(session, &mut call, tool, &args);
        session.envelope(tool, call, done)
    }

    fn journal(fx: &Fake) -> String {
        let config = fx.shared.config().as_ref().clone().unwrap();
        fs::read_to_string(crate::session::journal_path(&config)).unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_tools_send_their_verbs_and_journal_the_ones_that_taint() {
        let fx = served("channel-tools");
        let server = fake_game(
            &token(&fx),
            6,
            Box::new(|r| match &r.verb {
                Verb::ListSaves {} => vec![reply(r.id, true, "2 saves", Some(json!(["a", "b"])))],
                Verb::Weather { name } if name == "WT_Nope" => {
                    let why = "unknown weather WT_Nope; this area has: WT_Clear";
                    vec![reply(r.id, false, why, None)]
                }
                Verb::WorldGet {} => {
                    let world = json!({"time": {"day": 3, "hour": 22}, "weather": "WT_Clear"});
                    vec![reply(r.id, true, "the world", Some(world))]
                }
                _ => vec![reply(r.id, true, "done", None)],
            }),
        );
        // Finding 34: a listed name without a file in gamesaves (a cloud-only save) is in no_file.
        fs::write(fx.dir.join("docs/gamesaves/A.sav"), "synthetic").unwrap();
        let mut session = fx.session();
        let saves = run(&mut session, "game_listsaves", json!({"token": "tok"}));
        assert_eq!(saves["ok"], true, "{saves}");
        assert_eq!(saves["saves"], json!(["a", "b"]));
        assert_eq!(saves["no_file"], json!(["b"]), "{saves}");
        let pause = run(
            &mut session,
            "game_pause",
            json!({"token": "tok", "on": true}),
        );
        assert_eq!(pause["reply"], "done", "{pause}");
        let time = json!({"token": "tok", "day": 3, "hour": 22});
        assert_eq!(run(&mut session, "game_settime", time)["ok"], true);
        let tp = json!({"token": "tok", "pos": [1.5, -2, 30]});
        assert_eq!(run(&mut session, "game_teleport", tp)["ok"], true);
        let nope = json!({"token": "tok", "name": "WT_Nope"});
        let nope = run(&mut session, "game_weather", nope);
        assert_eq!(nope["refused"], true, "{nope}");
        // The game's words are in game_text, never in quen's reason.
        assert!(
            nope["game_text"].as_str().unwrap().contains("WT_Clear")
                && !nope["reason"].as_str().unwrap().contains("WT_Clear"),
            "{nope}"
        );
        let verbs: Vec<Verb> = server.join().unwrap().into_iter().map(|r| r.verb).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            verbs,
            [
                Verb::ListSaves {},
                Verb::Pause { on: true },
                Verb::SetTime { day: 3, hour: 22 },
                Verb::WorldGet {},
                Verb::Teleport {
                    pos: [1.5, -2.0, 30.0],
                    rot: [0.0; 3]
                },
                Verb::Weather {
                    name: "WT_Nope".into()
                },
            ]
        );
        // settime, the teleport and the weather were journaled first; the two that ran have their done line, the
        // refused weather's step went back off (feature tests 2c). Only what ran taints the saves.
        let journal = journal(&fx);
        assert_eq!(journal.matches("game_memory").count(), 2, "{journal}");
        assert_eq!(journal.matches(r#""rec":"done""#).count(), 2, "{journal}");
        assert!(
            journal.contains(r#"\"verb\":\"settime\""#) && !journal.contains("WT_Nope"),
            "{journal}"
        );
        let patches = session.live.as_ref().unwrap().patches.borrow();
        let what: Vec<&str> = patches
            .iter()
            .map(|(_, p)| p["what"].as_str().unwrap())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(what.len(), 2, "{what:?}");
        assert!(
            what[0].contains("settime") && what[1].contains("teleport"),
            "{what:?}"
        );
        assert!(patches.iter().all(|(_, p)| p["taints"] == true));
    }

    /// world_get sends world.get and answers the game's read-back as `world`, journaling nothing: it taints no save. While
    /// the user has the controls in a play session it runs too. Without a loaded game nothing is sent.
    #[test]
    fn world_get_reads_the_world_and_changes_nothing() {
        let fx = served("channel-world");
        let world = json!({"player": {"pos": [-101.5, 200.25, 3.0], "heading": 90.5},
                           "time": {"day": 3, "hour": 22}, "weather": "WT_Clear"});
        let data = world.clone();
        let server = fake_game(
            &token(&fx),
            1,
            Box::new(move |r| {
                assert_eq!(r.verb, Verb::WorldGet {});
                vec![reply(r.id, true, "the world", Some(data.clone()))]
            }),
        );
        fx.shared.set_hands(Some(crate::hands::Hands::User));
        let mut session = fx.session();
        let out = run(&mut session, "world_get", json!({"token": "tok"}));
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["world"], world, "{out}");
        assert!(out.get("saves").is_none(), "{out}");
        assert!(journal(&fx).is_empty(), "{}", journal(&fx));
        assert!(session.live.as_ref().unwrap().patches.borrow().is_empty());
        assert_eq!(server.join().unwrap().len(), 1);
        let extra = run(&mut session, "world_get", json!({"token": "tok", "x": 1}));
        assert_eq!(extra["refused"], true, "{extra}");
        fs::write(
            fx.dir.join("game/bin/x64_dx12/W3QuenState.log"),
            "push flags=0\n",
        )
        .unwrap();
        let menu = run(&mut session, "world_get", json!({"token": "tok"}));
        let why = menu["reason"].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(why.contains("needs a loaded game"), "{menu}");
    }

    /// Finding 51: world_actors sends world.actors with the defaults or the asked radius and max, answers the game's
    /// read-back as found and actors, journals nothing, and runs while the user has the controls. A radius or max
    /// outside the protocol's range is refused, nothing sent.
    #[test]
    fn world_actors_reads_the_actors_and_changes_nothing() {
        let fx = served("channel-actors");
        let actor = json!({"name": "Guard", "entity": "novigrad_guard", "pos": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0], "heading": 90.0,
            "velocity": [0.5, 0.0, 0.0], "distance": 2.5, "combat": false, "hostile": false, "guard": true,
            "at_work": false, "action_point": true, "scene": false});
        let data = json!({"found": 7, "actors": [actor]});
        let answer = data.clone();
        let server = fake_game(
            &token(&fx),
            3,
            Box::new(move |r| vec![reply(r.id, true, "the actors", Some(answer.clone()))]),
        );
        fx.shared.set_hands(Some(crate::hands::Hands::User));
        let mut session = fx.session();
        let out = run(&mut session, "world_actors", json!({"token": "tok"}));
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(
            (&out["found"], &out["actors"]),
            (&data["found"], &data["actors"]),
            "{out}"
        );
        let asked = json!({"token": "tok", "radius": 100, "max": MAX_ACTORS});
        assert_eq!(run(&mut session, "world_actors", asked)["ok"], true);
        let filtered =
            json!({"token": "tok", "radius": 8, "max": 5, "tag": "q1", "class": "CNewNPC"});
        assert_eq!(run(&mut session, "world_actors", filtered)["ok"], true);
        for bad in [
            json!({"radius": 0}),
            json!({"radius": 100.5}),
            json!({"max": 0}),
            json!({"max": 51}),
            json!({"tag": "a b"}),
            json!({"class": 3}),
        ] {
            let mut args = bad.clone();
            args["token"] = json!("tok");
            let out = run(&mut session, "world_actors", args);
            assert_eq!(out["refused"], true, "{bad}: {out}");
        }
        assert!(journal(&fx).is_empty(), "{}", journal(&fx));
        let verbs: Vec<Verb> = server.join().unwrap().into_iter().map(|r| r.verb).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            verbs,
            [
                Verb::WorldActors {
                    radius: 30.0,
                    max: 20,
                    tag: None,
                    class: None,
                },
                Verb::WorldActors {
                    radius: 100.0,
                    max: MAX_ACTORS,
                    tag: None,
                    class: None,
                },
                Verb::WorldActors {
                    radius: 8.0,
                    max: 5,
                    tag: Some("q1".into()),
                    class: Some("CNewNPC".into()),
                },
            ]
        );
    }

    /// world.get's answer: the clock at day 3 hour 22, and `weather`.
    fn world(r: &Request, weather: &str) -> Vec<String> {
        let world = json!({"time": {"day": 3, "hour": 22}, "weather": weather});
        vec![reply(r.id, true, "the world", Some(world))]
    }

    /// Finding 42: game_items sends the item's name as it is, spaces and all, journals it as tainting, and answers the
    /// game's read-back as inventory; nothing added is the game's refusal, an equip not shown fails.
    #[test]
    fn game_items_adds_by_name_and_reads_the_inventory_back() {
        let fx = served("channel-items");
        let server = fake_game(
            &token(&fx),
            3,
            Box::new(|r| match &r.verb {
                Verb::ItemsAdd { name, .. } if name == "Nope" => {
                    let data = json!({"before": 0, "after": 0, "equipped": false});
                    vec![reply(
                        r.id,
                        false,
                        "nothing added: no item is named Nope",
                        Some(data),
                    )]
                }
                Verb::ItemsAdd { count, equip, .. } => {
                    let data =
                        json!({"before": 1, "after": 1 + count, "equipped": *equip && *count == 1});
                    vec![reply(r.id, true, "added", Some(data))]
                }
                _ => unreachable!(),
            }),
        );
        let mut session = fx.session();
        let wolf = json!({"token": "tok", "name": "Red Wolf Armor 2", "equip": true});
        let out = run(&mut session, "game_items", wolf);
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["inventory"]["after"], 2, "{out}");
        let nope = run(
            &mut session,
            "game_items",
            json!({"token": "tok", "name": "Nope"}),
        );
        assert_eq!(nope["refused"], true, "{nope}");
        let two = json!({"token": "tok", "name": "Wolf Armor 4", "count": 2, "equip": true});
        let two = run(&mut session, "game_items", two);
        assert_eq!(
            (&two["ok"], &two["refused"]),
            (&json!(false), &json!(false)),
            "{two}"
        );
        assert_eq!(two["inventory"]["after"], 3, "{two}");
        let bad = json!({"token": "tok", "name": "Wolf Armor 4", "count": 0});
        assert_eq!(run(&mut session, "game_items", bad)["refused"], true);
        let verbs: Vec<Verb> = server.join().unwrap().into_iter().map(|r| r.verb).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            verbs[0],
            Verb::ItemsAdd {
                name: "Red Wolf Armor 2".into(),
                count: 1,
                equip: true
            }
        );
        assert!(journal(&fx).contains("items.add"), "journaled as tainting");
    }

    /// game_settime and game_weather read the world back until it shows the change: the clock at once, the weather on
    /// the third read here (a blend). Ok, with the last read-back as `world`.
    #[test]
    fn settime_and_weather_read_the_change_back() {
        let fx = served("channel-confirm");
        let reads = std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let server = fake_game(
            &token(&fx),
            6,
            Box::new(move |r| match &r.verb {
                Verb::WorldGet {} => match reads.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst) {
                    0..=2 => world(r, "WT_Clear"),
                    _ => world(r, "WT_Mid_Clouds"),
                },
                _ => vec![reply(r.id, true, "done", None)],
            }),
        );
        let mut session = fx.session();
        let time = json!({"token": "tok", "day": 3, "hour": 22});
        let time = run(&mut session, "game_settime", time);
        assert_eq!(time["ok"], true, "{time}");
        assert_eq!(
            time["world"]["time"],
            json!({"day": 3, "hour": 22}),
            "{time}"
        );
        // Finding 41: settle_s is checked before anything is sent; in gameplay the result says what blends on, and
        // the call waits settle_s once the change shows.
        let late = json!({"token": "tok", "name": "WT_Mid_Clouds", "settle_s": 121});
        assert_eq!(run(&mut session, "game_weather", late)["refused"], true);
        let weather = json!({"token": "tok", "name": "WT_Mid_Clouds", "settle_s": 0.3});
        let started = Instant::now();
        let weather = run(&mut session, "game_weather", weather);
        assert!(started.elapsed() >= Duration::from_millis(300));
        assert_eq!(weather["ok"], true, "{weather}");
        assert_eq!(weather["world"]["weather"], "WT_Mid_Clouds", "{weather}");
        assert_eq!(weather["settled_s"], 0.3, "{weather}");
        assert!(
            weather["blend"].as_str().unwrap().contains("45 s"),
            "{weather}"
        );
        let verbs: Vec<Verb> = server.join().unwrap().into_iter().map(|r| r.verb).collect();
        assert_eq!(verbs.iter().filter(|v| **v == Verb::WorldGet {}).count(), 4);
    }

    /// A change the read-back never shows fails, the change sent and journaled, with the last read-back as `world`; the
    /// reason names photo mode when quen's state shows it (finding 26).
    #[test]
    fn a_change_the_world_never_shows_fails() {
        let fx = served("channel-unconfirmed");
        fs::write(
            fx.dir.join("game/bin/x64_dx12/W3QuenState.log"),
            "push flags=129\n",
        )
        .unwrap();
        let server = fake_game(
            &token(&fx),
            1 + CONFIRM_READS,
            Box::new(|r| match &r.verb {
                Verb::WorldGet {} => world(r, "WT_Clear"),
                _ => vec![reply(r.id, true, "weather changing to WT_Mid_Clouds", None)],
            }),
        );
        let mut session = fx.session();
        // Photo mode (flags 129) and quen's pause: both named, and the change said to be possibly pending (finding 31).
        session.live.as_ref().unwrap().paused.set(true);
        let weather = json!({"token": "tok", "name": "WT_Mid_Clouds"});
        let out = run(&mut session, "game_weather", weather);
        assert_eq!(
            (&out["ok"], &out["refused"]),
            (&json!(false), &json!(false)),
            "{out}"
        );
        let why = out["reason"].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(
            why.contains("WT_Mid_Clouds") && why.contains("photo mode"),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert!(
            why.contains("quen's pause is on")
                && why.contains("may still apply once photo mode closes and quen's pause lifts"),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert_eq!(out["world"]["weather"], "WT_Clear", "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["reply"], "weather changing to WT_Mid_Clouds", "{out}");
        assert_eq!(server.join().unwrap().len(), 1 + CONFIRM_READS);
        assert_eq!(
            journal(&fx).matches(r#""rec":"done""#).count(),
            1,
            "the change was sent"
        );
    }

    /// A package without world.get (quen-w3 0.1.4 and older refuse the unknown verb): the change is sent, but the result
    /// fails as unverified, never ok.
    #[test]
    fn without_a_read_back_the_change_is_unverified() {
        let fx = served("channel-unverified");

    }

    /// A load the game refuses as "not exactly one save matches" names the game's saves that match, as listsaves names
    /// them, or says none did (finding 28).
    #[test]
    fn a_refused_load_names_the_matching_saves() {
        let fx = served("channel-load-matches");
        fs::write(fx.dir.join("docs/gamesaves/ManualSave_A.sav"), "").unwrap();
        let lists = std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let server = fake_game(
            &token(&fx),
            4,
            Box::new(move |r| match &r.verb {
                Verb::ListSaves {} => {
                    let saves = match lists.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst) {
                        0 => json!(["manualsave_a", "ManualSave_A.sav", "quicksave"]),
                        _ => json!([]),
                    };
                    vec![reply(r.id, true, "saves", Some(saves))]
                }
                _ => {
                    let why = "not exactly one save matches ManualSave_A (listsaves lists them)";
                    vec![reply(r.id, false, why, None)]
                }
            }),
        );
        let args = json!({"token": "tok", "save": "ManualSave_A"});
        let two = fx.run("game_load", args.clone());
        assert_eq!(two["refused"], true, "{two}");
        let why = two["reason"].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(
            why.ends_with("held 3 saves, matching: manualsave_a, ManualSave_A.sav"),
            "{two}"
        );
        assert!(
            two["game_text"].as_str().unwrap().starts_with(NOT_ONE),
            "{two}"
        );
        let none = fx.run("game_load", args);
        let why = none["reason"].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(why.ends_with("held 0 saves, none matching"), "{none}");
        assert_eq!(server.join().unwrap().len(), 4);
    }

    /// game_load sends the load verb and confirms the load on quen's state: nothing typed, no console to close. A load
    /// the game didn't take in time is refused, nothing typed either.
    #[test]
    fn game_load_goes_through_the_channel() {
        let fx = served("channel-load");
        fs::write(fx.dir.join("docs/gamesaves/QuickSave.sav"), "").unwrap();
        let state = fx.dir.join("game/bin/x64_dx12/W3QuenState.log");
        let answered = std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let server = fake_game(
            &token(&fx),
            2,
            Box::new(move |r| {
                if answered.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst) > 0 {
                    return vec![reply(
                        r.id,
                        false,
                        "expired: waited 5100 ms, ttl 5000 ms",
                        None,
                    )];
                }
                // The load: its 0, then gameplay.
                let mut log = fs::OpenOptions::new().append(true).open(&state).unwrap();
                log.write_all(b"push flags=0\npush flags=1\n").unwrap();
                vec![reply(
                    r.id,
                    true,
                    "loading the save matching quicksave",
                    None,
                )]
            }),
        );
        let out = fx.run(
            "game_load",
            json!({"token": "tok", "save": "quicksave.sav"}),
        );
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["via"], "channel", "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["reply"], "loading the save matching quicksave", "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["flags_after"], json!(["valid"]), "{out}");
        let late = fx.run("game_load", json!({"token": "tok", "save": "QuickSave"}));
        assert_eq!(late["refused"], true, "{late}");
        assert!(
            late["game_text"].as_str().unwrap().starts_with("expired"),
            "{late}"
        );
        let verbs: Vec<Verb> = server.join().unwrap().into_iter().map(|r| r.verb).collect();
        let load = Verb::Load {
            save: "quicksave".into(),
        };
        assert_eq!(verbs[0], load);
        assert!(fx.calls().is_empty(), "typed: {:?}", fx.calls());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_tools_refuse_before_sending() {
        let fx = served("channel-refuse");
        let server = fake_game(
            &token(&fx),
            1,
            Box::new(|r| vec![reply(r.id, true, "ok", None)]),
        );
        for (tool, args) in [
            ("game_pause", json!({"token": "nope", "on": true})),
            ("game_pause", json!({"token": "tok"})),
            (
                "game_pause",
                json!({"token": "tok", "on": true, "extra": 1}),
            ),
            (
                "game_settime",
                json!({"token": "tok", "day": 1, "hour": 24}),
            ),
            (
                "game_settime",
                json!({"token": "tok", "day": -1, "hour": 2}),
            ),
            ("game_weather", json!({"token": "tok", "name": ""})),
            ("game_teleport", json!({"token": "tok", "pos": [1, 2]})),
            (
                "game_teleport",
                json!({"token": "tok", "pos": [1e39, 0, 0]}),
            ),
            (
                "game_teleport",
                json!({"token": "tok", "pos": [0, 0, 0], "rot": "north"}),
            ),
        ] {
            let out = fx.run(tool, args.clone());
            assert_eq!(out["refused"], true, "{tool} {args}: {out}");
        }
        // The 0.1.15 live check: hour alone was refused as if day were out of range.
        let out = fx.run("game_settime", json!({"token": "tok", "hour": 9}));
        assert!(
            out["reason"]
                .as_str()
                .unwrap()
                .starts_with("day is required"),
            "{out}"
        );
        // No game loaded: the state-changing verbs wait for one; listsaves goes anyway.
        fs::write(
            fx.dir.join("game/bin/x64_dx12/W3QuenState.log"),
            "push flags=0\n",
        )
        .unwrap();
        let menu = fx.run("game_pause", json!({"token": "tok", "on": true}));
        let why = menu["reason"].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(why.contains("needs a loaded game"), "{menu}");
        let saves = fx.run("game_listsaves", json!({"token": "tok"}));
        assert_eq!(saves["ok"], true, "{saves}");
        assert_eq!(server.join().unwrap().len(), 1, "only listsaves was sent");
        assert!(journal(&fx).is_empty(), "{}", journal(&fx));
        // Without the package: refused with needs.
        for part in PARTS {
            fs::remove_file(fx.dir.join("game").join(part)).unwrap(); // this test's own synthetic files
        }
        let none = fx.run("game_listsaves", json!({"token": "tok"}));
        assert_eq!(
            none["needs"][0]["dependency"],
            doctor::PACKAGE.name,
            "{none}"
        );
    }
}

```

`crates/quen/src/config.rs`:

```rs
//! The untracked local config: `%USERPROFILE%\.quen\config.toml`, or the file `QUEN_CONFIG` names. Every
//! machine-specific path lives there, never in the code. Not AppData: Windows redirects an app package's AppData writes
//! (Claude Desktop is one, and so is every process it starts) into the package's private folder, which other clients
//! don't see (relocate.rs).
//!
//! ```toml
//! game_dir = '%GAME_DIR%'                                        # the folder holding bin\ and Mods\
//! documents = '%USERPROFILE%\Documents\The Witcher 3'            # dx12user.settings and gamesaves
//! game_exe = 'witcher3.exe'                                      # optional: the game's image name, in bin\x64_dx12
//! data_root = '%USERPROFILE%\.quen'                              # optional, the default
//! capture_root = '%USERPROFILE%\.quen\captures'                  # optional, the default: <data_root>\captures
//! capture_budget_gb = '20'                                       # optional, the default: GB of captures before quen
//!                                                                # warns (capture_usage, capture_clean)
//! kb = '%USERPROFILE%\Projects\witcher3-mods\re'                # optional: the RE KB the mem_* tools read
//! redkit = '%REDKIT%'                                            # optional: The Witcher 3 REDkit's folder (script_compile,
//!                                                                # the data tools' where: redkit)
//! presentmon = '%PRESENTMON%'                                    # optional: PresentMon's console exe; unset: on PATH
//! known_builds = 'steam <sha256> <label>; gog <sha256> <label>'   # optional: game builds verified here, beside the
//!                                                                # adapter's own (quen_core::build::KnownBuilds)
//! idle_focus = 'false'                                           # optional, default 'true': quen brings the agent's
//!                                                                # client forward when it waits (status.rs)
//! indicator = 'off'                                              # optional, default 'on': the game shows quen's
//!                                                                # lasting status line (status.rs)
//! window_sound = 'gui_global_panel_open'                         # optional, default none: a game sound event at each
//!                                                                # measuring window's start and end
//! # Optional features, each off unless set:
//! renodx_addon = 'renodx-thewitcher3remastered.addon64'          # RenoDX in bin: ReShade.ini and ReShadePreset.ini
//!                                                                # patched, preset values, ReShade.log readiness
//! renodx_build = '%RENODX_BUILD%\x.addon64'                      # with it: refused while the installed one differs
//! devkit = 'devkit\renodx-devkit.addon64'                        # the devkit, as ReShade.ini [ADDON] LoadFromDllMain
//! nsys = '%NSIGHT_SYSTEMS%\nsys.exe'                             # profiler launches (profiler: nsys:NAME, ngfx:NAME)
//! ngfx = '%NSIGHT_GRAPHICS%\ngfx.exe'
//! ngfx_args = '--architecture <GPU> --metric-set-id 0'           # added to every ngfx launch
//! ngfx_capture = '%NSIGHT_GRAPHICS%\ngfx-capture.exe'            # profiler: ngfx-capture:NAME; unset: the one beside
//!                                                                # ngfx, else ngfx itself; ngfx.exe here: that route
//! renderdoc = '%RENDERDOC%\renderdoccmd.exe'                     # profiler: renderdoc:NAME, with the dev interposer
//! streamline_dev_interposer = '%STREAMLINE%\_artifacts\sl.interposer\Develop_x64\sl.interposer.dll'
//!                                                                # (tools/streamline) swapped in for RenderDoc runs
//! tracy_capture = '%TRACY%\tracy-capture.exe'                    # profiler: tracy:NAME (Tracy's capture tool, the
//!                                                                # version of the client in quen's package: 0.14.1)
//! # This machine's Python harness while it exists: the game_* tools' scripts, and the interlock against its sessions.
//! harness = '%USERPROFILE%\renodx\tmp\witcher3\ini_session.py'
//! python = 'python'                                              # optional
//! ```
//!
//! (Real, absolute paths, not placeholders: nothing is expanded.)

use std::env;
use std::fs;
use std::io::{ErrorKind, Write};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use quen_core::build::KnownBuilds;
use quen_core::journal::sha256_hex;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Config {
    /// Where quen keeps what it produces: `state\` (lock, journal) and `logs\`. Never inside the source tree.
    pub data_root: PathBuf,
    pub python: String,
    /// The game's image name. quen launches none while one runs, and replays no journal while one runs outside its job
    /// (it holds the files a replay restores, and rewrites some at exit).
    pub game_exe: String,
    /// The Python harness: the game_* tools' scripts and, while it is set, the interlock against its sessions.
    pub harness: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub game_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub documents: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Where captures go, one folder per boot; unset: `<data_root>\captures`.
    pub capture_root: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// GB of captures before quen warns; unset: 20.
    pub capture_budget_gb: Option<f64>,
    /// The RenoDX add-on's file name in bin: turns the RenoDX boot on (ReShade.ini, ReShadePreset.ini, preset values).
    pub renodx_addon: Option<String>,
    /// With `renodx_addon`: the build a launch requires installed (unless `W3_ADDON_ANY`).
    pub renodx_build: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// The devkit add-on as ReShade.ini `[ADDON] LoadFromDllMain` takes it: launches may load the devkit.
    pub devkit: Option<String>,
    /// The profilers' exes, and the arguments every ngfx launch gets (its GPU architecture, a metric set).
    pub nsys: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub ngfx: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub ngfx_args: Option<String>,
    /// The `ngfx-capture:NAME` launch's exe: Nsight Graphics' ngfx-capture.exe, or ngfx.exe for its Graphics Capture
    /// activity (profile.rs); unset: the ngfx-capture.exe beside `ngfx`, else `ngfx`.
    pub ngfx_capture: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// renderdoccmd.exe, and the patched dev build of Streamline's interposer that a `renderdoc:NAME` launch swaps in
    /// for the game's signed one (tools/streamline, profile.rs).
    pub renderdoc: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub streamline_dev_interposer: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Tracy's command-line capture tool (`tracy-capture.exe`), which a `tracy:NAME` launch starts beside the game.
    pub tracy_capture: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// A test switch, not in quen_setup: `force_duplication = 'true'` makes game_screenshot's HDR path skip
    /// Windows.Graphics.Capture, so a live boot exercises its Desktop Duplication fallback.
    pub force_duplication: bool,
    /// The game's RE knowledge base: the per-build tables the `mem_*` tools and game_cvar read.
    pub kb: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// The Witcher 3 REDkit's folder (its `bin\x64_RedKit\wcc_lite.exe`, its depot `r4data`): script_compile and the data
    /// tools' `where: redkit`. The user installs it; quen never does.
    pub redkit: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// PresentMon's console exe (a prerequisite, never bundled); unset: `PresentMon.exe` on PATH.
    pub presentmon: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// The game builds a launch accepts: the adapter's own ([`crate::w3::KNOWN_BUILDS`]), then `known_builds`.
    pub known_builds: KnownBuilds,
    /// Whether quen brings the agent's client forward when the agent waits with the game in front (status.rs); unset:
    /// true.
    pub idle_focus: Option<bool>,
    /// Whether the game shows quen's lasting status line (status.rs); unset: on.
    pub indicator: Option<bool>,
    /// A game sound event played at each measuring window's start and end (status.rs); unset: none.
    pub window_sound: Option<String>,
}

impl Config {
    pub fn state_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.data_root.join("state")
    }

    /// The harness's folder, `harness`'s: `quen ledger migrate` imports its history from its `cap` folder by default.
    pub fn harness_dir(&self) -> Option<&Path> {
        self.harness.as_deref().and_then(Path::parent)
    }

    pub fn capture_root(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.capture_root
            .clone()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| self.data_root.join("captures"))
    }

    /// GB of captures before quen warns.
    pub fn capture_budget_gb(&self) -> f64 {
        self.capture_budget_gb.unwrap_or(20.0)
    }

    pub fn idle_focus(&self) -> bool {
        self.idle_focus.unwrap_or(true)
    }

    pub fn indicator(&self) -> bool {
        self.indicator.unwrap_or(true)
    }

    /// The game's binaries: the exe, the ASIs, ReShade and its add-ons.
    pub fn bin_dir(&self) -> Option<PathBuf> {
        Some(self.game_dir.as_ref()?.join("bin").join("x64_dx12"))
    }

    /// The user's saves.
    pub fn saves_dir(&self) -> Option<PathBuf> {
        Some(self.documents.as_ref()?.join("gamesaves"))
    }
}

/// quen's own folder, `%USERPROFILE%\.quen`: the default data root, and the config's folder.
/// Unit tests get a folder of their own, so none reads or writes the user's: a live session's journal there once
/// failed setup's `confirmed_values_are_written_keeping_other_keys_and_comments`, whose config names no data_root
/// (2026-10-19).
pub fn home() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    if cfg!(test) {
        let own = format!("quen-test-home-{}", std::process::id());
        return Some(env::temp_dir().join(own));
    }
    env::var_os("USERPROFILE").map(|p| PathBuf::from(p).join(".quen"))
}

/// The config file, as an absolute path: `QUEN_CONFIG`, else `%USERPROFILE%\.quen\config.toml`.
pub fn path() -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    let path = match env::var_os("QUEN_CONFIG") {
        Some(path) => PathBuf::from(path),
        None => home().ok_or("USERPROFILE is not set")?.join("config.toml"),
    };
    std::path::absolute(&path).map_err(|e| format!("config {}: {e}", path.display()))
}

/// One `quen serve` per config file. Its pipe is `\\.\pipe\` + this, and the startup mutex `Local\` + this. The
/// daemon takes up an edited config between calls while no session is live (session.rs `Session::reload`), so its
/// connections, old and new, run on the file's config, and a session never sees two.
pub fn daemon_name() -> Result<String, String> {
    let key = path()?.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase();
    Ok(format!("quen-{}", &sha256_hex(key.as_bytes())[..16]))
}

/// Reads the config and checks the data root. A missing file means the defaults.
pub fn load() -> Result<Config, String> {
    let path = path()?;
    loaded(&read(&path)?, &path)
}

/// The config `text` (the file `path`'s) holds, its roots checked.
pub fn loaded(text: &str, path: &Path) -> Result<Config, String> {
    let config = parse(text, path)?;
    check_roots(&config)?;
    Ok(config)
}

/// The config file's text; empty when there is none.
pub fn read(path: &Path) -> Result<String, String> {
    match fs::read_to_string(path) {
        Ok(text) => Ok(text),
        Err(e) if e.kind() == ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(String::new()),
        Err(e) => Err(format!("config {}: {e}", path.display())),
    }
}

/// The config `text` holds (`path` names it in errors), over the defaults. The roots aren't checked here.
pub fn parse(text: &str, path: &Path) -> Result<Config, String> {
    let mut config = Config {
        data_root: home().unwrap_or_default(),
        python: "python".into(),
        game_exe: "witcher3.exe".into(),
        ..Config::default()
    };
    let mut known_builds = "";
    for (n, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.is_empty() || line.starts_with('#') {
            continue;
        }
        let at = || format!("config {}:{}", path.display(), n + 1);
        let (key, value) = parse_line(line).ok_or_else(|| {
            format!(
                "{}: quen reads only `key = 'value'` lines (single quotes for paths)",
                at()
            )
        })?;
        match key {
            "data_root" => config.data_root = value.into(),
            "python" => config.python = value.into(),
            "game_exe" => config.game_exe = value.into(),
            "harness" => config.harness = Some(value.into()),
            "game_dir" => config.game_dir = Some(value.into()),
            "documents" => config.documents = Some(value.into()),
            "capture_root" => config.capture_root = Some(value.into()),
            "capture_budget_gb" => {
                let gb = value
                    .parse()
                    .ok()
                    .filter(|gb: &f64| *gb > 0.0 && gb.is_finite());
                let why = || format!("{}: capture_budget_gb is a number of GB above 0", at());
                config.capture_budget_gb = Some(gb.ok_or_else(why)?);
            }
            "renodx_addon" => config.renodx_addon = Some(value.into()),
            "renodx_build" => config.renodx_build = Some(value.into()),
            "devkit" => config.devkit = Some(value.into()),
            "nsys" => config.nsys = Some(value.into()),
            "ngfx" => config.ngfx = Some(value.into()),
            "ngfx_args" => config.ngfx_args = Some(value.into()),
            "ngfx_capture" => config.ngfx_capture = Some(value.into()),
            "renderdoc" => config.renderdoc = Some(value.into()),
            "streamline_dev_interposer" => config.streamline_dev_interposer = Some(value.into()),
            "tracy_capture" => config.tracy_capture = Some(value.into()),
            "force_duplication" | "idle_focus" => {
                let on = match value {
                    "true" => true,
                    "false" => false,
                    _ => return Err(format!("{}: {key} is 'true' or 'false'", at())),
                };
                match key {
                    "idle_focus" => config.idle_focus = Some(on),
                    _ => config.force_duplication = on,
                }
            }
            "indicator" => {
                config.indicator = Some(match value {
                    "on" => true,
                    "off" => false,
                    _ => return Err(format!("{}: indicator is 'on' or 'off'", at())),
                });
            }
            "window_sound" if quen_core::trace::plain_name(value) => {
                config.window_sound = Some(value.into());
            }
            "window_sound" => {
                let why = format!(
                    "{}: window_sound is a sound event: 1 to 64 letters, digits and _",
                    at()
                );
                return Err(why);
            }
            "kb" => config.kb = Some(value.into()),
            "redkit" => config.redkit = Some(value.into()),
            "presentmon" => config.presentmon = Some(value.into()),
            "known_builds" => {
                KnownBuilds::parse(value).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", at()))?;
                known_builds = value;
            }
            _ => return Err(format!("{}: unknown key {key:?}", at())),
        }
    }
    // The config's own entries are numbered as the user wrote them above; here only a clash with the adapter's fails.
    config.known_builds =
        KnownBuilds::parse(&format!("{};{known_builds}", crate::w3::KNOWN_BUILDS))
            .map_err(|e| format!("config {}: known_builds: {e}", path.display()))?;
    // A relative path would resolve against wherever quen was started, and quietly miss the real folders.
    let paths = [
        ("harness", &config.harness),
        ("game_dir", &config.game_dir),
        ("documents", &config.documents),
        ("renodx_build", &config.renodx_build),
        ("nsys", &config.nsys),
        ("ngfx", &config.ngfx),
        ("ngfx_capture", &config.ngfx_capture),
        ("renderdoc", &config.renderdoc),
        (
            "streamline_dev_interposer",
            &config.streamline_dev_interposer,
        ),
        ("tracy_capture", &config.tracy_capture),
        ("kb", &config.kb),
        ("redkit", &config.redkit),
        ("presentmon", &config.presentmon),
    ];
    for (key, value) in paths {
        if let Some(value) = value.as_ref().filter(|p| !p.is_absolute()) {
            return Err(format!(
                "config {}: {key} {:?} is not an absolute path",
                path.display(),
                value.display()
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(config)
}

/// The `key = 'value'` pairs `text` sets, in order.
pub fn pairs(text: &str) -> Vec<(&str, &str)> {
    text.lines()
        .filter_map(|line| parse_line(line.trim()))
        .collect()
}

/// `text` with each of `values` set: every line that sets the key gets the new value (its comment kept), and a key
/// it doesn't set yet is added at the end. Every other line, comments included, stays as it was.
pub fn with_values(text: &str, values: &[(&str, &str)]) -> String {
    let eol = if text.contains("\r\n") { "\r\n" } else { "\n" };
    let mut lines: Vec<String> = text.lines().map(String::from).collect();
    for (key, value) in values {
        let mut found = false;
        for line in &mut lines {
            let trimmed = line.trim();
            let Some((k, old)) = parse_line(trimmed).filter(|(k, _)| k == key) else {
                continue;
            };
            // What follows the closing quote: spaces and the comment, if any.
            let at = old.as_ptr() as usize - trimmed.as_ptr() as usize + old.len() + 1;
            *line = format!("{k} = '{value}'{}", &trimmed[at..]);
            found = true;
        }
        if !found {
            lines.push(format!("{key} = '{value}'"));
        }
    }
    let mut out = lines.join(eol);
    out.push_str(eol);
    out
}

/// Writes the config file atomically: a temp file beside it, flushed to disk, then renamed over it.
pub fn write(path: &Path, text: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let at = |e: std::io::Error| format!("config {}: {e}", path.display());
    let dir = path
        .parent()
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("config {}: no folder", path.display()))?;
    fs::create_dir_all(dir).map_err(at)?;
    let tmp = path.with_extension("toml.quen-tmp");
    let mut file = fs::File::create(&tmp).map_err(at)?;
    file.write_all(text.as_bytes())
        .and_then(|()| file.sync_all())
        .map_err(at)?;
    drop(file);
    fs::rename(&tmp, path).map_err(at)
}

/// `key = 'value'` (a TOML literal string) or `key = "value"` without escapes, then at most a `# comment`.
/// ponytail: a TOML subset; add the `toml` crate when the config needs more than flat strings.
fn parse_line(line: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str)> {
    let (key, rest) = line.split_once('=')?;
    let rest = rest.trim_start();
    let quote = rest.chars().next().filter(|c| matches!(c, '\'' | '"'))?;
    let (value, tail) = rest[1..].split_once(quote)?;
    let tail = tail.trim();
    let escaped = quote == '"' && value.contains('\\');
    (!escaped && (tail.is_empty() || tail.starts_with('#'))).then_some((key.trim(), value))
}

/// Neither the data root nor the capture root is inside quen's source tree, its install folder, any git
/// work tree, the game folder, the game's documents folder or Pictures (a personal folder, often cloud-synced).
pub fn check_roots(config: &Config) -> Result<(), String> {
    let install = env::current_exe()
        .ok()
        .and_then(|exe| Some(exe.parent()?.to_owned()));
    let forbidden = [
        install.map(|dir| (dir, "quen's install folder")),
        config.game_dir.clone().map(|dir| (dir, "the game folder")),
        config
            .documents
            .clone()
            .map(|dir| (dir, "the game's documents folder")),
        crate::win::pictures().map(|dir| (dir, "Pictures (a personal folder)")),
    ];
    for (root, name) in [
        (config.data_root.clone(), "data root"),
        (config.capture_root(), "capture root"),
    ] {
        if !root.is_absolute() {
            return Err(format!(
                "{name} {:?} is not an absolute path (set {}, or USERPROFILE)",
                root.display(),
                name.replace(' ', "_")
            ));
        }
        for (dir, what) in forbidden.iter().flatten() {
            if inside(&root, dir) {
                return Err(format!("{name} {} is inside {what}", root.display()));
            }
        }
        // quen's source tree by its own files, a copy without .git too: never by a build-time path, which would name
        // the build machine's folders in every binary.
        let source = |dir: &Path| {
            dir.join("AGENTS.md").is_file() && dir.join(r"crates\quen\Cargo.toml").is_file()
        };
        if let Some(tree) = root.ancestors().find(|dir| source(dir)) {
            return Err(format!(
                "{name} {} is inside quen's source tree {}",
                root.display(),
                tree.display()
            ));
        }
        if let Some(tree) = root.ancestors().find(|dir| dir.join(".git").exists()) {
            return Err(format!(
                "{name} {} is inside the git work tree {}",
                root.display(),
                tree.display()
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Whether `path` is `dir` or under it, compared lexically and case-insensitively (as Windows paths are).
/// ponytail: links and junctions aren't resolved.
fn inside(path: &Path, dir: &Path) -> bool {
    let norm = |p: &Path| {
        let p = std::path::absolute(p).unwrap_or_else(|_| p.to_owned());
        let mut parts = Vec::new();
        for part in p.components() {
            match part {
                std::path::Component::ParentDir => {
                    parts.pop();
                }
                std::path::Component::CurDir => {}
                part => parts.push(part.as_os_str().to_string_lossy().to_lowercase()),
            }
        }
        parts
    };
    norm(path).starts_with(&norm(dir))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn reads_single_and_plain_double_quoted_values() {
        assert_eq!(
            parse_line(r"harness = 'C:\h\ini_session.py'  # the harness"),
            Some(("harness", r"C:\h\ini_session.py"))
        );
        assert_eq!(parse_line(r#"python = "py""#), Some(("python", "py")));
        assert_eq!(parse_line(r#"harness = "C:\\h""#), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_line("harness = C:/h"), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_line("harness = 'C:/h' trailing"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_capture_test_switch_is_off_unless_set_true() {
        let path = Path::new("test.toml");
        assert!(!parse("", path).unwrap().force_duplication);
        assert!(
            parse("force_duplication = 'true'", path)
                .unwrap()
                .force_duplication
        );
        assert!(parse("force_duplication = 'yes'", path).is_err());
        let relative = parse("streamline_dev_interposer = 'sl.interposer.dll'", path);
        assert!(relative.unwrap_err().contains("not an absolute path"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_status_line_is_on_and_silent_unless_set() {
        let path = Path::new("test.toml");
        let config = parse("", path).unwrap();
        assert!(config.indicator() && config.window_sound.is_none());
        assert!(!parse("indicator = 'off'", path).unwrap().indicator());
        assert!(parse("indicator = 'false'", path).is_err());
        let sound = parse("window_sound = 'gui_global_panel_open'", path).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(sound.window_sound.as_deref(), Some("gui_global_panel_open"));
        assert!(parse("window_sound = 'a b'", path).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn known_builds_are_the_adapter_s_then_the_config_s() {
        let path = Path::new("test.toml");
        let adapter = KnownBuilds::parse(crate::w3::KNOWN_BUILDS).unwrap();
        assert!(!adapter.0.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(parse("", path).unwrap().known_builds, adapter);
        let sha = sha256_hex(b"synthetic build");
        let config = parse(&format!("known_builds = 'gog {sha} test (GOG)'"), path).unwrap();
        let known = config.known_builds.0;
        assert_eq!(known[..adapter.0.len()], adapter.0);
        assert_eq!(
            (known[adapter.0.len()].platform, known.len()),
            ("gog", adapter.0.len() + 1)
        );
        let err = parse(
            "
known_builds = 'epic x y'",
            path,
        )
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            err.contains("test.toml:2: known_builds entry 1") && err.contains("not steam or gog"),
            "{err}"
        );
        // The adapter's build under another label: which is it?
        let first = &adapter.0[0];
        let clash = format!(
            "known_builds = '{} {} relabelled'",
            first.platform, first.sha256
        );
        let err = parse(&clash, path).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("listed before as"), "{err}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn inside_is_case_insensitive_and_on_component_boundaries() {
        assert!(inside(
            Path::new(r"C:\Src\Quen\state"),
            Path::new(r"c:\src\quen")
        ));
        assert!(inside(
            Path::new(r"C:\src\quen"),
            Path::new(r"C:\src\quen\")
        ));
        assert!(inside(
            Path::new(r"C:\src\x\..\quen\a"),
            Path::new(r"C:\src\quen")
        ));
        assert!(!inside(
            Path::new(r"C:\src\quen-data"),
            Path::new(r"C:\src\quen")
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn refuses_a_data_or_capture_root_in_the_source_tree_or_pictures() {
        let mut config = Config {
            data_root: Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("data"),
            python: "python".into(),
            game_exe: "witcher3.exe".into(),
            ..Config::default()
        };
        let err = check_roots(&config).unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            err.starts_with("data root") && err.contains("source tree"),
            "{err}"
        );
        config.data_root = std::env::temp_dir().join("quen-roots-test");
        config.capture_root = Some(config.data_root.join("x"));
        assert_eq!(check_roots(&config), Ok(()));
        config.capture_root = Some(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("captures"));
        let err = check_roots(&config).unwrap_err();
        assert!(
            err.starts_with("capture root") && err.contains("source tree"),
            "{err}"
        );
        // A copy of the source without .git, known by its own files.
        let copy = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("quen-roots-copy-{}", std::process::id()));
        fs::create_dir_all(copy.join(r"crates\quen")).unwrap();
        fs::write(copy.join("AGENTS.md"), "synthetic").unwrap();
        fs::write(copy.join(r"crates\quen\Cargo.toml"), "synthetic").unwrap();
        config.capture_root = Some(copy.join(r"x\captures"));
        let err = check_roots(&config).unwrap_err();
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&copy); // this test's own temp folder
        assert!(
            err.starts_with("capture root") && err.contains("quen's source tree"),
            "{err}"
        );
        // A folder under Pictures, if this account has one at all.
        if let Some(pictures) = crate::win::pictures() {
            config.capture_root = Some(pictures.join("quen"));
            let err = check_roots(&config).unwrap_err();
            assert!(err.contains("Pictures"), "{err}");
        }
    }
}

`crates/quen/src/data.rs`:

//! The game-data tools: `data_find` (paths in the bundles' tables of contents, or in REDkit's depot), `data_read` (one
//! file decoded: a CR2W file's tables and property tree), `data_scan` (one names-level question over many files,
//! paged, with a deadline) and `script_compile` (REDkit's wcc_lite on a scratch copy of the scripts). The readers are
//! quen-core's `gamedata`; nothing is written into the game folder or REDkit's. The bundles' tables of contents stay in
//! memory while quen runs, each read again once its bundle's size or write time changes.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::fs::{self, File};
use std::io::{self, Read};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, PoisonError};

use serde_json::{Map, Value, json};

use crate::config::Config;
use crate::doctor;

use crate::session::{self, Call, Done, JournalFs, Session, Shared};
use crate::win::Job;

/// A page's rows when the call gives no `limit`, and the most it takes.

const MAX_LIMIT: u64 = 1000;

/// script_compile's errors inline, at most (all go to messages.json beside wcc.log).
const ERRORS_INLINE: usize = 100;

const COMPILE_S: u64 = 600;
const MAX_COMPILE_S: u64 = 1800;
/// quen_setup licence: how long REDkit's licence dialog waits for the user's answer, and wcc_lite's run after it closes.
const ANSWER: Duration = Duration::from_secs(600);
const AFTER_ANSWER: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);
pub(crate) const REDKIT_APPID: &str = "2684660";
pub(crate) const WCC_LITE: &str = r"bin\x64_RedKit\wcc_lite.exe";

pub fn tools() -> Vec<Value> {
    let token = json!({"type": "string", "description": "the live session's token, needed while one is live"});
    let wheres = json!({"type": "string", "enum": ["all", "game", "mods", "redkit"], "description": "all (default): \
