```rs
        t.put(
            r"redkit\r4data\t\new.w2ent",
            cr2w(&["", "CEntityTemplate"], &[steer]),
        );
        let s = |t: &str| [&[0x80 | t.len() as u8][..], t.as_bytes()].concat();
        let (table, deps) = (s("CEntityTemplate"), s(steer));
        let mut old = b"CR2W".to_vec();
        let d0 = 44 + table.len() as u32;
        for w in [141, 0, 44, 1, d0 + deps.len() as u32, 0, d0, 0, d0, 2] {
            old.extend(w.to_le_bytes());
        }
        old.extend([table, deps].concat());
        t.put(r"redkit\r4data\t\old.w2ent", old);
        t.put(r"redkit\r4data\t\other.xbm", "x");
        let config = Config {
            redkit: Some(t.0.join("redkit")),
            ..t.config()
        };
        let found = find(
            &Shared::new(Ok(config.clone())),
            &json!({"where": "redkit", "kinds": ["w2ent"]}),
        );
        assert_eq!(found["total"], 2, "{found}");
        let args = json!({"where": "redkit", "imports": ["pc_steering.w2steer"], "limit": 0});
        let scan = run(&config, "data_scan", args);
        assert_eq!(
            (&scan["matched"], &scan["skipped_count"]),
            (&json!(2), &json!(0)),
            "{scan}"
        );
        let read = run(
            &config,
            "data_read",
            json!({"where": "redkit", "path": r"t\old.w2ent"}),
        );
        assert_eq!(read["cr2w"]["imports"][0]["path"], steer, "{read}");
    }

    /// The app manifest's buildid and installed depots, only when it names the folder; the key is the manifests'.
    #[test]
    fn the_content_build_comes_from_the_app_manifest() {
        let t = Temp::new("manifest");
        let game = t.0.join(r"steamapps\common\Game Folder");
        fs::create_dir_all(&game).unwrap();
        t.put(
            r"steamapps\appmanifest_123.acf",
            "\"AppState\" { \"installdir\" \"Game Folder\" \"buildid\" \"42\" \"InstalledDepots\" { \"124\" { \
             \"manifest\" \"999\" \"size\" \"1\" } \"125\" { \"manifest\" \"888\" } } }",
        );
        let c = content(&game, "123", std::iter::empty::<&str>());
        assert_eq!(c["steam_buildid"], "42");
        assert_eq!(c["depot_manifests"], json!({"124": "999", "125": "888"}));
        assert_eq!(c["key"].as_str().unwrap().len(), 16);
        let other = t.0.join(r"steamapps\common\Other");
        fs::create_dir_all(&other).unwrap();
        let c = content(&other, "123", ["a", "b"].into_iter());
        assert_eq!(c["steam_buildid"], Value::Null);
        assert_eq!(c["key"], json!(sha256_hex(b"a\nb")[..16]));
        assert_eq!(
            content(&other, "123", std::iter::empty::<&str>())["key"],
            Value::Null
        );
    }

    /// A mod's scripts are copied with the imports named stubbed, UTF-8 and UTF-16 alike, each with the names it
    /// imports; without stubs, as they are.
    #[test]
    fn scripts_are_copied_with_stubs() {
        let t = Temp::new("scripts");
        t.put(
            r"mod\local\a.ws",
            "import function A() : int;\nimport function Bound();\n",
        );
        let utf16: Vec<u8> = [0xFF, 0xFE]
            .into_iter()
            .chain(
                "import function B();"
                    .encode_utf16()
                    .flat_map(u16::to_le_bytes),
            )
            .collect();
        t.put(r"mod\b.ws", &utf16);
        let stub = ["A", "B"].map(String::from).into();
        let mut files = copy_scripts(&t.0.join("mod"), &t.0.join("tree"), Some(&stub)).unwrap();
        files.sort();
        let names = |n: &[&str]| n.iter().map(|n| n.to_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        assert_eq!(
            files,
            [
                ("b.ws".into(), names(&["B"])),
                (r"local\a.ws".into(), names(&["A", "Bound"]))
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            fs::read_to_string(t.0.join(r"tree\local\a.ws")).unwrap(),
            "function A() : int { return 0; }\nimport function Bound();\n"
        );
        let b = fs::read(t.0.join(r"tree\b.ws")).unwrap();
        let back: Vec<u16> = b[2..]
            .chunks_exact(2)
            .map(|c| u16::from_le_bytes([c[0], c[1]]))
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(String::from_utf16(&back).unwrap(), "function B() { }");
        let plain = copy_scripts(&t.0.join("mod"), &t.0.join("plain"), None).unwrap();
        assert!(plain.iter().all(|(_, names)| names.is_empty()));
        assert_eq!(fs::read(t.0.join(r"plain\b.ws")).unwrap(), utf16);
    }

    /// A depot path stays inside the depot.
    #[test]
    fn depot_paths_stay_inside() {
        let root = Path::new(r"R:\depot");
        assert_eq!(inside(root, r"a\b.w2ent").unwrap(), root.join(r"a\b.w2ent"));
        assert!(
            inside(root, r"..\x").is_err()
                && inside(root, r"C:\x").is_err()
                && inside(root, r"\x").is_err()
        );
    }
}

```

`crates/quen/src/disk.rs`:

```rs
//! Capture management: quen keeps its captures, and its other leftovers under the data root, from piling up unseen.
//! quen_doctor, session_plan, session_launch and session_end report the capture root's size against
//! `capture_budget_gb`; `capture_usage` (read-only) says what is there and what a cleanup would take; `capture_clean`,
//! with the user's OK, takes it: to the Recycle Bin, or, a file the bin can't take whole, through Windows' own dialog,
//! which asks the user whether to delete it permanently (the owner's rule, 2026-10-19: never a silent permanent
//! delete; no file moves to `_to_delete` any more). The ledger rows stay, marked removed. The selection and the plan
//! are quen-core's (`disk`).

use std::fs;
use std::io;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::thread;
use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime};

use quen_core::disk::{self, File, Select, To};
use quen_core::ledger::Ledger;
use serde_json::{Map, Value, json};
use windows::Win32::Foundation::HWND;

use crate::config::Config;
use crate::session::{self, Call, Done, Session, Shared};
use crate::{capture, doctor, game, input, measure, win};

/// The selection keys both tools take.
const SELECT: [&str; 5] = [
    "boots",
    "older_than_days",
    "kinds",
    "capture_ids",
    "missing",
];

pub fn tools() -> Vec<Value> {
    let ints =
        |what: &str| json!({"type": "array", "items": {"type": "integer"}, "description": what});
    let select = json!({
        "boots": ints("boot ids: their files, and their sessions' logs"),
        "older_than_days": {"type": "number", "minimum": 0, "description": "files older than this many days"},
        "kinds": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "file extensions, e.g. rdc, png, csv, or leftover kinds: session_logs, settings_backups, query_spills, ledger_backups, packages, to_delete"},
        "capture_ids": ints("capture rows, taken even when cited"),
        "missing": {"type": "boolean", "description": "true: the rows in missing too (file gone): capture_clean marks them removed, removed_to missing, and moves no file for them"},
    });
    let mut clean = select.clone();
    clean["user_ok"] = json!({"type": "boolean", "description": "true only after the user saw what goes (capture_usage with the same selection) and agreed. Required."});
    let schema = |props: Value| json!({"type": "object", "properties": props, "additionalProperties": false});
    vec![
        json!({
            "name": "capture_usage",
            "description": "Read-only: what quen's capture root holds (screenshots, PresentMon CSVs, profiler \
                outputs, files you copied there): files and GB by boot, kind and age, every file over 1 GB, the \
                budget (capture_budget_gb in quen's config, default 20), and the capture rows whose file is gone \
                (missing: under neither the capture root nor the harness's cap folder). leftovers: quen's other \
                files under the data root, the same way, by kind: session_logs, settings_backups, query_spills, ledger_backups, packages (zips but the installed package's) and \
                to_delete (what earlier cleanups moved there); their paths are relative to the data root. With a \
                selection (boots, older_than_days, kinds, capture_ids, missing; every filter given must match, \
                capture_ids are taken anyway): what capture_clean would take (recycle_bin, ask_delete), the cited \
                files it keeps, the folders it empties and the rows it marks missing. After session_end, check it \
                and offer the user a cleanup; never clean on your own.",
            "inputSchema": schema(select),
        }),
        json!({
            "name": "capture_clean",
            "description": "Take quen's files off the disk, with the user's OK: show them capture_usage with the \
                same selection first. The client asks the user on every call (user_ok is only your word). Takes the \
                files every given filter matches (boots, older_than_days, kinds) and those named in capture_ids. \
                Keeps a cited file (a claim's evidence, a pose's image, pinned, or named in a document) unless \
                capture_ids names it. Files go to the Recycle Bin. For one it can't take whole (over the bin's \
                size, or no bin on the drive), Windows' own dialog asks the user whether to delete it for \
                good, and the call waits: yes deletes it (deleted), no keeps it in place (kept). Ledger rows stay, \
                with removed_at and removed_to. Emptied folders go (folders, leftover_folders). missing: true also \
                marks the rows in capture_usage's missing (removed_to missing). Refused, nothing moved: no \
                selection, no user_ok, a session live, a journal a dead quen left, quen's PresentMon running, \
                another quen holding the game lock. What it couldn't take: left.",
            // Claude Code prompts for this tool on every call, in every permission mode, as for session_launch.
            "_meta": {"anthropic/requiresUserInteraction": true},
            "inputSchema": schema(clean),
        }),
    ]
}

/// What the capture root and the data root hold, joined to the ledger.
struct Found {
    /// The capture root's files.
    files: Vec<File>,
    /// quen's other leftovers under the data root ([`disk::leftovers`]).
    leftovers: Vec<File>,
    /// Capture rows marked on disk whose file isn't under the capture root, nor under the harness's `cap` folder
    /// ([`disk::missing`]).
    missing: disk::Missing,
    /// The folder names that belong to a boot (`Ledger::boot_folders`).
    folders: Vec<(String, i64)>,
    /// The ledger's error, when it can't be read.
    note: Option<String>,
}

/// The files under the capture root and quen's leftovers, joined to the ledger when it can be read (its error
/// otherwise).
fn files(config: &Config) -> Found {
    let db = config.state_dir().join("quen.db");
    let ledger = match db.exists() {
        true => Ledger::open_readonly(&db).and_then(|l| Ok((l.capture_rows()?, l.boot_folders()?))),
        false => Ok((Vec::new(), Vec::new())),
    };
    let (rows, folders, note) = match ledger {
        Ok((rows, folders)) => (rows, folders, None),
        Err(e) => (
            Vec::new(),
            Vec::new(),
            Some(format!("ledger: {e}: no file counts as cited")),
        ),
    };
    let now = SystemTime::now();
    let files = disk::scan(&config.capture_root(), now, &rows, &folders);
    // The zips of this quen and of the package in the game stay: they are no leftovers.
    let package = doctor::package_version(config).map(|v| format!("{}.zip", v.replace(' ', "-")));
    let quen = format!("quen-{}-windows-x64.zip", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
    let keep: Vec<String> = [Some(quen), package].into_iter().flatten().collect();
    // The harness's history: where `quen ledger migrate` imports it from by default.
    let harness = config.harness_dir().map(|d| d.join("cap"));
    Found {
        missing: disk::missing(&rows, &files, harness.as_deref()),
        leftovers: disk::leftovers(&config.data_root, now, &folders, &keep),
        files,
        folders,
        note,
    }
}

impl Found {
    /// The cleanup `select` asks for: of the capture root's files, by `max.0` (its volume's [`recycle_max`]), and of
    /// the leftovers, by `max.1` (the data root's).
    fn plan(&self, select: &Select, max: (Option<u64>, Option<u64>)) -> disk::Plan {
        let mut plan = disk::plan(&self.files, select, max.0);
        plan.take
            .extend(disk::plan(&self.leftovers, select, max.1).take);
        plan
    }

    /// The folders a cleanup by `select` taking `plan` empties ([`disk::emptied`]): the capture root's, relative to it,
    /// and the leftovers' (in `logs` and `_to_delete`), relative to the data root.
    fn emptied(
        &self,
        config: &Config,
        select: &Select,
        plan: &disk::Plan,
    ) -> (Vec<String>, Vec<String>) {
        let taken = |leftover: bool| -> Vec<&str> {
            let taken = plan.take.iter().filter(|(f, _)| f.leftover == leftover);
            taken.map(|(f, _)| f.rel.as_str()).collect()
        };
        let picked = |boot: &i64| select.boots.as_ref().is_some_and(|b| b.contains(boot));
        let boots: Vec<&str> = self
            .folders
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, boot)| picked(boot))
            .map(|(folder, _)| folder.as_str())
            .collect();
        let root = config.capture_root();
        let captures = disk::emptied(&disk::folders(&root), &self.files, &taken(false), &boots);
        let dirs: Vec<String> = ["logs", "_to_delete"]
            .into_iter()
            .flat_map(|area| {
                let dirs = disk::folders(&config.data_root.join(area));
                dirs.into_iter().map(move |d| format!("{area}/{d}"))
            })
            .collect();
        let leftovers = disk::emptied(&dirs, &self.leftovers, &taken(true), &[]);
        (captures, leftovers)
    }
}

/// The largest file the Recycle Bin takes whole on `path`'s volume: its size as the registry gives it (this PC's,
/// 2026-10-20: 188 GB; an earlier 4 GB cap had no source), or `u64::MAX` where the registry doesn't say, since
/// [`win::shell_delete`] lets Windows ask before it deletes a file the bin can't take. Or why it takes none.
fn recycle_max(path: &Path) -> Result<u64, String> {
    Ok(win::recycle_bin(path)?.unwrap_or(u64::MAX))
}

fn to_delete(config: &Config) -> PathBuf {
    config.data_root.join("_to_delete")
}

/// The capture root against the budget, and what waits in `_to_delete`: quen_doctor's and session_end's report.
fn budget(config: &Config, bytes: u64) -> Map<String, Value> {
    let budget = config.capture_budget_gb();
    let waiting = to_delete(config);
    let mut out = Map::new();
    out.insert("root".into(), json!(config.capture_root()));
    out.insert("gb".into(), json!(disk::gb(bytes)));
    out.insert("budget_gb".into(), json!(budget));
    out.insert("over_budget".into(), json!(bytes as f64 > budget * 1e9));
    if let Some(why) = warning(config, bytes) {
        out.insert("warning".into(), json!(why));
    }
    let left = disk::total(&waiting);
    if left > 0 {
        let note = "files quen 0.1.5 and older moved there in a cleanup: capture_clean with kinds [\"to_delete\"] \
                    takes them, with the user's OK";
        out.insert(
            "to_delete".into(),
            json!({"path": waiting, "gb": disk::gb(left), "note": note}),
        );
    }
    out
}

/// The warning when the capture root holds more than the budget.
fn warning(config: &Config, bytes: u64) -> Option<String> {
    let budget = config.capture_budget_gb();
    (bytes as f64 > budget * 1e9).then(|| {
        format!(
            "the capture root holds {} GB, over capture_budget_gb {budget}: capture_usage shows what is there; \
             capture_clean takes what the user agrees to",
            disk::gb(bytes)
        )
    })
}

/// quen_doctor's `captures`.
pub(crate) fn summary(config: &Config) -> Value {
    json!(budget(config, disk::total(&config.capture_root())))
}

/// session_plan's and session_launch's: the warning, when the capture root is over the budget.
pub(crate) fn over_budget(config: &Config) -> Option<String> {
    warning(config, disk::total(&config.capture_root()))
}

/// session_end's `captures`: the budget report, the boot's folders (its id's, for a profiler's output, and its
/// session's) and their files over 1 GB.
pub(crate) fn after_end(config: &Config, boot: i64, session: &str) -> Value {
    let root = config.capture_root();
    let mut out = budget(config, disk::total(&root));
    let folders: Vec<PathBuf> = [boot.to_string(), session.to_owned()]
        .into_iter()
        .map(|f| root.join(f))
        .filter(|f| f.is_dir())
        .collect();
    let bytes: u64 = folders.iter().map(|f| disk::total(f)).sum();
    let mut files = Vec::new();
    for folder in &folders {
        let name = folder.file_name().unwrap_or_default().to_string_lossy();
        let found = disk::scan(folder, SystemTime::now(), &[], &[]);
        // Both folders are the boot's (feature tests 2b: large[].boot was null).
        files.extend(found.into_iter().map(|mut f| {
            f.rel = format!("{name}/{}", f.rel);
            f.boot = Some(boot);
            f
        }));
    }
    let boot =
        json!({"folders": folders, "gb": disk::gb(bytes), "large": disk::large(files.iter())});
    out.insert("boot".into(), boot);
    json!(out)
}

/// `capture_usage`, on the connection's thread: read-only.
pub fn usage(shared: &Shared, args: &Value) -> Value {
    let done = (|| -> Result<Map<String, Value>, String> {
        let config = shared.config();
        let config = config
            .as_ref()
            .as_ref()
            .map_err(|e| format!("quen's config: {e}"))?;
        let select = selection(args, &[])?;
        let found = files(config);
        let (files, missing) = (&found.files, &found.missing);
        let mut out = budget(config, files.iter().map(|f| f.bytes).sum());
        let usage = disk::usage(files);
        out.extend(usage.as_object().cloned().unwrap_or_default());
        let max = recycle_max(&config.capture_root());
        match &max {
            Ok(u64::MAX) => out.insert(
                "recycle_bin".into(),
                json!("its size isn't in the registry: Windows asks before it deletes a file it can't take"),
            ),
            Ok(max) => out.insert("recycle_bin_max_gb".into(), json!(disk::gb(*max))),
            Err(why) => out.insert("recycle_bin".into(), json!(format!("none: {why}"))),
        };
        let mut leftovers = disk::usage(&found.leftovers);
        leftovers["root"] = json!(config.data_root);
        out.insert("leftovers".into(), leftovers);
        if !select.is_empty() {
            let data = recycle_max(&config.data_root).ok();
            let plan = found.plan(&select, (max.ok(), data));
            let mut cleanup = plan.summary();
            let (folders, leftover_folders) = found.emptied(config, &select, &plan);
            cleanup["folders"] = json!(folders);
            cleanup["leftover_folders"] = json!(leftover_folders);
            if select.missing {
                cleanup["missing"] = json!(missing.ids.len());
            }
            out.insert("cleanup".into(), cleanup);
        }
        if missing.ids.len() + missing.in_harness + missing.unresolved > 0 {
            let note = "rows: capture rows the ledger says are on disk, with no file under the capture root (removed \
                        by hand, or under another capture root) nor under the harness's cap folder (the folder of \
                        harness in quen's config, as quen ledger migrate imports from), by origin: quen_boots, \
                        imported_boots (harness_info) and no_boot (recorded without a boot: the harness import \
                        records each file of its cap folder so, its boot logs aside, by its path in that folder); \
                        ids lists the first 50, quen's boots' first. in_harness: rows whose file is in that cap \
                        folder, not missing. unresolved: rows of imported boots and of no boot not counted in rows, \
                        as that folder holds none of them (or harness is unset)";
            let by = missing.by;
            let ids = &missing.ids[..missing.ids.len().min(50)];
            out.insert(
                "missing".into(),
                json!({"rows": missing.ids.len(), "quen_boots": by[0], "imported_boots": by[1],
                       "no_boot": by[2], "in_harness": missing.in_harness,
                       "unresolved": missing.unresolved, "ids": ids, "note": note}),
            );
        }
        if let Some(note) = &found.note {
            out.insert("note".into(), json!(note));
        }
        Ok(out)
    })();
    let done = done.map_or_else(Done::Refused, Done::Ok);
    session::envelope(
        shared,
        "capture_usage",
        Map::new(),
        Vec::new(),
        Map::new(),
        done,
    )
}

/// The selection in `args`, which may hold only its keys and `also`.
fn selection(args: &Value, also: &[&str]) -> Result<Select, String> {
    let map = args.as_object().ok_or("arguments must be an object")?;
    if let Some(key) = map
        .keys()
        .find(|k| !SELECT.contains(&k.as_str()) && !also.contains(&k.as_str()))
    {
        return Err(format!("unknown argument {key:?}"));
    }
    Select::parse(args)
}

/// `capture_clean`, on the session thread, under the game lock: the ledger's writers hold it.
pub(crate) fn clean(session: &mut Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Done {
    let config = match session.config() {
        Ok(config) => config.clone(),
        Err(why) => return why.into(),
    };
    let select = match selection(args, &["user_ok"]) {
        Ok(select) if select.is_empty() => {
            return "name what goes: boots, older_than_days, kinds, capture_ids or missing (capture_usage with the same shows it)"
                .to_string()
                .into();
        }
        Ok(select) => select,
        Err(why) => return why.into(),
    };
    if args.get("user_ok") != Some(&json!(true)) {
        return "user_ok: show the user what capture_usage with this selection takes, and get their OK first"
            .to_string()
            .into();
    }
    if session.live.is_some() {
        return "a session is live: session_end first (a boot still writes its captures)"
            .to_string()
            .into();
    }
    if let Err(why) = session.take_lock(&config, "capture_clean") {
        return why.into();
    }
    // With the lock, a journal is a dead quen's: its backups are among the leftovers, and its replay needs them.
    if session::journal_path(&config).exists() {
        session.release_lock();
        return "a journal a dead quen left exists: session_recover first"
            .to_string()
            .into();
    }
    // Windows' question before a permanent delete takes the focus, and the game pauses without it.
    if let Some((pid, exe)) = measure::presentmon_running(&config, game::images) {
        session.release_lock();
        return format!(
            "PresentMon {} runs (pid {pid}, a measurement): a cleanup may open a Windows dialog, which takes the \
             focus; clean once it ends",
            exe.display()
        )
        .into();
    }
    let max = (
        recycle_max(&config.capture_root()),
        recycle_max(&config.data_root),
    );
    let done = take(&config, call, &select, max, &remove);
    session.release_lock();
    done
}

/// What became of a file a cleanup took.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Went {
    Recycled,
    /// Deleted for good, after the user said yes to Windows' question.
    Deleted,
    /// The user said no: it stays where it was.
    Kept,
}

/// What became of a file, and whether Windows' question came to the front (None: none showed).
type Removed = io::Result<(Went, Option<bool>)>;

/// Takes `path` off the disk through the Windows shell ([`win::shell_delete`]): `to` the Recycle Bin, or for good with
/// Windows asking the user first. `quen serve` shows no window of its own, so one of its process that shows meanwhile
/// is the shell's question: a watcher brings it to the front ([`input::focus`]), as a window a windowless background
/// process opens may come up behind the client's (memory-design §4.2; checked live).
fn remove(path: &Path, to: To) -> Removed {
    let done = AtomicBool::new(false);
    let (gone, front) = thread::scope(|s| {
        let watcher = s.spawn(|| {
            while !done.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
                if let Some(window) = own_window() {
                    return Some(input::focus(window).is_ok());
                }
                thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
            }
            None
        });
        let gone = win::shell_delete(path, to == To::RecycleBin);
        done.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
        (gone, watcher.join().unwrap_or(None))
    });
    let went = match (gone?, front) {
        (false, _) => Went::Kept,
        (true, None) if to == To::RecycleBin => Went::Recycled,
        (true, _) => Went::Deleted,
    };
    Ok((went, front))
}

/// A window this process shows ([`capture::shown`]).
fn own_window() -> Option<HWND> {
    let me = std::process::id();
    let all = capture::top_windows().ok()?;
    all.into_iter()
        .find(|&w| capture::shown(w).is_some_and(|(pid, ..)| pid == me))
}

/// Takes what `select` takes, then marks its ledger rows; the lock is held. `max`: [`recycle_max`] of the capture
/// root's volume and of the data root's; `remove` takes a file off the disk ([`remove`]).
fn take(
    config: &Config,
    call: &mut Call,
    select: &Select,
    max: (Result<u64, String>, Result<u64, String>),
    remove: &dyn Fn(&Path, To) -> Removed,
) -> Done {
    let found = files(config);
    let plan = found.plan(select, (max.0.clone().ok(), max.1.clone().ok()));
    let root = config.capture_root();
    let (emptied, leftovers_emptied) = found.emptied(config, select, &plan);
    call.lap("plan");
    let (mut gone, mut deleted, mut kept, mut left) =
        (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    for (n, (file, to)) in plan.take.iter().enumerate() {
        if call.stopped() {
            left.push(json!({"path": file.rel, "why": "cancelled before it"}));
            continue;
        }
        let under = if file.leftover {
            &config.data_root
        } else {
            &root
        };
        let path = under.join(file.rel.replace('/', "\\"));
        match remove(&path, *to) {
            Ok((went, in_front)) => {
                let entry = json!({"path": file.rel, "kind": file.kind, "gb": disk::gb(file.bytes), "in_front": in_front});
                match went {
                    Went::Recycled => gone.push((file, "recycle_bin")),
                    Went::Deleted => {
                        gone.push((file, "deleted"));
                        deleted.push(entry);
                    }
                    Went::Kept => kept.push(entry),
                }
            }
            Err(e) => left.push(json!({"path": file.rel, "why": e.to_string()})),
        }
        call.progress(&format!("{} of {} files", n + 1, plan.take.len()));
    }
    call.lap("remove");
    // The folders the cleanup emptied go, deepest first: only empty ones (remove_dir refuses any other, so a file that
    // stayed keeps its folders), never a link's target (feature tests 2b: a recovered ngfx boot's folder stayed).
    let removed = |under: &Path, dirs: Vec<String>| -> Vec<String> {
        dirs.into_iter()
            .filter(|dir| fs::remove_dir(under.join(dir.replace('/', "\\"))).is_ok())
            .collect()
    };
    let folders = removed(&root, emptied);
    let leftover_folders = removed(&config.data_root, leftovers_emptied);
    // Rows whose file was gone already, marked in one transaction (feature tests 2c: batches 1-2's 3,887).
    let missing = match select.missing {
        true => found.missing.ids.as_slice(),
        false => &[],
    };
    let mut fields = Map::new();
    let marked = Ledger::open(config.state_dir().join("quen.db")).and_then(|mut ledger| {
        let t = ledger.utc(session::now() as i64)?;
        for (file, to) in &gone {
            if let Some(id) = file.capture {
                ledger.mark_removed(id, &t, to)?;
                call.row("captures", id);
            }
        }
        ledger.atomic(|l| {
            missing
                .iter()
                .try_for_each(|id| l.mark_removed(*id, &t, "missing"))
        })
    });
    call.lap("ledger");
    if let Err(e) = marked {
        fields.insert("ledger_error".into(), json!(e.to_string()));
    }
    let recycled: Vec<&&File> = gone
        .iter()
        .filter(|(_, to)| *to == "recycle_bin")
        .map(|(f, _)| f)
        .collect();
    let bytes = recycled.iter().map(|f| f.bytes).sum();
    fields.insert(
        "recycle_bin".into(),
        json!({"files": recycled.len(), "gb": disk::gb(bytes)}),
    );
    fields.insert("deleted".into(), json!(deleted));
    fields.insert("kept".into(), json!(kept));
    if let Err(why) = max.0.as_ref().and(max.1.as_ref()) {
        fields.insert("recycle_bin_off".into(), json!(why));
    }
    let kept_cited: Vec<Value> = plan
        .kept
        .iter()
        .map(|f| json!({"path": f.rel, "capture_id": f.capture}))
        .collect();
    fields.insert("kept_cited".into(), json!(kept_cited));
    fields.insert("folders".into(), json!(folders));
    fields.insert("leftover_folders".into(), json!(leftover_folders));
    if select.missing {
        let marked = if fields.contains_key("ledger_error") {
            0
        } else {
            missing.len()
        };
        let ids = &missing[..marked.min(50)];
        fields.insert("missing".into(), json!({"rows": marked, "ids": ids}));
    }
    fields.insert("left".into(), json!(left));
    fields.insert("captures".into(), json!(budget(config, disk::total(&root))));
    if let Some(note) = found.note {
        fields.insert("note".into(), json!(note));
    }
    if left.is_empty() {
        Done::Ok(fields)
    } else {
        Done::Failed(
            format!("{} files not taken (left says why)", left.len()),
            fields,
        )
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use quen_core::ledger::Capture;

    /// The budget's warning names the tools, and only over the budget.
    #[test]
    fn the_budget_warns_over_its_size_and_names_the_tools() {
        let mut config = Config::default();
        assert_eq!(config.capture_budget_gb(), 20.0);
        assert_eq!(warning(&config, 20_000_000_000), None);
        let why = warning(&config, 20_100_000_000).unwrap();
        assert!(
            why.contains("20.1 GB") && why.contains("capture_clean"),
            "{why}"
        );
        config.capture_budget_gb = Some(0.5);
        assert!(warning(&config, 600_000_000).is_some());
    }

    /// capture_clean on a fake session's data root: refused while the session is live, without a selection or user_ok,
    /// and with a dead quen's journal. Then (with a stand-in Recycle Bin that takes 9 bytes, and a stand-in user who
    /// answers Windows' question) the small files go to the bin, the session's logs among them, the bigger one is
    /// deleted on a yes, the cited one stays unless named, and kept on a no; the rows are marked.
    #[test]
    fn clean_takes_what_it_selects_and_marks_the_rows() {
        let fx = crate::game::tests::Fake::new("clean");
        let config = fx.shared.config().as_ref().clone().unwrap();
        let root = config.capture_root();
        let put = |rel: &str| {
            let path = root.join(rel);
            fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
            fs::write(&path, rel).unwrap();
        };
        put(r"1\run.nsys-rep");
        put(r"s1\kf0.png");
        put(r"s1\f1.png");
        // Session s1's logs, and the daemon's own log, which no cleanup takes.
        for rel in [
            r"logs\1792-s1\game.log",
            r"logs\1792-s1\game-logs\a.log",
            r"logs\serve.log",
        ] {
            let path = config.data_root.join(rel);
            fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
            fs::write(&path, "log").unwrap();
        }
        let mut ledger = Ledger::open(config.state_dir().join("quen.db")).unwrap();
        let row = |path: &str| Capture {
            boot_id: Some(1),
            path: path.into(),
            sha256: quen_core::journal::sha256_hex(path.as_bytes()),
            bytes: 1,
            kind: "png".into(),
            t: "2026-10-18T00:00:00Z".into(),
            pinned: true,
            ..Capture::default()
        };
        let cited = ledger.add_capture(&row("s1/kf0.png")).unwrap();
        let plain = ledger
            .add_capture(&Capture {
                pinned: false,
                ..row("s1/f1.png")
            })
            .unwrap();
        let rep = ledger
            .add_capture(&Capture {
                pinned: false,
                ..row("1/run.nsys-rep")
            })
            .unwrap();
        // Feature tests 2b: a row whose file is gone is counted by capture_usage.
        let gone = ledger.add_capture(&row("old/gone.png")).unwrap();
        // A row the harness import wrote (no boot), its file in the harness's cap folder: not missing.
        let harness = config.harness_dir().unwrap().join("cap").join("old");
        fs::create_dir_all(&harness).unwrap();
        fs::write(harness.join("kept.png"), "x").unwrap();
        let imported = Capture {
            boot_id: None,
            pinned: false,
            ..row("old/kept.png")
        };
        let imported = ledger.add_capture(&imported).unwrap();
        drop(ledger);
        let used = usage(&fx.shared, &json!({}));
        assert_eq!(used["missing"]["rows"], 1, "{used}");
        assert_eq!(used["missing"]["ids"], json!([gone]), "{used}");
        assert_eq!(used["missing"]["in_harness"], 1, "{used}");
        // Finding 36: counted by origin; this row is a quen boot's.
        let by = ["quen_boots", "imported_boots", "no_boot"].map(|k| used["missing"][k].clone());
        assert_eq!(by, [json!(1), json!(0), json!(0)], "{used}");
        let kinds = used["leftovers"]["by_kind"].as_array().unwrap();
        assert!(
            kinds.contains(&json!({"kind": "session_logs", "files": 2, "gb": 0.0})),
            "{used}"
        );
        // And a selected boot's empty folder goes with the cleanup, as usage says first (feature tests 2c), its
        // session's log folder too.
        fs::create_dir_all(root.join(r"s1\l3c\deeper")).unwrap();
        let folders = json!(["s1/l3c/deeper", "s1/l3c", "1"]);
        let logs = json!(["logs/1792-s1/game-logs", "logs/1792-s1"]);
        let planned = usage(&fx.shared, &json!({"boots": [1]}));
        assert_eq!(planned["cleanup"]["folders"], folders, "{planned}");
        assert_eq!(planned["cleanup"]["leftover_folders"], logs, "{planned}");
        assert_eq!(planned["cleanup"]["ask_delete"]["files"], 0, "{planned}");

        let mut session = fx.session();
        let run = |session: &mut Session, args: Value| {
            let mut call = session.call(crate::mcp::Conn::nobody(), Value::Null, None);
            let done = clean(session, &mut call, &args);
            session.envelope("capture_clean", call, done)
        };
        let all = json!({"boots": [1], "user_ok": true});
        let live = run(&mut session, all.clone());
        assert!(
            live["reason"].as_str().unwrap().contains("session is live"),
            "{live}"
        );
        session.live = None;
        for (args, why) in [
            (json!({"user_ok": true}), "name what goes"),
            (json!({"boots": [1]}), "user_ok"),
            (
                json!({"boots": [1], "user_ok": true, "x": 1}),
                "unknown argument",
            ),
        ] {
            let out = run(&mut session, args);
            assert!(
                out["reason"].as_str().unwrap().contains(why),
                "{why}: {out}"
            );
        }
        // A dead quen's journal: its backups are among the leftovers, and its replay needs them.
        let journal = session::journal_path(&config);
        fs::write(&journal, "").unwrap();
        let out = run(&mut session, all.clone());
        let why = out["reason"].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(why.contains("session_recover"), "{out}");
        fs::remove_file(&journal).unwrap(); // this test's own file
        assert!(
            root.join(r"s1\f1.png").exists(),
            "the refusals moved nothing"
        );

        let bin = fx.dir.join("recycled");
        fs::create_dir_all(&bin).unwrap();
        // The stand-in user answers Windows' question: no for the key frame, yes for the rest.
        let remove = |path: &Path, to: To| match to {
            To::RecycleBin => fs::rename(path, bin.join(path.file_name().unwrap()))
                .map(|()| (Went::Recycled, None)),
            To::AskDelete if path.ends_with("kf0.png") => Ok((Went::Kept, Some(true))),
            To::AskDelete => fs::remove_file(path).map(|()| (Went::Deleted, Some(true))),
        };
        let moved = |select: Value| {
            let mut call = session.call(crate::mcp::Conn::nobody(), Value::Null, None);
            let select = Select::parse(&select).unwrap();
            let done = take(&config, &mut call, &select, (Ok(9), Ok(9)), &remove);
            session.envelope("capture_clean", call, done)
        };
        let out = moved(json!({"boots": [1]}));
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["recycle_bin"]["files"], 3, "f1.png and the logs: {out}");
        let deleted =
            json!([{"path": "1/run.nsys-rep", "kind": "nsys-rep", "gb": 0.0, "in_front": true}]);
        assert_eq!(out["deleted"], deleted, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["kept_cited"][0]["capture_id"], cited, "{out}");
        assert!(bin.join("f1.png").exists() && bin.join("game.log").exists());
        assert!(root.join(r"s1\kf0.png").exists());
        assert!(config.data_root.join(r"logs\serve.log").exists());
        assert!(!root.join("1").exists(), "the emptied folder went");
        assert_eq!(out["folders"], folders, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["leftover_folders"], logs, "{out}");
        assert!(
            !root.join(r"s1\l3c").exists() && root.join("s1").is_dir(),
            "the empty folder went, the one holding a kept file stayed"
        );
        assert_eq!(out["ledger"]["captures"], json!([rep, plain]), "{out}");
        let ledger = Ledger::open_readonly(config.state_dir().join("quen.db")).unwrap();
        let sql = "SELECT id, removed_to FROM captures WHERE removed_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY id";
        let marked = ledger
            .query(sql, &[], std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))
            .unwrap();
        let want = [
            [json!(plain), json!("recycle_bin")],
            [json!(rep), json!("deleted")],
        ];
        assert_eq!(marked.rows, want);
        // Named by id, the cited file is taken too (10 bytes: over the stand-in bin's 9); on the user's no, it stays.
        let named = moved(json!({"capture_ids": [cited]}));
        assert_eq!(named["ok"], true, "{named}");
        assert_eq!(named["kept"][0]["path"], "s1/kf0.png", "{named}");
        assert!(root.join(r"s1\kf0.png").exists());
        assert_eq!(named["ledger"]["captures"], json!(null), "{named}");
        // Feature tests 2c: missing: true marks the row whose file is gone and moves nothing; usage counts it no more.
        let planned = usage(&fx.shared, &json!({"missing": true}));
        assert_eq!(planned["cleanup"]["missing"], 1, "{planned}");
        let marked = moved(json!({"missing": true}));
        assert_eq!(
            marked["missing"],
            json!({"rows": 1, "ids": [gone]}),
            "{marked}"
        );
        assert_eq!(marked["recycle_bin"]["files"], 0, "{marked}");
        let sql =
            format!("SELECT removed_to FROM captures WHERE id = {gone} AND removed_at IS NOT NULL");
        let row = ledger
            .query(&sql, &[], std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(row.rows, [[json!("missing")]]);
        let after = usage(&fx.shared, &json!({}));
        assert_eq!(after["missing"]["rows"], 0, "{after}");
        let sql = format!("SELECT removed_at FROM captures WHERE id = {imported}");
        let row = ledger
            .query(&sql, &[], std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            row.rows,
            [[Value::Null]],
            "the harness's file stays unmarked"
        );
    }

    /// The owner's rule, on the real shell: a permanent delete only on the user's yes in Windows' own dialog, which
    /// comes to the front from a process with no window of its own. It takes the foreground, so it runs only when
    /// asked, with the PC free: `cargo test -p quen windows_asks -- --ignored`. A stand-in user answers: no, then yes.
    #[test]
    #[ignore]
    fn windows_asks_before_a_permanent_delete_and_its_question_comes_to_the_front() {
        use windows::Win32::Foundation::{LPARAM, WPARAM};
        use windows::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{IDYES, PostMessageW, WM_CLOSE, WM_COMMAND};
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("quen-ask-delete-{}", std::process::id()));
        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let file = dir.join("synthetic.bin");
        for yes in [false, true] {
            fs::write(&file, b"synthetic").unwrap();
            // The question, once in front: no closes it, yes is its Yes button.
            let user = thread::spawn(move || {
                for _ in 0..200 {
                    if let Some(w) = own_window().filter(|&w| input::in_front(w)) {
                        let (msg, button) = match yes {
                            true => (WM_COMMAND, IDYES.0 as usize),
                            false => (WM_CLOSE, 0),
                        };
                        // SAFETY: a message to a live window of this process.
                        return unsafe { PostMessageW(Some(w), msg, WPARAM(button), LPARAM(0)) }
                            .is_ok();
                    }
                    thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
                }
                false
            });
            let (went, front) = remove(&file, To::AskDelete).unwrap();
            assert!(
                user.join().unwrap(),
                "yes {yes}: no question came to the front"
            );
            assert_eq!(front, Some(true), "yes {yes}");
            let want = if yes { Went::Deleted } else { Went::Kept };
            assert_eq!((went, file.exists()), (want, !yes), "yes {yes}");
        }
        fs::remove_dir(&dir).unwrap(); // this test's own folder, empty now
    }
}
```

```rs
//! terminal.

/// Whether measure_ab's console actions go as exec verbs: only for a pinned package with the verb (an unpinned dev
/// build may lack it, so its lines are typed, as before).
pub(crate) fn has_exec(version: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    version.is_some_and(|v| !BEFORE_SCENE.contains(&v))
}

/// Refused with needs, nothing sent, while quen's package in the game is one of `before`: releases without what
/// `tool` needs, which came in quen-w3 `since`. An unpinned package (a dev build) goes on: its ASI refuses a verb it
/// doesn't know.
pub(crate) fn package_at_least(
    config: &Config,
    before: &[&str],
    tool: &str,
    since: &str,
) -> Result<(), Done> {
    let Some(old) = package_version(config).filter(|v| before.contains(v)) else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    let mut why =
        format!("quen's package in the game is {old}: {tool} needs quen-w3 {since} or later");
    let inv = crate::vortex::read(config);
    let game = config.game_dir.as_deref();
    if let Some(m) = game.and_then(|g| vortex_owner(inv.as_ref(), g, &PACKAGE_OWNED)) {
        why.push_str(&format!(", and it is Vortex's ({m}): update it in Vortex"));
    }
    let need = json!({
        "dependency": PACKAGE.name,
        "status": "wrong_version",
        "needed_for": tool,
        "how_to_get": PACKAGE.how_to_get,
    });
    Err(Done::Needs(why, vec![need]))
}

/// [`PINS`], plus the exact pins `QUEN_TEST_PINS` lists (`file=sha256`, `;` between them; version "test"): the
/// end-to-end tests' synthetic parts. Read once.
fn pins() -> &'static [Pin] {
    static IN_USE: OnceLock<Vec<Pin>> = OnceLock::new();
    IN_USE.get_or_init(|| {
        let test = env::var("QUEN_TEST_PINS").unwrap_or_default();
        let test = test.split(';').filter_map(|e| e.split_once('='));
        let test = test.map(|(file, sha256)| Pin {
            file: String::leak(file.into()),
            version: "test",
            sha256: String::leak(sha256.into()),
            exact: true,
        });
        PINS.iter().copied().chain(test).collect()
    })
}

/// The Vortex mods whose deployment manifests (`inv`) list a file of `rels` (in the game folder `game`), None when none
/// does: then quen's installer or the user installed it. What Vortex owns is updated in Vortex; install.ps1 leaves it.
fn vortex_owner(inv: Option<&Inventory>, game: &Path, rels: &[&str]) -> Option<String> {
    let owners = rels
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|rel| inv.map(|inv| inv.owners(&game.join(rel))));
    let mut mods: Vec<String> = owners.flatten().map(|m| m.id.display()).collect();
    mods.sort();
    mods.dedup();
    (!mods.is_empty()).then(|| mods.join(" + "))
}

/// The version of quen's package in the game: its W3Quen.asi's pin, None when it has none.
pub(crate) fn package_version(config: &Config) -> Option<&'static str> {
    let asi = fs::read(config.game_dir.as_ref()?.join(PACKAGE_ASI)).ok()?;
    let sha = sha256_hex(&asi);
    let pin = pins()
        .iter()
        .find(|p| p.file == PACKAGE_ASI && p.sha256 == sha);
    pin.map(|p| p.version)
}

/// The sha256s of NVIDIA's signed interposer that quen accepts (its pins, test pins included).
pub(crate) fn signed_interposer() -> Vec<&'static str> {
    pins()
        .iter()
        .filter(|p| p.file == INTERPOSER)
        .map(|p| p.sha256)
        .collect()
}

/// One dependency, as quen_doctor lists it and a refused tool names it in `needs`.
pub(crate) struct Dep {
    pub(crate) name: &'static str,
    /// Needed for any session; the others each enable some tools.
    required: bool,
    enables: &'static str,
    pub(crate) how_to_get: &'static str,
    check: fn(&Cx) -> State,
}

    how_to_get: "quen-w3-<version>.zip from the GitHub Releases of quen-mcp, unzipped into the game folder: \
        bin\\x64_dx12\\W3Quen.asi and Mods\\modQuen. Move an old Mods\\modQuen and any Mods\\modQuenRpc to the \
        Recycle Bin first. It needs the Witcher Native Bridge.",
    check: package,

/// quen's package: W3Quen.asi and quen.ws from one release, with nothing left of the old layout. Anything else
/// breaks the game's script compile at boot or calls functions the other half lacks, so it is the wrong version, with
/// how to fix it.
fn package(cx: &Cx) -> State {
    let Some(game) = cx.game_dir else {
        return State::missing("no game folder: run quen_setup".into());
    };
    let there = |rel: &str| game.join(rel).exists();
    let sha = fs::read(game.join(PACKAGE_SCRIPT))
        .map(|b| sha256_hex(&b))
        .ok();
    // Every release that ships these script bytes: a release may keep the last one's quen.ws (0.1.3 kept 0.1.2's).
    let scripts: Vec<&str> = cx
        .pins
        .iter()
        .filter(|p| p.file == PACKAGE_SCRIPT && Some(p.sha256) == sha.as_deref())
        .map(|p| p.version)
        .collect();
    let broken = if there(r"Mods\modQuenRpc") {
        Some(
            "Mods\\modQuenRpc is left from quen's old layout: modQuen has its functions now, and the two together \
             break the game's script compile. Move Mods\\modQuenRpc to the Recycle Bin",
        )
    } else if scripts.contains(&OLD_MODQUEN) {
        Some(
            "Mods\\modQuen is the old pure-script modQuen: replace it with the release package (move Mods\\modQuen \
             to the Recycle Bin, then unzip the package into the game folder)",
        )
    } else if there(PACKAGE_SCRIPT) && !there(PACKAGE_ASI) {
        Some(
            "Mods\\modQuen without bin\\x64_dx12\\W3Quen.asi, half the package: the game's script compile fails at \
             boot. Unzip the whole release package into the game folder, or move Mods\\modQuen to the Recycle Bin",
        )
    } else if there(PACKAGE_ASI) && !there(PACKAGE_SCRIPT) {
        Some(
            "bin\\x64_dx12\\W3Quen.asi without Mods\\modQuen, half the package. Unzip the whole release package \
             into the game folder, or move W3Quen.asi to the Recycle Bin",
        )
    } else {
        None
    };
    if let Some(why) = broken {
        return State {
            status: "wrong_version",
            ..State::missing(why.into())
        };
    }
    let mut state = cx.files(&[PACKAGE_ASI, PACKAGE_SCRIPT]);
    if state.status == "found"
        && !state
            .version
            .as_deref()
            .is_some_and(|v| scripts.contains(&v))
    {
        state.status = "wrong_version";
        let script = match scripts.is_empty() {
            true => "unpinned".to_owned(),
            false => scripts.join(" or "),
        };
        state.note = Some(format!(
            "W3Quen.asi ({}) and quen.ws ({script}) are from different releases",
            state.version.as_deref().unwrap_or("unpinned"),
        ));
    }
    // From quen-w3 0.1.16 its release's HUD bundle too (PACKAGE_HUD), when the ASI's release has pins for it.
    let version = state.version.clone().unwrap_or_default();
    let mut hud = cx
        .pins
        .iter()
        .filter(|p| PACKAGE_HUD.contains(&p.file) && p.version == version);
    let stale = hud.find(|p| {
        fs::read(game.join(p.file))
            .map(|b| sha256_hex(&b))
            .ok()
            .as_deref()
            != Some(p.sha256)
    });
    if let Some(pin) = stale.filter(|_| state.status == "found") {
        state.status = "wrong_version";
        state.note = Some(format!("{} is not {version}'s", pin.file));
    }
    if state.status == "wrong_version" {
        state.note = state
            .note
            .map(|n| format!("{n}: unzip one release package into the game folder"));
    }
    state
}

pub(crate) const NGFX_REPLAY: Dep = Dep {
    name: "NVIDIA Nsight Graphics replayer (ngfx-replay)",
    required: false,
    enables: "ngfx_extract (a capture's metadata, final image, calls, objects, log errors) and ngfx_replay",
    how_to_get: "part of NVIDIA Nsight Graphics (https://developer.nvidia.com/nsight-graphics): ngfx-replay.exe beside \
        the ngfx.exe quen's config names (quen_setup). Nsight asks a privacy question once per version: the user \
        opens Nsight Graphics once and answers it; quen only reads the answer",
    check: ngfx_replay,
};

/// ngfx-replay.exe beside the configured ngfx.exe (only that install runs, never a capture's bundled replayer), its
/// version, and whether that version of Nsight asked its first-start privacy question: read from Nsight's settings
/// file, never written.
fn ngfx_replay(cx: &Cx) -> State {
    let Some(ngfx) = &cx.config.ngfx else {
        return State::missing("no ngfx in quen's config: quen_setup sets it".into());
    };
    let exe = ngfx.with_file_name("ngfx-replay.exe");
    if !exe.is_file() {
        return State::missing(format!("no ngfx-replay.exe beside {}", ngfx.display()));
    }
    let version = crate::win::file_version(&exe);
    let asked = nsight_ini().map(fs::read_to_string);
    let note = match (&version, asked) {
        (None, _) => "no version resource: Nsight's first-start question can't be checked".into(),
        (_, None | Some(Err(_))) => {
            "Nsight's settings file wasn't found: it hasn't asked its first-start question yet"
                .into()
        }
        (Some(v), Some(Ok(ini))) if quen_core::ngfx::privacy_asked(&ini, v) => {
            format!("Nsight {v} asked its first-start privacy question")
        }
        (Some(v), Some(Ok(_))) => format!(
            "Nsight {v} hasn't asked its first-start privacy question yet: the user opens Nsight Graphics once and \
             answers it (quen never answers it)"
        ),
    };
    State {
        version,
        note: Some(note),
        ..State::found(exe)
    }
}

/// Nsight Graphics' settings file, where it records its first-start privacy question per version: read, never written.
pub(crate) fn nsight_ini() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    env::var_os("APPDATA")
        .map(|d| PathBuf::from(d).join(r"NVIDIA Corporation\NVIDIA Nsight Graphics.ini"))
}

pub(crate) const GPU_COUNTERS: Dep = Dep {
    name: "NVIDIA GPU performance counters for all users",
    required: false,
    enables: "session_launch profiler ngfx:NAME: GPU Trace reads them, and says \"GPU Performance Counters \
        unavailable\" while the driver keeps them to administrators",
    how_to_get: "a system setting the user changes, never quen or its agents: NVIDIA Control Panel > Desktop > \
        Enable Developer Settings, then Developer > Manage GPU Performance Counters > Allow access to the GPU \
        performance counters to all users",
    check: |cx| {
        if !cx.probes {
            return State::missing("not probed".into());
        }
        counters(profiling_admin_only())
    },
};

/// The NVIDIA driver's `RmProfilingAdminOnly`, which the Control Panel's counter setting writes (0: all users), and
/// where it was: the driver's service parameters first, then the display adapters' class keys.
/// ponytail: which copy the driver reads is inferred; on the one PC checked both held 0 after the user allowed it.
fn profiling_admin_only() -> Option<(u32, String)> {
    const VALUE: &str = "RmProfilingAdminOnly";
    const SERVICE: &str = r"SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\nvlddmkm\Parameters\Global\NVTweak";
    const DISPLAYS: &str =
        r"SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Class\{4d36e968-e325-11ce-bfc1-08002be10318}";
    let adapters = crate::win::reg_subkeys(DISPLAYS)
        .into_iter()
        .map(|sub| format!(r"{DISPLAYS}\{sub}"));
    std::iter::once(SERVICE.to_owned())
        .chain(adapters)
        .find_map(|key| Some((crate::win::reg_dword(true, &key, VALUE)?, key)))
}

/// The counters' state from [`profiling_admin_only`] (read-only: the setting is the user's to change).
fn counters(admin_only: Option<(u32, String)>) -> State {
    match admin_only {
        Some((0, key)) => State {
            path: None,
            note: Some(format!(r"allowed for all users (HKLM\{key} RmProfilingAdminOnly = 0)")),
            ..State::found(PathBuf::new())
        },
        Some((n, key)) => State::missing(format!(
            r"administrators only (HKLM\{key} RmProfilingAdminOnly = {n}): GPU Trace can't read them"
        )),
        None => State::missing(
            "RmProfilingAdminOnly is not set: the driver's default, administrators only (or no NVIDIA driver)"
                .into(),
        ),
    }
}

pub(crate) const STREAMLINE_DEV: Dep = Dep {
    name: "Streamline dev interposer (patched, for RenderDoc)",

                "wrong_version"

/// The saves game_save made that are still in gamesaves, by the ledger (schema 0010), oldest first: each stays in the
/// user's save list until the user deletes it. A ledger from before 0010 has none.
fn quen_saves(config: &Config) -> Value {
    let db = config.state_dir().join("quen.db");
    let Some(dir) = config.saves_dir().filter(|_| db.exists()) else {
        return json!([]);
    };
    let read = |l: &Ledger, sql: &str| l.query(sql, &[], Duration::from_secs(5));
    let rows = Ledger::open_readonly(&db).and_then(|l| {
        let has = "SELECT 1 FROM pragma_table_info('saves') WHERE name = 'made_by_boot'";
        if read(&l, has)?.rows.is_empty() {
            return Ok(Vec::new());
        }
        let sql = "SELECT file, made_by_boot, tainted_by_boot IS NOT NULL FROM saves
                   WHERE made_by_boot IS NOT NULL ORDER BY id";
        Ok(read(&l, sql)?.rows)
    });
    match rows {
        Ok(rows) => rows
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|r| r[0].as_str().is_some_and(|file| dir.join(file).is_file()))
            .map(|r| json!({"file": r[0], "boot": r[1], "tainted": r[2] == 1}))
            .collect(),
        Err(e) => json!(format!("the ledger can't be read: {e}")),
    }
}

/// The measurement rows whose method family is outside the playbook's list, by family: written before quen refused
/// them (finding 32), reported and never rewritten. Empty when there are none.
fn unknown_families(config: &Config) -> Value {
    let db = config.state_dir().join("quen.db");
    if !db.exists() {
        return json!([]);
    }
    match Ledger::open_readonly(&db).and_then(|l| l.unknown_families()) {
        Ok(rows) => rows
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(family, ids)| json!({"family": family, "rows": ids.len(), "ids": ids}))
            .collect(),
        Err(e) => json!(format!("the ledger can't be read: {e}")),
    }
}

/// Whether the ledger's KB index is of the commit the KB has checked out: its `.git` files read, no git process.
fn kb_index_state(cx: &Cx) -> State {
    let Some(kb) = &cx.config.kb else {
        return State::missing("no kb in quen's config".into());
    };
    let Some(head) = git_head(kb) else {
        return State::missing(format!(
            "kb {} isn't in a git work tree with a commit",
            kb.display()
        ));
    };
    let db = cx.config.state_dir().join("quen.db");
    let index = match db.exists() {
        true => Ledger::open_readonly(&db).and_then(|l| l.kb_index()),
        false => Ok(None),
    };
    match index {
        Err(e) => State::missing(format!("the ledger's KB index can't be read: {e}")),
        Ok(None) => State::missing("the KB was never scanned: quen kb scan".into()),
        Ok(Some((commit, at))) => State {
            status: if commit == head {
                "found"
            } else {
                "wrong_version"
            },
            version: Some(format!("commit {commit}, scanned {at}")),
            note: (commit != head).then(|| {
                format!(
                    "the index is of commit {commit}; the KB has {head} checked out: quen kb scan"
                )
            }),
            ..State::found(kb.clone())
        },
    }
}

/// The KB's tables that name the build they were made on.
const KB_BUILT: [&str; 2] = ["names.tsv", "hooks.tsv"];

/// The build the KB's tables name: `None` while none of them has a build line (a KB not pinned yet: nothing is checked).
/// Once one has it, a table there without one or with a malformed one is refused, and two that name different builds.
pub(crate) fn kb_build(kb: &Path) -> Result<Option<Build>, String> {
    let tables: Vec<(&str, Result<Build, String>)> = KB_BUILT
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|&file| Some((file, Build::of_kb(&fs::read_to_string(kb.join(file)).ok()?))))
        .collect();
    // ponytail: "no build line" is Build::of_kb's own error for a table without one.
    let unpinned =
        |b: &Result<Build, String>| b.as_ref().is_err_and(|e| e.starts_with("no build line"));
    if tables.iter().all(|(_, b)| unpinned(b)) {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let mut named: Option<(&str, Build)> = None;
    for (file, build) in tables {
        let build = build.map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", kb.join(file).display()))?;
        match &named {
            Some((first, b)) if *b != build => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "the KB's {first} is for {b}, but its {file} for {build}: one KB, one build"
                ));
            }
            Some(_) => {}
            None => named = Some((file, build)),
        }
    }
    Ok(named.map(|(_, b)| b))
}

/// Refuses unless the config's KB names no build, or names `exe`'s: names and RVAs from one build never reach
/// another. The mem_* tools and game_cvar check the build the session's launch read.
pub(crate) fn kb_matches(config: &Config, exe: &Build) -> Result<(), String> {
    match config.kb.as_deref().map(kb_build).transpose()?.flatten() {
        Some(kb) => kb.check_exe(exe),
        None => Ok(()),
    }
}

fn kb_build_state(cx: &Cx) -> State {
    let Some(kb) = &cx.config.kb else {
        return State::missing("no kb in quen's config".into());
    };
    if !kb.is_dir() {
        return State::missing(format!("kb {} is not a folder", kb.display()));
    }
    let named = match kb_build(kb) {
        Ok(Some(named)) => named,
        Ok(None) => {
            return State::missing(format!(
                "no build line in {}: the KB isn't checked against the exe",
                KB_BUILT.join(" or ")
            ));
        }
        Err(why) => {
            return State {
                status: "wrong_version",
                note: Some(why),
                ..State::found(kb.clone())
            };
        }
    };
    let checked = cx
        .game_build()
        .map_err(|e| format!("the game's exe: {e}"))
        .and_then(|game| named.check_exe(&game.build));
    State {
        status: if checked.is_ok() {
            "found"
        } else {
            "wrong_version"
        },
        version: Some(format!("PE stamp {}", named.stamp)),
        sha256: Some(named.sha256),
        note: checked.err(),
        ..State::found(kb.clone())
    }
}
```
