```rs
    }

    #[test]
    fn find_export_reads_a_synthetic_table() {
        // A table at RVA 0x1000: directory (40 bytes), functions, names, ordinals, then the name strings.
        let dir = 0x1000u32;
        let names = ["A_GetState", "A_SetMode", "Fwd_SetMode"];
        let mut t = vec![0u8; 40];
        let put =
            |t: &mut Vec<u8>, off: usize, v: u32| t[off..off + 4].copy_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());
        let (funcs, name_ptrs, ords, strings) = (40u32, 52u32, 64u32, 70u32);
        put(&mut t, 20, 3);
        put(&mut t, 24, 3);
        put(&mut t, 28, dir + funcs);
        put(&mut t, 32, dir + name_ptrs);
        put(&mut t, 36, dir + ords);
        t.resize(strings as usize, 0);
        // The third export's RVA points into the table: a forwarder.
        for (i, rva) in [0x2000u32, 0x2100, dir + 60].into_iter().enumerate() {
            put(&mut t, funcs as usize + 4 * i, rva);
        }
        let mut at = strings;
        for (i, name) in names.iter().enumerate() {
            put(&mut t, name_ptrs as usize + 4 * i, dir + at);
            t[ords as usize + 2 * i..ords as usize + 2 * i + 2]
                .copy_from_slice(&(i as u16).to_le_bytes());
            t.extend(name.as_bytes());
            t.push(0);
            at += name.len() as u32 + 1;
        }
        assert_eq!(
            find_export(&t, dir, &|n| n == "A_SetMode"),
            Ok(("A_SetMode".into(), 0x2100))
        );
        assert!(
            find_export(&t, dir, &|n| n.ends_with("_SetMode"))
                .unwrap_err()
                .contains("2 matching")
        );
        assert!(
            find_export(&t, dir, &|n| n == "Fwd_SetMode")
                .unwrap_err()
                .contains("forwards")
        );
        assert!(
            find_export(&t, dir, &|n| n == "Nope")
                .unwrap_err()
                .contains("0 matching")
        );
        assert!(find_export(&t[..30], dir, &|_| true).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn actions_parse_and_refuse_unknown_shapes() {
        assert_eq!(
            Action::parse(&json!({"cvar": "Rendering/X", "set": false})),
            Ok(Action::Cvar {
                name: "Rendering/X".into(),
                value: "false".into()
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            Action::parse(&json!({"keys": ["f9:150"]})),
            Ok(Action::Keys(vec!["f9:150".into()]))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            Action::parse(&json!({"asi": "W3BoneFix.asi", "set_mode": 1})),
            Ok(Action::SetMode {
                asi: "W3BoneFix.asi".into(),
                export: None,
                mode: 1
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            Action::parse(&json!({"asi": "a.asi", "export": "A_SetMode", "set_mode": 0})),
            Ok(Action::SetMode {
                asi: "a.asi".into(),
                export: Some("A_SetMode".into()),
                mode: 0
            })
        );
        for bad in [
            json!({"cvar": "X"}),
            json!({"keys": "e"}),
            json!({"asi": "a.asi", "set_mode": -1}),
            json!({"asi": "a.asi", "export": 1, "set_mode": 0}),
            json!({"exec": "x"}),
            json!([]),
        ] {
            assert!(Action::parse(&bad).is_err(), "{bad}");
        }
    }

```

`crates/quen/src/hands.rs`:

```rs
//! Who has the controls of the game, and the hand-overs between the user and the agent. In a play session (session_launch
//! mode play) the user has them from the launch and hands them to the agent to look into something at that spot; in a
//! test session the agent has them and may hand them to the user to set something up. quen keeps who has them (`hands`,
//! in every envelope's state). While the user has them, it refuses every call that sends input, writes to the game or
//! moves the focus, and lets reads run. `hands_take` (the client asks the user on every call) gives the agent the
//! controls, `hands_give` gives them to the user. quen sorts gamesaves at each hand-over: what changed while the user had
//! the controls is theirs (allowed, listed at the end); a save while the agent had them fails that call, and gives the
//! controls back to the user in a play session or ends a test session. When the connection that launched a play session
//! closes while the agent has the controls, quen undoes that hand-over's memory writes, then gives the user the controls
//! ([`dropped`]).

use std::cell::{Cell, RefCell};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;
use std::time::SystemTime;

use quen_core::mem::Write;
use quen_core::protocol::Verb;
use quen_core::saves::{self, Snapshot};
use serde_json::{Map, Value, json};

use crate::channel::{self, REPLY_MAX};
use crate::game::{self, Ctx, Fields, flag, hex_bytes, schema};
use crate::session::{Call, Done, Live, Session};
use crate::status::{self, State};
use crate::{focus, input};

/// Who has the controls.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Hands {
    User,
    Agent,
}

impl Hands {
    pub(crate) fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Hands::User => "user",
            Hands::Agent => "agent",
        }
    }
}

/// A session's hand-overs and the saves sorted at each, on its [`Live`].
pub(crate) struct Handovers {
    /// hands_take calls so far: quen's run ids in a play boot are `<session>-h<n>-<tag>`.
    pub(crate) takes: Cell<u32>,
    /// gamesaves as quen last sorted it (the launch, a hand-over, a save the guard found): what changed beyond it is the
    /// user's while they have the controls, unexpected while the agent has them.
    pub(crate) baseline: RefCell<Snapshot>,
    /// The saves sorted so far: the user's, and the ones written while the agent had the controls.
    pub(crate) user: RefCell<BTreeSet<String>>,
    pub(crate) unexpected: RefCell<BTreeSet<String>>,
    /// The session's patch list's length at the last hands_take: the writes after it are this hand-over's.
    pub(crate) since: Cell<usize>,
}

impl Handovers {
    pub(crate) fn new(saves: Snapshot) -> Handovers {
        Handovers {
            takes: Cell::new(0),
            baseline: RefCell::new(saves),
            user: RefCell::default(),
            unexpected: RefCell::default(),
            since: Cell::new(0),
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn tools() -> Vec<Value> {
    vec![
        json!({
            "name": "hands_take",
            "description": "Take the controls of the game from the user, once the user asked for it here: in a play \
                session (session_launch mode play), where the user has them from the launch, or in a test session \
                after hands_give. The client asks the user on every call (user_ok is only your word): never route \
                around a denial. While the user has the controls, quen refuses what sends input, writes to the game or \
                moves the focus (game_keys, game_console, game_exec, game_asi, game_load, game_pause, game_settime, \
                game_weather, game_teleport, game_place, game_items, game_save, game_camera with a pose, game_frame, \
                game_freecam but status, game_cvar set or restore, mem_patch, mem_unpatch and their _instances, \
                measure_ab, sweep_play, focus) and runs reads. Answers hand_over (n: in a play session quen's run ids \
                are <session>-h<n>-<tag>) and user_saves (the saves the user made since the last hand-over, theirs). \
                Refused, nothing changed: no user_ok, the agent has them already, the game not running, a wrong token, \
                another connection's session.",
            // Claude Code prompts for this tool on every call, in every permission mode, as for session_launch.
            "_meta": {"anthropic/requiresUserInteraction": true},
            "inputSchema": schema(json!({
                "user_ok": {"type": "boolean", "description": "true only after the user asked in this conversation for you to take the controls, and agreed. Required."},
            }), &["user_ok"]),
        }),
        json!({
            "name": "hands_give",
            "description": "Give the controls of the game to the user: back in a play session, or in a test session \
                for the user to do something in the game. No prompt. applied: memory patches and cvar writes still \
                applied; asi_modes: ASI mode sets, the last per export (quen can't undo one); in a play session, this \
                hand-over's. A play session refuses while there is one, unless keep_writes with the user's OK. Then \
                the free camera, quen's pause and a camera path end (freecam, pause, path: the game's replies); unless \
                to_client, the game comes to the front as focus to game brings it, tried twice (to_game: what it did, \
                or why not); the game shows that the user has the controls (status). kept: this \
                hand-over's teleports, settime, weather and items; unexpected_saves: saves written while the agent had \
                them. in_front: the window in front at the end (game, client or other). Refused: the user has them \
                already, a wrong token, to_client with no client window found at connect. Failed: one wasn't undone \
                (left); the controls went to the user.",
            "inputSchema": schema(json!({
                "keep_writes": {"type": "boolean", "description": "play session: give the controls back with this hand-over's memory patches, cvar writes and ASI mode sets still applied, the user having agreed. Default false: refused while any is"},
                "to_client": {"type": "boolean", "description": "true: bring this client's window to the front last, as focus to client does, so the user sees the chat (to_client in the result: why it didn't). Default false: the game comes to the front"},
            }), &[]),
        }),
    ]
}

/// Whether `tool` with `args` may run while the user has the controls: the session's own tools (each refuses by its
/// own rules) and reads. Everything else sends input, writes to the game or moves the focus.
pub(crate) fn user_may(tool: &str, args: &Value) -> bool {
    let has = |key: &str| args.get(key).is_some();
    match tool {
        "game_cvar" => !has("set") && args.get("restore").is_none_or(|r| r == false),
        "game_camera" => !has("pos") && !has("rot") && !has("fov"),
        "game_photo" => matches!(args["action"].as_str(), Some("get" | "list")),
        "game_freecam" => args["action"] == "status",
        "game_screenshot" | "game_listsaves" | "world_get" | "world_actors" | "world_frame"
        | "world_ground" | "world_ray" | "world_nav" | "world_map" | "game_scriptlog"
        | "measure_presentmon" | "mem_read" | "mem_scan" | "mem_follow" | "mem_walk"
        | "mem_find" | "mem_regions" | "sweep_save" | "capture_clean" | "measure_image"
        | "ngfx_extract" => true,
        tool => tool.starts_with("session_") || tool.starts_with("hands_"),
    }
}

/// Why `tool` is refused while the user has the controls.
pub(crate) fn user_has(tool: &str) -> String {
    format!(
        "the user has the controls: {tool} sends input, writes to the game or moves the focus. Nothing done. Ask the \
         user in the chat; with their OK, hands_take"
    )
}

/// Sorts what changed in gamesaves since the last sort, beyond the game's own saves and quen's, as the user's saves
/// (`user`) or as unexpected ones, and sorts from now on next time. The names it sorted.
pub(crate) fn sort(live: &Live, user: bool) -> Vec<String> {
    let h = &live.handovers;
    let now = saves::snapshot(&live.saves);
    let (_, found) = live.sorted(&now);
    let to = if user { &h.user } else { &h.unexpected };
    to.borrow_mut().extend(found.iter().cloned());
    *h.baseline.borrow_mut() = now;
    found
}

/// `hands_take`.
pub(crate) fn take(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Done {
    taken(session, call, args).map_or_else(|done| done, Done::Ok)
}

fn taken(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let cx = game::ctx(session, args, &["user_ok"])?;
    let h = &cx.live.handovers;
    if cx.hands != Some(Hands::User) {
        return Err(
            "the agent has the controls already (hands_give gives them to the user)"
                .to_string()
                .into(),
        );
    }
    if !flag(args, "user_ok")? {
        let why = "user_ok: the user asks in this conversation for you to take the controls, and agrees, first";
        return Err(why.to_string().into());
    }
    if cx.live.job.pids().unwrap_or_default().is_empty() {
        let why = match cx.live.play {
            true => "the game isn't running: the session ends by itself",
            false => "the game isn't running: session_end",
        };
        return Err(why.to_string().into());
    }
    let user_saves = sort(cx.live, true);
    h.takes.set(h.takes.get() + 1);
    h.since.set(cx.live.patches.borrow().len());
    session.shared.set_hands(Some(Hands::Agent));
    call.lap("take");
    let mut fields = Map::from_iter([
        ("hand_over".into(), json!(h.takes.get())),
        ("user_saves".into(), json!(user_saves)),
    ]);
    if let Some(shown) = status::set(&cx, Some(call), State::Working) {
        fields.insert("status".into(), json!(shown));
    }
    Ok(fields)
}

/// `hands_give`.
pub(crate) fn give(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Done {
    given(session, call, args).map_or_else(|done| done, Done::Ok)
}

fn given(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let cx = game::ctx(session, args, &["keep_writes", "to_client"])?;
    let h = &cx.live.handovers;
    if cx.hands == Some(Hands::User) {
        return Err("the user has the controls already".to_string().into());
    }
    let keep = flag(args, "keep_writes")?;
    let client = match flag(args, "to_client")? {
        true => Some(call.conn.client.clone()?),
        false => None,
    };
    let (applied, kept, modes) = {
        let patches = cx.live.patches.borrow();
        let mine = patches.get(h.since.get()..).unwrap_or_default();
        // A test session's writes stay applied across its hand-overs: all of them count.
        let writes = if cx.live.play { mine } else { &patches[..] };
        let mut applied: Vec<Value> = applied(writes).iter().map(|a| a[3].clone()).collect();
        // An instance patch's fields are one entry: named once.
        applied.dedup();
        (applied, kept(mine), modes(writes))
    };
    let mut fields = Map::new();
    let mut why = Vec::new();
    if !applied.is_empty() {
        fields.insert("applied".into(), json!(applied));
        why.push(
            "a memory patch or cvar write of this hand-over is still applied (applied): undo each (mem_unpatch, \
             mem_unpatch_instances, game_cvar restore)",
        );
    }
    if !modes.is_empty() {
        fields.insert("asi_modes".into(), json!(modes));
        why.push(
            "this hand-over set an ASI's mode (asi_modes), which quen can't undo: it can't read an ASI's mode",
        );
    }
    if cx.live.play && !keep && !why.is_empty() {
        let why = format!(
            "{}. keep_writes: true, with the user's OK, gives the controls with them. Nothing done",
            why.join("; ")
        );
        return Err(Done::RefusedWith(why, fields));
    }
    fields.insert("kept".into(), json!(kept));
    // quen's pause, a camera path a sweep left and the free camera quen read on end with the hand-over.
    let mut left = Vec::new();
    match crate::freecam::off_if_on(&cx) {
        Some(Ok(done)) => {
            fields.insert("freecam".into(), json!(done));
        }
        Some(Err(why)) => left.push(format!("freecam: {why}")),
        None => {}
    }
    let undo = [
        (cx.live.path.get(), "path", Verb::CamStop {}),
        (cx.live.paused.get(), "pause", Verb::Pause { on: false }),
    ];
    for (_, what, verb) in undo.into_iter().filter(|(due, ..)| *due) {
        let sent = cx
            .channel()
            .and_then(|c| c.call(verb, REPLY_MAX).map_err(|e| e.why().to_string()));
        match sent {
            Ok(reply) => {
                match what {
                    "pause" => channel::note_pause(cx.live, &reply),
                    _ => cx.live.path.set(false),
                }
                fields.insert(what.into(), json!(reply.text));
            }
            Err(why) => left.push(format!("{what}: {why}")),
        }
        call.lap(what);
    }
    // Boot 264: a hands_give left the client in front (quen's idle focus and the client's prompt hook can bring it there,
    // and nothing brought the game back). The game comes back as focus to game brings it, checked, tried once more.
    if client.is_none() && in_front(&cx, call) != "game" {
        let mut tried = Err(String::new());
        for _ in 0..2 {
            tried = focus::to_game(&cx, call).map_err(|done| crate::boot::reason(&done));
            if tried.is_ok() && in_front(&cx, call) == "game" {
                break;
            }
        }
        let shown = match tried {
            Ok(done) if in_front(&cx, call) == "game" => {
                cx.live.away.set(false);
                json!(done)
            }
            Ok(_) => json!("the game isn't in front: it came to the front and lost it again"),
            Err(why) => json!(format!("the game isn't in front: {why}")),
        };
        fields.insert("to_game".into(), shown);
        call.lap("to_game");
    }
    // The user may be in the game when the controls go to them: it says so, and where to hand them back.
    if let Some(shown) = status::set(&cx, Some(call), State::Yours) {
        fields.insert("status".into(), json!(shown));
    }
    fields.insert("unexpected_saves".into(), json!(sort(cx.live, false)));
    session.shared.set_hands(Some(Hands::User));
    // Finding 43: the user missed a question twice behind the game. to_client fronts the chat; in_front says which.
    if let Some((pid, name)) = &client
        && let Err(done) = focus::to_client(*pid, name)
    {
        fields.insert("to_client".into(), json!(crate::boot::reason(&done)));
    }
    fields.insert("in_front".into(), json!(in_front(&cx, call)));
    if !left.is_empty() {
        fields.insert("left".into(), json!(left));
        let why = "the controls went to the user, but quen's pause, the camera path or the free camera wasn't \
                   undone (left)";
        return Err(Done::Failed(why.into(), fields));
    }
    Ok(fields)
}

/// Which window is in front: the game's, this connection's client's, or another.
fn in_front(cx: &Ctx, call: &Call) -> &'static str {
    let game = cx.window().is_ok_and(|(_, w)| input::in_front(w));
    let client = call
        .conn
        .client
        .as_ref()
        .ok()
        .and_then(|(pid, _)| focus::window_of(*pid).ok().flatten());
    match (game, client.is_some_and(input::in_front)) {
        (true, _) => "game",
        (false, true) => "client",
        _ => "other",
    }
}

/// The connection that launched a play session closed. While the agent has the controls, this hand-over's memory
/// patches and cvar writes still applied are undone, newest first: each journaled like any write, and only while the
/// bytes there are still the ones it wrote, as mem_unpatch checks (another writer's are left); an instance patch's
/// fields as mem_unpatch_instances undoes them, one step per patch. Its ASI mode sets are left ([`modes`]). A write kept
/// by agreement (hands_give's keep_writes) is an earlier hand-over's and stays. Then the user has the controls. What it
/// undid, what it left and why, and the hand-over's teleports, settime and weather (kept), for the log.
pub(crate) fn dropped(session: &Session) -> Value {
    let Some(live) = &session.live else {
        return Value::Null;
    };
    let (mut undone, mut left, mut keep) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    if session.shared.hands() == Some(Hands::Agent) {
        let todo: Vec<(Write, String, Value)> = {
            let patches = live.patches.borrow();
            let mine = patches
                .get(live.handovers.since.get()..)
                .unwrap_or_default();
            keep = kept(mine);
            left.extend(modes(mine).iter().map(|what| {
                let what = what.as_str().unwrap_or_default();
                format!("{what}: an ASI's mode set, which quen can't undo")
            }));
            let applied =
                applied(mine)
                    .into_iter()
                    .filter_map(|[address, old, new, what, meta]| {
                        let what = what.as_str().unwrap_or_default();
                        let what = match meta.is_null() {
                            true => what.rsplit_once(" at ").map_or(what, |(w, _)| w),
                            false => what,
                        };
                        let undo = Write {
                            address: address.as_u64()?,
                            old: hex_bytes(new)?,
                            new: hex_bytes(old)?,
                        };
                        Some((undo, what.into(), meta.clone()))
                    });
            applied.collect()
        };
        let game = session.config().and_then(|config| {
            let cx = Ctx {
                config,
                live,
                hands: Some(Hands::Agent),
            };
            cx.game().map(|game| (cx, game))
        });
        // An instance patch's fields come one after another: undone together.
        for run in todo.chunk_by(|a, b| !a.2.is_null() && (&a.1, &a.2) == (&b.1, &b.2)) {
            let (what, meta) = (&run[0].1, &run[0].2);
            let step = format!("undo of {what}");
            let made = match (&game, meta.is_null()) {
                (Ok((cx, game)), true) => cx.write(game, &step, &run[0].0, &mut Map::new()),
                (Ok((cx, game)), false) => {
                    let writes: Vec<Write> = run.iter().map(|(w, ..)| w.clone()).collect();
                    let results = cx.undo_instances(game, &step, meta, &writes, &mut Map::new());
                    results.and_then(|results| {
                        let n = results.iter().filter(|r| r.is_ok()).count();
                        let Some(why) = results.iter().find_map(|r| r.clone().err()) else {
                            return Ok(());
                        };
                        let note = format!(
                            "{} of {} fields left ({why})",
                            results.len() - n,
                            results.len()
                        );
                        if n == 0 {
                            return Err(Done::Refused(note));
                        }
                        left.push(format!("{what}: {note}"));
                        Ok(())
                    })
                }
                (Err(why), _) => Err(Done::Refused(why.clone())),
            };
            match made {
                Ok(()) => undone.push(what.clone()),
                Err(Done::Failed(why, _) | Done::Refused(why)) => {
                    left.push(format!("{what}: {why}"))
                }
                Err(_) => left.push(what.clone()),
            }
        }
    }
    session.shared.set_hands(Some(Hands::User));
    json!({"undone": undone, "left": left, "kept": keep})
}

/// The memory writes among `patches` (mem_patch and mem_unpatch, game_cvar's, measure_ab's cvars, and each field of an
/// instance patch's `writes`) still applied, newest first: per address, the last write's new bytes differ from what the
/// first found there. Each as the address, the first write's old bytes, the last one's new bytes, its `what` and its
/// entry's `instances` (null but for an instance patch's).
/// ponytail: quadratic in the writes; a few thousand instance fields take milliseconds.
pub(crate) fn applied(patches: &[(SystemTime, Value)]) -> Vec<[&Value; 5]> {
    let writes = || {
        patches.iter().flat_map(|(_, p)| {
            let one = std::iter::once(&p["write"]).filter(|w| !w.is_null());
            let many = p["writes"].as_array().into_iter().flatten();
            one.chain(many)
                .map(move |w| (w, &p["what"], &p["instances"]))
        })
    };
    let mut seen = Vec::new();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for (w, what, meta) in writes().rev() {
        if seen.contains(&&w["address"]) {
            continue;
        }
        seen.push(&w["address"]);
        let first = writes().find(|(f, ..)| f["address"] == w["address"]);
        let old = &first.unwrap_or((w, what, meta)).0["old"];
        if *old != w["new"] {
            out.push([&w["address"], old, &w["new"], what, meta]);
        }
    }
    out
}

/// The teleports, settime and weather among `patches`: what taints without a write.
fn kept(patches: &[(SystemTime, Value)]) -> Vec<Value> {
    patches
        .iter()
        .filter(|(_, p)| p["write"].is_null() && p["writes"].is_null() && p["taints"] == true)
        .map(|(_, p)| p["what"].clone())
        .collect()
}

/// The ASI mode sets among `patches` (`Ctx::set_mode`'s entries: no write, tainting no save), the last per export,
/// newest first. quen can't read an ASI's mode, so it can't put back the one before a set.
fn modes(patches: &[(SystemTime, Value)]) -> Vec<Value> {
    let export = |what: &Value| {
        what.as_str()
            .and_then(|w| w.split('(').next())
            .map(str::to_owned)
    };
    let mut out: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
    for (_, p) in patches.iter().rev() {
        let set = p["write"].is_null() && p["writes"].is_null() && p["taints"] == false;
        if set && !out.iter().any(|o| export(o) == export(&p["what"])) {
            out.push(p["what"].clone());
        }
    }
    out
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::game::tests::Fake;

    /// With the user's hands, input, writes and focus moves are refused, reads run.
    #[test]
    fn with_the_users_hands_only_reads_run() {
        let none = json!({"token": "t"});
        for tool in [
            "game_keys",
            "game_console",
            "game_asi",
            "game_load",
            "game_pause",
            "game_settime",
            "game_weather",
            "game_teleport",
            "game_items",
            "game_save",
            "sweep_play",
            "measure_ab",
            "mem_patch",
            "mem_unpatch",
            "mem_patch_instances",
            "mem_unpatch_instances",
            "focus",
        ] {
            assert!(!user_may(tool, &none), "{tool}");
        }
        for (tool, args) in [
            ("game_cvar", json!({"name": "X", "set": "1"})),
            ("game_cvar", json!({"name": "X", "restore": true})),
            ("game_camera", json!({"pos": [0, 0, 0], "rot": [0, 0, 0]})),
            ("game_camera", json!({"fov": 40})),
            ("game_freecam", json!({"action": "on"})),
            ("game_freecam", json!({"action": "set", "relative": {}})),
        ] {
            assert!(!user_may(tool, &args), "{tool} {args}");
        }
        for (tool, args) in [
            ("game_cvar", json!({"name": "X"})),
            ("game_cvar", json!({"name": "X", "restore": false})),
            ("game_camera", none.clone()),
            ("game_freecam", json!({"action": "status"})),
        ] {
            assert!(user_may(tool, &args), "{tool} {args}");
        }
        for tool in [
            "game_screenshot",
            "game_listsaves",
            "world_get",
            "world_actors",
            "game_scriptlog",
            "measure_presentmon",
            "mem_read",
            "mem_scan",
            "mem_follow",
            "mem_walk",
            "mem_find",
            "mem_regions",
            "sweep_save",
            "session_end",
            "hands_take",
            "hands_give",
        ] {
            assert!(user_may(tool, &none), "{tool}");
        }
    }

    /// The Fake's session, a play session or a test one, the agent holding the controls since its first hand-over.
    fn handed_over(fx: &Fake, play: bool) -> Session<'_> {
        let mut session = fx.session();
        let live = session.live.as_mut().unwrap();
        live.play = play;
        live.handovers.takes.set(1);
        fx.shared.set_hands(Some(Hands::Agent));
        session
    }

    fn run(session: &Session, tool: &str, args: Value) -> Value {
        let mut call = session.call(crate::mcp::Conn::nobody(), Value::Null, None);
        let done = match tool {
            "hands_take" => take(session, &mut call, &args),
            _ => give(session, &mut call, &args),
        };
        session.envelope(tool, call, done)
    }

    fn patch(session: &Session, what: &str, write: Value) {
        let taints = !write.is_null() || what.starts_with("channel");
        let p = json!({"what": what, "t": 0, "write": write, "taints": taints});
        let live = session.live.as_ref().unwrap();
        live.patches.borrow_mut().push((SystemTime::now(), p));
    }

    /// In a play session hands_give refuses while a memory patch or cvar write of this hand-over is applied, unless
    /// keep_writes; an undone one doesn't count, an earlier hand-over's isn't its own, and a teleport is listed as kept.
    #[test]
    fn hands_give_in_a_play_session_refuses_while_a_write_of_the_hand_over_is_applied() {
        let fx = Fake::new("play-return");
        let session = handed_over(&fx, true);
        let tok = json!({"token": "tok"});
        patch(
            &session,
            "an earlier hand-over's",
            json!({"address": 7, "old": "00", "new": "01"}),
        );
        session.live.as_ref().unwrap().handovers.since.set(1);
        patch(
            &session,
            "cvar X set 1 at 0x10",
            json!({"address": 16, "old": "00", "new": "01"}),
        );
        patch(&session, "channel {\"verb\":\"teleport\"}", Value::Null);
        patch(
            &session,
            "mem_patch cull at 0x20",
            json!({"address": 32, "old": "aa", "new": "bb"}),
        );
        patch(
            &session,
            "mem_unpatch cull at 0x20",
            json!({"address": 32, "old": "bb", "new": "aa"}),
        );
        let out = run(&session, "hands_give", tok.clone());
        assert_eq!(out["refused"], true, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["applied"], json!(["cvar X set 1 at 0x10"]), "{out}");
        assert_eq!(fx.shared.hands(), Some(Hands::Agent), "nothing changed");
        let bad = run(
            &session,
            "hands_give",
            json!({"token": "tok", "keep_writes": "yes"}),
        );
        assert_eq!(bad["refused"], true, "{bad}");
        // Restored: the controls go back, the teleport listed as what the user plays with now.
        patch(
            &session,
            "cvar X back to its value before quen's first write at 0x10",
            json!({"address": 16, "old": "01", "new": "00"}),
        );
        let out = run(&session, "hands_give", tok.clone());
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(
            out["kept"],
            json!(["channel {\"verb\":\"teleport\"}"]),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert_eq!(out["state"]["hands"], "user", "{out}");
        // The Fake's game serves no channel: the status says why it isn't shown, and the controls went anyway.
        assert!(
            out["status"].as_str().unwrap().contains("isn't up"),
            "{out}"
        );
        let again = run(&session, "hands_give", tok.clone());
        assert_eq!(again["refused"], true, "{again}");
        // keep_writes: the controls go back with the write still applied, named.
        fx.shared.set_hands(Some(Hands::Agent));
        patch(
            &session,
            "cvar Y set 2 at 0x30",
            json!({"address": 48, "old": "00", "new": "02"}),
        );
        let out = run(
            &session,
            "hands_give",
            json!({"token": "tok", "keep_writes": true}),
        );
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["applied"][0], "cvar Y set 2 at 0x30", "{out}");
    }

    /// A test session gives the controls with its writes applied, all of the session's named.
    #[test]
    fn hands_give_in_a_test_session_keeps_the_agents_writes() {
        let fx = Fake::new("test-give");
        let session = handed_over(&fx, false);
        patch(
            &session,
            "mem_patch cull at 0x20",
            json!({"address": 32, "old": "aa", "new": "bb"}),
        );
        session.live.as_ref().unwrap().handovers.since.set(1);
        // Finding 43: to_client needs a client window found at connect, checked before anything changes.
        let front = run(
            &session,
            "hands_give",
            json!({"token": "tok", "to_client": true}),
        );
        assert_eq!(front["refused"], true, "{front}");
        assert_eq!(fx.shared.hands(), Some(Hands::Agent), "nothing changed");
        let out = run(&session, "hands_give", json!({"token": "tok"}));
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["applied"], json!(["mem_patch cull at 0x20"]), "{out}");
        // No window here is the dummy game's or a client's: the game couldn't come to the front, and to_game says why.
        assert_eq!(out["in_front"], "other", "{out}");
        let to_game = out["to_game"].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(
            to_game.starts_with("the game isn't in front: no visible window"),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert_eq!(fx.shared.hands(), Some(Hands::User));
    }

    /// An ASI mode set can't be undone (quen can't read the mode before it): in a play session hands_give names this
    /// hand-over's, the last per export, and refuses unless keep_writes; a dropped connection leaves them, named.
    #[test]
    fn an_asi_mode_set_holds_a_play_hand_over_until_keep_writes() {
        let fx = Fake::new("play-asi");
        let session = handed_over(&fx, true);
        for what in [
            "W3X.asi!W3X_SetMode(0) returned 1",
            "W3Y.asi!W3Y_SetMode(1) returned 1",
            "W3X.asi!W3X_SetMode(1) returned 1",
        ] {
            patch(&session, what, Value::Null);
        }
        let modes = json!([
            "W3X.asi!W3X_SetMode(1) returned 1",
            "W3Y.asi!W3Y_SetMode(1) returned 1"
        ]);
        let out = run(&session, "hands_give", json!({"token": "tok"}));
        assert_eq!(
            (&out["refused"], &out["asi_modes"]),
            (&json!(true), &modes),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert!(
            out["reason"].as_str().unwrap().contains("can't undo"),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert_eq!(fx.shared.hands(), Some(Hands::Agent), "nothing changed");
        let out = dropped(&session);
        assert_eq!(out["undone"], json!([]), "{out}");
        assert_eq!(
            out["left"][0],
            "W3X.asi!W3X_SetMode(1) returned 1: an ASI's mode set, which quen can't undo"
        );
        assert_eq!(out["left"].as_array().unwrap().len(), 2, "{out}");
        fx.shared.set_hands(Some(Hands::Agent));
        let out = run(
            &session,
            "hands_give",
            json!({"token": "tok", "keep_writes": true}),
        );
        assert_eq!((&out["ok"], &out["asi_modes"]), (&json!(true), &modes));
    }

    /// The free camera quen last read on goes off before the controls go to the user, and the result says so; when it
    /// can't (no channel), the controls go anyway and the call fails with it in left.
    #[test]
    fn hands_give_turns_the_free_camera_off_first() {
        use crate::channel::tests::{fake_game_until, reply, served, token};
        use quen_core::protocol::Request;
        use std::sync::Arc;
        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
        let fx = served("give-freecam");
        let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let answer = Box::new(|r: &Request| {
            let text = match r.verb {
                Verb::FreeCam { on: false } => "EnableFreeCamera(0) called",
                Verb::Notice { .. } | Verb::NoticeHide {} => "notice shown",
                ref v => panic!("{v:?}"),
            };
            vec![reply(r.id, true, text, None)]
        });
        let server = fake_game_until(&token(&fx), answer, stop.clone());
        let session = handed_over(&fx, false);
        let live = session.live.as_ref().unwrap();
        live.freecam.set(true);
        let out = run(&session, "hands_give", json!({"token": "tok"}));
        stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        assert!(
            out["freecam"]
                .as_str()
                .unwrap()
                .contains("quen turned it off"),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert!(!live.freecam.get());
        assert_eq!(fx.shared.hands(), Some(Hands::User));
        let sent: Vec<Verb> = server.join().unwrap().into_iter().map(|r| r.verb).collect();
        assert_eq!(sent[0], Verb::FreeCam { on: false }, "{sent:?}");
        // No channel: the controls go to the user, and the free camera is left.
        let fx = Fake::new("give-freecam-down");
        let session = handed_over(&fx, false);
        session.live.as_ref().unwrap().freecam.set(true);
        let out = run(&session, "hands_give", json!({"token": "tok"}));
        assert_eq!(
            (&out["ok"], &out["refused"]),
            (&json!(false), &json!(false)),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert!(
            out["left"][0].as_str().unwrap().starts_with("freecam: "),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert_eq!(fx.shared.hands(), Some(Hands::User));
    }

    /// The connection that launched a play session closes while the agent has the controls: this hand-over's two dummy
    /// patches are undone, newest first and journaled; a write another writer changed since is left; a write kept by
    /// agreement at an earlier hand-over stays; the teleport is listed as kept; the user has the controls.
    #[test]
    fn a_dropped_play_session_undoes_the_hand_overs_writes() {
        use crate::mem::tests::{BUF, this_exe};
        let fx = Fake::new("play-drop");
        let (_, image) = this_exe();
        let buf = BUF.address() - image.base;
        let row = |name: &str, at: u64, old: &str, new: &str| {
            format!(
                "{name}\t{:#x}\t{old}\t{new}\t{}\ttest\n",
                buf + at,
                image.stamp
            )
        };
        let tsv = [
            "name\trva\told\tnew\tbuild\tboundaries-checked\n".to_string(),
            row("kept", 11, "62 75", "42 55"),
            row("a", 0, "71 75 65 6e", "51 55 45 4e"),
            row("b", 8, "6d 79", "4d 59"),
        ];
        std::fs::write(fx.dir.join("kb/patches.tsv"), tsv.concat()).unwrap();
        let mut session = handed_over(&fx, true);
        let mem = |session: &mut Session, tool: &str, args: Value| {
            let mut call = session.call(crate::mcp::Conn::nobody(), Value::Null, None);
            let done = crate::mem::call(session, &mut call, tool, &args);
            session.envelope(tool, call, done)
        };
        let on = |name: &str| json!({"token": "tok", "name": name});
        assert_eq!(mem(&mut session, "mem_patch", on("kept"))["ok"], true);
        let back = run(
            &session,
            "hands_give",
            json!({"token": "tok", "keep_writes": true}),
        );
        assert_eq!(back["ok"], true, "{back}");
        let took = run(
            &session,
            "hands_take",
            json!({"token": "tok", "user_ok": true}),
        );
        assert_eq!(took["ok"], true, "{took}");
        for name in ["a", "b"] {
            let out = mem(&mut session, "mem_patch", on(name));
            assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        }
        patch(&session, "channel {\"verb\":\"teleport\"}", Value::Null);
        // A write quen thinks it made at BUF + 4, whose bytes aren't what it wrote: another writer's.
        let game = crate::game::ctx(&session, &json!({"token": "tok"}), &[])
            .unwrap()
            .game()
            .unwrap();
        let other = game.image.base + buf + 4;
        patch(
            &session,
            &format!("mem_patch other at {other:#x}"),
            json!({"address": other, "old": "aa", "new": "bb"}),
        );

        let out = dropped(&session);
        assert_eq!(
            out["undone"],
            json!(["mem_patch b", "mem_patch a"]),
            "{out}"
        );
        let left = out["left"].as_array().unwrap();
        assert!(
            left.len() == 1 && left[0].as_str().unwrap().starts_with("mem_patch other: "),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert!(
            left[0].as_str().unwrap().contains("another writer"),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            out["kept"],
            json!(["channel {\"verb\":\"teleport\"}"]),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert_eq!(fx.shared.hands(), Some(Hands::User));
        let now = mem(
            &mut session,
            "mem_read",
            json!({"token": "tok", "rva": buf, "type": "bytes", "len": 16}),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            now["value"], "71 75 65 6e 2d 64 75 6d 6d 79 2d 42 55 66 01 02",
            "a and b undone, kept still applied: {now}"
        );
        let journal = std::fs::read_to_string(fx.dir.join("data/state/journal.jsonl")).unwrap();
        let b = journal.find("undo of mem_patch b at 0x").unwrap();
        let a = journal.find("undo of mem_patch a at 0x").unwrap();
        assert!(b < a, "newest first: {journal}");
        assert!(
            !journal.contains("undo of mem_patch other"),
            "taken back: {journal}"
        );
        // With the user's hands, a drop changes nothing.
        let again = dropped(&session);
        assert_eq!(again, json!({"undone": [], "left": [], "kept": []}));
    }

    /// The connection that launched a play session closes while the agent has the controls: this hand-over's instance
    /// patch, listed once by hands_give while applied, is undone as one journaled step, every field it wrote back.
    #[test]
    fn a_dropped_play_session_undoes_the_hand_overs_instance_patches() {
        use crate::mem::tests::{instances_tsv, obj_fields, run as mem};
        let fx = Fake::new("play-drop-instances");
        std::fs::write(fx.dir.join("kb/instance_patches.tsv"), instances_tsv()).unwrap();
        let mut session = handed_over(&fx, true);
        let on = json!({"token": "tok", "name": "steer", "user_ok": true});
        let out = mem(&mut session, "mem_patch_instances", on);
        assert_eq!(out["counts"]["written"], 3, "{out}");
        let what = json!(["mem_patch_instances steer: 3 instances of CQuenTest"]);
        let give = run(&session, "hands_give", json!({"token": "tok"}));
        assert_eq!(
            (&give["refused"], &give["applied"]),
            (&json!(true), &what),
            "{give}"
        );
        let out = dropped(&session);
        assert_eq!(out, json!({"undone": what, "left": [], "kept": []}));
        let v = |f: f32| json!(f);
        assert_eq!(obj_fields(&mut session), [v(0.2), v(0.2), v(0.5), v(0.2)]);
        let journal = std::fs::read_to_string(fx.dir.join("data/state/journal.jsonl")).unwrap();
        assert!(
            journal.contains("undo of mem_patch_instances steer: 3 instances of CQuenTest"),
            "{journal}"
        );
        assert_eq!(fx.shared.hands(), Some(Hands::User));
    }

    /// hands_take: refused without user_ok and while the agent has the controls; then it sorts the user's saves since
    /// the last hand-over and counts the hand-overs, in a play session and in a test one.
    #[test]
    fn hands_take_takes_the_controls_with_the_users_ok() {
        let fx = Fake::new("play-take");
        let dir = fx.dir.join("gamesaves");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        for play in [true, false] {
            let session = handed_over(&fx, play);
            let held = run(
                &session,
                "hands_take",
                json!({"token": "tok", "user_ok": true}),
            );
            assert!(
                held["reason"].as_str().unwrap().contains("already"),
                "{held}"
            );
            fx.shared.set_hands(Some(Hands::User));
            for args in [
                json!({"token": "tok"}),
                json!({"token": "tok", "user_ok": false}),
                json!({"token": "x", "user_ok": true}),
            ] {
                let out = run(&session, "hands_take", args.clone());
                assert_eq!(out["refused"], true, "{args}: {out}");
            }
            assert_eq!(fx.shared.hands(), Some(Hands::User));
            let user = format!("ManualSave_user_{play}.sav");
            std::fs::write(dir.join(&user), "the user's").unwrap();
            std::fs::write(dir.join("AutoSave_1.sav"), format!("the game's {play}")).unwrap();
            let out = run(
                &session,
                "hands_take",
                json!({"token": "tok", "user_ok": true}),
            );
            assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
            assert_eq!(out["hand_over"], 2, "{out}");
            // The session's baseline is the launch's (empty): every manual save so far is the user's.
            assert!(
                out["user_saves"].as_array().unwrap().contains(&json!(user)),
                "{out}"
            );
            assert_eq!(out["state"]["hands"], "agent", "{out}");
        }
    }
}

```

`crates/quen/src/image.rs`:

```rs
//! `measure_image` (the runner design's phase 3, finding 39): numbers from a screenshot quen took, over a crop, as
//! measurement rows with its `capture_id`, family `screenshot`. quen-core's image module decodes and measures; here the
//! captures rows are found, each file checked against its sha256, and the rows written in one transaction. It reads
//! the files only, and runs on the session thread, so never inside another call's window.

use std::fs;
use std::time::Duration;

use quen_core::hdr::Encoding;
use quen_core::image::{Image, Row};
use quen_core::journal::sha256_hex;
use quen_core::ledger::{Ledger, Measurement, Tag};
use serde_json::{Map, Value, json};

use crate::config::Config;
use crate::game::Fields;
use crate::session::{self, Call, Done, Session};

const METRICS: [&str; 4] = ["channels", "luminance", "hue_share", "diff"];
const KEYS: [&str; 14] = [
    "token",
    "capture",
    "metrics",
    "crop",
    "crop_unit",
    "hue",
    "s_min",
    "v_min",
    "reference",
    "noise_ref",
    "name",
    "state_label",
    "run_id",
    "note",
];

pub fn tool() -> Value {
    let capture = |what: &str| {
        json!({"type": "string", "description": format!("{what}: its captures id, or its path as captures.path has \
            it (<session>/<tag>.png)")})
    };
    let unit = json!({"type": "number", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 1, "description": "a fraction"});
    json!({
        "name": "measure_image",
        "description": "Numbers from a screenshot quen took (game_screenshot, game_frame, sweep_play) over a crop, \
            written as measurement rows: method_family screenshot, tag M, its capture_id and boot (quen_guide: \
            measure_image). metrics: channels (per R, G, B the mean and median of the file's values, srgb8 0-255, pq \
            0-1 or scrgb, and the mean of linear light), luminance (BT.709 Y of linear light: mean, median, p95, max; \
            nits from the HDR files, relative from srgb8: sRGB white = 1), hue_share (the share of pixels in an HSV hue \
            range), diff (against reference, and noise_ref as the floor). Reads the files only, each checked against \
            its sha256, on the session thread: never during a window. Refused, nothing written: not quen's screenshot \
            or not an image (an .rdc, a CSV, Nsight's final.png: its encoding is unknown), the file removed or changed, an argument a metric doesn't take, a crop \
            off the frame, a reference of another method, encoding, size or display state.",
        "inputSchema": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "token": {"type": "string", "description": "optional: the live session's token (run_plan passes it)"},
                "capture": capture("the screenshot"),
                "metrics": {"type": "array", "minItems": 1, "items": {"type": "string", "enum": METRICS, "description": "a metric"}, "description": "which numbers"},
                "crop": {"type": "array", "minItems": 4, "maxItems": 4, "items": {"type": "number", "description": "x, y, width or height"}, "description": "[x, y, width, height] from the top-left; default the whole frame"},
                "crop_unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["px", "fraction"], "description": "px (default): whole pixels. fraction: of the frame's width and height, each edge rounded to a pixel"},
                "hue": {"type": "array", "minItems": 2, "maxItems": 2, "items": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 360, "description": "degrees"}, "description": "hue_share: [from, to] degrees, both included; from above to wraps through 0"},
                "s_min": unit.clone(),
                "v_min": unit,
                "reference": capture("diff: the capture to compare with"),
                "noise_ref": capture("diff: a second capture of the screenshot's own state, the noise floor"),
                "name": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$", "description": "prefixes each metric's name (geralt: geralt_r_lin_mean)"},
                "state_label": {"type": "string", "description": "the rows' A/B label"},
                "run_id": {"type": "string", "description": "the rows' run id"},
                "note": {"type": "string", "description": "added to the rows' note"},
            },
            "required": ["capture", "metrics"],
            "additionalProperties": false,
        },
    })
}

/// A screenshot's captures row, its file read and decoded.
struct Shot {
    id: i64,
    path: String,
    method: String,
    boot: Option<i64>,
    display: Value,
    image: Image,
}

/// The screenshot `v` (an id, as a number or text, or a path) names, for argument `key`: one of quen's own
/// (capture.rs's methods), an image encoding, on disk and unchanged since its row.
fn shot(ledger: &Ledger, config: &Config, key: &str, v: &Value) -> Result<Shot, String> {
    let by_id = v
        .as_i64()
        .or_else(|| v.as_str().and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()));
    let (column, param) = match (by_id, v.as_str()) {
        (Some(id), _) => ("id = ?1", json!(id)),
        (None, Some(path)) if !path.is_empty() => {
            ("path = ?1 COLLATE NOCASE", json!(path.replace('\\', "/")))
        }
        _ => return Err(format!("{key} is a captures id or path")),
    };
    let sql = format!(
        "SELECT id, path, sha256, method, encoding, boot_id, removed_at, display_state FROM captures WHERE {column}"
    );
    let found = ledger.query(&sql, &[param], Duration::from_secs(5));
    let rows = found.map_err(session::ledger_error)?.rows;
    let [row] = &rows[..] else {
        return Err(format!("{key}: no capture {v}"));
    };
    let id = row[0].as_i64().unwrap_or_default();
    let text = |i: usize| row[i].as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_string();
    let (path, method) = (text(1), text(3));
    if method == "ngfx_extract" && path.ends_with("/final.png") {
        return Err(format!(
            "{key}: capture {id} ({path}) is Nsight's final image (ngfx_extract's screenshot op): Nsight makes it from \
             the presented back buffer by a conversion it doesn't name (boot 259's: an 8-bit RGBA PNG with no \
             colour-space chunk, from a 10-bit back buffer on an HDR display), so its encoding is unknown and \
             measure_image doesn't read it"
        ));
    }
    if !crate::capture::IMAGE_METHODS.contains(&method.as_str()) {
        return Err(format!(
            "{key}: capture {id} ({path}) was taken by {method:?}, not by quen's screenshot (methods {}): its numbers \
             aren't family screenshot",
            crate::capture::IMAGE_METHODS.join(", ")
        ));
    }
    let encoding: Encoding = serde_json::from_value(row[4].clone()).map_err(|_| {
        format!(
            "{key}: capture {id} ({path}) has encoding {}: measure_image reads srgb8, pq_bt2020_u16 and scrgb_f16",
            row[4]
        )
    })?;
    if !row[6].is_null() {
        return Err(format!(
            "{key}: capture {id} ({path}) was removed at {}",
            row[6]
        ));
    }
    let file = config.capture_root().join(&path);
    let bytes = fs::read(&file).map_err(|e| format!("{key}: {}: {e}", file.display()))?;
    if sha256_hex(&bytes) != text(2) {
        return Err(format!(
            "{key}: {}: changed since quen wrote it (sha256)",
            file.display()
        ));
    }
    let image = Image::decode(&bytes, encoding)
        .map_err(|why| format!("{key}: capture {id} ({path}), {encoding}: {why}"))?;
    Ok(Shot {
        id,
        path,
        method,
        boot: row[5].as_i64(),
        display: row[7].clone(),
        image,
    })
}

pub(crate) fn call(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let map = args
        .as_object()
        .ok_or("arguments must be an object".to_string())?;
    if let Some(key) = map.keys().find(|k| !KEYS.contains(&k.as_str())) {
        return Err(format!("unknown argument {key:?}").into());
    }
    if let Some(token) = args.get("token") {
        let live = session
            .live
            .as_ref()
            .ok_or("a token, but this quen has no live session".to_string())?;
        if token.as_str() != Some(live.token.as_str()) {
            return Err(
                "wrong token: only the agent that launched the session passes one"
                    .to_string()
                    .into(),
            );
        }
    }
    let metrics: Vec<&str> = args["metrics"]
        .as_array()
        .into_iter()
        .flatten()
        .map(|m| m.as_str().filter(|m| METRICS.contains(m)))
        .collect::<Option<_>>()
        .filter(|m: &Vec<&str>| !m.is_empty())
        .ok_or(format!("metrics is a list of {}", METRICS.join(", ")))?;
    if (1..metrics.len()).any(|i| metrics[..i].contains(&metrics[i])) {
        return Err("metrics names a metric twice".to_string().into());
    }
    let wants = |m: &str| metrics.contains(&m);
    for (key, metric) in [
        ("hue", "hue_share"),
        ("s_min", "hue_share"),
        ("v_min", "hue_share"),
        ("reference", "diff"),
        ("noise_ref", "diff"),
    ] {
        if map.contains_key(key) && !wants(metric) {
            return Err(format!("{key} is for {metric}, which metrics doesn't list").into());
        }
    }
    let hue = match (wants("hue_share"), args["hue"].as_array()) {
        (false, _) => None,
        (true, Some(h)) => match h
            .iter()
            .map(|d| d.as_u64().filter(|d| *d <= 360))
            .collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()
        {
            Some(d) if d.len() == 2 => Some([d[0] as u32, d[1] as u32]),
            _ => {
                return Err("hue is [from, to], whole degrees from 0 to 360"
                    .to_string()
                    .into());
            }
        },
        (true, None) => return Err("hue_share needs hue: [from, to] degrees".to_string().into()),
    };
    let fraction_of = |key: &str| match args.get(key) {
        None => Ok(0.0),
        Some(v) => v
            .as_f64()
            .filter(|f| (0.0..=1.0).contains(f))
            .ok_or(format!("{key} is a number from 0 to 1")),
    };
    let (s_min, v_min) = (fraction_of("s_min")?, fraction_of("v_min")?);
    if wants("diff") && !map.contains_key("reference") {
        return Err("diff needs reference: the capture to compare with"
            .to_string()
            .into());
    }
    let crop = match args.get("crop") {
        None => None,
        Some(v) => Some(
            v.as_array()
                .filter(|a| a.len() == 4)
                .and_then(|a| a.iter().map(Value::as_f64).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>())
                .map(|c| [c[0], c[1], c[2], c[3]])
                .ok_or("crop is [x, y, width, height]".to_string())?,
        ),
    };
    let fraction = match (args.get("crop_unit").map(Value::as_str), crop) {
        (None | Some(Some("px")), _) => false,
        (Some(Some("fraction")), Some(_)) => true,
        (Some(Some("fraction")), None) => return Err("crop_unit without crop".to_string().into()),
        _ => return Err("crop_unit is px or fraction".to_string().into()),
    };
    let text = |key: &str| match args.get(key) {
        None => Ok(None),
        Some(v) => v
            .as_str()
            .map(|s| Some(s.to_string()))
            .ok_or(format!("{key} must be a string")),
    };
    let (name, label, run, note) = (
        text("name")?,
        text("state_label")?,
        text("run_id")?,
        text("note")?,
    );
    if let Some(n) = &name {
        let ok = n.len() <= 40
            && n.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_lowercase())
            && n.bytes()
                .all(|b| b.is_ascii_lowercase() || b.is_ascii_digit() || b == b'_');
        if !ok {
            return Err(format!("name {n:?}: 1-40 of a-z, 0-9 and _, from a letter").into());
        }
    }
    let config = session.config()?;
    let mut ledger = session::open_ledger(config)?;
    let main = shot(&ledger, config, "capture", &args["capture"])?;
    call.lap("decode");
    let region = main.image.region(crop, fraction)?;
    let mut rows: Vec<Row> = Vec::new();
    let mut about = vec![format!(
        "measure_image {} {}x{} crop {},{} {}x{} px",
        main.image.encoding(),
        main.image.width(),
        main.image.height(),
        region.x,
        region.y,
        region.width,
        region.height
    )];
    let mut compared = Map::new();
    for metric in &metrics {
        match *metric {
            "channels" => rows.extend(main.image.channels(region)?),
            "luminance" => rows.extend(main.image.luminance(region)?),
            "hue_share" => {
                let [from, to] = hue.unwrap_or_default();
                rows.push(main.image.hue_share(region, [from, to], s_min, v_min)?);
                about.push(format!("hue {from}-{to} s>={s_min} v>={v_min}"));
            }
            _ => {
                let mut against = Vec::new();
                for key in ["reference", "noise_ref"] {
                    let Some(v) = args.get(key) else { continue };
                    let other = shot(&ledger, config, key, v)?;
                    if (&other.method, &other.display) != (&main.method, &main.display) {
                        return Err(format!(
                            "{key}: capture {} was taken by {} with display state {}, the screenshot by {} with {}: \
                             compare only captures of one method, encoding and display state",
                            other.id, other.method, other.display, main.method, main.display
                        )
                        .into());
                    }
                    about.push(format!("{key} capture {}", other.id));
                    compared.insert(key.into(), json!({"id": other.id, "path": other.path}));
                    against.push(other.image);
                }
                rows.extend(main.image.diff_rows(&against[0], against.get(1), region)?);
            }
        }
    }
    let non_finite = main.image.non_finite(region)?;
    if non_finite > 0 {
        about.push(format!(
            "{non_finite} pixels with a NaN or infinity left out"
        ));
    }
    about.extend(note);
    call.lap("metrics");
    let note = about.join("; ");
    if let Some(n) = &name {
        for r in &mut rows {
            r.metric = format!("{n}_{}", r.metric);
        }
    }
    let ids = ledger
        .atomic(|l| {
            rows.iter()
                .map(|r| {
                    l.add_measurement(&Measurement {
                        boot_id: main.boot,
                        capture_id: Some(main.id),
                        metric: r.metric.clone(),
                        value: Some(r.value),
                        unit: Some(r.unit.into()),
                        state_label: label.clone(),
                        method_family: "screenshot".into(),
                        tag: Tag::M,
                        run_id: run.clone(),
                        note: Some(note.clone()),
                        extraction_id: None,
                        world: None,
                    })
                })
                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
        })
        .map_err(session::ledger_error)?;
    for id in ids {
        call.row("measurements", id);
    }
    call.lap("ledger");
    let mut fields = Map::new();
    fields.insert(
        "capture".into(),
        json!({"id": main.id, "path": main.path, "method": main.method, "encoding": main.image.encoding(),
               "size": [main.image.width(), main.image.height()]}),
    );
    fields.insert(
        "crop".into(),
        json!([region.x, region.y, region.width, region.height]),
    );
    fields.extend(compared);
    fields.insert("values".into(), json!(rows));
    if non_finite > 0 {
        fields.insert("non_finite".into(), json!(non_finite));
    }
    Ok(fields)
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Writes `bytes` as `<capture root>/s1/<name>` with a captures row on boot 1 (the Fake's): its id.
    pub(crate) fn stored(
        fx: &Fake,
        name: &str,
        bytes: &[u8],
        method: &str,
        encoding: Option<Encoding>,
    ) -> i64 {
        let dir = fx.dir.join("data/captures/s1");
        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        fs::write(dir.join(name), bytes).unwrap();
        let mut ledger = Ledger::open(fx.dir.join("data/state/quen.db")).unwrap();
        let row = Capture {
            boot_id: Some(1),
            path: format!("s1/{name}"),
            sha256: sha256_hex(bytes),
            bytes: bytes.len() as i64,
            kind: name.rsplit('.').next().unwrap().into(),
            method: Some(method.into()),
            encoding,
            display_state: json!({"color_mode": "hdr"}).as_object().cloned(),
            t: "2026-10-17T13:16:00Z".into(),
            ..Capture::default()
        };
        ledger.add_capture(&row).unwrap()
    }

    /// An 8-bit RGB PNG of `px`, as capture.rs encodes the SDR grab.
    pub(crate) fn srgb8(width: u32, height: u32, px: &[[u8; 3]]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let mut encoder = png::Encoder::new(&mut out, width, height);
        encoder.set_color(png::ColorType::Rgb);
        encoder.set_depth(png::BitDepth::Eight);
        let mut writer = encoder.write_header().unwrap();
        writer.write_image_data(&px.concat()).unwrap();
        writer.finish().unwrap();
        out
    }

    fn db(fx: &Fake, sql: &str) -> Vec<Vec<Value>> {
        let l = Ledger::open_readonly(fx.dir.join("data/state/quen.db")).unwrap();
        l.query(sql, &[], Duration::from_secs(5)).unwrap().rows
    }

    /// The design's accept: hand-computed values from each encoding quen's screenshots use, written as rows with the
    /// capture's id and boot, family screenshot; ids and paths both name a capture.
    #[test]
    fn rows_carry_the_capture_id_and_hand_computed_values() {
        let fx = Fake::new("image-rows");
        let px = [[255, 0, 0], [0, 255, 0], [0, 0, 255], [128, 128, 128]];
        let a = stored(
            &fx,
            "A1.png",
            &srgb8(2, 2, &px),
            "printwindow",
            Some(Encoding::Srgb8),
        );
        let mut moved = px;
        moved[3] = [128, 148, 128];
        let b = stored(
            &fx,
            "B1.png",
            &srgb8(2, 2, &moved),
            "printwindow",
            Some(Encoding::Srgb8),
        );
        let mut noisy = px;
        noisy[3] = [130, 128, 128];
        let n = stored(
            &fx,
            "A2.png",
            &srgb8(2, 2, &noisy),
            "printwindow",
            Some(Encoding::Srgb8),
        );
        let out = fx.run(
            "measure_image",
            json!({"token": "tok", "capture": a, "metrics": ["channels", "luminance", "hue_share", "diff"],
                   "hue": [200, 280], "reference": "S1\\b1.PNG", "noise_ref": n.to_string(), "name": "geralt",
                   "state_label": "A", "run_id": "s1-img", "note": "a test"}),
        );
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        let value = |metric: &str| {
            let v = out["values"]
                .as_array()
                .unwrap()
                .iter()
                .find(|r| r["metric"] == metric);
            v.unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no {metric}: {out}"))["value"]
                .as_f64()
                .unwrap()
        };
        assert_eq!(value("geralt_r_srgb8_mean"), 95.75);
        assert_eq!(value("geralt_r_srgb8_median"), 64.0);
        assert_eq!(value("geralt_hue_200_280_share"), 0.25);
        // 20 levels in one pixel of four against B1, 2 against A2.
        assert_eq!(value("geralt_diff_srgb8_mean"), 5.0);
        assert_eq!(value("geralt_floor_srgb8_mean"), 0.5);
        assert_eq!(value("geralt_diff_over_floor"), 10.0);
        assert_eq!(
            (
                out["reference"]["id"].clone(),
                out["noise_ref"]["id"].clone()
            ),
            (json!(b), json!(n))
        );
        let ids = out["ledger"]["measurements"].as_array().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(ids.len(), 9 + 4 + 1 + 3, "{out}");
        let rows = db(
            &fx,
            "SELECT DISTINCT method_family, tag, capture_id, boot_id, state_label, run_id, note \
                            FROM measurements",
        );
        let note = format!(
            "measure_image srgb8 2x2 crop 0,0 2x2 px; hue 200-280 s>=0 v>=0; reference capture {b}; \
                            noise_ref capture {n}; a test"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            rows,
            [[
                json!("screenshot"),
                json!("M"),
                json!(a),
                json!(1),
                json!("A"),
                json!("s1-img"),
                json!(note)
            ]]
        );

        // HDR: the .npy and the PQ PNG of one shot, 100 and 400 nits gray, give the same luminance in nits.
        let s: Vec<f16> = [100.0f32, 400.0]
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|n| [n / 80.0, n / 80.0, n / 80.0, 1.0])
            .map(f16::from_f32)
            .collect();
        let frame = Frame::new(2, 1, Pixels::ScrgbF16(s)).unwrap();
        let (mut npy, mut png) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        frame.write_npy(&mut npy).unwrap();
        frame.write_png_pq(&mut png).unwrap();
        let ids = [
            stored(&fx, "H1.npy", &npy, "wgc_fp16", Some(Encoding::ScrgbF16)),
            stored(&fx, "H1.png", &png, "wgc_fp16", Some(Encoding::PqBt2020U16)),
        ];
        for id in ids {
            let out = fx.run(

            );
            assert_eq!(out["crop"], json!([1, 0, 1, 1]), "{out}");

            );
        }
    }
```

`crates/quen/src/input.rs`:

```rs
//! Focus-safe input into the game, ported from w3ctl.py (keys) and console_type.py (console lines). quen-core
//! plans the events; this sends them with SendInput as Set-1 scancodes, only to the game's own window (the window of
//! the session's game process, never one found by title), and only while that window is in front: the game pauses into
//! its menu when it loses focus, and keys sent then would land in another window or act on that menu.

use std::io;
use std::thread::sleep;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use quen_core::input::{Event, GRAVE, describe};
use windows::Win32::Foundation::HWND;
use windows::Win32::System::Threading::{AttachThreadInput, GetCurrentThreadId};
use windows::Win32::UI::Input::KeyboardAndMouse::{
    GetKeyboardLayout, INPUT, INPUT_0, INPUT_KEYBOARD, INPUT_MOUSE, KEYBDINPUT,
    KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY, KEYEVENTF_KEYUP, KEYEVENTF_SCANCODE, MAPVK_VK_TO_VSC, MapVirtualKeyExW,
    SendInput, VIRTUAL_KEY, VK_OEM_3,
};
use windows::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{
    BringWindowToTop, GetForegroundWindow, GetWindowThreadProcessId, SetForegroundWindow,
};

/// Marks quen's own key events (their dwExtraInfo), so a window can tell them from the user's keys.
pub(crate) const MARK: usize = 0x5155_454E; // "QUEN"

pub(crate) fn in_front(window: HWND) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: a plain query.
    unsafe { GetForegroundWindow() == window }
}

/// The game's console key and where it came from. The game has no console binding to read (input.settings binds no
/// console action, bin\config only switches the console on): the engine opens it on IK_Tilde, the virtual key
/// VK_OEM_3, which sits wherever the active layout puts it (w3ctl's rule, verified live on a non-US layout). So it is
/// that key's scancode on the layout of the window's thread, or the US position if the layout has no VK_OEM_3.
pub(crate) fn console_key(window: HWND) -> (u16, &'static str) {
    match layout_scancode(window)(VK_OEM_3.0) {
        Some(sc) => (sc, "VK_OEM_3 on the game window's keyboard layout"),
        None => (
            GRAVE,
            "the US position: the game window's layout has no VK_OEM_3",
        ),
    }
}

/// Virtual key → scancode on the keyboard layout of the window's thread, the layout the game reads keys through (the
/// console maps each key's virtual key there through a US table). None: the layout has no key for it.
pub(crate) fn layout_scancode(window: HWND) -> impl Fn(u16) -> Option<u16> {
    // SAFETY: plain queries; a window that closed meanwhile gives thread 0, the current thread's layout.
    let layout = unsafe { GetKeyboardLayout(GetWindowThreadProcessId(window, None)) };
    move |vk| {
        // SAFETY: a plain query.
        let sc = unsafe { MapVirtualKeyExW(u32::from(vk), MAPVK_VK_TO_VSC, Some(layout)) };
        u16::try_from(sc).ok().filter(|&sc| sc != 0)
    }
}

/// w3ctl's `focus`: brings `window` to the front. Ok(true) if it was there already, Ok(false) if it came; Err if it
/// wouldn't (no input sent).
pub(crate) fn focus(window: HWND) -> Result<bool, String> {
    if in_front(window) {
        return Ok(true);
    }
    // SAFETY: plain window calls; the thread input attached here is detached again before the next attempt.
    unsafe {
        let me = GetCurrentThreadId();
        for attempt in 0..6u64 {
            if attempt > 0 {
                // PowerToys' trick: an empty mouse input (no move, no button) makes quen the source of the last input,
                // which lifts the foreground lock without a keystroke to another window.
                let empty = INPUT {
                    r#type: INPUT_MOUSE,
                    ..Default::default()
                };
                SendInput(&[empty], size_of::<INPUT>() as i32);
            }
            let front = GetForegroundWindow();
            let thread = if front.is_invalid() {
                0
            } else {
                GetWindowThreadProcessId(front, None)
            };
            let attached =
                thread != 0 && thread != me && AttachThreadInput(me, thread, true).as_bool();
            let _ = BringWindowToTop(window);
            let _ = SetForegroundWindow(window);
            if attached {
                let _ = AttachThreadInput(me, thread, false);
            }
            sleep(Duration::from_millis(50 + 50 * attempt));
            if in_front(window) {
                return Ok(false);
            }
        }
    }
    Err("the game's window would not come to the front; no input sent".into())
}

/// Why a plan stopped part-way, and how many keys went out before it did.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct Stopped {
    pub(crate) why: String,
    pub(crate) keys: usize,
}

/// Sends `plan` to `window`. The keys between two sleeps go out as one SendInput call (a chord: nothing of the user's or
/// another program's input comes between them; a console line's keys are `CHAR_MS` apart); before each such run, and
/// right after it, it checks
/// that the window is in front, and before it that `stop` (a cancel) isn't set; a sleep ends early on `stop`. On
/// either, or a failed SendInput, it sends nothing more but key-ups for the keys it holds down, last first (no key stays
/// down, in whatever window is in front), and stops.
pub(crate) fn send(window: HWND, plan: &[Event], stop: &dyn Fn() -> bool) -> Result<(), Stopped> {
    let mut held: Vec<u16> = Vec::new();
    let mut keys = 0;
    let mut at = 0;
    while at < plan.len() {
        if let Event::Sleep { ms, .. } = plan[at] {
            let end = Instant::now() + Duration::from_millis(ms);
            while !stop() && Instant::now() < end {
                sleep((end - Instant::now()).min(Duration::from_millis(50)));
            }
            at += 1;
            continue;
        }
        let run: Vec<(u16, bool)> = plan[at..]
            .iter()
            .map_while(|e| match e {
                Event::Key { sc, up, .. } => Some((*sc, *up)),
                Event::Sleep { .. } => None,
            })
            .collect();
        let mut why = if stop() {
            Some("stopped (a cancel, or quen shutting down)".to_string())
        } else if !in_front(window) {
            Some("the game lost the foreground".to_string())
        } else {
            None
        };
        let mut went = 0;
        if why.is_none() {
            let out = send_keys(&run);
            went = out.as_ref().map_or_else(|(n, _)| *n, |()| run.len());
            why = out.err().map(|(_, e)| e).or_else(|| {
                (!in_front(window))
                    .then(|| "the game lost the foreground as its keys went out".into())
            });
        }
        for &(sc, up) in &run[..went] {
            keys += 1;
            if !up {
                held.push(sc);
            } else if let Some(i) = held.iter().rposition(|&h| h == sc) {
                held.remove(i);
            }
        }
        if let Some(why) = why {
            let _ = send_keys(&held.iter().rev().map(|&sc| (sc, true)).collect::<Vec<_>>());
            let next = plan[at + went..]
                .iter()
                .find(|e| matches!(e, Event::Key { .. }))
                .map_or("the end".into(), describe);
            let why = format!("{why} before `{next}`; {keys} keys were sent, none is left down");
            return Err(Stopped { why, keys });
        }
        at += run.len();
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Key events by scancode, marked as quen's, in one SendInput call. Err: how many went out, and why the rest didn't.
fn send_keys(keys: &[(u16, bool)]) -> Result<(), (usize, String)> {
    let inputs: Vec<INPUT> = keys
        .iter()
        .map(|&(sc, up)| {
            let mut flags = KEYEVENTF_SCANCODE;
            if sc > 0xFF {
                flags |= KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY;
            }
            if up {
                flags |= KEYEVENTF_KEYUP;
            }
            let ki = KEYBDINPUT {
                wVk: VIRTUAL_KEY(0),
                wScan: sc & 0xFF,
                dwFlags: flags,
                time: 0,
                dwExtraInfo: MARK,
            };
            INPUT {
                r#type: INPUT_KEYBOARD,
                Anonymous: INPUT_0 { ki },
            }
        })
        .collect();
    if inputs.is_empty() {
        return Ok(());
    }
    // SAFETY: fully initialised INPUTs of the size passed.
    let went = unsafe { SendInput(&inputs, size_of::<INPUT>() as i32) } as usize;
    if went != inputs.len() {
        let e = io::Error::last_os_error();
        return Err((
            went,
            format!("SendInput sent {went} of {}: {e}", inputs.len()),
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use quen_core::input::{console_line, plan};
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicIsize, AtomicU32, Ordering};
    use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard, mpsc};
    use std::thread;
```
