```rs
                .unwrap()
                .contains("is not a file"),
            "{missing}"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            missing["needs"][0]["dependency"],
            crate::doctor::PRESENTMON.name,
            "{missing}"
        );
        fake_presentmon(&fx);
        let out = fx.run(
            "measure_presentmon",
            json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "base", "secs": 3, "presentmon_flags": ["--track_pc_latency"]}),
        );
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        assert!(
            out["presentmon"]
                .as_str()
                .unwrap()
                .ends_with("PresentMon.exe"),
            "{out}"
        );
        let csv = fx
            .dir
            .join("data")
            .join("captures")
            .join("s1")
            .join("base.csv");
        assert!(csv.is_file());
        // By the game's pid (the dummy game's, the only process in the fixture's job), in quen's own trace session.
        let pid = fx.job.pids().unwrap()[0].to_string();
        let csv_arg = csv.display().to_string();
        let want = [
            "--process_id",
            &pid,
            "--timed",
            "3",
            "--terminate_after_timed",
            "--output_file",
            &csv_arg,
            "--no_console_stats",
            "--session_name",
            "quen",
            "--stop_existing_session",
            "--track_pc_latency",
        ];
        let argv = fs::read_to_string(fx.dir.join("harness/argv.txt")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(argv.lines().collect::<Vec<_>>(), want);
        assert_eq!(out["window"]["frame_ms"]["mean"], 20.0);
        assert_eq!(out["window"]["present_mode"], "Hardware: Independent Flip");
        assert_eq!(out["ledger"]["measurements"].as_array().unwrap().len(), 12);
        let db =
            quen_core::ledger::Ledger::open_readonly(fx.dir.join("data/state/quen.db")).unwrap();
        let sql = "SELECT DISTINCT boot_id FROM measurements";
        let boots = db.query(sql, &[], Duration::from_secs(5)).unwrap().rows;
        assert_eq!(boots, [[json!(1)]], "the rows name the live session's boot");
        // Feature tests 1: the CSV relative to the capture root, the quiet check on the note and on the boot.
        let sql = "SELECT DISTINCT note FROM measurements";
        let notes = db.query(sql, &[], Duration::from_secs(5)).unwrap().rows;
        let note = notes[0][0].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(
            note.starts_with("s1/base.csv; Hardware: Independent Flip; ")
                && (note.ends_with("; a quiet machine") || note.contains("; warned: ")),
            "{note}"
        );
        let sql = "SELECT json_type(busy_with) FROM boots WHERE id = 1";
        let busy = db.query(sql, &[], Duration::from_secs(5)).unwrap().rows;
        assert_eq!(busy, [[json!("array")]]);
        assert_eq!(fx.calls(), ["presentmon base.csv 3"]);
        let again = fx.run("measure_presentmon", json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "base"}));
        assert_eq!(again["refused"], true, "{again}");
        let flag = json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "other", "presentmon_flags": ["--process_name", "x.exe"]});
        let flag = fx.run("measure_presentmon", flag);
        assert_eq!(flag["refused"], true, "{flag}");
        assert_eq!(fx.calls().len(), 1, "nothing ran for the refusals");
        fs::write(fx.dir.join("harness/exit.txt"), "5").unwrap();
        let failed = fx.run("measure_presentmon", json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "fail"}));
        let reason = failed["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
        assert_eq!(failed["ok"], false, "{failed}");
        assert!(
            reason.contains("PresentMon exit 5")
                && !reason.contains("the fake failed")
                && failed["presentmon_said"] == "error: the fake failed",
            "{failed}"
        );

        let db = Ledger::open_readonly(fx.dir.join("data/state/quen.db")).unwrap();
        let rows = db
            .query(
                "SELECT metric, value, state_label, method_family, tag FROM measurements WHERE metric = 'frame_ms_mean'",
                &[],
                Duration::from_secs(5),
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            rows.rows,
            [[
                json!("frame_ms_mean"),
                json!(20.0),
                json!("base"),
                json!("presentmon"),
                json!("M")
            ]]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn ab_alternates_restores_and_gives_the_verdict() {
        let fx = Fake::new("ab");
        fake_presentmon(&fx);
        // Feature tests 1: an ASI export that can't be called refuses before window 1, nothing run.
        let mut asi = ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A", "B"]));
        asi["states"][0]["actions"] = json!([{"asi": "W3NoSuch.asi", "set_mode": 0}]);
        asi["states"][1]["actions"] = json!([{"asi": "W3NoSuch.asi", "set_mode": 1}]);
        let refused = fx.run("measure_ab", asi);
        assert_eq!(refused["refused"], true, "{refused}");
        assert!(fx.calls().is_empty(), "{:?}", fx.calls());
        // A cvar the game hasn't, or a key token quen doesn't know, is refused before window 1 too.
        let mut typo = ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A", "B"]));
        typo["states"][0]["actions"][0]["cvar"] = json!("QuenTest/Typo");
        typo["states"][1]["actions"][0]["cvar"] = json!("QuenTest/Typo");
        let mut key = ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A", "B"]));
        key["states"][1]["actions"][1]["keys"] = json!(["nokey"]);
        for args in [typo, key] {
            let refused = fx.run("measure_ab", args.clone());
            assert_eq!(refused["refused"], true, "{args}: {refused}");
        }
        assert!(fx.calls().is_empty(), "{:?}", fx.calls());
        assert!(cvar_writes(&fx).is_empty());
        let out = fx.run("measure_ab", ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A", "B"])));
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["verdict"], "outside drift");
        assert_eq!(out["diff_ms"], 3.0);
        assert_eq!(out["drift_ms"]["A"], 0.0);
        let means: Vec<f64> = out["states"]
            .as_array()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .map(|w| w["frame_ms"]["mean"].as_f64().unwrap())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(means, [20.0, 23.0, 20.0, 23.0]);
        // Feature tests 4: each window's UTC times, in order, to cut another tool's capture by (ISO times sort as text).
        let times: Vec<String> = out["states"]
            .as_array()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|w| {
                ["apply", "settled", "presentmon_start", "presentmon_stop"]
                    .map(|k| w["utc"][k].clone())
            })
            .map(|t| t.as_str().unwrap().to_owned())
            .collect();
        assert!(times.len() == 16 && times.is_sorted(), "{times:?}");
        assert!(times[0].len() == 24 && times[0].ends_with('Z'), "{times:?}");
        assert_eq!(out["ledger"]["measurements"].as_array().unwrap().len(), 48);
        // Feature tests 1: every row names what each state did and the verdict.
        let db = Ledger::open_readonly(fx.dir.join("data/state/quen.db")).unwrap();
        let sql = "SELECT note FROM measurements WHERE metric = 'frame_ms_mean' ORDER BY id";
        let notes = db.query(sql, &[], Duration::from_secs(5)).unwrap().rows;
        let note = notes[1][0].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(
            note.starts_with("s1/run_2B.csv; Hardware: Independent Flip; A: cvar QuenTest/FrameMs set 20, keys f9; B: cvar QuenTest/FrameMs set 23, keys f9; verdict {")
                && note.contains("\"verdict\":\"outside drift\""),
            "{note}"
        );
        // The toggle runs on each switch only, never before the first window; the default comes back at the end, and
        // the toggle goes back to the first state. The first set finds the default already there: no write.
        assert_eq!(
            fx.calls(),
            [
                "presentmon run_1A.csv 1",
                "keys f9",
                "presentmon run_2B.csv 1",
                "keys f9",
                "presentmon run_3A.csv 1",
                "keys f9",
                "presentmon run_4B.csv 1",
                "keys f9",
            ]
        );
        let writes: Vec<String> = cvar_writes(&fx)
            .iter()
            .map(|w| w[..w.find(" at ").unwrap()].into())
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(
            writes,
            [
                "cvar QuenTest/FrameMs set 23",
                "cvar QuenTest/FrameMs set 20",
                "cvar QuenTest/FrameMs set 23",
                "cvar QuenTest/FrameMs back to its value before quen's first write",
            ]
        );
        let now = fx.run(
            "game_cvar",
            json!({"token": "tok", "name": "QuenTest/FrameMs"}),
        );
        assert_eq!(now["var"]["live"], 20.0, "{now}");
        // No loaded game in quen's state, so no world fingerprint: the run went on, and says so.
        let unread = out["drift_guard"][0].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
        assert!(unread.starts_with("world fingerprint unread: "), "{out}");
        assert!(
            note.contains(&format!("; drift guard: {unread}; ")),
            "{note}"
        );
    }

    /// Finding 73: the world fingerprint before and after each window, outside it; a read of one state that differs from
    /// that state's first is a drift_guard note, on the result and every row, the verdict as it was.
    #[test]
    fn ab_notes_a_world_that_changed_within_a_state() {
        use std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize;
        let fx = served("abguard");
        fake_presentmon(&fx);
        // The player stands at the origin for the first four world reads (windows 1 and 2), then 5 m off.
        let worlds = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let answer = Box::new(move |r: &Request| {
            let data = match r.verb {
                Verb::WorldGet {} => {
                    let x = if worlds.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) < 4 {
                        0
                    } else {
                        5
                    };
                    json!({"player": {"pos": [x, 0, 0], "heading": 0}, "weather": "WT_Clear"})
                }
                Verb::CamGet {} => json!({"pos": [0, -3, 2], "rot": [0, 0, 0], "fov": 60}),
                Verb::WorldActors { .. } => json!({"found": 9, "actors": []}),
                _ => panic!("{:?}", r.verb),
            };
            vec![reply(r.id, true, "read", Some(data))]
        });
        let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let server = fake_game_until(&token(&fx), answer, stop.clone());
        let mut args = ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A", "B"]));
        args["states"][0]["actions"] = json!([{"cvar": "QuenTest/FrameMs", "set": 20}]);
        args["states"][1]["actions"] = json!([{"cvar": "QuenTest/FrameMs", "set": 23}]);
        let out = fx.run("measure_ab", args);
        stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
        let reads: Vec<Verb> = server.join().unwrap().into_iter().map(|r| r.verb).collect();
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["verdict"], "outside drift", "{out}");
        // Per window, before and after it: world.get, cam.get, then the actors within 30 m (their count).
        let actors = Verb::WorldActors {
            radius: 30.0,
            max: 1,
            tag: None,
            class: None,
        };
        assert_eq!(reads.len(), 4 * 2 * 3, "{reads:?}");
        assert_eq!(reads[..3], [Verb::WorldGet {}, Verb::CamGet {}, actors]);
        assert_eq!(out["states"][0]["world"]["before"]["actors"], 9, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(
            out["drift_guard"],
            json!([
                "window 3 (A) before differs from window 1 (A) before: the player moved 5.00 m",
                "window 4 (B) before differs from window 2 (B) before: the player moved 5.00 m"
            ]),
            "{out}"
        );
        let sql = "SELECT note FROM measurements WHERE metric = 'frame_ms_mean' ORDER BY id";
        let note = rows(&fx, sql)[3][0].as_str().unwrap().to_owned();
        assert!(
            note.contains("; drift guard: window 3 (A) before differs from window 1 (A) before: "),
            "{note}"
        );
    }

    /// Finding 59: console lines toggle like keys, each followed by its script-log line; one that doesn't show (only
    /// an older line holds the text) fails the run.
    #[test]
    fn ab_switches_by_console_line_and_checks_the_script_log() {
        let fx = Fake::new("abconsole");
        fake_presentmon(&fx);
        fs::write(
            fx.dir.join("game/bin/x64_dx12/W3QuenState.log"),
            "push flags=1\n",
        )
        .unwrap();
        let log = fx.dir.join("docs").join(crate::w3::SCRIPTS_LOG);
        fs::write(&log, "[NpcAvoid] on\r\n").unwrap();
        let (to, mut on) = (log.clone(), false);
        fx.on_input(move |what| {
            assert_eq!(what, "console npcavoid()");
            on = !on;
            let mut f = fs::OpenOptions::new().append(true).open(&to).unwrap();
            use std::io::Write as _;
            write!(f, "[npcavoid] aura {}\r\n", if on { "on" } else { "off" }).unwrap();
            Ok(())
        });
        let state = |label, word| {
            json!({"label": label, "actions": [
                {"console": "npcavoid()", "expect_log": {"channel": "NpcAvoid", "contains": format!("aura {word}")}}
            ]})
        };
        let args = json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "con", "settle": 0, "secs": 1,
                          "states": [state("A", "off"), state("B", "on")]});
        let out = fx.run("measure_ab", args.clone());
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        // On each switch, and once more at the end to leave the first state's.
        let console = "console npcavoid()";
        let want = [
            "presentmon con_1A.csv 1",
            console,
            "presentmon con_2B.csv 1",
            console,
        ];
        let want = [
            &want[..],
            &[
                "presentmon con_3A.csv 1",
                console,
                "presentmon con_4B.csv 1",
                console,
            ],
        ]
        .concat();
        assert_eq!(fx.calls(), want);
        let db = Ledger::open_readonly(fx.dir.join("data/state/quen.db")).unwrap();
        let sql = "SELECT note FROM measurements WHERE metric = 'frame_ms_mean' ORDER BY id";
        let notes = db.query(sql, &[], Duration::from_secs(5)).unwrap().rows;
        let note = notes[0][0].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(
            note.contains("A: console npcavoid() expect [NpcAvoid] \"aura off\"; B: "),
            "{note}"
        );
        // A line that doesn't reach the log: window 2 fails, the old lines don't count, nothing to toggle back.
        fx.on_input(|_| Ok(()));
        let mut args = args;
        args["tag"] = json!("none");
        let out = fx.run("measure_ab", args);
        let reason = out["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
        assert!(
            out["ok"] == false
                && reason.contains(
                    "window 2 (B): console npcavoid(): no new [NpcAvoid] line holding \"aura on\""
                ),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert_eq!(fx.calls().len(), want.len() + 2, "{:?}", fx.calls());
        // Refused before anything: a bad line, a bad expect_log, a console line in one state only.
        let bad = |actions_a: Value| {
            json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "bad", "settle": 0, "secs": 1,
                   "states": [{"label": "A", "actions": actions_a}, state("B", "on")]})
        };
        for actions in [
            json!([{"console": "say(\"hi\")"}]),
            json!([{"console": "npcavoid()", "expect_log": {"channel": "Npc Avoid", "contains": "x"}}]),
            json!([{"console": "npcavoid()", "expect_log": {"channel": "NpcAvoid", "contains": ""}}]),
            json!([{"console": "npcavoid()", "expect_log": {"channel": "NpcAvoid", "contains": "x", "more": 1}}]),
            json!([]),
        ] {
            let out = fx.run("measure_ab", bad(actions.clone()));
            assert_eq!(out["refused"], true, "{actions}: {out}");
        }
        assert_eq!(fx.calls().len(), want.len() + 2, "ran for a refusal");
    }

    #[test]
    fn ab_stops_on_another_present_mode_and_still_restores() {
        let fx = Fake::new("abmode");
        fake_presentmon(&fx);
        fs::write(fx.dir.join("harness/mode_after.txt"), "Composed: Flip").unwrap();
        let mut args = ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "B", "A"]));
        args["states"][0]["actions"] = json!([{"cvar": "QuenTest/FrameMs", "set": 20}]);
        args["states"][1]["actions"] = json!([{"cvar": "QuenTest/FrameMs", "set": 23}]);
        let out = fx.run("measure_ab", args);
        assert_eq!(

                .as_str()
                .unwrap()
                .contains("window 2 (B) ran in PresentMode"),

        );

            "{last}"
        );
    }

    /// Finding 88: no window measures a paused world. quen's state showing the game's menu before a window refuses the
    /// call when the game can't be brought back (the stand-in has no window), nothing measured; the menu during a window
    /// stops measure_ab there, its rows' world paused and the drift guard saying so; the run still restores.
    #[test]
    fn a_menu_refuses_or_stops_the_measuring() {
        let fx = Fake::new("abmenu");
        fake_presentmon(&fx);
        let log = fx.dir.join("game/bin/x64_dx12/W3QuenState.log");
        fs::write(
            &log,
            "100 push=1 flags=2049
",
        )
        .unwrap();
        let pm = fx.run("measure_presentmon", json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "m"}));
        let mut ab = ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A", "B"]));
        ab["states"][0]["actions"] = json!([{"cvar": "QuenTest/FrameMs", "set": 20}]);
        ab["states"][1]["actions"] = json!([{"cvar": "QuenTest/FrameMs", "set": 23}]);
        let refused = fx.run("measure_ab", ab.clone());
        for out in [&pm, &refused] {
            let reason = out["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
            assert!(
                out["refused"] == true
                    && reason.contains("shows the game's menu")
                    && reason.ends_with("nothing measured"),
                "{out}"
            );
        }
        assert!(fx.calls().is_empty(), "{:?}", fx.calls());
        assert!(cvar_writes(&fx).is_empty());
        // Photo mode's own menu bit doesn't count.
        fs::write(
            &log,
            "100 push=1 flags=2177
",
        )
        .unwrap();
        let out = fx.run("measure_ab", ab.clone());
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        // Gameplay, then the menu during window 2 (a push at the furthest tick: after the window began).
        fs::write(
            &log,
            "100 push=1 flags=1
",
        )
        .unwrap();
        let push = format!(
            "menu_2B.csv {} push=2 flags=2049
",
            u64::MAX
        );
        fs::write(fx.dir.join("harness/menu.txt"), push).unwrap();
        ab["tag"] = json!("menu");
        let out = fx.run("measure_ab", ab);
        let reason = out["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
        assert!(
            out["ok"] == false
                && reason.starts_with("window 2 (B): quen's state showed the game's menu"),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert_eq!(out["states"][1]["menu_during"], true, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["restored"][0]["ok"], true, "{out}");
        let guard = out["drift_guard"].to_string();
        assert!(
            guard.contains(
                "window 2 (B): quen's state showed the game's menu during it, a paused world"
            ),
            "{out}"
        );
        let sql = "SELECT DISTINCT state_label, world FROM measurements WHERE run_id = 's1-menu' ORDER BY 1";
        assert_eq!(
            rows(&fx, sql),
            [[json!("A"), json!("live")], [json!("B"), json!("paused")]]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn ab_refuses_bad_runs_before_acting() {
        let fx = Fake::new("abrefuse");
        let mut bad = vec![
            ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A"])),
            ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "C", "A", "B"])),
            ab_args(json!([
                "A", "A", "B", "B", "A", "B", "A", "B", "A", "B", "A", "B", "A"
            ])),
        ];
        let mut other_cvar = ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A", "B"]));
        other_cvar["states"][0]["actions"] = json!([{"cvar": "QuenTest/Other", "set": 1}]);
        bad.push(other_cvar);
        // A has no keys of its own, so nothing would press them back.
        let mut toggles = ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A", "B"]));
        toggles["states"][0]["actions"] = json!([{"cvar": "QuenTest/FrameMs", "set": 20}]);
        bad.push(toggles);
        let mut same = ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A", "B"]));
        same["states"][1]["label"] = json!("A");
        bad.push(same);
        let mut three = ab_args(Value::Null);
        three.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("order");
        three["states"]
            .as_array_mut()
            .unwrap()
            .push(json!({"label": "C", "actions": []}));
        bad.push(three);
        let mut file = ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A", "B"]));
        file["tag"] = json!("../x");
        bad.push(file);
        // A good run, but no PresentMon where the config says; and a flag quen doesn't pass on.
        bad.push(ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A", "B"])));
        let mut flags = ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A", "B"]));
        flags["presentmon_flags"] = json!(["--output_stdout"]);
        bad.push(flags);
        for args in bad {
            let out = fx.run("measure_ab", args.clone());
            assert_eq!(out["refused"], true, "{args}: {out}");
        }
        assert!(fx.calls().is_empty(), "{:?}", fx.calls());
        assert!(cvar_writes(&fx).is_empty());
    }

    /// Feature tests 2b: an ASI whose SetMode was rejected changed nothing, yet the restore called it again and failed
    /// with the same long reason. An ASI that accepted no mode in the run is skipped; one that did is restored.
    #[test]
    fn the_restore_skips_an_asi_that_took_no_mode() {
        let fx = Fake::new("abskip");
        let session = fx.session();
        let mut call = session.call(crate::mcp::Conn::nobody(), Value::Null, None);
        let cx = ctx(&session, &json!({"token": "tok"}), &[]).unwrap();
        let mut args = ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A", "B"]));
        args["states"][0]["actions"] = json!([{"asi": "W3NoSuch.asi", "set_mode": 0}]);
        args["states"][1]["actions"] = json!([{"asi": "W3NoSuch.asi", "set_mode": 1}]);
        let run = Run::parse(&args).unwrap();
        let skipped = restore(&cx, &mut call, &run, 0, &[]);
        assert_eq!(
            (skipped[0]["ok"].clone(), skipped[0]["skipped"].is_string()),
            (json!(true), true),
            "{skipped:?}"
        );
        let tried = restore(&cx, &mut call, &run, 0, &[switch_of("W3NoSuch.asi", None)]);
        assert_eq!(tried[0]["ok"], false, "{tried:?}");
    }

    /// A stand-in game for traces, until the flag is set: world.get answers the player standing at the origin, cam.get a
    /// camera behind him, and world.actors one walker (id 9) passing along y = 0.5 at 1 m/s, from x = -1 at the first
    /// read.
    fn tracing(fx: &Fake) -> (std::thread::JoinHandle<Vec<Request>>, Arc<AtomicBool>) {
        let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let start = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
        let answer = Box::new(move |r: &Request| {
            let data = match r.verb {
                Verb::WorldGet {} => {
                    json!({"player": {"pos": [0, 0, 0], "heading": 0}, "weather": "WT_Clear"})
                }
                Verb::CamGet {} => json!({"pos": [0, -3, 2], "rot": [0, 0, 0], "fov": 60}),
                Verb::WorldActors { .. } => {
                    let x = -1.0 + start.get_or_init(Instant::now).elapsed().as_secs_f64();
                    json!({"found": 1, "actors": [{"id": 9, "pos": [x, 0.5, 0], "heading": -90,
                        "velocity": [1, 0, 0], "entity": "walker", "actor": true}]})
                }
                _ => panic!("{:?}", r.verb),
            };
            vec![reply(r.id, true, "read", Some(data))]
        });
        (fake_game_until(&token(fx), answer, stop.clone()), stop)
    }

    fn rows(fx: &Fake, sql: &str) -> Vec<Vec<Value>> {
        let db = Ledger::open_readonly(fx.dir.join("data/state/quen.db")).unwrap();
        db.query(sql, &[], Duration::from_secs(5)).unwrap().rows
    }

    /// Finding 57: a trace window samples the player and the actors, writes its CSV with a captures row, its metrics as
    /// game_state rows citing it, and its sampler on the boot.
    #[test]
    fn a_trace_window_records_its_csv_metrics_and_sampler() {
        let fx = served("trace");
        for bad in [
            json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "x", "trace": {"hz": 11}}),
            json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "x", "trace": {"every": 1}}),
            json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "x", "trace": {"class": "C Actor"}}),
            json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "../x"}),
            json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "x", "secs": 0}),
        ] {
            let out = fx.run("measure_trace", bad.clone());
            assert_eq!(out["refused"], true, "{bad}: {out}");
        }
        let (server, stop) = tracing(&fx);
        let out = fx.run(
            "measure_trace",
            json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "walk", "secs": 2}),
        );
        stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
        let reads = server.join().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        let m = &out["window"]["trace"]["metrics"];
        assert_eq!(
            (m["passes"].clone(), m["samples"].clone()),
            (json!(1), json!(21)),
            "{out}"
        );
        let closest = m["closest_m_min"].as_f64().unwrap();
        assert!((0.5..0.6).contains(&closest), "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["budget"]["cost_ms_per_frame"], "unmeasured", "{out}");
        assert_eq!(
            out["sampler"],
            "actor_trace 10 Hz r8 max20 ref player contact 0.75"
        );
        // Per sample world.get, then world.actors with the default radius and max.
        assert_eq!(reads.len(), 42);
        assert_eq!(reads[0].verb, Verb::WorldGet {});
        let actors = Verb::WorldActors {
            radius: 8.0,
            max: 20,
            tag: None,
            class: None,
        };
        assert_eq!(reads[1].verb, actors);
        let csv = fx.dir.join("data/captures/s1/walk-trace.csv");
        let text = fs::read_to_string(&csv).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(text.lines().count(), 1 + 2 * 21, "{text}");
        let captures = rows(&fx, "SELECT id, path, kind, method FROM captures");
        assert_eq!(
            captures,
            [[
                json!(1),
                json!("s1/walk-trace.csv"),
                json!("csv"),
                json!("actor_trace")
            ]]
        );
        let sql =

        assert_eq!(
            rows(&fx, sql),

            note.starts_with(

        );

                Value::Null
            ]]

        let again = fx.run("measure_trace", json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "walk"}));
        assert_eq!(again["refused"], true, "{again}");
    }

    /// The game's replies to the measuring line, as modQuen gives them: shown, then up already.
    fn notices() -> impl Fn(&Request) -> &'static str + Send {
        let sent = AtomicBool::new(false);
        move |r| match r.verb {
            Verb::Notice { .. } if sent.swap(true, Ordering::SeqCst) => status::ALREADY,
            _ => "notice shown",
        }
    }

    /// The status line is down before every window: the game gets the hide before PresentMon starts, PresentMon starts
    /// HIDE_WAIT or more after the game's reply, and the result carries the budget line and the measuring state's reply.
    #[test]
    fn the_status_line_is_down_half_a_second_before_a_window() {
        let fx = served("pm-status");
        fake_presentmon(&fx);
        fx.shared.set_hands(Some(Hands::Agent));
        let calls = fx.dir.join("harness/calls.txt");
        let hidden = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None));
        let (seen, started) = (hidden.clone(), calls.clone());
        let notice = notices();
        let answer = Box::new(move |r: &Request| {
            if r.verb == (Verb::NoticeHide {}) {
                assert!(!started.exists(), "a window started before the hide");
                *seen.lock().unwrap() = Some(SystemTime::now());
            }
            vec![reply(r.id, true, notice(r), None)]
        });
        let server = fake_game(&token(&fx), 3, answer);
        let args = json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "st", "secs": 1});
        let out = fx.run("measure_presentmon", args);
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        let sent: Vec<Verb> = server.join().unwrap().into_iter().map(|r| r.verb).collect();
        assert!(
            matches!(
                sent[..],
                [
                    Verb::Notice { .. },
                    Verb::Notice { .. },
                    Verb::NoticeHide {}
                ]
            ),
            "the line, again until the game says it is up, then its hide: {sent:?}"
        );
        let hid = hidden.lock().unwrap().expect("hidden");
        let window = fs::metadata(&calls).unwrap().modified().unwrap();
        let after = window.duration_since(hid).unwrap();
        assert!(
            after >= status::HIDE_WAIT,
            "PresentMon started {after:?} after the hide"
        );
        assert_eq!(out["status"], "notice shown", "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["indicator"]["shown_before"], "measuring", "{out}");
        assert!(
            out["timing_s"]["status_hide"].as_f64().unwrap() >= 0.5,
            "{out}"
        );
    }

    /// The owner, 2026-10-22: before each A/B window the line names its state, window 1's in the measuring line (whose
    /// estimate counts the later lines' waits), each later one after the window before; every one is up NEXT_SHOWN or
    /// more from the game's answer, and taken down before its window starts.
    #[test]
    fn each_ab_window_s_state_is_named_before_its_hide() {
        let fx = served("ab-labels");
        fake_presentmon(&fx);
        fx.shared.set_hands(Some(Hands::Agent));
        let calls = fx.dir.join("harness/calls.txt");
        // Per notice and hide: its text ("hide"), the windows started by then, when the game had it.
        let seen = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let log = seen.clone();
        let up = std::sync::Mutex::new(None);
        let answer = Box::new(move |r: &Request| {
            let windows = fs::read_to_string(&calls).map_or(0, |c| c.lines().count());
            let mut up = up.lock().unwrap();
            let (what, says) = match &r.verb {
                Verb::Notice { text, .. } if up.as_ref() == Some(text) => {
                    (text.clone(), status::ALREADY)
                }
                Verb::Notice { text, .. } => {
                    *up = Some(text.clone());
                    (text.clone(), "notice shown")
                }
                Verb::NoticeHide {} => {
                    *up = None;
                    ("hide".into(), "done")
                }
                _ => return vec![reply(r.id, true, "done", None)],
            };
            log.lock().unwrap().push((what, windows, Instant::now()));
            vec![reply(r.id, true, says, None)]
        });
        let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let server = fake_game_until(&token(&fx), answer, stop.clone());
        let mut args = ab_args(json!(["A", "B", "A", "B"]));
        args["states"][0]["actions"] = json!([{"cvar": "QuenTest/FrameMs", "set": 20}]);
        args["states"][1]["actions"] = json!([{"cvar": "QuenTest/FrameMs", "set": 23}]);
        let out = fx.run("measure_ab", args);
        stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
        server.join().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        // 4 windows of 0 + 1 + 0.5 + 0.5 s, and 3 lines of 0.5 + 3 s: 18.5.
        let first = "quen: measuring for about 19 s. Next: A (window 1 of 4). Hands off.";
        let next =
            |l: &str, n: usize| format!("quen: measuring. Next: {l} (window {n} of 4). Hands off.");
        let seen = seen.lock().unwrap();
        let mut want = Vec::new();
        for (n, text) in [
            (0, first.to_string()),
            (1, next("B", 2)),
            (2, next("A", 3)),
            (3, next("B", 4)),
        ] {
            want.extend([(text.clone(), n), (text, n), ("hide".to_string(), n)]);
        }
        let got: Vec<(String, usize)> = seen.iter().map(|(w, n, _)| (w.clone(), *n)).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            got, want,
            "each window's line, then its hide, then the window"
        );
        for k in [1, 2, 3] {
            let up = seen[3 * k + 2].2 - seen[3 * k + 1].2;
            assert!(up >= status::NEXT_SHOWN, "window {}: up {up:?}", k + 1);
        }
        let label = out["timing_s"]["status_label"].as_f64().unwrap_or(-1.0);
        assert!(
            label >= 3.0 * (0.5 + 2.0),
            "three answers and waits, summed: {out}"
        );
    }

    /// The runner design's Q2 and Q4: the same trace beside PresentMon in every window, its sampler named on the frame
    /// rows and in the verdict, per metric a behaviour verdict; or the trace alone, without PresentMon at all.
    /// Finding 79: job_cancel's flag (a cancel of a `wait: false` call: it sets the flag the session thread's call
    /// checks) during the wait after the status line's hide starts no window, and one during the window kills
    /// PresentMon; both fail and say when. The live check saw the window start 3 s after the notice and run on to a
    /// plain ok.
    #[test]
    fn a_cancel_in_the_hide_wait_or_the_window_measures_nothing() {
        // The cancel waits for an event, not a fixed delay: a slow runner (CI's Windows, busy building) reached the
        // hide wait after a 300 ms cancel had already been dropped, and the window then measured.
        let cancel_when = |fx: &Fake, ready: &(dyn Fn() -> bool + Sync), tool, args: Value| {
            std::thread::scope(|s| {
                s.spawn(|| {
                    let t = Instant::now();
                    while !ready() && t.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(10) {
                        sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));
                    }
                    fx.shared.cancel(0, &Value::Null);
                });
                let t = Instant::now();
                (fx.run(tool, args), t.elapsed())
            })
        };
        let fx = served("pmcancel-gap");
        fake_presentmon(&fx);
        fx.shared.set_hands(Some(Hands::Agent));
        let hid = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
        let seen = hid.clone();
        let says = notices();
        let notice = Box::new(move |r: &Request| {
            if matches!(r.verb, Verb::NoticeHide {}) {
                seen.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
            }
            vec![reply(r.id, true, says(r), None)]
        });
        let server = fake_game(&token(&fx), 3, notice);
        let args = json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "gap", "secs": 30});
        let in_hide_wait = || hid.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
        let (out, took) = cancel_when(&fx, &in_hide_wait, "measure_presentmon", args);
        let sent: Vec<Verb> = server.join().unwrap().into_iter().map(|r| r.verb).collect();
        assert!(
            matches!(
                sent[..],
                [
                    Verb::Notice { .. },
                    Verb::Notice { .. },
                    Verb::NoticeHide {}
                ]
            ),
            "the line, again until the game says it is up, then its hide: {sent:?}"
        );
        let reason = out["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
        assert!(
            out["ok"] == false
                && reason.starts_with(
                    "the call was cancelled during the 0.5 s wait for quen's line in the game to be gone"
                ),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert!(fx.calls().is_empty(), "a window started: {:?}", fx.calls());
        assert!(
            took < status::MEASURING_SHOWN + Duration::from_secs(2),
            "the measuring line's wait and the hide's, no window: {took:?}"
        );
        // During the window: PresentMon killed, no rows.
        let fx = served("pmcancel-window");
        fake_presentmon(&fx);
        fs::write(fx.dir.join("harness/sleep.txt"), "20000").unwrap();
        let args = json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "mid", "secs": 10});
        let in_window = || !fx.calls().is_empty();
        let (out, took) = cancel_when(&fx, &in_window, "measure_presentmon", args);
        let reason = out["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
        assert!(
            out["ok"] == false
                && reason.starts_with("the call was cancelled ")
                && reason.contains("s into the 10 s window: PresentMon was killed"),
            "{out}"
        );
        assert!(took < Duration::from_secs(5), "{took:?}");
        assert_eq!(fx.calls(), ["presentmon mid.csv 10"]);
        let db = Ledger::open_readonly(fx.dir.join("data/state/quen.db")).unwrap();
        let none = db
            .query(
                "SELECT count(*) FROM measurements",
                &[],
                Duration::from_secs(5),
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(none.rows, [[json!(0)]]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ab_traces_every_window_beside_or_instead_of_presentmon() {
        let fx = served("abtrace");

        let (server, stop) = tracing(&fx);

        let mut only = json!({"token": "tok", "tag": "cost", "settle": 0, "secs": 1, "trace": {"max": 4},

    #[test]
    fn busy_images_are_named_once_any_case() {
        let running = [
            (1, "CARGO.EXE".to_string()),
            (2, "cargo.exe".into()),

        ];

    /// Only the PresentMon quen starts is a measurement, by its full path: Intel's service's and AMD's overlay's copies,
    /// and a copy of the same exe elsewhere, aren't (2026-10-22: two of them blocked capture_clean). Without a
    /// PresentMon quen can run, no process is looked at. The process lists are synthetic.
    #[test]
    fn only_quens_own_presentmon_is_a_measurement() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("quen-pm-running-{}", std::process::id()));
        let put = |rel: &str| {
            let path = dir.join(rel);
            fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
            fs::write(&path, "synthetic").unwrap();
            path
        };
        let exe = put(r"Intel\PresentMon\PresentMonConsoleApplication\PresentMon-2.4.1-x64.exe");
        let others = vec![
            (
                1,
                put(r"Intel\PresentMon\PresentMonService\PresentMon_x64.exe"),
            ),
            (2, put(r"WindowsApps\AMD\PresentMon-x64.exe")),
            (3, put(r"copy\PresentMon-2.4.1-x64.exe")),
            (4, dir.join(r"gone\PresentMon-2.4.1-x64.exe")),
        ];
        let config = Config {
            presentmon: Some(exe.clone()),
            ..Config::default()
        };
        let mut asked = Vec::new();
        let running = presentmon_running(&config, |name| {
            asked.push(name.to_owned());
            others.clone()
        });
        assert_eq!(
            (running, &asked[..]),
            (None, &["PresentMon-2.4.1-x64.exe".to_owned()][..])
        );
        // quen's own, its path in another case, as a process list may give it.
        let mine = PathBuf::from(exe.to_string_lossy().to_uppercase());
        let all = [others, vec![(5, mine)]].concat();
        assert_eq!(presentmon_running(&config, |_| all), Some((5, exe)));
        let config = Config {
            presentmon: Some(dir.join("nowhere.exe")),
            ..Config::default()
        };
        let running = presentmon_running(&config, |_| panic!("the processes were looked at"));
        assert_eq!(running, None);
        fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).unwrap(); // this test's own folder
    }
}
```

`crates/quen/src/mem.rs`:

```rs
//! The live-memory tools: `mem_read`, `mem_scan`, `mem_find`, `mem_follow`, `mem_walk`, `mem_regions`, `mem_patch`,
//! `mem_unpatch`, `mem_patch_instances` and `mem_unpatch_instances`, and the Windows half of quen-core's `mem`. [`Process`] reads the game through a handle with read
//! access only, on the pid from the session's job (never "the first witcher3.exe"). [`Ctx::write`] journals a planned
//! write, then makes it with a handle open for that write only. game_cvar and measure_ab's cvar actions (game.rs) go
//! through the same two. Every result ends in [`result`]: where its addresses lie, its provenance, and a big one in a
//! captures file.

use std::cmp::Reverse;
use std::ffi::c_void;
use std::fmt::Display;

use std::io;
use std::mem::{size_of, zeroed};
use std::ops::ControlFlow;

use quen_core::journal::sha256_hex;
use quen_core::ledger::{Capture, Ledger};
use quen_core::mem::{
    self, Elements, Field, Filter, Find, Image, Kind, Memory, Module, Op, Pattern, Region, Scope,
    Section, Type, Walk, Which, Write,
};

    FlushInstructionCache, ReadProcessMemory, WriteProcessMemory,
};
use windows_sys::Win32::System::Memory::{
    MEM_COMMIT, MEM_IMAGE, MEM_MAPPED, MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE,
    PAGE_GUARD, PAGE_NOACCESS, VirtualProtectEx, VirtualQueryEx,
};

    OpenProcess, PROCESS_ACCESS_RIGHTS, PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION, PROCESS_VM_OPERATION,
    PROCESS_VM_READ, PROCESS_VM_WRITE,

use crate::config::Config;

use crate::ledger::{self, INLINE_BYTES};

/// A scan or find page's hits when the call gives no `limit`.
const LIMIT: usize = 100;
/// A find hit's context bytes on each side when the call gives no `context`.
const CONTEXT: u64 = 16;
/// A scan or find page's `deadline_s` when the call gives none, and the most it takes.
const DEADLINE_S: u64 = 60;
const MAX_DEADLINE_S: u64 = 600;
/// How many of the biggest regions mem_regions names.
const LARGEST: usize = 16;

pub fn tools() -> Vec<Value> {
    let token = json!({"type": "string", "description": "the token session_launch returned"});
    let schema = |props: Value, required: &[&str]| {
        let mut props = props;
        props["token"] = token.clone();
        let mut required = required.to_vec();
        required.insert(0, "token");
        json!({"type": "object", "properties": props, "required": required, "additionalProperties": false})
    };
    let number = |what: &str| json!({"type": "string", "description": format!("{what}: a number or 0x hex")});
    let chain = |what: &str| json!({"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": format!("{what}: numbers or (-)0x hex")});
    let types = json!([
        "u8", "u16", "u32", "u64", "i32", "i64", "f32", "f64", "ptr", "bytes"
    ]);
    let ty = json!({"type": "string", "enum": types, "description": "a number's type (ptr: a u64 shown as 0x hex), or bytes (with len)"});
    let len =
        json!({"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 4096, "description": "bytes: how many"});
    let limit = json!({"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 1000, "description": "hits per page, default 100"});
    let deadline = json!({"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 600, "description": "seconds before the page stops early, default 60"});
    let sections = json!({"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "image sections: .text, .rdata, .data"});
    let regions = json!({"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "region bases (mem_regions, skipped): numbers or 0x hex"});
    let kinds = json!({"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string", "enum": ["image", "mapped", "private"]}, "description": "what backs the regions"});
    let uncached = json!({"type": "boolean", "description": "true: also search the write-combined (protect 0x400) and \
        no-cache (0x200) regions. Default false. Measured on one PC on 2026-10-19: 13.42 of the game's 21.06 GB \
        readable was private 0x404, read at 107 MB/s against 2,390 MB/s for private 0x4, and frame times rose while it \
        was read"});
    let fields = json!({"type": "array", "minItems": 1, "description": "what to read from each struct", "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
            "name": {"type": "string", "description": "its key in each row"},
            "offset": {"type": "string", "description": "from the struct's start (mem_find: the hit), before it when \
                negative: a number or (-)0x hex"},
            "type": ty,
            "len": len,
        },
        "required": ["name", "offset", "type"],
        "additionalProperties": false,
    }});
    let filter = json!({"type": "object", "description": "keep only the rows that match", "properties": {
        "field": {"type": "string", "description": "a field's name"},
        "eq": {"type": "string", "description": "the field holds this: a number, 0x hex, a float, or hex bytes"},
        "ne": {"type": "string", "description": "the field doesn't hold this (0: nonzero)"},
    }, "required": ["field"], "additionalProperties": false});
    let name = json!({"type": "string", "description": "a patch's name in the KB's patches.tsv"});
    let instances =
        json!({"type": "string", "description": "a row's name in the KB's instance_patches.tsv"});
    let patch = |verb: &str, does: &str| {
        json!({
            "name": format!("mem_{verb}"),
            "description": format!("{does} Refused, nothing written: no row of that name for the running build in \
                the KB's patches.tsv, boundaries-checked not set, a row that breaks the rules (1 to 8 bytes inside one \
                aligned qword, old and new the same length), or live bytes other than expected (another build or \
                another writer); with needs: no KB in the local config or no patches.tsv in it, or a GOG install \
                (the KB is Steam 5.01's). \
                The write is journaled first and taints saves the game writes after it. Numbers and provenance as \
                mem_read's."),
            "inputSchema": schema(json!({"name": name}), &["name"]),
        })
    };
    vec![
        json!({
            "name": "mem_read",
            "description": "Read the running game's memory: one little-endian number, or 1 to 4096 raw bytes as hex. \
                The game is the one in the session's job, with read access only. Give address, or rva (from the \
                game's image base, as the KB writes them). Every mem_* result gives addresses, ptr and u64 values as \

            "inputSchema": schema(json!({

            }), &["type"]),
        }),
        json!({
            "name": "mem_scan",
            "description": "Search the running game's memory for a byte pattern (IDA-style `48 8B ?? ?? 4?`, with an \
                optional hex bit mask), an ASCII string or a UTF-16LE one (exact, no terminator). Scope, one of: \

                (image, mapped, private); by default every readable region. The scope leaves out the regions whose \
                protect has 0x400 (write-combined) or 0x200 (no-cache) unless uncached: true; a region named in \

                "utf16": {"type": "string", "description": "a string to find as UTF-16LE"},

        json!({
            "name": "mem_find",
            "description": "Search the running game's memory for 64-bit values at 8-byte-aligned addresses: value, or \

            "inputSchema": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "a": {"type": "integer", "description": "the earlier result's captures id"},

            "description": "Follow a 64-bit pointer chain in the running game: each hop adds its offset to the pointer \

            "description": "Read structs in the running game, with read access only: count elements stride bytes apart \

            "inputSchema": schema(json!({

                "addresses": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "minItems": 1, "maxItems": 100000, "description": "the elements, instead of address or rva, offsets, stride and count: numbers or 0x hex"},

                "fields": fields,

        json!({
            "name": "mem_regions",
            "description": "List the running game's readable memory regions (committed, neither guard nor no-access \

            "inputSchema": schema(json!({
                "list": {"type": "boolean", "description": "true: every region too. Default false"},
            }), &[]),
        }),
        patch(
            "patch",
            "Apply a live code or data patch defined in the KB's patches.tsv: its new bytes over its old ones, at its \

        ),
        patch(
            "unpatch",
            "Undo a mem_patch: the old bytes back, only while the live bytes are still the patched ones.",
        ),
        json!({
            "name": "mem_patch_instances",
            "description": "Write a field in every live instance of a class, as a row of the KB's instance_patches.tsv \

            "_meta": {"anthropic/requiresUserInteraction": true},
            "inputSchema": schema(json!({
                "name": instances,
                "user_ok": {"type": "boolean", "description": "true only after telling the user in this conversation the row, the class, the field's old and new values and that every live instance found (with addresses, every one listed) is written (the count comes back), and they agreed.                 "addresses": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "minItems": 1, "maxItems": 1000, "description": "only these instances (mem_find hits' addresses): numbers or 0x hex. counts' unlisted: the ones found and not listed; a listed one the search didn't find is left"},

pub(crate) fn call(session: &mut Session, call: &mut Call, name: &str, args: &Value) -> Done {
    let out = match name {
        "mem_read" => read(session, call, args),
        "mem_scan" => scan(session, call, args),
        "mem_find" => find(session, call, args),
        "mem_follow" => follow(session, call, args),
        "mem_walk" => walk(session, call, args),
        "mem_regions" => regions(session, call, args),
        "mem_patch" => patch(session, call, args, Op::Patch),
        "mem_unpatch" => patch(session, call, args, Op::Unpatch),
        "mem_patch_instances" => patch_instances(session, call, args),
        "mem_unpatch_instances" => unpatch_instances(session, call, args),
        _ => Err(Done::Refused(format!("unknown tool {name:?}"))),
    };
    out.map_or_else(|done| done, Done::Ok)
}

/// The game's memory, read only: a handle with `PROCESS_VM_READ | PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION` on one pid.
pub(crate) struct Process {
    pid: u32,
    handle: OwnedHandle,
    /// The game's image: its build stamp, and the sections its regions are named by.
    pub(crate) image: Image,
    /// Its modules as the call began, in address order: where a result's addresses lie ([`mem::place`]).
    modules: Vec<Module>,
}

impl Process {
    /// Opens `pid` for reading, and reads the headers of its image `exe`.
    pub(crate) fn open(pid: u32, exe: &str) -> Result<Process, String> {
        let mut modules = game::modules(pid).map_err(|e| format!("modules of pid {pid}: {e}"))?;
        modules.sort_by_key(|m| m.base);
        let base = modules
            .iter()
            .find(|m| m.name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(exe))
            .ok_or(format!("{exe} is not loaded in pid {pid}"))?
            .base;
        let handle = open(pid, PROCESS_VM_READ | PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION)
            .map_err(|e| format!("open pid {pid} for reading: {e}"))?;
        let image = Image {
            base,
            stamp: String::new(),
            sections: Vec::new(),
        };
        let mut process = Process {
            pid,
            handle,
            image,
            modules,
        };
        process.image = mem::image(&process, base).map_err(|e| format!("{exe}'s headers: {e}"))?;
        Ok(process)
    }

    /// Makes `w` if the bytes there are still `w.old`: with a handle that has write access for this write only, the
    /// pages made writable around it and put back, and the instruction cache flushed (a code patch runs the new
    /// bytes). Same-length writes, so a torn one is harmless. Err says why, and whether any byte may have been
    /// written (false: it failed before WriteProcessMemory, nothing changed).
    fn write(&self, w: &Write) -> Result<(), (String, bool)> {
        let unwritten = |why: String| (why, false);
        let mut live = vec![0; w.old.len()];
        self.read(w.address, &mut live)
            .map_err(|e| unwritten(format!("can't read it again: {e}")))?;
        if live != w.old {
            return Err(unwritten(format!(
                "the bytes changed since they were read ({live:02x?}): another writer"
            )));
        }
        let handle = open(self.pid, PROCESS_VM_WRITE | PROCESS_VM_OPERATION)
            .map_err(|e| unwritten(format!("open pid {} for writing: {e}", self.pid)))?;
        let (h, at, len) = (
            handle.as_raw_handle(),
            w.address as *const c_void,
            w.new.len(),
        );
        let mut protect = 0;
        // SAFETY: a handle this opened, closed when `handle` drops; the protection change covers the bytes written
        // and is put back; the source buffer holds `len` bytes.
        unsafe {
            if VirtualProtectEx(h, at, len, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, &mut protect) == 0 {
                let why = format!("VirtualProtectEx: {}", io::Error::last_os_error());
                return Err(unwritten(why));
            }
            let mut wrote = 0;
            let ok = WriteProcessMemory(h, at, w.new.as_ptr().cast(), len, &mut wrote);
            let error = io::Error::last_os_error();
            VirtualProtectEx(h, at, len, protect, &mut protect);
            FlushInstructionCache(h, at, len);
            if ok == 0 || wrote != len {
                let why = format!("WriteProcessMemory wrote {wrote} of {len} bytes: {error}");
                return Err((why, wrote > 0));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// `r` cut where the image's sections begin and end, each piece named by the section it lies in.
    fn split(&self, r: Region) -> Vec<Region> {
        let end = r.base + r.size;
        let section_end = |s: &Section| (s.base + s.size).next_multiple_of(0x1000);
        let sections = &self.image.sections;
        let mut cuts: Vec<u64> = sections
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|s| [s.base, section_end(s)])
            .filter(|&c| r.base < c && c < end)
            .chain([end])
            .collect();
        cuts.sort_unstable();
        cuts.dedup();
        let mut at = r.base;
        cuts.into_iter()
            .map(|cut| {
                let section = sections
                    .iter()
                    .find(|s| s.base <= at && at < section_end(s));
                let piece = Region {
                    base: at,
                    size: cut - at,
                    section: section.map(|s| s.name.clone()),
                    ..r
                };
                at = cut;
                piece
            })
            .collect()
    }
}

fn open(pid: u32, access: PROCESS_ACCESS_RIGHTS) -> io::Result<OwnedHandle> {
    // SAFETY: the handle is checked, then owned (closed on drop).
    let handle = unsafe { OpenProcess(access, 0, pid) };
    if handle.is_null() {
        return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
    }
    Ok(unsafe { OwnedHandle::from_raw_handle(handle) })
}

impl Memory for Process {
    fn read(&self, address: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<()> {
        let mut got = 0;
        // SAFETY: the buffer holds `buf.len()` bytes.
        let ok = unsafe {
            ReadProcessMemory(
                self.handle.as_raw_handle(),
                address as *const c_void,
                buf.as_mut_ptr().cast(),
                buf.len(),
                &mut got,
            )
        };
        if ok == 0 {
            return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
        }
        if got != buf.len() {
            return Err(io::Error::other(format!(
                "{got} of {} bytes read",
                buf.len()
            )));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn regions(&self) -> io::Result<Vec<Region>> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let mut at = 0u64;
        loop {
            // SAFETY: a zeroed MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION is valid, and VirtualQueryEx fills it in.
            let mut info: MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION = unsafe { zeroed() };
            let size = size_of::<MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION>();
            let h = self.handle.as_raw_handle();
            // SAFETY: as above; `info` is `size` bytes.
            if unsafe { VirtualQueryEx(h, at as *const c_void, &mut info, size) } == 0 {
                // Past the top of user space: done. Failing on the first query is an error.
                if out.is_empty() {
                    return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
                }
                return Ok(out);
            }
            let (base, size) = (info.BaseAddress as u64, info.RegionSize as u64);
            let readable = info.State == MEM_COMMIT
                && info.Protect != 0
                && info.Protect & (PAGE_GUARD | PAGE_NOACCESS) == 0;
            if readable {
                let kind = match info.Type {
                    MEM_IMAGE => Kind::Image,
                    MEM_MAPPED => Kind::Mapped,
                    _ => Kind::Private,
                };
                out.extend(self.split(Region {
                    base,
                    size,
                    kind,
                    protect: info.Protect,
                    section: None,
                }));
            }
            match base.checked_add(size) {
                Some(next) if next > at => at = next,
                _ => return Ok(out),
            }
        }
    }
}

impl Ctx<'_> {
    /// The game in the session's job, open for reading.
    pub(crate) fn game(&self) -> Result<Process, String> {
        Process::open(self.game_pid()?, &self.config.game_exe)
    }

    /// The KB table `table` for `needed_for`, parsed. Refused with `needs` without it.
    pub(crate) fn kb<T, E: Display>(
        &self,
        table: &doctor::Dep,
        needed_for: &str,
        parse: fn(&str) -> Result<T, E>,
    ) -> Result<T, Done> {
        doctor::kb_matches(self.config, &self.live.build)?;
        let path = doctor::require(table, self.config, needed_for)?.path;
        let path = path.unwrap_or_default();
        let text = fs::read_to_string(&path).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        Ok(parse(&text).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?)
    }

    /// Makes the planned write `w` in `game`, and puts it in `fields` (`write`). It is journaled first as `what`: its
    /// time taints every save the game writes after it. A write that changes nothing is skipped (`unchanged`).
    /// Refused if the journal can't be written; failed after that.
    pub(crate) fn write(
        &self,
        game: &Process,
        what: &str,
        w: &Write,
        fields: &mut Fields,
    ) -> Result<(), Done> {
        fields.insert("write".into(), json!(w));
        if w.old == w.new {
            fields.insert("unchanged".into(), json!(true));
            return Ok(());
        }
        let what = format!("{what} at {:#x}", w.address);
        let (mut journal, id) = self.journal(&what, Some(w), true)?;
        let written = game.write(w);
        let happened = !matches!(written, Err((_, false)));
        if let Some(note) = self.settle(&mut journal, id, happened) {
            fields.insert("journal_note".into(), json!(note));
        }
        written.map_err(|(why, maybe)| {
            fields.insert("maybe_written".into(), json!(maybe));
            Done::Failed(format!("{what}: {why}"), fields.clone())
        })
    }

    /// Makes `writes` in instances of a class in `game` (a field `offset` bytes into each, whose first qword was
    /// `vtable`), each only as [`mem::write_instances`] allows. They are journaled first as one step `what`, whose entry
    /// on the session's patch list holds every one (`writes`) and `instances`: `meta` (the row's name and class, and
    /// counts) with `vtable`, `offset` and, once done, `written`; then only the ones made. None made: the step is taken
    /// back. Per write, in order, made or why it was left. Refused if the game can't be opened for writing or the
    /// journal can't be written.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub(crate) fn write_instances(
        &self,
        game: &Process,
        what: &str,
        vtable: u64,
        offset: u64,
        mut meta: Value,
        writes: &[Write],
        fields: &mut Fields,
    ) -> Result<Vec<Result<(), String>>, Done> {
        let handle = open(game.pid, PROCESS_VM_WRITE | PROCESS_VM_OPERATION)
            .map_err(|e| format!("open pid {} for writing: {e}", game.pid))?;
        meta["vtable"] = json!(format!("{vtable:#x}"));
        meta["offset"] = json!(offset);
        let entry = |writes: Value, meta: &Value| {
            if let Some((_, p)) = self.live.patches.borrow_mut().last_mut() {
                p["writes"] = writes;
                p["instances"] = meta.clone();
            }
        };
        let (mut journal, id) = self.journal(what, None, true)?;
        entry(json!(writes), &meta);
        let results = mem::write_instances(game, vtable, offset, writes, &mut |w| poke(&handle, w));
        let made: Vec<&Write> = writes
            .iter()
            .zip(&results)
            .filter(|(_, r)| r.is_ok())
            .map(|(w, _)| w)
            .collect();
        meta["written"] = json!(made.len());
        entry(json!(made), &meta);
        if let Some(note) = self.settle(&mut journal, id, !made.is_empty()) {
            fields.insert("journal_note".into(), json!(note));
        }
        Ok(results)
    }

    /// Undoes `writes` (each the undo of a field a mem_patch_instances wrote: its new bytes back to its old) of one
    /// instance patch, whose patch-list entry's `instances` is `meta`, through [`Ctx::write_instances`] as one step
    /// `what`: mem_unpatch_instances, and a dropped play session's undo.
    pub(crate) fn undo_instances(
        &self,
        game: &Process,
        what: &str,
        meta: &Value,
        writes: &[Write],
        fields: &mut Fields,
    ) -> Result<Vec<Result<(), String>>, Done> {
        let vtable = meta["vtable"].as_str().and_then(mem::number);
        let vtable = vtable.and_then(|n| u64::try_from(n).ok());
        let (Some(vtable), Some(offset)) = (vtable, meta["offset"].as_u64()) else {
            return Err(format!("{what}: its patch list entry has no vtable or offset").into());
        };
        let meta = json!({"name": meta["name"], "class": meta["class"], "applied": writes.len()});
        self.write_instances(game, what, vtable, offset, meta, writes, fields)
    }
}

/// Writes `w.new` at `w.address` with `handle` (write access), in a page that is writable: an instance field lies inside
/// one aligned qword, so in one page, which WriteProcessMemory writes whole or not at all.
fn poke(handle: &OwnedHandle, w: &Write) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (at, len) = (w.address as *const c_void, w.new.len());
    let mut wrote = 0;
    // SAFETY: a handle opened for writing, owned by the caller; the source buffer holds `len` bytes.
    let ok = unsafe {
        WriteProcessMemory(
            handle.as_raw_handle(),
            at,
            w.new.as_ptr().cast(),
            len,
            &mut wrote,
        )
    };
    match ok != 0 && wrote == len {
        true => Ok(()),
        false => Err(format!(
            "WriteProcessMemory wrote {wrote} of {len} bytes: {}",
            io::Error::last_os_error()
        )),
    }
}

/// [`ctx`] for a mem_* tool, refused while the KB's tables name another build than the session's exe: its
/// addresses come from them.
fn checked<'s>(session: &'s Session, args: &Value, known: &[&str]) -> Result<Ctx<'s>, String> {
    let cx = ctx(session, args, known)?;
    doctor::kb_matches(cx.config, &cx.live.build)?;
    Ok(cx)
}

/// `v` as an object's fields.
fn fields(v: Value) -> Fields {
    match v {
        Value::Object(map) => map,
        other => Map::from_iter([("value".to_string(), other)]),
    }
}

/// A whole number, as JSON gives it or as text: decimal, or `0x` hex, either with a `-` before it.
fn signed(v: &Value) -> Option<i128> {
    if let Some(n) = v.as_i64() {
        return Some(n.into());
    }
    if let Some(n) = v.as_u64() {
        return Some(n.into());
    }
    v.as_str().and_then(mem::number)
}

fn unsigned(v: &Value) -> Option<u64> {
    signed(v).and_then(|n| u64::try_from(n).ok())
}

/// The `type` in `args`, with its `len`.
fn ty(args: &Value) -> Result<Type, String> {
    let len = match args.get("len") {
        Some(v) => Some(v.as_u64().ok_or("len must be a whole number")? as usize),
        None => None,
    };
    Type::named(text(args, "type")?, len)
}

/// A pointer chain's offsets: `args[key]`.
fn offsets(args: &Value, key: &str) -> Result<Vec<i64>, String> {
    args.get(key)
        .and_then(Value::as_array)
        .and_then(|o| o.iter().map(|v| signed(v)?.try_into().ok()).collect())
        .ok_or(format!(
            "{key} must be an array of whole numbers or (-)0x hex"
        ))
}

/// A scan or find page's `from` and `limit`.
fn paging(args: &Value) -> Result<(u64, usize), String> {
    let from = match args.get("from") {
        Some(v) => unsigned(v).ok_or("from must be a number or 0x hex")?,
        None => 0,
    };
    let limit = match args.get("limit") {
        Some(v) => v.as_u64().ok_or("limit must be a whole number")? as usize,
        None => LIMIT,
    };
    Ok((from, limit))
}

/// The scope `args` give: `sections`, `regions` or `kinds`, at most one of them, `default` without; and `uncached`.
fn scope(args: &Value, default: Which) -> Result<Scope, String> {
    let list = |key: &str| {
        args.get(key)
            .map(|v| v.as_array().ok_or(format!("{key} must be an array")))
    };
    let which = match (list("sections"), list("regions"), list("kinds")) {
        (None, None, None) => default,
        (Some(s), None, None) => Which::Sections(
            s?.iter()
                .map(|v| v.as_str().map(String::from))
                .collect::<Option<_>>()
                .ok_or("sections must be names")?,
        ),
        (None, Some(r), None) => Which::Regions(
            r?.iter()
                .map(unsigned)
                .collect::<Option<_>>()
                .ok_or("regions must be bases: numbers or 0x hex")?,
        ),
        (None, None, Some(k)) => Which::Kinds(
            serde_json::from_value(Value::Array(k?.clone()))
                .map_err(|_| "kinds must be image, mapped or private")?,
        ),
        _ => return Err("one of sections, regions and kinds, not two".into()),
    };
    let uncached = flag(args, "uncached")?;
    Ok(Scope { which, uncached })
}

/// A scan or find page's `deadline_s`.
fn deadline(args: &Value) -> Result<Duration, String> {
    let secs = match args.get("deadline_s") {
        Some(v) => v
            .as_u64()
            .filter(|s| (1..=MAX_DEADLINE_S).contains(s))
            .ok_or(format!("deadline_s must be 1 to {MAX_DEADLINE_S}"))?,
        None => DEADLINE_S,
    };
    Ok(Duration::from_secs(secs))
}

/// A scan's tick ([`mem::scan`]): stops it once `budget` has run out or the call was cancelled, and reports its
/// progress.
fn ticker(call: &Call, budget: Duration) -> impl FnMut(u64, u64) -> ControlFlow<&'static str> {
    let deadline = Instant::now() + budget;
    move |bytes, total| {
        if call.stopped() {
            return ControlFlow::Break("cancelled");
        }
        if Instant::now() >= deadline {
            return ControlFlow::Break("deadline");
        }
        call.progress(&format!("{} of {} MiB searched", bytes >> 20, total >> 20));
        ControlFlow::Continue(())
    }
}

/// The address `args` give: `key`, or `rva` from the game's image base; exactly one of them.
fn address(game: &Process, args: &Value, key: &str) -> Result<u64, String> {
    match (args.get(key), args.get("rva")) {
        (Some(v), None) => unsigned(v).ok_or(format!("{key} must be a number or 0x hex")),
        (None, Some(v)) => unsigned(v)
            .and_then(|r| u32::try_from(r).ok())
            .map(|r| game.image.base + u64::from(r))
            .ok_or("rva must be a number or 0x hex of at most 32 bits".into()),
        _ => Err(format!("give {key} or rva, one of them")),
    }
}

fn read(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let cx = checked(session, args, &["address", "rva", "type", "len"])?;
    let ty = ty(args)?;
    let game = cx.game()?;
    let address = address(&game, args, "address")?;
    let (value, bytes) = mem::read(&game, address, ty).map_err(|e| format!("{address:#x}: {e}"))?;
    call.lap("read");
    let out = json!({"address": format!("{address:#x}"), "value": value, "bytes_sha256": sha256_hex(&bytes)});
    result(&cx, call, &game, "mem_read", args, out, None)
}

fn scan(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let known = [
        "pattern",
        "mask",
        "ascii",
        "utf16",
        "sections",
        "regions",
        "kinds",
        "uncached",
        "from",
        "limit",
        "deadline_s",
    ];
    let cx = checked(session, args, &known)?;
    let string = |key| {
        args.get(key)
            .map(|v| v.as_str().ok_or(format!("{key} must be a string")))
    };
    let pattern = match (string("pattern"), string("ascii"), string("utf16")) {
        (Some(p), None, None) => Pattern::parse(p?),
        (None, Some(a), None) => Pattern::ascii(a?),
        (None, None, Some(u)) => Pattern::utf16le(u?),
        _ => Err("give one of pattern, ascii and utf16".into()),
    }?;
    let pattern = match string("mask") {
        Some(_) if args.get("pattern").is_none() => {
            return Err("mask is for pattern only".to_string().into());
        }
        Some(mask) => pattern.masked(mask?)?,
        None => pattern,
    };
    let scope = scope(args, Which::All)?;
    let (from, limit) = paging(args)?;
    let budget = deadline(args)?;
    let game = cx.game()?;
    let page = mem::scan(
        &game,
        &pattern,
        &scope,
        from,
        limit,
        &mut ticker(call, budget),
    )
    .map_err(|e| format!("the game's regions: {e}"))?;
    call.lap("scan");
    let hits: Vec<Value> = page
        .hits
        .iter()
        .map(|a| json!({"address": format!("{a:#x}")}))
        .collect();
    let mut out = json!(page);
    out["hits"] = json!(hits);
    result(&cx, call, &game, "mem_scan", args, out, Some("hits"))
}

fn follow(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let cx = checked(session, args, &["base", "rva", "offsets"])?;
    let offsets = offsets(args, "offsets")?;
    let game = cx.game()?;
    let base = address(&game, args, "base")?;
    let chain = mem::follow(&game, base, &offsets);
    call.lap("follow");
    result(&cx, call, &game, "mem_follow", args, json!(chain), None)
}

fn find(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let known = [
        "value",
        "values",
        "context",
        "fields",
        "filter",
        "sections",
        "regions",
        "kinds",
        "uncached",
        "from",
        "limit",
        "deadline_s",
        "keep",
    ];
    let cx = checked(session, args, &known)?;
    flag(args, "keep")?;
    let values = match (args.get("value"), args.get("values")) {
        (Some(v), None) => vec![
            unsigned(v)
                .ok_or_else(|| String::from("value must be a number or 0x hex of 64 bits"))?,
        ],
        (None, Some(v)) => v
            .as_array()
            .and_then(|a| a.iter().map(unsigned).collect())
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                String::from("values must be an array of numbers or 0x hex of 64 bits")
            })?,
        _ => return Err("give value or values, one of them".to_string().into()),
    };
    let context = match args.get("context") {
        Some(v) => v
            .as_u64()
            .ok_or_else(|| String::from("context must be a whole number"))?,
        None => CONTEXT,
    };
    let (fields, filter) = layout(args)?;
    let f = Find {
        values,
        context,
        fields,
        filter,
    };
    let scope = scope(args, Which::Kinds(vec![Kind::Image, Kind::Private]))?;
    let (from, limit) = paging(args)?;
    let budget = deadline(args)?;
    let game = cx.game()?;
    let mut tick = ticker(call, budget);
    let found = mem::find(&game, &f, &scope, from, limit, &mut tick);
    drop(tick);
    let (page, sha) = found?;
    call.lap("find");
    let mut out = json!(page);
    out["bytes_sha256"] = json!(sha);
    result(&cx, call, &game, "mem_find", args, out, Some("hits"))
}

/// The `fields` and `filter` in `args`, for mem_walk and mem_find: none without them.
fn layout(args: &Value) -> Result<(Vec<Field>, Option<Filter>), String> {
    let wanted = match args.get("fields") {
        None => &[][..],
        Some(v) => v
            .as_array()
            .ok_or("fields must be an array of {name, offset, type}")?
            .as_slice(),
    };
    let mut fields = Vec::new();
    for f in wanted {
        ledger::object(f, &["name", "offset", "type", "len"])
            .map_err(|e| format!("fields: {e}"))?;
        let name = text(f, "name").map_err(|e| format!("fields: {e}"))?;
        let offset = f.get("offset").and_then(signed);
        let offset = offset.and_then(|o| i64::try_from(o).ok());
        let offset = offset.ok_or(format!(
            "field {name}: offset must be a number or (-)0x hex"
        ))?;
        let ty = ty(f).map_err(|e| format!("field {name}: {e}"))?;
        let name = name.into();
        fields.push(Field { name, offset, ty });
    }
    let filter = match args.get("filter") {
        None => None,
        Some(f) => {
            ledger::object(f, &["field", "eq", "ne"]).map_err(|e| format!("filter: {e}"))?;
            let field = text(f, "field").map_err(|e| format!("filter: {e}"))?.into();
            let (eq, value) = match (f.get("eq"), f.get("ne")) {
                (Some(v), None) => (true, v),
                (None, Some(v)) => (false, v),
                _ => return Err("filter: give eq or ne, one of them".into()),
            };
            let value = value
                .as_str()
                .map_or_else(|| value.to_string(), String::from);
            Some(Filter { field, eq, value })
        }
    };
    Ok((fields, filter))
}

fn walk(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let known = [
        "address",
        "rva",
        "offsets",
        "stride",
        "count",
        "addresses",
        "deref",
        "fields",
        "filter",
    ];
    let cx = checked(session, args, &known)?;
    let (fields, filter) = layout(args)?;
    let deref = match args.get("deref") {
        Some(_) => offsets(args, "deref")?,
        None => Vec::new(),
    };
    let listed = match args.get("addresses") {
        None => None,
        Some(_)
            if ["address", "rva", "offsets", "stride", "count"]
                .iter()
                .any(|k| args.get(k).is_some()) =>
        {
            let why = "addresses instead of address or rva, offsets, stride and count";
            return Err(why.to_string().into());
        }
        Some(v) => Some(
            v.as_array()
                .and_then(|a| a.iter().map(unsigned).collect::<Option<Vec<u64>>>())
                .ok_or_else(|| String::from("addresses must be an array of numbers or 0x hex"))?,
        ),
    };
    let whole = |key: &str| {
        let n = args.get(key).and_then(Value::as_u64);
        n.ok_or(format!("{key} must be a whole number"))
    };
    let game = cx.game()?;
    let mut out = json!({});
    let elements = match listed {
        Some(list) => Elements::List(list),
        None => {
            let (stride, count) = (whole("stride")?, whole("count")?);
            let chain = match args.get("offsets") {
                Some(_) => offsets(args, "offsets")?,
                None => Vec::new(),
            };
            let start = address(&game, args, "address")?;
            let followed = mem::follow(&game, start, &chain);
            let base = followed.end.ok_or_else(|| {
                let why = followed.broken.map(|b| b.why).unwrap_or_default();
                format!("offsets: {why}")
            })?;
            out["base"] = json!(format!("{base:#x}"));
            Elements::Array {
                base,
                stride,
                count,
            }
        }
    };
    let w = Walk {
        elements,
        deref,
        fields,
        filter,
    };
    let (rows, sha) = mem::walk(&game, &w)?;
    call.lap("walk");
    let errors = rows.iter().filter(|r| r.contains_key("why")).count();
    out["row_count"] = json!(rows.len());
    out["errors"] = json!(errors);
    out["rows"] = json!(rows);
    out["bytes_sha256"] = json!(sha);
    result(&cx, call, &game, "mem_walk", args, out, Some("rows"))
}

fn regions(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let cx = checked(session, args, &["list"])?;
    let list = flag(args, "list")?;
    let game = cx.game()?;
    let all = game
        .regions()
        .map_err(|e| format!("the game's regions: {e}"))?;
    call.lap("regions");
    let mut largest = all.clone();
    largest.sort_by_key(|r| Reverse(r.size));
    largest.truncate(LARGEST);
    let bytes: u64 = all.iter().map(|r| r.size).sum();
    let mut out = json!({
        "regions": all.len(),
        "bytes": bytes,
        "groups": mem::census(&all),
        "largest": largest,
    });
    if list {
        out["list"] = json!(all);
    }
    result(&cx, call, &game, "mem_regions", args, out, Some("list"))
}

/// A mem tool's result: `out` with where each of its addresses lies ([`mem::place`]), its provenance (`image_base`,
/// `build`, `read_at`) and the world in its `state` (`measurements.world`'s words). With `list`, a result over
/// [`INLINE_BYTES`] goes whole to `<tool>-<secs>-<random>.json` in the session's capture folder, under a `header` (the
/// tool, the call's arguments less its token, the boot, the build, the image base, `read_at`), with a captures row
/// (`ledger.captures`); inline only the first of its `list` that fit (`truncated`, `file`). With `keep` in `args`, any
/// result goes there too, kept whole inline when it fits.
fn result(
    cx: &Ctx,
    call: &mut Call,
    game: &Process,
    tool: &str,
    args: &Value,
    mut out: Value,
    list: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    mem::place(&mut out, game.image.base, &game.modules);
    let now = SystemTime::now();
    out["image_base"] = json!(format!("{:#x}", game.image.base));
    out["build"] = json!(game.image.stamp);
    out["read_at"] = json!(session::utc_ms(now));
    out["state"] = json!({"world": crate::measure::world(cx)});
    let big = out.to_string().len() > INLINE_BYTES;
```
