`crates/quen/src/relocate.rs`:

```rs
//! Where quen keeps its config and data: `%USERPROFILE%\.quen`, never AppData. Claude Desktop is an MSIX app
//! package, and Windows redirects AppData writes from a package, and from every process it starts (`quen mcp`, `quen
//! serve`, shells), into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\<package>\LocalCache\{Roaming,Local}`. A client outside the package
//! then saw another config, another ledger and another game lock (measured 2026-10-18). The doctor warns while quen's
//! AppData is redirected (GetCurrentPackageFullName, or one file under a package's copy and AppData alike: the first
//! says nothing in Claude Desktop's processes) and while it finds quen's old folders; `quen_setup` `move` (and
//! `quen setup --move`) copies them
//! into `.quen` once, checks every copy by sha256, rewrites what pointed at them, and renames the old folders
//! `quen.moved-<date>`. Nothing is deleted.

use std::env;
use std::fs::{self, File};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::SystemTime;

use quen_core::journal::sha256_file;
use quen_core::ledger::Ledger;
use serde_json::{Map, Value, json};

use crate::config;
use crate::session::{self, Done};
use crate::win;

/// The folders the move looks at and writes to.
pub(crate) struct Places {
    /// `%USERPROFILE%\.quen`.
    pub(crate) home: PathBuf,
    /// `%APPDATA%` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%`.
    pub(crate) roaming: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub(crate) local: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// The app package whose private folder this process's AppData is redirected into, if any.
    pub(crate) package: Option<String>,
}

impl Places {
    pub(crate) fn here() -> Result<Places, String> {
        let roaming = env::var_os("APPDATA").map(PathBuf::from);
        let local = env::var_os("LOCALAPPDATA").map(PathBuf::from);
        let id = |p: &Path| win::file_id(p).ok();
        // GetCurrentPackageFullName says nothing for the processes Claude Desktop starts, though their AppData is
        // redirected (feature tests 2b, measured twice): the redirection itself is the test.
        let package =
            win::package().or_else(|| redirected(local.as_deref(), roaming.as_deref(), &id));
        Ok(Places {
            home: config::home().ok_or("USERPROFILE is not set")?,
            roaming,
            local,
            package,
        })
    }

    /// The default places of an older quen, `%APPDATA%\quen` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\quen`: what its config may name.
    fn defaults(&self) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
        [&self.roaming, &self.local]
            .into_iter()
            .flatten()
            .map(|d| d.join("quen"))
            .collect()
    }

    /// quen's old folders that hold anything: each app package's private `LocalCache\{Roaming,Local}\quen`, and the
    /// defaults, but those only outside a package (inside one, their paths show the package's private copy). A folder
    /// seen under two paths (the same file id: a redirection this process can't tell) counts once.
    pub(crate) fn old(&self) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let packages = self.local.iter().map(|l| l.join("Packages"));
        for package in packages.flat_map(fs::read_dir).flatten().flatten() {
            for kind in ["Roaming", "Local"] {
                out.push(package.path().join("LocalCache").join(kind).join("quen"));
            }
        }
        if self.package.is_none() {
            out.extend(self.defaults());
        }
        out.retain(|d| fs::read_dir(d).is_ok_and(|mut e| e.next().is_some()));
        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        out.retain(|d| win::file_id(d).map_or(true, |id| seen.insert(id)));
        out
    }
}

/// The app package whose private copy this process's `%LOCALAPPDATA%` (`local`) and `%APPDATA%` (`roaming`) show: a
/// name in a package's `LocalCache\Local` (or `Roaming`) with the same file id (`id`) under them. Reads only.
fn redirected(
    local: Option<&Path>,
    roaming: Option<&Path>,
    id: &dyn Fn(&Path) -> Option<String>,
) -> Option<String> {
    for package in fs::read_dir(local?.join("Packages")).ok()?.flatten() {
        for (kind, base) in [("Local", local), ("Roaming", roaming)] {
            let Some(base) = base else { continue };
            let cache = package.path().join("LocalCache").join(kind);
            // ponytail: the first 20 names of each copy; a redirected copy shows from its first.
            for entry in fs::read_dir(&cache)
                .into_iter()
                .flatten()
                .flatten()
                .take(20)
            {
                let theirs = id(&entry.path());
                if theirs.is_some() && theirs == id(&base.join(entry.file_name())) {
                    return Some(package.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned());
                }
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

/// The doctor's warnings: quen's AppData is redirected into an app package, or an older quen's folders are there to
/// move.
pub(crate) fn warnings(places: &Places) -> Vec<String> {
    let home = places.home.display();
    let mut out: Vec<String> = places
        .package
        .iter()
        .map(|p| {
            format!(
                "Windows redirects this quen's AppData into the app package {p}'s private folder, which other \
                 clients don't see. quen keeps its config and data in {home} instead"
            )
        })
        .collect();
    out.extend(places.old().iter().map(|old| {
        format!(
            "an older quen's files are at {}: move them into {home} once (quen_setup with move: true, then user_ok; \
             or quen setup --move --user-ok in a terminal)",
            old.display()
        )
    }));
    out
}

/// A file to copy: where from, where to, its sha256.
struct Copy {
    from: PathBuf,
    to: PathBuf,
    sha: String,
    bytes: u64,
}

/// What the move would do, after every check that needs no lock. Err: refused, nothing changed.
struct Survey {
    old: Vec<PathBuf>,
    copies: Vec<Copy>,
    /// Destinations that exist already (a log the new quen wrote): the old file goes beside, `<name>.moved`.
    beside: Vec<PathBuf>,
}

fn walk(dir: &Path, out: &mut Vec<PathBuf>) {
    for entry in fs::read_dir(dir).into_iter().flatten().flatten() {
        let path = entry.path();
        if path.is_dir() {
            walk(&path, out);
        } else {
            out.push(path);
        }
    }
}

fn survey(places: &Places) -> Result<Survey, String> {
    let old = places.old();
    if old.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!(
            "no older quen folders found: nothing to move into {}",
            places.home.display()
        ));
    }
    let home = &places.home;
    for dir in old.iter().chain([home]) {
        let journal = dir.join("state").join("journal.jsonl");
        if journal.exists() {
            return Err(format!(
                "{} is a session's journal: replay it first (session_recover, with the quen that wrote it), then move",
                journal.display()
            ));
        }
    }
    for taken in ["config.toml", r"state\quen.db"] {
        if home.join(taken).exists() {
            return Err(format!(
                "{} exists already: quen won't merge two configs or ledgers. Move one aside yourself first",
                home.join(taken).display()
            ));
        }
    }
    let mut copies: Vec<Copy> = Vec::new();
    let mut beside = Vec::new();
    for dir in &old {
        let mut files = Vec::new();
        walk(dir, &mut files);
        for from in files {
            let rel = from.strip_prefix(dir).unwrap_or(&from).to_owned();
            // The lock holds only who held it last; the new quen has its own.
            if rel == Path::new(r"state\game.lock") {
                continue;
            }
            let sha = sha256_file(&from).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", from.display()))?;
            let bytes = fs::metadata(&from).map_or(0, |m| m.len());
            let mut to = home.join(&rel);
            if let Some(other) = copies.iter().find(|c| c.to == to) {
                if other.sha == sha {
                    continue;
                }
                return Err(format!(
                    "{} and {} differ: both would be {}. Keep one (rename the other folder), then move",
                    other.from.display(),
                    from.display(),
                    to.display()
                ));
            }
            if to.exists() {
                let mut name = to.as_os_str().to_owned();
                name.push(".moved");
                to = PathBuf::from(name);
                beside.push(to.clone());
            }
            copies.push(Copy {
                from,
                to,
                sha,
                bytes,
            });
        }
    }
    Ok(Survey {
        old,
        copies,
        beside,
    })
}

/// `quen_setup` `move`: without `user_ok` what it would do; with it, the move: refused while `busy` (this quen's
/// session or its lock), a journal is left or another quen holds a lock; then every file copied into `.quen` and checked
/// by sha256, the config's paths into the old folders rewritten, the ledger's journal paths rebased, and the old
/// folders renamed `quen.moved-<date>`.
pub(crate) fn run(places: &Places, user_ok: bool, busy: Option<&str>) -> Done {
    let survey = match survey(places) {
        Ok(survey) => survey,
        Err(why) => return why.into(),
    };
    let bytes: u64 = survey.copies.iter().map(|c| c.bytes).sum();
    let mut fields = Map::new();
    fields.insert("from".into(), json!(survey.old));
    fields.insert("to".into(), json!(places.home));
    fields.insert("files".into(), json!(survey.copies.len()));
    fields.insert("gb".into(), json!(quen_core::disk::gb(bytes)));
    fields.insert("beside".into(), json!(survey.beside));
    if !user_ok {
        let next =
            "tell the user what moves (from, to, files, gb), then call again with user_ok: true";
        fields.insert("next".into(), json!(next));
        return Done::Ok(fields);
    }
    if let Some(why) = busy {
        return why.to_string().into();
    }
    // Every lock, old and new, held through the copy: no quen starts a session meanwhile.
    let holder = json!({"pid": std::process::id(), "session": "move", "t_start": session::now()});
    let mut locks: Vec<File> = Vec::new();
    for dir in survey.old.iter().chain([&places.home]) {
        let state = dir.join("state");
        let path = state.join("game.lock");
        if dir != &places.home && !path.exists() {
            continue;
        }
        let taken = fs::create_dir_all(&state).and_then(|()| win::try_lock(&path, &holder));
        match taken {
            Ok(Some(file)) => locks.push(file),
            Ok(None) => {
                return format!(
                    "another quen holds {}: a session is live there; end it first",
                    path.display()
                )
                .into();
            }
            Err(e) => return format!("{}: {e}", path.display()).into(),
        }
    }
    for copy in &survey.copies {
        let copied = copy
            .to
            .parent()
            .map_or(Ok(()), fs::create_dir_all)
            .and_then(|()| fs::copy(&copy.from, &copy.to))
            .and_then(|_| sha256_file(&copy.to));
        match copied {
            Ok(sha) if sha == copy.sha => {}
            other => {
                let why = other.map_or_else(
                    |e| e.to_string(),
                    |sha| format!("the copy's sha256 is {sha}"),
                );
                let why = format!(
                    "{} didn't copy to {} ({why}): the old folders are untouched; the copy in {} is incomplete: move \
                     it aside, then move again",
                    copy.from.display(),
                    copy.to.display(),
                    places.home.display()
                );
                return Done::Failed(why, fields);
            }
        }
    }
    let mut prefixes: Vec<PathBuf> = survey.old.clone();
    prefixes.extend(places.defaults());
    fields.insert(
        "config_rewritten".into(),
        json!(rewrite_config(places, &prefixes)),
    );
    fields.insert(
        "ledger_journal_paths".into(),
        json!(rebase_ledger(places, &prefixes)),
    );
    drop(locks);
    let date = &session::utc(SystemTime::now())[..10];
    let (mut renamed, mut left) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    for dir in &survey.old {
        let to = (1..)
            .map(|n| match n {
                1 => dir.with_file_name(format!("quen.moved-{date}")),
                n => dir.with_file_name(format!("quen.moved-{date}-{n}")),
            })
            .find(|p| !p.exists())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        match win::rename_no_replace(dir, &to) {
            Ok(()) => renamed.push(json!({"from": dir, "to": to})),
            Err(e) => left.push(json!({"path": dir, "why": format!(
                "copied and checked, but not renamed ({e}): an older quen serve may still have a file open there. \
                 Rename it to {} yourself once no quen runs",
                to.display()
            )})),
        }
    }
    fields.insert("renamed".into(), json!(renamed));
    fields.insert("left".into(), json!(left));
    let applies = "a quen serve on .quen\\config.toml takes the moved config up for every connection at its next \
                   connection or session tool call; any other quen serve still running (an older quen's, or one whose \
                   QUEN_CONFIG names another file) keeps its config until the MCP clients restart (Claude Code: /mcp)";
    fields.insert("applies".into(), json!(applies));
    Done::Ok(fields)
}

/// Rewrites the copied config's values that point into an old folder (`prefixes`) to the same place under `.quen`: the
/// keys rewritten, or the error.
fn rewrite_config(places: &Places, prefixes: &[PathBuf]) -> Value {
    let path = places.home.join("config.toml");
    let Ok(text) = fs::read_to_string(&path) else {
        return json!([]);
    };
    /// What follows the old folder `value` is in, if it is in one.
    fn under<'a>(value: &'a str, prefixes: &[PathBuf]) -> Option<&'a str> {
        prefixes.iter().find_map(|old| {
            let old = old.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase();
            let head = value.get(..old.len())?;
            let rest = value.get(old.len()..)?;
            (head.to_lowercase() == old && (rest.is_empty() || rest.starts_with('\\')))
                .then_some(rest)
        })
    }
    let home = places.home.display();
    let moved: Vec<(&str, String)> = config::pairs(&text)
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(|(key, value)| Some((key, format!("{home}{}", under(value, prefixes)?))))
        .collect();
    if moved.is_empty() {
        return json!([]);
    }
    let values: Vec<(&str, &str)> = moved.iter().map(|(k, v)| (*k, v.as_str())).collect();
    let new = config::with_values(&text, &values);
    match config::parse(&new, &path).and_then(|_| config::write(&path, &new)) {
        Ok(()) => json!(values.iter().map(|(k, _)| *k).collect::<Vec<_>>()),
        Err(e) => json!({"error": e}),
    }
}

/// Rebases the copied ledger's journal paths from the old folders to `.quen`: how many rows, or the error.
fn rebase_ledger(places: &Places, prefixes: &[PathBuf]) -> Value {
    let db = places.home.join("state").join("quen.db");
    if !db.exists() {
        return json!(0);
    }
    let home = places.home.to_string_lossy();
    let rebased = Ledger::open(&db).and_then(|mut ledger| {
        prefixes
            .iter()
            .map(|old| ledger.rebase_journal_paths(&old.to_string_lossy(), &home))
            .sum::<Result<usize, _>>()
    });
    rebased.map_or_else(|e| json!({"error": e.to_string()}), |n| json!(n))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A user profile of this test's own: AppData, a fake app package's private copy, and the new home.
    struct Temp(PathBuf);

    impl Temp {
        fn new(name: &str) -> Temp {
            let dir = env::temp_dir().join(format!("quen-relocate-{name}-{}", std::process::id()));
            let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir); // this test's own temp folder, from an earlier run
            Temp(dir)
        }

        fn put(&self, rel: &str, text: &str) -> PathBuf {
            let path = self.0.join(rel);
            fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
            fs::write(&path, text).unwrap();
            path
        }

        fn places(&self, package: Option<&str>) -> Places {
            Places {
                home: self.0.join(r"profile\.quen"),
                roaming: Some(self.0.join(r"profile\AppData\Roaming")),
                local: Some(self.0.join(r"profile\AppData\Local")),
                package: package.map(String::from),
            }
        }
    }

    impl Drop for Temp {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0); // this test's own temp folder
        }
    }

    const PKG: &str = r"profile\AppData\Local\Packages\Claude_test\LocalCache";

    /// The old layout as Claude Desktop left it: the config in the package's private Roaming copy, the data in its
    /// Local copy, and the deny-list written by hand into the real AppData.
    fn old_layout(t: &Temp) {
        let local = t.0.join(r"profile\AppData\Local\quen");
        t.put(
            &format!(r"{PKG}\Roaming\quen\config.toml"),
            &format!(
                "data_root = '{}'\ngame_exe = 'witcher3.exe'\n",
                local.display()
            ),
        );
        t.put(r"profile\AppData\Roaming\quen\deny.txt", "# synthetic\n");
        t.put(&format!(r"{PKG}\Local\quen\logs\serve.log"), "old log\n");
        t.put(&format!(r"{PKG}\Local\quen\captures\1\shot.png"), "png");
        let db = t.0.join(format!(r"{PKG}\Local\quen\state\quen.db"));
        fs::create_dir_all(db.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
        let mut ledger = Ledger::open(&db).unwrap();
        let game = quen_core::ledger::Game {
            name: "synthetic".into(),
            exe_path: "game.exe".into(),
            exe_sha256: "0".repeat(64),
            build_stamp: None,
        };
        ledger.add_game(&game).unwrap();
        let journal = local.join(r"logs\1-abc\journal.jsonl");
        let boot = quen_core::ledger::BootStart {
            game_id: 1,
            t_start: "2026-10-17T13:15:00Z".into(),
            journal_path: Some(journal.display().to_string()),
            ..Default::default()
        };
        ledger.start_boot(&boot).unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_doctor_finds_a_package_copy_and_the_old_defaults() {
        let t = Temp::new("find");
        old_layout(&t);
        let outside = t.places(None);
        let found = outside.old();
        assert_eq!(found.len(), 3, "{found:?}");
        assert!(found.iter().any(|p| p.ends_with(r"LocalCache\Local\quen")));
        // Inside a package, AppData shows the package's copy: only the real package paths count.
        let inside = t.places(Some("Claude_test"));
        assert_eq!(inside.old().len(), 2);
        let warned = warnings(&inside);
        assert!(warned[0].contains("app package Claude_test"), "{warned:?}");
        assert!(warned[1].contains("quen_setup with move"), "{warned:?}");
    }

    /// Feature tests 2b: GetCurrentPackageFullName said nothing for a process Claude Desktop started, though its AppData
    /// was redirected. A name in a package's private copy with the same file id under %LOCALAPPDATA% shows the
    /// redirection; distinct files don't.
    #[test]
    fn a_redirection_shows_as_one_file_under_two_names() {
        let t = Temp::new("redirect");
        let local = t.0.join(r"profile\AppData\Local");
        let cached = t.put(&format!(r"{PKG}\Local\Synthetic_a.txt"), "copy");
        t.put(r"profile\AppData\Local\Synthetic_a.txt", "other");
        let real = |p: &Path| win::file_id(p).ok();
        assert_eq!(redirected(Some(&local), None, &real), None, "two files");
        let seen = local.join("Synthetic_a.txt");
        let same = |p: &Path| (p == cached || p == seen).then(|| "1".to_string());
        assert_eq!(
            redirected(Some(&local), None, &same).as_deref(),
            Some("Claude_test")
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_move_refuses_with_a_live_lock_then_copies_checks_rewrites_and_renames() {
        let t = Temp::new("move");
        old_layout(&t);
        let places = t.places(None);
        // A plan first: nothing changes.
        let Done::Ok(plan) = run(&places, false, None) else {
            panic!("no plan")
        };
        // config.toml, deny.txt, serve.log, shot.png, quen.db (and its WAL files, if SQLite left them).
        assert!(plan["files"].as_u64().unwrap() >= 5, "{plan:?}");
        assert!(!places.home.exists());
        // Another quen holds the old data's lock: refused, nothing copied.
        let lock = t.0.join(format!(r"{PKG}\Local\quen\state\game.lock"));
        let held = win::try_lock(&lock, &json!({"pid": 1})).unwrap().unwrap();
        let Done::Refused(why) = run(&places, true, None) else {
            panic!("not refused")
        };
        assert!(why.contains("another quen holds"), "{why}");
        assert!(!places.home.join("config.toml").exists());
        drop(held);
        let Done::Refused(why) = run(&places, true, Some("a session is live")) else {
            panic!("not refused")
        };
        assert_eq!(why, "a session is live");

        // The new quen already wrote its own log.
        t.put(r"profile\.quen\logs\serve.log", "new log\n");
        let Done::Ok(moved) = run(&places, true, None) else {
            panic!("not moved")
        };
        let home = &places.home;
        assert_eq!(
            fs::read_to_string(home.join(r"logs\serve.log")).unwrap(),
            "new log\n"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            fs::read_to_string(home.join(r"logs\serve.log.moved")).unwrap(),
            "old log\n"
        );
        assert!(home.join("deny.txt").exists() && home.join(r"captures\1\shot.png").exists());
        let config = fs::read_to_string(home.join("config.toml")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            config,
            format!(
                "data_root = '{}'\ngame_exe = 'witcher3.exe'\n",
                home.display()
            )
        );
        assert_eq!(moved["config_rewritten"], json!(["data_root"]), "{moved:?}");
        assert_eq!(moved["ledger_journal_paths"], 1, "{moved:?}");
        let ledger = Ledger::open_readonly(home.join(r"state\quen.db")).unwrap();
        let rows = ledger
            .query(
                "SELECT journal_path FROM boots",
                &[],
                std::time::Duration::from_secs(5),
            )
            .unwrap()
            .rows;
        assert_eq!(rows[0][0], json!(home.join(r"logs\1-abc\journal.jsonl")));
        assert_eq!(moved["renamed"].as_array().unwrap().len(), 3, "{moved:?}");
        assert!(places.old().is_empty(), "nothing left to warn about");
        let date = &session::utc(SystemTime::now())[..10];
        let kept = t.0.join(format!(
            r"{PKG}\Local\quen.moved-{date}\captures\1\shot.png"
        ));
        assert!(kept.exists(), "the old files stay, renamed");
        // .quen has a ledger now: a second move is refused.
        t.put(&format!(r"{PKG}\Local\quen\x.txt"), "x");
        let Done::Refused(why) = run(&places, true, None) else {
            panic!("not refused")
        };
        assert!(why.contains("won't merge"), "{why}");
    }
}

```

`crates/quen/src/save.rs`:

```rs
//! `game_save`: a new manual save, written by the game itself through quen's command channel (the `save` verb,
//! quen-w3 0.1.4), as the menu's "Empty save slot" writes one: the game names it, and the verb can't name a slot, so it
//! never overwrites. quen checks gamesaves before and after: one new `ManualSave_*` and nothing else, which the guard
//! then passes (session.rs); anything else ends the session. Not journaled: quen never deletes a save, so nothing is
//! undone.

use std::thread::sleep;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use quen_core::bridge_log;
use quen_core::journal::sha256_file;
use quen_core::ledger::Save;
use quen_core::protocol::Verb;
use quen_core::saves::{self, W3_AUTO_SAVES, W3_MANUAL};
use serde_json::{Map, Value, json};

use crate::channel::REPLY_MAX;
use crate::doctor;
use crate::game::{Fields, ctx, flag, schema, shown};
use crate::session::{Call, Done, Session, ledger_error, open_ledger};

/// How long the game may take to start writing the save, and how long gamesaves must then stay unchanged: the end's
/// own wait for the folder.
const SAVE_MAX: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
const QUIET: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
const POLL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(100);
/// The longest note, in characters.
const NOTE_MAX: usize = 500;

pub(crate) fn tool() -> Value {
    json!({
        "name": "game_save",
        "description": "Write a new manual save, as the game's menu does into its \"Empty save slot\": the game \
            names it (ManualSave_...), never overwrites one, and lists it with the user's own saves. The client asks \
            the user on every call (user_ok is only your word): never route around a denial. Call focus to client \
            first: the prompt shows in the client's window. quen checks gamesaves before and after: one new save \
            (its .sav, .png, .json) and nothing else. Answers save (the name \
            game_load takes), files, tainted. Refused, nothing sent: no user_ok; quen's state not plain gameplay (the \
            main menu, photo mode, a scene, cutscene, fade or the dialogue flag); a write that taints saves earlier in \
            this boot (tainted_by) without tainted_ok; the game's own save lock (combat, a menu: game_text); with \
            needs: quen-w3 0.1.3 or older. Failed: no new save within 30 s (a dialog may wait for OK), or anything \
            else changed in gamesaves (the session was ended). The save is the user's: never delete it.",
        // Claude Code prompts for this tool on every call, in every permission mode, as for session_launch.
        "_meta": {"anthropic/requiresUserInteraction": true},
        "inputSchema": schema(json!({
            "user_ok": {"type": "boolean", "description": "true only after telling the user in this conversation that the game is about to write a new save into their save list, and they agreed. Required."},
            "tainted_ok": {"type": "boolean", "description": "true to save after a write that taints saves (mem_patch, game_cvar set, game_teleport, game_settime, game_weather), the user having agreed to a tainted save. Default false: refused"},
            "note": {"type": "string", "description": "a note for the save's ledger row, at most 500 characters; it never reaches the game"},
        }), &["user_ok"]),
    })
}

/// game_save's checks, the verb, the wait for the files and their check; then the files go into the session's
/// accepted saves and the .sav into the ledger.
pub(crate) fn call(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let cx = ctx(session, args, &["user_ok", "tainted_ok", "note"])?;
    let note = args.get("note").map(|n| {
        let text = n.as_str().filter(|n| n.chars().count() <= NOTE_MAX);
        text.ok_or(format!(
            "note must be text of at most {NOTE_MAX} characters"
        ))
    });
    let note = note.transpose()?;
    let tainted_ok = flag(args, "tainted_ok")?;
    if !flag(args, "user_ok")? {
        let why = "user_ok: tell the user the game is about to write a new save into their save list, and get \
                   their OK first";
        return Err(why.to_string().into());
    }
    doctor::installed(&[&doctor::PACKAGE], cx.config, "game_save")?;
    doctor::package_at_least(cx.config, doctor::BEFORE_SAVE, "game_save", "0.1.4")?;
    let last = cx.last_flags();
    if !last.is_some_and(|f| bridge_log::plain(f) && !bridge_log::in_photo(f)) {
        return Err(format!(
            "quen's state shows {}: game_save needs plain gameplay (not the main menu, photo mode, a scene, a \
             cutscene, a fade or the dialogue flag). Nothing sent",
            shown(last)
        )
        .into());
    }
    // finish's rule (session.rs): every save after the boot's first tainting write is tainted.
    let tainted_by: Vec<Value> = cx
        .live
        .patches
        .borrow()
        .iter()
        .filter(|(_, patch)| patch["taints"] != false)
        .map(|(_, patch)| json!({"what": patch["what"], "t": patch["t"]}))
        .collect();
    let tainted = !tainted_by.is_empty();
    let mut fields = Map::new();
    fields.insert("tainted".into(), json!(tainted));
    fields.insert("tainted_by".into(), json!(tainted_by));
    if tainted && !tainted_ok {
        let why = "this boot made a write that taints saves (tainted_by), so a save now carries it: pass \
                   tainted_ok: true, with the user's OK to a tainted save, to save anyway. Nothing sent";
        return Err(Done::RefusedWith(why.into(), fields));
    }
    session.guard_saves()?;
    let channel = cx.channel()?;
    call.lap("check");

    let dir = &cx.live.saves;
    let before = saves::snapshot(dir);
    let reply = channel.call(Verb::Save {}, REPLY_MAX);
    call.lap("reply");
    let reply = reply.map_err(|e| e.done(fields.clone()))?;
    fields.insert("reply".into(), json!(reply.text));
    // The game names the save and writes it after the verb returns (feature tests 3: its .sav, .png and .json).
    let start = Instant::now();
    let begun = |now: &saves::Snapshot| {
        now.keys()
            .any(|n| !before.contains_key(n) && n.starts_with(W3_MANUAL) && n.ends_with(".sav"))
    };
    while !begun(&saves::snapshot(dir)) && start.elapsed() < SAVE_MAX {
        sleep(POLL);
    }
    let (_, quiet) = saves::wait_quiet(dir, QUIET, SAVE_MAX.saturating_sub(start.elapsed()));
    let secs = (start.elapsed().as_secs_f64() * 100.0).round() / 100.0;
    fields.insert("saves_wait".into(), json!({"s": secs, "quiet": quiet}));
    call.lap("files");

    let after = saves::snapshot(dir);
    let files = match saves::new_save(&before, &after, W3_AUTO_SAVES) {
        Ok(files) if files.is_empty() => {
            let why = format!(
                "no new save within {} s: the game may show a dialog that waits for OK (game_screenshot shows it)",
                SAVE_MAX.as_secs()
            );
            return Err(Done::Failed(why, fields));
        }
        Ok(files) if quiet => files,
        Ok(files) => {
            fields.insert("changed".into(), json!(files));
            let why = format!(
                "the new save was still being written after {} s, so quen didn't accept it",
                SAVE_MAX.as_secs()
            );
            return Err(Done::Failed(why, fields));
        }
        Err(changed) => {
            fields.insert("changed".into(), json!(changed));
            let why = "gamesaves changed beyond one new manual save (changed)";
            return Err(Done::Failed(why.into(), fields));
        }
    };
    cx.live
        .quen_saves
        .borrow_mut()
        .extend(files.iter().map(|name| (name.clone(), after[name])));

    let mut listed = Vec::new();
    let mut sav = None;
    for name in &files {
        let sha = sha256_file(&dir.join(name)).map_err(|e| e.to_string());
        if name.ends_with(".sav") {
            sav = Some((name, sha.clone()));
        }
        listed.push(json!({"file": name, "bytes": after[name].0, "sha256": sha.ok()}));
    }
    let (sav, sha) = sav.expect("new_save gives a .sav");
    let row = sha.and_then(|sha256| {
        let save = Save {
            game_id: cx.live.game,
            file: sav.clone(),
            sha256,
            note: note.map(String::from),
            tainted_by_boot: tainted.then_some(cx.live.boot),
            made_by_boot: Some(cx.live.boot),
        };
        open_ledger(cx.config)?
            .add_save(&save)
            .map_err(ledger_error)
    });
    match row {
        Ok(id) => call.row("saves", id),
        Err(e) => {
            fields.insert("ledger_error".into(), json!(e));
        }
    }
    call.lap("ledger");
    let name = sav.strip_suffix(".sav").unwrap_or(sav).to_lowercase();
    fields.insert("save".into(), json!(name));
    fields.insert("files".into(), json!(listed));
    Ok(fields)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::channel::tests::{fake_game, reply, served, token};
    use crate::game::tests::{Fake, PARTS};
    use quen_core::protocol::Request;
    use std::fs;
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    use std::thread::JoinHandle;
    use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

    /// A file of `data`, written at Unix second `secs`.
    fn touch(path: &Path, data: &str, secs: u64) {
        fs::write(path, data).unwrap();
        let file = fs::File::options().write(true).open(path).unwrap();
        file.set_modified(UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::from_secs(secs))
            .unwrap();
    }

    /// The Fake's session over a gamesaves folder holding the user's saves (a manual save, a quicksave, an autosave) as
    /// they were at the launch.
    fn session(fx: &Fake) -> (Session<'_>, PathBuf) {
        let dir = fx.dir.join("gamesaves");
        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        touch(&dir.join("ManualSave_user.sav"), "user save", 100);
        touch(&dir.join("ManualSave_user.png"), "user png", 100);
        touch(&dir.join("QuickSave.sav"), "quick", 100);
        touch(&dir.join("AutoSave_1.sav"), "auto", 100);
        let mut session = fx.session();
        let live = session.live.as_mut().unwrap();
        live.saves_before = saves::snapshot(&dir);
        live.handovers = crate::hands::Handovers::new(live.saves_before.clone());
        (session, dir)
    }

    fn run(session: &Session, args: Value) -> Value {
        let mut call = session.call(crate::mcp::Conn::nobody(), Value::Null, None);
        let done = super::call(session, &mut call, &args).map_or_else(|done| done, Done::Ok);
        session.envelope("game_save", call, done)
    }

    /// A stand-in game whose `save` runs `write` on `dir`, then answers as modQuen does.
    fn saving_game(fx: &Fake, dir: PathBuf, write: fn(&Path)) -> JoinHandle<Vec<Request>> {
        fake_game(
            &token(fx),
            1,
            Box::new(move |r| {
                assert_eq!(r.verb, Verb::Save {});
                write(&dir);
                vec![reply(r.id, true, "save requested", None)]
            }),
        )
    }

    /// The menu's "Empty save slot" as seen live: a new ManualSave's .sav, .png and .json; the game's autosave beside.
    fn new_save(dir: &Path) {
        for ext in ["sav", "png", "json"] {
            fs::write(dir.join(format!("ManualSave_new.{ext}")), ext).unwrap();
        }
        fs::write(dir.join("AutoSave_2.sav"), "auto").unwrap();
    }

    fn ledger_rows(fx: &Fake, sql: &str) -> Vec<Vec<Value>> {
        let config = fx.shared.config().as_ref().clone().unwrap();
        let ledger = open_ledger(&config).unwrap();
        ledger.query(sql, &[], Duration::from_secs(5)).unwrap().rows
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_game_writes_one_new_save_and_the_guard_passes_only_its_files() {
        let fx = served("save-ok");
        let (session, dir) = session(&fx);
        let user = saves::snapshot(&dir);
        let server = saving_game(&fx, dir.clone(), new_save);
        let args = json!({"token": "tok", "user_ok": true, "note": "a test save"});
        let out = run(&session, args);
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["save"], "manualsave_new", "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["tainted"], false, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["reply"], "save requested", "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["saves_wait"]["quiet"], true, "{out}");
        let files: Vec<&str> = out["files"]
            .as_array()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .map(|f| f["file"].as_str().unwrap())
            .collect();
        let three = [
            "ManualSave_new.json",
            "ManualSave_new.png",
            "ManualSave_new.sav",
        ];
        assert_eq!(files, three);
        let sha = sha256_file(&dir.join(three[2])).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(out["files"][2]["sha256"], sha, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(server.join().unwrap().len(), 1);
        let now = saves::snapshot(&dir);
        assert!(
            user.iter().all(|(name, was)| now.get(name) == Some(was)),
            "nothing the user had changed"
        );
        let sql = "SELECT id, file, made_by_boot, tainted_by_boot, note FROM saves";
        let row = vec![
            out["ledger"]["saves"][0].clone(),
            json!(three[2]),
            json!(1),
            Value::Null,
            json!("a test save"),
        ];
        assert_eq!(ledger_rows(&fx, sql), [row]);

        // The guard passes quen's files while they are as quen found them, and nothing else: a menu save, the menu
        // overwriting quen's save and a quicksave each end the session (session.rs guard_after).
        assert_eq!(session.guard_saves(), Ok(()));
        for (name, data) in [
            ("ManualSave_menu.sav", "the menu's save"),
            ("ManualSave_new.sav", "the menu overwrote quen's"),
            ("QuickSave.sav", "a quicksave"),
        ] {
            let path = dir.join(name);
            let was = now.get(name).copied();
            let kept = fs::read(&path).ok();
            fs::write(&path, data).unwrap();
            let why = session.guard_saves().unwrap_err();
            assert!(why.contains(name), "{name}: {why}");
            match (kept, was) {
                (Some(bytes), Some((_, Some(t)))) => {
                    fs::write(&path, bytes).unwrap();
                    let file = fs::File::options().write(true).open(&path).unwrap();
                    file.set_modified(t).unwrap();
                }
                _ => fs::remove_file(&path).unwrap(), // this test's own synthetic file
            }
            assert_eq!(session.guard_saves(), Ok(()), "{name} put back");
        }
    }

    /// A save that came with any other change (here the stand-in also overwrites the user's save) fails, none of it
    /// accepted, so the guard ends the session.
    #[test]
    fn anything_beside_one_new_save_fails_and_the_guard_ends_the_session() {
        let fx = served("save-overwrite");
        let (session, dir) = session(&fx);
        let server = saving_game(&fx, dir, |dir| {
            new_save(dir);
            fs::write(dir.join("ManualSave_user.sav"), "overwritten").unwrap();
        });
        let out = run(&session, json!({"token": "tok", "user_ok": true}));
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], false, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["refused"], false, "{out}");
        let why = out["reason"].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(why.contains("beyond one new manual save"), "{out}");
        let changed = out["changed"].as_array().unwrap();
        assert!(changed.contains(&json!("ManualSave_user.sav")), "{out}");
        let live = session.live.as_ref().unwrap();
        assert!(live.quen_saves.borrow().is_empty());
        assert!(session.guard_saves().is_err());
        server.join().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn refuses_before_sending() {
        let fx = served("save-refuse");
        let state = fx.dir.join("game/bin/x64_dx12/W3QuenState.log");
        let (session, dir) = session(&fx);
        let user = saves::snapshot(&dir);
        // The game's own lock: refused with its words in game_text.
        let server = fake_game(
            &token(&fx),
            1,
            Box::new(|r| vec![reply(r.id, false, "the game locks saves now", None)]),
        );
        let ok = json!({"token": "tok", "user_ok": true});
        let locked = run(&session, ok.clone());
        assert_eq!(locked["refused"], true, "{locked}");
        assert_eq!(locked["game_text"], "the game locks saves now", "{locked}");
        for args in [
            json!({"token": "tok"}),
            json!({"token": "tok", "user_ok": false}),
            json!({"token": "nope", "user_ok": true}),
            json!({"token": "tok", "user_ok": true, "slot": 0}),
            json!({"token": "tok", "user_ok": true, "note": 7}),
            json!({"token": "tok", "user_ok": true, "note": "x".repeat(NOTE_MAX + 1)}),
            json!({"token": "tok", "user_ok": true, "tainted_ok": "yes"}),
        ] {
            let out = run(&session, args.clone());
            assert_eq!(out["refused"], true, "{args}: {out}");
        }
        // Every state but plain gameplay: no flags yet, the main menu, photo mode, a scene, a cutscene, a fade, the
        // dialogue flag. Combat (64) is the game's own lock's to refuse.
        for flags in ["", "0", "129", "17", "33", "257", "513"] {
            let line = match flags {
                "" => String::new(),
                f => format!("push flags={f}\n"),
            };
            fs::write(&state, line).unwrap();
            let out = run(&session, ok.clone());
            let why = out["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
            assert!(
                out["refused"] == true && why.contains("plain gameplay"),
                "{flags:?}: {out}"
            );
        }
        fs::write(&state, "push flags=65\n").unwrap();
        // A write that taints saves: refused without tainted_ok, naming it.
        let patch = json!({"what": "mem_patch cull", "t": "2026-10-19T00:00:00Z", "taints": true});
        let live = session.live.as_ref().unwrap();
        live.patches.borrow_mut().push((SystemTime::now(), patch));
        let tainted = run(&session, ok.clone());
        assert_eq!(tainted["refused"], true, "{tainted}");
        assert_eq!(
            tainted["tainted_by"][0]["what"], "mem_patch cull",
            "{tainted}"
        );
        // Without the package: needs.
        for part in PARTS {
            fs::remove_file(fx.dir.join("game").join(part)).unwrap(); // this test's own synthetic files
        }
        let none = run(
            &session,
            json!({"token": "tok", "user_ok": true, "tainted_ok": true}),
        );
        let need = &none["needs"][0]["dependency"];
        assert_eq!(need, doctor::PACKAGE.name, "{none}");
        assert_eq!(
            server.join().unwrap().len(),
            1,
            "only the first reached the game"
        );
        assert_eq!(saves::snapshot(&dir), user, "nothing written");
        assert!(ledger_rows(&fx, "SELECT id FROM saves").is_empty());
        // No session.
        let out = run(&Session::new(&fx.shared, None), ok);
        let why = out["reason"].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(why.contains("no live session"), "{out}");
    }

    /// With tainted_ok after a tainting write, the save is made, and tainted in its result and its ledger row; an ASI's
    /// mode switch doesn't taint.
    #[test]
    fn a_tainted_save_needs_tainted_ok_and_is_marked() {
        let fx = served("save-tainted");
        let (session, dir) = session(&fx);
        let live = session.live.as_ref().unwrap();
        for (what, taints) in [("channel teleport", true), ("W3BoneFix.asi mode", false)] {
            let patch = json!({"what": what, "t": "2026-10-19T00:00:00Z", "taints": taints});
            live.patches.borrow_mut().push((SystemTime::now(), patch));
        }
        let server = saving_game(&fx, dir, new_save);
        let args = json!({"token": "tok", "user_ok": true, "tainted_ok": true});
        let out = run(&session, args);
        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
        assert_eq!(out["tainted"], true, "{out}");
        let by = out["tainted_by"].as_array().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(by.len(), 1, "{out}");
        let sql = "SELECT tainted_by_boot, made_by_boot FROM saves";
        assert_eq!(ledger_rows(&fx, sql), [[json!(1), json!(1)]]);
        server.join().unwrap();
    }
}
```

```rs
//! The scene tools (quen-w3 0.1.13; the runner design's phase 4): `world_frame`, `world_ground`, `world_ray` and
//! `world_nav` read the scene through the game's scripts (the channel's scene.frame, scene.ground, scene.ray and nav.line
//! verbs) and change nothing; `world_map` reads the space around a point into a top-down map with them (a grid, a
//! street's width profile, or walkers' look-aheads), its files and captures rows quen's own; `game_frame` sets the
//! photo-mode camera to frame a subject from its sides, each pose checked first with a sphere sweep and then set with
//! no-clip; `game_place` puts the player on the navmesh. The placement maths is quen-core's `scene`, the map's `map`.

/// The runner design's per-tick caps for readings (§4.4), until an overhead boot measures them.

    ("traces", "grid"),

    "/layers",
];

pub fn tools() -> Vec<Value> {
    let vec3 = |what: &str| json!({"type": "array", "items": {"type": "number"}, "minItems": 3, "maxItems": 3, "description": what});
    let segments = json!({
        "type": "array", "minItems": 1, "maxItems": MAX_QUERIES,
        "description": "1 to 16 segments",
        "items": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"from": vec3("[x, y, z] in metres"), "to": vec3("[x, y, z] in metres")},
            "required": ["from", "to"], "additionalProperties": false,
        },
    });
    let reads = "Changes nothing, taints no save; runs while the user has the controls. quen-w3 0.1.13 or later. \
        budget: the rays and queries of its one game tick (cap 64 and 16; their frame-time cost unmeasured). Refused, \
        nothing sent: wrong token, an older package (with needs), no loaded game in quen's state, a value past its \
        range. Failed: no reply within 5 s";
    vec![
        json!({
            "name": "world_frame",
            "description": format!("Read what the rendered camera sees (the free camera's from quen-w3 0.1.18): the \
                alive actors within radius of it, the player among them, nearest first, at most max; found counts \
                all; camera is its pose (rot as game_camera gives it). Each: id, name, \

/// One of [`tools`], from game.rs's dispatch.
pub(crate) fn call(
    session: &Session,
    call: &mut Call,
    name: &str,
    args: &Value,
) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    match name {
        "world_frame" => frame_read(session, call, args),
        "world_ground" => ground(session, call, args),
        "world_ray" | "world_nav" => ray(session, call, name, args),
        "world_map" => world_map(session, call, args),
        "game_frame" => frame(session, call, args),
        "game_place" => place(session, call, args),
        _ => Err(Done::Refused(format!("unknown tool {name:?}"))),
    }
}

/// Refused with needs, nothing sent, without quen-w3 0.1.13; refused unless quen's state shows a loaded game (and photo
/// mode when `photo`).
fn ready(cx: &Ctx, tool: &str, photo: bool) -> Result<(), Done> {
    doctor::installed(&[&doctor::PACKAGE], cx.config, tool)?;
    doctor::package_at_least(cx.config, doctor::BEFORE_SCENE, tool, "0.1.13")?;
    let last = cx.last_flags();
    if !last.is_some_and(|f| f & VALID != 0 && (!photo || in_photo(f))) {
        let need = if photo { "photo mode" } else { "a loaded game" };
        return Err(format!(
            "quen's state shows {}: {tool} needs {need}. Nothing sent",
            shown(last)
        )
        .into());
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// One verb on a connection of its own, its reply; the verb's own checks (quen-core's) before anything is sent.
fn send(cx: &Ctx, verb: Verb, fields: &Fields) -> Result<Reply, Done> {
    let channel = cx
        .channel()
        .map_err(|why| Done::Failed(why, fields.clone()))?;
    channel
        .call(verb, REPLY_MAX)
        .map_err(|e| e.done(fields.clone()))
}

/// A verb's reply data as an array of `n`.
fn items(reply: &Reply, n: usize, fields: &Fields) -> Result<Vec<Value>, Done> {
    match reply.data.as_ref().and_then(Value::as_array) {
        Some(a) if a.len() == n => Ok(a.clone()),
        _ => Err(Done::Failed(
            format!("the game's read-back isn't {n} items: {:?}", reply.data),
            fields.clone(),
        )),
    }
}

/// What a read cast in its tick, against the design's caps.
fn budget(rays: usize, queries: usize) -> Value {
    json!({"ticks": 1, "rays": rays, "queries": queries, "cap": {"rays": RAYS_PER_TICK, "queries": MAX_QUERIES},
           "cost_ms_per_frame": "unmeasured"})
}

/// An optional number argument within `range`, `default` when absent.
fn num(
    args: &Value,
    key: &str,
    default: f64,
    range: std::ops::RangeInclusive<f64>,
) -> Result<f64, String> {
    match args.get(key) {
        None => Ok(default),
        Some(v) => v.as_f64().filter(|x| range.contains(x)).ok_or(format!(
            "{key} must be a number from {} to {}",
            range.start(),
            range.end()
        )),
    }
}

/// An optional whole-number argument within `range`, `default` when absent.
fn whole(
    args: &Value,
    key: &str,
    default: u32,
    range: std::ops::RangeInclusive<u32>,
) -> Result<u32, String> {
    match args.get(key) {
        None => Ok(default),
        Some(v) => v
            .as_u64()
            .and_then(|n| u32::try_from(n).ok())
            .filter(|n| range.contains(n))
            .ok_or(format!(
                "{key} must be a whole number from {} to {}",
                range.start(),
                range.end()
            )),
    }
}

/// `v` as `N` numbers.
fn numbers<const N: usize>(v: &Value) -> Option<[f64; N]> {
    let n: Vec<f64> = v
        .as_array()?
        .iter()
        .map(Value::as_f64)
        .collect::<Option<_>>()?;
    n.try_into().ok()
}

/// `[x, y, z]` of a read-back, if it is one.
fn point(v: &Value) -> Option<[f64; 3]> {
    numbers::<3>(v)
}

/// 1 to [`MAX_QUERIES`] items of `key`, each read by `one`.
fn list<T>(
    args: &Value,
    key: &str,
    one: impl Fn(&Value) -> Option<T>,
    what: &str,
) -> Result<Vec<T>, String> {
    let bad = || format!("{key} must be 1 to {MAX_QUERIES} {what}");
    let a = args.get(key).and_then(Value::as_array).ok_or_else(bad)?;
    if a.is_empty() || a.len() > MAX_QUERIES {
        return Err(bad());
    }
    a.iter().map(|v| one(v).ok_or_else(bad)).collect()
}

/// A segment `{from, to}`.
fn segment(v: &Value) -> Option<([f64; 3], [f64; 3])> {
    let map = v.as_object()?;
    (map.len() == 2).then_some(())?;
    Some((point(&v["from"])?, point(&v["to"])?))
}

fn flat(v: impl IntoIterator<Item = f64>) -> Vec<f32> {
    v.into_iter().map(|x| x as f32).collect()
}

/// A camera's [pitch, yaw, roll] in a read-back, each in (-180, 180] on a 0.0001 grid, as game_camera reads them
/// (finding 91: the director's pitch read 350 for -10): world_frame's and game_freecam's.
pub(crate) fn wrap_rot(rot: Option<&mut Value>) {
    for a in rot.and_then(Value::as_array_mut).into_iter().flatten() {
        if let Some(deg) = a.as_f64() {
            *a = json!((scene::wrap(deg) * 1e4).round() / 1e4);
        }
    }
}

fn frame_read(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let cx = ctx(session, args, &["radius", "max", "points"])?;
    let radius = num(args, "radius", 30.0, 0.0..=f64::from(MAX_ACTORS_RADIUS))?;
    if radius <= 0.0 {
        return Err("radius must be above 0".to_string().into());
    }
    let verb = Verb::SceneFrame {
        radius: radius as f32,
        max: whole(args, "max", MAX_FRAME, 1..=MAX_FRAME)?,
        points: whole(args, "points", 3, 0..=3)?,
        at: None,
        entity_id: None,
    };
    ready(&cx, "world_frame", false)?;
    if cx.live.freecam.get() {
        // quen-w3 0.1.17 projected x, y, in_front and share from the gameplay camera under the free camera (boot 238).
        let before = [doctor::BEFORE_FREECAM, &["quen-w3 0.1.17"]].concat();
        let tool = "world_frame with the free camera on";
        doctor::package_at_least(cx.config, &before, tool, "0.1.18")?;
    }
    call.lap("check");
    let mut fields = Map::new();
    let reply = send(&cx, verb, &fields)?;
    call.lap("reply");
    let Some(Value::Object(data)) = reply.data else {
        return Err(Done::Failed(
            "the game's read-back isn't an object".into(),
            fields,
        ));
    };
    fields.extend(data);
    wrap_rot(fields.get_mut("camera").and_then(|c| c.get_mut("rot")));
    let entities = fields["entities"].as_array().cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    let rays = entities
        .iter()
        .map(|e| {
            ["head", "torso", "origin"]
                .iter()
                .filter(|k| !e["visible"][**k].is_null())
                .count()
        })
        .sum();
    fields.insert("budget".into(), budget(rays, entities.len()));
    Ok(fields)
}

fn ground(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let cx = ctx(session, args, &["points", "range", "radius", "search"])?;
    let points = list(args, "points", point, "points of [x, y, z]")?;
    let range = num(args, "range", 10.0, 0.0..=f64::from(MAX_GROUND_RANGE))?;
    let verb = Verb::SceneGround {
        xyz: flat(points.iter().flatten().copied()),
        range: range as f32,
        radius: num(args, "radius", 0.0, 0.0..=f64::from(MAX_GROUND_RADIUS))? as f32,
        search: num(args, "search", 0.0, 0.0..=f64::from(MAX_GROUND_SEARCH))? as f32,
    };
    check(&verb)?;
    ready(&cx, "world_ground", false)?;
    call.lap("check");
    let mut fields = Map::new();
    let reply = send(&cx, verb, &fields)?;
    call.lap("reply");
    let read = items(&reply, points.len(), &fields)?;
    let read: Vec<Value> = points
        .iter()
        .zip(read)
        .map(|(p, mut r)| {
            r["at"] = json!(p);
            r["water_depth"] = json!(map::water_depth(&r["water_depth"]));
            r
        })
        .collect();
    fields.insert("points".into(), json!(read));
    fields.insert("budget".into(), budget(points.len(), points.len()));
    Ok(fields)
}

/// world_ray and world_nav: one verb per call over segments.
fn ray(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, name: &str, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let nav = name == "world_nav";
    let size = if nav { "width" } else { "radius" };
    let cx = ctx(session, args, &["segments", size])?;
    let segments = list(args, "segments", segment, "segments of {from, to}")?;
    let coords = flat(
        segments
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|(a, b)| a.iter().chain(b).copied()),
    );
    let verb = match nav {
        true => Verb::NavLine {
            segments: coords,
            width: num(args, "width", 0.4, 0.0..=f64::from(MAX_NAV_WIDTH))? as f32,
        },
        false => Verb::SceneRay {
            segments: coords,
            radius: num(args, "radius", 0.0, 0.0..=f64::from(MAX_SWEEP_RADIUS))? as f32,
        },
    };
    check(&verb)?;
    ready(&cx, name, false)?;
    call.lap("check");
    let mut fields = Map::new();
    let reply = send(&cx, verb, &fields)?;
    call.lap("reply");
    let read = items(&reply, segments.len(), &fields)?;
    let read: Vec<Value> = segments
        .iter()
        .zip(read)
        .map(|((a, b), mut r)| {
            r["from"] = json!(a);
            r["to"] = json!(b);
            // FLT_MAX (3.4e38): no obstacle within width of the line (every segment at width 0, the 0.1.15 live check).
            if nav && r["edge_m"].as_f64().is_some_and(|d| d > NO_OBSTACLE) {
                r["edge_m"] = Value::Null;
            }
            r
        })
        .collect();
    fields.insert("segments".into(), json!(read));
    let rays = if nav { 0 } else { segments.len() };
    fields.insert("budget".into(), budget(rays, segments.len()));
    Ok(fields)
}

/// The protocol's own checks of a verb, as a refusal before anything is sent.
fn check(verb: &Verb) -> Result<(), String> {
    let request = quen_core::protocol::Request {
        id: 1,
        ttl_ms: 0,
        verb: verb.clone(),
    };
    quen_core::protocol::encode_request(&request)
        .map(|_| ())
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

/// game_frame's subject: its world_frame entry, found within `radius` of the player (scene.frame around the player's
/// position): the player's own entry without an id, else the entity with that id.
fn subject(cx: &Ctx, id: Option<i32>, fields: &Fields) -> Result<Value, Done> {
    let world = send(cx, Verb::WorldGet {}, fields)?;
    let at = world.data.as_ref().and_then(|d| point(&d["player"]["pos"]));
    let at = at.ok_or_else(|| {
        Done::Failed(
            "world.get read back no player position".into(),
            fields.clone(),
        )
    })?;
    let verb = Verb::SceneFrame {
        radius: if id.is_some() { MAX_ACTORS_RADIUS } else { 2.0 },
        max: MAX_FRAME,
        points: 0,
        at: Some(at.map(|x| x as f32)),
        entity_id: id,
    };
    let reply = send(cx, verb, fields)?;
    let entities = reply
        .data
        .as_ref()
        .and_then(|d| d["entities"].as_array().cloned())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let found = entities.into_iter().find(|e| match id {
        Some(id) => e["id"] == id,
        None => e["player"] == true,
    });
    found.ok_or_else(|| {
        let who = id.map_or("the player".to_string(), |id| {
            format!("no entity of id {id} within 100 m of the player")
        });
        Done::Refused(format!("{who}: not found by scene.frame. Nothing set"))
    })
}

/// A side of game_frame's `sides`: its label (also the capture's suffix) and degrees.
fn sides(args: &Value) -> Result<Vec<(String, f64)>, String> {
    let Some(v) = args.get("sides") else {
        return Ok(vec![("front".into(), 0.0)]);
    };
    let bad = || {
        format!(
            "sides: 1 to {MAX_SIDES} of front, left, back, right or whole degrees from -180 to 180"
        )
    };
    let a = v
        .as_array()
        .filter(|a| !a.is_empty() && a.len() <= MAX_SIDES)
        .ok_or_else(bad)?;
    let mut out: Vec<(String, f64)> = Vec::new();
    for s in a {
        let s = s.as_str().ok_or_else(bad)?;
        let side = match (scene::side(s), s.parse::<i32>()) {
            (Some(d), _) => (s.to_string(), d),
            (None, Ok(d)) if (-180..=180).contains(&d) => (format!("y{d}"), f64::from(d)),
            _ => return Err(bad()),
        };
        if out.iter().any(|(label, _)| *label == side.0) {
            return Err(format!("sides: {} twice", side.0));
        }
        out.push(side);
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// The world_frame fields of a framing's reading.
fn reading(e: &Value) -> Value {
    let keys = [
        "in_front",
        "in_view",
        "x",
        "y",
        "share",
        "box_whole",
        "distance",
        "visible",
        "visible_points",
    ];
    json!(Map::from_iter(
        keys.iter().map(|k| (k.to_string(), e[*k].clone()))
    ))
}

fn frame(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let known = [
        "entity_id",
        "sides",
        "distance",
        "height",
        "fov",
        "aim",
        "clearance",
        "tag",
        "settle_ms",
    ];
    let cx = ctx(session, args, &known)?;
    let id = match args.get("entity_id") {
        None => None,
        Some(v) => Some(
            v.as_i64()
                .and_then(|n| i32::try_from(n).ok())
                .ok_or("entity_id must be a whole number in int's range".to_string())?,
        ),
    };
    let sides = sides(args)?;
    let framing = |side| -> Result<Framing, String> {
        Ok(Framing {
            side,
            distance: num(args, "distance", 3.0, 0.5..=50.0)?,
            height: num(args, "height", 0.0, -10.0..=10.0)?,
            fov: num(args, "fov", 40.0, FOV)?,
        })
    };
    framing(0.0)?;
    let aim = match args.get("aim").map(Value::as_str) {
        None => "torso",
        Some(Some(a @ ("head" | "torso" | "origin"))) => a,
        Some(_) => return Err("aim is head, torso or origin".to_string().into()),
    };
    let clearance = num(args, "clearance", 0.3, 0.05..=f64::from(MAX_SWEEP_RADIUS))?;
    let settle = Duration::from_millis(u64::from(whole(
        args,
        "settle_ms",
        SETTLE_MS as u32,
        0..=SETTLE_MAX_MS as u32,
    )?));
    let tag = args.get("tag").map(tag).transpose()?;
    if let Some(tag) = &tag {
        let dir = cx.config.capture_root().join(&cx.live.id);
        if let Some((label, _)) = sides
            .iter()
            .find(|(label, _)| dir.join(format!("{tag}-{label}.png")).exists())
        {
            return Err(format!("{tag}-{label}.png exists: pick a tag new in this session").into());
        }
    }
    ready(&cx, "game_frame", true)?;
    let mut fields = Map::new();
    let body = subject(&cx, id, &fields)?;
    let at = match aim {
        "origin" => point(&body["pos"]),
        bone => point(&body[bone]),
    };
    let at = at.ok_or_else(|| {
        format!("the subject has no {aim} bone: aim at origin, or at another point")
    })?;
    let heading = body["heading"].as_f64().unwrap_or_default();
    let subject_id = body["id"].as_i64().and_then(|n| i32::try_from(n).ok());
    fields.insert(
        "subject".into(),
        json!({"id": body["id"], "name": body["name"], "entity": body["entity"], "player": body["player"],
               "pos": body["pos"], "heading": body["heading"], "aim": aim, "aim_at": at}),
    );
    let poses: Vec<Pose> = sides
        .iter()
        .map(|(_, deg)| framing(*deg).map(|f| scene::frame_pose(at, heading, &f)))
        .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
    // Every pose's space checked before any is set: a sphere sweep from the aim point to the camera. The origin is at
    // the feet, on the ground: a sphere there touches it at once (0.0095 m in the 0.1.15 live check), so it starts above.
    let from = match aim {
        "origin" => [at[0], at[1], at[2] + clearance + ORIGIN_LIFT_M],
        _ => at,
    };
    let segments = flat(
        poses
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|p| from.iter().chain(&p.pos).copied()),
    );
    let sweep = send(
        &cx,
        Verb::SceneRay {
            segments,
            radius: clearance as f32,
        },
        &fields,
    )?;
    let swept = items(&sweep, poses.len(), &fields)?;
    let sweep: Vec<Value> = sides
        .iter()
        .zip(&swept)
        .map(|((label, _), r)| json!({"side": label, "clear": r["hit"] == false, "hit": r["pos"], "distance": r["distance"]}))
        .collect();
    fields.insert("sweep".into(), json!(sweep));
    let blocked: Vec<String> = sweep
        .iter()
        .filter(|s| s["clear"] == false)
        .map(|s| {
            format!(
                "{} at {} m",
                s["side"].as_str().unwrap_or_default(),
                s["distance"]
            )
        })
        .collect();
    if !blocked.is_empty() {
        let why = format!(
            "the sphere sweep (radius {clearance} m) from the subject's {aim} towards the camera hits geometry: {}. \
             Nothing set (a shorter distance, another height or side)",
            blocked.join(", ")
        );
        return Err(Done::RefusedWith(why, fields));
    }
    call.lap("check");
    // Its captures: quen's status line down once for all the sides (status.rs).
    if tag.is_some() {
        crate::status::hide(&cx, call, false).map_err(Done::Refused)?;
    }
    let noclip = send(&cx, Verb::CamNoclip { on: true }, &fields)?;
    fields.insert("noclip".into(), json!(noclip.text));
    let mut done = Vec::new();
    for ((label, _), pose) in sides.iter().zip(&poses) {
        if call.stopped() {
            fields.insert("sides".into(), json!(done));
            return Err(Done::Failed(
                format!("cancelled after {} of {} sides", done.len(), sides.len()),
                fields,
            ));
        }
        let set = Verb::CamSet {
            pos: pose.pos.map(|x| x as f32),
            rot: pose.rot.map(|x| x as f32),
            fov: Some(pose.fov as f32),
        };
        let mut side = Map::from_iter([
            ("side".to_string(), json!(label)),
            ("pose".into(), camera::pose_json(pose)),
        ]);
        let failed =
            |why: String, side: Map<String, Value>, mut done: Vec<Value>, mut fields: Fields| {
                done.push(json!(side));
                fields.insert("sides".into(), json!(done));
                Done::Failed(why, fields)
            };
        let got = send(&cx, set, &fields)
            .and_then(|r| camera::read_back(&r).map_err(|why| Done::Failed(why, fields.clone())));
        let (_, got) = match got {
            Ok(got) => got,
            Err(e) => {
                return Err(failed(
                    format!("side {label}: {}", why(e)),
                    side,
                    done,
                    fields,
                ));
            }
        };
        side.insert("off".into(), camera::off_json(camera::off(&got, pose)));
        if let Some(why) = camera::short(&got, pose) {
            return Err(failed(format!("side {label}: {why}"), side, done, fields));
        }
        sleep(settle);
        let read = Verb::SceneFrame {
            radius: (pose_distance(pose, at) + 5.0).min(f64::from(MAX_ACTORS_RADIUS)) as f32,
            max: 1,
            points: 3,
            at: None,
            entity_id: subject_id,
        };
        let entity =
            send(&cx, read, &fields).map(|r| r.data.and_then(|d| d["entities"].get(0).cloned()));
        match entity {
            Ok(Some(e)) => side.insert("reading".into(), reading(&e)),
            Ok(None) => side.insert(
                "reading".into(),
                json!("the subject isn't within the read's radius of the camera"),
            ),
            Err(e) => {
                return Err(failed(
                    format!("side {label}, reading: {}", why(e)),
                    side,
                    done,
                    fields,
                ));
            }
        };
        if let Some(tag) = &tag {
            match camera::grab(session, &cx.live.token, &format!("{tag}-{label}"), "sdr") {
                // The 0.1.12 live check: a plan's result lacked them. Each side's file and row are game_frame's.
                Ok((id, path)) => {
                    call.row("captures", id);
                    if let Some(path) = path {
                        call.artifact(&path);
                    }
                    side.insert("capture_id".into(), json!(id))
                }
                Err(e) => {
                    return Err(failed(
                        format!("side {label}, capture: {}", why(e)),
                        side,
                        done,
                        fields,
                    ));
                }
            };
        }
        call.lap(&format!("side_{label}"));
        done.push(json!(side));
    }
    fields.insert("sides".into(), json!(done));
    Ok(fields)
}

/// The camera's distance from `at`.
fn pose_distance(p: &Pose, at: [f64; 3]) -> f64 {
    (0..3)
        .map(|c| (p.pos[c] - at[c]).powi(2))
        .sum::<f64>()
        .sqrt()
}

/// A failure's or refusal's reason.
fn why(done: Done) -> String {
    match done {
        Done::Refused(why)
        | Done::RefusedWith(why, _)
        | Done::Needs(why, _)
        | Done::Failed(why, _) => why,
        Done::Ok(_) => String::new(),
    }
}

fn place(session: &Session, call: &mut Call, args: &Value) -> Result<Fields, Done> {
    let cx = ctx(session, args, &["pos", "face", "yaw", "radius", "search"])?;
    let pos: Vec<f64> = args
        .get("pos")
        .and_then(Value::as_array)
        .filter(|a| (2..=3).contains(&a.len()))
        .and_then(|a| a.iter().map(Value::as_f64).collect())
        .ok_or("pos must be [x, y] or [x, y, z]".to_string())?;
    let face = match args.get("face") {
        None => None,
        Some(v) => Some(numbers::<2>(v).ok_or("face must be [x, y]".to_string())?),
    };
    let yaw = match args.get("yaw") {
        None => None,
        Some(v) => Some(
            v.as_f64()
                .filter(|y| y.is_finite())
                .ok_or("yaw must be a number".to_string())?,
        ),
    };
    if face.is_some() && yaw.is_some() {
        return Err("face or yaw, not both".to_string().into());
    }
    let radius = num(args, "radius", 0.5, 0.1..=f64::from(MAX_GROUND_RADIUS))?;
    let search = num(args, "search", 0.0, 0.0..=f64::from(MAX_GROUND_SEARCH))?;
    ready(&cx, "game_place", false)?;
    let mut fields = Map::new();
    let world = send(&cx, Verb::WorldGet {}, &fields)?
        .data
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let player = &world["player"];
    let z = match pos.get(2) {
        Some(z) => *z,
        None => {
            point(&player["pos"]).ok_or("world.get read back no player position".to_string())?[2]
        }
    };
    let verb = Verb::SceneGround {
        xyz: flat([pos[0], pos[1], z]),
        range: PLACE_RANGE,
        radius: radius as f32,
        search: search as f32,
    };
    check(&verb)?;
    let ground = send(&cx, verb, &fields)?;
    let ground = items(&ground, 1, &fields)?.remove(0);
    // What the placement reads: the navmesh. The read's own ground ray, from 5 m up, can hit an overhang (the 0.1.12 live
    // check: 15.236 at a wall's foot), so it isn't reported here.
    let navmesh = json!({"nav_z": ground["nav_z"], "free": ground["free"], "safe": ground["safe"]});
    fields.insert("navmesh".into(), navmesh);
    let Some(nav_z) = ground["nav_z"].as_f64() else {
        let why = format!(
            "no navmesh within {PLACE_RANGE} m of z {z} at x {}, y {}: nothing moved",
            pos[0], pos[1]
        );
        return Err(Done::RefusedWith(why, fields));
    };
    let mut spot = [pos[0], pos[1], nav_z];
    if ground["free"] == false {
        match point(&ground["safe"]) {
            Some(safe) if search > 0.0 => {
                let moved = ((safe[0] - spot[0]).powi(2) + (safe[1] - spot[1]).powi(2)).sqrt();
                fields.insert("moved_m".into(), json!((moved * 1e3).round() / 1e3));
                spot = safe;
            }
            _ => {
                let why = format!(
                    "the navmesh circle of radius {radius} m there isn't free{}: nothing moved",
                    if search > 0.0 {
                        ", and no safe spot was found within search"
                    } else {
                        " (search finds a safe spot near it)"
                    }
                );
                return Err(Done::RefusedWith(why, fields));
            }
        }
    }
    let yaw = match (face, yaw) {
        (Some(f), _) => scene::facing([spot[0], spot[1]], f)
            .ok_or("face is the spot itself: give another point, or yaw".to_string())?,
        (None, Some(y)) => scene::wrap(y),
        (None, None) => player["heading"].as_f64().unwrap_or_default(),
    };
    call.lap("check");
    let teleport = Verb::Teleport {
        pos: spot.map(|x| x as f32),
        rot: [0.0, yaw as f32, 0.0],
    };
    let what = format!(
        "channel {}",
        serde_json::to_string(&teleport).unwrap_or_default()
    );
    let (mut journal, step) = cx.journal(&what, None, true)?;
    let sent = send(&cx, teleport, &fields);
    let ran = !matches!(sent, Err(Done::Refused(_) | Done::RefusedWith(..)));
    if let Some(note) = cx.settle(&mut journal, step, ran) {
        fields.insert("journal_note".into(), json!(note));
    }
    let reply = sent?;
    fields.insert("reply".into(), json!(reply.text));
    fields.insert("sent".into(), json!({"pos": spot, "yaw": yaw}));
    call.lap("teleport");
    sleep(PLACE_READ);
    let back = send(&cx, Verb::WorldGet {}, &fields)?
        .data
        .unwrap_or_default();
    fields.insert("world".into(), back.clone());
    // Finding 91: the game sets the player on the ground below the navmesh z sent (0.4-1.3 m in boot 190).
    let placed = json!({"pos": back["player"]["pos"], "yaw": back["player"]["heading"]});
    fields.insert("placed".into(), placed);
    let off = point(&back["player"]["pos"])
        .map(|p| ((p[0] - spot[0]).powi(2) + (p[1] - spot[1]).powi(2)).sqrt());
    fields.insert("off_m".into(), json!(off.map(|o| (o * 1e3).round() / 1e3)));
    call.lap("read");
    match off {
        Some(off) if off <= PLACE_OFF_M => Ok(fields),
        _ => Err(Done::Failed(
            format!("the player read back more than {PLACE_OFF_M} m from the spot in xy (off_m)"),
            fields,
        )),
    }
}

/// A capture's tag: 1 to 58 letters, digits, _ or -.
fn tag(v: &Value) -> Result<String, String> {
    let t = v.as_str().filter(|t| {
        (1..=58).contains(&t.len())
            && t.chars()
                .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || "_-".contains(c))
    });
    Ok(t.ok_or("tag: 1-58 letters, digits, _ or -".to_string())?
        .to_string())
}

/// What world_map's reads cast: the verbs, their points or segments, the rays among them, and when the first went.
struct Reads<'a, 's> {
    cx: &'a Ctx<'s>,
    calls: usize,
    queries: usize,
    rays: usize,
    start: Instant,
}

impl Reads<'_, '_> {
    fn send(&mut self, verb: Verb, fields: &Fields) -> Result<Reply, Done> {
        let (queries, rays) = match &verb {
            Verb::SceneGround { xyz, .. } => (xyz.len() / 3, xyz.len() / 3),
            Verb::SceneRay { segments, .. } => (segments.len() / 6, segments.len() / 6),
            Verb::NavLine { segments, .. } => (segments.len() / 6, 0),
            _ => (0, 0),
        };
        let reply = send(self.cx, verb, fields)?;
        self.calls += 1;
        self.queries += queries;
        self.rays += rays;
        Ok(reply)
    }

    /// Each verb one game tick, its frame-time cost unmeasured; never inside a measure window.
    fn budget(&self) -> Value {
        json!({"calls": self.calls, "ticks": self.calls, "queries": self.queries, "rays": self.rays,
               "span_s": (self.start.elapsed().as_secs_f64() * 100.0).round() / 100.0,
               "cost_ms_per_frame": "unmeasured", "in_window": false})
    }
}

/// The occupants: one world.actors read within `reach` of the player (3-D, through walls; the protocol's cap), each on
/// `frame` and its level or not; `found` and when it came.
fn occupants(
    reads: &mut Reads,
    frame: &Frame,
    z_range: f64,
    reach: f64,
    class: &Option<String>,
    fields: &Fields,
) -> Result<(Vec<map::Occupant>, Value), Done> {
    let radius = reach.min(f64::from(MAX_ACTORS_RADIUS));
    let verb = Verb::WorldActors {
        radius: radius as f32,
        max: MAX_ACTORS,
        tag: None,
        class: class.clone(),
    };
    let data = reads.send(verb, fields)?.data.unwrap_or_default();
    let list = map::occupants(&data, frame, z_range)
        .map_err(|why| Done::Failed(format!("world.actors: {why}"), fields.clone()))?;
    let about = json!({"found": data["found"], "at_t": session::utc_ms(SystemTime::now()),
                       "radius_m": (radius * 100.0).round() / 100.0,
                       "list": list.iter().map(map::Occupant::json).collect::<Vec<_>>()});
    Ok((list, about))
}

/// world_map's `key` (traces, traces_b): each a captures id or a measure_trace tag of this session (its
/// `<tag>-trace.csv`, or a measure_ab window's `<tag>_<n><label>`), the file checked against its captures row, the
/// sampler's radius and contact from its measurement rows' note; with when each CSV was written (seconds since 1970).
fn traces(cx: &Ctx, args: &Value, key: &str) -> Result<(Vec<map::Trace>, Vec<i64>), String> {
    let Some(v) = args.get(key) else {
        return Ok((Vec::new(), Vec::new()));
    };
    let bad = || format!("{key} must be 1 to {MAP_TRACES} captures ids or measure_trace tags");
    let items = v
        .as_array()
        .filter(|a| (1..=MAP_TRACES).contains(&a.len()))
        .ok_or_else(bad)?;
    let db = Ledger::open_readonly(cx.config.state_dir().join("quen.db"))
        .map_err(|e| format!("the ledger: {e}"))?;
    let query = |sql: &str, p: Value| {
        db.query(sql, &[p], Duration::from_secs(5))
            .map(|r| r.rows)
            .map_err(|e| format!("the ledger: {e}"))
    };
    let (mut out, mut written) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    for item in items {
        let row =
            "SELECT id, path, sha256, method, CAST(strftime('%s', t) AS INTEGER) FROM captures";
        let id = item
            .as_i64()
            .or_else(|| item.as_str().and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()));
        let (rows, what) = match id {
            Some(id) => (
                query(&format!("{row} WHERE id = ?1"), json!(id))?,
                format!("capture {id}"),
            ),
            None => {
                let t = tag(item).map_err(|_| bad())?;
                let path = format!("{}/{t}-trace.csv", cx.live.id);
                (
                    query(&format!("{row} WHERE path = ?1"), json!(path))?,
                    format!("tag {t}"),
                )
            }
        };
        let Some([id, Value::String(path), Value::String(sha), method, t]) =
            rows.first().map(Vec::as_slice)
        else {
            return Err(format!("{key}: no capture for {what}"));
        };
        if *method != "actor_trace" {
            return Err(format!("{key}: {what} is no actor trace (method {method})"));
        }
        let file = cx.config.capture_root().join(path);
        let at = |e: &dyn std::fmt::Display| format!("{key}: {}: {e}", file.display());
        let bytes = fs::read(&file).map_err(|e| at(&e))?;
        if sha256_hex(&bytes) != *sha {
            return Err(at(&"changed since quen wrote it"));
        }
        let samples = trace::parse_csv(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes)).map_err(|e| at(&e))?;
        let id = id.as_i64().unwrap_or_default();
        let note =
            "SELECT note FROM measurements WHERE capture_id = ?1 AND note IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1";
        let notes = query(note, json!(id))?;
        let note = notes
            .first()
            .and_then(|r| r[0].as_str())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let (radius, contact) = map::sampler_of(note);
        out.push(map::Trace {
            id,
            samples,
            contact,
            radius,
        });
        written.push(t.as_i64().unwrap_or_default());
    }
    Ok((out, written))
}

/// world_map's `base`: an earlier grid of this boot from its JSON capture, checked against its row, and how old.
fn base(cx: &Ctx, id: i64) -> Result<(Grid, Value), String> {
    let db = Ledger::open_readonly(cx.config.state_dir().join("quen.db"))
        .map_err(|e| format!("the ledger: {e}"))?;
    let query = |sql: &str, p: Value| {
        db.query(sql, &[p], Duration::from_secs(5))
            .map(|r| r.rows)
            .map_err(|e| format!("the ledger: {e}"))
    };
    let sql = "SELECT path, sha256, method, kind, boot_id FROM captures WHERE id = ?1";
    let row = query(sql, json!(id))?.pop();
    let Some([Value::String(path), Value::String(sha), method, kind, boot]) = row.as_deref() else {
        return Err(format!("base: no capture {id}"));
    };
    if *method != "world_map" || *kind != "json" {
        return Err(format!(
            "base: capture {id} is no world_map JSON (method {method}, kind {kind})"
        ));
    }
    if boot.as_i64() != Some(cx.live.boot) {
        return Err(format!(
            "base: capture {id} is of boot {boot}, not this one ({}): read the grid again",
            cx.live.boot
        ));
    }
    let file = cx.config.capture_root().join(path);
```
