```rs
/// The game's reactions to quen's input, faked: the daemon runs this (`QUEN_TEST_INPUT`) with what it would send
/// instead of sending it, as the fake game takes no keys. Each call is appended to `calls.txt`. `keys e` (Continue at
/// the main menu) holds at `continue` (see `hold`), writes `continue_done` after it, then the load's pushes (0, then 1)
/// unless `no_continue` exists; `keys u:200` (photo mode) pushes flag 129 to quen's state log.
/// `console quenload(...)`: the load's pushes (0, then 1), unless `no_load` exists. A hold point writes `at_<point>`, then waits while `hold_<point>` exists and `go` doesn't.
/// Each push line starts with the system tick, as W3Quen.asi's do; a load's gameplay push is stamped 17 s after its
/// first, the fade of live boot 1. With the W3 Game State Bridge installed, each push also puts a contrary one (0:
/// loading) in the bridge's log, which quen must never read.
pub const FAKE_SCRIPT: &str = r#"
import ctypes, os, sys, time
here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
log = os.path.join(here, "..", "game", "bin", "x64_dx12", "W3QuenState.log")
what, args = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2:]
open(os.path.join(here, "calls.txt"), "a").write(" ".join(sys.argv[1:]) + "\n")
def hold(point):
    open(os.path.join(here, "at_" + point), "w").close()
    while os.path.exists(os.path.join(here, "hold_" + point)) and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(here, "go")):
        time.sleep(0.05)
def push(*flags):
    tick = ctypes.windll.kernel32.GetTickCount64
    tick.restype = ctypes.c_uint64
    t = tick()
    open(log, "a").write("".join("%d push flags=%d\n" % (t + 17000 * i, f) for i, f in enumerate(flags)))
    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(log), "W3GameStateBridge.asi")):
        open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(log), "W3GameStateBridge.log"), "a").write("%d push=1 flags=0\n" % t)
if what == "keys" and "e" in args:
    hold("continue")
    open(os.path.join(here, "continue_done"), "w").close()
    if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(here, "no_continue")):
        push(0, 1)
if what == "keys" and "u:200" in args:
    push(129)
if what == "console" and args[0].startswith("quenload(") and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(here, "no_load")):
    push(0, 1)
"#;
/// A synthetic input.settings; the fake game writes its lines in another order at every start, as the game does.
pub const INPUT: &str =
    "[Exploration]\r\nIK_W=(Action=GI_AxisLeftY)\r\nIK_S=(Action=GI_AxisLeftY)\r\n";

/// The in-game parts a launch checks for, relative to the game folder: the Native Bridge (its ASI and loader, and the
/// Mods folder its download installs, which quen doesn't need) and quen's package (the last two), which [`test_pins`]
/// makes the version quen expects. No W3 Game State Bridge: quen doesn't need it.
pub const PARTS: [&str; 5] = [
    r"bin\x64_dx12\WitcherNativeBridge.asi",
    r"bin\x64_dx12\dinput8.dll",
    r"Mods\modNativeBridge\content\scripts\imports.ws",
    r"bin\x64_dx12\W3Quen.asi",
    r"Mods\modQuen\content\scripts\local\quen.ws",
];

/// The W3 Game State Bridge's two parts, a third-party mod quen doesn't need: installed only where a test says so.
pub const W3GSB: [&str; 2] = [
    r"bin\x64_dx12\W3GameStateBridge.asi",
    r"Mods\modW3GameStateBridge\content\scripts\local\w3gsb.ws",
];

/// What the W3 Game State Bridge's part `part` (of [`W3GSB`]) holds in a test, of the build `build`: its script imports
/// a function its ASI holds the name of, as the real one does, so quen learns the pair from the files.
pub fn w3gsb(part: &str, build: &str) -> String {
    match part.ends_with(".ws") {
        true => format!("import function GSB_State() : int; // {build}\n"),
        false => format!("GSB_State\0{build}"),
    }
}

/// `QUEN_TEST_PINS` for every quen these tests start: the synthetic package files are its one release.
pub fn test_pins() -> String {
    let sha = quen_core::journal::sha256_hex(b"synthetic");
    format!("{}={sha};{}={sha};{INTERPOSER}={sha}", PARTS[3], PARTS[4])
}

/// NVIDIA Streamline's interposer in the game folder: a renderdoc launch swaps it only when it is the pinned, signed
/// one. [`test_pins`] pins the bytes `synthetic` here, which carry no signature.
pub const INTERPOSER: &str = r"bin\x64_dx12\sl.interposer.dll";

/// A temp folder for one test: the fake scripts, the game folder (the fake game, a Mods folder, an ASI with its ini,
/// general.ini, steam_appid.txt), the game's documents folder (settings and a QuickSave), quen's data root, and the
/// daemons its configs started (it is removed once they have exited).
pub struct Fixture(pub PathBuf, pub Mutex<Vec<u32>>, pub String);

impl Fixture {
    pub fn new() -> Fixture {
        static N: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let n = N.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        let dir =
            std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("quen-session-test-{}-{n}", std::process::id()));
        // An image name of this fixture's own: tests run at once, and quen guards against any process of its name.
        let exe = format!("quen-test-game-{}-{n}.exe", std::process::id());
        let bin = dir.join("game").join("bin").join("x64_dx12");
        for folder in [
            dir.join("harness"),
            dir.join("game/Mods/modAlpha"),
            dir.join("game/bin/config/base"),
            dir.join("docs/gamesaves"),
            bin.clone(),
        ] {
            fs::create_dir_all(folder).unwrap();
        }
        fs::write(dir.join("harness").join("fake_input.py"), FAKE_SCRIPT).unwrap();
        fs::write(dir.join("docs/dx12user.settings"), SETTINGS).unwrap();
        let input = dir.join("docs/input.settings");
        fs::write(&input, INPUT).unwrap();
        let file = fs::File::options().write(true).open(&input).unwrap();
        file.set_modified(compiled_at()).unwrap();
        fs::write(bin.join("input_settings"), input.display().to_string()).unwrap();
        fs::write(dir.join("docs/gamesaves/QuickSave.sav"), "quick").unwrap();
        fs::write(dir.join("game/bin/config/base/general.ini"), GENERAL).unwrap();
        fs::write(dir.join("game/Mods/modAlpha/blob0.bundle"), "bundle").unwrap();
        fs::copy(fake_game(), bin.join(&exe)).unwrap();
        // The fake game is a build quen knows: a synthetic one of this fixture's config.
        let build = quen_core::journal::sha256_hex(&fs::read(bin.join(&exe)).unwrap());
        fs::write(bin.join("steam_appid.txt"), "292030").unwrap();
        // The compiled scripts, written long ago: the fake game rewrites them while a mod is parked.
        let compiled = dir.join(r"game\content\content0\x64.final.redscripts");
        fs::create_dir_all(compiled.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
        fs::write(&compiled, "compiled with every mod").unwrap();
        let file = fs::File::options().write(true).open(&compiled).unwrap();
        file.set_modified(compiled_at()).unwrap();
        fs::write(bin.join("W3Fake.asi"), "asi").unwrap();
        fs::write(bin.join("W3Fake.ini"), "[General]\nMode=raise\n").unwrap();
        // What a launch and game_load need installed: the Native Bridge and quen's package, synthetic.
        for part in PARTS {
            let path = dir.join("game").join(part);
            fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
            fs::write(path, "synthetic").unwrap();
        }
        let config = format!(
            "harness = '{}'\ngame_dir = '{}'\ndocuments = '{}'\ndata_root = '{}'\ngame_exe = '{exe}'\n\
             known_builds = 'steam {build} synthetic (the fake game)'\n",
            dir.join("harness").join("ini_session.py").display(),
            dir.join("game").display(),
            dir.join("docs").display(),
            dir.join("data").display(),
        );
        fs::write(dir.join("config.toml"), config).unwrap();
        Fixture(dir, Mutex::default(), exe)
    }

    pub fn path(&self, rel: &str) -> PathBuf {
        self.0.join(rel)
    }

    pub fn read(&self, rel: &str) -> String {
        fs::read_to_string(self.path(rel)).unwrap()
    }

    pub fn settings(&self) -> String {
        self.read("docs/dx12user.settings")
    }

    pub fn config(&self, more: &str) {
        let mut config = self.read("config.toml");
        config.push_str(more);
        fs::write(self.path("config.toml"), config).unwrap();
    }

    /// Holds the fake scripts at `point` (see FAKE_SCRIPT) until `go`.
    pub fn hold(&self, point: &str) {
        fs::write(self.path(&format!("harness/hold_{point}")), "").unwrap();
    }

    /// Waits until the fake scripts reached `point`.
    pub fn wait_at(&self, point: &str) {
        let t = Instant::now();
        while !self.path(&format!("harness/at_{point}")).exists() {
            assert!(
                t.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(30),
                "boot never reached {point}"
            );
            sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));
        }
    }

    /// The fake game's pid, as it wrote it.
    pub fn game_pid(&self) -> u32 {
        self.read("game/bin/x64_dx12/pid").parse().unwrap()
    }

    /// What the fake scripts were called with, in order.
    pub fn calls(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let calls = fs::read_to_string(self.path("harness/calls.txt")).unwrap_or_default();
        calls.lines().map(str::to_owned).collect()
    }

    /// Rows of a read-only query of quen's ledger.
    pub fn ledger(&self, sql: &str) -> Vec<Vec<Value>> {
        let ledger = Ledger::open_readonly(self.path("data/state/quen.db")).unwrap();
        ledger.query(sql, &[], Duration::from_secs(5)).unwrap().rows
    }

    /// The user's state is back, byte for byte: settings and general.ini restored, mods unparked, no parking folder,
    /// steam_appid.txt as it was, no journal.
    pub fn assert_restored(&self) {
        assert_eq!(self.settings(), SETTINGS);
        let compiled = self.path(r"game\content\content0\x64.final.redscripts");
        assert_eq!(
            fs::read_to_string(&compiled).unwrap(),
            "compiled with every mod"
        );
        let at = fs::metadata(&compiled).unwrap().modified().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(at, compiled_at(), "the compiled scripts' write time");
        assert_eq!(self.read("docs/input.settings"), INPUT);
        let at = fs::metadata(self.path("docs/input.settings"))
            .unwrap()
            .modified()
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(at, compiled_at(), "input.settings' write time");
        assert_eq!(self.read("game/bin/config/base/general.ini"), GENERAL);
        assert_eq!(
            self.read("game/Mods/modAlpha/blob0.bundle"),
            "bundle",
            "a mod stays parked"
        );
        assert!(
            !self.path("game/quen-parked").exists(),
            "the parking folder remains"
        );
        assert!(
            !self.path("data/state/journal.jsonl").exists(),
            "journal remains"
        );
    }

    /// Waits for the daemon to end the session on its own (no caller) and give everything back, then checks it. Returns
    /// the end's result, which the daemon writes to serve.log last, after the restore and the boot's ledger row: until
    /// it is there, the boot's outcome may still be NULL (CI, 2026-10-18).
    pub fn wait_restored(&self) -> Value {
        let t = Instant::now();
        loop {
            let log = fs::read_to_string(self.path("data/logs/serve.log")).unwrap_or_default();
            // Whole lines only: the daemon may be writing the last one.
            let whole = log.rsplit_once('\n').map_or("", |(lines, _)| lines);
            let end = whole
                .lines()
                .rfind(|l| l.contains(r#""tool":"session_end""#));
            let restored =
                self.settings() == SETTINGS && !self.path("data/state/journal.jsonl").exists();
            if let (Some(end), true) = (end, restored) {
                self.assert_restored();
                return serde_json::from_str(&end[end.find('{').unwrap()..]).unwrap();
            }
            assert!(
                t.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(30),
                "never restored and ended: {log}"
            );
            sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
        }
    }

    /// A second config file with the same contents: its own daemon, over the same data root.
    pub fn second_config(&self) -> &str {
        fs::copy(self.path("config.toml"), self.path("config2.toml")).unwrap();
        "config2.toml"
    }
}

impl Drop for Fixture {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // A daemon keeps its log open until it exits: no connection and no session for a few seconds.
        for &pid in self.1.lock().unwrap().iter() {
            dies_within(pid, Duration::from_secs(60));
        }
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0); // this test's own temp folder
    }
}

/// The fake game cargo built beside quen (an example of this crate).
pub fn fake_game() -> PathBuf {
    example("fake_game")
}

/// The stand-in for Tracy's capture tool (`examples/fake_tracy_capture.rs`).
pub fn fake_tracy_capture() -> PathBuf {
    example("fake_tracy_capture")
}

/// The stand-in for REDkit's wcc_lite (`examples/fake_wcc_lite.rs`).
pub fn fake_wcc_lite() -> PathBuf {
    example("fake_wcc_lite")
}

fn example(name: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let quen = Path::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_quen"));
    let exe = quen
        .parent()
        .unwrap()
        .join("examples")
        .join(format!("{name}.exe"));
    assert!(
        exe.exists(),
        "no {}: `cargo build -p quen --example {name}` (cargo test builds it)",
        exe.display()
    );
    exe
}

/// A running `quen mcp` proxy, its pipes, and the daemon serving it.
pub struct Quen {
    pub child: Child,
    pub stdin: Option<ChildStdin>,
    pub stdout: BufReader<ChildStdout>,
    pub next_id: u64,
    pub daemon: u32,
    /// The notifications read so far, in order.
    pub notes: Vec<Value>,
}

impl Quen {
    /// Starts a proxy for the fixture's config and initializes it; it starts the daemon if none runs for that config.
    pub fn start(fx: &Fixture) -> Quen {
        let mut quen = Quen::spawn(fx, "config.toml", 0);
        quen.init(fx);
        quen
    }

    /// Starts a proxy for `config` with these process creation flags, and sends it nothing yet: it finds or starts the
    /// daemon on its first line. cargo's own job (kill on close, no breakaway) holds the daemon too, so the proxy is
    /// told that's expected. What the daemon sends to the Recycle Bin goes into the fixture instead.
    pub fn spawn(fx: &Fixture, config: &str, flags: u32) -> Quen {
        Quen::spawn_with(fx, config, flags, &[])
    }

    pub fn spawn_with(fx: &Fixture, config: &str, flags: u32, env: &[(&str, &str)]) -> Quen {
        let mut child = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_quen"))
            .arg("mcp")
            .env("QUEN_CONFIG", fx.path(config))
            .env("QUEN_TEST_IN_JOB", "1")
            .env("QUEN_TEST_PINS", test_pins())
            .env("QUEN_TEST_RECYCLE_TO", fx.path("recycled"))
            .env("QUEN_TEST_WCC_IMAGE", "quen-test-no-such-wcc.exe")
            // Vortex's image: no test sees the user's own Vortex (a test names its stand-in's).
            .env("QUEN_TEST_VORTEX_IMAGE", "quen-test-no-such-vortex.exe")
            // REDkit's licence answer, accepted: no test reads the user's.
            .env("QUEN_TEST_EULA", "1")
            .env("QUEN_TEST_INPUT", fx.path("harness/fake_input.py"))
            .envs(env.iter().copied())
            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
            .creation_flags(flags)
            .spawn()
            .unwrap();
        Quen {
            stdin: child.stdin.take(),
            stdout: BufReader::new(child.stdout.take().unwrap()),
            child,
            next_id: 0,
            daemon: 0,
            notes: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// The MCP handshake as Claude Code, which waits for every call, then status for the daemon's pid.
    pub fn init(&mut self, fx: &Fixture) {
        self.init_as(fx, "claude-code");
    }

    /// The handshake as `client`: one other than Claude Code gets long calls as jobs once they outlive its budget.
    pub fn init_as(&mut self, fx: &Fixture, client: &str) {
        let init = self.request(
            "initialize",
            json!({"protocolVersion": "2025-06-18", "capabilities": {},
                   "clientInfo": {"name": client, "version": "0"}}),
        );
        assert_eq!(init["result"]["serverInfo"]["name"], "quen");
        self.send(&json!({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"}));
        let status = self.tool("session_status", json!({}));
        // Finding 22: the running quen's version, to tell a tool list kept from an older one.
        assert_eq!(status["quen"], init["result"]["serverInfo"]["version"]);
        self.daemon = status["serve_pid"].as_u64().unwrap() as u32;
        assert_ne!(self.daemon, self.child.id(), "the proxy served itself");
        fx.1.lock().unwrap().push(self.daemon);
    }

    /// A daemon crash: it dies (and with it the session's job); its proxy follows.
    pub fn kill_daemon(&mut self) {
        let pid = self.daemon.to_string();
        let out = Command::new("taskkill")
            .args(["/F", "/PID", &pid])
            .output()
            .unwrap();
        assert!(out.status.success(), "{out:?}");
        self.wait_exit();
    }

    pub fn send(&mut self, msg: &Value) {
        let stdin = self.stdin.as_mut().unwrap();
        writeln!(stdin, "{msg}").unwrap();
        stdin.flush().unwrap();
    }

    /// Sends a request and returns its id without waiting.
    pub fn post(&mut self, method: &str, params: Value) -> u64 {
        self.next_id += 1;
        let id = self.next_id;
        self.send(&json!({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id, "method": method, "params": params}));
        id
    }

    /// Reads lines until the response to `id`, keeping notifications in `notes`.
    pub fn response(&mut self, id: u64) -> Value {
        loop {
            let mut line = String::new();
            assert!(
                self.stdout.read_line(&mut line).unwrap() > 0,
                "quen closed stdout"
            );
            let msg: Value = serde_json::from_str(&line).unwrap();
            if msg["id"] == id {
                return msg;
            }
            assert!(
                msg.get("id").is_none(),
                "a response to another request: {msg}"
            );
            self.notes.push(msg);
        }
    }

    pub fn request(&mut self, method: &str, params: Value) -> Value {
        let id = self.post(method, params);
        self.response(id)
    }

    /// Calls a tool and returns its envelope, polling job_status if the call answered a job.
    pub fn tool(&mut self, name: &str, args: Value) -> Value {
        let answer = self.call(name, args);
        self.poll(&answer)
    }

    /// Calls a tool and returns what it answered: an envelope, or a job's `{job, state}`.
    pub fn call(&mut self, name: &str, args: Value) -> Value {
        let msg = self.request("tools/call", json!({"name": name, "arguments": args}));
        result(&msg)
    }

    /// `answer` if it is an envelope, else that job's envelope, from job_status once the call ended.
    pub fn poll(&mut self, answer: &Value) -> Value {
        let mut answer = answer.clone();
        while answer.get("ok").is_none() {
            let state = answer["state"].as_str().unwrap();
            assert!(["queued", "running"].contains(&state), "{answer}");
            answer = self.call("job_status", json!({"job": answer["job"]}));
        }
        answer
    }

    pub fn wait_exit(&mut self) {
        let t = Instant::now();
        while self.child.try_wait().unwrap().is_none() {
            assert!(t.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(60), "quen did not exit");
            sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for Quen {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = self.child.kill();
        let _ = self.child.wait();
    }
}

/// A `tools/call` response's JSON: an envelope (isError unless ok), or a job's `{job, state}` (never an error).
pub fn result(msg: &Value) -> Value {
    let text = msg["result"]["content"][0]["text"].as_str().unwrap();
    let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(text).unwrap();
    let job = value.get("ok").is_none();
    assert_eq!(
        msg["result"]["isError"],
        !job && value["ok"] != true,
        "{msg}"
    );
    value
}

pub fn alive(pid: u32) -> bool {
    let out = Command::new("tasklist")
        .args(["/FI", &format!("PID eq {pid}"), "/NH", "/FO", "CSV"])
        .output()
        .unwrap();
    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).contains(&format!("\"{pid}\""))
}

/// Waits up to 10 s for `pid` to be gone.
pub fn dies(pid: u32) -> bool {
    dies_within(pid, Duration::from_secs(10))
}

pub fn dies_within(pid: u32, max: Duration) -> bool {
    let t = Instant::now();
    while alive(pid) {
        if t.elapsed() > max {
            return false;
        }
        sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
    }
    true
}

/// A Job Object with `limits` holding `child`, like the one the MCP client starts its servers in. Closing the handle
/// closes the job.
pub fn job_holding(child: &Child, limits: JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT) -> HANDLE {
    // SAFETY: a fresh job; the limits struct outlives the call; the child's handle is valid while it is owned.
    unsafe {
        let job = CreateJobObjectW(null(), null());
        assert!(!job.is_null());
        let mut info: JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION = std::mem::zeroed();
        info.BasicLimitInformation.LimitFlags = limits;
        let set = SetInformationJobObject(
            job,
            JobObjectExtendedLimitInformation,
            (&raw const info).cast(),
            size_of_val(&info) as u32,
        );
        assert_ne!(set, 0);
        assert_ne!(AssignProcessToJobObject(job, child.as_raw_handle()), 0);
        job
    }
}

pub fn launch(quen: &mut Quen) -> Value {
    launch_with(quen, json!({}))
}

pub fn launch_with(quen: &mut Quen, mut args: Value) -> Value {
    args["user_ok"] = json!(true);
    let envelope = quen.tool("session_launch", args);
    assert_eq!(envelope["ok"], true, "{envelope}");
    envelope
}

/// A copy of the fake game under this fixture's image name, started outside quen's job: a game the user started.
pub fn outside_game(fx: &Fixture) -> Child {
    let dir = fx.path("outside");
    fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
    let exe = dir.join(&fx.2);
    fs::copy(fake_game(), &exe).unwrap();
    Command::new(exe).spawn().unwrap()
}

/// Game knowledge for the build `exe_sha256`, synthetic: an RE knowledge base in a git work tree
/// `<dir>/repo` (only HEAD and its branch's ref in `.git`), the KB at `repo/re` with a names.tsv, a hooks.tsv and a
/// note; and an REA evidence bundle `<dir>/rea.json` with a decompile of the KB's `Alpha_Draw` (0x140001000) and its
/// callers (`Beta_Setup`). Returns the KB root and the bundle.
pub fn knowledge(dir: &Path, exe_sha256: &str) -> (PathBuf, PathBuf) {
    let repo = dir.join("repo");
    for sub in [".git/refs/heads", "re/notes"] {
        fs::create_dir_all(repo.join(sub)).unwrap();
    }
    fs::write(repo.join(".git/HEAD"), "ref: refs/heads/main\n").unwrap();
    fs::write(repo.join(".git/refs/heads/main"), "c".repeat(40)).unwrap();
    let line = format!("# build: sha256={exe_sha256} stamp=0x0BADF00D\n");
    let kb = repo.join("re");
    fs::write(
        kb.join("names.tsv"),
        format!(
            "{line}rva\tname\tkind\tconfidence\tsource\tdate\n0x1000\tAlpha_Draw\tfunction\tO\ttest\t2026-10-18\n\
             0x2000\tBeta_Setup\tfunction\tO\ttest\t2026-10-18\n"
        ),
    )
    .unwrap();
    fs::write(
        kb.join("hooks.tsv"),
        format!("{line}site\tkind\tmod\tversion\tnote\n0x1000\thook\tModA\t1.0\tdraw\n"),
    )
    .unwrap();
    fs::write(
        kb.join("notes/alpha.md"),
        "# Alpha\n\n## Q1\nAlpha_Draw at 0x1000.\n",
    )
    .unwrap();
    let provider = json!({"id": "ghidra", "name": "Ghidra", "version": "12.1.4"});
    let record = |n: u32, operation: &str, raw: Value| {
        json!({
            "evidence_id": format!("ev_{n:064x}"),
            "subject": {"name": "game.exe", "digest": {"sha256": exe_sha256}, "format": "pe",
                        "architecture": "x86_64", "local_path": "%GAME_DIR%/game.exe"},
            "provider": provider,
            "analysis_profile": {"provider": provider, "parameters": {}, "digest": "7".repeat(64)},
            "predicate_type": "rea.static", "operation": operation,
            "parameters": {"procedure": "0x140001000"},
            "raw_result": raw, "normalized_result": {}, "confidence": "observed",
            "authority": "shipped-artifact", "environment": null, "limitations": [],
            "locations": [{"kind": "address", "address": "0x140001000"}], "evidence_links": [],
        })
    };
    let bundle = json!({"records": [
        record(1, "procedure_pseudo_code", json!("void synthetic(void) {}")),
        record(2, "procedure_callers", json!(["0x140002000"])),
    ]});
    let path = dir.join("rea.json");
    fs::write(&path, bundle.to_string()).unwrap();
    (kb, path)
}

```

`crates/quen/tests/concurrency.rs`:

```rs
//! Several agents at once (docs/agents.md "Several agents at once"): real `quen mcp` connections to one daemon, each
//! driven from a thread of its own, plus a second daemon over the same data root, the CLI, and plain SQLite
//! connections holding the ledger open as a viewer or script would. Synchronised by barriers, channels and the fake
//! scripts' hold points, never by sleeps; every wait is bounded by a generous [`LIMIT`]. A test binary of its own, on
//! session.rs's fixture (`common`): cargo runs binaries one after another, so these daemons never add to the load
//! session.rs's timing tests run under.
#![cfg(windows)]

use std::fs;
use std::io::Write;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::{Command, Output, Stdio};
use std::sync::{Barrier, mpsc};
use std::thread;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use quen_core::ledger::{Ledger, SCHEMA_VERSION};
use rusqlite::Connection;
use serde_json::{Value, json};

mod common;

use common::*;

/// The longest a call that should answer at once may take: generous, so a slow machine never fails it.
const LIMIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);

/// A tool call's envelope, checked to come within [`LIMIT`].
fn timed(quen: &mut Quen, name: &str, args: Value) -> Value {
    let t = Instant::now();
    let out = quen.tool(name, args);
    assert!(t.elapsed() < LIMIT, "{name} took {:?}: {out}", t.elapsed());
    out
}

/// Whether `out` was refused with a reason containing `why`.
fn refused(out: &Value, why: &str) -> bool {
    out["refused"] == true && out["reason"].as_str().is_some_and(|r| r.contains(why))
}

/// Lets a boot held at a hold point go on (FAKE_SCRIPT).
fn go(fx: &Fixture) {
    fs::write(fx.path("harness/go"), "").unwrap();
}

/// A measurement row for ledger_ingest, named by its metric.
fn row(metric: &str) -> String {
    json!({"table": "measurements", "boot_id": null, "capture_id": null, "metric": metric, "value": 1.0,
           "unit": "ms", "state_label": "A", "method_family": "tracy", "tag": "M", "run_id": null, "note": null})
    .to_string()
}

/// The ids a ledger_ingest envelope returned.
fn ids(out: &Value) -> Vec<i64> {
    let ids = out["ledger"].as_array().unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{out}"));
    ids.iter().map(|id| id.as_i64().unwrap()).collect()
}

/// `quen ARGS` for the fixture's config, with `env` beside it and `stdin` on its input: its exit code and the JSON it
/// printed.
fn cli(fx: &Fixture, args: &[&str], env: &[(&str, PathBuf)], stdin: &str) -> (i32, Value) {
    let mut child = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_quen"))
        .args(args)
        .env("QUEN_CONFIG", fx.path("config.toml"))
        .envs(env.iter().map(|(k, v)| (*k, v)))
        .stdin(Stdio::piped())
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::piped())
        .spawn()
        .unwrap();
    child
        .stdin
        .take()
        .unwrap()
        .write_all(stdin.as_bytes())
        .unwrap();
    let Output { status, stdout, .. } = child.wait_with_output().unwrap();
    let out = serde_json::from_slice(&stdout)
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{e}: {}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&stdout)));
    (status.code().unwrap(), out)
}

/// The fixture's ledger, opened as a plain SQLite connection from outside quen.
fn outside(fx: &Fixture) -> Connection {
    let conn = Connection::open(fx.path("data/state/quen.db")).unwrap();
    conn.busy_timeout(LIMIT).unwrap();
    conn
}

/// The shipped migrations up to schema 6, applied by hand: a ledger an older quen left.
const OLD: [&str; 6] = [
    include_str!("../../../schema/0001_init.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0002_mods.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0003_harness_info.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0004_claims_strict.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0005_views.sql"),
    include_str!("../../../schema/0006_sweeps.sql"),
];

/// Writes a schema-6 ledger holding one claim, `kept`, in WAL mode as quen leaves it, and returns a connection to it.
fn old_ledger(fx: &Fixture) -> Connection {
    fs::create_dir_all(fx.path("data/state")).unwrap();
    let conn = outside(fx);
    for (i, sql) in OLD.iter().enumerate() {
        conn.execute_batch(sql).unwrap();
        conn.pragma_update(None, "user_version", i as i64 + 1)
            .unwrap();
    }
    let mode: String = conn
        .pragma_update_and_check(None, "journal_mode", "wal", |r| r.get(0))
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(mode, "wal");
    conn.execute("INSERT INTO claims (text) VALUES ('kept')", [])
        .unwrap();
    conn
}

fn user_version(conn: &Connection) -> i64 {
    conn.pragma_query_value(None, "user_version", |r| r.get(0))
        .unwrap()
}

fn integrity(conn: &Connection) -> String {
    conn.pragma_query_value(None, "integrity_check", |r| r.get(0))
        .unwrap()
}

/// While one connection's launch is in flight on the session thread, two others read: status, the ledger, the
/// capture root, the guide and a plan answer at once, each its own (their query echoes their own parameter), and
/// neither sees the launch's answer or its progress.
#[test]
fn reads_answer_during_another_connections_launch_and_are_their_own() {
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    fx.hold("continue");
    let mut a = Quen::start(&fx);
    let launch = a.post(
        "tools/call",
        json!({"name": "session_launch", "arguments": {"user_ok": true}, "_meta": {"progressToken": "a"}}),
    );
    fx.wait_at("continue");
    let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
    thread::scope(|s| {
        for who in ["b", "c"] {
            let (fx, tx) = (&fx, tx.clone());
            s.spawn(move || {
                let mut q = Quen::start(fx);
                for _ in 0..5 {
                    let status = timed(&mut q, "session_status", json!({}));
                    assert_eq!(status["state"]["lock"], "held here", "{status}");
                    assert_eq!(status["state"]["game"]["running"], true, "{status}");
                    let boot = &status["state"]["boot"];
                    assert!(boot.is_i64(), "{status}");
                    let sql = "SELECT ?1 AS who, count(*) FROM boots WHERE id = ?2";
                    let query = json!({"sql": sql, "params": [who, boot.to_string()]});
                    let rows = timed(&mut q, "ledger_query", query);
                    assert_eq!(rows["rows"], json!([[who, 1]]), "{rows}");
                    let found = timed(&mut q, "ledger_search", json!({"text": who}));
                    assert_eq!(found["ok"], true, "{found}");
                    let usage = timed(&mut q, "capture_usage", json!({}));
                    assert_eq!(usage["ok"], true, "{usage}");
                    let guide = timed(&mut q, "quen_guide", json!({}));
                    assert!(
                        guide["text"]
                            .as_str()
                            .unwrap()
                            .starts_with("# Agent playbook")
                    );
                    let plan = timed(&mut q, "session_plan", json!({}));
                    assert!(refused(&plan, "a session is live"), "{plan}");
                }
                assert!(q.notes.is_empty(), "{who} got {:?}", q.notes);
                tx.send(()).unwrap();
            });
        }
        drop(tx);
        // Both readers finish while the launch is still held, or the hold goes and the test fails.
        let done = (0..2).all(|_| rx.recv_timeout(LIMIT * 2).is_ok());
        go(&fx);
        assert!(done, "a read waited behind the launch");
    });
    let launched = result(&a.response(launch));
    assert_eq!(launched["ok"], true, "{launched}");
    assert!(!a.notes.is_empty(), "the launch sent no progress");
    for note in &a.notes {
        assert_eq!(note["params"]["progressToken"], "a", "{note}");
    }
    let ended = a.tool("session_end", json!({"token": launched["token"]}));
    assert_eq!(ended["ok"], true, "{ended}");
    fx.assert_restored();
}

/// A job belongs to its connection: another one can't see, poll or cancel it, by its job id or by the request id
/// (each connection numbers its own requests from 1).
#[test]
fn only_its_connection_sees_polls_or_cancels_a_job() {
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    fx.hold("continue");
    let mut a = Quen::start(&fx);
    let mut b = Quen::start(&fx);
    let answer = a.call("session_launch", json!({"user_ok": true, "wait": false}));
    let request = a.next_id;
    let job = answer["job"].as_str().unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{answer}"));
    fx.wait_at("continue");
    for tool in ["job_status", "job_cancel"] {
        let out = timed(&mut b, tool, json!({"job": job}));
        assert!(refused(&out, "another connection"), "{tool}: {out}");
    }
    let cancel = json!({"requestId": request, "reason": "not B's"});
    b.send(&json!({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/cancelled", "params": cancel}));
    let status = timed(&mut b, "session_status", json!({}));
    assert_eq!(status["state"]["game"]["running"], true, "{status}");
    go(&fx);
    let launched = a.poll(&answer);
    assert_eq!(
        launched["ok"], true,
        "B's cancel reached A's launch: {launched}"
    );
    let again = timed(&mut a, "job_status", json!({"job": job}));
    assert!(refused(&again, "already returned"), "{again}");
    assert!(b.notes.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.notes);
    let ended = a.tool("session_end", json!({"token": launched["token"]}));
    assert_eq!(ended["ok"], true, "{ended}");
    fx.assert_restored();
}

/// Four connections write at once from a fresh data root: every ingest is all or nothing, every id it returns is the
/// row it wrote, and nothing is lost or written twice.
#[test]
fn concurrent_ingests_are_whole_and_return_their_own_rows() {
    const CONNS: usize = 4;
    const ROUNDS: usize = 15;
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    let start = Barrier::new(CONNS);
    let written: Vec<(i64, String)> = thread::scope(|s| {
        let runs: Vec<_> = (0..CONNS)
            .map(|c| {
                let (fx, start) = (&fx, &start);
                s.spawn(move || {
                    let mut q = Quen::start(fx);
                    start.wait();
                    let mut mine = Vec::new();
                    for i in 0..ROUNDS {
                        let names = [format!("c{c}-{i}-x"), format!("c{c}-{i}-y")];
                        let rows = json!({"rows": [row(&names[0]), row(&names[1])]});
                        let out = timed(&mut q, "ledger_ingest", rows);
                        assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
                        mine.extend(ids(&out).into_iter().zip(names));
                        // A second row naming a boot that doesn't exist: the first row goes too.
                        let mut bad: Value = serde_json::from_str(&row("lost")).unwrap();
                        bad["boot_id"] = json!(999_999);
                        let rows = json!({"rows": [row(&format!("c{c}-{i}-lost")), bad.to_string()]});
                        let out = timed(&mut q, "ledger_ingest", rows);
                        assert!(refused(&out, "row 1"), "{out}");
                        let claim = json!({"action": "open", "text": format!("c{c}-{i}"),
                                           "support": [{"measurement_id": mine[mine.len() - 1].0}]});
                        let out = timed(&mut q, "ledger_claim", claim);
                        assert_eq!(out["claim"]["text"], format!("c{c}-{i}"), "{out}");
                    }
                    mine
                })
            })
            .collect();
        runs.into_iter().flat_map(|r| r.join().unwrap()).collect()
    });
    let mut want: Vec<Vec<Value>> = written
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(id, metric)| vec![json!(id), json!(metric)])
        .collect();
    want.sort_by_key(|r| r[0].as_i64());
    assert_eq!(want.len(), CONNS * ROUNDS * 2);
    assert_eq!(
        fx.ledger("SELECT id, metric FROM measurements ORDER BY id"),
        want
    );
    let claims = "SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT c.text) FROM claims c JOIN claim_support s ON s.claim_id = c.id \
                  JOIN measurements m ON m.id = s.measurement_id WHERE m.metric = c.text || '-y'";
    let n = (CONNS * ROUNDS) as i64;
    assert_eq!(fx.ledger(claims), [[json!(n), json!(n)]]);
}

/// Several connections rescan one KB and import one REA bundle at once: every call is answered whole, and the
/// ledger holds the bundle once, each record once and the KB's sections once.
#[test]
fn concurrent_imports_of_the_same_knowledge_add_it_once() {
    const CONNS: usize = 4;
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    let exe = "e".repeat(64);
    fs::create_dir_all(fx.path("data/state")).unwrap();
    let mut l = Ledger::open(fx.path("data/state/quen.db")).unwrap();
    l.add_game(&quen_core::ledger::Game {
        name: "synthetic".into(),
        exe_path: "%GAME_DIR%/game.exe".into(),
        exe_sha256: exe.clone(),
        build_stamp: None,
    })
    .unwrap();
    drop(l);
    let (kb, bundle) = knowledge(&fx.0, &exe);
    let start = Barrier::new(CONNS);
    thread::scope(|s| {
        for _ in 0..CONNS {
            let (fx, start, kb, bundle) = (&fx, &start, &kb, &bundle);
            s.spawn(move || {
                let mut q = Quen::start(fx);
                start.wait();
                // The scan first: the bundle's callers become links only between functions the KB names.
                let scan = timed(&mut q, "ledger_import", json!({"kind": "kb", "path": kb}));
                assert_eq!(scan["ok"], true, "{scan}");
                let args = json!({"kind": "rea_bundle", "path": bundle, "rea_version": "6.5.0"});
                let rea = timed(&mut q, "ledger_import", args);
                assert_eq!(rea["ok"], true, "{rea}");
                let about = timed(
                    &mut q,
                    "ledger_about",
                    json!({"kind": "function", "key": "Alpha_Draw"}),
                );
                assert_eq!(about["about"]["extracted"], true, "{about}");
            });
        }
    });
    let counts = "SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM captures WHERE method = 'rea'), (SELECT count(*) FROM extractions),                   (SELECT count(*) FROM links WHERE rel = 'calls'), (SELECT count(*) FROM kb_sections),                   (SELECT count(*) FROM entities)";
    assert_eq!(
        fx.ledger(counts),
        [[json!(1), json!(2), json!(1), json!(2), json!(3)]]
    );
}

/// Four connections support one claim with the same evidence, and withdraw another, at once: one of each wins
/// whole, the others are refused with a reason that says why, and the claim's status is the winner's.
#[test]
fn claims_on_the_same_evidence_at_once_stay_consistent() {
    const CONNS: usize = 4;
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    let mut seed = Quen::start(&fx);
    let mut pm: Value = serde_json::from_str(&row("pm")).unwrap();
    pm["method_family"] = json!("presentmon");
    let out = seed.tool(
        "ledger_ingest",
        json!({"rows": [pm.to_string(), row("tracy")]}),
    );
    let m = ids(&out);
    let open = |q: &mut Quen, text: &str| {
        let out = q.tool("ledger_claim", json!({"action": "open", "text": text}));
        out["claim"]["id"]
            .as_i64()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{out}"))
    };
    let (x, y) = (open(&mut seed, "x"), open(&mut seed, "y"));
    let start = Barrier::new(CONNS);
    let outs: Vec<(Value, Value)> = thread::scope(|s| {
        let runs: Vec<_> = (0..CONNS)
            .map(|c| {
                let (fx, start, m) = (&fx, &start, &m);
                s.spawn(move || {
                    let mut q = Quen::start(fx);
                    start.wait();
                    let support = json!([{"measurement_id": m[0], "supports": c % 2 == 0},
                                         {"measurement_id": m[1]}]);
                    let s = json!({"action": "support", "claim_id": x, "support": support});
                    let w = json!({"action": "withdraw", "claim_id": y, "reason": format!("c{c}")});
                    (
                        timed(&mut q, "ledger_claim", s),
                        timed(&mut q, "ledger_claim", w),
                    )
                })
            })
            .collect();
        runs.into_iter().map(|r| r.join().unwrap()).collect()
    });
    let won: Vec<&Value> = outs
        .iter()
        .map(|o| &o.0)
        .filter(|o| o["ok"] == true)
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(won.len(), 1, "{outs:?}");
    for (lost, _) in outs.iter().filter(|o| o.0["ok"] != true) {
        assert!(refused(lost, "already"), "{lost}");
    }
    let supports = &won[0]["claim"];
    let status = fx.ledger(&format!(
        "SELECT families, proven FROM claims_status WHERE id = {x}"
    ));
    assert_eq!(
        status,
        [[supports["families"].clone(), supports["proven"].clone()]]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        fx.ledger(&format!(
            "SELECT count(*) FROM claim_support WHERE claim_id = {x}"
        )),
        [[json!(2)]]
    );
    let withdrawn: Vec<&Value> = outs
        .iter()
        .map(|o| &o.1)
        .filter(|o| o["ok"] == true)
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(withdrawn.len(), 1, "{outs:?}");
    for (_, lost) in outs.iter().filter(|o| o.1["ok"] != true) {
        assert!(refused(lost, "already withdrawn"), "{lost}");
    }
    let reason = &withdrawn[0]["claim"]["withdrawn_reason"];
    assert_eq!(
        fx.ledger(&format!(
            "SELECT status, withdrawn_reason FROM claims WHERE id = {y}"
        )),
        [[json!("withdrawn"), reason.clone()]]
    );
}

/// While one connection's session is live, only it drives the session and writes on its boot: another connection's
/// session tools are refused at once, its rows stay off the boot, capture_clean is refused for the live boot, and
/// another daemon over the same data root and the CLI can't write rows about a boot.
#[test]
fn only_the_launching_connection_writes_about_its_boot() {
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    let mut a = Quen::start(&fx);
    let mut b = Quen::start(&fx);
    let launched = launch(&mut a);
    let token = &launched["token"];
    let boot = launched["ledger"]["boots"][0].as_i64().unwrap();
    for (tool, args) in [
        ("game_screenshot", json!({"token": token, "tag": "B1"})),
        ("measure_presentmon", json!({"token": token})),
        ("game_console", json!({"token": token, "line": "x"})),
        ("focus", json!({"token": token, "to": "client"})),
        ("game_save", json!({"token": token, "user_ok": true})),
        ("hands_take", json!({"token": token, "user_ok": true})),
        ("world_get", json!({"token": token})),
        ("capture_clean", json!({"boots": [boot], "user_ok": true})),
        ("session_end", json!({"token": token})),
        ("session_recover", json!({})),
    ] {
        let out = timed(&mut b, tool, args);
        assert!(refused(&out, "another connection"), "{tool}: {out}");
    }
    let relaunch = timed(&mut b, "session_launch", json!({"user_ok": true}));
    assert!(refused(&relaunch, "a session is live"), "{relaunch}");
    let clean = timed(
        &mut a,
        "capture_clean",
        json!({"boots": [boot], "user_ok": true}),
    );
    assert!(refused(&clean, "a session is live"), "{clean}");
    let free = ids(&timed(
        &mut b,
        "ledger_ingest",
        json!({"rows": [row("b-free")]}),
    ));
    let wrong = timed(
        &mut b,
        "ledger_ingest",
        json!({"rows": [row("b-wrong")], "token": "not-a"}),
    );
    assert!(refused(&wrong, "wrong token"), "{wrong}");
    let boots = json!({"table": "boots", "game_id": 1}).to_string();
    let out = timed(&mut b, "ledger_ingest", json!({"rows": [boots]}));
    assert_eq!(out["refused"], true, "{out}");
    // Without a boot_id key, the token puts the row on its boot (an explicit null keeps it off).
    let mut mine: Value = serde_json::from_str(&row("a-own")).unwrap();
    mine.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("boot_id");
    let own = ids(&timed(
        &mut a,
        "ledger_ingest",
        json!({"rows": [mine.to_string()], "token": token}),
    ));
    // Another daemon over the same data root is read-only for rows about a boot, as is the CLI.
    let mut other = Quen::spawn(&fx, fx.second_config(), 0);
    other.init(&fx);
    assert_ne!(other.daemon, a.daemon);
    for (tool, args) in [
        ("ledger_ingest", json!({"rows": [row("other")]})),
        ("capture_clean", json!({"boots": [boot], "user_ok": true})),
        ("session_launch", json!({"user_ok": true})),
    ] {
        let out = timed(&mut other, tool, args);
        assert!(
            refused(&out, "another quen holds the game lock"),
            "{tool}: {out}"
        );
    }
    let (code, out) = cli(&fx, &["ledger", "add"], &[], &row("cli"));
    assert_eq!(code, 1, "{out}");
    assert!(refused(&out, "another quen holds the game lock"), "{out}");
    let ended = a.tool("session_end", json!({"token": token}));
    assert_eq!(ended["ok"], true, "{ended}");
    fx.assert_restored();
    assert_eq!(
        fx.ledger("SELECT id, outcome FROM boots"),
        [[json!(boot), json!("ok")]]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        fx.ledger("SELECT id, boot_id, metric FROM measurements ORDER BY id"),
        [
            vec![json!(free[0]), Value::Null, json!("b-free")],
            vec![json!(own[0]), json!(boot), json!("a-own")],
        ]
    );
}

/// A daemon migrates an older ledger at its start while another process reads it (an older quen, a viewer): the
/// reader keeps its snapshot, the migration and its backup complete, nothing is lost and the file stays sound.
#[test]
fn serve_start_migrates_beside_an_outside_reader() {
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    let reader = old_ledger(&fx);
    reader.execute_batch("BEGIN").unwrap();
    let count = |c: &Connection| -> i64 {
        c.query_row("SELECT count(*) FROM claims", [], |r| r.get(0))
            .unwrap()
    };
    assert_eq!(count(&reader), 1);
    let mut q = Quen::start(&fx);
    // A session-thread call queues behind the startup migration.
    let out = timed(&mut q, "session_recover", json!({}));
    assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
    let new = timed(
        &mut q,
        "ledger_query",
        json!({"sql": "SELECT count(removed_to) FROM captures"}),
    );
    assert_eq!(new["ok"], true, "not migrated: {new}");
    assert_eq!(count(&reader), 1);
    assert_eq!(user_version(&reader), 6, "the reader's snapshot moved");
    reader.execute_batch("COMMIT").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(user_version(&reader), SCHEMA_VERSION);
    assert_eq!(integrity(&reader), "ok");
    assert_eq!(count(&reader), 1);
    let backups: Vec<PathBuf> = fs::read_dir(fx.path("data/state/backups"))
        .unwrap()
        .map(|e| e.unwrap().path())
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(backups.len(), 1, "{backups:?}");
    let name = backups[0].file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy();
    assert!(name.starts_with("quen-v6-"), "{name}");
    let backup = Connection::open(&backups[0]).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(user_version(&backup), 6);
    assert_eq!(count(&backup), 1);
}

/// A daemon starting while another process holds the older ledger's write lock: the start migration waits, gives
/// up with a reason in serve.log and changes nothing; writes are refused with a reason while the lock is held; the
/// first write after it is released migrates, with its backup.
#[test]
fn serve_start_waits_out_an_outside_writer_then_migrates_at_the_next_write() {
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    let writer = old_ledger(&fx);
    writer.execute_batch("BEGIN IMMEDIATE").unwrap();
    let mut q = Quen::start(&fx);
    let out = q.tool("session_recover", json!({}));
    assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
    let log = fx.read("data/logs/serve.log");
    assert!(log.contains("migrates at the next write"), "{log}");
    let read = timed(
        &mut q,
        "ledger_query",
        json!({"sql": "SELECT text FROM claims"}),
    );
    assert_eq!(read["rows"], json!([["kept"]]), "{read}");
    let held = q.tool("ledger_ingest", json!({"rows": [row("held")]}));
    assert!(refused(&held, "busy"), "{held}");
    assert!(!fx.path("data/state/backups").exists());
    assert_eq!(user_version(&writer), 6);
    writer.execute_batch("COMMIT").unwrap();
    let out = timed(&mut q, "ledger_ingest", json!({"rows": [row("after")]}));
    assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
    assert_eq!(user_version(&writer), SCHEMA_VERSION);
    assert_eq!(integrity(&writer), "ok");
    assert_eq!(
        fx.ledger("SELECT metric FROM measurements"),
        [[json!("after")]]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        fs::read_dir(fx.path("data/state/backups")).unwrap().count(),
        1
    );
}

/// The CLI beside a daemon: `quen ledger add` writes alongside two connections' ingests, nothing lost; while a
/// session is live, `quen ledger add|migrate` and `quen recover` are refused and change nothing, and the session goes
/// on.
#[test]
fn the_cli_beside_a_running_daemon_is_refused_or_safe() {
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    let start = Barrier::new(3);
    thread::scope(|s| {
        for c in ["a", "b"] {
            let (fx, start) = (&fx, &start);
            s.spawn(move || {
                let mut q = Quen::start(fx);
                start.wait();
                for i in 0..10 {
                    let out = timed(
                        &mut q,
                        "ledger_ingest",
                        json!({"rows": [row(&format!("{c}{i}"))]}),
                    );
                    assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
                }
            });
        }
        start.wait();
        for i in 0..10 {
            let (code, out) = cli(&fx, &["ledger", "add"], &[], &row(&format!("cli{i}")));
            assert_eq!(code, 0, "{out}");
        }
    });
    let n = fx.ledger("SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT metric) FROM measurements");
    assert_eq!(n, [[json!(30), json!(30)]]);
    let mut a = Quen::start(&fx);
    let launched = launch(&mut a);
    let journal = fx.read("data/state/journal.jsonl");
    for args in [&["ledger", "add"][..], &["ledger", "migrate"], &["recover"]] {
        let (code, out) = cli(&fx, args, &[], &row("live"));
        assert_eq!(code, 1, "{args:?}: {out}");
        let why = out["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
        assert!(
            why.contains("another quen holds the game lock"),
            "{args:?}: {out}"
        );
    }
    assert_eq!(fx.read("data/state/journal.jsonl"), journal);
    let status = timed(&mut a, "session_status", json!({}));
    assert_eq!(status["state"]["game"]["running"], true, "{status}");
    let ended = a.tool("session_end", json!({"token": launched["token"]}));
    assert_eq!(ended["ok"], true, "{ended}");
    fx.assert_restored();
    assert_eq!(
        n,
        fx.ledger("SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT metric) FROM measurements")
    );
}

/// `quen setup --move` while a daemon serves the old folder: refused while its session is live, nothing copied;
/// with the daemon idle, every file is copied and checked, and the old folder, which the daemon's open files keep from
/// being renamed, is named in `left`; the daemon goes on serving it.
#[test]
fn moving_quens_folder_beside_a_running_daemon_is_refused_or_reported() {
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    // quen's older layout: config and data under a synthetic %APPDATA%\quen.
    let old = fx.path(r"roaming\quen");
    fs::create_dir_all(&old).unwrap();
    let config = fx.read("config.toml").replace(
        &format!("data_root = '{}'", fx.path("data").display()),
        &format!("data_root = '{}'", old.display()),
    );
    fs::write(old.join("config.toml"), config).unwrap();
    let env = [
        ("QUEN_CONFIG", old.join("config.toml")),
        ("APPDATA", fx.path("roaming")),
        ("LOCALAPPDATA", fx.path("local")),
        ("USERPROFILE", fx.path("profile")),
    ];
    let home = fx.path(r"profile\.quen");
    let mut a = Quen::spawn(&fx, r"roaming\quen\config.toml", 0);
    a.init(&fx);
    let launched = launch(&mut a);
    let (code, out) = cli(&fx, &["setup", "--move", "--user-ok"], &env, "");
    assert_eq!(code, 1, "{out}");
    assert!(refused(&out, "journal"), "{out}");
    assert!(!home.exists(), "copied while a session was live");
    let ended = a.tool("session_end", json!({"token": launched["token"]}));
    assert_eq!(ended["ok"], true, "{ended}");
    let (code, out) = cli(&fx, &["setup", "--move", "--user-ok"], &env, "");
    assert_eq!(code, 0, "{out}");
    assert!(out["files"].as_u64().unwrap() > 0, "{out}");
    assert_eq!(out["renamed"], json!([]), "{out}");
    assert_eq!(out["left"][0]["path"], json!(old), "{out}");
    let copy = Ledger::open_readonly(home.join(r"state\quen.db")).unwrap();
    let boots = copy.query("SELECT outcome FROM boots", &[], LIMIT).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(boots.rows, [[json!("ok")]]);
    let status = timed(&mut a, "session_status", json!({}));
    let root = status["data_root"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
    assert!(root.ends_with(r"\roaming\quen"), "{status}");
}

/// A plain SQLite connection holding a read transaction, as a viewer does, never makes quen fail: a whole session
/// and every ledger tool run beside it, and the reader keeps its snapshot until it ends it.
#[test]
fn an_outside_reader_never_makes_quen_fail() {
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    let mut a = Quen::start(&fx);
    let out = a.tool("ledger_ingest", json!({"rows": [row("before")]}));
    assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
    let reader = outside(&fx);
    reader.execute_batch("BEGIN").unwrap();
    let count = |c: &Connection| -> i64 {
        c.query_row("SELECT count(*) FROM measurements", [], |r| r.get(0))
            .unwrap()
    };
    assert_eq!(count(&reader), 1);
    let launched = launch(&mut a);
    let token = &launched["token"];
    let out = timed(
        &mut a,
        "ledger_ingest",
        json!({"rows": [row("during")], "token": token}),
    );
    let m = ids(&out)[0];
    let claim =
        json!({"action": "open", "text": "beside a reader", "support": [{"measurement_id": m}]});
    let out = timed(&mut a, "ledger_claim", claim);
    assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
    let out = timed(
        &mut a,
        "ledger_query",
        json!({"sql": "SELECT count(*) FROM measurements"}),
    );
    assert_eq!(out["rows"], json!([[2]]), "{out}");
    let ended = a.tool("session_end", json!({"token": token}));
    assert_eq!(ended["ok"], true, "{ended}");
    assert!(ended.get("ledger_error").is_none(), "{ended}");
    fx.assert_restored();
    assert_eq!(count(&reader), 1, "the reader's snapshot moved");
    reader.execute_batch("COMMIT").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(count(&reader), 2);
    let boot = fx.ledger("SELECT outcome FROM boots");
    assert_eq!(boot, [[json!("ok")]]);
}

/// A plain SQLite connection holding the write lock past quen's busy timeout: each write waits, then is refused with
/// a reason that says the ledger is busy, and nothing of it is written; a launch is refused before it changes anything;
/// reads go on.
#[test]
fn an_outside_writer_past_the_busy_timeout_gets_a_clear_refusal_and_nothing_half_written() {
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    let mut a = Quen::start(&fx);
    let out = a.tool("ledger_ingest", json!({"rows": [row("before")]}));
    let m = ids(&out)[0];
    let writer = outside(&fx);
    writer.execute_batch("BEGIN IMMEDIATE").unwrap();
    let calls = [
        ("ledger_ingest", json!({"rows": [row("x"), row("y")]})),
        (
            "ledger_claim",
            json!({"action": "open", "text": "held", "support": [{"measurement_id": m}]}),
        ),
        ("session_launch", json!({"user_ok": true})),
    ];
    let outs: Vec<Value> = thread::scope(|s| {
        let runs: Vec<_> = calls
            .iter()
            .map(|(tool, args)| {
                let fx = &fx;
                s.spawn(move || timed(&mut Quen::start(fx), tool, args.clone()))
            })
            .collect();
        let read = timed(
            &mut a,
            "ledger_query",
            json!({"sql": "SELECT metric FROM measurements"}),
        );
        assert_eq!(read["rows"], json!([["before"]]), "{read}");
        let found = timed(&mut a, "ledger_search", json!({"text": "before"}));
        assert_eq!(found["tables"], json!({"measurements": 1}), "{found}");
        runs.into_iter().map(|r| r.join().unwrap()).collect()
    });
    for out in &outs {
        assert!(refused(out, "busy"), "{out}");
        let why = out["reason"].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(
            !why.contains("database is locked"),
            "a raw SQLite error: {why}"
        );
    }
    fx.assert_restored();
    let status = timed(&mut a, "session_status", json!({}));
    assert_eq!(status["state"]["lock"]["free"], true, "{status}");
    writer.execute_batch("COMMIT").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        fx.ledger(
            "SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM measurements), (SELECT count(*) FROM claims), \
                   (SELECT count(*) FROM boots)"
        ),
        [[json!(1), json!(0), json!(0)]]
    );
}

/// The write lock held by another program as a session ends: the end still restores everything and releases the
/// lock, and its result says the ledger was busy. The boot row keeps no end (t_end null): nothing records it later.
#[test]
fn an_end_beside_an_outside_writer_restores_and_says_the_ledger_was_busy() {
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    let mut a = Quen::start(&fx);
    let launched = launch(&mut a);
    let boot = launched["ledger"]["boots"][0].as_i64().unwrap();
    let writer = outside(&fx);
    writer.execute_batch("BEGIN IMMEDIATE").unwrap();
    let ended = a.tool("session_end", json!({"token": launched["token"]}));
    writer.execute_batch("COMMIT").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(ended["ok"], true, "{ended}");
    let why = ended["ledger_error"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
    assert!(
        why.contains("busy") && !why.contains("database is locked"),
        "{ended}"
    );
    assert_eq!(ended["state"]["lock"]["free"], true, "{ended}");
    fx.assert_restored();
    let row = fx.ledger(&format!(
        "SELECT outcome, t_end FROM boots WHERE id = {boot}"
    ));
    assert_eq!(row, [[Value::Null, Value::Null]]);
}

/// What quen_setup writes reaches every connection of the running daemon at once, with no reconnect, and a new
/// connection finds that same daemon (one per config file). While a session is live the daemon keeps its config, to
/// the session's end, then takes the new one up: a session never sees two.
#[test]
fn quen_setup_s_write_reaches_every_connection_once_no_session_is_live() {
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    let mut a = Quen::start(&fx);
    let mut b = Quen::start(&fx);
    assert_eq!(a.daemon, b.daemon);
    let budget = |q: &mut Quen| timed(q, "capture_usage", json!({}))["budget_gb"].clone();
    assert_eq!(budget(&mut b), json!(20.0));
    let set = |gb: &str| json!({"values": {"capture_budget_gb": gb}, "user_ok": true});
    let out = timed(&mut a, "quen_setup", set("7"));
    assert_eq!(
        (&out["ok"], &out["reloaded"]),
        (&json!(true), &json!(true)),
        "{out}"
    );
    assert_eq!(budget(&mut b), json!(7.0));
    let mut c = Quen::start(&fx);
    assert_eq!(c.daemon, a.daemon, "a second daemon for one config");
    assert_eq!(budget(&mut c), json!(7.0));
    // With a session live: written, and taken up once the session ends.
    let launched = launch(&mut a);
    let out = timed(&mut a, "quen_setup", set("9"));
    assert_eq!(
        (&out["ok"], &out["reloaded"]),
        (&json!(true), &json!(false)),
        "{out}"
    );
    let applies = out["applies"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
    assert!(applies.contains("a session is live"), "{out}");
    assert_eq!(budget(&mut b), json!(7.0));
    let ended = a.tool("session_end", json!({"token": launched["token"]}));
    assert_eq!(ended["ok"], true, "{ended}");
    assert_eq!(
        ended["captures"]["budget_gb"],
        json!(7.0),
        "the session ran on one config to its end"
    );
    fx.assert_restored();
    assert_eq!(budget(&mut b), json!(9.0));
    assert_eq!(budget(&mut a), json!(9.0));
}

/// An edit by hand (here the CLI's `quen setup`) is taken up too, at the next connection, once no session is live.
#[test]
fn an_edit_outside_the_daemon_is_taken_up_at_the_next_connection() {
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    let mut a = Quen::start(&fx);
    let (code, out) = cli(
        &fx,
        &["setup", "capture_budget_gb=11", "--user-ok"],
        &[],
        "",
    );
    assert_eq!(code, 0, "{out}");
    assert_eq!(out["reloaded"], false, "{out}");
    let mut b = Quen::start(&fx);
    assert_eq!(b.daemon, a.daemon);
    for q in [&mut a, &mut b] {
        let usage = timed(q, "capture_usage", json!({}));
        assert_eq!(usage["budget_gb"], json!(11.0), "{usage}");
    }
}
```

`crates/quen/tests/data.rs`:

```rs
//! script_compile and quen_setup licence end to end: the real binary's daemon runs a stand-in wcc_lite
//! (`examples/fake_wcc_lite.rs`) over the synthetic game of the session tests' fixture, with what it sends to the
//! Recycle Bin kept in the fixture. `QUEN_TEST_EULA` stands in for REDkit's licence answer (accepted unless a test says
//! otherwise): no test reads or writes the user's.
#![cfg(windows)]

mod common;

use std::fs;
use std::path::PathBuf;

use serde_json::{Value, json};

use common::*;

/// A synthetic REDkit in the fixture, its wcc_lite the stand-in, writing the fixture's documents folder; in the config.
fn redkit(fx: &Fixture) {
    let bin = fx.path(r"redkit\bin\x64_RedKit");
    fs::create_dir_all(&bin).unwrap();
    fs::copy(fake_wcc_lite(), bin.join("wcc_lite.exe")).unwrap();
    fs::write(
        bin.join("fake_docs.txt"),
        fx.path("docs").display().to_string(),
    )
    .unwrap();
    fx.config(&format!("redkit = '{}'\n", fx.path("redkit").display()));
}

/// The scratch folder a result names, shown as %USERPROFILE% when the fixture is under the user's folder (TEMP is).
fn scratch(out: &Value) -> PathBuf {
    let home = std::env::var("USERPROFILE").unwrap_or_default();
    PathBuf::from(
        out["scratch"]
            .as_str()
            .unwrap()
            .replace("%USERPROFILE%", &home),
    )
}

/// The tree holds the game's scripts and the mods' (the first in name order winning a conflict), the switches are
/// passed, the log's errors and warnings are parsed, and the documents folder's settings are put back (bytes and write
/// time), the file wcc_lite made recycled, the journal retired. Without stubs, one run on the scripts as they are. With
/// stubs, that run, then one with only the imports it couldn't bind stubbed: an engine native a mod imports is left to
/// bind, as a stub of it is an error (finding 100). Without REDkit: refused with needs.
#[test]
fn script_compile_runs_wcc_lite_and_puts_the_settings_back() {
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    let put = |rel: &str, text: &str| {
        let path = fx.path(rel);
        fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
        fs::write(&path, text).unwrap();
        path
    };
    put(r"game\content\content0\scripts\game\x.ws", "class X {}\n");
    let a = "import function A() : int;\n";
    put(r"game\Mods\modA\content\scripts\local\a.ws", a);
    put(r"game\Mods\modB\content\scripts\local\a.ws", "// modB\n");
    let native = "import function SetCommunityRadius(r : float);\n";
    put(r"game\Mods\modGraphics\content\scripts\local\g.ws", native);
    let profile = put(r"docs\profile.settings", "[Telemetry]\noriginal=1\n");
    let mtime = fs::metadata(&profile).unwrap().modified().unwrap();
    let put_back = || {
        assert_eq!(
            fs::read_to_string(&profile).unwrap(),
            "[Telemetry]\noriginal=1\n"
        );
        assert_eq!(fs::metadata(&profile).unwrap().modified().unwrap(), mtime);
        assert!(!fx.path(r"docs\editoruser.settings").exists());
        assert!(!fx.path(r"data\state\journal.jsonl").exists());
    };
    let mut quen = Quen::start(&fx);
    let without = quen.tool("script_compile", json!({}));
    assert_eq!(
        without["needs"][0]["dependency"], "The Witcher 3 REDkit",
        "{without}"
    );
    drop(quen);
    redkit(&fx);
    let mut quen = Quen::start(&fx);

    let plain = quen.tool("script_compile", json!({}));
    assert_eq!(plain["ok"], true, "{plain}");
    assert_eq!(
        (&plain["exit_code"], &plain["error_count"]),
        (&json!(1), &json!(1))
    );
    let first = json!({"file": r"local\a.ws", "line": 1, "msg": "Cannot find global function 'A' to import."});
    assert_eq!(plain["errors"], json!([first]));
    assert_eq!(plain["warning_count"], 1);
    assert_eq!(plain["conflicts"][0]["file"], r"local\a.ws");
    assert_eq!(plain["conflicts"][0]["used"], "modA");
    assert!(plain.get("imports_stubbed").is_none(), "{plain}");
    put_back();
    let dir = scratch(&plain);
    assert!(dir.join("journal.jsonl").is_file());
    assert_eq!(
        fs::read_to_string(dir.join(r"scripts\local\a.ws")).unwrap(),
        a
    );
    assert!(dir.join(r"scripts\game\x.ws").is_file());
    assert!(!dir.join("stubbed").exists());
    let said = fs::read_to_string(dir.join("wcc_lite.log")).unwrap();
    assert!(
        said.contains("-agreetoterms -noninteractivecrash"),
        "{said}"
    );
    assert!(dir.join("wcc.log").is_file());

    // The scratch folder is named by the second.
    std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(1100));
    let out = quen.tool("script_compile", json!({"stubs": true}));
    assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
    assert_eq!(
        (&out["exit_code"], &out["error_count"]),
        (&json!(0), &json!(0)),
        "{out}"
    );
    assert_eq!(out["imports_stubbed"], json!(["A"]));
    assert_eq!(out["imports_bound"], json!(["SetCommunityRadius"]));
    put_back();
    let dir = scratch(&out);
    let shipped = fs::read_to_string(dir.join("wcc.log")).unwrap();
    assert!(shipped.contains("'A' to import"), "{shipped}");
    assert!(
        out["wcc_log"]
            .as_str()
            .unwrap()
            .ends_with(r"stubbed\wcc.log"),
        "{out}"
    );
    let stubbed = |rel: &str| fs::read_to_string(dir.join(r"stubbed\scripts").join(rel)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(stubbed(r"local\a.ws"), "function A() : int { return 0; }\n");
    assert_eq!(stubbed(r"local\g.ws"), native);
    assert!(dir.join(r"stubbed\journal.jsonl").is_file());
    assert!(fx.path("recycled").read_dir().unwrap().count() >= 1);
}

/// REDkit's licence is the user's answer in its own dialog. Until it is 1, quen_doctor says so and script_compile is
/// refused with needs, nothing changed. quen_setup licence is refused as script_compile is (no REDkit, a journal left,
/// the game running, a live session); otherwise it runs wcc_lite once without -agreetoterms and with no command, puts
/// the documents folder's settings back, and reports the answer read again.
#[test]
fn the_licence_is_the_users_answer_in_redkits_dialog() {
    let fx = Fixture::new();
    let profile = fx.path(r"docs\profile.settings");
    fs::write(&profile, "[Telemetry]\noriginal=1\n").unwrap();
    let start = |fx: &Fixture| {
        let mut quen = Quen::spawn_with(fx, "config.toml", 0, &[("QUEN_TEST_EULA", "0")]);
        quen.init(fx);
        quen
    };
    let licence = json!({"licence": true});
    let mut quen = start(&fx);
    let without = quen.tool("quen_setup", licence.clone());
    assert_eq!(
        without["needs"][0]["dependency"], "The Witcher 3 REDkit",
        "{without}"
    );
    quen.kill_daemon();
    redkit(&fx);
    let mut quen = start(&fx);
    let doctor = quen.tool("quen_doctor", json!({}));
    let deps = doctor["dependencies"].as_array().unwrap();
    let row = deps
        .iter()
        .find(|d| d["name"] == "The Witcher 3 REDkit")
        .unwrap();
    let note = row["note"].as_str().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(row["status"], "found", "{row}");
    assert!(
        note.contains("not accepted (DoNotShowEula = 0)") && note.contains("quen_setup"),
        "{note}"
    );
    let refused = quen.tool("script_compile", json!({}));
    assert_eq!(refused["refused"], true, "{refused}");
    assert_eq!(refused["needs"][0]["status"], "licence_not_accepted");
    assert_eq!(refused["needs"][0]["needed_for"], "script_compile");
    assert!(!fx.path(r"docs\editoruser.settings").exists());

    let reason = |out: Value| out["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_owned();
    let journal = fx.path(r"data\state\journal.jsonl");
    fs::create_dir_all(journal.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
    fs::write(&journal, "").unwrap();
    let left = reason(quen.tool("quen_setup", licence.clone()));
    fs::remove_file(&journal).unwrap(); // the test's own
    assert!(left.contains("session_recover first"), "{left}");
    let mut game = outside_game(&fx);
    let running = reason(quen.tool("quen_setup", licence.clone()));
    let _ = game.kill();
    let _ = game.wait();
    assert!(running.contains("the game runs"), "{running}");
    let launched = launch(&mut quen);
    let live = reason(quen.tool("quen_setup", licence.clone()));
    assert!(live.contains("a session is live"), "{live}");
    let ended = quen.tool("session_end", json!({"token": launched["token"]}));
    assert_eq!(ended["ok"], true, "{ended}");
    assert!(!fx.path(r"docs\editoruser.settings").exists());

    let out = quen.tool("quen_setup", licence);
    assert_eq!(out["ok"], true, "{out}");
    assert_eq!(
        (&out["accepted"], &out["do_not_show_eula"]),
        (&json!(false), &json!(0))
    );
    assert_eq!(
        (&out["exit_code"], &out["dialog_shown"]),
        (&json!(0), &json!(false))
    );
    let said = fs::read_to_string(scratch(&out).join("wcc_lite.log")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(said.trim(), "", "no command and no switch");
    assert_eq!(
        fs::read_to_string(&profile).unwrap(),
        "[Telemetry]\noriginal=1\n"
    );
    assert!(!fx.path(r"docs\editoruser.settings").exists());
    assert!(!journal.exists());
}
```
