`w3/probes/freecam/modQuenProbeFreecam/content/scripts/local/quenProbeFreecam.ws`:

```ws
// modQuenProbeFreecam: a PROBE for a later quen free-camera tool, not for play (README.md beside this mod).
// Do the game's developer free-camera natives (CR4Game's EnableFreeCamera, MoveFreeCamera, GetFreeCameraPosition,
// IsFreeCameraEnabled) work in the retail 5.01, with the world running? Console execs turn it on and off, move it, and
// log one line each on LogChannel('QuenFC'). Nothing runs until typed. No resources, no wrapped vanilla method, no field.

function QuenFcPos(v : Vector) : string
{
	return FloatToStringPrec(v.X, 2) + "," + FloatToStringPrec(v.Y, 2) + "," + FloatToStringPrec(v.Z, 2);
}

function QuenFcRot(r : EulerAngles) : string
{
	return FloatToStringPrec(r.Pitch, 2) + "," + FloatToStringPrec(r.Yaw, 2) + "," + FloatToStringPrec(r.Roll, 2);
}

// The alive actors within radius of at, the player among them when in range (FindGameplayEntitiesInSphere with
// FLAG_OnlyAliveActors, as vanilla's GetActorsInRange asks).
function QuenFcCount(at : Vector, radius : float) : int
{
	var ents : array<CGameplayEntity>;

	FindGameplayEntitiesInSphere(ents, at, radius, 1000, '', FLAG_OnlyAliveActors);
	return ents.Size();
}

// One line: the free camera (on, its position), the rendered camera (theCamera: does it follow the free one?), the
// player, the camera's distance from him, the world's clocks and pause, and the alive actors within radius (default 30
// m, as world_actors) of the free camera and of the player.
function QuenFcStatus(what : string, radius : float)
{
	var fc, p : Vector;

	if (radius <= 0) radius = 30;
	fc = theGame.GetFreeCameraPosition();
	p = thePlayer.GetWorldPosition();
	LogChannel('QuenFC', what + " on=" + theGame.IsFreeCameraEnabled() + " fc=" + QuenFcPos(fc)
		+ " cam=" + QuenFcPos(theCamera.GetCameraPosition()) + " cam_rot=" + QuenFcRot(theCamera.GetCameraRotation())
		+ " player=" + QuenFcPos(p) + " heading=" + FloatToStringPrec(thePlayer.GetHeading(), 2)
		+ " dist=" + FloatToStringPrec(VecDistance(fc, p), 2) + " paused=" + theGame.IsPaused()
		+ " game_s=" + GameTimeToSeconds(theGame.GetGameTime()) + " engine_s=" + FloatToStringPrec(theGame.GetEngineTimeAsSeconds(), 2)
		+ " r=" + FloatToStringPrec(radius, 0) + " near_fc=" + QuenFcCount(fc, radius) + " near_player=" + QuenFcCount(p, radius));
}

// MoveFreeCamera, then the position read back at once (the move may land a tick later: qfcstatus reads it again).
function QuenFcMove(what : string, pos : Vector, rot : EulerAngles)
{
	var fc : Vector;

	theGame.MoveFreeCamera(pos, rot);
	fc = theGame.GetFreeCameraPosition();
	LogChannel('QuenFC', what + " sent=" + QuenFcPos(pos) + " rot=" + QuenFcRot(rot) + " on=" + theGame.IsFreeCameraEnabled()
		+ " read=" + QuenFcPos(fc) + " off_m=" + FloatToStringPrec(VecDistance(pos, fc), 2));
}

// qfcon() / qfcoff(): EnableFreeCamera(true / false), then the status line.
exec function qfcon()
{
	theGame.EnableFreeCamera(true);
	QuenFcStatus("on", 0);
}

exec function qfcoff()
{
	theGame.EnableFreeCamera(false);
	QuenFcStatus("off", 0);
}

// qfcmove(x, y, z, pitch, yaw, roll): the free camera to that pose (metres; degrees, EulerAngles(Pitch, Yaw, Roll)).
exec function qfcmove(x : float, y : float, z : float, optional pitch : float, optional yaw : float, optional roll : float)
{
	QuenFcMove("move", Vector(x, y, z), EulerAngles(pitch, yaw, roll));
}

// qfcrel(fwd, right, up): the free camera fwd m along Geralt's heading and right m to his right (both 0: fwd 10), up m
// (default 2) above the navmesh there (NavigationComputeZ within 30 m of his z; else above his z: ground= says which),
// aimed at 1.7 m above his position: yaw VecHeading (forward (-sin, cos), as game_camera's), pitch the drop's angle,
// negative looking down, as quen's photo-mode framing has it. The free camera's own convention is what the probe asks.
exec function qfcrel(optional fwd : float, optional right : float, optional up : float)
{
	var p, f, c, d : Vector;
	var z : float;
	var ground : string = "player";

	if (fwd == 0 && right == 0) fwd = 10;
	if (up == 0) up = 2;
	p = thePlayer.GetWorldPosition();
	f = VecNormalize2D(thePlayer.GetHeadingVector());
	c = p + fwd * f + right * Vector(f.Y, -f.X, 0);
	if (theGame.GetWorld().NavigationComputeZ(c, p.Z - 30, p.Z + 30, z))
	{
		c.Z = z;
		ground = "nav";
	}
	c.Z += up;
	d = p + Vector(0, 0, 1.7) - c;
	QuenFcMove("rel fwd=" + FloatToStringPrec(fwd, 1) + " right=" + FloatToStringPrec(right, 1) + " up=" + FloatToStringPrec(up, 1)
		+ " ground=" + ground, c, EulerAngles(Rad2Deg(AtanF(d.Z, VecLength2D(d))), VecHeading(d), 0));
}

// qfcstatus(radius): the status line, changing nothing.
exec function qfcstatus(optional radius : float)
{
	QuenFcStatus("status", radius);
}

```

`w3/probes/indicator/README.md`:

```md
# modQuenProbeIndicator: PROBE BUILD, not for play

A throwaway script mod for phase 0 of quen's status-indicator design (internal; its §3.8). It answers in one boot of about 25 minutes, with the PC free, whether the game's own GUI can carry a lasting "what the agent does" line:
- the overlay notification made lasting (phase 1);
- a dormant vanilla HUD module revived at run time (phase 2).

Two folders, each a `stage_mods` folder with one `.ws` and no resources. No vanilla file is changed.

| Folder | Staged | What it adds |
|---|---|---|
| `modQuenProbeIndicator` | in the boot | 8 exec functions, a class, one field and two methods on `CR4Player` (the walker probe's pattern). No wrapped vanilla method |
| `modQuenProbeIndicatorWrap` | only in the fallback boot, beside the first | one wrapped method, `CR4ScriptedHud.OnConfigUI` (below) |

Nothing runs until an exec is called. Every line goes to the log channel `QuenInd`: `game_exec`'s `log` returns them (boot 190), and `game_scriptlog` with `channel: "QuenInd"` reads them (needs `debugscripts`).

## What it rests on

Read in REDkit's depot on 2026-10-21 (its scripts are byte-identical to 5.01's). `gui` is `r4data\gameplay\gui_new\actionscript\red\game\witcher3`.

- **The notification:**
  - `gui\popups\NotificationModule.as` 98-110: a Flash `Timer` of the duration (0 gives 4000 ms), then a 0.3 s tween out (89-96), then `visible = false` (135-139).
  - `gui\popups\OverlayPopupMenu.as`:
    - `showNotification` (127-146): with `queue` false, a shown one is hidden and the new one shows after that tween;
    - `hideNotification` (148-154): the tween only, the queue kept. No vanilla script calls it;
    - `clearNotificationsQueue` (156-164): the tween and the queue emptied.
  - Closing the hub menu (inventory, map, ...) calls `ClearNotificationsQueue` (`game\gui\menus\commonMenu.ws` 567), so a lasting notification ends there.
- **The HUD module table:**
  - `gui\hud\Hud.as` 54: `public var moduleManager`.
  - `HudModuleManager.as` 18-23: `AddEntry(name, file, depth)` fills `entries` (a `Vector`) and a dictionary.
  - `Hud.as` 287-301: `loadModule` looks the name up; an unknown name loads nothing.
  - The AreaInfo and Watermark entries are commented out (`Hud.as` 246, 234). `hud.ws` 385 creates AreaInfoModule anyway, so its movie never arrives.
- **A module loaded late sits hidden:**
  - A module starts in its Flash `Hide` state (`HudModuleBase.as` 59-68). On load it takes its entry's `m_state` (`Hud.as` 337), which `SetInputContext` sets only for entries already in the table (383-460). An entry added later gets none, so the module stays in `Hide` until the input context changes.
  - In `Hide`, `ShowElement` only records the wish (`states\HideState.as`).
  - `CR4ScriptedHud.UpdateHUD()` (`hud.ws` 1544) sends the current context again. In `Exploration` AreaInfo is `OnDemand`, where `ShowElement(true, true)` sets `visible` and `alpha` within the call (`HudModuleBase.as` 137-175).
  - AreaInfo is `Hide` in the contexts `Combat`, `CombatFists`, `Combat_Replacer_Ciri`, `Scene`, `RadialMenu` and `Death` (`Hud.as` 70-222).
  - `ShowElement`'s third argument, `bIgnoreState`, skips the state (`HudModuleBase.as` 119-129).
- **AreaInfo itself:**
  - `HudModuleAreaInfo.as` 38-42: `SetText` upper-cases its text into `textField`.
  - Its 3 s Flash timer ends in nothing (76-80).
  - The script class hides it after its own `ShowAreaInfo` only (`hudModuleAreaInfo.ws`), which no vanilla script calls but the `testarea` exec. The probe never calls it.

## Console commands

All of them are exec functions, called with `game_exec` (no typing). Arguments are optional, and a string goes in `"`.

| Command | What it does | Log lines |
|---|---|---|
| `qinote(text, secs)` | `ShowNotification(text, secs × 1000)`, as quen's `notice` sends it with 8000. Default text: phase 1's "working" line (56 bytes); default `secs` 3600 | `note shown duration_ms=3600000 popup_before=.. now visible=.. alpha=.. x=.. y=.. scale=.. text=[..]` |
| `qinhide(clear)` | `HideNotification()`; with `clear` true, `ClearNotificationsQueue()`. Starts the watch | `note hide sent clear=.. now ..`; then `watch notification hidden t=<s> ticks=<n> ..` |
| `qiadd(which)` | The run-time entry for slot `which` (0 AreaInfo, the default; 1 Watermark), then `DiscardHudModule` and `CreateHudModule` (next section). Does nothing once the module is loaded | `add <name>: before, script object=..`, `entry root ..`, `entry <name> <file> depth=.. added: entries 29 -> 30` (or `entry refused: ..`), `add <name>: DiscardHudModule called ..`, `add <name>: CreateHudModule called ..` |
| `qishow(text, which, force)` | AreaInfo: the Flash `SetText` (default "quen: agent at work"), then `ShowElement(true, true)`. First `UpdateHUD()` if the module's state isn't `OnDemand`. `force` true: the third argument, `bIgnoreState`, instead | `show: state Hide, UpdateHUD() for context Exploration: state now OnDemand`; `show slot=0 force=false now visible=true alpha=0.80 .. state=OnDemand text=[QUEN: AGENT AT WORK]` |
| `qihide(which)` | `ShowElement(false, true)`, then `ShowElement(false, true, true)` (hides in any state), read back in the same call. Starts the watch | `hide slot=0 in the same call: visible=false alpha=0.00 ..`; `watch module hidden t=.. ticks=..` |
| `qiblink(after, which)` | Both elements shown with their default texts, both hidden `after` s later (default 2.5) by the probe's tick (the notification with `ClearNotificationsQueue`). For check 7 | `blink shown module=.. hide due in 2.50 s at t=..`; `blink hid notification=true module=true t=..`; the watch lines |
| `qisave(on)` | The overlay's saving spinner on, or off at once | `save indicator on=.. now visible=..` |
| `qistate(which)` | Read-backs only: <br>- the notification's sprite and text; <br>- the spinner; <br>- the HUD root, its `loadError` (module movies that failed to load) and the input context; <br>- slot `which`'s script object, sprite, Flash state, `isEnabled` and text; <br>- the engine time | `state t=.. note ..`, `state spinner ..`, `state hud root .. loadError=.. context=..`, `state AreaInfoModule: script object=.. state=.. enabled=.. text=[..]` |

**The watch:** after a hide, the probe's timer on the player looks at each hidden element every tick. It logs the first tick on which the element's sprite reads hidden (`visible` false or `alpha` 0), with `t`, the engine seconds since the hide, and gives up after 3 s. It runs on the world's clock, which stops in photo mode and under the pause menu. So it measures hides in gameplay only.

**Null checks:** each function checks the GUI manager, the popup, the HUD, its root sprite, `moduleManager`, `AddEntry`, the module's sprite and the Flash functions before it calls anything. On a null it logs `.. refused: ..` and changes nothing.

## The run-time module entry, and its fallback

**The order in `qiadd`** (`QuenIndEntry`, then the HUD calls). Every read comes before the first change:
1. Read the HUD (`theGame.GetHud()`) and its root sprite (`GetHudFlash()`).
   - It logs the root's public `isDynamic` and `loadError`: this proves `GetMember*` reaches the root's AS3 members.
   - Then `GetMemberFlashObject("moduleManager")` and its `GetMemberFlashFunction("AddEntry")`. A null stops here.
2. Read the table: `GetMemberFlashArray("entries")`, and vanilla's `GetObjectFromArrayWithLabel(entries, "m_name", name)`. An entry already there isn't added twice.
3. `AddEntry(name, file, depth)`, with the file name and depth of the commented-out line (`hud_areainfo.swf`, 14).
   - It reads the table back: the entry must be there.
   - If the `Vector` doesn't read as an array, the log says `unconfirmed` and the probe goes on.
   - If the table reads but lacks the entry, nothing more happens.
4. `DiscardHudModule(name)`, then `CreateHudModule(name)`.
   - Vanilla `OnConfigUI` already created AreaInfo with no entry. Whether the engine keeps a record of that, and so ignores a second `Create`, is unknown; `Discard` clears it first.
   - On a module whose movie never loaded, `Discard` should reach Flash's `unloadModule` (through `CoreHud.as`'s `_HOOK_unloadModule`, 64-67), which finds no clip and removes nothing (`Hud.as` 305-321). Inferred: the engine's side can't be read here.
   - No script holds the old module: `AddHudModuleReference` runs only from the module's own `OnConfigUI`, which never ran.
5. The movie loads asynchronously (`Loader`, then `registerChild`, then the module's `OnConfigUI`). So `qistate` reads the result in a later call.

**What can't be known before the boot:**
- whether GFx hands back a plain AS3 object (`moduleManager`) and its method through `GetMemberFlashObject` / `GetMemberFlashFunction` (no vanilla script calls `GetMemberFlashObject`);
- whether `InvokeSelf` runs a method taken from such an object;
- whether `CreateHudModule` works after the HUD's `OnConfigUI`.

The log names the first step that fails.

**The fallback (`modQuenProbeIndicatorWrap`):**
- Use it only if the entry was added (`entry .. added` or `unconfirmed`) but `qistate` never shows a loaded module. That is, the engine refuses a late `Create`.
- It wraps `CR4ScriptedHud.OnConfigUI`, the one script hook between the HUD movie's construction and its module loop (`hud.ws` 340-412). It adds the entry with the same `QuenIndEntry`, then runs the vanilla body, whose own `CreateHudModule("AreaInfoModule")` (385) then finds it.
- No `Discard`, no late `Create`. This is why it is a wrap: the run-time route needs none.
- It runs once per HUD creation, so it needs its own launch with both folders staged.
- If `GetMemberFlashObject("moduleManager")` itself gives null, the wrap can't help: it uses the same call. Then no script route exists, and phase 2 needs another way in (not built here).

## Offline compile (2026-10-21)

Through quen's `script_compile` (`stubs: true`), with wcc_lite's `-agreetoterms`. The tree: the game's scripts, every installed `Mods\*\content\scripts` and the probe. The game wasn't running, and the lock was free.

| Run | `extra` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| clean | `modQuenProbeIndicator` | exit 0, 0 errors, 724 warnings, none in the probe's file |
| fallback | `modQuenProbeIndicator`, `modQuenProbeIndicatorWrap` | exit 0, 0 errors; the same 724 warnings (`messages.json` byte-identical to the clean run's) |
| control | a scratch copy with `QuenNoSuchCall();` planted after `AddEntry`'s call in `QuenIndEntry`, plus the wrap | exit 1: `local\quenProbeIndicator.ws[235]: Could not find function 'QuenNoSuchCall'`, the planted line |

The compiled files' sha256:
- `quenProbeIndicator.ws` `8c8a63f4cef662dd639433a92d472d9c99bd8bdff938e229abfe4d4b19bbb112`
- `quenProbeIndicatorWrap.ws` `6f7b5075deea210889fce8eeccd6f51ca4bca517f4a40c927a207c9723c69f7f`

What the compiler taught on the way:
- `name` and `set` are keywords;
- a `var` initialiser can't hold a cast;
- an object can't be compared with `!= NULL`: test it in an `if`;
- a wrapped event can call `wrappedMethod();` without returning its value.

## Boot plan (about 25 minutes, the PC free)

The owner and the main session schedule it. Nothing here launches the game.

**Needs:** quen 0.1.11 with quen-w3 0.1.13 or later (`game_exec`), PresentMon, no other load on the PC (a frame-time check). With quen 0.1.12 installed, the timed pairs below can go in `run_plan` (see "Timing").

**Launch:** `session_plan`, then `session_launch` after the owner's yes:
```json
{"save": "<the Hierarch Square save, the walker probe's>",
 "stage_mods": ["<checkout>\\w3\\probes\\indicator\\modQuenProbeIndicator"],
 "debugscripts": true, "photo": false, "devkit": false, "vsync": false,
 "park": "<the owner's usual park list for clean tests>", "user_ok": true}
```
- `photo: false`: HUD modules don't show in photo mode.
- `devkit: false` and `vsync: false`: a timing boot (quen_guide).

**Where to stand:** Hierarch Square, Novigrad, at the ledger's pose `hierarch-geralt-front`: `game_teleport {pos: [668.99, 1875.87, 9.94], rot: [0, 52.3, 0]}`.
- It is quen's proven test spot (boots 187-191): a stable third-person view, with merchants nearby for the dialogue.
- Checks 1-5 run at noon: `world_get` (note `day`), then `game_settime {day: <day>, hour: 12}` and `game_weather {name: "WT_Clear"}`.
- Checks 6-7, the frame-time windows, run at 02:00 (`game_settime {day: <day>, hour: 2}`), when fewer townsfolk walk.
  - Teleport to the pose again, wait 30 s (`game_keys {tokens: ["wait:30000"]}`), and note `world_actors {radius: 30}`'s `found`.
  - `measure_ab`'s drift guard then watches the count.

**Timing:**
- quen runs one call at a time, and each call is an agent turn. A screenshot can't be placed at +0.1 s or +0.5 s by hand.
- So each hide is timed by two methods:
  - the probe's watch line: `t`, engine seconds from the hide to the first tick on which Flash reads it hidden;
  - a `game_screenshot` at a known delay. With quen 0.1.12 that is one `run_plan`, e.g. `{"tag": "c1h", "steps": [{"game_exec": {"line": "qinhide()"}}, {"wait": 0.5}, {"game_screenshot": {"tag": "c1_hide05"}}]}`. Keep each plan under 30 s of estimate, so that quen shows no notice of its own.
- With quen 0.1.11 the screenshot is the very next call. It shows the hide was done by then, a few seconds at most, not at 0.5 s: `W3Quen.log` stamps ticks, and a capture's `t` has whole seconds. The 0.5 s itself then rests on the watch alone.
- Waits: `game_keys {tokens: ["wait:<ms>"]}` (up to 60000 a token). It sends no key, and the 60 s idle focus counts only from a call's end. Never leave 60 s without a quen call: idle focus would bring the chat forward and pause the game into its menu.
- quen's own notices replace the probe's notification: one before a `measure_ab` of 30 s or more, and one at `hands_give`. Show it again after them.

**The checks, in order** (the crash-prone check 3 comes after the notification's checks):

0. **Baseline:** `game_exec qistate()`. Expect:
   - `note .. visible=false`;
   - `state hud root visible=true .. loadError=0 context=Exploration`;
   - `state AreaInfoModule: script object=<true|false>`. This tells whether vanilla's `CreateHudModule` left a script object behind.
   - Then `game_screenshot {tag: "c0_plain"}`.

1. **The lasting notification** (about 3 min):
   1. `game_exec qinote()`. The log: `duration_ms=3600000`, `text=[quen: agent at work. Please keep off the mouse and keys.]`.
   2. `game_keys {tokens: ["wait:8000"]}`, then `game_screenshot {tag: "c1_t10"}`.
   3. `game_keys {tokens: ["wait:45000"]}`, then `game_screenshot {tag: "c1_t60"}`, then `game_exec qistate()` (`visible=true alpha=1.00`).
   4. The hide: `game_exec qinhide()`, then at once `game_screenshot {tag: "c1_hide"}` (or the `run_plan` above).
   5. `game_scriptlog {channel: "QuenInd", lines: 40}`: `watch notification hidden t=..`.
   6. A longer text (an exec argument holds at most 100 bytes): `game_exec qinote("quen: you have the controls. Tell the agent in the chat to take them back.")` (74 bytes), then `game_screenshot {tag: "c1_long"}` and `game_exec qistate()`: does the box fit it, and did the text arrive whole through the console's parser? Then `game_exec qinhide(true)`.

2. **Replacement** (about 2 min):
   1. `game_exec qinote()`, then `game_exec testnotify()` (vanilla: "Some test notification", 4 s).
   2. `game_screenshot {tag: "c2_vanilla"}`.
   3. `game_keys {tokens: ["wait:6000"]}`, then `game_screenshot {tag: "c2_after"}` and `game_exec qistate()`. Expected: nothing on screen, `text=[Some test notification]`: quen's line doesn't come back.
   4. The hub menu: `game_exec qinote()`, `game_keys {tokens: ["i"]}` (the inventory), `game_screenshot {tag: "c2_hub"}`, `game_keys {tokens: ["escape"]}`, `game_screenshot {tag: "c2_hub_closed"}`. Expected: cleared on closing (`commonMenu.ws` 567).
   5. Then `game_exec qinhide(true)`.

3. **The run-time module entry** (about 2 min):
   1. `game_exec qiadd()`. Read its `log` line by line: which step passed, and whether the entry count went 29 to 30.
   2. `game_exec qistate()`. Expect `script object=true visible=true alpha=0.00 .. state=Hide`.
      - If it shows `sprite=null`: `game_keys {tokens: ["wait:2000"]}` and `qistate()` again. A movie load takes frames.
      - Compare `loadError` with check 0's: a rise means the movie file failed to load.
   3. **If the game exits** (every result's `state.game` says `exited`): `session_end`, report the log's last `QuenInd` line, and stop. The fallback needs the owner's call after a crash.
   4. **If the entry was added but no module loads** after two reads: the fallback boot (below).
   5. **If a step before `AddEntry` refused:** the fallback can't help. Record which step, and skip checks 4, 5 (module part) and 9.

4. **Text, look, hide latency** (about 2 min):
   1. `game_exec qishow()`. The log: `state Hide, UpdateHUD() .. state now OnDemand`, then `visible=true alpha=0.80 .. text=[QUEN: AGENT AT WORK]`.
      - If the state stays `Hide` (another context): `game_exec qishow("quen: agent at work", 0, true)`.
   2. `game_screenshot {tag: "c4_shown"}`. Expected: gold upper-case, about 50 px at 1080p, centred near the top (the anchor `mcAnchorAreaInfo`, 960 / 167 at 1920 × 1080). Note where, how big, which font, against the HUD's other text.
   3. A longer line: `game_exec qishow("quen: measuring for about 60 s. Hands off until it ends.")`, then `game_screenshot {tag: "c4_long"}`: does the 729 px field wrap it?
   4. The hide: `game_exec qihide()`, then at once `game_screenshot {tag: "c4_hide"}` (with 0.1.12: `run_plan` with `{"wait": 0.1}`).
      - The log must say `in the same call: visible=false alpha=0.00`.
      - The watch must say `watch module hidden t=0.0.. ticks=1`.

5. **Where the game hides each element** (about 5 min). Both up first: `game_exec qinote()`, then `game_exec qishow()`, then `game_screenshot {tag: "c5_gameplay"}`.
   1. Photo mode, its UI shown:
      - `game_photo {action: "enter"}`, then `game_screenshot {tag: "c5_photo"}` and `game_exec qistate()` (is the HUD root `visible=false`?);
      - `game_keys {tokens: ["tab"]}`, then `game_screenshot {tag: "c5_photo_tab"}`;
      - `game_keys {tokens: ["tab"]}`, then `game_photo {action: "exit"}`, then `game_screenshot {tag: "c5_back"}`: do both come back?
   2. The pause menu: `game_keys {tokens: ["escape"]}`, `game_screenshot {tag: "c5_pause"}`, `game_exec qistate()` (exec works behind the menu, boot 190), then `focus {to: "game"}`.
   3. A dialogue (optional; skip it if no merchant stands within 30 m):
      - `world_actors {radius: 30}`: pick an actor whose `name` holds "Merchant" and whose `scene` is false;
      - `game_place {pos: <1.2 m from it>, face: [<its x>, <its y>]}`, then `game_keys {tokens: ["e"]}`;
      - `game_screenshot {tag: "c5_dialog"}`, then `game_exec qistate()`: the context `Scene`, the module's state `Hide`;
      - end it on its "Goodbye" line: arrows, then `enter`, with a screenshot before the `enter`;
      - `game_screenshot {tag: "c5_after_dialog"}`: does the module come back (`OnDemand` restores the shown wish)?
   4. Teleport back to the pose. Then `game_exec qinhide(true)` and `game_exec qihide()`.

6. **Frame-time cost, shown against hidden** (about 3 min, at 02:00, both hidden at the start):
   - The call:
     ```json
     {"tag": "c6", "secs": 30, "settle": 10, "strict": true,
      "states": [{"label": "hidden", "actions": [{"console": "qinhide(true)"}, {"console": "qihide()"}]},
                 {"label": "shown",  "actions": [{"console": "qinote()"}, {"console": "qishow()"}]}]}
     ```
   - The order is the default: hidden, shown, hidden, shown.
   - Window 1 measures the game as it is, so `hidden` goes first.
   - quen's own measuring notice shows before window 1, and the window starts 9 s after it, when it is gone. The `shown` lines run only later, at the switches.
   - The run ends in `shown`, so quen runs `hidden`'s lines again at the end.
   - After it: `game_scriptlog {channel: "QuenInd", lines: 60}`: each switch's `show` and `hide` lines must hold `visible=true` / `visible=false`.
   - **No measurable cost** means all of these:
     - the verdict is not `outside drift`;
     - `|diff|` of the mean frame time ≤ 0.05 ms, and of p99 ≤ 0.5 ms (the design's sampler cap; `measure_ab` gives p95, so p99 comes from each window's CSV);
     - CPU busy's diff inside its drift;
     - one PresentMode.
   - The verdict is inside drift but a drift is over 0.05 ms: "no cost seen, resolution <drift> ms". That is not a pass of the cap.
   - It is a claim of one method (PresentMon); a Tracy boot's `CBaseEngine_Tick` zones are the second.

7. **A window 0.5 s after a hide** (about 1.5 min, both hidden at the start):
   ```json
   {"tag": "c7", "secs": 10, "settle": 3, "strict": true,
    "states": [{"label": "plain", "actions": [{"console": "qinhide(true)"}]},
               {"label": "after_hide", "actions": [{"console": "qiblink(2.5)"}]}]}
   ```
   - `qiblink(2.5)` shows both elements, then hides them 2.5 s later. The window starts after the 3 s settle, about 0.5 s after the hide.
   - Check it two ways:
     - the log's `blink hid .. t=` and the watch lines (the notification gone about 0.3 s after its hide);
     - each window's `apply` / `settled` / `presentmon_start` UTC.
   - **Pass:** the verdict not `outside drift`, and every `after_hide` window's mean inside the `plain` windows' range ± their drift.

8. **The saving spinner** (optional, about 1.5 min):
   - `game_exec qisave(true)`, then `game_screenshot {tag: "c8_t0"}`;
   - `game_keys {tokens: ["wait:20000"]}`, then `game_screenshot {tag: "c8_t20"}` and `game_exec qistate()`;
   - `game_exec qisave(false)`, then `game_screenshot {tag: "c8_off"}`.

9. **Watermark** (optional, only if check 3 passed; not run in boot 200): superseded by the 0.1.16 boot's check 9 (below), which runs the same chain with quen's own movie in the slot.

**Teardown:**
1. `game_exec qinhide(true)`, `game_exec qihide()`, `game_exec qisave(false)`, then `game_screenshot {tag: "c_end"}`: nothing of the probe's.
2. `game_scriptlog {channel: "QuenInd", lines: 500}`: keep it for the report.
3. `session_end`. It recycles the staged copy. The revived module lives only in this run of the game; nothing is saved (the boot plan writes no save).

**The fallback boot** (only after check 3's "no module loads", about 8 min more):
1. `session_end`, then `session_launch` with the same arguments and `stage_mods` holding both folders: `..\modQuenProbeIndicator` and `..\modQuenProbeIndicatorWrap`.
   - Not `again`: that replays every exec of the first boot, `qiadd` included.
2. The pose and the time as before, then `game_exec qistate()`.
   - Expect `script object=true` with a sprite already. In the script log, at the load, the wrap's `entry AreaInfoModule hud_areainfo.swf depth=14 added: entries 29 -> 30`.
3. Then checks 4, 5 (the module part) and 6 as above.

## Pass / fail

| Check | Pass | Fail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 lasting | `c1_t10` and `c1_t60` show quen's text; `qistate` `visible=true` at +60 s | gone before 60 s, or the text cut |
| 1 hide | the watch's `t` ≤ 0.5 s, and `c1_hide` shows none (with 0.1.12: `c1_hide05`) | `t` over 0.5 s, or the watch gives up |
| 2 replacement | as expected: vanilla's text replaces quen's, which doesn't come back; the hub's close clears it | quen's comes back (then a queue is in play: note it) |
| 3 entry | `entry .. added`, then `qistate` shows a sprite, with no crash | a refusal before `AddEntry` (no script route), no module after `Create` (the fallback), or a crash |
| 4 look and hide | `c4_shown` readable; the hide `in the same call: visible=false`, the watch `ticks=1`, and `c4_hide` shows none | the module draws nothing while `visible=true`, or the watch's `t` is over 0.1 s |
| 5 where | each screenshot answers one cell of the design's §3.5 table; nothing to fail | — |
| 6 cost | no measurable cost, as defined in check 6 | outside drift, or over the cap |
| 7 after a hide | inside the plain windows' drift | outside it: a longer wait before windows |
| 8, 9 | answered, or skipped | — |

## What the results mean

**Phase 1** (the lasting notification and quen's states) needs checks 1, 2, 6 and 7:
- **1 passes:** `notice` takes a `duration_ms` up to 3,600,000, and the hide is a new verb.
  - The hide wait before windows and captures becomes the watch's `t` plus a margin (the design proposes 0.5 s), instead of 9 s.
  - Use `ClearNotificationsQueue` for that hide: the same tween, and a queued notification can't follow it into a window.
- **2:** confirms re-sending on quen's next transition only. The game's own notifications and the hub menu's close end quen's line until then.
- **6:**
  - No measurable cost: the line may stay up between windows.
  - Over the cap: it still shows between windows, since it is hidden in every window anyway. The budget's "may it stay up" stays no.
- **7 passes:** the 0.5 s wait holds. If it fails: lengthen the wait, then check 7 again.
- **1 fails** (the timer cuts a long duration short, or the hide doesn't work): the notification stays transition-only (today's behaviour), and phase 2 or the design's route 5 carries the lasting line.

**Phase 2** (the HUD look) needs checks 3, 4 and 5:
- **3 passes:** route B is open from script alone. quen.ws gets `QuenIndEntry`'s calls, `UpdateHUD` and the two-call hide.
  - The same entry serves route C (quen's own movie under `WatermarkModule`).
  - Check 9 shows that slot's chain.
- **3 passes only with the wrap:**
  - route B needs a wrapped `CR4ScriptedHud.OnConfigUI` in `modQuen`: one more conflict surface. No installed mod wraps it (a grep of the installed mods, 2026-10-21);
  - the module exists from the HUD's creation, not on first use.
- **3 fails before `AddEntry`:** no script route into the HUD's table.
  - Phase 2 then needs another way in (a movie of quen's loaded otherwise), or stops at the notification.
  - Route 5 stays the fallback for the look.
- **4:** the module's look decides between B as is and C (quen's own movie, styled). Its hide latency (one call, one tick) sets phase 2's wait at 0.1 s.
- **5:** fills the design's §3.5 table. The expected answer: hidden with the HUD in photo mode and menus, and by its state in combat and scenes, coming back after. The notification covers those, as the design proposes.

## The 0.1.16 boot: quen's own HUD movie (checks 9 to 14, about 18 minutes)

Boot 200 ran checks 0 to 7. quen-w3 0.1.16 puts quen's own movie in the `WatermarkModule` slot (`w3\README.md`, section HUD line). This boot checks it. The owner and the main session schedule it; nothing here launches the game.

**Needs:** quen-w3 0.1.16 installed (the doctor pins its bundle), the config's `indicator` on, quen 0.1.19 or later. Stage this probe for its read-backs only: `qistate(1)` reads the slot (its `textField` read gives `text=null`: quen's field is `tfText`), and `qihide(1)` plus the watch time a hide. **Never `qiadd(1)` or `qishow(..., 1)`:** they would add vanilla's `hud_watermark.swf` to the slot.

**Launch, pose and time** as above (a test session, `debugscripts`, `photo: false`, noon, `WT_Clear`). The lasting line is quen's own: "agent at work" from the first call, sent again every 10 s.

9. **The chain** (about 2 min):
   - `game_exec qistate(1)` at once after the launch, then after `game_keys {tokens: ["wait:12000"]}` (one re-send). Expect, by the second read, `state WatermarkModule: script object=true visible=true alpha=80 .. state=OnDemand`, and the root's `loadError` as at the first read.
   - `game_screenshot {tag: "c9_module"}`: the line at the top centre, not bottom left.
   - **No module after two re-sends** (`script object=false`, or `loadError` up by 1): the movie didn't load from the bundle. The notification keeps carrying the line. Note `loadError`, keep `scriptslog.txt` and `W3Quen.log`, and skip 10 to 12.
   - **The game exits:** `session_end`, report the last lines of `scriptslog.txt`, stop.
10. **Look, font and place** (about 2 min): from `c9_module` and, after a `measure_presentmon {secs: 5}` (its measuring line, the longest text), `c10_long`:
    - the text in the game's font, every glyph drawn (no boxes, nothing missing), white on the dark box, at about the HUD's other text's size;
    - its place against the boss and oxygen bars' (top centre) and the minimap; the long line wrapped or whole within 1000 px;
    - note x, y and height in px at 1080p: `QuenHud.as`'s `TOP` and `CENTRE` are set by eye and tuned from these.
11. **The hide** (about 1 min): `game_screenshot {tag: "c11_capture"}`: quen takes its line down 0.5 s before (`status_hide` in `timing_s`), so the frame shows none. Then `game_keys {tokens: ["wait:12000"]}` (the line back), `game_exec qihide(1)`, and `game_scriptlog {channel: "QuenInd", lines: 20}`: `in the same call: visible=false`, the watch `ticks=1`.
12. **The moves** (about 5 min). After each step a screenshot, and `game_exec qistate(1)` (exec works in photo mode and behind the menu):
    - photo mode on (`game_photo {action: "enter"}`): the line on the notification within about 0.25 s (the state poll), the module not drawn: `c12_photo`;
    - photo mode off: back on the module, the notification gone: `c12_back`;
    - the pause menu (`game_keys {tokens: ["escape:400"]}`): the notification, `c12_pause`; then `focus {to: "game"}`;
    - the inventory key (`game_keys {tokens: ["i"]}`), and after the menu closes: back on the module, `c12_hub`;
    - a dialogue if one is reached (as check 5): the notification while it plays, the module after it.
13. **No flicker on a re-send** (about 1 min): `game_keys {tokens: ["wait:25000"]}` with the line up, then `logs\serve.log`: two re-sends answered `notice already shown`; and `c13_resend` shows the line as in `c9_module`.
14. **A game notification doesn't touch quen's HUD line** (about 3 min; the reason for the movie: the notification is one slot, and in Crowds' A/B boot 214 other notices took quen's "Next" labels off it before they were read):
    - with the line on the movie: `game_exec testnotify()` (vanilla, 4 s), then at once `game_screenshot {tag: "c14_vanilla"}` and `game_exec qistate(1)`: vanilla's text bottom left and quen's line still at the top centre, `visible=true`, state `OnDemand`;
    - `game_keys {tokens: ["i"]}` (the inventory key), then `game_screenshot {tag: "c14_hub"}` once quen's state shows no menu: quen's line on the movie (while a menu is open it is on the notification, by design);
    - a "Next" label against a notice: `measure_ab {tag: "c14", secs: 5, settle: 3, order: ["A", "B"], states: [{label: "A", actions: [{console: "testnotify()"}]}, {label: "B", actions: [{console: "testnotify()"}]}]}`. Before the call, tell the owner: from the call's start, watch the top centre of the game for about 30 s; "quen: measuring ... Next: A" and then "Next: B" stay there, each at least 3 s before its window, while "Some test notification" comes and goes bottom left. Ask only whether each label stayed up until it vanished for its window. `status_label` and `status_confirm` in `timing_s` show the holds counted from the movie's answer.

**What decides:**
- 9 passes: phase 2 C works in the game. 9 fails: the notification stays the carrier (0.1.15's behaviour, which 0.1.16 keeps wherever the movie isn't drawn), and the bundle's format is the first suspect (`hud.py`'s `cooked()`).
- 10: the owner's eye decides the look; `TOP`, `CENTRE`, the size and the box are one constant each in `QuenHud.as`.
- 11: the module's 0.1 s hide is within quen's 0.5 s wait either way.
- 12: every place the HUD isn't drawn must show the notification; a place with neither is a bug in `QUEN_HudDrawn`.
- 14 passes: in gameplay no game notice takes quen's line off. A label gone before its window is a bug (the movie read `visible` and the text while not drawn, or the line went to the notification in gameplay).

## Cleanup

`session_end` recycles the staged copies. This folder is source: nothing the boot produces is written here.

```

`w3/probes/indicator/modQuenProbeIndicator/content/scripts/local/quenProbeIndicator.ws`:

```ws
// modQuenProbeIndicator: a PROBE for quen's in-game status indicator, not for play (README.md beside this mod).
// Can the game's own GUI carry a lasting status line, and hide it at once? Console execs show the overlay notification
// for up to an hour and hide it, add a run-time table entry for a dormant HUD module (AreaInfo, or Watermark) and create
// it, show, hide and read back both. Every line goes to LogChannel('QuenInd'). Nothing runs until typed. No resources, no
// wrapped vanilla method; one added field and two added methods on the player (the walker probe's pattern).

// One watch at a time: after a hide, the tick looks for each hidden element's sprite to read hidden.
class QuenIndWatch
{
	var t0, blink : float;  // engine time of the hide; qiblink: engine time its hide is due, 0 none
	var note, mod : bool;   // still watched: the notification, the module
	var ticks, which : int; // timer calls since the hide; the module slot
}

@addField(CR4Player) var quenInd : QuenIndWatch;

@addMethod(CR4Player) function QuenIndGet() : QuenIndWatch
{
	if (!quenInd)
		quenInd = new QuenIndWatch in this;
	return quenInd;
}

// Every tick while a hide is watched or a blink waits: qiblink's hide when it is due, then the first tick on which each
// watched element reads hidden (its sprite gone, not visible, or alpha 0), with the engine time since the hide. Gives up
// after 3 s. The world's clock: it stops in photo mode and under the pause menu.
@addMethod(CR4Player) timer function QuenIndTick(dt : float, id : int)
{
	var s : CScriptedFlashSprite;
	var now, t : float;

	now = theGame.GetEngineTimeAsSeconds();
	if (quenInd.blink > 0 && now >= quenInd.blink)
	{
		quenInd.blink = 0;
		QuenIndHideBoth(quenInd.which, "blink");
	}
	if (quenInd.note || quenInd.mod)
	{
		quenInd.ticks += 1;
		t = now - quenInd.t0;
		if (quenInd.note)
		{
			s = QuenIndNoteSprite();
			if (!s || !s.GetVisible() || s.GetAlpha() <= 0)
			{
				quenInd.note = false;
				LogChannel('QuenInd', "watch notification hidden t=" + FloatToStringPrec(t, 3) + " ticks=" + quenInd.ticks + " " + QuenIndSprite(s));
			}
		}
		if (quenInd.mod)
		{
			s = QuenIndModuleSprite(quenInd.which);
			if (!s || !s.GetVisible() || s.GetAlpha() <= 0)
			{
				quenInd.mod = false;
				LogChannel('QuenInd', "watch module hidden t=" + FloatToStringPrec(t, 3) + " ticks=" + quenInd.ticks + " " + QuenIndSprite(s));
			}
		}
		if ((quenInd.note || quenInd.mod) && t > 3)
		{
			LogChannel('QuenInd', "watch gave up after 3 s: still shown notification=" + quenInd.note + " module=" + quenInd.mod);
			quenInd.note = false;
			quenInd.mod = false;
		}
	}
	if (!quenInd.note && !quenInd.mod && quenInd.blink == 0)
		RemoveTimer('QuenIndTick');
}

function QuenIndWatchFrom(note : bool, mod : bool, which : int)
{
	var w : QuenIndWatch;

	if (!thePlayer)
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "watch skipped: no player");
		return;
	}
	w = thePlayer.QuenIndGet();
	w.t0 = theGame.GetEngineTimeAsSeconds();
	w.ticks = 0;
	w.note = note;
	w.mod = mod;
	w.which = which;
	thePlayer.AddTimer('QuenIndTick', 0.001, true, , , , true);
}

// The module slots: 0 AreaInfoModule, 1 WatermarkModule, with the file names and depths of the two entries Hud.as's
// table has commented out (gui_new actionscript red\game\witcher3\hud\Hud.as 222-254).
function QuenIndSlot(which : int, out modName : string, out file : string, out depth : int) : bool
{
	if (which == 0)
	{
		modName = "AreaInfoModule";
		file = "hud_areainfo.swf";
		depth = 14;
		return true;
	}
	if (which == 1)
	{
		modName = "WatermarkModule";
		file = "hud_watermark.swf";
		depth = 10;
		return true;
	}
	LogChannel('QuenInd', "refused: module slot " + which + " is not 0 (AreaInfo) or 1 (Watermark)");
	return false;
}

function QuenIndPopup() : CR4OverlayPopup
{
	var gui : CR4GuiManager = theGame.GetGuiManager();

	if (!gui)
		return NULL;
	return (CR4OverlayPopup)gui.GetPopup('OverlayPopup');
}

// The notification's sprite: OverlayPopupMenu.as's public notificationModule (a NotificationModule).
function QuenIndNoteSprite() : CScriptedFlashSprite
{
	var popup : CR4OverlayPopup = QuenIndPopup();
	var flash : CScriptedFlashSprite;

	if (!popup)
		return NULL;
	flash = popup.GetPopupFlash();
	if (!flash)
		return NULL;
	return flash.GetChildFlashSprite("notificationModule");
}

// The module's sprite: NULL until its movie has loaded and registered.
function QuenIndModuleSprite(which : int) : CScriptedFlashSprite
{
	var hud : CHud = theGame.GetHud();
	var module : CHudModule;
	var modName, file : string;
	var depth : int;

	if (!hud || !QuenIndSlot(which, modName, file, depth))
		return NULL;
	module = hud.GetHudModule(modName);
	if (!module)
		return NULL;
	return module.GetModuleFlash();
}

function QuenIndSprite(s : CScriptedFlashSprite) : string
{
	if (!s)
		return "sprite=null";
	return "visible=" + s.GetVisible() + " alpha=" + FloatToStringPrec(s.GetAlpha(), 2) + " x=" + FloatToStringPrec(s.GetX(), 1)
		+ " y=" + FloatToStringPrec(s.GetY(), 1) + " scale=" + FloatToStringPrec(s.GetXScale(), 2);
}

function QuenIndText(s : CScriptedFlashSprite, field : string) : string
{
	var tf : CScriptedFlashTextField;

	if (!s)
		return "text=null";
	tf = s.GetChildFlashTextField(field);
	if (!tf)
		return "text=null";
	return "text=[" + tf.GetText() + "]";
}

// A HUD module's Flash state (HudModuleBase.as stateMachine.current): Hide, Show, OnDemand or OnUpdate. Also a test of
// GetMemberFlashObject on a plain AS3 object.
function QuenIndFsm(s : CScriptedFlashSprite) : string
{
	var sm : CScriptedFlashObject;

	if (!s)
		return "null";
	sm = s.GetMemberFlashObject("stateMachine");
	if (!sm)
		return "unreadable";
	return sm.GetMemberFlashString("current");
}

// The run-time entry (design 3.2): AddEntry(name, file, depth) on the HUD root's public moduleManager (Hud.as 54), as
// Hud.as's constructor adds the other 29. Every read first: a null changes nothing. True when the table holds the name
// afterwards, or when AddEntry ran and the table can't be read back. The fallback's wrap calls it too.
function QuenIndEntry(hud : CHud, which : int) : bool
{
	var root : CScriptedFlashSprite;
	var mm, found : CScriptedFlashObject;
	var entries : CScriptedFlashArray;
	var add : CScriptedFlashFunction;
	var modName, file : string;
	var depth, n : int;

	if (!QuenIndSlot(which, modName, file, depth))
		return false;
	if (!hud)
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "entry refused: no HUD");
		return false;
	}
	root = hud.GetHudFlash();
	if (!root)
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "entry refused: GetHudFlash() gave null");
		return false;
	}
	LogChannel('QuenInd', "entry root " + QuenIndSprite(root) + " isDynamic=" + root.GetMemberFlashBool("isDynamic")
		+ " loadError=" + root.GetMemberFlashInt("loadError"));
	mm = root.GetMemberFlashObject("moduleManager");
	if (!mm)
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "entry refused: GetMemberFlashObject(moduleManager) gave null");
		return false;
	}
	add = mm.GetMemberFlashFunction("AddEntry");
	if (!add)
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "entry refused: moduleManager.GetMemberFlashFunction(AddEntry) gave null");
		return false;
	}
	n = -1;
	entries = mm.GetMemberFlashArray("entries");
	if (entries)
	{
		n = entries.GetLength();
		if (GetObjectFromArrayWithLabel(entries, "m_name", modName, found))
		{
			LogChannel('QuenInd', "entry " + modName + " already in the table (" + n + " entries): not added again");
			return true;
		}
	}
	add.InvokeSelfThreeArgs(FlashArgString(modName), FlashArgString(file), FlashArgInt(depth));
	entries = mm.GetMemberFlashArray("entries");
	if (!entries)
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "entry " + modName + " " + file + " depth=" + depth + ": AddEntry called; the table (a Vector) reads as no array, so unconfirmed");
		return true;
	}
	if (GetObjectFromArrayWithLabel(entries, "m_name", modName, found))
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "entry " + modName + " " + file + " depth=" + depth + " added: entries " + n + " -> " + entries.GetLength());
		return true;
	}
	LogChannel('QuenInd', "entry refused: AddEntry called but the table (" + n + " -> " + entries.GetLength() + " entries) doesn't hold " + modName);
	return false;
}

// The lasting notification as phase 1 would send it: the GUI manager's ShowNotification with a duration (quen.ws's
// notice passes 8000), queue false, so it replaces one on screen after that one's 0.3 s hide (OverlayPopupMenu.as
// showNotification). NotificationModule.as runs a Flash Timer of the duration, then hides.
function QuenIndNoteShow(text : string, secs : float) : bool
{
	var gui : CR4GuiManager = theGame.GetGuiManager();
	var had : bool;

	if (!gui)
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "note refused: no GUI manager");
		return false;
	}
	if (QuenIndPopup())
		had = true;  // else ShowNotification requests the popup, with the text as its init data
	if (text == "")
		text = "quen: agent at work. Please keep off the mouse and keys.";
	if (secs <= 0)
		secs = 3600;
	gui.ShowNotification(text, secs * 1000);
	LogChannel('QuenInd', "note shown duration_ms=" + FloatToStringPrec(secs * 1000, 0) + " popup_before=" + had
		+ " now " + QuenIndSprite(QuenIndNoteSprite()) + " " + QuenIndText(QuenIndNoteSprite(), "tfMessage"));
	return true;
}

// The notification's hide: HideNotification (Flash hideNotification: a 0.3 s tween, then visible false), or with clear
// ClearNotificationsQueue (the same tween, and a queued notification dropped). No vanilla script calls the first.
function QuenIndNoteHide(clear : bool) : bool
{
	var popup : CR4OverlayPopup = QuenIndPopup();

	if (!popup || !popup.GetPopupFlash())
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "note hide refused: no overlay popup");
		return false;
	}
	if (clear)
		popup.ClearNotificationsQueue();
	else
		popup.HideNotification();
	LogChannel('QuenInd', "note hide sent clear=" + clear + " now " + QuenIndSprite(QuenIndNoteSprite()));
	return true;
}

// The module's text and show. A module loaded after the HUD's last input context sits in its Flash Hide state (its
// table entry had no state to give it, Hud.as 337), where ShowElement only records the wish: then UpdateHUD() sends the
// current context again (hud.ws 1544) first. force: ShowElement's third argument, bIgnoreState (HudModuleBase.as 119).
function QuenIndModShow(text : string, which : int, force : bool) : bool
{
	var hud : CR4ScriptedHud;
	var s : CScriptedFlashSprite;
	var show, setText : CScriptedFlashFunction;
	var fsm : string;

	hud = (CR4ScriptedHud)theGame.GetHud();
	s = QuenIndModuleSprite(which);
	if (!hud || !s)
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "show refused: module slot " + which + " not loaded (qiadd, then qistate)");
		return false;
	}
	show = s.GetMemberFlashFunction("ShowElement");
	setText = s.GetMemberFlashFunction("SetText");
	if (!show || (which == 0 && !setText))
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "show refused: ShowElement or SetText gave null");
		return false;
	}
	fsm = QuenIndFsm(s);
	if (fsm != "OnDemand" && !force)
	{
		hud.UpdateHUD();
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "show: state " + fsm + ", UpdateHUD() for context " + hud.currentInputContext + ": state now " + QuenIndFsm(s));
	}
	if (which == 0)
	{
		if (text == "")
			text = "quen: agent at work";
		setText.InvokeSelfOneArg(FlashArgString(text));
	}
	if (force)
		show.InvokeSelfThreeArgs(FlashArgBool(true), FlashArgBool(true), FlashArgBool(true));
	else
		show.InvokeSelfTwoArgs(FlashArgBool(true), FlashArgBool(true));
	LogChannel('QuenInd', "show slot=" + which + " force=" + force + " now " + QuenIndSprite(s) + " state=" + QuenIndFsm(s) + " " + QuenIndText(s, "textField"));
	return true;
}

// The module's hide: ShowElement(false, true) as hudModuleBase.ws sends it (in OnDemand it also records the wish), then
// ShowElement(false, true, true), which hides in any state. Both set visible and alpha within the call.
function QuenIndModHide(which : int) : bool
{
	var s : CScriptedFlashSprite = QuenIndModuleSprite(which);
	var show : CScriptedFlashFunction;

	if (!s)
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "hide refused: module slot " + which + " not loaded");
		return false;
	}
	show = s.GetMemberFlashFunction("ShowElement");
	if (!show)
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "hide refused: ShowElement gave null");
		return false;
	}
	show.InvokeSelfTwoArgs(FlashArgBool(false), FlashArgBool(true));
	show.InvokeSelfThreeArgs(FlashArgBool(false), FlashArgBool(true), FlashArgBool(true));
	LogChannel('QuenInd', "hide slot=" + which + " in the same call: " + QuenIndSprite(s) + " state=" + QuenIndFsm(s));
	return true;
}

function QuenIndHideBoth(which : int, why : string)
{
	var note, mod : bool;

	note = QuenIndNoteHide(true);
	mod = QuenIndModuleSprite(which) && QuenIndModHide(which);
	LogChannel('QuenInd', why + " hid notification=" + note + " module=" + mod + " t=" + FloatToStringPrec(theGame.GetEngineTimeAsSeconds(), 3));
	QuenIndWatchFrom(note, mod, which);
}

// qinote(text, secs): the notification, up an hour by default (secs 3600) or until qinhide. Text default: phase 1's
// "working" line. At most 100 bytes through game_exec.
exec function qinote(optional text : string, optional secs : float)
{
	QuenIndNoteShow(text, secs);
}

// qinhide(clear): the notification's hide; clear true also drops a queued one. The tick logs when it reads hidden.
exec function qinhide(optional clear : bool)
{
	if (QuenIndNoteHide(clear))
		QuenIndWatchFrom(true, false, 0);
}

// qiadd(which): the dormant module of slot which (0 AreaInfo, default; 1 Watermark) made at run time, in this order:
// every read, the table entry (QuenIndEntry), DiscardHudModule (vanilla OnConfigUI's CreateHudModule found no entry
// and loaded nothing), CreateHudModule. Its movie loads on a later tick: qistate reads it. Does nothing once loaded.
exec function qiadd(optional which : int)
{
	var hud : CHud = theGame.GetHud();
	var module : CHudModule;
	var modName, file, had : string;
	var depth : int;

	if (!QuenIndSlot(which, modName, file, depth))
		return;
	if (!hud)
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "add refused: no HUD");
		return;
	}
	module = hud.GetHudModule(modName);
	if (module && module.GetModuleFlash())
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "add " + modName + ": already loaded " + QuenIndSprite(module.GetModuleFlash()));
		return;
	}
	had = "false";
	if (module)
		had = "true";
	LogChannel('QuenInd', "add " + modName + ": before, script object=" + had);
	if (!QuenIndEntry(hud, which))
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "add " + modName + ": no entry, nothing discarded or created");
		return;
	}
	hud.DiscardHudModule(modName);
	had = "false";
	if (hud.GetHudModule(modName))
		had = "true";
	LogChannel('QuenInd', "add " + modName + ": DiscardHudModule called, script object=" + had);
	hud.CreateHudModule(modName);
	module = hud.GetHudModule(modName);
	if (module)
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "add " + modName + ": CreateHudModule called, script object=true " + QuenIndSprite(module.GetModuleFlash()) + " (the movie loads on a later tick: qistate)");
	else
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "add " + modName + ": CreateHudModule called, script object=false (the movie loads on a later tick: qistate)");
}

// qishow(text, which, force): the module's text (AreaInfo only: Watermark shows its own) and ShowElement(true, true).
exec function qishow(optional text : string, optional which : int, optional force : bool)
{
	QuenIndModShow(text, which, force);
}

// qihide(which): the module's hide, read back in the same call; the tick logs it too.
exec function qihide(optional which : int)
{
	if (QuenIndModHide(which))
		QuenIndWatchFrom(false, true, which);
}

// qiblink(after, which): both shown with their default texts, both hidden after s later (default 2.5) by the tick, the
// notification with ClearNotificationsQueue. For measure_ab: settle 3 then starts the window about 0.5 s after the hide.
exec function qiblink(optional after : float, optional which : int)
{
	var w : QuenIndWatch;
	var mod : bool;

	if (!thePlayer)
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "blink refused: no player");
		return;
	}
	if (after <= 0)
		after = 2.5;
	QuenIndNoteShow("", 0);
	mod = QuenIndModuleSprite(which) && QuenIndModShow("", which, false);
	w = thePlayer.QuenIndGet();
	w.blink = theGame.GetEngineTimeAsSeconds() + after;
	w.which = which;
	thePlayer.AddTimer('QuenIndTick', 0.001, true, , , , true);
	LogChannel('QuenInd', "blink shown module=" + mod + " hide due in " + FloatToStringPrec(after, 2) + " s at t=" + FloatToStringPrec(w.blink, 3));
}

// qisave(on): the overlay's saving spinner on or off (CR4GuiManager.ShowSavingIndicator / HideSavingIndicator(true)):
// does it last? A text-free "busy" marker.
exec function qisave(optional on : bool)
{
	var gui : CR4GuiManager = theGame.GetGuiManager();
	var popup : CR4OverlayPopup = QuenIndPopup();

	if (!gui || !popup || !popup.GetPopupFlash())
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "save refused: no GUI manager or overlay popup");
		return;
	}
	if (on)
		gui.ShowSavingIndicator();
	else
		gui.HideSavingIndicator(true);
	LogChannel('QuenInd', "save indicator on=" + on + " now " + QuenIndSprite(popup.GetPopupFlash().GetChildFlashSprite("mcIndicatorSave")));
}

// qistate(which): read-backs only, changes nothing. The notification (sprite, text), the spinner, the HUD root, the input
// context, the module of slot which (script object, sprite, Flash state, enabled, text) and the engine time.
exec function qistate(optional which : int)
{
	var hud : CR4ScriptedHud;
	var popup : CR4OverlayPopup = QuenIndPopup();
	var module : CHudModule;
	var s, root : CScriptedFlashSprite;
	var modName, file : string;
	var depth : int;

	hud = (CR4ScriptedHud)theGame.GetHud();
	s = QuenIndNoteSprite();
	LogChannel('QuenInd', "state t=" + FloatToStringPrec(theGame.GetEngineTimeAsSeconds(), 3) + " note "
		+ QuenIndSprite(s) + " " + QuenIndText(s, "tfMessage"));
	if (popup && popup.GetPopupFlash())
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "state spinner " + QuenIndSprite(popup.GetPopupFlash().GetChildFlashSprite("mcIndicatorSave")));
	if (!hud || !QuenIndSlot(which, modName, file, depth))
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "state hud: none");
		return;
	}
	root = hud.GetHudFlash();
	if (root)  // loadError: Hud.as counts the module movies that failed to load (handleMovieLoadError)
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "state hud root " + QuenIndSprite(root) + " loadError=" + root.GetMemberFlashInt("loadError") + " context=" + hud.currentInputContext);
	else
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "state hud root: GetHudFlash() gave null");
	module = hud.GetHudModule(modName);
	if (!module)
	{
		LogChannel('QuenInd', "state " + modName + ": script object=false");
		return;
	}
	s = module.GetModuleFlash();
	LogChannel('QuenInd', "state " + modName + ": script object=true " + QuenIndSprite(s) + " state=" + QuenIndFsm(s)
		+ " enabled=" + (s && s.GetMemberFlashBool("isEnabled")) + " " + QuenIndText(s, "textField"));
}

`w3/probes/walkers/README.md`:

```md
# modQuenProbeWalkers: PROBE BUILD, not for play

A throwaway script mod. It answers one question in one boot: **do spawned commoners, not a community's, walk where a script tells them, the same way twice?** quen builds its walker-scenario verbs (spawn, walk, despawn by tag) only if they do. Community NPCs refused `ActionMoveToAsync` in boot 178 (0 of 8, 0 of 2); spawned ones are untested.

- One file: `modQuenProbeWalkers\content\scripts\local\quenProbeWalkers.ws`. It goes in with quen's `stage_mods`; no resources.
- No wrapped vanilla method. It adds a class, one field and one timer function to `CR4Player` (`@addField`, `@addMethod`, the way installed mods add their timers).
- Nothing runs until a console line is typed.

## What it spawns, and how it orders the walk

- **Template:** `characters\npc_entities\crowd_npc\novigrad_citizen\novigrad_citizen.w2ent`, in `bob.bundle` and `ep1.bundle` (quen `data_read`, 2026-10-20).
  - It is a `CNewNPC` on `gameplay\trees\npc_base.w2behtree`, group `ENGT_Commoner` (`CAINPCGroupTypeRedefinition`), with the commoner reaction trees.
  - Those are the same AI trees as `crowd_npc\novigrad_citizen\community\novigrad_citizen_community.w2ent`, the copy that communities spawn. So the walkers are townsfolk in all but their spawner.
  - Created as vanilla's animation test spawner creates test NPCs (`game\animations\animationTestSpawner.ws:173`): `CreateEntity(template, pos, rot, true, false, false, PM_DontPersist, tags)`, with the tag `quen_walker` set at creation.
- **The lane:** walker *i* starts `dist` m ahead of Geralt, at a lateral offset `side + (i - (n-1)/2) × 1.2` m to his right, and walks to the mirror point `dist` m behind him.
  - The walkers come towards the camera.
  - Both Z values come from `NavigationComputeZ` (±5 m), as the scene player corrects a walk target (`game\scenes\scenePlayer.ws:424`). A point off the navmesh skips that walker, and the log says so.
  - `lane_clear` is `NavigationLineTest(start, target, 0.4)`: whether a straight 0.4 m lane exists on the navmesh.
  - The lane depends only on Geralt's position and heading: a `game_teleport` to the same pose gives the same lane.
- **Method 0 (default):** a `CAIMoveToPoint` tree (`resdef:ai\scripted_actions/move_to_point`), walk speed, destination and heading set, then `ForceAIBehavior(tree, BTAP_Emergency)`.
  - That is how vanilla walks non-player actors: the scene player (`scenePlayer.ws:417-457`) and the `MovePlayerFwd` exec (`game\temp.ws`) build the tree the same way.
- **Method 1:** `ActionMoveToAsync(target, MT_Walk, 1.0, 1.0)`, the call community NPCs refused.
  - The latent `ActionMoveTo` is left out: an exec can't wait on a latent call, and it would need an entity state of its own.
- **The walk's clock:** a timer on the player, every 0.2 s. Per walker it records:
  - path length and the largest distance from the start-target line, both horizontal;
  - arrival: within 1.0 m of the target, horizontally (`CAIMoveToPoint`'s default `maxDistance`);
  - failure: the timeout, or the walker gone.

## Console commands

Exec functions need the console on (quen's launch turns it on). Every line goes to the log channel `QuenWalk`: read it with `game_scriptlog` and `channel: "QuenWalk"` (needs `debugscripts`).

| Command | What it does | Log lines |
|---|---|---|
| `qwspawn(n, dist, side)` | Clears first (as `qwclear`), then spawns `n` walkers (default 3, at most 12) in the lane, `dist` m each way (default 10), its middle `side` m to Geralt's right (default 0: through his spot) | `spawn i=.. lane=.. at=x,y,z to=x,y,z lane_clear=true/false` per walker; `spawn lane=.. skipped/failed: ..`; then `spawned K of n player=x,y,z heading=h template=..` |
| `qwgo(method, timeout, delay)` | Orders every walker that isn't walking or waiting. The walks start `delay` s later (default 0), all on one tick, each from where its walker stands then. A walk fails `timeout` s after its start (default 60). A failed or arrived walker can be ordered again, by either method | `ordered K method=.. timeout=.. delay=..`; at the start `order i=.. method=.. id=.. from=x,y,z dist=..`. `id` is ForceAIBehavior's action id, or 1/0 for ActionMoveToAsync's true/false |
| (the tick) | | `arrived i=.. t=<s since start> dist=.. path=.. straight=.. dev=..`, `failed i=.. why=timeout\|gone ..`; when no walker walks or waits, `qwstatus`'s lines |
| `qwstatus()` | Changes nothing | `status i=.. state=spawned\|waiting\|walking\|arrived\|failed t=.. dist=<to target now> path=.. straight=.. dev=.. at=x,y,z` per walker (a waiting walker's `t` is negative: the seconds until its start), then `status tracked=.. spawned=.. walking=.. arrived=.. failed=.. waiting=.. tagged=<entities in the world with the tag>` |
| `qwclear()` | Destroys every entity tagged `quen_walker` (`GetEntitiesByTag`, `Destroy`), stops the tick, forgets the list. Idempotent | `clear destroyed=N` |

After a load the list is empty (it lives on the player), so `qwstatus`'s `tagged` is the persistence count.

## Offline compile (2026-10-20)

`script_compile` refused: quen's config has no `redkit`. So the compile ran by hand, as `w3/README.md` describes:
- wcc_lite `compilescripts <tree> -out=<dir> -agreetoterms`, run from REDkit's `bin\x64_RedKit`;
- the tree a scratch copy of `content\content0\scripts`, with every installed `Mods\*\content\scripts` over it (quen's package included) and then this mod;
- the mods' `import function`s replaced by plain stubs;
- the four `Documents\The Witcher 3` settings files backed up before each run and put back after, bytes and write times checked.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| clean | `Success! Scripts cooked`, exit 0, 362 warnings (the package's own count), none in this file |
| control: an unknown call planted in `qwclear`'s body | exit 1: `local\quenProbeWalkers.ws[274]: Could not find function 'QuenNoSuchCall'`, the planted line |

The file compiled: `quenProbeWalkers.ws` sha256 `5a2fdc723ecf049d0a2f2626b1f48e5ef7202f2ab997b1c12c034e37a82930a8`.

What the compiler taught on the way: `state` is a keyword; an exec function can't call another exec; a field can't be assigned through `thePlayer` from outside the class.

## Boot plan (about 10 minutes of game time)

The owner and the main session schedule the boot. Nothing here launches the game.

**Launch:**
- Needs quen-w3 0.1.12, for `world_actors`' and the trace's `tag`. Install no NPC mod and stage none: the Crowds brain probe swaps `npc_base.w2behtree`, which these walkers run on.
- `session_plan`, then `session_launch` with:
  - `save`: a save in Novigrad (the Crowds probes' Hierarch Square daytime save will do);
  - `stage_mods: ["<this checkout>\\w3\\probes\\walkers\\modQuenProbeWalkers"]`;
  - `debugscripts: true`, so `LogChannel` reaches `scriptslog.txt`;
  - `photo: false`, because photo mode pauses the world;
  - `devkit: false`;
  - the owner's usual `park` for clean tests;
  - `user_ok: true`, after the owner's yes.

**Where to stand:** Hierarch Square, Novigrad, at Geralt's pose from the ledger's poses (`hierarch-geralt-front`):
- `game_teleport {pos: [668.99, 1875.87, 9.94], rot: [0, 52.3, 0]}`.
- If any `spawn` line says `skipped` or `lane_clear=false`, run `qwclear()`, teleport again with yaw 142.3 (then 232.3, then 322.3), and use the first heading whose lanes are all clear for every run.

**Before the first spawn:** `game_listsaves`. Note the newest AutoSave, for the persistence check.

**Each run.** One run is the same six calls; `<lane>` and `<method>` are in the table below.
1. `game_teleport`, the pose above.
2. `game_console "qwspawn(3, 12, <lane>)"`.
3. `world_actors {tag: "quen_walker", radius: 30}`: 3 found, each with an `id`; note their positions.
4. `game_console "qwgo(<method>, 60, 15)"`: the walks start 15 s later, so the trace (the next call) covers them from standing.
5. `measure_trace {tag: "<run>", secs: 50, trace: {tag: "quen_walker", radius: 30, max: 12}}`. quen runs one game call at a time, so the trace starts only after the console line.
6. `game_scriptlog {channel: "QuenWalk", lines: 60}`: the `order`, `arrived` / `failed` and `status` lines.

| Run | `<lane>` | `<method>` | Asks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `walk_a1` | 3 (lanes at 1.8, 3.0 and 4.2 m right of Geralt) | 0 | do they arrive, straight? |
| `walk_a2` | 3 | 0 | the same paths again? |
| `walk_b` | 0 (the middle lane through Geralt's spot) | 0 | the Crowds case: walkers meeting the player |
| `walk_c` | 3 | 1 | does ActionMoveToAsync move spawned NPCs? |

If method 0 fails in `walk_a1`, skip `walk_a2` and `walk_b`. Instead order the same walkers by method 1 where they stand: `qwgo(1, 60, 15)`, then the trace and the log as in steps 5 and 6.

**Teardown:**
1. `game_console "qwclear()"` twice: `clear destroyed=3`, then `clear destroyed=0`.
2. `game_console "qwstatus()"`, then `game_scriptlog`: `tagged=0`.
3. `world_actors {tag: "quen_walker", radius: 100}`: `found: 0`.

**The persistence check:**
1. `game_listsaves`.
2. `game_load` the newest AutoSave.
3. `game_console "qwstatus()"`, then `game_scriptlog`: `tracked=0 ... tagged=0`.
4. `world_actors {tag: "quen_walker", radius: 100}`: `found: 0`.

The check is decisive for `PM_DontPersist` only if that AutoSave is new since the first spawn, that is, written while walkers lived. If it is older, the check only shows that a load brings back none. Then report `PM_DontPersist` as untested. The boot plan writes no save. Testing it fully needs one `game_save` while walkers stand, and that is the owner's call.

Then `session_end`.

## What counts as "walkers obey"

Each criterion needs both methods to agree: the probe's own 0.2 s samples (its log) and quen's 10 Hz trace (the CSV). Match a walker to its trace track by `id`: its first trace rows sit at its `spawn ... at=` point.

1. **Arrive:** every walker of `walk_a1` logs `arrived` with `t` ≤ 40 s (24 m at walking pace takes about 15-20 s). Its last trace sample is within 1.0 m of its `to=` point.
2. **Straight-ish:** `path` ≤ 1.2 × `straight`, and `dev` ≤ 1.0 m, in the log; the trace's largest lateral offset from the lane is ≤ 1.0 m.
3. **Twice the same:** for `walk_a1` and `walk_a2`, lane by lane:
   - `t` within 2 s, `path` within 1.0 m and `dev` within 0.5 m (log);
   - the lateral offset at each metre of progress along the lane within 0.5 m (trace CSVs).

**Obey** means all three for one method. The town's own crowd isn't controlled, so a single bump can break 3. Then run `walk_a2` once more at night (`game_settime`, hour 2: fewer townsfolk) before calling it.

## What each outcome means

| Seen | Meaning, next step |
|---|---|
| Method 0 meets 1-3 | **Obey.** Build `spawn` / `walk` / `despawn` on `CAIMoveToPoint` + `ForceAIBehavior` |
| Method 0 refuses (`id` < 0, or no motion), method 1 meets 1-3 | Obey by ActionMoveToAsync: build the verbs on it |
| They arrive but miss 2 or 3 | They walk, but not reproducibly: shorter legs (waypoints), or night runs. The owner decides before any verb |
| Neither method moves them | Spawned commoners refuse too: no scenario verbs as designed. Next: another template, or a forced tree from a resource |
| `walk_b` walkers stop or detour at Geralt | Expected vanilla avoidance: the Crowds mod's subject, not a probe failure |
| `tagged` > 0 after `qwclear` | Destroy by tag fails: blocking, cleanup needs another way |
| `tagged` > 0 after the AutoSave load | `PM_DontPersist` lets walkers into saves: a scenario run must forbid saves |

## Cleanup

`session_end` recycles the staged copy. A crash takes the walkers with the game. This folder is source: nothing it produces is written here.

`w3/probes/walkers/modQuenProbeWalkers/content/scripts/local/quenProbeWalkers.ws`:

```ws
// modQuenProbeWalkers: a PROBE for quen's walker scenarios, not for play (README.md beside this mod).
// Do spawned commoners, not a community's, walk where a script tells them? Console execs spawn N in a lane through
// or beside Geralt, order them to its far end, log each walk on LogChannel('QuenWalk') and destroy them by tag.
// Nothing runs until typed. No resources, no wrapped vanilla method; one added timer on the player.

class QuenWalker
{
	var npc : CNewNPC;
	var start, target, last : Vector;  // the walk's line (from where it stood at its start), the last sample
	var t0, t1, timeout : float;       // engine time of the walk's start (while waiting, when it is due) and of
	                                   // arrival or failure; the walk's limit
	var path, dev : float;             // horizontal: length walked, largest distance from the start-target line
	var phase, method : int;           // phase 0 spawned, 1 walking, 2 arrived, 3 failed, 4 ordered (waits for its start)
}

@addField(CR4Player) var quenWalkers : array<QuenWalker>;

function QuenWalkPos(v : Vector) : string
{
	return FloatToStringPrec(v.X, 2) + "," + FloatToStringPrec(v.Y, 2) + "," + FloatToStringPrec(v.Z, 2);
}

// qwspawn(n, dist, side): clears the lane, then spawns n walkers (default 3, at most 12) dist m ahead of Geralt
// (default 10), 1.2 m apart across the lane, its middle side m to his right (default 0: through his spot). Each one's
// target is the mirror point dist m behind him; both Z from the navmesh. The lane is set by Geralt's position and
// heading, so a teleport to the same pose gives the same lane.
exec function qwspawn(optional n : int, optional dist : float, optional side : float)
{
	// The non-community copy of the Novigrad commoner: a CNewNPC on npc_base.w2behtree, group ENGT_Commoner, the same
	// AI trees as crowd_npc\novigrad_citizen\community\novigrad_citizen_community.w2ent (quen data_read, 2026-10-20).
	var path : string = "characters\npc_entities\crowd_npc\novigrad_citizen\novigrad_citizen.w2ent";
	var world : CWorld = theGame.GetWorld();
	var tpl : CEntityTemplate;
	var tags : array<name>;
	var w : QuenWalker;
	var npc : CNewNPC;
	var p, f, r, a, b : Vector;
	var lat, z : float;
	var i : int;

	if (n <= 0) n = 3;
	if (n > 12) n = 12;  // the design's cap for a run
	if (dist <= 0) dist = 10;
	QuenWalkersClear();
	tpl = (CEntityTemplate)LoadResource(path, true);
	if (!tpl)
	{
		LogChannel('QuenWalk', "spawn refused: template not loaded " + path);
		return;
	}
	p = thePlayer.GetWorldPosition();
	f = VecNormalize2D(thePlayer.GetHeadingVector());  // forward (-sin h, cos h)
	r = Vector(f.Y, -f.X, 0);                           // its right
	tags.PushBack('quen_walker');
	for (i = 0; i < n; i += 1)
	{
		lat = side + ((float)i - (float)(n - 1) * 0.5) * 1.2;
		a = p + dist * f + lat * r;  // ahead, walking towards the camera
		b = p - dist * f + lat * r;
		if (!world.NavigationComputeZ(a, p.Z - 5, p.Z + 5, z))
		{
			LogChannel('QuenWalk', "spawn lane=" + i + " skipped: start off the navmesh at=" + QuenWalkPos(a));
			continue;
		}
		a.Z = z;
		if (!world.NavigationComputeZ(b, p.Z - 5, p.Z + 5, z))
		{
			LogChannel('QuenWalk', "spawn lane=" + i + " skipped: target off the navmesh at=" + QuenWalkPos(b));
			continue;
		}
		b.Z = z;
		// vanilla's idiom for test NPCs (animationTestSpawner.ws), the tag set at creation
		npc = (CNewNPC)theGame.CreateEntity(tpl, a, EulerAngles(0, VecHeading(b - a), 0), true, false, false, PM_DontPersist, tags);
		if (!npc)
		{
			LogChannel('QuenWalk', "spawn lane=" + i + " failed: CreateEntity gave no CNewNPC");
			continue;
		}
		w = new QuenWalker in thePlayer;
		w.npc = npc;
		w.start = a;
		w.target = b;
		thePlayer.quenWalkers.PushBack(w);
		LogChannel('QuenWalk', "spawn i=" + (thePlayer.quenWalkers.Size() - 1) + " lane=" + i + " at=" + QuenWalkPos(a) + " to=" + QuenWalkPos(b)
			+ " lane_clear=" + world.NavigationLineTest(a, b, 0.4));
	}
	LogChannel('QuenWalk', "spawned " + thePlayer.quenWalkers.Size() + " of " + n + " player=" + QuenWalkPos(p)
		+ " heading=" + FloatToStringPrec(thePlayer.GetHeading(), 2) + " template=" + path);
	theGame.GetGuiManager().ShowNotification("quen walkers: " + thePlayer.quenWalkers.Size() + " of " + n + " spawned", 8000);
}

// qwgo(method, timeout, delay): orders every walker that isn't walking or waiting to its target. The walks start
// delay s later (default 0), all on one tick, each from where its walker stands then: so a trace started after this
// line sees the whole walk. method 0 (default): a CAIMoveToPoint tree forced at BTAP_Emergency, as the scene player
// walks NPCs (scenePlayer.ws) and the MovePlayerFwd exec builds it (temp.ws). method 1: ActionMoveToAsync, which
// community NPCs refused in boot 178. A walk fails timeout s after its start (default 60).
exec function qwgo(optional method : int, optional timeout : float, optional delay : float)
{
	var w : QuenWalker;
	var i, n : int;

	if (timeout <= 0) timeout = 60;
	for (i = 0; i < thePlayer.quenWalkers.Size(); i += 1)
	{
		w = thePlayer.quenWalkers[i];
		if (w.phase == 1 || w.phase == 4)
			continue;
		w.method = method;
		w.timeout = timeout;
		w.t0 = theGame.GetEngineTimeAsSeconds() + delay;
		w.phase = 4;
		n += 1;
	}
	if (n > 0)
		thePlayer.AddTimer('QuenWalkersTick', 0.2, true, , , , true);
	LogChannel('QuenWalk', "ordered " + n + " method=" + method + " timeout=" + FloatToStringPrec(timeout, 0) + " delay=" + FloatToStringPrec(delay, 1));
}

// Every 0.2 s while a walk runs or waits: starts the walks that are due; path and deviation per walker; arrival
// within 1.0 m (horizontal) of its target, the CAIMoveToPoint default maxDistance; a failure at the timeout or when
// the walker is gone. When none walks or waits, the status.
@addMethod(CR4Player) timer function QuenWalkersTick(dt : float, id : int)
{
	var tree : CAIMoveToPoint;
	var w : QuenWalker;
	var pos, ab : Vector;
	var t, len : float;
	var i, oid, walking : int;

	t = theGame.GetEngineTimeAsSeconds();
	for (i = 0; i < quenWalkers.Size(); i += 1)
	{
		w = quenWalkers[i];
		if (w.phase == 4)
		{
			if (t < w.t0)
			{
				walking += 1;
				continue;
			}
			if (!w.npc || !w.npc.IsAlive())
			{
				w.phase = 3;
				w.t1 = w.t0;
				LogChannel('QuenWalk', "order i=" + i + " failed: gone");
				continue;
			}
			oid = 0;  // ForceAIBehavior's action id, or ActionMoveToAsync's bool as 0 or 1
			if (w.method == 1)
			{
				if (w.npc.ActionMoveToAsync(w.target, MT_Walk, 1.0, 1.0))
					oid = 1;
			}
			else
			{
				tree = new CAIMoveToPoint in w.npc;
				tree.OnCreated();
				tree.enterExplorationOnStart = false;
				tree.params.moveType = MT_Walk;
				tree.params.destinationPosition = w.target;
				tree.params.destinationHeading = VecHeading(w.target - w.npc.GetWorldPosition());
				oid = w.npc.ForceAIBehavior(tree, BTAP_Emergency);
			}
			w.start = w.npc.GetWorldPosition();  // the walk's line and clock start here
			w.last = w.start;
			w.t0 = t;
			w.path = 0;
			w.dev = 0;
			w.phase = 1;
			walking += 1;
			LogChannel('QuenWalk', "order i=" + i + " method=" + w.method + " id=" + oid + " from=" + QuenWalkPos(w.start)
				+ " dist=" + FloatToStringPrec(VecDistance2D(w.start, w.target), 2));
			continue;
		}
		if (w.phase != 1)
			continue;
		if (!w.npc || !w.npc.IsAlive())
		{
			w.phase = 3;
			w.t1 = t;
			LogChannel('QuenWalk', "failed i=" + i + " why=gone t=" + FloatToStringPrec(t - w.t0, 2));
			continue;
		}
		pos = w.npc.GetWorldPosition();
		w.path += VecDistance2D(w.last, pos);
		w.last = pos;
		ab = w.target - w.start;
		len = VecLength2D(ab);
		if (len > 0.01)
			w.dev = MaxF(w.dev, AbsF(ab.X * (pos.Y - w.start.Y) - ab.Y * (pos.X - w.start.X)) / len);
		if (VecDistance2D(pos, w.target) <= 1.0)
		{
			w.phase = 2;
			w.t1 = t;
			LogChannel('QuenWalk', "arrived i=" + i + " t=" + FloatToStringPrec(t - w.t0, 2) + " dist=" + FloatToStringPrec(VecDistance2D(pos, w.target), 2)
				+ " path=" + FloatToStringPrec(w.path, 2) + " straight=" + FloatToStringPrec(len, 2) + " dev=" + FloatToStringPrec(w.dev, 2));
		}
		else if (t - w.t0 > w.timeout)
		{
			w.phase = 3;
			w.t1 = t;
			LogChannel('QuenWalk', "failed i=" + i + " why=timeout t=" + FloatToStringPrec(t - w.t0, 2) + " dist=" + FloatToStringPrec(VecDistance2D(pos, w.target), 2)
				+ " path=" + FloatToStringPrec(w.path, 2) + " straight=" + FloatToStringPrec(len, 2) + " dev=" + FloatToStringPrec(w.dev, 2) + " at=" + QuenWalkPos(pos));
		}
		else
			walking += 1;
	}
	if (walking == 0)
	{
		RemoveTimer('QuenWalkersTick');
		QuenWalkersStatus();
	}
}

// qwstatus(): one line per walker this player spawned (state, time, distance to target now, path, deviation, where),
// then the totals and how many entities in the world carry the tag. After a load the list is empty, so the tag count
// is the persistence check.
exec function qwstatus()
{
	QuenWalkersStatus();
}

function QuenWalkersStatus()
{
	var states : array<string>;
	var ents : array<CEntity>;
	var w : QuenWalker;
	var pos : Vector;
	var t : float;
	var i : int;
	var counts : array<int>;

	states.PushBack("spawned");
	states.PushBack("walking");
	states.PushBack("arrived");
	states.PushBack("failed");
	states.PushBack("waiting");
	counts.Resize(5);
	for (i = 0; i < thePlayer.quenWalkers.Size(); i += 1)
	{
		w = thePlayer.quenWalkers[i];
		counts[w.phase] += 1;
		if (!w.npc)
		{
			LogChannel('QuenWalk', "status i=" + i + " state=" + states[w.phase] + " gone");
			continue;
		}
		pos = w.npc.GetWorldPosition();
		t = w.t1;
		if (w.phase == 1 || w.phase == 4)
			t = theGame.GetEngineTimeAsSeconds();
		LogChannel('QuenWalk', "status i=" + i + " state=" + states[w.phase] + " t=" + FloatToStringPrec(t - w.t0, 2)
			+ " dist=" + FloatToStringPrec(VecDistance2D(pos, w.target), 2) + " path=" + FloatToStringPrec(w.path, 2)
			+ " straight=" + FloatToStringPrec(VecDistance2D(w.start, w.target), 2) + " dev=" + FloatToStringPrec(w.dev, 2) + " at=" + QuenWalkPos(pos));
	}
	theGame.GetEntitiesByTag('quen_walker', ents);
	LogChannel('QuenWalk', "status tracked=" + thePlayer.quenWalkers.Size() + " spawned=" + counts[0] + " walking=" + counts[1]
		+ " arrived=" + counts[2] + " failed=" + counts[3] + " waiting=" + counts[4] + " tagged=" + ents.Size());
	theGame.GetGuiManager().ShowNotification("quen walkers: " + counts[2] + " arrived, " + counts[3] + " failed, " + ents.Size() + " tagged", 8000);
}

// qwclear(): destroys every entity tagged quen_walker, stops the tick and forgets the list. Idempotent.
exec function qwclear()
{
	QuenWalkersClear();
}

function QuenWalkersClear()
{
	var ents : array<CEntity>;
	var i : int;

	thePlayer.RemoveTimer('QuenWalkersTick');
	theGame.GetEntitiesByTag('quen_walker', ents);
	for (i = 0; i < ents.Size(); i += 1)
		ents[i].Destroy();
	thePlayer.quenWalkers.Clear();
	LogChannel('QuenWalk', "clear destroyed=" + ents.Size());
}

```
